# Mandu Observability Dashboard — trace + invariant oracle

> Companion to `docs/design/architecture/mandu.md` (architecture, the four
> boundaries, the two views, T-LLM/U-LLM, symbols, and the arbiter IPC the
> dashboard's data feed extends) and `docs/design/architecture/implementation-plan.md`
> (§9 the e2e invariant oracle). Terminology pairs the paper term with the
> adfi-openclaw repo term — e.g. *AgentView (repo: Agent File System /
> agent-view worktree)*.
>
> **Status: implemented** (`dashboard/`). One server serves **two
> front-ends** over the same data (§4.25): the **product page** at `/`
> (`dashboard/public/`, for the person whose agent runs under Mandu, fed by
> server projections such as `/api/home`, never by the inspector's client) and
> the **inspector** at `/dev/` (the developer view, for developers and
> reviewers; not part of the public tree or package since 2026-10-15,
> §4.25ac). The main parts: §2 the event model (canonical schema:
> `dashboard/src/event-model.ts`), §3 where events come from and how they
> travel, §4 the UI (§4.1–§4.20 the inspector's trace and panels; §4.21–§4.31
> session health, drills, secrets, the product page and the test views), §6
> server security (bind address, auth). The reference dashboard
> (adfi-openclaw `test/dashboard/`) is what we reused from; provenance in §5.

---

## 1. Purpose & audience

The dashboard is the **privileged human view of a Mandu session** — a
debugging and demo surface, *and* a visual proof of the security invariant.
Four audiences:

1. **Defense developers** debugging a run: "this `openat` ran under
   AgentView; this `connect` was desymbolized at the HumanView egress; this
   `inspect_symbol` was handled by U-LLM."
2. **Reviewers / paper readers** who must *see* DUALVIEW work: every action
   labeled with its view, every model call of both families, every value in
   both its symbolized and original form.
3. **The invariant auditor**: per session, whether any **un-symbolized
   untrusted** byte ever reached **T-LLM (repo: privileged LLM)**. The model-API
   proxy is the oracle (implementation-plan.md §9); the dashboard renders its
   verdict and drills into the exact event that would have violated it.
4. **The end user**, with no security background, asking *"is this protecting
   me?"* and *"what needs my OK?"* — answerable without the words *symbol*,
   *egress*, or *invariant*.

Audiences 1–3 get the **inspector** (most of §4, at `/dev/`); audience 4 gets
the **product page** (§4.25, at `/`), which replaced the inspector's §4.18
Simple register.

**The security invariant the dashboard must make obvious** (mandu.md §1):

> Untrusted data reaches **T-LLM** only as a **symbol** (`$MDU:*`), across
> the context, filesystem, network, and shell, and even after store-and-re-read.

Under the default `secrets` mode the confidentiality form applies (a secret
reaches a model only as a symbol unless its level admits that model); the
trace says plainly when untrusted text was not masked (§4.2f).

The dashboard is itself a **privileged human view** (like HumanView), so it *may*
reveal what a symbol stands for. That power makes the symbolized-vs-original
side-by-side possible, and it is why the dashboard must never be exposed to the
agent or to an untrusted network (§6).

### Non-goals

- Not on the enforcement path. The gate lives in the interceptors and the
  policy engine; a dead dashboard never blocks or leaks anything. (The first
  design was read-only throughout; the Policy panel now round-trips
  Approve/Deny to the arbiter's approval queue — policy-surface.md §9.8 —
  but the decision and its enforcement stay in the arbiter.)
- Not a replacement for the e2e oracle test — it *visualizes* the same property
  the test asserts (§7).

---

## 2. Event / data model

The dashboard consumes a single **canonical, append-only event stream** emitted
into the arbiter (the "event log", §3). One schema for every event kind keeps
the timeline mergeable and the view/symbolized-vs-original modeling uniform.
This is the Mandu analog of the reference dashboard's union of *conversation
entries + audit events + llm-requests*, unified into one typed record instead
of three parallel JSONL families. The canonical definition is
`dashboard/src/event-model.ts`; the emitters carry narrow mirrors of it.

**Runaway backstop (arbiter-side coalescing).** Before persisting, the arbiter
runs each emit through an `EmitCoalescer` (`arbiter/events/coalescer.ts`): the
first `burst` of an identical-consecutive run is stored verbatim, the rest are
suppressed, and a single `coalesced` summary event carries the suppressed
count (periodically and at run end). No misbehaving emitter can balloon a
session to millions of near-identical rows (a net-proxy self-loop once wrote
~36k in 21 s). Observability-only and fail-open: invariant-violating events
are never coalesced, distinct events always break the run, and
`coalesceEvents:false` disables it.

### 2.1 The view dimension (first-class)

Every event carries the view it ran under. This is the most important field for
the core requirement and drives the lane layout (§4).

```ts
type View =
  | "AgentView"    // repo: Agent File System / agent-view worktree.
                   //   What T-LLM sees: symbolized context, AgentFS reads,
                   //   AgentShell (net off, FS=AgentView).
  | "HumanView"    // repo: Human File System / human-view.
                   //   Original data: on-disk files others see, desymbolized
                   //   egress, HumanShell (net on, FS=HumanView).
  | "Quarantine";  // repo: quarantined LLM / inspect_symbol sandbox.
                   //   The U-LLM lane: untrusted text processed in isolation,
                   //   result re-symbolized before it can re-enter T-LLM.
```

### 2.2 The two-representation model (symbolized vs original)

Every input and output is a `DualRepr`: the value as **T-LLM / AgentView saw
it** (symbolized) and as **HumanView / the real world saw it** (original). They
differ exactly when symbolization happened; when identical the UI collapses
them.

A value the model never saw goes only in `original` (or a symbol's `value`),
never in `symbolized`: the signed-out projection (§6 "Reads and the admin
session") drops values by field and keeps every `symbolized`. That holds for a
`symbolize` event's input too, the value before masking: its `symbolized` form
is the symbol the event's output records, its `original` the value
(`makeSymbolize` in both proxies, fs-sync `makeBirthEvent`, since
2026-10-06). Before that the three recorded the value in both forms, so the
projection does not trust that slot (§6).

```ts
interface DualRepr {
  /** What T-LLM / AgentView saw. Untrusted spans are $MDU:* here. */
  symbolized: string;
  /** What HumanView / the real world saw. null if not desymbolized for this
   *  event (an AgentView-only read whose original never left the boundary).
   *  The privileged dashboard may still resolve on demand → "(revealed)". */
  original: string | null;
  /** True iff symbolized !== original. Drives side-by-side vs collapsed. */
  differs: boolean;
  /** Symbols referenced in `symbolized`, with provenance (SymbolRef). */
  symbols: SymbolRef[];
}
```

### 2.3 Symbol provenance

Mirrors the arbiter symbol table's entry (`tool / field / origin / session_key
/ call_id`, plus `derived_from` / `line_range`). The dashboard, being the
privileged view, may show the resolved value.

```ts
interface SymbolRef {
  name: string;            // "$MDU:web_fetch[a1b2].text"
  tool: string;            // emitting tool/origin chokepoint, e.g. "web_fetch"
  field: string | null;    // schema field path, e.g. "text"
  origin: string | null;   // URL / channel id / dir path the value came from
  value: string | null;    // resolved original (privileged reveal); null if N/A
  derivedFrom?: string;    // re-symbolization lineage (U-LLM output, git blame)
  lineRange?: string;      // FS provenance for blame-based re-symbolization
}
```

### 2.4 The canonical event

The kinds, grouped (full list and per-kind comments: `EVENT_KINDS` in
`event-model.ts`):

```ts
type EventKind =
  // model-API proxies
  | "tllm_call" | "ullm_call" | "tool_use" | "tool_result"
  // arbiter — policy + symbol table
  | "classify" | "symbolize" | "desymbolize"
  | "egress_request" | "egress_decision"   // schema only, no production emitter (§4.7)
  | "path_rewrite"         // ViewMap: HumanView↔AgentView path SPELLING translated on
                           //   the model wire (fs-sync.md §1.3); structured
                           //   `rewrite` detail {direction, tool, field, human, agent}
  // OS chokepoints and the proxies' tool-call gates
  | "fs_action" | "net_action" | "exec_action"
  // arbiter-admin audit stream (policy-surface.md §9.6)
  | "approval_resolved" | "approval_consumed" | "posture_change"
  | "config_change" | "policy_model_call"
  // session health (§4.21): the posture the session actually runs at
  | "launch_posture" | "relay_mode" | "client_info" | "tool_surface" | "session_exit"
  // the arbiter raised the session's high-watermark (a secret read into the
  // model's context): `sessionLevel` {from, to, symbol (a name), bindings}
  | "session_level"
  // the prompt filter: what it found in user-role text, never a value
  | "prompt_filter"
  // test harness — meta records kept OUT of the trace projections
  | "assertion"            // the e2e SECURITY/UTILITY/FIDELITY verdict (§4.13)
  | "workspace_seed"       // files planted before the run, raw content (§4.11)
  | "workspace_final";     // end-of-run per-view file trees, capped (§4.12)

interface ManduEvent {
  // ── Identity & ordering ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
  id: string;              // stable, globally unique (ULID — sorts by time)
  sessionId: string;       // Mandu scope id (launcher MANDU_SCOPE_ID)
  turn: number;            // T-LLM request index within the session
  ts: string;              // ISO 8601 wall clock (coerceEvent normalizes epoch-ms)
  seq: number;             // monotonic per-session counter (tiebreak, §3.2)
  callId: string | null;   // tool_use id; correlates tool_use → fs/net/exec → tool_result
  parentId: string | null; // causal parent (e.g. a fs_action's originating tool_use)

  // ── Classification ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  kind: EventKind;
  view: View;              // AgentView | HumanView | Quarantine (§2.1, the lane)
  boundary: Boundary;      // "model_context" | "network" | "filesystem" | "shell"
  emitter: Emitter;        // which component emitted it (§3)
  claimed?: true;          // set by the ARBITER: arrived where the agent's programs
                           //   reach, so every field is the sender's word; shown as
                           //   such, read by no decision (arbiter-human-plane.md §10.2)

  // ── Payload, in both representations ─────────────────────────────────────
  input: DualRepr | null;  // request/argv/path/body the action consumed
  output: DualRepr | null; // response/stdout/file content the action produced

  // ── Policy decision attached to this event ───────────────────────────────
  policy?: {
    trust?: "TRUSTED" | "UNTRUSTED";        // classify (data trust policy)
    category?: string | null;               // URL/CHANNEL/DIR rule that fired
    reason?: string;
    usage?: "allow" | "deny" | "needs_approval"; // desymbolizationDecision
    shell?: "AgentShell" | "HumanShell";     // exec view selection
    ruleRef?: { source: "rule" | "verdict" | "fail-closed"; id: string };
    approvalId?: string;                     // the queue row a deny created
    confidentiality?: string;                // the level half of the label
  };

  // ── The invariant flag (the whole point) ─────────────────────────────────
  invariant: {
    /** True iff this event would put UN-symbolized UNTRUSTED data into
     *  T-LLM's context. MUST be false in a healthy session; the §9 oracle
     *  asserts ∀ events: !violatedInvariant. The UI flares red on true. */
    violatedInvariant: boolean;
    detail?: string;        // what leaked + where (for the drill-down)
  };

  model?: { id: string; inputTokens?: number; outputTokens?: number };
  // …plus optional per-kind fields (fullInput §4.3.3, callShape §4.2c,
  //   rewrite, launch posture, assertion checks, seed/final trees).
}

type Emitter =
  | "anthropic-proxy" | "openai-proxy"     // model context (Claude Code / Codex)
  | "arbiter" | "inspect-mcp"              // policy + symbols; the U-LLM path
  | "fs-supervisor" | "net-supervisor" | "exec-supervisor"
  | "reply-filter" | "fs-sync"             // user-reply egress; FS symbol births
  | "dashboard" | "launcher" | "test-harness";
```

### 2.5 Modeling notes

- **View vs boundary are orthogonal.** `view` answers "AgentView or
  HumanView?"; `boundary` answers "which of the four chokepoints?" (mandu.md
  §2). A file *read* is `boundary=filesystem, view=AgentView`; the same file as
  a human sees it is `boundary=filesystem, view=HumanView`.
- **T-LLM vs U-LLM is `kind` + `view`.** `tllm_call` always runs under
  AgentView; `ullm_call` always under Quarantine. The renderer keys color and
  lane off both so the two model families are never confusable (§4.4).
- **Symbolized vs original lives in `DualRepr`, not in two event copies.** The
  reference dashboard reconstructed "Before/After" from separate audit fields;
  we keep that rendering idea (§5) but feed it from one typed field.
- **The invariant flag is computed at emit time by the proxy oracle**, not by
  the UI — the dashboard only renders it, so the UI can never mask a violation.

---

## 3. Instrumentation map — where each event comes from

Every `EventKind` maps to the chokepoint that observes it (mandu.md §3/§4).
The dashboard does not scrape logs; emitters **append canonical `ManduEvent`
records to the arbiter's event log** over the existing IPC.

**Tolerant consumption (`coerceEvent`).** Emitters must produce canonical
records, but the read path defends against drift: `event-model.ts coerceEvent`
normalizes an epoch-ms `ts` to ISO 8601 and supplies a non-violated
`invariant` when an OS-interceptor trace omits it (a `net_action`/`fs_action`/
`exec_action` is observability, not a model-context ingress), so one
non-conforming emitter cannot silently blank a whole session. The strict
`isManduEvent` predicate stays for producers and tests.

| EventKind | Emitter | Boundary | What it captures |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tllm_call` | anthropic-proxy / openai-proxy | model_context | The privileged request/response. `input` = the request as a `▸ role` transcript (§4.3.1, symbolized); `output` = the T-LLM response (tool_use + text). |
| `tool_use` | model proxies | model_context | A tool-call decision parsed from the T-LLM response (= adfi-openclaw's `before_tool_call` read side). Carries `callId`. |
| `tool_result` | model proxies | model_context | A tool result re-entering context — the **ingress into T-LLM** (= `transform_tool_result`). `input.symbolized` is what T-LLM will read. |
| `ullm_call` | inspect-mcp | model_context | Quarantined call (`inspect_symbol`). `input` symbolized (instruction + symbol); `output` re-symbolized before return. |
| `classify` | arbiter (policy engine) | any | Data trust policy decision (`ClassifyRequest`→`ClassifyResult`). |
| `symbolize` | model proxies; fs-sync (births, `callId` null) | any | Allocation of a `$MDU:*` for an untrusted or secret span; carries the `SymbolRef`. |
| `desymbolize` | arbiter; reply-filter | network / shell | Resolution of symbols to originals on egress; the reply-filter's frames name the symbols resolved for the human's terminal. |
| `path_rewrite` | model proxies (ViewMap) | model_context | One HumanView↔AgentView path-spelling translation on the model wire. `forward` = response `tool_use` args (the model asked for the HumanView path; the agent executes the AgentView twin); `reverse` = `tool_result` content / echoed args restored to HumanView for T-LLM. Observability only, emitted per changed typed field or per applied root pair for free text. |
| `fs_action` | model proxies (tool-call gate); fs-supervisor | filesystem | A file access routed to AgentFS vs HumanFS or denied; `view` set accordingly. |
| `net_action` | net-proxy (emitter `net-supervisor`) | network | Non-model HTTP: forwarded / tunneled / blocked, with the symbols withheld. |
| `exec_action` | model proxies (tool-call gate); exec-supervisor | shell | A command routed to AgentShell vs HumanShell or denied; `policy.shell` set; argv in both reprs. |

The remaining kinds (admin audit, session health, prompt filter, test harness)
are listed in §2.4 with the sections that consume them.

### 3.1 Transport — extend the arbiter IPC, do not fork it

The arbiter is already the hub: a Unix-socket NDJSON server
(`arbiter/ipc/protocol.ts`, `server.ts`) every interceptor talks to. The
dashboard's feed extends it with ops on the same socket and framing:

1. **`emit`** (interceptor → arbiter): append one `ManduEvent` to the
   session's append-only log, `${MANDU_HOME:-~/.mandu}/events/<sessionId>.ndjson`
   (on-disk-layout.md §3, runtime-instances.md §12), plus the in-memory ring the
   dashboard tails. Interceptors already hold an arbiter connection — one more
   op, no new socket.
2. **`sessions` / `events`** (dashboard → arbiter): the session summaries and a
   paged read of one session's log (`{ sessionId, sinceSeq? }` →
   `ManduEvent[]`), backing `GET /api/sessions` and
   `GET /api/events?session=<id>`.
3. **Live feed = Server-Sent Events** at `GET /api/stream?session=<id>`: the
   server subscribes to the arbiter's append notifications (`subscribe`) and
   relays new events as `text/event-stream`. SSE, not WebSocket, because the
   feed is one-directional, rides plain HTTP through the same server, and needs
   no dependency; it replaced the reference dashboard's `setInterval` polling.
   Writes (approvals, control) go over normal REST.
4. **`policySnapshot`** (dashboard → arbiter): the active inbound/outbound/origin
   rule table (`PolicyRuleSnapshot`) for the per-tool-call policy modal (§4.9),
   backing `GET /api/policy`. OBSERVABILITY ONLY — it mirrors the specs the gate
   enforces and decides nothing.
5. **`desymbolize`** (dashboard → arbiter): the deep/fixpoint resolver that
   serves fs-sync's HumanView writes and the reply-filter, also consumed by
   `EventSource.desymbolize()` for the delivered-reply reveal (§4.2c) and the
   paired rows' originals (§4.2f). Fail-soft: without an arbiter-backed source
   the reveal degrades to the event-carried one-level values.
6. **`deleteSession`** (dashboard → arbiter): remove one session's event log,
   backing `DELETE /api/session` and the sidebar's 🗑 (§4.10). The arbiter
   unlinks the file, drops the session's seq/coalescer state and ends its
   `subscribe` streams; the symbol table, policy and approval queue are
   untouched. Any session is deletable behind the mutating-route gates and a
   client confirm; the store rejects traversal-shaped ids.

### 3.2 Ordering

`ts` (wall clock) is the primary sort key; `seq` (monotonic per session,
assigned by the arbiter at append) breaks ties so causally-ordered events that
share a millisecond render deterministically. This replaces the reference
dashboard's hand-tuned `kindOrder` within a 50 ms window. `parentId` + `callId`
give the causal DAG for correlation (§4).

### 3.3 Scale — incremental session summaries

Listing sessions must stay cheap on a large event dir (hundreds of files and
MB) and with one very large session (a 4-hour interactive session reached
16.7 MB of `tllm_call` context). Naively every sidebar poll re-parsed every
file and re-fetched every session's events, blowing the 5 s per-op IPC deadline
so the rail rendered empty. Cost is now proportional to change, not size,
without pagination or pruning (the later client-side work — listing caches,
one copy on the wire, a polite poll — is §4.30):

- **Arbiter (`events/event-store.ts` `summaryCache`).** Per file, the summary
  (count / firstTs / lastTs), the identity `(ino, size, mtimeMs)` and the byte
  offset past the last consumed newline. Same identity → cached; same inode
  grown → parse only the appended suffix; anything else → re-parse that file.
  A torn tail line waits for its newline; deleted files evict.
- **Dashboard (`event-source/arbiter-source.ts` `refCache`).** The derived
  `SessionRef` (label / violated / agent / verdicts / batch) memoized at the
  summary's `(count, lastTs)`: an unchanged key is the same event list, so only
  changed sessions re-fetch events (typically 0–2 per poll). `FileEventSource`
  carries the same memo keyed by `(ino, size, mtimeMs)`.
- **Cold start.** The first `sessions` op after an arbiter restart pays one
  full scan, so `listSessions` gives it a 30 s deadline
  (`COLD_SESSIONS_SCAN_TIMEOUT_MS`); warm polls answer in milliseconds. A
  timed-out first poll self-heals: the arbiter finishes populating its cache
  and the next poll is warm.
- **Linear NDJSON framing.** The common idiom `buf += chunk; while ((nl =
  buf.indexOf("\n")) >= 0)` rescans the whole buffer per chunk — quadratic for
  one long line (a 16 MB `events` reply). `arbiter/ipc/ndjson-lines.ts`
  (`NdjsonLineSplitter`, scans only the new chunk) frames the `ArbiterClient`
  socket and its subscribe stream; its twin
  `dashboard/src/event-source/ndjson-lines.ts` frames `ArbiterEventSource`
  (the dashboard does not import the arbiter package;
  `arbiter/test/unit/ndjson-lines.test.ts` pins the copies identical). A 16.7 MB
  reply lands in under a second end to end.
- **One session's failure is not the rail's failure.** A per-session
  `readEvents` rejection still lists the session — from its last derived ref,
  else from the summary alone — and the next poll retries.

**Contract this leans on.** Event logs are append-only, written by the single
arbiter (or an O_APPEND co-writer at line granularity). An out-of-contract
in-place rewrite that keeps the inode AND never shrinks is the one shape the
identity check cannot tell from growth; every other mutation is detected and
resynced. Retention is separate: an age-based sweep in the arbiter (default 90
days, `MANDU_EVENT_RETENTION_DAYS`, runtime-instances.md §12) keeps the dir
bounded; the cache keeps it fast (age-based pruning alone would not help — the
heavy traffic is recent).

**Open.** A growing session re-replays its full event list on every poll where
its `(count, lastTs)` changed (~0.8 s per poll at 16 MB). The derivations are
folds, so an incremental `sinceSeq` fold per session would make that
proportional to the appended events; deferred until a session outgrows the
linear cost in practice.

Tests: `arbiter/test/unit/event-store-cache.test.ts` (suffix merge, torn tails,
UTF-8 offsets, replacement, truncation, delete); `arbiter/test/unit/ipc.test.ts`
(a 16 MB reply inside the default deadline);
`dashboard/test/component/arbiter-source-sessions.test.ts` §5 (only changed
sessions re-fetch) and §6 (the 16 MB shape through `listSessions`, and a wedged
session); `dashboard/test/unit/event-source/file-source-cache.test.ts`. The
size tests bound CPU time, not wall time (the regression is work; a loaded CI
guest's wait is not a framing bug): 12× a calibrated linear pass, where the
linear listing costs ~2.4× and the quadratic idiom ~20–27×.

### 3.3a A foreign arbiter at `current` is displaced, not adopted

On restart the dashboard adopts an arbiter already listening at the account's
`current` rendezvous. One started under a different `HOME` (a test launch with
a scratch `HOME` that autostarted a stack) has a different symbol DB, policy
and event dir, and adopting it shows the wrong sessions. So the adopt step
compares the listener's `hello` `eventDir` with its own
(`supervisor.ts foreignArbiterReason`); on a mismatch in instance mode it
starts its own instance, which takes `current` over by promotion, and waits
until `current` answers with a different pid. The foreign arbiter keeps running
for whoever joined it. A pinned socket cannot be displaced: it is adopted with
a `FOREIGN — its event dir is …` warning. Upstream, the launcher's autostart
uses the account's real `HOME` and the arbiter refuses promotion from a foreign
`HOME` (runtime-instances.md §13). Tests:
`dashboard/test/unit/supervisor/supervisor-adopt.test.ts`.

## 4. UI / panels & layout

Vanilla TS server + vanilla-JS client, matching the reference dashboard (§5).
This section describes the **inspector** at `/dev/` (the page itself is
titled **Developer view**, §4.32; this doc keeps the older name); the product
page at `/` is §4.25. The inspector is six pages under one nav (§4.32); on the
three session pages one session is shown at a time, its trace in a tab beside
the other views of it (§4.33). Color is load-bearing (§4.1 "Theme").

### 4.1 Top-level layout

```
┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Mandu · Developer view  Sessions Drills Tests | Approvals(2) Rules Settings   │
│ [⛔ VIOLATION only]  ● Protection: Secrets · live  Product ↗                  │  ← one row on a desktop, drawn as two (§4.32, §4.6)
├──────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ SESSIONS     │ Read the config and summarise it           ← #session-title    │
│ + New run    │ Claude Code · secrets · 42 events · 4 turns · Copy id          │
│ [search    ] │ Open in product ↗  🛡 Protected · 3 masked  ← #protection-chip │
│ ▾ Today      │ Protected. 3 secret values masked · 1 approval asked           │
│  Read the c… │ [ Trace 18 steps | Secrets 3 | Files none | Checks — ]         │
│  3 masked …  │ ┌ step rail ──┐ ┌ what the AI saw ─────┬ what really happened ┐ │
│ ▾ Yesterday  │ │ You         │ │ 👤 User input (one wide card)               │ │
│  …           │ │ Read masked │ │ 🔒 Read $MDU:Read[9c] │ original bytes      │ │
│ ▸ System logs│ │ AI replied  │ │ 💬 Reply …            │ 🤖 delivered        │ │
│              │ └─────────────┘ └───────────────────────┴─────────────────────┘ │
└──────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

On the three session pages (Sessions, Drills, Tests) two columns: the
**session list** (§4.3.2, §4.33; its head holds the page's own tools) and the
**main pane**, which opens on the **session header** (title, facts, the
§4.16 chip, the summary) and a tab strip, **Trace · Secrets · Files ·
Checks** (§4.33; a drill session has its own strip, §4.35). The Trace tab
holds the **step rail** (clicking a step selects its card and scrolls it into
view) and the trace, §4.2; Secrets holds the **symbol table** (§4.5) and the
**lineage panel** (§4.15); Files the **Git/Files panel** (§4.12); Checks the
test setup and assertion banners (§4.11, §4.13). Approvals, Rules and
Settings use the main column alone (`body[data-layout="full"]`).

**Layout model.** The top bar and the session list are `position: fixed` and
scroll their own lists; the main pane flows in the document, so the **page
scroll is the main scroll**, which no nested element or re-render can swallow
(an inner `overflow:auto` pane proved fragile). app.js sets `--col-l` (the
list's width: 260px by default, resizable from 180px to 600px but never past
the window less 500px for the main pane, a 30px rail when folded;
`applySizing`, §4.33 *The list leaves the trace room*) and the *measured* `--topbar-h`
(`trackTopbarHeight`). Drags end on
`pointerup`/`pointercancel`/`lostpointercapture`. The top bar is one row on a
desktop and two on a phone (§4.32).

**Theme (§4.25k).** The inspector wears the product page's visual system
(`public/mandu.css` loads before dashboard.css; light by default, dark
following the system) with a fixed color language on the shared tokens: `--ok`
green = trusted/AgentView, `--bad` red = untrusted/HumanView, `--accent` blue =
delivered reply and links, `--sym` gold = symbols. Red and green in a drill's
checks mean FAIL and PASS only: a check's `security` kind label wears
`--purple`, `utility` and `fidelity` the neutral chip. Settings → Appearance (§4.8)
picks System / Light / Dark (`wireTheme`, pinning `data-theme` on `<html>`).

**Mobile (≤760px).** The session list hides, `#main` takes the full width, and
a ☰ button (`wireNavToggle`) slides the list over as an overlay (from the
keyboard: §4.32 *The phone's session list works from the keyboard*); the step rail
becomes a "Jump to step" `<select>` (§4.33); the Files tab's commit list
sits above a commit's changes (§4.12). Stacked
trace cards lose the side-by-side position cue, so each announces its side
with a chip (`● AgentView · symbolized` / `● HumanView · original` /
`HumanView · delivered`). A card carries exactly one colored vertical line —
its side's color, violation red overriding.

### 4.2 The trace — dual-lane mode (the Expert trace)

The trace is built in two stages. **`view-model/dual-lanes.ts toDualLanes`**
turns a session's events into ordered, deduplicated **steps** (the step model
in this section); **§4.2f paired rows** renders those steps one per row. The
earlier three-column rendering — the reference dashboard's DualView lane mode
(`renderBotDualLanes`, `dv-*` classes): an AgentView lane, a hatched "trust
wall" with translation bands, and a HumanView lane — is superseded by §4.2f;
the step model below is unchanged and is what §4.2f is built from.

**Sides.** *What the AI saw* = AgentView (Symbolized) · T-LLM: the user's
prompt, tool *calls*, the *symbolized* results it receives (`$MDU:*` tokens
render as clickable symbol chips), and its prose. **No raw untrusted byte ever
renders on this side.** *What really happened* = HumanView (Original): an
untrusted tool's execution on original data, the U-LLM (Quarantine) card for
`inspect_symbol`, uncorrelated OS actions, and the **delivery card** (the reply
the user actually receives, symbols resolved). Where data crosses, the step
carries **bands**: down (AgentView ➔ HumanView, symbols resolved for
execution/egress), up (HumanView ➔ AgentView, `symbol ← raw value`), and
**path rewrite** (each ViewMap application from `path_rewrite` events,
labeled with `Tool.field`). Every band item uses one convention: the
trusted/AgentView form on the left, the untrusted/HumanView form on the right,
only the arrow carrying direction.

An UNTRUSTED tool call reads as the reference's ①②③ story: ① call → ② executes
on original data → ③ symbolized result received. A TRUSTED call never crosses.
The step rail's row of a judged call carries its trust (§4.33); an unjudged
one, every call with the integrity axis off, says "trust not checked".

**A twin read does NOT cross.** Under the filesystem chokepoint (fs-sync) the
agent's CWD is the AgentView worktree, whose files were symbolized ON DISK
when the twin was seeded. An untrusted workspace read therefore gets a symbol
back with no raw-data crossing at read time. `toDualLanes` flags such steps
`readsTwin` — the call's own result is already a symbol, or a ViewMap
`path_rewrite` translated the path to its twin (Quarantine excluded) — and they
render as an AgentView card with the path band, never as a HumanView execution
(which would put a HumanView label on an agent-view path). The e2e oracle
enforces the same distinction (§4.13 `read-view-dir-consistency` /
`no-agentview-path-in-model`).

**Every rewrite names its technique.** A band carries a **technique chip**
derived from the contributing events' emitter (`symbolizedBy` /
`desymbolizedBy` / `quarantinedBy`; `app.js TECHNIQUES`): *model-context
rewrite · anthropic-proxy*, *U-LLM quarantine · inspect-mcp*, an OS chokepoint,
or *arbiter symbol table*. The delivery band is labeled the **dashboard's
privileged reveal** — the reply leaves the agent still symbolic. Symbol tokens
carry a provenance tooltip (full tool name — names embed a shortened tag, e.g.
`$MDU:inspect[ee19]` for `mcp__mandu-inspect__inspect_symbol` — plus field,
origin, derivation).

**Input cards.** Each newly appearing user message is an input card
(`toDualLanes` tracks the conversation's prompt list, `convoPrompts`); a call
whose user messages do not *extend* that list (a summarizer call, a
compaction-rewritten history) mints none. Cards and the sidebar label strip the
proxy's `[system-reminder]` placeholders and the inline slash-command record
(`stripHarnessTags`, `transcript.ts`), so each shows what the human typed.
Known gap: a prompt edited and resubmitted keeps its pre-edit spelling.

**Display order within a turn.** The proxy emits `tool_use` and its gate
events mid-stream but the `tllm_call` carrying the prose only at stream end.
`toDualLanes` floats each response ahead of the contiguous run of same-turn
tool/OS steps just before it, and each input ahead of the steps it caused
(display-only; the log is untouched), so a turn reads prompt → announcing
prose → tool cards → reply. Turn-0 `net_action` cards (the net side knows no
turns) and turn-0 reply-filter cards ("user reply · reply-filter": the
launcher's PTY relay knows no turns either, and flushes a repaint wherever it
lands) are transit the floats cross; other turn-0 OS cards (the U-LLM
quarantine card, the §4.2e birth card) are deliberate stops. A repaint used
to stop the float: it landed between a `curl`'s `tool_use` and the
`tllm_call` carrying the NEXT question, so the curl read as the previous
turn's on both front-ends (live tour 2026-10-05). render-lint's
*turn-order-coherent* (§4.2c) enforces the contract on the render.

**Deduplication.** The stateless Messages API re-sends the whole conversation
every turn, so the proxy re-emits `tool_result` / `symbolize` / `path_rewrite`
for the same `callId` on later calls. `toDualLanes` folds those into one step
(first emission wins, so the step records what the AI got at its own turn;
a `re-guarded ×N` badge; symbols deduped by value; a re-send masked where
the first delivery was not is noted as `maskedLater`, §4.25b), and
consecutive identical OS actions collapse to one `×N` card. The fold key
includes the recorded `usage`, `action` and violation flag, so an allowed
command followed by a denied one never folds together.

**Retired renderings.** The per-event card view (§4.3) and the tool-centric
view before it are gone; their server projections stay (`toTimeline` feeds
`groupToolCalls` → the ⚖ policy modal, §4.9; `toLaneModel` keeps turn rails and
causal links).

#### 4.2c Side calls and the delivered-reply reveal

*(Cited from the model proxies as "the side-call detection seam".)*

The delivery card — what the human actually received — is the final
conversation reply (`final`). Claude Code also makes model calls outside the
conversation: title generation, the **typeahead suggestion** (a trailing
`[SUGGESTION MODE: …]` instruction), the **startup quota probe** (a lone
`quota` message, or the proxy's `⚠ no model response` explainer when it
errors), the **away recap**, and the **WebFetch summarizer** (`Web page
content:`). Any of them landing last would steal `final`. `toDualLanes`
(`isSideCall`) excludes them **structurally** — each `tllm_call` carries
`callShape` (`TllmCallShape`: `toolCount`, `maxTokens`, `userMessages`); the
conversation loop always sends the tool battery and most side calls send none,
so `toolCount === 0` is a side call whatever a future release makes the prompt
say — and by **string heuristics** for older events and tool-carrying side
calls (typeahead). Every `tllm_call` is classified conversation / side /
unknown (`DualLanesModel.calls`). A side call mints no input or response card.
An explainer on a real errored turn still renders but never sets `final`
(nothing was delivered). Classification never gates rendering: a history
rewrite makes the real conversation non-extending, and its replies must keep
the delivery zone.

**The reveal is deep.** Events carry one level of symbol value, but a
delivered symbol is often a nested chain (a Read symbol whose value is the
twin's on-disk content, itself a token fs-sync minted earlier). The
`/api/events` route runs `revealDeliveredReply` (`view-model/delivery.ts`):
for each symbol the final reply references that is unresolved, it
fixpoint-substitutes the session's own band values (enough when the session's
arbiter is gone, e.g. a containerized e2e run), then asks the arbiter's deep
`desymbolize` via `EventSource.desymbolize()`, and ships the originals in the
step's band. Utility-only posture, like the reply-filter: any failure degrades
to the event-carried value; unknown tokens stay tokens; nothing is fabricated
or newly exposed. Only the DELIVERED reply is deepened — interim AI-side cards
keep their opaque tokens, which is the defense working.

**Reply-filter cards.** Each PTY repaint that resolved a symbol emits a
`desymbolize` event; the cards name the surface (`user reply · reply-filter`)
and the symbols resolved for the human's terminal, and identical frames fold to
one `×N` card. The event's `symbolized` form is the placeholders the frame
named, space-separated (`placeholderNames`, names only); its `original` is the
frame the human saw. Never the frame itself as `symbolized`: a terminal write
or a json-mode record can hold text the AI never saw (a tool's output as the
agent process got it, the human's prompt before the prompt filter), and the
signed-out projection keeps every `symbolized` (§6). Until 2026-10-06 the
filter recorded the whole frame there; the projection reduces such a frame to
its placeholders.

**The render self-check (`view-model/render-lint.ts`)** — invariants that need
no ground truth: *final-not-explainer* (ERROR: the delivered card is an
upstream-error explainer); *delivered-reply-resolved* (WARN: a final-card
symbol no reply-filter frame resolved — the frames are ground truth for the
human's terminal); *model-call-classified* (WARN: an UNKNOWN call with prose
output, the canary for the next new side call or history rewrite);
*turn-order-coherent* (ERROR: within a turn, prompt → prose → the tool cards it
issued).

It runs in three places: a unit sweep over `dashboard/fixtures/live/`
(recorded sessions that once rendered wrong, each a permanent fixture with
golden delivered-reply assertions, personal details neutralized;
`render-lint-sweep.test.ts`), a `fidelity` check block in the live claude-e2e
suite (error → blocking FAIL, warn → advisory), and on every session view
(`SessionViewModel.renderLint` → a badge on the verdict strip).

What "neutralized" means for a recorded fixture (2026-10-19, before the public
flip): the structure, symbols and counts stay as recorded; host names, paths,
user and project names and the fetched page's text (and every model reply that
describes it) are rewritten to fakes (`labs.example.test`, "Example Lab",
`/home/user/…`, a zero scratchpad session id), in every field, inside
JSON-encoded strings and inside reply-filter frames whose cursor moves split a
word. The agent's own system prompt and its WebFetch summarizer instructions
are replaced by an `[… omitted from this fixture]` line; the one line kept is
` - Primary working directory:` (`sessionCwd` reads it). Tools the agent
advertised that are not public (connector and unreleased tools) are dropped
from `tool_surface` and the counts follow. `recorded-fixtures-scrubbed.test.ts`
fails when a fixture under `dashboard/fixtures/`, `dashboard/test/fixtures/` or
`tests/fixtures/` carries any of the scrubbed markers once ANSI escapes are
stripped, so a re-recorded session cannot bring them back; it keeps its marker
list encoded, since a plain list would itself name what it hides.

Shapes that print-mode runs never produce get their own drivers: an
integration e2e drives the real anthropic-proxy with an injected 429 on a
probe-shaped request and asserts the explainer never takes `final`; and the
**interactive driver** (`interactive-driver.ts`) runs a real
interactive `claude` under the reply-filter PTY relay, emulating the human at
the PTY master so the typeahead call fires. The claude-e2e scenarios
`interactive-smoke`, `interactive-typeahead-ipi` (the §9 raw-injection check
over side-call bodies) and `interactive-reply-filter-live` assert that no side
call takes the delivery zone. Away-recap is idle-gated and left to the
model-call-classified canary.

#### 4.2d The simplified dataflow overview (⊙ overview) — RETIRED

A top-bar **⊙ overview / ⊞ detailed** toggle once switched the trace to a
compact spine of one-line trust-colored nodes with hover popovers. Retired with
the §4.18 register split: it was a compact *expert* view that still assumed
audiences 1–3. The detailed trace is the only rendering; the end user has the
product page (§4.25). Its lasting precedent: an alternate presentation derives
from the same tested view-model with zero server change. The `mandu.dvMode`
localStorage key is ignored.

#### 4.2e Thin-entry ⓘ drawers + the uncorrelated-symbolize birth card

**Derivation rule.** Every uncorrelated OS card and correlated gate line
carries a server-built `detail?: DetailSection[]`
(`src/view-model/dual-lanes-detail.ts`, the Policy panel's `detail.ts`
vocabulary), rendered as an ⓘ opening the shared drawer
(`dev/js/detail-drawer.js`, textContent-only). **ⓘ = this event's facts**;
**⚖ = the tool's rule/schema + per-call verdict** (§4.9). A card's drawer
is titled by its kind and title, the kind said once ("net_action · blocked
collector.example", §4.2f *The kind, said once*); a gate line's drawer is
titled by its recorded text.

Every drawer follows the policy-visibility §8.3 template (*What this is* /
*What it decided* / *Where it's specified*, from `policy.ruleRef` / *Where it
came from*) and register: lowercase `key: value` facts, **absence stated in
words**, values capped at 160 chars, **symbolized spellings only**, never an
`original`. Per kind:

- **net_action**: action / method / destination, plus one `withheld:` line per
  symbol (normalized from both wire shapes, `string[]` and `{symbol}[]`) — "its
  value never left the machine".
- **exec_action**: the gated input, the result (`BLOCKED → exit 77` /
  `ALLOW (AgentShell)`), the shell, the reason; a deny states the original
  command never ran.
- **fs_action**: operation / result / classification.
- **path_rewrite**, uncorrelated card only: direction, field, both spellings.
  (The correlated band gets no ⓘ — it already shows every field.)
- **reply-filter `desymbolize`**: the surface + one `resolved:` line per symbol.

A fold keeps the FIRST detail, matching the card keeping the first `ts`.

**The uncorrelated-symbolize birth card.** callId-null `symbolize` events (the
fs-sync births, workspace seed or eager sync) render each consecutive run as
ONE card, `symbolize · workspace sync`, with the §4.14 ⊕ mint badge per fresh
name and a drawer listing `name ← path` per birth ("a mint, not a gate
decision"). It gives fs-sync-born names a minting step for the §4.5 Born cell
(`mintStepFor`). Accepted nuance: a turn-0 batch card stops the §4.2 floats —
right for seeds — so a mid-turn eager-sync birth could pin an input above it.
Tests: `dashboard/test/unit/view-model/dual-lanes-detail.test.ts`.

#### 4.2f Paired rows — the trace, one step per row

**Status: shipped; supersedes the three-column rendering of §4.2.**
`toDualLanes` stays the dedupe/order source of truth; the rows are a pure
projection of it.

**Why.** Reviewed against 15 recorded sessions, the three-column lanes were
mostly noise: 65% of rows were OS cards repeating a fact a tool card showed or
recording background connections; one crossing tool call stacked up to 8
blocks; a masked **twin read** left the HumanView side empty; in `secrets`
mode the verdict claimed untrusted data reached T-LLM only as symbols over
results never classified; and a flagged step showed only its token.

**The rule.** Each row is one step. The left half is *what the AI saw*
(AgentView · T-LLM), the right half is *what really happened* (HumanView ·
original data), and the right half exists only when the two differ. A step
whose sides agree is ONE wide card ("same on both sides").

**Server: `view-model/paired-rows.ts` → `vm.paired`.** `toPairedTurns(dual,
symbols)` groups steps into turns (one per user prompt, plus a leading "Before
your first prompt" turn when anything preceded it) and classifies each step
into a row that references it by id:

| row | from | renders |
|---|---|---|
| `tool` | every tool step | `masked` (the AI received a token it did not only echo) splits the row; else one wide card |
| `reply` | the LAST AI message of a turn | split when its text carried tokens this page filled in (left: what the AI wrote, right: what the human saw); one card with a *not filled in* line when it filled in none |
| `note` | earlier AI messages of the turn | one muted line |
| `aside` | a context-compaction summary (`<analysis>…<summary>`) | folded; it rides a conversation-extending call, so the call class cannot catch it |
| `setup` | the fs-sync seed (birth batch) | "Workspace prepared: N files masked", names from the symbols' `field` |
| `action` | any other OS card | inline: blocks, denials, violations, uncorrelated fs actions |

A per-turn **Background** fold takes bookkeeping cards (allowed connections,
uncorrelated path mappings, reply-filter resolutions, allowed command checks,
a U-LLM record an `inspect_symbol` row already shows). A violated, denied or
blocked card NEVER folds.

**The moments data leaves this machine** (2026-10-05). A net send that
carried masked items NEVER folds either: the net-proxy records them on the
event, `resolved` on a forwarded request (their real value was filled in on
the way out) and `withheld` on a blocked one (mitm.ts / proxy.ts, both wire
shapes, `string[]` and `{symbol}[]`). `toDualLanes` carries them on the OS
step as `carried` (part of its fold key, so two sends of different items stay
two steps), and `backgroundOf` keeps such a step an inline `action` row. A
bound send of a secret used to sit in "Background: N connections" next to
the model API traffic, so the reader never saw the moment their token left.
The row says it in words beside the event name (app.js `sendWords`): "left
this machine: Mandu filled in the real value of `$MDU:…` for this request to
`api.github.com`, a destination allowed to receive it", "kept on this
machine: … carried `$MDU:…`, and Mandu blocked it, so it never left", or
"held" while it waits for an answer; the step rail labels it *Sent out*
(mark `sent`), *Blocked send* or *Send held* instead of the event name,
then the host the card names ("Blocked send `api.stripe.com`", since
2026-10-13: §4.33 *A send names where it went*). A
send that carried nothing (the model API, telemetry) folds as before.

**A check says what Mandu decided** (2026-10-05). A guard event correlated to
a tool call (the proxies' exec, net and fs gates; the exec-supervisor) is a
line on that tool's card, not a row of its own. The proxy's exec gate records
every allowed command too (`ALLOW (AgentShell)`), and the line used to be
drawn as the P3 denial line for all of them: red, dashed, `🛡 exec_action`. In
a Secrets-mode session, every Bash card seemed to carry a refusal. Now
`toDualLanes` copies two facts onto each `DualGate`: `kind`, and `usage`, the
event's own `policy.usage` or null. app.js `gateWords` says the decision in
words and colours the line by it:

| decision | line | look |
|---|---|---|
| `allow` | ✓ "Mandu checked this command and let it run." (request: "let it through"; file access: "allowed it") | green, solid |
| `deny` | ⛔ "Mandu blocked this command. It never ran." (request: "It never left this machine.") | red, dashed |
| `needs_approval` | ✋ "Mandu held this command for your answer." | amber, dashed |
| none recorded | 🛡 "Mandu checked this command. What it decided was not recorded." | grey |

Without `usage`, the block words in the recorded text (`blocked`, `denied`, …)
read as `deny`, the rule the product page's `actionOutcome` uses. Otherwise
the line says the decision is not known, and never guesses "allowed". The
exec-supervisor's AgentShell routing records no `usage`, so it reads as not
recorded. Its shell stays in the ⓘ drawer. The event kind becomes a small pill
on the line. Recorded text that says more than the kind (an fs gate's
`Read.file_path → /etc/shadow · DENIED → …`, a net gate's "blocked
evil.example") stays on the line, muted, without the kind again (*The kind,
said once*, below). The ⚖
rule chip and the ⓘ drawer are as before (§4.2e). The view-model's `text` is
unchanged, so the product page reads gates as it did. An older bundle without
`kind` or `usage` falls back to the text rule, and a pre-provenance string
gate still renders.

**A check joins its call in whichever order they were recorded**
(2026-10-07). The anthropic-proxy decides its exec, net and fs gates in
its tool-input transform, ahead of the sniffer that records the call
(`streamAndSniffSse` and its JSON and OpenAI-wire twins), so each gate is
recorded one event BEFORE its `tool_use`: every live
recording shows it (`fixtures/live/1783675777-1365724.ndjson`, seq 4 then
5). `toDualLanes` joined an `exec_action` or `net_action` to its call only
once it had seen the call, so in a real Claude Code session no Bash card
ever carried its check. An allowed command's check folded into Background
as a command check "with no tool call" (§4.25b), the trace's path read
"Mandu checked — no check recorded" over "Background: 1 command check",
and a blocked command was two cards, an unblocked-looking Bash card and a
block beside it. The fixtures recorded each gate after its call, so no test
saw it. Now a gate with a call id joins that call's card whenever the
session recorded a `tool_use` for the id (`recordedCalls`), before or after
it; the card starts at the gate's time. A gate whose call was never
recorded, and the openai-proxy's (recorded with `callId: ""`, so Codex's
checks cannot be joined), stay cards of their own as before. Three rules
keep the join safe now that a card can open on a check and carry several
(a net gate, then the exec gate; an exec gate, then a stdin or MCP-command
gate):

- the call's own `tool_use` names the card, whatever event opened it (a
  gate's name is its first symbol's tool, so the blocked `rm -rf` of a
  placeholder read "Used `nomodel_Env`");
- the call's decision is the severer of its checks' (deny, then a hold,
  then allow; `severerUsage`), never the first recorded, so an allowed
  check followed by a block reads blocked;
- an exec or net line is deduplicated by its title AND its decision (the
  title is only the kind, `exec_action`), as `pushOs` folds OS cards, so
  an allow and a block on one call are two lines.

The product page draws no line for an allowed check, so its turn's
background line no longer counts the agent's own commands; a block or hold
is the call's own step. The listing cache's schema is 5 (§4.30). Tests:
`dual-lanes-gate-order.test.ts` (each order, allow / block / hold, a net
gate, several checks on one call, an unrecorded call, the empty call id,
the live recording), the walkthrough fixture records each gate before its
call as the proxy does (`app-js-dual-lanes`, `session-walkthrough`), and
`tests/stack/dashboard-proxy-check-on-card.test.ts` (the real proxy, an
allowed and a blocked Bash call, the inspector's and the product's routes).

**A check says why** (2026-10-05). Since §4.25b's *A block says why*, the
session page said of the tour's 10:38 blocked send "**Why:** No rule lets this
secret go to `api.stripe.com`. Mandu sends a secret only where a rule lets it
go, or with your OK." The trace drew the same moment with only its raw rule
chip, `⚖ egress:secret-unbound`, so a reader saw a block and, one turn later,
a send of the same key to the same host, with nothing but a rule id to tell
them apart. Now `toDualLanes` stamps the session page's words
(`view-model/block-why.ts`) as `why` on a check that blocked or held the call
(`DualGate.why`) and on an OS step that did (`DualOsStep.why`):

- **Which decision.** `checkOutcome` reads the check as its line is drawn:
  the recorded `usage` (`needs_approval` a hold, `deny` a block, `allow`
  nothing), else the block words in the recorded text (a gate's text, an OS
  step's `action`), as `gateWords` does. A why never sits under a check
  that let the call through. A flagged step and a sandboxed reader's record
  get none, as on the session page.
- **The same words.** An OS send passes its recorded host (`:443` left out)
  and how many items it carried, as the session page's `osSentence` does; a
  check on a tool card passes neither (its recorded text names the host), as
  its `decidingGate` does. `osSubject` and `netHost` moved into `dual-lanes.ts` so
  both views split a step's title the same way. An unknown or integrity-only
  id, an allowing rule or no rule gives no line, as there. A net check also
  keeps the destination it recorded, `DualGate.target` (2026-10-07: the
  net-proxy's `destination`, else the host in the model proxy's `WebFetch
  → <host>`; null when it named none). The session page's step for a fetch
  the proxy rewrote to its reserved host names that host and passes it to
  the why, since its own input no longer holds it (§4.25b, *A call Mandu
  rewrote reads as what it stopped*); the inspector's line is unchanged.
- **Where.** app.js `whyHtml` draws "**Why:** …" in ink, the host as code: on
  a send row right under its *Kept on this machine* or *Held* line (above the
  how-it-was-gated note), on a tool card as the check's own last line. The ⚖
  chip stays and still opens the rule under Rules (§9.5 of
  policy-surface.md); the word key's *Guard event* entry says a block or a
  hold also says why.
- **Never a value.** The line reads only the rule id, the recorded host and
  the carried count; a signed-out viewer gets the same line.

Tests: `block-why.test.ts` (`checkOutcome`), `dual-lanes.test.ts`,
`ui/app-js-osdetail.test.ts`, `test/component/inspector-record.test.ts` (the
tour record: the 10:38 row's why is the session page's `/api/home/agent` why
for the same step, word for word; nothing let through says one) and
`tests/stack/block-why.test.ts` (the real net-proxy's block, through a real
arbiter, carries the same why in the real dashboard's `/api/events`).

**A check says it asked** (2026-10-06). The tour's header read "1 step
blocked · no approvals asked", though the 10:38 block had put a row on
Approvals (`egr-1`) and the person's next prompt says they allowed it there.
The ask counted only a hold (`usage: needs_approval`), and a block that
queues a row is a deny. Now:

- **The id on the step.** `toDualLanes` keeps the event's
  `policy.approvalId` as `askId` on a check (`DualGate.askId`) or an OS step
  (`DualOsStep.askId`) that blocked or held the call, by the decision its
  line draws (`checkOutcome`, as the why). One that let the call through, a
  flagged step and a sandboxed reader's record keep none, nor does an id
  not of the queue's shape.
- **The line.** app.js `askedHtml` draws "Mandu asked for your OK in
  Approvals (`egr-1`)." under the why: the session page's words (§4.25b, *A
  stop says Mandu asked you*), with the row's id as inert code.
- **The count.** A step asked when it was held (`stepAsked`) or filed a row
  (`stepFiledAsk`: an OS step's `askId`, any of a tool step's gates', or a
  tool step's program read held until nobody answered, `readRefused.held`,
  §4.25b *A refused read is a block, not a mask*). The
  header, the step rail's `asked` mark and the list's `asks` chip
  (session-counts.ts mirrors app.js, §4.33) count both, so the tour reads
  "1 step blocked · 1 approval asked", its rail "Blocked send
  api.stripe.com · asked · blocked", its row "2 masked · 1 read before marked · 1 ask · 1 blocked"
  (§4.33). A blocked step that
  asked counts in both. The rail's label still reads "Send held" only for
  a hold.
- **The Secrets tab.** *Where each went* and the symbol card say the same
  under the block, by the same rule (§4.15, *A block says Mandu asked*).

### 4.3 Call detail — the flat pipeline view's per-event panes (RETIRED)

The retired pipeline view showed each event as a card with its input and
output in both representations side by side (symbolized | original, collapsed
when identical) and an invariant footer quoting any leaked span. In the trace
the side IS the representation, so these panes are gone. Still live from this
section: the `▸ role` transcript and `annotateTranscript` (§4.3.1), which feed
`toDualLanes`' input/response steps and the sidebar labels; the session list
(§4.3.2); and the `fullInput` event contract (§4.3.3).

#### 4.3.1 Structured input — a conversation, not a JSON blob

A `tllm_call` / `ullm_call` input is a whole conversation, so the model-API
proxy emits a **`▸ role` transcript**, not `JSON.stringify(request)`: the
system prompt plus each message as a `▸ <role>` block, a `tool_use` as
`→ name(args)`, a `tool_result` as a labeled block, symbols intact
(anthropic-proxy `summarizeRequest`; the Mandu handling block collapses to a
placeholder). The dashboard parses it (`src/transcript.ts` `parseTranscript`,
mirrored to `dev/js/transcript.js`). The raw forwarded bytes are checked for
un-symbolized leaks by the §9 oracle separately (`forwardedText`), so this is a
display contract only.

The agent's own system prompt (tens of KB for Claude Code) comes first, so two
things keep the human's prompt findable: the proxy caps the `▸ system` block on
its own (`SYSTEM_SUMMARY_CAP`, well under `PROMPT_SUMMARY_CAP`) and fits the
rest by eliding the **longest blocks first** (`fitBlocks` — every `▸` block
keeps its head, so a long first message cannot cut later turns, such as the
typeahead's trailing `[SUGGESTION MODE: …]` that §4.2c's classifier needs);
and `annotateTranscript` collapses `▸ system` and flags the first `▸ user` as
primary. The same summary feeds the sidebar label (`deriveSessionLabel` →
`firstUserPrompt`).

#### 4.3.2 Session list — labeled by what it does; resizable panes

The sidebar labels each session by its **first user prompt** (`SessionRef.label`,
derived server-side by `deriveSessionLabel` → `firstUserPrompt`, tolerant of the
transcript / raw-JSON / legacy shapes). A row reads that name on line 1 and
its badges, start and duration and state chips (`flagged`, the "N masked · N
asks · N blocked" counts, `secrets gated`, `N commands could not run`) on
line 2, the chips moving whole to a line of their own when they do not fit; the
opaque `<ts>-<pid>` scope id and the event count ride the tooltip (§4.33). The list is 260px by
default, resizable, its width persisted in `localStorage` (`mandu.layout`;
§4.1); on Sessions it is grouped by day, with a search box (§4.33).

**Test rows lead with the scenario chip.** An e2e session's name line reads
`🧪 E13` `trusted-and-untrusted`: `app.js scenarioBadge` renders the registry
badge `SessionRef.testNumber` (`Re<n>` / `E<n>` / `C<n>` / `OCl<n>` /
`OCo<n>`, §4.10), then the scenario from the id (`testNameFromId`). The chip
leads the one line that always renders, so overflow trims the scenario, never
the chip (`app-js-sidebar.test.ts`; `css-inspector-contract.test.ts` contract
4: no rule hides a strip badge).

**Per-session deep links.** The selected session is reflected into the address
bar as `/dev/<page>/<scopeId>` on the three session pages (`/dev/sessions/`,
`/dev/drills/`, `/dev/tests/`; `app.js reflectSessionInUrl`, via
`history.replaceState`), elsewhere as `?session=<scopeId>` (§4.32), and a
fresh load honors it
(`initialSessionId`), falling back to the first session. The older
`?session=<id>` form is 302'd to the path (§4.25v).

#### 4.3.3 Full model-call input — complete, source-tagged, on demand

The transcript (§4.3.1) is capped and redacts the Mandu-injected handling block
to `[Mandu IPI handling prompt]`. So a reviewer can read the *complete* prompt
the model received — and see exactly what Mandu injected — the model-call
emitters also set an optional `ManduEvent.fullInput`:

```ts
fullInput?: {
  blocks: Array<{
    role: "system" | "user" | "assistant" | "tool_result";
    source: "mandu" | "agent" | "conversation"; // mandu = the injected prompt
    text: string;        // full SYMBOLIZED text — no cap
    label?: string;      // e.g. "tool_result tu1"
  }>;
};
```

`text` is the **symbolized** form the model received, so it adds **no raw-leak
surface**. T-LLM (`anthropic-proxy buildFullInput`): the system block carrying
the `HANDLING_MARKER` → `"mandu"`, other system blocks → `"agent"`, messages
role-tagged. U-LLM (`inspect-mcp`): the quarantine prompt → `"mandu"`, the
inspected data → `"conversation"` (instruction + symbol, never the raw value).

**Rendering.** The user-input card's **`⤢ full prompt`** button
(`showFullPromptModal`) maps the step id back to its `tllm_call` and lists the
`fullInput` blocks keyed by origin: **`👤 User (original prompt)`** (loudest),
**`⚙ injected by Mandu`** (amber, sentinel line stripped), `agent system
prompt` (neutral), other turns dimmed. Symbols stay opaque tokens with
privileged click-to-reveal; all text is escaped; no `fullInput`, no button.
The button is named by its turn, the heading above it ("full prompt: Turn 2",
§4.33 *A prompt, a reply and a note say their words*, 2026-10-13).
Tests: the full-prompt cases in `dashboard/test/unit/ui/app-js-dual-lanes.test.ts`
and `app-js-turn-words.test.ts`.

### 4.4 T-LLM vs U-LLM distinction

`tllm_call` cards live on the AgentView side; `ullm_call` cards render as
Quarantine cards tagged `U-LLM · quarantined`, attached to the spawning
`inspect_symbol` tool step — mirroring the reference dashboard's
`renderInlineUllm`. Each model call shows its prompt and response, model id and
token usage (`model`), so *all* model calls of *both* families are shown with
input and output.

**Orphan `ullm_call` correlation.** MCP gives inspect-mcp no way to learn the
`tool_use` id that invoked it (a `tools/call` carries only name and arguments),
so its `ullm_call` events arrive with `callId: null, turn: 0`. Before all
projections, `toSessionViewModel` runs a display-only pre-pass
(`view-model/correlate.ts correlateUllmCalls`): an orphan `ullm_call` adopts
the `callId` (and turn) of the nearest **preceding**
`mcp__mandu-inspect__inspect_symbol` `tool_use` whose args contain the inspected
symbol, each tool_use claimed at most once; uncorrelatable events keep an
orphan card. The heuristic is off the security path — a wrong guess mis-groups
a card, never alters a decision or leaks data.

### 4.5 Symbol table — symbol → what it stands for → where it flowed

An inline panel, **Masked values** in the session's Secrets tab (§4.33) — the
session's **current symbol table**, live over SSE — listing every `SymbolRef` seen in the session, sorted by birth; its heading
carries the distinct-symbol count. (It absorbed the former "symbol inspector";
the §4.14 modal remains only as the table-as-of-a-step view.) Per symbol:

- **name** (`$MDU:read[9c].iban`) and **tool / origin / field** (provenance);
- **resolved value** (privileged reveal, click to show);
- **born** — turn + birth time; the `⊕ t<n> · <time>` cell opens the §4.14
  modal anchored at that birth;
- **flow trace**: every event whose `DualRepr.symbols` references it — "created
  at `tool_result` t0 → read by `tllm_call` t1 → desymbolized at `net_action`
  t2". The name and Flow cells open the §4.17 symbol card (whose lineage section
  is the §4.15 evidence graph). Lineage design: `symbol-lineage.md`.

After those rows come the masked values the lineage holds that no event
carries as a typed symbol: a key masked when the session started, which only
a program's send or the AI's own writing named (§4.33 *A masked value with no
masking step in the session*). Each reads "—" for tool/field and value, Born
"not recorded", and Flow the events it was seen in ("· net_action t0").

*A name breaks only between its parts (2026-10-19).* The table and its ⊕
as-of-a-step modal (§4.14) used to break every cell anywhere, so the narrow
columns cut names at a letter while Flow had room to spare: on the recorded
sessions at 1280 px, "WebFetc" over "h" (a 67 px column), "inspect_symbol.re"
over "sult", "$MDU:WebFetch[8962" over "]" and "https://labs" /
".example.te" / "st"; at 1024 px also "(case-insensitive)" in a value and 14
names in one session's scratchpad paths. Now a `$MDU:` token up to 40
characters (every recorded one: the longest is 33) stays on one line and its
column grows to fit it; a longer one, a deep encoded field path, is cut after
its `]` and each `.`, so a 150-character name still wraps inside the panel.
app.js `namePartsHtml` cuts a
tool/field after each `.` and `__` ("inspect_symbol." over "result"), and an
origin or value word longer than 24 characters after each `/` (a path, a
URL), else each `.` (a bare host), each part a `.name-part` the stylesheet
keeps on one line; a part still longer than 24 is cut after its `-` and `_`
("-home-user-" over "project-mandu/") and then, a key or a hash with no word
in it, every 24 characters, so one key never pushes the table sideways. A
folded root (`.path-fold`) is never cut. The text, every link, button,
title and the reveal's value are unchanged. Measured in headless Chromium
over the three recorded live sessions, signed in: the words whose letters
sat on two lines went from 14, 7 and 2 to none at 1280 px, and from 16, 11
and 4 to none at 1024 px. The cost: at 1024 px, the two sessions with 25-character tokens and long paths
no longer fit the panel (784 and 776 px in 675 px) and their table scrolls
sideways in its own box (§4.34). In *Where each went* (§4.15), the
masked-as line wraps: a "+1 derived" or "birth unrecorded" chip that does
not fit beside the token moves under it whole, and only the token
ellipsizes (it read "+1 deri…": at 1280 px it ended at x=776 in a column
clipping at 764, at 1024 px every derived chip was cut).

### 4.6 Invariant / oracle status indicator

A top-bar **banner** for the §9 oracle verdict. Holding is the quiet default:
the banner is hidden while the invariant holds and appears only as the red
`INVARIANT VIOLATION` alarm, with a count and a jump to the offending event.
Computed purely from `∀ events: !violatedInvariant` — the property the e2e
oracle asserts (§7). The view-model still computes the holding label; the
per-session verdict strip on the trace (§4.2f banner) restates it.

### 4.7 Egress approval queue (data usage policy) — RETIRED

The first design had a read-only panel of `egress_request` /
`egress_decision` events. Those kinds never got a production emitter: approval
shipped as the arbiter's approval queue, with live Approve/Deny in the Policy
panel (`dev/js/egress.js` over `/api/policy/panel`), narrated on the trace by
the gate events and audited by `approval_resolved` in the `arbiter-admin`
stream (policy-surface.md §9.6). The panel and its projection were removed; the
two kinds remain in the schema pending a cleanup.

### 4.8 Operational drawers — ▶ Run & Tests, and ⚙ Settings

The session pages are pure observability; the operational control plane
(`server.ts`, `supervisor/`, `agent-runner.ts`, `test-runs/`, driven by
`dev/js/control.js`) lives on the pages that use it (§4.32): the Settings
page (`#settings-area`; the nav item keeps `#settings-toggle`), **+ New run**
on Sessions and **▶ Run drills** on Drills (two dialogs), and the tool
sub-pages Drills › Matrix and Tests › Run a suite · Coverage · VM matrix ·
CI. It began as two drawers behind a ▶ Run and a ⚙ button, which is where
the section's name comes from; where the text below says "drawer" or "tab",
read the page or dialog. A dialog is a **centered modal** over a dimmed
backdrop (the shared `.drawer-*` shell; its hosts are `#new-run-dialog`,
`#run-drills-dialog` and the lazily-built modals, the DOM contract for
control.js and the JSDOM tests; `test/unit/ui/css-dialog-contract.test.ts`
pins the single geometry). Each takes the keyboard focus and gives it back
(§4.32 *A dialog takes the focus and gives it back*). This is the **operational** control plane (start
services, launch a run), not a security control plane.

**Settings** (`#settings-area`, §4.34 for its sub-menu) — sections ordered by blast radius:

**Services** (`#control-panel`) acts on the five supervised services (arbiter,
anthropic-proxy, openai-proxy, net-proxy, test-arbiter) and nothing else:
*Start / Stop / Restart services* (`POST /api/control/{start,stop,restart}-all`)
and per-service rows with live log disclosures, polled every 3 s. Every button
names its scope (the stack trio says **services**, never *all*; per-service
tooltips, `control.js SCOPE_TIP`), because when one service, the stack and the
dashboard itself looked alike no button's blast radius was legible.

**One row per supervised service.** The rows are the supervisor's own list
(`control.js SERVICE_IDS` is `supervisor-defs.ts SERVICE_IDS`, in its order;
`control-js-services.test.ts` pins the two together), so the test-tenant
arbiter (§6.y) has its row: its state, its Start or Stop · Restart, its error
line and its logs. That row is where the Tests page's store-down banner sends
you ("Start test-arbiter under Settings › Services"). Until 2026-10-09 the
panel drew four rows from a copy of the list made before the test tenant, so
the banner led to no row, Start / Stop services silently acted on a fifth
service, and the sub-menu said "4 of 4 running" with the test arbiter stopped
(`tests/stack/inspector-services-test-arbiter.test.ts` follows the banner to
the row and starts the real test arbiter from it).

**A request out holds its buttons (2026-10-13).** A row's Start, Stop or
Restart is answered only once the supervisor is done (a stop waits for the
process to exit, a start for it to be ready), and *Start / Stop / Restart
services* once every service is. The 3 s poll draws the rows again
meanwhile. A row whose own request is out (`h.out`, `doAction`) keeps every
button off until its answer draws it, and while a stack request is out
(`C.stackOut`, `doStack`) every row does, from the press; an armed Replace
ends at a stack press, since the stack is about to move its daemon. The dot
and the meta keep following the service (running, stopped, starting), as
under Replace. The stack's answer draws the rows from its snapshot, else
(a refusal, no answer) each from the status it last showed, so no row is
left off where no poll can repaint it; a row no answer has drawn yet gets
its buttons back as built. The three stack buttons and their line were
already held: they are static, and the poll never draws them. Words,
routes, POST bodies and refusals are unchanged; the product page's row has
held itself the same way since 2026-10-10 (§4.25, `S.serviceOut`). Until
then the poll turned a row's buttons back on mid-request: a row read
stopped mid-restart offered a live Start, whose press went out beside the
Restart, and under *Restart services* every row's Start, Stop and Restart
were live. Tests: `control-js-request-out.test.ts` (jsdom: a row across
running, stopped and starting polls; a 503 answer; another row; the stack
across a poll, an adopted row's Replace and an armed one; a refused and an
unanswered stack press; a row never drawn; a row's request inside the
stack's) and the stack e2e `tests/stack/inspector-service-request-out.test.ts`
(a real Supervisor whose stand-in holds its SIGTERM until the test lets it
go, a real DashboardServer, the served Settings page: signed in a row's
Restart and *Restart services* each hold across a poll, a second press sends
nothing and the service restarts once; signed out the real 403 gives every
row its buttons back; the token oracle).

**A row's request out holds the stack (2026-10-14).** The reverse was not
held: while a row's Start, Stop, Restart or Replace was out, *Start / Stop /
Restart services* stayed live, and the supervisor does not order two
requests (`restart()` is a `stop()` then a `start()`; `stopAll()` stops each
service). Over the real supervisor, a row's Restart held in its stop and
*Stop services* pressed meanwhile posted `stop-all` beside it, and once the
stop ended the stack line said "services stopped." while that service ran
again (the restart's start came after). Now, while any row's own request is
out (`h.out` or `h.replacing`), the three stack buttons are off
(`holdStack`, called where a row's request starts and ends, and at the end
of `doStack` in place of turning them on); they come back with the last
row's answer, whatever it is (worked, refused, no answer). Arming Replace
sends nothing and holds nothing; its confirm does. Words, routes and POST
bodies are unchanged. Tests: `control-js-request-out.test.ts` (jsdom: a row's
Restart across polls, the stack's presses sending nothing; a 403, a 503 and
no answer; two rows out; Replace worked and refused; a row's own hold still
outlasting a stack answer reached through `doStack`) and the stack e2e
`tests/stack/inspector-service-request-out.test.ts` Q1 (the held Restart:
the stack's buttons off across a poll, their presses sending nothing, every
other service still running after it, the buttons back with the answer).
Not covered: another tab, the Rules page's own *Restart services* (§4.32
*The restart keeps its state*, on another page) or a script can still send
a stack request beside a row's; ordering them in the supervisor is a
change to the control routes' semantics, left to the human.

**The focus stays on its row (2026-10-13).** A pressed button turns off
while its request is out, and a browser drops the focus of a button turned
off to `<body>`; a Stop that worked hides Stop and draws Start in its
place, and the poll hides or turns off what a service's new state does not
offer. Until 2026-10-13 nothing gave the focus back, so after every press
here the keyboard started over at the top of the page. Now, for a press
made with the focus on a row's line (`inRowLine`: one of its buttons, or
the line) or among the stack's buttons, and only while the focus is where
the press left it (fallen to `<body>`, or still there), the answer places
it (`rowFocus`, `stackFocus` in `control.js`):

- an answer that worked (Start, Stop, Restart, a confirmed Replace) gives
  it to the row's line (`.svc-head`: its label, state, pid and buttons;
  `tabindex="-1"`, no Tab stop, no ring), which says what the service does
  now. Never a button: a second Enter must send nothing, and never Start
  after a Stop;
- a refusal (signed out, a 503, no answer) gives it to the button pressed,
  on again, `aria-describedby` the row's error line (`svc-err-<id>`) while
  that holds the refusal; with no such button (a refused Restart that left
  the service crashed offers Start), the line. A refusal that brought no
  status gets its buttons back from the poll that follows, so `doAction`
  places the focus after that poll;
- *Start / Stop / Restart services*: worked, the stack's line
  (`#control-all-status`, "services restarted."); refused, the button
  pressed, `aria-describedby` that line;
- the poll: a focused button the state drawn hides or turns off (a crash
  hides Stop and Restart, a start turns them off, an adopted daemon turns
  them off, a Replace target that vanished hides Replace) gives the focus
  to its row's line. Not while a request of the row or the stack is out:
  its answer places the focus.

The next press drops the description a refusal gave (`undescribe`), and so
does the row once its refusal goes. A press made with the focus elsewhere
(a click in a browser that gives no focus on click), or a focus the reader
moved on meanwhile, moves nothing. Words, routes, POST bodies, CSRF and
refusals are unchanged; the product page's service line has kept the focus
the same way since 2026-10-13 (§4.25 *The service row keeps the focus*).
Tests: `control-js-service-focus.test.ts` (jsdom, buttons dropping their
focus when turned off: each answer that worked, refused, with no status,
with a crashed or starting status and with no answer; a refusal the poll
after it already dropped, and its description going with it; a browser
that keeps the focus on a button turned off; the stack worked, refused and
unanswered; Replace refused and worked; the poll over a crash, a start and
no change; a press without the focus, a focus moved on) and the stack e2e
`tests/stack/inspector-service-focus.test.ts` (a real Supervisor over
stand-ins, a real DashboardServer, the served Settings page: signed out a
row's Restart and *Restart services* keep the focus on the button, described
by the real refusal; signed in a Stop and a Start land on the row's line,
*Restart services* on the stack's line, and a SIGKILL the poll draws moves
a focused Restart to its row's line, never Start; the token oracle). Not
covered: a row's focused button that a stack press turns off, when that
press came from a click that gives no focus.

**With the service controls off.** A dashboard started with
`DASHBOARD_CONTROL=0` builds no supervisor (`server-main.ts`), so every
`/api/control/*` route answers 404 "control plane disabled". The panel reads
that status (`control.js renderControlOff`). Services is then one note:
"Service controls are off: this dashboard was started with
`DASHBOARD_CONTROL=0`, so it cannot show, start or stop the arbiter and the
proxies. Start it without that setting to manage them here." It has no row,
hint or button. Dashboard server says why it has no row ("Not shown: this
server's identity and its restart come with the service controls, which are
off …"), and the sub-menu shows no count. A later answer from a server with
its controls on draws the panel again.

Until 2026-10-09 the panel read the 404 as an empty list of services. It
drew all five rows "stopped", each with a live Start, under a top bar that
read the arbiter as live. Start / Stop / Restart services stayed live too,
and every one of those buttons could only 404.
`tests/stack/inspector-services-no-control.test.ts` spawns the real
`server-main` with the switch off beside a running arbiter. The product
page's Settings already said "started without the service controls"
(§4.25).

The same switch builds no agent runner, no test runner and no drill runner,
so `/api/run*`, `/api/test*`, `GET /api/drills/scenarios`, `POST
/api/drills` and `/api/drills/replay` answer the same 404. Each surface reads
its own route (`control.js renderOff`, shared with Services; drills.js and
drill-replay-run.js do the same for their panels):

- **Tests › Run a suite** reads `GET /api/test`, fetched each time the page
  is shown (`renderTestOff`). On a 404 the page is one note: "Running suites
  from the dashboard is off: this dashboard was started with
  `DASHBOARD_CONTROL=0`, so it cannot start a suite or show the run history.
  Run them from a terminal with `scripts/test-all.sh`." The run buttons, the
  picker, the history and the output are hidden. The test specifications
  stay, because their route needs no runner.
- **+ New run** reads `GET /api/run` each time the dialog opens
  (`renderRunOff`). On a 404 the dialog is one note instead of the form:
  "Starting an agent from the dashboard is off: this dashboard was started
  with `DASHBOARD_CONTROL=0`. Start one from a terminal with `mandu claude`
  or `mandu codex`."
- **▶ Run drills** (§4.22, §4.35) has two panels, and each reads its routes
  each time the dialog opens:
  - *Run the catalog* reads `GET /api/drills/scenarios` (`drills.js
    renderDrillsOff`). On a 404 it is one note: "Running drills from the
    dashboard is off: this dashboard was started with `DASHBOARD_CONTROL=0`,
    so it cannot list the catalog or start a run. Run them from a terminal
    with `cd tests && npm run drills:run`; their runs still show under Runs."
    The quick picks, the catalog, the launch row and the log are hidden.
