    Runs stays, because `GET /api/drills` needs no runner, and its empty
    line is "No runs yet.", without "Pick scenarios above and press Start".
    A checkout with no drill suite (the public tree, §4.22 "No drill
    tree") answers 503 `{unavailable: true}` on the catalog and on ▶ Start.
    The panel then shows the other note the same way (`#drills-unavailable`):
    "Drills are not available in this checkout: it has no drill suite (the
    maintainers keep it out of the public tree), so there is no catalog to
    list or run. Runs recorded elsewhere still show under Runs."
  - *Replay a drill* reads the catalog and `GET /api/drills/replay`
    (`drill-replay-run.js renderReplayOff`). Either 404 makes it one note:
    "Replaying a drill from the dashboard is off: this dashboard was started
    with `DASHBOARD_CONTROL=0`. Replay drills from a terminal with
    `scripts/test-all.sh --kind replay-drill`; recorded replay runs still
    show under Drills › Replay." Its launch row, notes, log, result and
    recent runs are hidden. The catalog's route is open, so the note shows
    signed out too, where the replay route answers 403 first. Two answers
    with neither 404 draw the panel again.
- **The sidebar's empty lists** read `canStart` on `GET /api/sessions`
  (§4.10.2). It holds `{ agent, suite, drill }`: whether this server has the
  agent runner, the test runner, and the drill runner with its store behind
  `/api/run`, `/api/test` and `POST /api/drills`. Each empty list's line
  (`app.js emptyHint`) names that dashboard's button while the runner is
  there, and the terminal command while it is not:
  - Sessions: "no sessions — starting one from the dashboard is off
    (DASHBOARD_CONTROL=0); in a terminal: mandu claude or mandu codex"
  - Tests: "no test runs — running suites from the dashboard is off
    (DASHBOARD_CONTROL=0); in a terminal: scripts/test-all.sh"
  - Live drills: "no live drills — running drills from the dashboard is off
    (DASHBOARD_CONTROL=0); in a terminal: cd tests && npm run drills:run"

  `canStart` is part of the list's signature, so a server restarted with the
  other setting redraws the lines at the next poll. An older server sends no
  `canStart` and keeps the buttons' lines. The field is no new disclosure:
  the three routes it describes are open and already answer 404 without
  their runner. Until 2026-10-10 the lines were fixed: "no sessions — + New
  run starts one", "no test runs — Run a suite → ▶ Run e2e" and "no live
  drills — ▶ Run drills starts one". Each pointed at a button whose surface
  then said that starting from the dashboard is off.

A Run, Start or Replay that answers 404 (a page left open while the server
restarted with the switch) also switches its surface to the note. A later
200 draws the controls again. A network failure keeps what is drawn. Until
2026-10-09 these surfaces stayed live: ▶ Run e2e, ▶ Run all and New run's Run
each printed "control plane disabled", under "no suites listed" and "no runs
yet — start one above." ▶ Run drills kept its nine quick picks over no
catalog and a live ▶ Start that answered "pick at least one scenario"; its
catalog said "Launching from the dashboard is off (control plane disabled)"
and Runs "Pick scenarios above and press Start". Replay a drill kept a live
agent picker beside an empty drill picker under two messages for one cause
("Could not read the replay runner's state." or "Replay runs from the
dashboard are off here …", and "The drill catalog is not available …"). The
same stack test opens each surface over the real routes, ▶ Run drills
signed out and signed in. It also reads the real `/api/sessions` (all three
`canStart` false) and the sidebar's three empty lines in the inspector
bundle over that listing. `app-js-sidebar.test.ts` pins each line to its own
runner, an older server and the redraw, and `control-routes.test.ts` pins
the flags to the runners a real `DashboardServer` was built with.

**Signed out.** Every button on these surfaces POSTs, and a POST needs the
admin session (§6.x). Signed out, the server answers 403 with
`ADMIN_SESSION_REQUIRED`, which is written for a developer: it names
`DASHBOARD_PASSWORD` and prints its command between backticks. Each surface
says it in the inspector's words, with the command as code, as its log views
do (§6): "Sign in to start a service: run `mandu dashboard` in your own
terminal and open the sign-in link it prints." The verb is the button's:

- a row's Start, Stop, Restart or Replace: "… a service";
- Start / Stop / Restart services: "… the services";
- Restart dashboard + services: "… the dashboard", also on the stale banner
  when it was pressed there;
- + New run's Run: "start an agent"; Run a suite: "run a suite"; their Cancel
  buttons: "cancel this run", "cancel the run";
- ▶ Run drills' Start: "run drills"; its Cancel: "cancel the run" (until
  2026-10-10 a refused Cancel said "cancelling…" for good). Replay a
  drill's ▶ Replay says its panel's own "Sign in to replay a drill: …".

control.js, drills.js and drill-replay-run.js match the refusal on its text
(`/^admin session required\b/`), as the product page does (§4.25
"Refusals"), because a 403 can also be the CSRF or origin check. Any other
refusal keeps the server's words.

A service row keeps the answer to its last button (`control.js
keepRefusal`). The line stays over the 3 s repaints while the service is in
the state it was refused in, until the next button on that row. It comes
before the service's own error or staleness, which shows again once it goes.
The dashboard row keeps the answer to a restart that did not happen the same
way, until the next arm or another server pid. Until 2026-10-09 the repaint
that follows every row button cleared the line at once, so signed out a
row's Start, Stop or Restart changed nothing on the page. Replace and Restart
dashboard lost their refusal at the next poll, and the other surfaces printed
the server's text whole, backticks included. Tests:
`control-js-signed-out.test.ts`, `drills-js.test.ts`,
`drill-replay-run-js.test.ts`, and the stack e2e
`tests/stack/inspector-actions-signed-out.test.ts` (a real supervisor and
server: the routes' 403s move no service, the served page's sign-in lines
outlast a poll, and Start works signed in).

**No answer** (2026-10-10). The dashboard server stopped, or the
connection dropped, under an open inspector: a browser's `fetch` throws
instead of answering. The request helpers of control.js (`apiPost`),
prompt-filters.js (`pfGet`, `pfPost`) and drills.js (`apiPost`) answer it as
status 0, never a throw, as protection.js and drill-replay-run.js already
did. Each surface says one sentence in its place: "the dashboard server did
not answer — reload this page once it is running again". The sentence is the
same in the three files, which stay import-free (`control-js-no-answer.test.ts`
pins the copies equal). Every button the click disabled comes back:

- a service row's Start, Stop, Restart or Replace: the line on the row, kept
  like a refusal (above). The row is drawn again from the status it last
  showed (`h.status`), since no poll can repaint it, so an adopted daemon's
  Stop stays disabled, and Replace arms again;
- Start / Stop / Restart services: the stack line, the three buttons free;
- Restart dashboard + services: the row's line (and the stale banner's, when
  pressed there). The row leaves "restarting the dashboard server…" and
  arms again. A dead server cannot restart itself, and the words do not say
  it will;
- + New run's Run and Cancel, Run a suite's Run and Cancel: their status
  line, Run free again;
- ▶ Run drills' Start and Cancel: the dialog's status line, never
  "starting…" or "cancelling…" for good;
- the Prompt filters panel (§4.31): every read and control.

Until then none of these callers caught the throw. Start / Stop / Restart
services stayed disabled under "starting services…", a row's buttons stayed
disabled with nothing said, and Replace stayed "replacing — …" and never
armed again. Restart dashboard + services stayed "restarting the dashboard
server…" even once the server answered again (`renderDashboardRow` returns
early while restarting); it is the button a person presses when the
dashboard seems stuck. New run, Run a suite and Run drills stayed
"starting…". Each rejected unhandled. The product page has had the same
contract since the same day (§4.25 *A click with no answer says so*), in its
own words. Tests: `control-js-no-answer.test.ts`, the *no answer* cases of
`prompt-filters-js.test.ts` and `drills-js.test.ts`, and the stack e2e
`tests/stack/inspector-click-no-answer.test.ts`. That e2e runs a real
supervisor and server, and the served Settings page with control.js and
prompt-filters.js, signed in. The server stops under the page. A row's
Start, Start services, Restart dashboard and the test bench each say the
sentence and leave no button disabled. Nothing rejects unhandled, and the
oracle finds no token on the page.

**No answer to a poll** (2026-10-10). The page's polls met the same silence
and changed nothing, or blamed the arbiter. Now each says so within one tick:

- the top bar (app.js `loadSessionsOnce`, `renderStatusLine`): the session
  poll's read throws, `S.serverGone` is set, and the status line reads
  "● Dashboard: not answering · not live", grey, its tooltip "The dashboard
  server did not answer, so this page shows the last state it reported.
  Reload this page once it is running again." It outranks a store that is
  down and any posture republished meanwhile; the next answer clears it
  (§4.32). The session list keeps what it shows;
- Settings › Services (control.js `pollStatus`, `renderNoAnswer`): "the
  dashboard server did not answer — showing the last known state" over the
  rows (`#control-no-answer`); the sub-menu's "N of 5 running" goes; the
  Dashboard server row turns grey and says the sentence, except while a
  restart you asked for is under way or armed (its own line speaks then).
  The next answer hides the note and draws every row again;
- Rules and Approvals (egress.js `renderStale`): the kept panel's note and
  the Approvals card's say "the dashboard server did not answer — showing
  the last known state"; with nothing painted yet, the panel and both cards
  say the sentence. The arbiter's own silence (`available: false`) keeps
  "arbiter unreachable — showing the last known state";
- the Secrets panel (secrets.js `apiGet` answers status 0): its status line
  says "UNKNOWN — " and the sentence, its tables cleared as for any answer
  it cannot read.

`NO_ANSWER_STALE` is the same in control.js and egress.js, and `NO_ANSWER` in
egress.js and secrets.js too (the pin test above). Until then, with the
server gone, the top bar kept "Protection: Secrets", Services kept "running"
rows with live dots and "2 of 5 running" (their processes had stopped with
the server), Rules and Approvals said "arbiter unreachable", and the session
and Secrets polls rejected unhandled every 4 and 5 s. A restart you asked
for reads the same while the server is down, which is true; the page
reloads when the new one answers. Tests: `inspector-polls-no-answer.test.ts`
and the stack e2e `tests/stack/inspector-server-gone.test.ts`: a real arbiter
behind the production adapter with a registered key, a real supervisor and
server, and the served Settings page with app.js, control.js, egress.js and
secrets.js, signed in. The server stops and each of the page's polls runs
once (the served-page harness's `polls`). Nothing rejects unhandled, and the
oracle finds neither the key nor a token on the page.

**No answer to a write in Approvals, Rules, Secrets and Protection**
(2026-10-10). The writes of egress.js, secrets.js and protection.js met the
same silence after the panels above had their sentence. egress.js's request
helpers (`apiRequest`) and secrets.js's `apiSend` now answer status 0, never
a throw, as their reads already did; protection.js turned the throw into
status 0 at each call already. Each write says so where it was made, and
gives its buttons back as it does after a refusal:

- Approvals (§4.34): Block, Allow once, Always allow, a held message's answer
  and "Always allow from …": the sentence on the card's or row's line, kept
  across a poll like a refusal (`refusal` answers it at status 0);
- Rules: ＋ Add a rule (each kind; a website or a connection reads the
  policy file first), the Lists editor and Test a flow: the sentence in the
  form's line;
- a row's ⓘ: "could not read this decision: " and the sentence, never "from
  the arbiter"; View the handling prompt: "could not fetch the handling
  prompt: " and the sentence; the Audit trail: "could not read the audit
  stream: " and the sentence, never "the protection service may be
  unreachable";
- the Secrets panel's Label path: the sentence in the form's error line;
  Remove and Clear taint: in the line under their own table (`refusalOf`;
  since 2026-10-12, §4.32 *Remove and Clear taint say what they did*);
- the Protection block (§4.19.v3): ⏸ Pause sending, ▶ Resume and ⟳ Restart
  services say the sentence; a Sandbox switch says `could not save "<key>": `
  and the sentence, a level card or Protection axes switch "could not save
  the change: " and the sentence. Each switch shows the saved setup again.

Until then they said "request failed" (Block, Add a rule, Lists, Label
path), "the tester is unavailable — request failed", "the restart request
failed", "the request failed — nothing changed" (which a page with no answer
cannot know), "… — request failed; nothing was changed" and "… — the
dashboard did not answer". `NO_ANSWER` is the same in protection.js too (the
pin test above). A catch that remains around a write is for a throw that is
not a request's; it keeps its old words. Tests:
`inspector-writes-no-answer.test.ts` and the stack e2e
`tests/stack/inspector-writes-no-answer.test.ts`: a real arbiter with a
registered key and one waiting question, behind the production adapter; a
real server; the served Rules page signed in with egress.js, protection.js
and secrets.js. The server stops under the page. Block, Add a rule, New
list, Test a flow, Pause sending, a Sandbox switch and Label path each say
the sentence and leave no button disabled; nothing changed, nothing rejects
unhandled, and the oracle finds neither the key nor a token on the page.

**No answer to a session's read** (2026-10-10). A session pick reads
`/api/events` (app.js `loadEvents`), and that read can fail three ways: no
answer (the server is gone), a 503 (the store's arbiter is down, §4.35), or
an error or a body that is not the session's events. Until then
`loadEvents` threw on each of them. The pick had already moved the URL and
the list's highlight, so the header and the trace stayed the last session's
under the new one's name. The click rejected unhandled, and on the 503
`ingest(undefined)` also left `S.events` undefined. Now `loadEvents` never
throws: it returns true when it drew the events, else why it could not
(`readFailure`):

- the no-answer sentence above;
- "Mandu's arbiter is not running — start it under Settings › Services"
  (or the test store's, with test-arbiter), as the store-down banner says it;
- the server's own error;
- "the dashboard server answered with an error (HTTP 500)".

A failed pick (`paintUnread`) puts the page back in its own state before any
session loaded (`S.vm` null), and the header says so (§4.33 *A session that
could not be read*). The last session's stream closes, and the dot says "not
live". The page reads it again by itself (*Read again*, below); clicking the
row again, or reloading, also reads it. Elsewhere:

- "Load all N" with no answer says "Could not load the rest: …" beside the
  first-N line and gives its button back. It no longer stays "Loading…".
- A `?step=` or `?ask=` link past the loaded window whose rest cannot be
  read says so in its note and marks nothing. It never says "that step is
  not in its trace".
- A live refetch that fails keeps the trace it shows (the session's own;
  the status line already says the feed is down).
- An answer for a session the page has left draws nothing. This covers its
  events, its git log and its stream. Until then a slower read of the last
  pick painted over the one just made.

`NO_ANSWER` in app.js is pinned with the other copies. Tests:
`app-js-session-unread.test.ts` and the stack e2e
`tests/stack/inspector-session-unread.test.ts`. The e2e runs a real arbiter
with a labelled `.env`, the real anthropic-proxy (two sessions through it, one
reading the file), a real server, and the served Sessions page with app.js,
signed out:

- the arbiter stops, then a pick of the other session says the store-down
  words with none of the first session's cards;
- the arbiter comes back, and the same pick draws the session;
- the server stops, and a pick says the no-answer sentence;
- nothing rejects unhandled, and the oracle finds the secret on no model
  request, page or answer.

**Read again** (2026-10-10). Until then a failed pick waited for a click.
When the server or the store's arbiter came back, the session-list poll put
the top bar back to live, but the header kept "Could not read this session."
and its advice to reload, under a server that was running. After an outage
no poll saw (the server restarted between two 4 s polls, as *Restart
dashboard + services* does), it stayed that way for good. Now the poll reads
the open pick again by itself (app.js `readUnreadAgain`; `S.unread` holds the
pick):

- on the first list answer after the failed pick, which covers an outage no
  poll saw;
- on any list answer after one that did not: no answer, or the store's 503.
  The list's own 503 is not an answer, so nothing is read while the store
  is down.

A read again that succeeds draws the session as a click would (header,
trace, git log, stream, and the marks of a `?step=` or `?ask=` link), with
no click and with the URL unchanged. A read again that fails keeps the line,
with the latest cause, and waits for the next return. So a lasting error
(a log the server cannot read) costs one more read, not one per poll. A
session the person has left for another is never read again. Not covered:
the drill and replay panels' own reads, which follow the pick
(`mdu:session-selected`), and "Load all N", whose button is given back.
Presentation only: no route or server string changed. Tests:

- `app-js-session-read-again.test.ts`. The server is back after a poll saw
  it gone. An outage no poll saw (the list answering 304). The store's
  arbiter is back. A read again that fails waits for a return. A session
  left for another is not read again. A link's pick that failed at load is
  marked once read.
- The stack e2e `tests/stack/inspector-session-read-again.test.ts`, with
  the setup above, signed out. The arbiter stops, and a pick says the
  store-down words. A poll gets the list's 503, and the pick stays unread.
  The arbiter comes back, and one poll draws the session. Then the server
  stops with no poll to see it, and a pick says the no-answer sentence. A
  new server starts on the same port, and one poll draws the session, its
  Read as a placeholder. Nothing rejects unhandled, and the oracle holds.

**Readiness kinds** (`ServiceDefinition.ready`, `net-probes.ts checkReady`):
`socket`, `tcp` (a fixed host:port accepts) and `port-file`
(test-organization.md §8.4): the service binds port 0 and writes the port it
got to `MANDU_PORT_FILE` (tmp + rename); ready means that port accepts. A
`port-file` service is never adopted. The supervisor's unit harness uses it for
every TCP fake, so no test picks a free port and races to bind it
(`supervisor.test.ts`, `port-file.test.ts`).

**How a service is started** (`supervisor-defs.ts buildDefinitions`,
`Supervisor.spawnForm`; packaging.md §5.1). Every service is ONE node process
leading its own process group; none starts through `npm run serve` (npm, sh
and the tsx binary in front of each proxy cost about a second a start, and
the arbiter's admin channel, an inherited fd, survives only a direct node
spawn). Installed: `node <pkg>/dist/<name>.mjs`. In a checkout the definition
is the source form, `node --import <the package's tsx> <entry.ts>` with the
package as cwd, and carries the bundled form (`checkoutBundle`: the
checkout's `launcher/dist/<name>.mjs`, cwd `launcher/`, the proxies pointed
at `dist/arbiter-client.mjs`). The supervisor reads the build record at EVERY
spawn, a restart included, because the dashboard outlives builds: the bundle
runs only while the launcher's own check (`launcher/scripts/bundle-stamp.mjs
checkStamp`, loaded from the checkout at run time; any error reads as stale)
calls it fresh, else the source runs and the log says why. A stale bundle is
never started. Start, restart, the readiness probes and the group kill on
stop are the same for both forms. The arbiter's policy classifier
(`--classifier`, inspect-mcp's `classify-main`) follows the arbiter's form:
the bundled arbiter runs `policy-classifier.mjs` from the same build, the
source arbiter the source through tsx (`arbiterClassifierArgs`, packaging.md
§5.1, 2026-10-09). The resident dashboard itself runs from
that build when a bundled launch starts it (server-main reads a `dist/`
beside `src/run.ts` as a checkout's build and keeps the dev layout). Tests:
`supervisor-checkout-bundle.test.ts` (unit: the choice per spawn, the record
check), `supervisor-defs-installed.test.ts` (the forms) and
`tests/stack/supervisor-checkout-bundle.test.ts` (the real arbiter and proxies
from a private build, fresh then stale; they serve; every pid reaped).

**Adopted services.** A service already listening when the supervisor starts
it is *adopted*: no child pid, so the dashboard does not own it. Stop and
Restart are disabled and `Supervisor.stop()` **refuses**, rather than marking
the row stopped while the daemon keeps serving (the stale-daemon trap). A
promoted arbiter serving current code is the shared stack's deliberate posture
(it outlives dashboard restarts) and reads as steady state; a stale or legacy
daemon keeps an amber warning.

**Replace** (`Supervisor.replace()`, `POST /api/control/<id>/replace`) is the
sanctioned takeover of an adopted arbiter, a separate named action so Restart
never silently escalates into killing a process the dashboard does not own.
It targets a **verified pid only** — the `hello` pid, else the socket owner
found through the OS — after its command line confirms an arbiter
(`/proc/<pid>/cmdline` on Linux, `ps -ww -o args=` on macOS; the
recycled-pid guard from `launcher/src/reap.ts`); no verifiable pid, no button.
It hands over on the same DB (runtime-instances.md §9: SIGTERM, then SIGKILL,
the successor spawning once the endpoint clears), is **armed** (a second click
confirms), and keeps a refusal on the row past the 3 s poll (*Signed out*
above). While a row is adopted and
identity-less, each poll (throttled to 10 s) retries the hello probe and runs
**OS socket-owner discovery** (`src/supervisor/socket-owner.ts`): Linux
uses `/proc/net/unix` and a same-uid `/proc/<pid>/fd` sweep; macOS uses
`lsof -U -F pn`, matching the literal or canonical bound path. More than one
holder, a missing or hung probe, or a probe error returns no owner, never
a guessed kill target. Replace repeats discovery fresh at kill time and
checks the command line again. The fire-and-forget identity refresh catches
and logs probe failures, avoiding an unhandled rejection on macOS. Tests:
`supervisor-replace.test.ts`, `socket-owner.test.ts`,
`supervisor-identity-refresh.test.ts`.

**Per-module logs** (`src/supervisor/service-logs.ts`): an in-memory ring
(50000 lines) that `GET /api/control/<id>/logs` replays then follows over SSE,
and a durable `<logDir>/<id>.log` per service served by
`GET /api/control/<id>/logfile` (the row's **"full log ↗"** link). Both are
`admin` reads (§6: a log may echo a value). A line reaches the ring at once
and the file through asynchronous writes, so `logfile` first waits until
every line the ring holds is in the file (`Supervisor.logFileWritten`, at
most 2 s; an exited service's ended stream until it closes): the full log
holds every line the live view already showed. Until 2026-10-17 it read the
file at once and could miss the newest lines (CI pipeline 11021). The row's **logs** fold opens the
stream. A dropped connection reconnects by itself. A refused one closes the
EventSource for good, and an EventSource cannot read the status, so control.js
asks the same URL once (`refusalStatus`). Signed out (403) the fold says
"Sign in to read this log: run `mandu dashboard` …", the sentence the other
log views use, and hides the row's "full log ↗", which would open the same
refusal. Any other refusal says "Could not open this log (HTTP <n>). Close
logs and open them again to retry." Reopening the fold reads the log again.
Until 2026-10-09 a refused fold opened on an empty box.

**Each fold names its service (2026-10-12).** The fold, its link and its log
box read the same on every row. A headless Chromium (a real supervisor whose
stand-ins print 80 lines each, a real dashboard, signed in) read the five
folds as "logs full log ↗" and the five links as "full log ↗". An open log
that overflowed was a Tab stop of its own: a `generic` named by all its
lines, though a log may echo a value. Now the fold is named "logs of <the
row's label>" and the link "full log of <label>". The log box is a `group`
named as its fold (control.js `nameLogs`, `aria-label` set with
`setAttribute`). The label is the one the row draws: the id until the first
status answer, then the supervisor's `label` ("Arbiter", "Anthropic proxy
(Claude)", …), and a later label renames all three. Sighted readers see no
change. Chromium gives a named `<summary>` its words as a description ("logs
full log of Arbiter"). That is left as it is: moving the link out of the
fold would change the row as drawn. The row's Start, Stop and Restart
already say their service in their description (`SCOPE_TIP`). Tests:
`control-js-services.test.ts` covers the names by label, no two rows alike,
the open log as the panel's one box that may scroll and a named group, no
name holding a line, and a new label renaming them. The stack e2e
`tests/stack/inspector-service-log-names.test.ts` runs a real supervisor's
stand-ins and reads the served page and styles signed in and out. It checks
that each link opens its own service's log, and runs the oracle.

The ring holds only the output of a child the supervisor spawned, so an
adopted service's log stays empty for good, and so does the log of a service
that has written nothing since the dashboard started. An open fold that no
line has reached says why in place of the empty box, worded by the row's
state (control.js `drawLogEmpty`): adopted, "No log here: this service was
started outside this dashboard, so its output goes wherever the program that
started it sends it."; starting or running, "No lines yet: this service has
written nothing since it started. New lines show here as it writes them.";
crashed, "No lines: this service stopped without writing anything.";
stopped, "No lines yet: this service has written nothing since this
dashboard started. Start it to see its output here." The 3 s poll rewords
it when the row's state changes; the first line, or a refusal's line, takes
its place. "full log ↗" stays. Until 2026-10-10 each such fold opened on an
empty box. (With nothing to replay, the stream sends its headers only with
its first line or the 15 s heartbeat, so the words cannot wait for the
stream to open.) Tests: `control-js-services.test.ts`, the stack e2e
`tests/stack/inspector-service-logs-signed-out.test.ts` and
`tests/stack/inspector-service-logs-empty.test.ts` (a real arbiter adopted,
a real supervisor's silent, not-started and talking stand-ins, the served
folds' words over the real streams, a started service's first line taking
their place).

**Appearance**: the theme picker (§4.1). **Docs & slides**: optional deck
links served by `GET /slides/<file>` only from `MANDU_SLIDES_DIR` (read-only,
flat filenames; unset → 404 and hidden links; `slides-route.test.ts`), and
**⬇ Open design doc**, `GET /api/context-pack.md` (`src/context-pack.ts`): the
curated core design docs verbatim (`CONTEXT_PACK_MANIFEST`), an index of the
rest and recent suite runs, as one markdown file for an LLM conversation. A
missing doc becomes a `⚠ MISSING` marker, never a 500; tests pin every
manifest path and a 1 MB budget (`CONTEXT_PACK_MAX_BYTES`) — the fix for growth
is re-curating: drop a doc to the index, or include only its lead (a manifest
entry's `lead`: the doc up to its first `## ` heading, then a "Lead only"
marker; the index marks it ◐). 2026-10-16: the two frozen integrity-axis
design docs moved from the pack to its index when the pack reached the budget;
2026-10-17: `exec-routing.md` (~196 KB, mostly frozen integrity routing) went
lead only when it reached it again, leaving ~0.81 MB.

**Running things** — where each of the retired ▶ Run drawer's seven tabs
lives now (§4.32): Run agent → + New run; 🎬 Drills (§4.22) → ▶ Run drills;
▦ Drill matrix (§4.29) → Drills › Matrix; 🧪 Tests, ◫ Coverage (§4.29),
🖥 VM matrix (§4.26), ⚑ CI (§4.27) → the Tests sub-pages. The panels are
unchanged; control.js `wireDialogs` opens the two dialogs and `wireSubpages`
pings the module that paints a sub-page when it shows, so each loads only
when seen.

- **+ New run** (`#run-panel` in `#new-run-dialog`): a sample-prompt picker
  (`GET /api/run/samples`, the eval corpus, Benign / Red-team) fills prompt
  and target (`claude -p` / `codex exec`); the OS chokepoint options
  (`--net-proxy`, `--exec-wrap`) are on by default, with an
  equivalent-command echo. Run brings up the services it needs, then streams
  output over SSE.
- **Tests › Run a suite** (`#test-panel`, §4.10): run buttons (`POST /api/test`), a suite
  picker over every entry of `tests/suites.mjs` grouped by kind, the run history
  (`GET /api/test`: per-case ✓/✗/− results, failures first, `# SKIP` reasons),
  the spec browser and the live output.
- **Spec browser** (`#test-specs`): `GET /api/test/specs` serves each suite's
  spec **sliced server-side from its source** (`src/test-runs/test-specs.ts`,
  a comment/string-aware scanner, not a TS parser), so what renders is the
  spec that runs: the file-header doc block, then each `SCENARIOS` entry with
  its registry badge, flag chips and literal. Registry entries missing from the
  source render as **RETIRED**; unreadable files degrade, never a 500.

The dialogs are one at a time (✕, the backdrop, Esc, a page change or
`mdu:close-dialog` close them) and wired on boot regardless, so polling and
streaming continue while closed. Every mutating call sends the
`X-Mandu-Control` CSRF header; all untrusted text (log lines, prompts, labels,
test titles, suite source) is inserted with `textContent`, never `innerHTML`.

**Boot autostart.** On startup the server brings the stack up
(`supervisor.startAll()`; `DASHBOARD_AUTOSTART=0` opts out), each start waiting
10 s or `MANDU_SERVICE_READY_TIMEOUT_MS` (runtime-instances.md §14.6). Under
`DASHBOARD_AUTOSTART=arbiter` (the launcher's autostart) a failed arbiter start
exits 1 so the launcher can start its own (runtime-instances.md §10). The
approvals/secrets surfaces, whose connect necessarily fails before the arbiter
exists, are late-bound once it is up (`server.attachArbiterSurfaces()`), else
stay an honest 404.

**Dashboard self-status + self-restart** (`src/self-status.ts`). The
view-model is computed server-side from sources imported once at boot, so a
dashboard started before a code change keeps rendering the old model while
looking healthy. Its own panel (`#dashboard-panel` — it is not a service)
flags **STALE** when HEAD moved and the diff since boot touches `dashboard/`,
or a file under `dashboard/src` has an mtime after boot; unknown repository
state fails quiet. The arbiter check uses the same package-scoped rule
(`arbiterStaleness`) but fails **loud** on an unresolvable rev — a foreign
daemon's claim (runtime-instances.md §4); before it, another release or
another bundle of this one than the dashboard would start flags the arbiter
too (`arbiterReleaseStaleness`, 2026-10-17), with or without a checkout.
Staleness also turns the Settings nav item
red.

The restart (**⟳ Restart dashboard + services**, on the stale banner and under
**Advanced**, armed) answers 202, then (1) **reaps the services this process
spawned** — children run with `stdio: pipe`, so one outliving the dashboard
dies with EPIPE; adopted instances are skipped; (2) spawns a detached
successor whose autostart brings the services back (including any the operator
had stopped — hence the narrower **Restart services**); (3) exits **without**
`server.close()`, which would wait on open SSE responses. Known gap: an
adopted service that later dies keeps showing `running` until re-probed.

**Runtime registry.** The dashboard registers in the runtime registry
(`src/registry.ts` → `<runtimeBase>/dashboards/<id>.json`, with the bound port,
removed on deliberate exit, dead entries swept at boot), so `mandu status` and
`mandu reap` see forgotten dashboards like every other Mandu daemon
(runtime-instances.md §10).

### 4.9 Per-tool-call policy modal — schema-first, per-field trust

Each tool card (§4.2f) carries a **⚖** button opening a centered modal,
**Rules · <tool>** (`#policy-modal`, the shared `.drawer-*` shell; "⚖ Policy"
until §4.35; since 2026-10-13 the tool and what the call touched, "Rules ·
Bash npm test", §4.32 *A dialog says which item it shows*), that presents the tool's input/output schema with a per-field
TRUSTED / UNTRUSTED badge, then the decision this call got
(`policyModalHtml`). Its headings are in the product's words: "Input fields:
what the tool is given", "Output fields: what gets masked on the way in",
"This call: what was decided"; a tool no built-in rule names says "the
fail-closed default applies", and a rule-reference chip opens it "under
Rules".

- **INPUT FIELDS** (the tool *args* — the outbound data-usage schema). Trust is
  derived from egress handling: `not_resolve` (kept symbolic, AgentView) →
  TRUSTED; `resolve` (desymbolized at egress, HumanView) → UNTRUSTED;
  `no_symbols_expected` → TRUSTED. (Trust is an inbound concept, so the input
  badge is this derived view, noted inline.)
- **OUTPUT FIELDS** (the tool *result* — the inbound data-trust schema): the
  literal marker, or a conditional (origin-keyed) field rendered UNTRUSTED with
  an "unless `URL`/`DIR` trusted" qualifier.
- **this call** — the per-call decision folded onto the tool unit
  (`view-model.ts toolUnitPolicy` → `ToolCallGroup.policy`): the result trust
  (+ category) from the `classify` / `symbolize` event, and the egress `usage`
  + `shell` from the `desymbolize` / `exec_action` events.

The per-field schema is the **governing rule**, the static per-tool spec that
lives arbiter-side (`claude-code-inbound.ts`, `tool-outbound.ts`, the origin
categories). The arbiter serializes it via the `policySnapshot` op
(`arbiter/policy/policy-snapshot.ts` → `PolicyRuleSnapshot`); the dashboard
reads it once via `GET /api/policy` and joins by tool name (`ruleForToolJs`:
exact, then the `mcp__*` prefix fallback mirroring `getToolInboundSpec`). One
source of truth, so the modal cannot drift from what the arbiter enforces.
Limitation: the snapshot is the policy at fetch time, so a mid-session reload
can skew the displayed rule; the per-call **decision** stays time-accurate.

**Fail-soft.** Without an arbiter `GET /api/policy` returns `{ policy: null }`
at 200 and the modal shows the decision with "rule unavailable". It adds no
untrusted-data path (policy metadata and the `DualRepr` the trace already
exposes), so the §9 invariant is unaffected.

### 4.10 Sidebar sections — Sessions, Live drills, Replay drills, Tests, with test-run results

The session sidebar (§4.3.2) is shaped server-side by the pure, unit-tested
`dashboard/src/session-batches.ts` (shapes in `session-batch-types.ts`);
`app.js` only renders its output. Sessions run together fold into **batches**
(§4.10.1); the batches split into four **sections** (§4.10.2); a test batch
joins the test-runner's run record so its pass/fail results are first-class
(§4.10.3). All of it is observability: no new untrusted-data path (test titles
are process output, escaped like all card text), and the §9 invariant
machinery is untouched.

#### 4.10.1 Session batches

Sessions that were run together (one e2e run produces a dozen or more) appear
as one **batch**: a collapsible group, folded by default, newest first.

**Batch identity rides the session-id rails.** A batch is keyed by an explicit
`ManduEvent.batchId`. The arbiter persists events verbatim, so the field needs
no arbiter change:

- The **e2e harnesses** send `x-mandu-batch-id: <id>` on every request of a
  run, beside `x-mandu-session-id`. The id is `MANDU_BATCH_ID` when set (a
  dashboard run), else one id minted per process (a standalone `npm test`
  still forms one batch). Both mint sites (`tests/lib/batch-id.ts
  mintBatchId`, the developer view's `test-run-model.ts` mintRunId`,
  deliberate twins since the packages install independently) produce
  `YYYYMMDD-HHMM-<4 hex>`: the id names the kept fsSync workspace directory
  (`<tmpdir>/mandu-e2e-fs-<uid>/<batch>/<ws-hash>/`, a private per-uid root,
  docker-e2e-rig.md §3; `<ws-hash>` an opaque hash so
  the model's working-directory note never reveals the scenario name), so it
  is short, sortable and says when the batch ran. Consumers treat it as
  opaque.
- **anthropic-proxy** reads it (`BATCH_ID_HEADERS` / `batchIdFor`, mirroring
  `sessionIdFor`) and stamps `batchId` on the events it emits.
- The **dashboard test-runner** sets `MANDU_BATCH_ID=<runId>` in the spawned
  env, so one run is one batch, and that id is the run-record join key
  (§4.10.3).
- The **`mandu` launcher** reads `MANDU_BATCH_ID` into `plan.batchId`, packs
  it into the session-id header as the `;x-mandu-batch-id: <id>` pair the
  proxy already unpacks (Claude Code sends only one custom header), and
  stamps it on its own `launch_posture` / `session_exit` events, so a session
  carries it from its first event even if it ends before any model call.
  openai-proxy stamps nothing (it strips Mandu's headers); a Codex session
  gets its batch from the launcher's events.
- `MANDU_BATCH_MEMBER` (`scenario:<key>` or `posture:<key>`, set per pane by
  the watch runner) is recorded on `launch_posture` as `batchMember` and
  surfaces as `SessionRef.batchMember`; the sidebar badges a watch row by it
  (§4.22). It groups nothing.

**Grouping** (`groupSessionsIntoBatches`). The event source reads `batchId`
from the first event that carries one, in the scan it already makes. One batch
per distinct `batchId`; sessions without one group into synthetic **per-day
batches** (the day of `lastTs` in the viewer's time zone, id
`day:<YYYY-MM-DD>`, ts-less → `day:undated`), which replaced an earlier single
"Ungrouped" bucket that grew meaningless. All batches, real and day, order by
their newest session. A batch carries `{ id, title, ungrouped, sessions,
firstTs, lastTs, violated }`: `firstTs` is the earliest member's first event,
`violated` is true if any member violated the invariant (a folded batch still
flags it), and `title` is server-computed (`batchTitle`): the joined run's
label, else `"<suite> e2e run"` for test members, else the first member's task
label (a live batch is one launcher / + New run invocation, named by what it
did; truncated to 60 chars), else `"run"`; a day batch's title is the ISO
day, which the client prettifies (Today / Yesterday / "Jun 21").

**Rendering.** Each batch is a header plus its rows, folded by default; the
header toggles (`role="button"` + `aria-expanded`), and the fold state persists
per batch id (`mandu.batchFold`). Selecting a session (deep link, live update)
expands its batch. Each `.batch` is a **card**: a bordered box with a filled
header bar, a gap between groups and a thin left rule binding the open rows to
their header; the indent stays tiny because the sidebar is narrow. A live row
is named by its label; a test row by its **scenario** with a compact 🧪
per-class badge (`Re<n>` / `E<n>` / `C<n>` …) and the `offline` / `live` suite
badge, the near-identical prompts moving to the tooltip. The client regroups
two pages' batches (§4.33, §4.35): Sessions shows its live batches as one
group per local day (Today · Yesterday · a date; the two newest open, the
System logs group last and folded), and Drills one group per run, named for
what it was ("Pipeline gl-8398", "Local run", "Live run").

**Day names at midnight (2026-10-04).** A day name is relative to the page's
own clock: `dayLabel(day, nowMs)` takes today and yesterday from the one
`nowMs`, and yesterday is the calendar day before today, not `nowMs - 24 h`
(in the first hour after a 23-hour DST day that was two days back, and the
run of the short day lost its "Yesterday"). The list's redraw signature
carries today's local day, so the first poll after midnight renames the
groups though the list did not change; a page left open overnight never
calls yesterday's runs "Today". The browser tests pin the page's clock
(`boot(…, { now })`, the harness's `installClock`, an offset `Date` whose
`set(ms)` moves it), so a suite run that crosses midnight cannot flip a label.

Tests: `session-batches.test.ts` (grouping, ordering, day groups, titles,
violated rollup, sections and joins below), the proxy's `batchIdFor` cases,
the event source's `batchId` exposure, `ui/app-js-sidebar.test.ts` and
`ui/app-js-render.test.ts` (folding, expand-on-select), `local-day.test.ts`
(both `dayLabel` twins either side of a midnight and after a 23-hour day) and
`ui/app-js-sessions-page.test.ts` (the page's clock passing midnight renames
the days at the next load).

#### 4.10.2 The four sections and the pages that list them

`buildSidebarSections(sessions, runs, nowMs, tz, watchRuns)` returns
`sections: { live, drills, replay, testing }` on `GET /api/sessions` (beside the
flat `sessions` list, `canDelete` and `canStart`, which says what the
dashboard can start and words the empty lists, §4.8; a client facing a
server with no `sections` falls back to one list). The UI labels are **Sessions** (`live`),
**Live drills** (`drills`), **Replay drills** (`replay`) and **Tests**
(`testing`); the wire keys keep their first names so an older client still
renders. Classification, in order:

1. **Replay drill** iff the recorded source made it (`SessionRef.replay`, set
   from a validated record and never from events, so an arbiter session
   cannot claim the section; §4.28). `buildReplayBatches` makes one batch per
   run, titled `replay · <ref or source> · <commit>`, with `replayRun` and a
   run tally (PASS = pass, WARN = the third bucket, FAIL and TIMEOUT = fail; the
   same buckets give each row its P/F/− badge). A replay row shows the drill
   title, badge, drill id, agent, size, script version (eight characters;
   tooltip: whole, origin, engine), the security and utility tallies
   (`2/2 · 1/3`) and 🎬 when the Mandu recording exists. Recorded rows are
   read-only (no 🗑).
2. **Live drill** iff a 🎬 watch run drove it (§4.22), whatever its tenant: the
   run names the session (`meta.sessions` / a chapter's `scopeId`), or its
   batch id is the run id, or its id starts with `<runId>-` (a run that died
   before recording its sessions), or its id or batch id has the watch
   runner's `watch-` prefix (a run whose record is gone). A drill without a
   batch stamp joins the run that names it (by id prefix, the longest
   matching run id). Drill day groups are keyed `day-drills:<date>`.
3. **Test** iff the session's tenant stamp is `test`, or, for an unstamped
   pre-tenancy session, its id-derived tags include `test` (`claude-e2e-*` /
   `codex-e2e-*` / `replay-e2e-*` / legacy `e2e-*`; event-source
   `sessionTags`). The tenant stamp (`SessionRef.tenant`, from
   `MANDU_TENANT` / `x-mandu-tenant`, the harness or a tenanted arbiter;
   policy-surface.md §2.7) is what moves launcher-driven tests into
   Tests. A `live` stamp normally strips the test tag (`registry.ts
   tenantedTags`), except for a **harness fragment**: a session with no
   conversation and no launch, only side traffic (a U-LLM inspection, net
   events) that a test run sent to the live arbiter. It files with the tests.
4. Everything else is a **Session**. Logs that are not sessions (the
   arbiter's admin audit log `arbiter-admin`, the net-guard fallback id
   `net-guard`, net-proxy's minted `eg_<a>_<b>`) sit in one **System logs**
   group last (`SYSTEM_LOGS_BATCH_ID`), each labeled by what it holds; opened,
   each reads as a log (§4.33 "A system log").

Each section is batched independently, so a loose test session never lands
between live batches; the test side's day groups are re-keyed
`day-testing:<date>` so batch ids stay unique. The client defers to the
server: a session in the drills section (`S.drillIds`) or carrying
`watch.scenario` is never treated as test traffic for its row name, the §4.11
banner or the delete wording (`isTestRef`).

**Row labels come from the conversation or the launch, never from data.** No
model call → the launcher's posture line, else `U-LLM inspection of <symbol>`,
else no label (the row shows its id); before this rule, the first event with
any input named the row, which could be the first line of a `.env`.
OpenClaw's wall-clock envelope (`[Sun 2026-09-27 07:45 GMT+9] …`) is stripped
from the prompt, and the prompt is read from OpenClaw's last envelope on, the
way the prompt filter places the human's text (anthropic-proxy
`prompt-filter.ts` `openclawPieces`): the header OpenClaw puts before it on a
Gateway channel's turn (2026.7's `Sender (untrusted metadata):`, 2026.9's
`Conversation info: ⟦openclaw:ctx⟧`, each with a JSON fence) is not the
prompt. A marked header with no envelope is skipped with its fence, and
2026.9's `<<<BEGIN_OPENCLAW_INTERNAL_CONTEXT>>>` block is dropped wherever it
sits (found 2026-10-09: an OpenClaw 2026.9 row read "Conversation info:
⟦openclaw:ctx⟧"). Pinned over the real server by
`test/component/live-section-names.test.ts`. The row carries where its label
came from (`SessionRef.labelFrom`: `prompt`, `posture`, `inspection`,
`system`). The product pages (Home's agent rows, the session page's title)
show only a `prompt` label (`view-model/home.ts` `promptLabel`): a posture
line ("claude launch: 7 rung(s) live […]") describes the launch to a
developer and told a person nothing (found 2026-10-05 on a live tour), so a
session with no prompt reads "No prompt yet" while running and "No prompt
reached the AI" under Earlier, and its page has no title line
(`test/component/home-first-session.test.ts`).

**One group at a time, chosen by the page.** The groups are not stacked and
the sidebar has no filter of its own (an earlier All / Live / E2E bar is
retired). Each session page lists one group (§4.32; a "which sessions"
switch in the top bar did this before the pages):

- **Sessions** lists `live`; **Drills** lists `replay` or `drills` (a
  **Replay | Live** switch in the sidebar, `mandu.drills.kind`); these are
  groups of one store, so moving between them re-lists with no reload and
  returns to the session last shown on that page (`S.lastOfGroup`), else the
  newest; a page whose group is empty selects nothing.
- **Tests** is the test tenant's store when one exists: entering it sets the
  `mandu_tenant` cookie and reloads, leaving it deletes the cookie and
  reloads (§4.32, §6.y), and the chrome tints. With no test tenant it lists
  the live store's test-tagged group without a reload.

A session named by the link (`/dev/sessions/<id>`, §4.25v) or opened from
elsewhere moves to its group's page (app.js `followSessionPage`: a drill id
under `/dev/sessions/` moves to `/dev/drills/<id>`, a test id to
`/dev/tests/<id>`). Test-tagged
sessions left in the live store although a test tenant exists end the
Sessions view with a remainder note, "N test sessions in the live store ·
show them" (`.side-remainder-note`, `paintLeftoverTestsNote`; persisted under
the historical key `mandu.simpleShowTests`).

Tests: `session-batches.test.ts` (each section, an arbiter id with a `/` that
is not a replay drill), `ui/app-js-sidebar.test.ts` (labels, empty notes,
replay rows and badges, record text as text), `ui/app-js-delete.test.ts`,
`ui/app-js-register-retired.test.ts`, `ui/css-inspector-contract.test.ts`
(the stylesheet hides no sidebar group; which group lists is app.js's call).

#### 4.10.3 Test-run results

**Parsing.** The `TestRunner` (§4.8, Tests › Run a suite) parses
streamed stdout into per-case results, live:

- **TAP** (`node --test` on a non-TTY pipe): unindented `ok N - title` /
  `not ok N - title` lines and `# SKIP <reason>` (kept as `skipReason`). The
  harnesses title every test `<class>[<scenario>]: …`, which yields the
  `{ cls, scenario }` join key; the class alternation is built from the
  registry's `TEST_SESSION_CLASSES`, never a hand copy.
- **test-all.sh rows**: a `▶ <label>` header and its `✓ PASS` / `✗ FAIL` line
  become a per-package result (the end-of-run summary deliberately does not
  match, so nothing double-counts).
- An entry whose output parses into no case (cargo, a shell suite) gets one
  result from its exit.

**The suite manifest.** The runner offers every entry of `tests/suites.mjs`,
grouped by kind (test-organization.md §5). `src/test-runs/suite-manifest.ts`
reads it through `node scripts/suites.mjs list --json --unsharded --platform
<platform>` in a child process, cached until a manifest file changes or a
minute passes. `GET /api/test` adds `groups` (entries by kind, with axis, cwd,
command, needs, timeout, flags and session class) and `manifest`
(`{ available }`, or why not). `POST /api/test {suite}` takes a `SUITE_ID_RE`
id:

- **an entry id** runs exactly what the manifest declares (never a shell
  string): its `cmd` in its `cwd`, with run-suites' fixed env
  (`MANDU_AXES_STRICT=1`, the no-policy `MANDU_POLICY_FILE`) plus the entry's
  `env` (a gated drill runs with its gate). An entry declaring a `session`
  also gets `MANDU_TEST_DASHBOARD=1`; a drill entry gets `--store <the
  dashboard's watch store>` (as run-suites' `withWatchStore` does) unless it
  names its own `--store` / `--out`, so its record appears in Live drills. Its
  `timeout` is enforced (the timeout report, SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after the
  grace; the run ends `failed`). Its output is kept as that entry's log,
  `<results>/<runId>/logs/<entry>.log` (§4.35, "Each entry's log").
- **`kind:<k>`** runs `scripts/test-all.sh --kind <k>` for the per-push kinds
  (unit, component, stack, replay-drill, sandbox); other kinds need a vendor
  login, an Ollama or VMs, and a `frozen` entry needs the frozen axis, so they
  run entry by entry. It passes `--out <results>/<runId> --run-id <runId>`, so
  run-suites keeps `summary.json`, `junit.xml` and `logs/` under the run's id
  (`defaultTestResultsDir`, the path table's `test-run-results`, mode 0700);
  that summary attributes the run to its suites in ◫ Coverage (§4.29). The
  runner removes the directory of a run its history drops.
- **`e2e`** is a batch: the suite file of every entry that declares a
  `session`, runs in `tests/` and has no `gate` (replay-, claude-, codex-,
  openclaw-, opencode-e2e), in one process. Docker mode runs this batch only,
  in the maintainers' e2e rig; a tree without the rig (the public one)
  answers 412 before any `docker` command (docker-e2e.md §2).
- **`all`** is `scripts/test-all.sh` with its default kinds, results kept as
  for `kind:<k>`.

The session class and label come from the entry's `session: { cls, file,
label }` (`scripts/suites.mjs check` validates it). `test-setup.ts
SUITE_LABELS` and `TEST_SESSION_CLASSES` remain built-in copies for the
synchronous banner and id parser, and `suite-manifest.test.ts` fails when
either differs from the manifest. The npm-published bundle (packaging.md §5)
ships no `tests/` or `scripts/`: the loader answers `available: false` ("the
suite list needs a source checkout") and the picker is disabled with that
reason.

**Process groups.** A run is rarely one process (`npm` → `tsx` → `node`;
`test-all.sh` forks each suite; a shell suite may background a helper). Every
run is spawned `detached` and every kill addresses the group (`kill(-pgid)`).
Cancel and the entry timeout SIGTERM the group and arm one SIGKILL after
`stopGraceMs` (4 s) that stays armed past the leader's exit. A normal finish
reaps too: if the group still has members when the leader exits, they get the
same SIGTERM + SIGKILL; an empty group disarms the timer, so a recycled pgid
is never signalled. Dashboard shutdown awaits `TestRunner.shutdown()`: SIGTERM,
wait up to `shutdownGraceMs` (2 s) for the group to empty, SIGKILL, wait at
most 1 s more (the armed SIGKILL is an unref'd timer, which the exiting
process would never fire). Docker mode signals the `docker run` CLI and still
removes the container.

**The timeout report.** Before the timeout's SIGTERM the runner reads the
run's process group off `/proc` and writes into the run's log (stderr, so it
is never parsed as a result): every process under the run as a tree (pid, age,
argv), `still running: <file>` (node's runner spawns one child per test file;
a cargo test binary is named by its crate), and any TAP subtest opened and
never closed. The run's `reason` (`timed out after Ns; still running: <file>`,
at most three names) is carried by `GET /api/test` and the history and shown
under the run's row. A report that cannot be built logs why and never delays
the kill. The logic is `scripts/lib/timeout-report.mjs`, of which
the developer view's `timeout-report.mjs` is a byte-identical copy (the
dashboard ships standalone; `scripts/test/run-suites.test.mjs` fails on
drift). A command-line argument (one with whitespace, such as `bash -c
"… x.test.ts"`) is never named as a file.

**A docker-mode run's report** (2026-10-17, the developer view's
`docker-timeout-report.ts`) is the container's, not the `docker run` client's,
which is all the run's own process group holds: the container's processes are
the docker daemon's shim's children. At the timeout, before the kill removes
the container, the runner asks `docker inspect` for the init's host pid of the
container it named (`--name mandu-e2e-<runId>`) and walks the tree from there
in the host's `/proc` (the container runs as the dashboard's uid, so argv and
cwd are readable), or, when this `/proc` does not show it (rootless or remote
docker), through `docker top <name> -eo pid,ppid,pgid,etimes,args`. The same
process list and `still running` summary follow, paths under the container's
source (`/host-repo`, else `/repo`) shown repo-relative. A container already
gone or invisible gives the client's report, said to be only that. No root is
needed. The e2e batch, docker mode's only suite, has a timeout for this to
fire at: the sum of its entries' timeouts, plus 300 s in docker mode for the
container's own stack to boot (it had none).

Tests: `test-runner-process-groups.test.ts` (a real grandchild checked gone
after cancel, timeout and a normal finish; the SIGTERM-ignoring fixture
asserts its `SIG_IGN` before acting, so no SIGKILL test passes vacuously),
`test-runner-suites.test.ts`, `component/manifest-runner.test.ts` (cancel, a
hung file's timeout, `server.close()`, over a real server),
`docker-timeout-report.test.ts` (the container's report through `/proc`,
through `docker top` and its fallback, and a docker-mode run timing out end to
end, with a stub docker CLI).

**History.** Terminal runs land in a history (newest first, capped at 50)
persisted best-effort to `test-runs.json` in the Mandu home
(`defaultTestHistoryPath`, the path table's `test-runs`, on-disk-layout.md §5),
so results survive dashboard restarts and host reboots like the sessions they
annotate. `GET /api/test` returns `runs` (the in-flight run with its results
so far, plus the history). Parsing and persistence are observability only and
never affect a run's exit state. A stored row of the retired whole-tier run
(`tier:<t>`) is kept as stored (`STORED_SUITE_ID_RE`), read as `<t> tier (now
<its kinds>)`, and never started again (`test-runner-history.test.ts`).

**The join.** Since the runner stamps `MANDU_BATCH_ID=<runId>`, **a test batch
is one test run**: `buildSidebarSections` joins `batch.id === run.runId`,
attaching a `BatchRunSummary` (`state` + pass/fail/skip counts) to the batch,
retitling it with the run's label, and giving each member a per-scenario
`testResult` (the result whose `{cls, scenario}` matches the session id
`<class>-<scenario>-<ts>`, `parseTestSessionId`). Rows in a test batch sort by
their badge number (`compareTestRows`: E2 < E10; unnumbered trail), while the
Sessions side keeps newest-first. Each test batch also tallies its members'
verdicts (`testResult ?? checksVerdict`) into `SessionBatch.marks`
(`tallyMarks`), so a standalone `npm test` batch with no run record still
shows a tally; a batch with no verdicts carries none.

**Marks without a run record.** A session's own `assertion` event yields
`SessionRef.checksVerdict` (`"fail"` iff any BLOCKING check fails; warn/skip
don't, matching §4.13) via the pure `event-source.ts assertionVerdicts`, and
`SessionRef.checksFailed` (which groups broke, aspect-refined,
blocking-first, for the F badge's tooltip). The same derivation yields
`SessionRef.historyFidelity`, the verdict over just the `HISTORY_FIDELITY_ASSERTS`
subset (claude-e2e's "dashboard render ≡ Claude Code's own transcript" oracle,
§4.13; key sync pinned by `tests/stack/claude-history.test.ts`). It has no
sidebar badge of its own (a fidelity failure already fails the session) but
stays on the API (`assertion-verdicts.test.ts`).

#### 4.10.4 Rows and batch headers

- **P/R/F status badge** on every row and batch header, from the
  server-computed `SessionRef.status` / `SessionBatch.status`: `P` green =
  passed, `R` pulsing yellow = running, `F` red = failed, a skipped scenario a
  muted `−`, nothing known → no badge. A member of a still-running run, or a
  verdict-less session whose last event is within `RUNNING_WINDOW_MS` (5 min)
  of the injected `nowMs`, is `R`: a live agent just stops emitting, so
  recency is the "still going" signal when nothing else says. A batch takes
  its joined run's state, else rolls up its members (running > fail > pass).
  An older server without `status` gets a client fallback from
  `testResult ?? checksVerdict` (`effectiveStatus`; `R` is only ever
  server-derived).
- **A recorded exit ends `R`** (2026-10-06). `SessionRef.exited` is the
  product pages' rule (view-model/session-exit.ts `sessionExited`: the
  launcher's `session_exit` with no model call or tool step after it), set
  by the sources that already read the session's events (file, arbiter, and
  the CI-live row builder the own-arbiter source shares; `withExited`).
  `sessionStatus` skips the recency rule for an exited session, so the row
  and its group lose `R` the moment the agent exits, and the row's clock
  shows how long it ran ("09:30 · 9m 7s"). Before, for five
  minutes after an exit the row pulsed `R` and its clock counted on ("10m 29s
  so far (still running)" for a session that ran 9m 7s), while Home and the
  session page on the same server said it had ended. Activity after an exit
  (a resumed session on the same log) is running again. A verdict and a
  joined run still executing come first, as before. A row the arbiter source
  keeps from an older derivation while a session's replay fails never keeps
  `exited`: the log grew since, so the exit may be stale, and the recency
  rule decides. Recorded drill sessions carry no exit fact and keep the
  recency rule. Tests: `session-exit.test.ts`, `session-batches.test.ts`,
  `file-source-cache.test.ts`, `ci-live-source.test.ts`,
  `arbiter-source-sessions.test.ts`, and `session-list-exited.test.ts` (the
  served list and inspector over the tour record, moved to end a minute
  ago).
- **Run tally** on a test batch header: `10✓ 2✗ 1−` (`tallyHtml`; pass
  first, so the fail count sits in the same place on every row; counts are
  colored by meaning, not by the badge's tint), falling back to the `marks`
  tally (`marksBadgeHtml`).
- **Agent badge** on every row (`claude` / `codex` …, `SessionRef.agent`,
  `event-source.ts deriveAgentKind`: the model-proxy emitter, outranked by a
  `launch_posture.target` naming OpenClaw or OpenCode, which ride the
  anthropic-proxy; with no proxy event the launcher's target is the fallback).
  No evidence → no badge rather than a guess. §4.11 repeats it as a row.
- **Start and elapsed time**: a row shows its local start clock and runtime
  (`14:32 · 3m 12s`, `transcript.ts clockLabel` / `elapsedLabel`); a batch
  header the day and the batch runtime (`Today · 3m 12s`, `batchTime`,
  preferring the joined run's `since` / `finishedAt`). A running row ticks
  against now. Day groups show no time (the title is the date, and a day is
  not a run).
- **Runtime chip**: `SessionBatch.runtime` = the joined run's runtime, else the
  members' uniform `SessionRef.runtime` (`batchRuntime`): 🐳 docker / host;
  mixed or unknown members badge nothing.
- **Origin chip**: `SessionBatch.origin` = the members' uniform origin tag
  (`batchOrigin`); only `ci` renders (a `CI` chip). Origin (who) is orthogonal
  to runtime (where), so a CI batch would show both. The current CI
  (continuous-integration.md §6) never writes its sessions into the live event
  store, so nothing sets `origin: "ci"` today; CI results are the ⚑ CI tab
  (§4.27). The chip code stays.
- **A batch heading keeps its name** (2026-10-19). The heading was one
  row where only the title could shrink, and every chip beside it kept its
  width. At the default 260 px list a CI batch ("claude e2e run" with `P`,
  `CI`, `🐳 docker`, `2✓`, `2` and "Jul 16 · 1m 25s") needs 285 px in a
  234 px box, so headless Chromium drew its title 0 px wide, cut the time
  after "Jul 16", and the 🗑 sat over what was left. Every CI batch read as
  the same row of chips. Now the heading is two groups on a wrapping row:
  the name (caret, status, title) and the rest (chips, count, time). When
  both do not fit, the rest moves to a line of its own under the name,
  pinned right; when it is too wide even for that line, the time goes
  under the chips. A long name alone on its line ends in an ellipsis
  there. A heading that fits stays one line, as before. A heading with a
  time and a 🗑 keeps the 🗑's width free at its right, so the 🗑 never
  covers the time. Clicks and the keyboard focus stay on the heading.
  Drill groups and day groups, which have no time, are unchanged. Tests:
  `app-js-sidebar.test.ts` and the inspector's stack test
  `batch-head-room` (a real Chromium at 761 and 1280 px windows and a
  600 px list).

The sessions poll's change signature includes run state, counts and statuses
(plus a ~15 s time bucket while anything runs), so a finishing run re-renders
without disrupting an interacting user. Tests: `ui/app-js-sidebar.test.ts`
(badges, aria, chips), `session-batches.test.ts` (status, marks, runtime and
origin derivations), `agent-kind.test.ts`.

#### 4.10.5 Deleting sessions

Any session or whole batch is deletable from a 🗑 on the row or batch header,
revealed on hover or on a keyboard focus (`.s-del` / `.batch-del`, `app.js
deleteSessions`; §4.32 *The session list works from the keyboard*):

- `DELETE /api/session?session=<id>` accepts any session id. What protects
  live traces is the standard mutating-route gates (the fail-closed
  source-IP allowlist §6, the cookie session `isAuthed`, the
  `X-Mandu-Control` CSRF header) and a client confirm whose wording flags a
  live session as "a real agent trace, not a test". The arbiter store's
  safe-session-id guard still rejects traversal-shaped ids.
- **Observability only**: it removes the session's NDJSON event log and its
  per-session in-memory state (watchers, the arbiter's seq and coalescer
  state, subscribe streams). The symbol table, policy and approval queue are
  untouched; so is `test-runs.json` (a batch disappears once its members do).
- **Capability-gated**: `GET /api/sessions` advertises `canDelete` (the
  EventSource implements `deleteSession`); a delete against a source without
  it answers 501.
- Batch delete loops the per-session API; partial failures collapse into one
  alert; the sidebar re-fetches and re-selects if needed.

#### 4.10.6 The local-model drill

The local-model drill (`tests/env/local-model.test.ts`; e2e-catalog.md §2e) runs
the real launcher around a real `claude -p` with a file labeled `local-model`,
a `models:` entry naming the host's Ollama, and recording relays in front of
Anthropic and the Ollama. It is the session class `local-model-e2e`: its
private arbiter and the launcher it drives are both the test tenant, its ids
are `local-model-e2e-<leg>-<ms>` and its titles `local-model-e2e[<leg>]: …`,
so its sessions file under Tests, badge **LM1** (`local-model`) / **LM2**
(`any-model`), say `claude`, and join a run's results like any suite (it
forwards `MANDU_BATCH_ID`).

It is its own manifest entry, `integration.local-model` (and
`integration.local-main-model` for `local-main-model-e2e`), not part of `e2e`:
it costs two subscription sessions, needs an Ollama with the model and is
host-only (the docker rig cannot reach the host's loopback Ollama). It runs
with its gate `MANDU_LIVE_LOCAL_MODEL=1`, which the §4.11 repro line carries
(`SuiteMeta.gateEnv`); a missing prerequisite is a TAP `# SKIP` whose reason
the history row shows. Its legs are `const` objects listed in `const
SCENARIOS: LegSpec[]`, which `extractSuiteSpec` resolves for the spec browser.
It has no 🎬 watch scenario (§4.22): a watch run uses the shared arbiter under
the user's own policy, while this drill needs a label and a `models:` entry
in force that a harness must not write, and its claim is about the vendor
wire, which only its recording relays observe. Tests:
`component/local-model-suite.test.ts`, `test-runs/test-runner-suites.test.ts`,
`test-runs/test-specs.test.ts`, `ui/app-js-suite-classes.test.ts` (app.js's
class lists track the registry).

#### 4.10.7 The browser drill (2026-10-18; a Drills run since 2026-10-19)

The browser drill (the drill suite's browser-jev, `integration.browser-jev`;
devtools-relay.md §7) runs the real jev-ultrafast in a real Chromium behind
the DevTools relay, on TypeSafe and OpenRouter, one task per drill. It is a
drill (a real agent on live models), so since 2026-10-19 a run of it is a
**live drill run**, listed on the Drills page (§4.22) like the catalog
runner's, not under Tests: the run writes the same record (`meta.json`,
`chapters.json`, `report.json`) into the live drill store
(`runs/drills/live/watch-<stamp>/`, or `MANDU_DRILL_STORE`), with its target
`jev`, one chapter and one report row per drill (the task's goal is its one
turn, the drill's checks that turn's checks, PASS only when all pass).

The run brings one arbiter (the test tenant, its own law: each drill's
workspace `.env` bound to the deploy host's pages; the person's policy is
never written) whose work dir is `<run>/arbiter`, so its events stay with
the record and the own-arbiter source (§4.22) lists each drill's session
(`<runId>-<drill>`) as a row of the run's batch, with the relay's
`browser_action` trace, the egress proxy's events and the drill's
`assertion` event. Where a terminal drill names its asciicast, a browser
drill names its **video** (`browser-<drill>.mp4`): the drill records Chrome
through its own DevTools connection (not the agent's, which the relay
refuses pixels) while the task runs, and ffmpeg makes an H.264 MP4 on the
frames' own clock. The player mounts a `<video>` in the asciicast player's
place, with the same seek, play and pause, so the checks table's jumps work
on it; a video that is gone is RECORD LOST, a signed-out viewer gets the
sign-in note. The run-file route streams the video with byte ranges (206,
416 past the end) and only to an admin session, as every run file: the video
is the HumanView, the pages as a person sees them, so a secret on a page is
in it (the drill's secrets are made up). Without ffmpeg the run has no video
and says so.

**The browser demos' two sides** (2026-10-19, the drill suite's
`browser-demos`, drill-runner.md §3.13): one run holds each demo twice, a
chapter per side with the demo as its `scenarioId`: without Mandu (setting
`baseline-none`, its session in the run's arbiter holds only the drill's
`assertion` event, so it lists by its checks alone) and with Mandu
(`secrets`). Both chapters name `sides`, the demo's two sides in one video
(`browser-<demo>-sides.mp4`, the run-file route's `browser-*.mp4` names).
Above a side's video the panel shows a bar (`drills.js sidesBar`): each side
in words ("Without Mandu", "With Mandu", any other baseline as "Under
<setting>") with its verdict, the one shown marked, the other a button to
its session, and **▶ side by side**, which mounts the two-in-one video in the
player's place (the shown side's button mounts its own again). The Files
list of a side keeps that video beside the side's own. A side without Mandu
that leaked is FAIL, as a baseline run's is (its FAIL is that setting's), so
the run reads failed in the sidebar with `at baseline-none` beside its ids.
The run's `meta.suite` (`browser-demos`, kept when it is a suite's name)
names the file the re-run line runs, with the demo's id as the test name
pattern. The demos are not catalog drills, so Drills › Comparison (§4.32b)
lists them in a section of their own under its battery grid (since
2026-10-19): each demo's latest take without and with Mandu, linked to its
session and to this two-in-one video.

From 2026-10-18 to 2026-10-19 the drill's sessions were a Tests class,
`browser-jev-e2e` (BJ1-BJ4), written into the dashboard arbiter's store when
the dashboard started the run; a run from a terminal wrote them into the
live store instead, where the Tests view never looked. The class and its
badges stay so those sessions still read as they were; the event-store
override that put them there is gone. It is manual: it spends the
maintainer's keys. Tests: the drill suite's `browser-drill-record.test.ts`
(the record's shapes, where it goes, the frame list, a real Chromium
recorded into an MP4) and `browser-demo-sites.test.ts` (the demos' sites,
the two-sided record, the two-in-one video), the inspector's own (the run as
a Drills batch, a demo run's two sides and their video over a real server,
the video route's ranges and gate, the player's `<video>`, the sides bar).

**The browser agent's badge (2026-10-19).** A browser agent is a program
the launcher starts as `--target shell` behind the relay, so it is no
supported agent and its rows had no agent badge. `SessionRef.browserAgent`
names it (`registry.ts` `deriveBrowserAgent`): `jev` for the
`browser-jev-e2e` class, the run's own target (`jev`, `browser-use`) for a
browser drill run's sessions (`own-arbiter-source.ts` `runBrowserAgent`),
else `browser` for any session whose launch posture lists `cdp-relay` live.
The inspector's sidebar shows it where the agent badge goes, in one colour
of its own (`.s-agent-browser`), and the session's facts list it as its
agent; only those three names are badged. Tests: `agent-kind.test.ts` (the
derivation, a file source's row), `own-arbiter-source.test.ts` (a run's
target), `app-js-sidebar.test.ts` (the badge, an unknown name unbadged).

### 4.11 Test-setup banner — how this test ran, and how to re-run it

Opening an e2e test session shows a **setup banner** in its Checks tab
(§4.33; it sat at the top of the main frame before the tabs; `#fixture-banner`,
`app.js renderTestSetup`), so the session describes itself. It is a native `<details>`, folded by default: the `<summary>` is the
one-line header (scenario + test number, the live/offline suite chip, the
✓/✗ result, the 📖 spec and ✂⛶ path buttons, which act without toggling the
fold), and an unfolded state survives SSE-driven re-renders.

The facts are server-computed by the pure `src/test-runs/test-setup.ts
buildTestSetup` and shipped as `/api/events`' optional `testSetup`:

- **scenario / cls / testNumber**, parsed from the session id
  (`parseTestSessionId` + the per-class badge registry, §4.10).
- **suiteKind + suiteLabel**: `live` (a real agent, e.g. claude-e2e's real
  `claude -p`, codex-e2e's real `codex exec`) vs `offline` (replay-e2e:
  canned-transcript replay, no model).
- **models** (distinct model ids on the session's model-call events) and
  **emitters** (which chokepoints participated).
- **command**: the copy-paste line that re-runs this one scenario
  (`reproCommand`): the test-runner's argv narrowed with
  `--test-name-pattern '<class>\[<scenario>\]'`, prefixed with
  `MANDU_TEST_DASHBOARD=1`, the entry's gate (`SuiteMeta.gateEnv`) and, when
  the server knows it (`DashboardServerOptions.testContext`), the
  `MANDU_ARBITER_SOCK` so the re-run lands in the same dashboard.
- **cwd / agentViewRoot / humanViewRoot** (`src/session-paths.ts`), derived
  only from what the session recorded; a missing value is `null` and renders
  "not recorded", never a guess from the dashboard's environment. `cwd` is
  parsed by `sessionCwd` from the agent's own system-prompt environment block
  (`source:"agent"` blocks only, so a poisoned `tool_result` cannot forge
  it). The view roots (`sessionViewRoots`) are the deepest common ancestors
  of the AgentView-side / HumanView-side paths on `fs_action` redirects and
  typed `path_rewrite` fields; a context-layer-only run records neither.
  `humanViewRoot` is by construction the workspace root `/api/git` and
  `/api/fs` resolve (`workspaceRootForSession` calls the same function), so
  the banner and the ⎇ Git/Files view never disagree.
- **seedFiles**: the files the harness prepared, with raw content
  (`sessionSeedFiles` over the `workspace_seed` event the harness emits right
  after seeding, `buildSeedEvent` in `tests/lib/assertions.ts`), so the
  initial disk state is event-sourced even for scenarios whose workspace is
  deleted at teardown. Its end-of-run twin is `workspace_final` (§4.12).
  Rows are collapsed `<details>` (path, size, a ☣ `poisoned` badge) and, for
  CONF-* runs, a label badge (🔒 strict, 🤖 model-ok, 🔓 public) from the
  arbiter's recorded label after the scenario's `arrange`. The raw content is
  a HumanView fact with `DualRepr.original`'s privilege posture: the event
  store is a human-facing surface and never re-enters T-LLM context.

**Path display, session-wide.** Recorded roots are deep on purpose (the
production `ViewLayout`), so they display short by default: the shared
ancestor collapsed to its last segment, deep middles to `…`, the full path in
the hover title. `/api/events` ships the recorded roots for every session
(`sessionPaths`), and `app.js escFold` folds any known root wherever the trace
renders text (dual-lane previews, the path-rewrite band, the symbol table's
Origin column, the U-LLM card, the lineage origin) as a `.path-fold` span.
Raw-data reveal surfaces (revealed symbol values, the egress queue's request
text, the Files tab's contents) are deliberately not folded. The banner's
⛶/✂ `.fx-path-btn` flips the persisted mode (`mandu.pathMode`) for the whole
session; nothing on disk or in events changes. Paths of four segments or fewer
never fold.

The client adds the session's **label** (the task prompt) and its
**testResult** chip (§4.10). The **📖 spec** button dispatches `mandu:show-spec
{cls, scenario}`; control.js opens the Tests tab's spec browser (§4.8) at that
scenario's row, so "what was this test supposed to do" is one click from what
it did. Legacy class-less `e2e-*` sessions get a minimal banner (no command,
no spec); normal sessions show nothing. Observability only, fail-soft
throughout. Tests: `test-runs/test-setup.test.ts`, `ui/app-js-test-banner.test.ts`.

### 4.12 Files snapshot — the per-session dual-view FS view (`GET /api/fs`)

The ⎇ Git/Files view is the session's **Files** tab (§4.33; `#git-fold`, an
inline foldable panel below the trace before the tabs; the body renders when
the tab shows). The line under its heading carries the dual-view commit
count, or the server's reason when there is none (`updateGitFoldSummary`).
It has two tabs, a strip named "Files" that the arrow keys work
(tabs.js, §4.32 *The Files strip is a tab strip*): **Commits** (§4.2's
commit list + diff pane, `GET /api/git`)
and **Both views** ("🗂 Files" before §4.33), a per-session
**filesystem snapshot** shown as two explorers side by side: the AgentView
root (left, green head) and the HumanView root (right, red head). Each lists
its own view's final tree, and a click opens that view's content: **AgentView
(repo: Agent File System) = the symbolized spelling** the T-LLM (privileged
LLM) side sees, **HumanView = the original bytes** of the user's workspace. The
same file in the two explorers shows the wall: a `$MDU:*` symbol on the left,
the original on the right.

**Commits are scoped to the session.** The substrate repo is per workspace, so
a reused workspace's log holds every session's commits. fs-sync stamps each
agent commit `run=<sessionId>`, and `/api/git` marks each commit `thisSession`
(`markSessionCommits`; the seed `run=none` and `[MDU-HUMAN]` commits belong to
no session). A scope bar, **this session · N | whole workspace · M**, opens on
the session's own commits when it wrote any, else on the whole log with a
note; in the whole log other sessions' commits dim.

**On a phone the list sits above the changes (2026-10-14).** Commits is the
commit list (`#git-commit-list`, 320 px, its box at most 70vh high) beside
the picked commit's changes (`#git-detail`). Until 2026-10-14 nothing changed
that at a phone's width, and a session with no commits kept the empty list's
320 px. A headless Chromium at 390 px, on a real session with four dual-view
commits (real fs-sync, proxy and dashboard), measured the changes 0 px wide:
a picked commit's hash, trust badge and diff spilled past the card, a word
per line. A session with no commits drew its "No dual-view commits for this
session" note 34 px wide, ending past the screen; at 1280 px the note sat
right of a blank column. Now:

- **A session with no commits draws no list** (`renderGitView` sets the
  list `hidden`, which mandu.css's `[hidden]` rule makes take no room). The
  note starts at the panel's edge at every width. A session read anew shows
  or hides the list by its own commits.
- **At ≤ 760 px** (the developer view's one phone breakpoint, §4.1) the
  Commits panel is a column: the list across the card, its box at most
  40vh high so the changes start close by, then the changes across the
  card, a long diff line scrolling inside its box (`.git-detail pre`). At
  390 px the changes are 328 px wide.
- A desktop with commits is unchanged (measured the same: a 320 px list
  beside 612 px of changes at 1280 px). **Both views** keeps its two trees
  side by side at every width (157 px each at 390 px, which reads).

Presentation only: no route, server text or value changed; the rows, the
scope bar and their keys are as before. Tests: `app-js-files-layout.test.ts`
(jsdom, app.js with the served styles applied at 390 and 1280 px through
`stylesAt`, which unwraps the `@media` blocks that hold at a width, since
jsdom applies no width query: no commits hides the list and it takes no
room; commits show it; none → two → none across session reads; the phone's
column and the desktop's row; Both views keeps its row) and stack
`inspector-files-tabs.test.ts` F4 (real fs-sync commits and a second
