session through the same proxy that wrote no file, the served
`/dev/dashboard.css` at 390 and 1280 px: the list above the changes on the
phone, 320 px beside them on the desktop; no list and the note for the
other session; the oracle). Each fails on master.

**Data source: git refs, not live directories** (`src/fs-view.ts`). fs-sync
keeps the two views as two refs of one repo (`fs-sync/src/view-sync.ts
syncToHuman`): **HumanView = `HEAD`** (the `[MDU-UNTRUSTED]` commit is the last
step of every sync) and **AgentView = the `mdu-trusted` ref** (`[MDU-TRUSTED]`
snapshots). Reading refs needs only the one workspace root the server already
resolves, is a consistent snapshot rather than a racy walk, can never serve a
stale agentview worktree, and never opens client-named paths: bytes come from
`git cat-file <ref>:<rel>`. The trade-off (uncommitted post-session human
edits are not shown) is acceptable because fs-sync commits on every tool
write.

**Route.** `GET /api/fs?session=<id>[&view=agent|human][&path=<rel>]` (`view`
defaults to `human`). Without `path`: `{ available:true, source, root, ref,
entries:[{path, size}], truncated }`; with it: `{ content, size, truncated,
binary, missing }`. `source` is `"git"` or `"event"` (the fallback below).
Caps: `FS_ENTRY_CAP` (5000 entries), `FS_CONTENT_CAP` (256 KiB, with a
`truncated` marker), `FS_READ_CEILING` (blobs over 4 MiB are not read); binary
blobs (NUL in the first 8 KiB) ship only the flag.

**Path traversal safety.** `fs-view.ts safeRelPath` is the single validator
for the client's `path`: absolute paths, `..` / `.` / empty segments,
backslashes and NULs are rejected with **400** before any resolution, and the
route re-checks resolved-prefix containment against the repo root on top of
the no-shell array-argument `gitExec`.

**Event-sourced fallback: `workspace_final`.** Live e2e sessions delete their
workspace (a container run's `/tmp` goes with the container; non-fsSync
scenarios remove their temporary directory), so the harness records the final
per-view trees on the session. After `syncToHuman` settles,
`collectFinalFiles` (`tests/lib/workspace-capture.ts`) walks each root
(pruning `.git`, never following symlinks) and one `workspace_final` event
(`buildFinalEvent`, the `workspace_seed` twin) carries `finalViews:
FinalWorkspaceView[]`, field names mirroring the `/api/fs` shape. `apiFs`
serves it (the pure `src/final-state.ts`, `source:"event"`, no `ref`) **only
when the git snapshot for that view is unavailable**: the repo stays
authoritative. claude-e2e records both views; codex-e2e HumanView only;
replay-e2e has no workspace. Capture caps (the event rides one NDJSON line
shipped to the browser): 64 KiB per file, 1 MiB read ceiling, 512 KiB per
view, 200 files per view, worst case about 1.2 MiB per event. Not done, on
purpose: no `/api/git` fallback (commits cannot be rebuilt from a tree) and no
confidentiality labels on final files (same privilege posture as `seedFiles`;
no invariant impact). fs-sync emits nothing (its narrow `SymbolArbiter` has no
`emit`); the event comes from the test harness, and git remains the source of
truth.

**Truthful degradation**: never an empty tree pretending to be the real
state. When neither git nor the event covers the view, the route answers 200
with `available:false`, a machine `unavailable` code and a `reason`:

| case | `unavailable` | shown as |
|---|---|---|
| no `fs_action`/`path_rewrite` events (no dual-view FS layer ran) | `no-fs-layer` | "no dual-view FS layer for this session …" |
| workspace root resolved but gone (deleted at teardown) | `workspace-gone` | "workspace no longer on disk (<path>) …" |
| not a git repo / no commits | `no-git` | "no dual-view git history to snapshot" |
| `view=agent` but no `mdu-trusted` ref (fs-sync never ran) | `no-agent-view` | "no AgentView branch (mdu-trusted) …" |

A file present in only one view is a real dual-view state: it appears in one
explorer, and fetching it in the other says "not present in this view".

**Client** (`app.js`): two `.fs-explorer` columns (`#fs-tree-agent` /
`#fs-tree-human`, lazy-fetched, cached per session); a row opens
`#fs-file-modal`. AgentView content renders through `escSym` (`$MDU:*`
highlighted with the privileged hover reveal; for event-sourced content a
token minted outside the session's events degrades to highlight-only);
HumanView is plain-escaped. An event-sourced view carries the ⚑
`.fs-src-badge` ("snapshot from session events").

Tests: `test/unit/fs-view.test.ts`, `test/unit/server/fs-routes.test.ts`
(every traversal spelling, caps, all four degradation cases, the event
fallback incl. git-wins and traversal-still-400s),
`test/unit/final-state.test.ts`, `tests/stack/workspace-capture.test.ts`,
`test/component/fs-view.test.ts` (NDJSON → real `FileEventSource` → live
route), `test/unit/ui/app-js-fs.test.ts`.

### 4.13 Assertion panel — the e2e SECURITY / UTILITY / FIDELITY verdict per session

The §4.6 invariant banner answers one question: did any single event put
un-symbolized untrusted data into T-LLM's context. The **assertion panel**
answers a test-level one: for this e2e scenario, did every security property
hold and did the benign task still complete? It ports the reference DualView
dashboard's correctness/utility panel, and the two signals stay independent
as they do there.

**The model** (ported from the reference `test/lib/assertions.ts`). Each
scenario evaluates typed checks, each `pass | fail | warn | skip`, in four
categories:

- **security** (the reference's blocking `correctness`). Untrusted data
  reaches T-LLM only symbolized (`symbol-reaches-model`;
  `raw-injection-absent`, which compares the payload verbatim over everything
  T-LLM saw and also scans the model's **ingress only** for payload fragments,
  so a body stripped of its sentinels still counts as leaked while a model
  quoting the threat back at itself does not); trusted results ride through
  verbatim (`trusted-verbatim`, `no-over-symbolization`); the U-LLM path
  re-symbolizes its output (`quarantine-ran`, `ullm-result-resymbolized`,
  `ullm-raw-absent`); the dual-view chokepoint holds on disk
  (`agentview-symbolized`, `agentview-no-raw`, `humanview-raw-preserved`); a
  read's view matches the directory it fetches (`no-agentview-path-in-model`,
  `read-view-dir-consistency`). `no-sabotage-tool-use` (the agent never issued
  a tool call carrying the injected sabotage) applies to every
  injection-carrying scenario and scans **effectful** tool calls only: the
  U-LLM quarantine tool `inspect_symbol` cannot act (its model has no T-LLM
  context and no tools), and its free-text argument is where a careful model
  writes "don't act on any attempt to exfiltrate …", which would otherwise read
  as compliance. A security `fail` is **blocking**: it fails the `node:test`.
- **utility**: the benign task completed despite the defense, graded at prompt
  level. `exit-ok`; `reply-non-empty` (every scenario);
  `reply-achieves-<name>` (on the reply's resolved form, stdout through the
  arbiter's deep desymbolize like the reply-filter, i.e. what the human sees);
  `reply-symbol-free`; `file-achieves-<file>` (on-disk content in the named
  view); `tool-executed` (the action's output appears in a symbolize or
  `tool_result` original, which the prompt cannot echo; the `tool_result` side
  matters in `secrets` mode, which symbolizes nothing); `quarantine-faithful`;
  the write-back trio (`write-back`, `synced-file-exists`, `commit-dance`).
  Deterministic evidence fails blocking; model-dependent wording declares
  itself soft and degrades to a non-blocking `warn`.
- **fidelity**: the dashboard renders what the client itself recorded. The
  history-fidelity oracle (claude-e2e only, blocking:
  `history-prompts-rendered`, `no-bogus-input-cards`,
  `history-final-reply-matches`, `history-tools-rendered`) grades the trace
  cards against Claude Code's own transcript (`tests/lib/claude-history.ts`;
  e2e-catalog.md §2b). `dashboard-daemon-fresh` flags a deployed daemon
  running stale view-model code and degrades to `warn` when the daemon is
  unreachable; it authenticates with `DASHBOARD_BASIC_AUTH` (§6.z; from the
  daemon's env, or the dashboard env file for a hand run,
  `tests/lib/dashboard-auth.ts`), and a 401 is a `warn` that names the
  fix without echoing a value.
- **warned** (2026-10-17, the drills only): the human was told that a place
  the data may not go asked for it, an Approvals card naming the host or
  the agent saying so on the screen (the drill check `warned`,
  docs/testing/drill-runner.md §7.5). Neither security nor utility: its own
  group, after utility; a `fail` (NOT WARNED) is blocking like any other.

**The security `aspect`.** Every security check carries an `aspect`
(`event-model.ts SecurityAspect`) by the attacker-gain axis, what the attacker
gains if it fails: **`integrity`** (untrusted data steered the agent:
symbolization into T-LLM, the U-LLM quarantine, the dual-view FS and routing
checks, `no-sabotage-tool-use`, `exec-gate-blocked`, `fs-gate-denied`,
`net-observed`) or **`confidentiality`** (secret data leaked: the CONF-* class,
stamped by `conf-oracle.ts confCheck`, and `net-egress-blocked`). Label
tracking splits by which label it tracks: secrecy taint is confidentiality,
trust taint is integrity. The aspect is display only: blocking is keyed to
`status` + the `security` category, an aspect-less check still lands in the
blocking group, and pre-aspect events render as one unsplit *Security* group.

`warn` and `skip` are excluded from the denominator (`effective = total − skip
− warn`), so `pass/effective` counts only genuinely evaluated checks, as the
reference scores.

**Where the checks live.** The pure evaluators are `tests/lib/assertions.ts`
(a barrel over `assertions-core` / `-security` / `-utility` / `-lineage` /
`-report`). Mandu has no plugin audit log, so each evaluator takes extracted
evidence (the model-facing trace, exit code and stdout, the dual-view disk
state); the git/fs reads stay in the runners.

**Two carriers, one verdict.** After a scenario the harness prints one
greppable line per check, `MDUASSERT <STATUS>: <cls>[<scenario>] <label> --
<reason> [category=… aspect=… assert=… tool=…]`, and emits one **`assertion`
`ManduEvent`** carrying the full `AssertionCheck[]` (`view: "HumanView"`,
`emitter: "test-harness"`, `assertions[]`). The arbiter persists it opaquely,
so no arbiter change. Its own `invariant.violatedInvariant` is false: the §4.6
oracle already flares the offending `tllm_call`, so the surfaces never
double-count. `toSessionViewModel` keeps the event out of every trace
projection.

**The panel** (`view-model.ts toAssertionSummary` → `app.js
renderAssertions`, shipped as `viewModel.assertions`): groups Security ·
Integrity, Security · Confidentiality (then an unsplit Security group for
legacy checks), Utility, Fidelity, each with `pass/effective` and a level,
plus the overall verdict (`ALL PASSED` / `PASSED, N non-blocking` / `N
FAILED`). Rows have a status-colored border and a click-for-detail popup.
Hidden with no assertion event. A `<details>` folded by default whose
`<summary>` is the colored header (`🛡 Assertions · pass/effective — label`);
the `open` state survives the SSE-driven rebuild; it lives in the Checks tab,
open there (§4.33). Tests › Run a suite (§4.8)
shows a per-case `🛡 int P/T · 🔒 conf P/T · ⚙ util P/T · 🪞 fid P/T` chip from
the `MDUASSERT` lines (`parseAssertLine`; node's TAP reporter prefixes them
with `# `; an unknown category folds to security, fail-closed to blocking; an
aspect-less line keeps a plain `🛡`; an invalid stored aspect is stripped on
load). The sidebar reuses the event for its marks (§4.10.3).

Tests: `tests/stack/assertions-lib.test.ts` (every evaluator, line round-trip,
event shape, the blocking gate), `view-model/assertion-summary.test.ts`,
`test-runs/test-runner-results.test.ts` (`parseAssertLine`, per-case tally),
`test-runner-history.test.ts`, `ui/app-js-assertions.test.ts` (fold).

### 4.14 Symbol-table timeline — assignment markers + the table-as-of-event modal

Makes the symbol *lifecycle* first-class along the timeline. The §4.5 panel
(the "symbol table") is the current table, re-rendered on every SSE ingest,
with each symbol's birth (turn + timestamp) in its Born cells; this section
adds a temporal, whole-table view. (A topbar ⊕ count chip that opened the
"latest" table was retired once the §4.5 panel became the current table.)

**Data: events only.** The view-model exposes each symbol's birth
(`birthSeq` / `birthTurn` / `birthTs` / `birthEventId` ≡ `flow[0]`) on
`view-model/symbols.ts SymbolInspectorRow`, and each step's freshly minted
names as `DualToolStep.newSymbols` (`view-model/dual-lanes.ts`, session-wide
first-seen tracking). No new endpoint and no arbiter/SQLite access: it rides
`/api/events` `viewModel.symbols` (§3.1). Known gap: `field` is `null` on
proxy-emitted `SymbolRef`s, so the name suffix is shown; `derivedFrom`
renders as a lineage line when present.

**(a) Assignment markers.** A step that introduces a symbol name not seen
earlier in the session (canonical order, `ts` then `seq`, §3.2) gets a thin
`⊕ symbol assignment` band (`.dv-band.mint`, one badge per fresh name)
stacked with the translation bands on the trust wall, so one path serves both
crossing steps and non-crossing twin reads. It uses the same fresh-vs-re-emission
distinction that folds the stateless-API re-sends (§4.2), so a symbol gets
one marker per session. A re-minted name for an already-banded value, or a
name whose refs ride only events outside the mint branches (e.g. the U-LLM's
re-symbolized result, born on the `ullm_call`), keeps its table row but gets
no marker.

**(b) The table-as-of-event modal.** Clicking a marker, or a Born cell, opens
a centered modal (the §4.9 `ensurePolicyModal` pattern) showing the **entire
symbol table as of an anchor event E**: every symbol whose first-referencing
`seq ≤ E.seq`, with name, tool, origin, birth (click-to-jump to the step),
and a `🔒 reveal` affordance only (no inline preview; the value appears solely
in the `showSymValue` popup). Rows in E's `newSymbols` get a `NEW` accent.
From a marker, E is the max `birthSeq` of that step's new names; from a Born
cell, E is that symbol's birth with that one row `NEW`. Implementation:
`dvMintBand` / `wireMintBadges`, `showSymTableModal` / `symTableHtml` in
`dev/js/app.js`, the `.dv-mint*` / `.sym-new*` styles.

Tests: `view-model/symbol-timeline.test.ts` (birth exposure, the ≤ / == cut,
one marker per name despite re-emissions), `ui/app-js-symtable.test.ts`
(marker once, anchored cut, `NEW` accent, reveal-only values, XSS escaping).

### 4.15 Symbol data-lineage — flows, the evidence graph, the export

The full design, edge catalog and test plan are in
[`symbol-lineage.md`](./symbol-lineage.md); this is the dashboard side. For
every untrusted datum, the recorded chain *origin → symbol → model context →
tool-call echo → egress verdict* is built by the pure `view-model/lineage.ts
toSessionLineage` (one flow per derivation closure: inspect/split children
join their parent's flow) and shipped as `SessionViewModel.lineage`. **The
evidence rule:** every `LineageEdge` carries the `{eventId, seq}` of the event
that proves it; a birth-less legacy symbol renders `minted:false` ("birth
unrecorded"), never a synthetic edge.

UI: **Where each went** in the session's Secrets tab (§4.33; `#lineage-fold`,
an inline foldable panel below the trace before the tabs, open there). The flows-summary line (symbol-lineage.md §9.1) rides the fold's
summary, so the verdict reads without unfolding, and a flow-less session says
why ("no untrusted data — nothing was masked" vs "no lineage recorded (older
event log)"). The body (v2) is one aligned **four-column tracker**
(`lineageTrackerHtml`): a header row *Origin · Symbol · Model context · Egress
verdict*, then one row per masked item (a token the AI composed itself gets
a line after the rows instead, below): the origin (icon, name, and its kind word:
file / web page / command output), the token (+ "+N derived", birth chips),
what the AI did ("AI saw the mask ×N" / "never entered the model context",
the command echo as sub-line), and the outcome chip with where it went ("to
notes-sink.test", the gate label, "in the agent's reply", or "no egress").
Hollow dots mark stations where nothing happened; the rail into a blocked
outcome is cut; the row's left border repeats the outcome colour. Text
ellipsizes inside its column (full text in the title), so the outcome is
always on screen and nothing scrolls sideways.

**Every outcome, not only the worst** (2026-10-05). The chip is the flow's
worst outcome (`summary.terminal`), and a row used to show only that one.
In a Secrets-mode session, `GITHUB_TOKEN` was sent to api.github.com under
its binding and blocked at collector.evil.example. Its row read only
"⛔ blocked from leaving · to collector.evil.example", so a reader took the
token for never having left. The Trace tab and the product's *Your secrets*
both showed the send. Now `lineageOutcomes` reads each outcome the flow's
evidence edges recorded (`gated`, `egress`, `revealed_reply`), worst first,
with the destinations from the edges. A sink node is one per destination and
keeps its first verdict, so reading nodes would lose a host's second
outcome. The first group stays the chip. Each later group adds two lines
under it, in its own colour: "also ✅ left with permission", then "to
api.github.com". The summary line tallies the rows by item, in the chips'
words, and an item counts under every outcome it had (`stats.outcomes`): "2
secret items · all masked before reaching the AI · 2 left with permission · 1
blocked from leaving". It used to say "N attempts to send data out
(1 allowed · 1 blocked)" over each item's worst outcome. That hid the
release, and it counted items, not attempts. The worst-outcome counts
(`egressAllowed`/`egressBlocked`/`egressPending`) stay as they were for the
badges and Home.

**A secret is a secret item.** A flow whose data is a secret (`isSecretFlow`,
shipped as `summary.secret`) is never called untrusted. In Secrets mode,
untrusted text is not masked at all, so the old wording contradicted the
session header. The panel line reads "one row per secret item" (or
"untrusted item", "untrusted or secret item", from the stats). The card's
title reads "the story of one secret item". Its first line reads "A secret —
where it came from was not recorded", and the story's origin step reads "A
secret came in from the file …". An untrusted flow (the frozen integrity
axis) keeps its words. With no flow, a `nomodel_`/`anymodel_`/`localmodel_`
token's card says secret.

**A token the AI composed is not masked** (2026-10-09; lineage.ts
`composedByModel`, `stats.composed`; app.js `lineageComposedHtml`). The
model can write a token-shaped string that nothing minted (symbol-lineage.md,
*Model-authored tokens are not symbols*). At Secrets, the shape seen live is
an invented field on a placeholder the session masked: the output of `cat
.env` masked as `$MDU:nomodel_Bash[93d1]`, then a reply "I will send
`$MDU:nomodel_Bash[93d1].value` to the API". A `nomodel_` name was always
taken for a real secret, since a secret registered at launch can reach the
model where the events do not show it. So the invented field was "2 secret
items", a row reading "🔒 masked … birth unrecorded · 🤖 AI saw the mask,
never the contents", a second masked value in the Secrets tab, and "2 masked"
on the session's row. Now:

- a secret's name is the model's own when it extends, by a field path, a
  symbol the session minted and no system-written surface ever showed it:
  the model learned the symbol from a recorded result, and a real field of
  it would have reached the model in that result. A field on a secret the
  session never minted (one registered at launch) is still taken as real;
- the stats count the masked items only (`stats.flows`, `secret`,
  `outcomes`, `egress*`, `readFirst`), and `stats.composed` counts the
  composed tokens apart. The row's counts (§4.33), the session summary, the
  🛡 chip and card (§4.16), the line under *Where each went* and Home's
  count at a masking level read them;
- *Where each went* draws one row per masked item, and after the rows one
  line names the composed tokens: "Not counted: 1 token the AI composed
  itself, shaped like a masked value but standing for nothing:
  `$MDU:nomodel_Bash[93d1].value`". Each name opens its card, which says
  "… looks like a masked reference, but the AI composed it itself — nothing
  was ever hidden behind it". A session with no item keeps the empty line
  and adds this one. The flows themselves stay in the lineage, so the card
  and the evidence graph still show them.

Tests: `lineage.test.ts`, `session-counts.test.ts`,
`ui/app-js-lineage-composed.test.ts`, and
`tests/stack/inspector-composed-token.test.ts`. The stack test runs the real
arbiter at Secrets and the real anthropic-proxy on its production client,
with a scripted reply carrying the invented field. It also runs the
launcher's record, the real routes and the real inspector bundle, and checks
that no byte of the key reaches the model or any page.

**Read before it was masked** (2026-10-05). An item whose content the AI
read as it was, before any request carried it masked (a file labelled after
the AI read it: dual-lanes `maskedLater`, §4.25b), was told as if the mask
came first. In the first-session tour, the AI read `deploy/staging.conf` at
10:41, and from 10:42 the proxy carried that result as
`$MDU:nomodel_Read[1131]`; the summary said "all masked before reaching the
AI", the row "🤖 AI saw the mask ×2 · never the contents", and the card
"masked it … before the AI could read it". `withReadFirst` (lineage.ts,
wired in `toSessionViewModel`) now marks each flow with a symbol a
`maskedLater` names, by base (`$MDU:tool[hash]`: a field token and its
result's token name the same delivery), with `summary.readFirst`, the
earliest moment the AI got it as it was, and counts them in
`stats.readFirst`. The summary splits its claim (`maskedPhrases`, app.js
`lineageMaskedPhrases`): "3 secret items · 2 masked before reaching the AI ·
1 read by the AI before it was masked · …"; with none read first it is as
before. The row's AI column reads "⚠ AI read it as it was · at 10:41:29,
then the mask ×2", amber (`.lin-ai-warn`). The card's story and its hidden
content say the same (§4.17), and so does the protection card (§4.16). The
times and tokens were already in the payload; nothing new is shown. Since
2026-10-06 the session's short counts say it too: the list row, the
protection chip and the summary count such an item as "read before marked",
never as masked (§4.33, *A read before it was masked is not counted as
masked*).

**Shown to you is not a send** (2026-10-06). The reply filter's reveal (a
`desymbolize` event from `reply-filter`, the `revealed_reply` edge into the
`snk:human` sink) puts the real value on the person's own screen, in the
agent's reply; it does not send it anywhere. It used to count as a release:
over the first-session tour the summary read "3 left with permission", and
the two `deploy/staging.conf` rows read "✅ left with permission · human
terminal (reply)", though only `STRIPE_KEY` was ever sent off the machine
(to api.stripe.com, at 10:39). The product's *Your secrets* already told the
two apart ("You saw its real value in the agent's replies"). Now a reveal is
its own outcome, `shown`, after the releases: a flow whose only release is a
reveal has `summary.terminal` "shown" (chip "👁 shown to you", sub "in the
agent's reply"; the card's summary chip says the same); a row with a send
too lists it as "also 👁 shown to you"; and `stats.outcomes` counts it
under `shown`, never `allowed`, so the tour reads "3 secret items · 2 masked
before reaching the AI · 1 read by the AI before it was masked · 1 left with
permission · 1 blocked from leaving · 3 shown to you in replies". The edge
itself keeps the reply filter's "allowed", and the worst-outcome counts drop
reveal-only items from `egressAllowed`. Only the reply filter's own events
(`emitter: "reply-filter"`) are the person's screen: a `desymbolize` from any
other emitter (a fill for a request, which the tests model) keeps the old
reading, a release, on its own sink (`snk:fill`, "real value filled in
(net-supervisor)"; its card step reads "It left — allowed by the rules"), so
the change can never hide a send as "shown" (fail-closed). A gate that let a
command through still counts as "left with permission", unchanged: its event
alone does not say whether the value left. The words come from the events the
payload already held; nothing new is shown. Tests: `lineage.test.ts`,
`app-js-lineage.test.ts`, `inspector-record.test.ts` (the tour served), and
the stack `tests/stack/reply-reveal-shown.test.ts` (the REAL reply-filter
CLI, arbiter and dashboard: the item the reply showed is "shown", the tally
counts no release, and the session page says the person saw it in the reply
and Mandu sent it nowhere).

**A block says Mandu asked** (2026-10-06). The trace's step (§4.2f, *A
check says it asked*), the session page and the product's *Your secrets*
(§4.25b, *A block says Mandu asked you*) say when a block put a row on
Approvals. *Where each went* did not. Over the first-session tour, the
`STRIPE_KEY` row read "⛔ blocked from leaving · to api.stripe.com", then
"also ✅ left with permission … to api.stripe.com": the same host blocked,
then allowed, with nothing between. Yet the 10:38 block's `net_action`
records the row the arbiter queued (`policy.approvalId`, `egr-1`).

- **The id on the edge.** A `gated` or `egress` edge whose verdict stopped
  the data (blocked, denied or pending) carries `askId`, its evidence
  event's `policy.approvalId`. It is read by dual-lanes `askIdOf`, the
  rule the trace and *Your secrets* use: only an id of the queue's shape
  counts. An edge that let the data through carries none, and neither does
  a block that filed no row. The evidence-JSON export carries it too.
- **The row.** Under a blocked group's destinations, `lineageAskIds`
  collects its edges' rows, each once and in order. `lineageAskedHtml`
  draws "Mandu asked for your OK (egr-1)" (`.lin-asked`). It is a short
  form, so the id fits the column at 1280px; the title keeps the trace's
  words, "… in Approvals (egr-1)". The line comes before any "also"
  outcome, so the tour's row reads: block, ask, send, shown.
- **The card** (§4.17). A blocked or denied sink step adds the trace's
  sentence on its own line: "Mandu asked for your OK in Approvals
  (`egr-1`)." (`.sc-asked`).
- **A hold** draws no line, because its chip already says "⏸ waiting for
  your OK".
- **The answer** (2026-10-09, §4.2f *The answer*). Once you answered, the
  card's line ends with it: "Mandu asked for your OK in Approvals
  (`egr-1`). Your answer: Block." The row's short line keeps its words,
  because it is already cut to the column ("Mandu asked for your OK
  (egr-1, eg…"). Its title carries the answers: "… (egr-1, egr-2). Your
  answer to egr-1: Block." Both are repainted in place when the answers
  change. Tested in `ui/app-js-lineage.test.ts` (*The answer*).

The id is the inert code the trace already shows, never a link, because
the row is itself a button. It comes from the event the payload already
held, and the signed-out projection keeps `policy` (§6), so nothing new is
shown. Tests:

- `view-model/lineage.test.ts`: a net block, a gate block and a hold carry
  the id; a send, a malformed id and a block with no id carry none; the
  tour record names only `egr-1`.
- `ui/app-js-lineage.test.ts`: the row and the card, with and without a
  row filed; the tour row.
- `test/component/inspector-record.test.ts`: the served tour.
- `tests/stack/block-why.test.ts` L3b: the real net-proxy's block, through
  a real arbiter, gives the real dashboard's lineage the queued row's id.

A row (or the symbol table's Flow column, or the egress queue's ⌁ button)
opens the §4.17 symbol card, whose lineage section is the per-flow **SVG
evidence graph** on the two-view geometry: AgentView left, HumanView right,
the hatched trust wall between, time flowing down in the story's order
(§4.17 *In the order it happened*: a gate's row below its command's, not
above it because the proxy recorded it first). A blocked egress edge ends
at the wall with ⛔ and the never-reached destination is dashed beyond it.
Node click jumps to the proving event; *⧉ copy evidence JSON* exports the
`SymbolLineage` (the evidence unit a SIEM export builds on). Confidentiality
badges (🔒/🤖) and the `content_kind` triage verdict ride the symbol nodes.

The builder doubles as a live oracle: `tests/lib/assertions.ts evalLineage*`
(category `fidelity`) ride the replay-e2e and claude-e2e scenarios
(symbol-lineage.md §9.1). Tests: `ui/app-js-lineage.test.ts` (tracker header,
four columns, destination sub-line, cut rail, hollow dots; a secret allowed
at one host and blocked at another draws both, the tally and the card say
"secret"), `view-model/lineage.test.ts` (`outcomes` on the walkthrough
session, the tally's words, observe-only wording, an older payload;
`withReadFirst` by name and base, the split summary, the tour record; a
reveal is `shown`, never `allowed`),
`test/component/session-walkthrough.test.ts` (the served inspector's Secrets
tab over the real server) and `test/component/inspector-record.test.ts` (the
served inspector over the tour record: the item read before it was masked).

### 4.16 Protection chip — the plain-language positive signal

The §4.6 invariant banner is silent while everything holds, which is right
for an alarm and wrong for reassurance (the browser lock-icon problem). The
**protection chip** (`#protection-chip`, `app.js renderProtectionChip`) is
its always-on positive twin, in end-user words. It rides the selected
session's own line (`#session-bar`, §4.32, §4.33), since it summarizes one
session; the top bar's status line carries the running protection level.

- **Holding**: green `🛡 Protected · N masked · M blocked · K waiting`
  (zero segments omitted; no untrusted flows → `no untrusted data yet`, or
  `nothing masked` for a session with no mode on record, below).
  When every masked item is a secret, it says `1 secret masked` or `2 secrets
  masked`. M and K count items by their worst outcome (§4.15).
- **By protection level** (§4.19, architecture/protection-modes.md), read from
  the live posture egress.js publishes (`window.__mduPosture`), or, while
  that is not known, from the session's own record (*Not connected, the
  session's own record*, below): *Injection*
  keeps the line above; *Full* appends `· secrets guarded`; *Secrets*
  (masking off, secrets guarded) is a calm `🛡 Protected · secrets guarded`
  with no masking claim at all, since masking is not running, then `N secrets
  masked`, `⚠ R read before marked` and `M blocked`. N counts only the items
  masked before the AI read them; R the ones it read as they were first
  (lineage `readFirst`, §4.15; the row's `early`, §4.33). With masking off, M is the trace's own blocked
  count (`howPathCounts`, the "Mandu checked" stop, §4.33), a blocked command
  included, not the items' worst outcome. A gated secrets
  posture (§4.23) shows the amber `⚠ secrets gated` instead of `secrets
  guarded`. Masking off with an unknown secrets state reads `🛡 Masking is off
  · secrets status unknown`: neither alarm nor claim.
- **Off level**: amber `⚠ Not protected — protection is turned off`, only
  when **both** axes are explicitly `off`. One axis off is a supported level,
  never an alarm; an unknown posture is never rendered as off.
- **Violated**: the chip hides; the red banner owns the top bar.
- Click → the **plain-terms card** (`#protection-modal`): one line per fact
  ("N untrusted items were masked before the AI read them", "M attempts to
  send masked data out were blocked", "K send attempts are waiting for your
  approval", "left with permission", "read by the sandboxed reader"), a
  verdict footer ("Protection held — the AI never saw the untrusted
  contents"), and *Where each went →*, which shows the Secrets tab (§4.33)
  and scrolls to the §4.15 lineage.
- **The card at Secrets** (2026-10-05) counts what the trace under it shows,
  from the trace's path (`howPathCounts`: its "Data out" and "Mandu checked"
  stops), so the card and the trace cannot disagree:
  - The first line says "Your keys and credentials are guarded: they leave
    this machine only where a rule or your OK allows." Its sub-line gives the
    limits the product page gives: "Only the secrets you registered and the
    files you labeled are guarded. Untrusted content is not masked at this
    level, so it does not stop prompt injection."
  - The tiles are "N secret items were masked before the AI read them", then
    "N sends left this machine with a real value filled in, each to a
    destination allowed to receive it" (each a *Left this machine* step),
    then "N requests carrying a secret were blocked, so they never left this
    machine" (each a *Kept on this machine* step that was blocked, not held),
    then "N actions blocked" for the other blocked steps (a command, a file
    access, a connection; "other" when blocked sends come first). The
    lineage's "send attempts are waiting for your approval" stays as it was.
  - The footer says "Your secrets are guarded: the AI never saw the real
    values of the N secret items."
  - A secret item the AI read before it was marked (§4.15, `readFirst`) is
    never counted as masked before it was read: its own amber tile (kind
    `raw`) says "N secret items were read by the AI before they were marked
    a secret", the masked tile counts the rest, and the footer reads "The AI
    never saw the real values of 2 of the 3 secret items; it read 1 before
    it was marked a secret." (`secretsVerdict`; "The AI read the secret item
    before it was marked a secret." when none was masked first). The frozen
    masking levels keep their lines, except for such an item (*An item read
    first, at every posture*, below).

  Until then the card said keys "cannot leave this machine without your OK"
  over sends a binding let out with no OK asked. "N attempts to send guarded
  data out were blocked" was the items' worst outcome, so a blocked `rm -rf`
  counted as a send. No line said that a secret left. "(a program read a
  credential file)" was said of every secret, an environment variable
  included. The sub-line pointed at "Change the level", and the levels that
  mask are frozen. The masking-off card with an unknown secrets state keeps
  its sentence and sub-line, and its tiles are the trace's counts too. The
  frozen masking levels (Injection, Full) keep their lines.

*An item read first, at every posture* (2026-10-06). The rule that a secret
the AI read before it was marked (`readSecret`, lineage `readFirst`) is never
counted as masked holds at every posture, not only at Secrets. With no
protection service connected, the posture is not known: egress.js publishes
`unknown` on both axes, and the status line reads "Protection: not known".
This happens to a dashboard reading recorded logs, or one whose stack has
stopped. The chip and the card then take the line the masking levels share.

Over the first-session tour, that line read as follows. The chip said
`🛡 Protected · 3 secrets masked · 1 blocked`. The tile said "3 secret items
were masked before the AI read them". The note said "never the original
contents". The footer said "Protection held: the AI never saw the secret
contents". The banner right under the chip said "2 secret values masked, ⚠ 1
read by the AI before it was marked a secret". At 10:41 the AI read
`deploy/staging.conf` as it was.

Now that line splits the count the same way:

- the chip reads `🛡 Protected · 2 secrets masked · ⚠ 1 read before marked ·
  1 blocked` (`N masked` when untrusted items are masked too);
- the card has the same amber `raw` tile;
- the note adds "except the secret item it read before it was marked a
  secret";
- the footer is `secretsVerdict`'s sentence, never "Protection held".

A session with no such read reads as before, at every posture. Nothing new
is read out of an event. Tests: `app-js-protection.test.ts` (the tour with
the posture not known and with none published, plus a control with no early
read) and `inspector-record.test.ts` (the served inspector with its own
egress.js over the real server, with no service behind it).

*Not connected, the session's own record* (2026-10-07). The chip and the card
tell one session ("This session, in plain terms"), yet they read only the
live posture, while the banner right under the chip reads the mode the
session recorded at its launch (`recordedProtection`, §4.2f). With no
protection service connected the live posture is not known, so the two
disagreed. Over the first-session tour, recorded in Secrets mode, the card
took the shared masking line under the banner's "Secrets mode. Untrusted
text is not masked in this session":

- "2 secret items were masked before the AI read them (a program read a
  credential file)", of a registered variable and a labeled file;
- "The AI works with masked references (like $MDU:…), never the original
  contents";
- no tile for the 10:39 send that left with a real value filled in, and the
  10:38 block as "an attempt to send masked data out".

A session recorded in Off mode read `🛡 Protected · no untrusted data yet` and
"No untrusted data reached the AI in this session." over the banner's "Off
mode. This session was only observed".

Now, while the live posture is not known (both axes `unknown`, or nothing
published yet), `protectionSummary` takes the level from the session's
record (`paired.mode`, set only when the arbiter reported the axes), for the
two product modes:

- **Secrets**: the Secrets card, tile for tile the one a connected Secrets
  dashboard shows. The tour reads `🛡 Protected · secrets guarded · 2 secrets
  masked · ⚠ 1 read before marked · 1 blocked`, with tiles for the 2 masked,
  the 1 read first, the 1 send that left and the 1 request blocked.
- **Off**: the amber off state, said of this session in the past tense:
  `⚠ Not protected — protection was off in this session`; the line "Protection
  was off in this session — the AI could see untrusted content as-is, and
  your secret files were not guarded."; the footer "⚠ Protection was off in
  this session — nothing here was masked or checked." It names no who/when
  and no "Turn it back on", since both are about the live setting, which is
  not known.

Either way the card's note says "The protection service is not connected,
so this card says what this session recorded when it started.", since the top
bar reads "Protection: not known". A known live posture still wins,
unchanged; when the two are known and differ, which one the chip should say
is still open. A frozen recorded mode (Injection, Full) keeps the shared
line, and so does a session with no recorded mode whose checked tool results
say which axis ran (`paired.integrity` "on" or "off"; *No mode on record*,
below). Whether an "off" one should get the Secrets card, as its banner
says Secrets mode, is still open: an Off session's results carry the same
integrity-OFF reason. That line's secret tile no longer adds
"(a program read a credential file)" at any level, for the reason the
Secrets card dropped it. Tests: `app-js-protection.test.ts` (the tour not
connected against the connected card, the same record with no mode, a live
Off over the record, an Off-recorded session with an Off audit published)
and `inspector-record.test.ts` (the served tour with no service against the
connected server's card, the unrecorded copy, and an Off-recorded session
served with no service).

*No mode on record* (2026-10-09). A session with no recorded mode and no
checked tool result (`paired.integrity` "unknown", §4.33 *A session with no
recorded mode*; an older view-model with no `paired` is read the same way)
kept the shared line while the live posture was not known, so the chip and
the card claimed what the banner under them no longer does:
`🛡 Protected · no untrusted data yet`, "No untrusted data reached the AI in
this session.", "Protection held: the AI never saw the untrusted contents.",
and, with a masked secret, the note "The AI works with masked references
(like $MDU:…), never the original contents." over the banner's "Mode not
recorded". At `secrets`, the default, untrusted text reaches the AI as it
was. Now such a session keeps its counts and tiles, but:

- with nothing masked, the chip reads `🛡 Protected · nothing masked`, the
  card's line "Nothing was masked in this session." and its footer "Whether
  untrusted content was masked is not known.";
- the card's note is the banner's sentence, "This session did not record its
  protection mode, so whether untrusted text was masked is not known.", in
  place of "never the original contents";
- the footer for masked items is unchanged ("Protection held: the AI never
  saw the secret contents.", of what was masked).

A known live posture, a recorded mode and a checked result keep their words.
Tests: `app-js-protection.test.ts` (an empty session at both not-known
postures, a masked secret with no record against the connected and recorded
cards) and `tests/stack/inspector-unrecorded-mode.test.ts` (the real
net-proxy's stopped sends and an older launcher's record with no mode, the
real inspector bundle's chip and card over the real routes, the recorded
control, the no-value oracle).

Everything is a **pure projection** of `vm.lineage.stats`, `vm.invariant`
and, with masking off, the trace's path counts, computed in one place
(`protectionSummary`, lines painted by `protLinesHtml`), so chip and card
cannot disagree. **Vocabulary rule** for every plain surface:
*masked / blocked / waiting / the AI*, never *symbolized / egress / invariant
/ T-LLM / U-LLM*; where plain is less precise, keep the distinction in a
sub-caption rather than flatten it. The expert terms stay on the trace, the
symbol table and the lineage graph. The product page at `/` (§4.25) inherits
this vocabulary and its sweep test.

Tests: `ui/app-js-protection.test.ts` (counts through the real
`toSessionViewModel`, wording, violation hiding, no raw attacker bytes, the
evidence hand-off, the 3×3 posture sweep proving the alarm fires only on
off/off, the Secrets, Full, gated and unknown wordings; the Secrets card's
tiles against the trace's path on the walkthrough session with its
refusals, and with only a blocked command; the tour record's item read
before it was marked); `test/component/session-walkthrough.test.ts`
(the served inspector, connected in Secrets mode, egress.js publishing the
posture: the chip and the card agree with the served path) and
`test/component/inspector-record.test.ts` (the same over the tour record).

### 4.17 Symbol card — click a token, get the whole story

Clicking a symbol opens **one centered modal per symbol** (`#symcard-modal`,
`showSymbolCard`) showing everything the session knows about it. **Every
symbol surface lands on the same card**: trace tokens (`.dv-sym` / `.dv-orig`,
in the trace and the full-prompt modal), the §4.15 tracker rows, the §4.5
table's name and Flow cells, and the egress queue's ⌁ button. The value popup
remains only for plain value cells (egress reveals, the §4.14 modal's 🔒). The
card tells the story of one item, top to bottom (v2):

1. **Summary strip**: the outcome chip, what the item is ("Content of the
   file `…/notes.md`", "Output of the command `curl …`", "Content fetched from
   the web page `…`"), when it was first seen; the left border repeats the
   outcome colour.
2. **What happened**: the flow's evidence graph flattened into a numbered
   timeline (`symCardStoryHtml`), one plain sentence per node in the order
   it happened (below), chosen by node kind and the edge that reached it
   ("The AI ran `curl …`" →
   "Untrusted content came in from …" → "Mandu masked it as `$MDU:…` before
   the AI could read it" → "The AI read the masked reference ×2 — never the
   original" → "⛔ Mandu blocked it from leaving to `sink.evil` — the original
   never left"; or waiting, approved, shown in the reply, read by the
   sandboxed reader, "looks like a masked reference, but the AI composed it
   itself"). Each step ends in a `t<turn> · hh:mm:ss · trace →` jump: no step
   is shown that no event recorded. The jump is named by its moment, then
   its step ("t1 · 09:00:05 · trace: step 2", the arrow left out as §4.33
   leaves a glyph out, `symControlName`), and described by its step's
   sentence (`aria-describedby` on the step's `.sc-text`, id
   `symcard-step-N`; one card is open at a time). Until 2026-10-13 its name
   was the moment alone, and steps proved within one second, or by one
   event, read alike: a real Secrets-mode session's card (a read, then the
   placeholder used in a command) read "t1 · 05:39:16 · trace →" five
   times. The words, the tooltip and the click are unchanged. An item the
   AI read before it was masked (§4.15, `summary.readFirst`) never reads
   "before the AI could read it": its mask step is amber, "Mandu masked it
   as `$MDU:…` from then on: the AI had already read it as it was, at
   10:41:29", and its context step "The AI
   read the masked reference ×2 after that", never "— never the original"
   (2026-10-05). A blocked step whose block filed an Approvals row adds, on
   its own line, "Mandu asked for your OK in Approvals (`egr-1`)." (§4.15,
   *A block says Mandu asked*; 2026-10-06). A symbol whose masking no event
   in the session recorded, and which the AI did not compose, reads "🔒
   Masked as `$MDU:…` outside this session's events — a key or secret file
   registered when the session started, or an older event log", with no
   warning (§4.33 *A masked value with no masking step in the session*).
   Until 2026-10-09 it read "⚠ … how it was masked is not recorded (older
   event log)", and a secret placeholder never has such a step. When one
   event proves two steps (a program's send names the value and where it
   went), the story's order breaks the tie: origin, symbol, context, action,
   sink. So the value comes before its stop, and never after it because of
   an alphabetical node id.

   **In the order it happened** (`storyOrder`, 2026-10-13). The steps run
   in event order (`seq`, ties as above), except that no step comes before
   the step its edge leaves from (a gate after its command, a mask after
   its file), and a step where a call carried the item comes before every
   command the AI wrote with it in that call's answer or a later one: a
   turn numbers the AI's requests, a tool call carries the turn of the
   request it answered, and a request goes before its answer. The
   anthropic-proxy records a model call when its answer ends, after the
   answer's tool calls and their gate, so by `seq` alone a real
   Secrets-mode session's card (a read, then the placeholder used in a
   command) read "The shell gate let that command through", then "The AI
   used the masked reference in a command", then "The AI read the masked
   reference ×2"; every hand-built test seed records the causal order, so
   no test saw it. A placeholder the AI wrote before any recorded request
   carried it (a secret's placeholder learned from the system prompt)
   keeps its command first. The second rule binds only calls and the AI's
   commands: the net-proxy, the reply filter and the arbiter stamp turn 0,
   so a send or a reveal they recorded keeps its edges and its event
   order. Event order that already keeps both rules is unchanged, and a
   loop in the edges, which no recorded flow has, falls back to event
   order, so every step is still shown exactly once. Only the order
   changes: each step keeps its words, its moment and the event that
   proves it, and the lineage itself (`view-model/lineage.ts`, the audit
   evidence) is not touched. The evidence graph draws its rows in the same
   order (§4.15).
3. **The hidden content**: the privileged reveal of the HumanView original in
   a capped scrollable pane, escaped, never parsed as DOM ("what the AI never
   saw — visible to you only"; for an item read before it was masked, "what
   the mask stands for: the AI read it before it was masked — visible to you
   only"), the same posture as the click-to-reveal popup it absorbed.
4. **Details for experts**, a `<details>` open by default: the table row
   (tool/field, origin, born with *⊕ table at birth* (§4.14) and *→ minting
   step*, derived from, the raw event flow), *⧉ copy evidence JSON*, and the
   SVG evidence graph in its own fold, closed by default. A symbol masked
   outside the session's events has no row. It reads "tool/field: not
   recorded — no step in this session's events masked it" and "born: not in
   this session's events (…)", never "model-authored, or an older event log".

A section with no data says so ("value not recorded…", "no lineage flow
recorded…"); a token with no known facts at all stays inert. Attacker bytes
appear only in the hidden-content pane. The card re-appends itself to
`<body>` on open so it stacks above an already-open modal, and
`.sym-value-popup` sits above the modals it can open from. Tests:
`ui/app-js-lineage.test.ts` (story steps in event order, per-step jumps, red
blocked step, expert fold, graph folded, no raw value in the story, every
entry point, XSS-escaped value; the tour record's item read before it was
masked), `ui/app-js-symtable-untabled.test.ts` (a symbol masked outside the
session's events: its step, the tie order, the expert rows),
`ui/app-js-story-jump-names.test.ts` (a read used in a command, and a
secret used three times within one second: each jump's name and
description, no two alike, no value in either, a second open names its
steps afresh), `tests/stack/inspector-story-jump-names.test.ts` (a
labelled file read, then its placeholder used in a command, through the
real arbiter, proxy and server; the served card signed out and in; the
no-value oracle), `ui/app-js-story-order.test.ts` (a session as the proxy
records it, and the same session in causal order: one story; the graph's
rows; a net-proxy send stamped turn 0 stays last; a placeholder written
before a request carried it; a loop shows every step once) and
`tests/stack/inspector-story-order.test.ts` (the real proxy's record
holds the inversion; the served card and its graph, signed out and in,
read it in the order it happened; the no-value oracle), and
`test/component/inspector-record.test.ts`.

### 4.18 Simple mode — the end-user register (retired)

**Status: superseded by §4.25 and retired from the inspector.** The end user
has a separate page at `/` (§4.25); the inspector at `/dev/` has one register.
The 🏠/🔬 toggle, `body.mode-simple`, the `mandu.mode` key (a stale value is
ignored) and the simple home cards are gone. Its premise carries over: one
color-coded verdict first, the approval prompt and the rule list as one
feature seen from two sides, and prompts rare and information-rich.

What outlived it, and what the product page inherits:

- **The approval verbs**: **Allow** (standing), **Allow once** (`approve-once`
  → `scope:"once"`: answers one matching attempt, then the pair asks again;
  policy-surface.md §9.8.7) and **Block** (standing), with honest copy: "Allow
  and Block are remembered — change them any time. Allow once lets just this
  one through." A once-scoped answer is not a standing rule; its row reads
  "one-time answer — next ask only" / "already used". The reversal is labeled
  for what it does (**Allow instead** / **Block instead**, never "Undo"). In
  the inspector: the Approvals page's "Waiting for your answer" cards
  (`#approvals-waiting`, egress.js `paintApprovalsWaiting`) and "Answered
  earlier" (§4.34), where the standing allow reads **Always allow**, as on
  the product.
- **The §4.16 vocabulary as law** for every plain string, with
  policy-surface.md §9.8.5's honesty rules: hiding is the user's explicit act,
  a reduced view never reads as "nothing else exists" (remainder counts), no
  zero-count theater ("no untrusted data yet"). Untrusted strings render via
  `createElement` / `textContent` only.
- The leftover-tests note (§4.10.2), the §4.16 chip and card, the §4.17 card.

Tests: `ui/app-js-register-retired.test.ts` (toggle gone; a stale
`mandu.mode=simple` renders the full layout), `ui/css-inspector-contract.test.ts`
(no register selector survives), `ui/egress-js-approvals.test.ts` (the card
and its vocabulary sweep), `test/component/approval-loop.test.ts` (panel VM
pending row → CSRF'd approve POST → arbiter resolve op → row re-served
approved, over the real HTTP server against a mock arbiter) and
`tests/stack/approval-loop.test.ts` (real ArbiterServer + DashboardServer: the
full §8.7 allow-once cycle, `scope:"once"` in the store, exactly one allowed
decision, the row re-queued, the `approval_resolved` → `approval_consumed`
audit pair).

### 4.19 Protection drawer — the policy-setup surface (🛡)

The §8 Policy panel shows the law; this surface is where the human sets the
parts that are theirs to set. It began as a drawer opened by a topbar 🛡
button and is now an inline block on the Rules page (§4.19.v3, §4.32); the design
below holds for both. Its first build had three sections, **① live posture**
(Pause / Resume), **② saved setup** (the protection axes in config.toml) and
**③ links** to the standing law; code comments still cite them, and the v2
matrix layout below absorbed all three. Design inputs: EDR and consumer
security setup UIs (plainly named layer toggles, a recommended preset,
one-click host isolation with a symmetric release, friction on disabling
tamper protection, loud-when-off status).

**Three kinds of state, never conflated:**

- `integrity` / `confidentiality` are **boot-time switches, global to the
  arbiter process** (`MANDU_INTEGRITY` / `MANDU_CONFIDENTIALITY`, resolved once
  at construction, `arbiter/policy/{integrity,confidentiality}-flag.ts`). The
  four named modes (`secrets` / `injection` / `full` / `off`,
  architecture/protection-modes.md) name the four axis pairs. No runtime op
  flips them, so changing one honestly means: write the config, restart the
  arbiter.
- The `egress` posture (`normal` | `lockdown`) is **runtime state**: global,
  in memory (`arbiter/policy/session-posture.ts`, cleared by a restart), set
  by the audited `setSessionPosture` op.
- The secret levels (`no-model` vs `any-model`) are **per-path** state; the
  surface explains and links to the secrets surface, never duplicates it.

**The canonical matrix (layout v2): data kinds × the two boundaries.**

- **Rows = what data**, each concept stated exactly once (a unit test pins
  it): *Untrusted content* (integrity axis); *Secrets — hidden* (`no-model`:
  the AI never reads it, a hard deny with no approval path); *Secrets —
  usable* (`any-model`: the AI may read it via a logged declassification,
  with your OK when untrusted content is around; network egress behaves like
  strict). The secret rows share the confidentiality axis under one group
  header, which links to the secrets surface for which paths carry which
  level.
- **Columns = the two boundaries**: *Into the AI* (model context) and *Out of
  the machine* (network/exec). The secret rules are enforced partly at the
  second (bound-destination-only release), which is why a flat feature list
  read as confusing.
- **Cells = a small vocabulary**, as short lines (`.prot-mx-line`): `masked` ·
  `never` · `your OK` · `allowed` · `own service only` · `not covered` ·
  `unknown` · `paused`. *Masked* is the end-user term for symbolized (the
  industry term for this reversible substitution); "sealed" no longer appears
  in end-user copy.
- **Live state rides the matrix**: the integrity chip on the untrusted row,
  the confidentiality chip on the secrets header, the egress chip
  (`on` / `paused`) on the *Out of the machine* header. Rows dim to a calm `not
  covered` by the **running** state (`.prot-mx-off`): the untrusted row at
  Secrets ("untrusted content reaches the AI as-is"), the secret rows at
  Injection ("secret files behave like ordinary files"), all three at Off.
  `unknown` stays unknown, never dimmed as off.
- **Level picker above the matrix**: four radio cards, **Secrets** (secrets
  guarded, masking off) / **Injection** (masking on, secrets not guarded) /
  **Full** (both) / **Off** (nothing enforced, Mandu only records). Injection
  and Full are the frozen integrity levels (§4.25o). Each card has one short
  plain line that repeats no matrix row sentence. The `default` tag rides the
  card the server names in `defaultMode`; the browser hardcodes no default
  (`DEFAULT_MODE` in `dashboard/src/config-axes.ts`, mirroring
  `launcher/src/mode.ts` and `arbiter/policy/protection-mode.ts`, `secrets`,
  pinned by `tests/stack/axis-defaults-parity.test.ts`). Picking a card POSTs
  `{mode}`. A facts line reads "running now: X · saved setting: Y"; a saved
  `mode` naming no level (`badMode`) is said plainly and ignored. Each radio
  is named by its level's word and described by its tags and sentence
  (§4.32 *A level radio is named by its word*).
- **The one runtime control sits in its column**: ⏸ Pause sending / ▶ Resume
  in the *Out of the machine* footer (one visible, audited action each way),
  with its volatility stated ("clears if the protection service restarts").
- **The standing-law links dissolve into the matrix**: the secrets surface on
  the secrets header, "your rules · N" in the Out-column footer, the
  arbiter-admin decision timeline as the footer.
- **Machinery** (`.prot-machinery`): per-row axis and op names, and the
  per-axis saved switches, env keys, config path and audit who/when, now in
  Settings (§4.19.v3).

**Friction on downgrade.** Any change that turns an axis off requires a typed
confirmation (`OFF`): Full → Secrets, Full → Injection, anything → Off, and a
sideways Secrets ⇄ Injection move. The text names only the axes being turned
off and what stops being covered, in §4.16 words. Turning axes on needs no
gate. No time-boxed axis-off: axis changes apply on restart, so an
auto-revert would misstate its timing. A TTL'd auto-resume for Pause and a
detect-only posture are possible future work.

**Running vs saved.** Every surface shows *running now* (live; `unknown` stays
unknown) and *saved* (config.toml) as distinct facts. When they differ, one
amber pending bar: "Changes saved — restart the protection service to apply ·
⟳ Restart services" (the scope-honest restart, warning that it clears the
in-memory pause). The restart under way and its answer are kept across
the bar's repaint, and an answer that changed nothing running says so
(§4.32 *The restart keeps its state*).

**The off-state escapes the surface.** Only at the **Off** level (both axes
explicitly `off` in the live posture) does the session's chip render "⚠ Not
protected — protection is turned off": amber, visually and verbally distinct
from "⛔ Protection failed" (a choice is not an incident). It links here and to
the decision timeline, and carries the who/when: protection.js publishes the
axes payload with its `audit` block (`window.__mduAxes` +
`mdu:axes-updated`), and the card reads "Turned off from this dashboard on
<when>" (or "by <actor>", text only). The act cited is the most recent
`config_change` that turned an axis off, across both axes; a later re-enable,
a hand edit or an empty stream yields no claim rather than a wrong one. The
calm levels cite nobody. One axis off is a supported level and never alarms:
escalating it would cry wolf on every install that runs that level by
default.

**API contract:**

- **① Posture.** Arbiter `setSessionPosture` takes `allowRelax?: boolean`: a
  loosen without it stays a refused no-op (`applied:false`, tighten-only by
  default); with it, `relaxGlobal` applies and `emitPostureChange` audits the
  relax like a tighten (`requestedBy` carried). Dashboard `POST
  /api/policy/posture` `{posture: "lockdown"|"normal"}` (CSRF
  `X-Mandu-Control`) → the op with `requestedBy: "dashboard"` and `allowRelax:
  posture === "normal"`; returns the op result (`applied` / `from` / `to`);
  400 invalid, 404 no arbiter, 403 CSRF. A narrow `PostureArbiter` surface
  beside `ApprovalsArbiter` / `SecretsArbiter` (`attachArbiterSurfaces`).
- **② Saved axes.** `GET /api/config/axes` → `{ok, path, exists, configured:
  {integrity, confidentiality} (null = key absent), defaults, effective, mode,
  badMode?, effectiveMode, defaultMode, audit?}`: `effective` is what the next
  cold arbiter start runs, per axis = axis key ?? the file mode's axis ??
  default (the launcher's in-file rule, `launcher/src/mode.ts`); `defaults`
  derives from the default mode; `badMode` is present only for an invalid
  mode string, which is ignored. `POST` accepts either `{mode}` (exact
  spelling; unknown → 400) or `{integrity?, confidentiality?}`; mixing is 400.
  A mode write goes through `applyModeEdit`, a byte-identical mirror of
  `launcher/src/config-edit.ts` (a cross-package parity test feeds both the
  same inputs): it sets the `mode` line and re-aligns any existing axis lines
  to the mode's pair, never appending axis lines. A single-axis write that
  finds a `mode` line rewrites it to the resulting pair's name, so the file
  never contradicts itself. Both writes (CSRF) surgically edit only the
  managed keys of the one config file, `~/.mandu/config.toml` (the launcher's
  own precedence source; every other byte preserved; created if absent), and
  return the GET shape.
- **The audit trail.** Every axis whose effective next-boot value flipped
  (for mode writes too: Full → Secrets emits one event, Secrets → Injection
  two) emits one `config_change` event into the arbiter-admin stream over the
  arbiter's opaque `emit` op (a narrow `ConfigAuditArbiter` surface; no
  arbiter change), with top-level `axis` / `from` / `to` /
  `requestedBy:"dashboard"` scalars for the SIEM (rules 100224 / 100225) and
  prose-only DualReprs. A no-flip write emits nothing, and an emit failure or
  absent arbiter never fails the POST. GET/POST answers carry `audit:
  {<axis>: {ts, from, to, requestedBy}}`, the latest act per axis.
- **Supervisor axis plumbing** (the "posture nobody runs" guard): the
  dashboard supervisor's arbiter spawn resolves config.toml's `mode` and axis
  keys into `MANDU_INTEGRITY` / `MANDU_CONFIDENTIALITY` (explicit process env
  wins; config fills only unset keys; an axis stated nowhere yields nothing,
  so the arbiter's default rules; provenance pointer to
  `launcher/src/config.ts`). A non-empty env `MANDU_MODE` speaks for both
  axes: nothing is seeded from the file and the env mode fills whichever axis
  var is not set, since the arbiter reads only the axis vars. An invalid
  `MANDU_MODE` is ignored and the file speaks. The test-tenant arbiter's
  pinned axes are untouched. Without this, ② would claim an effect the
  restart does not deliver.
- **Client**: egress.js publishes `window.__mduPosture` +
  `mdu:posture-updated` from its existing poll (the event's detail also
  carries the badge count, §4.20, and your answer to each answered row,
  §4.2f *The answer*); `dev/js/protection.js` paints
  the surface with `createElement` / `textContent` for every server string,
  CSRF'd POSTs, and honest fail-soft states (an unreachable arbiter disables
  controls with a note, never renders unknown as off).

Tests: `ui/protection-js.test.ts`, `ui/protection-js-level.test.ts`,
`config-axes.test.ts`, `config-axes-mode.test.ts`, the
`server/config-axes-routes` and `server/posture-routes` tests,
`supervisor/supervisor-axis-env.test.ts`, and over the real socket-op
contract `component/posture-loop.test.ts` and
`component/config-audit-loop.test.ts`.

#### 4.19.v3 — the drawer is retired; the block is inline; machinery + sandbox live in Settings

Stage 6 of policy-surface.md (§4, §6 item 6):

- **No `#protection-drawer`.** The level cards (`#protection-level`), the
  pending bar (`#protection-pending`) and the matrix (`#protection-matrix`)
  are children of one inline `#protection-panel` on the Rules page, before
  the Policy panel. It is never cloned, so every row sentence exists once.
- **A jump, not a toggle.** The top bar's status line (§4.32; a 🛡 button
  until then, `control.js wireProtectionJump`) goes to Rules, scrolls the
  block into view, flashes it, and dispatches `mdu:refresh-axes`.
  protection.js re-reads `/api/config/axes` and `/api/config/sandbox` on that
  event, when the Settings page is entered, and every 30 s while the page is
  visible.
- **Machinery moved to Settings** (`#protection-machinery-panel`,
  `renderMachinery`; the section is **Protection axes**, §4.34): per-axis
  switches, env keys, config path, audit who/when; the typed-OFF gate and
  applied-only audit are unchanged. A refused switch says why above the
  switches, as well as under the level cards on Rules: one saved setup, one
  note, drawn on both pages. Until 2026-10-09 it was drawn only under the
  level cards, so on Settings the switch sprang back without a word.
- **Settings → Sandbox** (`#sandbox-panel`; protection.js `renderSandbox`
  over `GET|POST /api/config/sandbox`, `config-sandbox-routes.ts` over
  `config-axes.ts SANDBOX_KEYS`): the launcher's boolean wrap keys in the same
  config.toml, written by the same surgical editor under their own provenance
  comment. They apply at the next `mandu` launch, and every string says so.
  `#sandbox-facts` is one sentence ("N of M protections wrap the agent at the
  next launch · off: … · applies at the next launch", prefixed "Portable
  posture — kernel-level protections are off." when `no-kernel` is on);
  `#sandbox-switches` groups the switches by chokepoint (commands / network /
  files / replies / portable posture), renders fs-sync's unset `auto` as an
  indeterminate box (never as off), disables kernel rungs dropped by
  no-kernel, and posts only the flipped key. Turning a protection off, or
  `no-kernel` on, takes the typed-OFF gate. A failed write keeps the last good
  state and says why. Each applied flip emits one `config_change` on
  `arbiter-admin` with the scalar `setting` (not `axis`, so the SIEM's
  protection-axis rules do not fire), and the GET's `audit` block carries the
  per-switch who/when. Defaults mirror `launcher/src/parse.ts` (tri-state
  rungs on; `landlock-net-strict` and `no-kernel` opt-in): change both in one
  commit, the "posture nobody runs" guard.
- **Signed out.** Every write here POSTs, and a POST needs the admin session
  (§6.x). Signed out the server answers 403 `ADMIN_SESSION_REQUIRED`, which
  is written for a developer (§4.8 "Signed out"). Each place says it in the
  inspector's words, with the command as code: "Sign in to change the
  sandbox: run `mandu dashboard` in your own terminal and open the sign-in
  link it prints." The verb is the control's:
  - a level card: "change the protection level"; a Protection axes switch:
    "change a protection axis";
  - ⏸ Pause sending and ▶ Resume: "pause sending", "resume sending";
  - a Sandbox switch: "change the sandbox";
  - the pending bar's ⟳ Restart services: "restart the services";
  - the Secrets panel (Rules): Label path "label a path", in its form's
    error line; Remove "remove a label" and Clear taint "clear a file's
    taint", in the line under their own table (since 2026-10-12, §4.32
    *Remove and Clear taint say what they did*).

  protection.js and secrets.js match the refusal on its text, as control.js
  does; any other refusal keeps the server's words. The typed-OFF question
  still comes first: the page learns the answer only by asking. Until
  2026-10-09 each place printed the server's text whole, backticks and
  `DASHBOARD_PASSWORD` included. Tests: `protection-js-signed-out.test.ts`,
  `secrets-js.test.ts`, and the stack e2e
  `tests/stack/inspector-policy-signed-out.test.ts` (a real arbiter and
  server: the routes' 403s change nothing, the served pages' sign-in lines,
  and the same writes landing signed in).
- **No answer.** With the dashboard server gone, each of these writes says
  "the dashboard server did not answer — reload this page once it is
  running again" in the same place (a switch: what it could not save, then
  the sentence), and the switch shows the saved setup again (§4.8 *No answer
  to a write in Approvals, Rules, Secrets and Protection*).
- **Contracts**: `css-inspector-contract` pins `#protection-panel` as hidden
  only by the page allow-list (§4.32; and the sandbox hosts exist); `css-dialog-contract` no longer lists the drawer;
  `protection-js-sandbox.test.ts` drives the re-read through
  `mdu:refresh-axes`.

### 4.19.v4 — areas: Status · Approvals · Policy · Settings

Stage 8 of policy-surface.md (§4) gave the inspector an area nav of four,
**Status · Approvals · Policy · Settings** (the Approvals area was called
Inbox before §4.25w). §4.32 replaced it, and the separate "which sessions"
switch beside it, with one nav of six **pages**: Status is **Sessions**
(with Drills and Tests beside it), Policy is **Rules**. `body[data-area]`
and its per-area deny-lists are gone; every panel declares its pages in
`data-pages` and one allow-list rule hides the rest. The page is persisted
as `mandu.area` (an old `status`, `policy` or `inbox` value opens the new
page and is written back), deep-linkable as `/dev/<page>` (§4.25v), and
other modules request one with `mdu:go-page` (alias `mdu:go-area`).

| Page | Surfaces |
|---|---|
| Sessions, Drills, Tests | the session list · the session header · the tabs (§4.33, §4.35) |
| Approvals | "Waiting for your answer" (`#approvals-waiting`, `paintApprovalsWaiting`) · "Answered earlier" (§4.34) |
| Rules | Protection block · Policy panel · Prompt filters · Secrets, under a sub-menu (§4.34) |
| Settings | stale banner, Services, Sandbox, Protection axes, Dashboard server, Appearance, Docs (§4.34) |

The Settings drawer is retired: its panels are the `#settings-area` section
inside `<main>`, and the Settings nav item keeps `#settings-toggle` so
`markSettingsStale` still lands on it. **Answered earlier**
(`#approvals-history`, `paintApprovalsHistory`; "History" before §4.34)
lists your resolved decisions newest first with the one-click reversal
(**Block instead** / **Allow instead**) through the same
`resolveEgressApproval` verbs; the Approvals nav item's badge
(`#area-approvals-count`, `paintApprovalsBadge`) is the pending count. protection.js re-reads the
saved setup when Settings is entered (`mdu:page-changed`). Tests:
`index-html.test.ts` (the pages inside `<main>`),
`css-dialog-contract.test.ts`, `control-js-boot.test.ts` (Settings is not
a drawer toggle), `page-nav.test.ts` (the nav and the allow-list per page).

### 4.20 Notification/badge entry points — the tab says when you're needed

"Visit when something needs your OK" only works if the user can tell without
visiting. The two cheapest entry points:

- **Title count.** `document.title` becomes `(N) Mandu · <page> · Developer
  view` while N approvals are pending, restored at 0. One writer (`paintDocTitle`)
  composes the `[TEST] ` prefix (the test store), the `(N) ` count and the
  page's title (§4.32 *The tab title names the page*), so a badge repaint
  never drops the prefix (§4.35) and a page change never drops the count. N is the **global pending-queue
  length** from the §4.19 `mdu:posture-updated` broadcast (`detail.pending`,
  egress.js's existing 3 s poll), deliberately not the per-session
  `lineage.stats.egressPending`, which counts one session's flows and can
  disagree with the queue.
- **Favicon badge.** index.html ships a baseline icon as an inline `data:`
  SVG (`#favicon`), and app.js redraws it as a red count tile (9+ cap) via an
  offscreen canvas while N > 0, restoring the baseline at 0. Without a 2d
  canvas it degrades to the baseline icon + counted title.

A count renders only for a **known** pending > 0: `verdictsKnown:false`
publishes `detail.pending: null` and the badge makes no claim (an unfetched
queue never badges as 0; `unknown ≠ off`). The listener runs with or without a
loaded session.

Not done here: browser/OS notifications (built on the product page, §4.25
*Notifications*; the agent's terminal is designed there, not built) (needs a permission prompt and a decision
on cadence vs the 3 s poll); a badge for non-approval attention states
(protection failed already owns the red banner).

Tests: `ui/app-js-badge.test.ts` (count, clear, unknown, the no-canvas
degrade), `ui/egress-js-approvals.test.ts` (`detail.pending` = queue count;
unknown publishes null, not 0).

### 4.21 Session health — the posture a session actually runs at

**Why.** A launch that ran thinner than the product (a dropped rung, a reply
relay in passthrough, a tool that could not execute, a tool the inbound spec
does not know) used to be visible only as a terminal banner nobody reads,
while the session list showed a healthy-looking row. The components now put
their real posture on the record, and the session list shows one chip per
session, so everyday use doubles as a continuous test.

**Events (event-model.ts, `EVENT_KINDS`):**

| kind | emitter | when | carries |
|---|---|---|---|
| `launch_posture` | launcher | after every rung is applied, before the spawn | `live[]` (rung names), `dropped[]` (banner lines), `notes[]` (capped), `target`, `argv0`; `batchId` (from `MANDU_BATCH_ID`, also on `session_exit`); `protection: {mode, integrity, confidentiality, reported}` (the effective axes, §4.2f); `agentVersion: {agent, name, version, verdict, min, max}` (the launcher's `--version` probe against the tested range, supported-agents.md); `secrets: {posture, gap?}` (§4.23); `batchMember: {kind: "scenario"\|"posture", key}` (from `MANDU_BATCH_MEMBER`, §4.22) |
| `relay_mode` | reply-filter | at its mode decision; again when its lookups start failing and when they answer again (reply-row-reservation.md §18) | `mode` (pty / pipe / passthrough) and the reason; `resolveFailure` (the error, no value) while the arbiter does not resolve |
| `client_info` | anthropic-proxy | first request of a session | `userAgent`, `clientVersion` (`claude-cli/<v>`), `clientModel` |
| `tool_surface` | anthropic-proxy | first request that carries a tool battery (the very first request is often a tool-less side call) | `names[]` advertised, `unknown[]` per the arbiter's `toolSurface` op |
| `session_exit` | launcher | when the agent exits | `code`, `durationMs`; `discardedWrites[]` when the session changed a protected file's placeholder copy (the files by path, never content; the summary text shows them with control and format characters as `?`; shown in the `/dev/` inspector, not on the product page; confidentiality-plan-10-flow-taint.md §4.1) |

The launcher builds `launch_posture` from the same banner lines a human sees
(`launcher/src/services/observe.ts postureFindings`), classified with the
phrases the differential harness's posture oracle uses
(`wrappedPostureFindings`), so the chip and the CI gate agree on "thinner
than the product". The proxy asks the arbiter which advertised tool names
have no inbound spec (`toolSurface`, tool-inbound.ts `unknownToolNames`):
their outputs fail closed, and a new agent release that adds a tool is
exactly the drift this surfaces. A session graded before a tool was mapped
keeps its verdict: the event that graded it is immutable history.

**Verdict (session-health.ts `deriveHealth`, on `SessionRef.health`):**

- `ok` — full posture, relay pty/pipe, conversation turns flowed, every
  advertised tool known, no command that could not run;
- `degraded` — the session works but thinner: a dropped or degraded rung, an
  unknown tool, an agent version outside the tested range (supported-agents.md:
  `client_info`'s version for Claude Code, else `launch_posture.agentVersion`,
  re-checked against the dashboard's own table; an unreadable version is a
  reason only), a command run that could not execute (`Exit code 126/127`,
  `bwrap: …`, `command not found`, `Operation not permitted`), or secrets
  `gated` (§4.23);
- `broken` — the session cannot be doing its job: relay in PASSTHROUGH
  (symbols stay opaque on the terminal), a relay whose LAST record carries
  `resolveFailure` (it runs, but the arbiter refuses or does not answer its
  lookups: the S8 miss, reply-row-reservation.md §18), model calls but no
  completed conversation turn, or every command run failing (as many failed
  command runs as the proxies' `exec_action` gate records);
- absent — no `launch_posture` (a proxy-only or test-harness trace).

**A command run that could not execute (2026-10-07).** Only a command
tool's results are read: a file or a web page may well say "command not
found". The proxies record a `tool_result` (and a `symbolize`) with its call
id only, never a tool name, so the result's tool is the one its call named:
the call's `tool_use` event (`Name({args})`), else the `→ Name(…)` line
before its `[tool_result <id>]` in a model call's transcript
(`tool-calls.ts` `extractToolUses`); an event that names its own tool keeps
it. A command tool is any tool `tool-family.ts` puts in the `exec` family,
so every supported agent's are read (Claude Code's `Bash` and `Monitor`,
Codex's `exec_command`, `shell_command`, `shell` and `local_shell`,
OpenClaw's `exec`, OpenCode's and Goose's `bash` / `shell`). Exit 126 and
127 are read as each runtime heads its output: Claude Code's `Exit code
127`, Codex's classic shell `Exit code: 127`, its unified exec `Process
exited with code 127` and its script cell `Script failed (exit code 127)`.
A failing call counts once, however many requests re-send its result, and
the calls are read only once some result's text matches, so grading the
session list stays cheap. Until this change the check read a `tool` field
no emitter writes, and the chip never counted a failure in a real session;
Codex's heads and `shell_command` were not read either. Unit
`session-health.test.ts`; stack `session-health-tool-failures.test.ts`
(the real proxies on their production wiring, the launcher's posture
event, `/api/sessions` over a real `ArbiterEventSource`).

**The words say "command" (2026-10-07).** Since the check reads only
command results, a failed `Read` or `WebFetch` is never counted, so the row
chip reads `1 command could not run` / `N commands could not run` (it read
`N tool failed`), and its tooltip says "commands the AI ran that could not
execute (exit 126/127: a sandbox or lookup failure)". The dot's reasons read
`1 command run could not execute (exit 126/127, sandbox or lookup
failure)` (`N command runs …` for several) and `every command run (N)
could not execute`. The `SessionRef.health.toolFailures` field keeps its name, the
wire shape an open inspector tab reads. Unit `session-health.test.ts` and
UI `app-js-sessions-page.test.ts`; stack
`session-health-tool-failures.test.ts` (the reasons on `/api/sessions`, the
chip in the served `/dev/js/app.js`).

**Chip.** `● ok` (green), `◐ degraded` (amber), `○ broken` (red) beside the
status badge; the tooltip lists the reasons verbatim plus the agent's
version, the live rungs, the relay mode, the turn count and the exit code.
Computed in the session-summary pass of both event sources and cached with
the ref, so the list stays cheap.

**Every agent's version (2026-10-07).** The tooltip and the session header
(§4.33) read the version check health resolved (`health.agentVersion`:
`client_info`'s version for Claude Code, else the launcher's `--version`
probe on `launch_posture`), so a Codex, OpenCode, Goose or OpenClaw session
names its version too; they read only `clientVersion` before, which only
