the anthropic-proxy fills, from Claude Code's user-agent. The tooltip names
the agent and the range the version was checked against ("Codex 0.160.0
(tested: 0.136.0 to 0.160.0)"; it read "claude-code 2.1.289", the
user-agent's token, for Claude Code only); an older server's ref with no
check falls back to `clientVersion` with no range. Inspector only (app.js
`agentVersionOf`). UI `app-js-sessions-page.test.ts` and
`app-js-drills-tests.test.ts`; stack `inspector-agent-version.test.ts` (the
launcher's real posture and version check, both real proxies, a real
`DashboardServer` over a real `ArbiterEventSource`, its `/api/sessions` and
`/api/events` rendered by the real inspector bundle).

**A preview agent (2026-10-09).** Goose, OpenCode 2 and (since the same
day) OpenCode 1 are a *preview* (supported-agents.md §2.0): each launch says
so in one line before the
agent starts, and `mandu doctor` on its version row, but until this change
the dashboard showed their sessions exactly like a Claude Code one. Now
health carries `preview`, the label of the tested line the agent's version
belongs to ("Goose", "OpenCode 2", "OpenCode" for OpenCode 1), judged on
the dashboard's own table
(`agent-versions.ts` `previewLineOf`, over the mirrored `supportStatusOf`
and `rangeLabel`; an unreadable Goose version is still Goose), never read
off the launch's notes. It is a note, never a downgrade: the verdict stays
`ok`, and the reasons carry "Goose support is a preview: tested less than
Claude Code and Codex". Where it shows:

- **The inspector**: the chip's tooltip carries that note, and the session
  header reads "Goose 1.53.0 (preview)", the note on hover.
- **The product page** (§4.25): a **Preview** tag by the agent's name on
  its Home row and on its agent page (home.ts `agentPreview`, on
  `HomeAgent.preview` and `AgentPageVM.preview`: the label, the sentence,
  the address problems go to). The tag is the "?" help drawn as the page's
  tags (home.js `agentPreviewMark` over `helpButton`): a click opens "Goose
  support is a preview: Mandu was tested less with it than with Claude Code
  and Codex. Report a problem." with a link to the launcher's `ISSUES_URL`
  (`rel="noopener noreferrer"`: the page's address names the session). It
  sits before the version's warning mark, which keeps its own sentence.
  The words say nothing about what Mandu enforces: the status is about how
  much testing stands behind the agent.
- **The version's warning on the agent page** (2026-10-09). The warning
  mark by a Home row's name (home.ts `agentNotice`: a version outside the
  tested range, or tools Mandu does not know where the level masks their
  output; supported-agents.md §3) was drawn on the row only, so the page
  "Details" opens said "Goose" and its tag and nothing about a Goose 1.54.0
  being newer than tested. `AgentPageVM.notice` now carries the same
  sentence, from the same function over the session's health, worded for
  the level running now as the row's is (the route passes `masking` from
  the Home view-model it builds), and home.js draws the same mark
  (`agentNoticeMark`) by the agent's name, after the tag, in the row's
  order. A tested version, a session with no version check, or no session
  draws none.
- **The name says the generation** (2026-10-09). The product page named a
  session by its agent kind only (home.ts `AGENT_NAMES`), so an OpenCode 2
  session read "OpenCode [Preview]" on Home, with a tag that opened "OpenCode
  2 support is a preview …", while the launch line and `mandu doctor` said
  "OpenCode 2". OpenCode 1 and 2 are different lines to Mandu (their own
  tested ranges, launch rule and status), so a person running both saw two
  "OpenCode" rows, one tagged. Now home.ts `agentName(kind, health)` adds the
  generation when the session's own version check, made for that same
  agent, belongs to a later tested line (`agent-versions.ts`
  `generationOf`, over the mirrored `TESTED_AGENT_GENERATIONS`): "OpenCode 2"
  on its Home row, its agent page's heading and tab title, and the asks it
  raised ("OpenCode 2 wants to send …", waiting and answered; `agentOf`
  carries each session's health, so an ask from a test session says it too).
  OpenCode 1, a session with no version check or an unreadable version, and
  every other agent keep the kind's name; OpenCode 1's tag says "OpenCode",
  the same name. The inspector, which shows the
  version itself ("OpenCode 2.0.23 (preview)"), is unchanged.

`MANDU_PREVIEW_NOTICE=0` hides the launch line only; the dashboard's tag is
a label, not a notice, and stays. A session with no version check (an older
launcher) is claimed to be nothing. Unit `agent-versions.test.ts`,
`agent-page.test.ts`; UI `home-js-home.test.ts`, `home-js-agent.test.ts`,
`app-js-sessions-page.test.ts`; stack `agent-versions-parity.test.ts` (the
mirrors equal, the labels the launch notice uses) and
`agent-preview-dashboard.test.ts` (the launcher's real version checks and
notices for Goose, OpenCode 2, OpenCode 1, Claude Code and a Goose with the
notice off;
a Goose read of a labelled file through the real anthropic-proxy; a real
`DashboardServer`: `/api/home`, `/api/home/agent`, the served Home and agent
pages, the real inspector bundle, and the no-value oracle; a Goose 1.55.0
launch, newer than tested, whose page carries its row's warning and draws
the mark after the tag; an OpenCode 1.18.13 launch and an OpenCode 2 send
asked by the arbiter's real egress gate: "OpenCode 2" on its row, its page
and its waiting card, "OpenCode" with its own tag for OpenCode 1). The name:
unit `agent-versions.test.ts` (`generationOf`, `agentName`, the Home rows
and asks) and `agent-page.test.ts`.

**The user-side twin.** `mandu doctor --live` (packaging.md §7b) runs the
same checks on demand.

### 4.22 ▶ Watch (🎬 Drills) — live drills through a real TUI, recorded and graded

**Why.** The live e2e suites prove the invariant headlessly, and the
interactive suites drive a PTY nobody looks at. A human asking "is Mandu
working with my Claude Code" wants to type the drill prompts
(`docs/testing/drills.md`) into a real `mandu claude`, watch, and know
afterwards which security and utility checks held. §4.22 makes that a
dashboard action with a permanent record.

The drill catalog, runner and seed script this section drives are the
maintainers' evidence tooling and are not in the public tree (decided
2026-10-08); the commands it shows (the re-run line, the seed script) run in
the maintainers' repository. What the drills show is in
[`drill-results.md`](../../testing/drill-results.md); to get access to them,
write to hello@mandusecurity.com.

**No drill tree** (2026-10-10). The dashboard finds the drill tree in one
place, `src/drill-tree.ts`, as `test-organization.md` §5 "The drill tree"
describes. That covers the catalog index the matrix and the short badges read
(`drill-matrix.ts readCatalog`), the live runner a Watch run and the scenario
listing spawn, and the files the listing is stamped with (`drill-runs.ts
buildWatchArgv`, `scenarioInputs`, §4.30). It also covers the agent suites'
files that the setup banner's repro line and the spec browser name
(`test-setup.ts SUITE_LABELS`, marked `inDrillTree`). Each of them names a
drill file by its path under the tree's root. Where the checkout has no tree
(the public tree, an installed bundle):

- `readCatalog` reports "drills are not available in this checkout (it has
  no drill suite)", so the matrix shows it.
- `WatchRunner.scenarios()` rejects and `start()` throws
  `DrillsUnavailableError`. `GET /api/drills/scenarios` and `POST
  /api/drills` answer 503 `{error, unavailable: true}`, and no child is
  spawned. The boot warm-up skips the listing.
- An agent-suite session's banner keeps its label but has no repro line,
  and the spec browser skips those suites.

The run list (`GET /api/drills`) and the stores read as before. Tests:
`drill-tree.test.ts` (the resolver, and its parity with
`scripts/drill-tree.mjs`), `drill-matrix.test.ts`, `drill-routes.test.ts`,
`test-setup.test.ts` and `drills-js.test.ts` (the no-tree cases).

**Placement.** Not a page of its own: the Drills page (§4.32) lists the
runs (its **Replay | Live** switch on Live) and **▶ Run drills** opens the
launcher (`#run-drills-dialog`, `dev/js/drills.js`, `#drills-panel`; a
third ▶ Run drawer tab until §4.32), with a scenario picker and quick picks,
a model box, an unattended switch, the live log and the run list. Each run
is one live batch in the Drills list (one group per run, §4.35); selecting
one of its sessions shows the **drill strip**, Recording & checks · Trace ·
Secrets · Files · Setup (§4.35), whose parts are the **recording panel**
(`#drill-run-panel`) described below: the player, the chapters, the checks
as a compact table per turn and a model run's matrix in Recording & checks;
the run's files and the 🌱 prepared workspace in Files; the run's facts
(status, agent and model, the scenario and its setting, the session line
with its tmux attach, the workspace, what to watch for, the re-run command
`cd tests && npm run drills:run -- --ids <id>`) in Setup; the verdict and
tallies as chips in the session header. The launcher was named 🎬 Watch
earlier: the old `/api/watch*` routes still answer as the `/api/drills*`
handlers, behind the same gates, for one release (`server.ts`). Internal
identifiers (`WatchRunner`, `SidebarWatchRun`, `.watch-*` classes, run ids
`watch-<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS>`) keep the old name. Tests: `run-views-js.test.ts`,
`index-html.test.ts`, `drill-routes.test.ts` (the old routes answer as the
new ones; a mutating one is still behind CSRF).

**Pieces.**

| piece | where | role |
|---|---|---|
| the runner | `drill-run.ts` + `drill-*.ts`; the drill catalog (all in the maintainers' drill suite, not published) | puts `mandu … <agent>` in a tmux pane, types each scenario's prompts, waits on the arbiter's `countConversationTurns`, answers the agent's dialogs from the screen, grades each turn with the e2e assertion library. **One agent session per scenario**: scope `<runId>-<scenario key>`, relaunched in the same pane (`tmux respawn-pane -k`) after the previous one exits, so no scenario sees another's context, cached tool results or TUI state, a wedged TUI costs one scenario, and each scenario is its own sidebar row. `--shared-session` keeps one launch per setting group with `/clear` between scenarios, for a quick smoke |
| the recording | `tmux pipe-pane` → `lib/asciicast-pipe.mjs` | every byte the pane's program writes → asciicast v2, **one cast per scenario** (`terminal-<key>.cast`). The pane opens on a placeholder and every launch is a `respawn-pane` with the pipe attached first (a pipe misses bytes written before it starts and survives a respawn), so each cast opens on its own launch banner. `chapters.json` carries each scenario's `scopeId`, `cast`, turn offsets on that cast's clock, verdict and tally |
| the store | `~/.mandu/runs/drills/live/<runId>/` (path table `live-drill-runs`), read by `src/drill-run-store.ts` | `meta.json` (status running/done/aborted, pid, session and cast per scenario key, tmux hint, `settings`, `target`, `workspaces`), `chapters.json`, `report.json`/`.md`, `matrix.json`, `run.log`, pane captures, `seed-<key>.json`. A CI run's records arrive as `<CI run>.<drill run>/` with a `ci-run.json` marker and each session's `events-<session>.ndjson`, neither of which the route serves (continuous-integration.md §6; the event lanes below) |
| the launcher | `src/drill-runs.ts` `WatchRunner` | the test runner's twin: package-local tsx, argv array, `shell:false`, `TMUX` unset (always a detached session a human can attach to), one run at a time, SIGTERM → tmux kill-session → SIGKILL |
| the routes | the developer view's `drill-routes.ts` | `GET /api/drills` (list, current run, the `store` directory), `GET /api/drills/scenarios` (the runner's `--list-json`, cached), `POST /api/drills` and `/api/drills/cancel` (CSRF + admin session), `GET /api/drills/runs/<id>` (the sidecars, a whitelisted file list and `lostCasts`), `GET …/file/<name>` (fixed name shapes only, never `meta.json`), `GET /api/drills/<id>/stream` (SSE), `GET`/`POST /api/drills/replay` (a local replay run of one drill, §4.35). A run dir or file that is gone, or a file that is not a regular file, is a 404 with `recordLost: true` (and `out` when its pointer says where the record went), never a 500; a run still in progress whose record is outside the store and not readable yet is a 404 with `recordPending: true` and `out`; a live run read from its own `--out` carries `recordAt` |
| the sidebar chip | `SessionRef.watch` (contract.ts), joined in `buildSidebarSections`; app.js `watchBadge` | a session a drill run drove carries 🎬 (solid: its own cast exists; struck: the run did not record), or a plain `record lost` chip when the recording is gone. A one-scenario session is named by the scenario's title, carries a **scenario-id badge** and its own verdict in the P/R/F badge (PASS → P, FAIL/TIMEOUT/PAUSED → F, WARN → −, still running → R), ordered in the run's order. The id comes from `SessionRef.batchMember` (set by the runner through `MANDU_BATCH_MEMBER` and recorded on `launch_posture`; a `posture:<setting>` member reads "<setting> group", dashed), else from the run's chapters, else from the session id (`<runId>-<key>`); the tooltip says which. Since 2026-10-03 the badge shows the drill's **short index** (`util-c5`, `con-c17` since 2026-10-16; §4.35, `SessionRef.drillShort`) when the server's catalog join names the drill, an old key mapped through it (`S6` → util-c17); the key as recorded otherwise. A session launched by hand has no chip: only the runner records |

**The recording panel (`drills.js`).** One row, one video: when the
selected session is one scenario (`chapterForSession`), the player
(asciinema-player, vendored under `dev/vendor/`, Apache-2.0) mounts that
scenario's own cast (`castToMount`), the scrubber markers and the chips
under it are its turns (a turn that never completed is flagged TIMEOUT),
and the panel shows that scenario only: its setting, its session line, its
cast and the run-level files, and its result unfolded. Siblings are the
sidebar's other rows of the batch; nothing of theirs appears in the main
column. A shared-session run shows the whole run, failures unfolded,
because every scenario ran in the selected session. Continuous playback of
a whole battery is not offered.

- *Answers are stops.* The runner records `done` per turn: the cast-clock
  second at which the answer was on screen and settled. Each answer gets a
  `turn N · answer` marker and a chip; clicking the chip jumps there,
  paused. During playback an answer marker pauses for `OUTPUT_HOLD_MS`
  (5 s), then continues; a seek or the viewer's own play cancels the
  pending resume. Prompt markers never hold. Older runs without `done` take
  the frame before the last ≥ 1.5 s quiet stretch of the turn.
- *The player's clock is not the recording's.* The player trims idle gaps to
  `idleTimeLimit` (2 s) but does not apply that cut to `markers` or
  `seek()`, so the panel fetches the cast once, rebuilds the same cut
  (`cast-clock.js`: `castEventTimes` → `buildTimeline`) and maps every
  marker, seek and chip time through `playerTime`. If the fetch fails the
  player mounts by URL unconverted; a 404 means the file is gone and shows
  "Record lost" instead of a player, and a 403 (signed out, §6) says "Sign
  in to watch this recording: run `mandu dashboard` …" instead (until
  2026-10-09 it mounted the player on the refused URL, which showed the
  player's 💥 error frame). A fetch that lands after another cast was
  mounted is dropped.
- *Record lost.* A run's recording can be gone while its sessions' events
  remain (a deleted run dir, an `--out` outside the store). Such runs are
  **marked, not hidden**, and the server decides: `drill-run-store.ts
  lostCastsOf` lists the casts the record names that the run dir lacks
  (none while running), and `summarize` flags the scenario and, when every
  cast is gone, the run. `buildSidebarSections(…, { watchStoreRead })` marks
  a drill session whose run is not in the store `recordLost` /
  `runMissing`; without a store read nothing is marked (absence from a list
  nobody read proves nothing). The inspector shows a `record lost` chip on
  the row and the batch, says it in one line where the recording would be
  (the why one unfold away; the panel's title reads `<run> · record lost`),
  names each lost cast in words without linking it, and still shows the
  verdicts. A
  focused scenario mounts its own cast or nothing. Replay drills (§4.28)
  carry the same mark. The product page shows no recordings, so it is
  unchanged.
- *A record outside the store is not lost while its run runs* (2026-10-03).
  A run started with an `--out` outside the store, or under a temporary
  home, read "record lost" from its first second until someone copied its
  directory in. The runner now leaves the store a **pointer**,
  `<store>/.outside/<runId>.json` (`drill-launch.ts writeOutsidePointer`,
  written atomically, 0600: `{schema: 1, runId, pid, out, startedAt}`, `out`
  the directory the run declared, absolute and normalized). The dashboard
  (`drill-run-store.ts readOutsidePointer`, `outsideRun`) reads the pointer
  strictly (exactly those fields, the file's own run id, a pid above 1, an
  absolute path equal to its `resolve()`, no control text, capped, no
  symlink) and tells four cases apart:
  - *running, its record readable there*: the runner's pid is alive and
    `out` is a real directory (not a symlink) whose `meta.json` names this
    run **and** this pid. The run is listed and its detail and files are read
    from `out`, read-only, through the store's own readers; the detail and
    summary carry `recordAt: out`, and Setup says "read from `<out>` while
    the run is in progress (outside the watch store)";
  - *running, not readable yet* (no such meta yet, another runner's record,
    a symlinked directory): the run is listed as running with
    `recordPending` (`pendingSummary`), `GET /api/drills/runs/<id>` answers
    404 `{recordPending: true, out}`, and the rows and the batch read
    **"running · record not in the store yet"** (`.s-record-pending`, the
    accent, not the warn colour; `SessionRef.watch.recordPending`,
    `SessionBatch.recordPending`); the panel says so where the recording
    would be (drills.js `showPendingRecord`) and the next poll opens the
    record once it is readable;
  - *finished, not copied in* (the pid is gone): record lost as before, and
    the 404 names where it went (`{recordLost: true, out}`), so the fold
    says `cp -a <out> <store>/`;
  - *finished and copied*: the store's copy is read first, as any stored run.
  Only the declared directory is read, only while the run is alive, only the
  names `RUN_FILE_RE` allows (no separator, so no traversal), and outside
  the store a symlinked file is refused (`lstat`). The pointer is a runner's
  claim about its own record, so a hostile one can at most show a directory
  whose `meta.json` already names that run and that live pid. Tests:
  `test/unit/drill-run-outside.test.ts`, the real-server
  `test/component/drill-record-outside.test.ts` (running outside, running
  and not readable, finished and lost, finished and copied, hostile
  pointers), `drills-js.test.ts`, `app-js-sidebar.test.ts`, and
  `drill-record-pointer.test.ts` (the runner's writer is the
  dashboard's reader).

**A CI live run's event lanes (built 2026-10-03).** A local drill run
against the shared arbiter has its sessions in the dashboard's own arbiter
(the test tenant), so their traces come from it (one with its own arbiter:
the next paragraph). A nightly's drill runs in a CI guest against the run's
own arbiter, which is discarded with the guest; the pipeline carries each
named session's event log out with the record, and the collector stores it
as `<run>/events-<session>.ndjson`, the session id namespaced by the CI run
(`<CI part>.<guest session>`, so it reads `<run>-<key>` like a local one;
continuous-integration.md §6). `src/event-source/ci-live-source.ts`
`CiLiveEventSource` serves those logs:

- **What it lists:** only a run carrying `ci-run.json` (a regular file),
  only a session the run names (`meta.sessions`, the chapters' `scopeId`),
  only its own log (no symlink, at most 32 MiB, `bounded-read.ts`), and the
  newest 50 such runs. A row is derived from the events as the file source
  derives a local one's, its `batchId` the host run, so the sidebar joins
  it to the run's batch in the Drills list and the drill matrix's live cell
  opens it like a local session.
- **How it reads:** every event stamped with the host session id and, where
  it had one, the host run as `batchId`; a log is re-read only when its
  identity changes, and the parsed events of the last 16 opened are kept.
- **What it owns:** `owns(id)` is true only for a session id whose prefix
  before a `-` names a marked run holding that log and naming that session.
  An id without a `.` (every local session) costs no syscall, and a local
  session never resolves to it.
- **Read-only, no arbiter:** `subscribe` is a no-op, a delete is a 403
  (`read-only`), and the server routes a CI id's reads to this source alone
  (`RecordedSources`, beside the replay store's `RecordedEventSource`,
  through `CompositeEventSource.sourceFor` and `sessionSource`), never to
  the tenant's store. A log's `$MDU:*` tokens belong to the guest's arbiter;
  resolving them against the host's table would show another table's values.
  The trace shows the log's own originals (`DualRepr.original`), as for any
  session.
- **Confidentiality:** the logs hold the drill's synthetic data. The store
  is owner-only (0700 / 0600, like every event log under `~/.mandu`), and
  the product page (`/api/home`) never lists a drill.

**A local run's own arbiter (built 2026-10-03).** A run started with
`drill-run.ts --own-arbiter` (the normal way to run the conf drills: the
hold drills need its admin socket, and so does the drill recorder's symbol
directory; drill-runner.md §3) runs every session against a PRIVATE
arbiter whose work dir is `<run dir>/arbiter`, so the logs are
`<run dir>/arbiter/events/<session>.ndjson`, in no arbiter the dashboard
talks to. Until this was built `/api/drills` listed such a run, running, and
the Drills list showed none of its sessions. `src/event-source/own-arbiter-source.ts`
`OwnArbiterEventSource` serves those logs, the third source in
`RecordedSources`:

- **What it lists:** only a run the live store reads (`readRun`: the store's
  run directory, or an in-progress run's own `--out` through its pointer,
  above), not one a CI collector brought (`ci-run.json`: the CI source's),
  whose `meta.json` carries `arbiter` (the runner writes it with
  `--own-arbiter`), and only `<that run dir>/arbiter/events` when both
  components are real directories (`lstat`, no symlink). No path is read out
  of the meta: a run whose arbiter work dir fell back to a temporary
  directory (a socket path over 100 bytes, `drill-arbiter.ts
  ownArbiterWorkDir`) is not served. Only a session the run names
  (`meta.sessions`, the chapters' `scopeId`) whose id is `<runId>-…` (the
  runner's scope ids) and a plain file name, so the arbiter's system logs
  (`arbiter-admin`, `net-guard`) are never rows; only its own log, opened
  without following a symlink, a regular file, at most 32 MiB read (a larger
  one shows the events within its first 32 MiB). The newest 50 such runs.
- **The ids as minted:** the private arbiter's ids are `<runId>-<key>`, and
  the run sent nothing to the dashboard's arbiter, so the main store holds
  none of them: they stay un-namespaced, and the live-row join
  (`session-batches.ts`: the run's batch, the 🎬 annotation, the verdict
  mark, the index badge, the recording and the per-turn verdicts;
  `drill-run-store.ts`, `drillShort`) applies unchanged: the rows read
  exactly as a shared-arbiter run's. Should an id be in both (a reused
  `--run-id`), `CompositeEventSource.listSessions` keeps the recorded side's
  row only, where its reads go.
- **Live while it runs:** a listing lstats each named log and re-derives a
  row (the file source's derivations, `ciLiveSessionRef`) only when the log
  moved (size, mtime, inode). A moved log is read INCREMENTALLY
  (`readLogTail`: only the bytes appended since, up to the last complete
  line, so a half-written line waits for its end; a replaced or shrunk log
  is read again whole), and the parsed events of the last 32 sessions read
  are kept. A session the runner launches shows on the next poll once the
  meta names it and its log exists. `subscribe` tails the log by polling it
  every second: `/api/stream` streams appended events (after `sinceSeq`), as
  for an arbiter session. Once the run ends the logs are static and cost one
  lstat each.
- **What it owns:** `owns(id)` is true only when a prefix of the id before
  a `-` names an own-arbiter run that names the session and holds its log;
  looked up on disk each time (a handful of syscalls per `/api/events`).
- **Read-only, no arbiter (the confidentiality invariant, applied to the
  dashboard):** no policy, no desymbolize, no symbol resolution. A log's
  `$MDU:*` tokens belong to the run's private arbiter; resolving them
  against the dashboard's arbiter would show another table's values under
  this trace (or a value that table holds under a token that never named
  it), so the server routes an owned id's reads to this source alone
  (`sourceFor`, `sessionSource`), a delete is a 403 (`read-only`), and the
  trace shows the log's own originals (`DualRepr.original`): the drill's
  synthetic data, in the owner-only store. The product page never lists a
  drill.

**Workspaces.** Each session runs in a **freshly seeded, isolated
workspace** (`ws-<hash of the key>`, a neutral name, under the run's workspace root, never inside a
Mandu home; `isolatedWorkspaceDir`, `scripts/drill-seed.sh`), seeded before
the launch so fs-sync mints the twins from it, with its own nonce and git.
A shared workspace let a utility check pass on a file an earlier scenario
left and mixed every session's commits in one dual-view log. `--ws DIR` opts
back into one shared, pre-seeded workspace. A scenario whose policy label
precondition is verifiably unmet is skipped, not graded (without the label
the session never goes HIGH); a `policy.yaml` pattern can cover the
isolated workspaces' changing paths.

**🌱 Prepared workspace.** Right before each launch the runner captures the
workspace (`drill-seed.ts collectWorkspaceSeed` → `seed-<key>.json`): the
seed script, the workspace's own git log, and every file (8 KB cap, 200
files) tagged `seeded`, `changed`, `added` or `ignored` against that git.
`annotateSeedLabels` then asks the session's arbiter for each file's level
(`pathLevel` by absolute HumanView path, read-only, data socket) — at
launch, because a label applies when a symbol is minted and a later lookup
could report a label the session never ran under. `pathLevel.rule` says
what decided (`label:<path>`, `derived:<path>`, `prefix:…` / `shape:…`, or
null = public by default); it is observability only. Labelling is all or
nothing per capture (`labels.status`: `captured`, `axis-off`,
`unavailable`): a half-labelled list would read as "the rest are public".
The panel's fold lists the files the prompt names first, inserts content as
text, and shows a chip per file in the Protection matrix's words (🔒 hidden
secret, 🔑 usable secret, public); a `public` a human label decided reads
`public · your rule`, an unknown level renders as the strictest, and an
arbiter that does not report `rule` reads "decided by: not reported", never
"public by default". The capture is HumanView content, a run artifact that
never enters a model context. Signed out the file route refuses it (403,
§6) and the fold keeps its workspace and seed-script lines and says "Sign in
to see the files <id> started from: run `mandu dashboard` …"; a listed
capture that fails to load otherwise says "Could not read this run's
prepared-workspace capture (seed-<key>.json)". Only a run that lists no
capture says it "is older than the prepared-workspace capture" (until
2026-10-09 a refused or failed load said that too).

**Grading contract.** Every prompt step carries checks resolved by the
shared evaluators (`tests/lib/assertions-*`). Security: symbolized under a
callId new to the turn, raw injection absent from model ingress, no
sabotage `tool_use`, the exec/net/fs gate fired, canary absent from every
model-facing surface (`canary_absent` also tries base64 at three
alignments, hex, reversed and rot13), `net_not_forwarded`,
`net_secret_withheld` (what a host received holds the canary in no
spelling; nothing received needs a block naming the host),
`file_not_contains`. Utility: the answer on the settled screen, no raw
`$MDU:` token on it, a file in the HumanView, nothing over-symbolized,
`net_forwarded` (the allowed half of a paired flow). Downgrades to WARN,
never FAIL: a gate the model never attempted ("gate not exercised"), and a
scenario whose `requiresTools` the session's `tool_surface` shows the
client never offered. A value that may arrive as one multi-line symbol is
graded with `human_sees`, which accepts the settled pane or the reply
filter's resolved frame, because the PTY relay renders such a value as one
clipped row (differential-interactive.md §10). Soft checks `twin_note` and
`twin_route` grade the symbol-twin signal of
symbol-twin-shell-blindness.md §4.6. Verdicts per scenario: PASS / WARN /
FAIL / TIMEOUT / PAUSED (the model's safeguards paused the session; counted
with the fails; drill-runner.md §3), with a security n/m · utility n/m
tally.

**Why a session per scenario.** The alternative was to split one long
session into per-scenario segments in the dashboard. That would have added
a second addressing scheme (session plus segment) to selection, deep links,
deletion, health, violated roll-ups and the transcript filter, for one
runner's benefit. A relaunch costs a few seconds per scenario and in
exchange every dashboard concept applies unchanged (a real session id, its
own health chip, events, deletion and deep link), scenarios become
genuinely independent (no cross-scenario evidence to key away), and a
wedged TUI takes down one scenario. One cast per scenario follows for the
same reason: row = session = video, each video opens on its own launch
banner (the health chip's evidence), and files stay small.

**Variants, matrix, steps.** `--models a,b,c` and `--repeat N` turn each
scenario into (scenario, model, repetition) variants, each its own session;
a variant key (`variantKey`, e.g. `<id>@sonnet#2`) stands wherever the
scenario id stood (chapters, report, scope id, cast and capture names), so
a variant is simply a row. `buildMatrix` folds results into scenario ×
model cells and per-model totals, including pass^k and sessions with a
**gate not exercised**: the oracles grade Mandu's events and are
model-independent, but a model that declines the command never exercises
the gate, so that pass belongs to the model. The matrix leads `report.md`,
is written to `matrix.json`, rides the run detail (shape-validated) and
renders as a fold with the selected session's cell outlined.
`buildWatchArgv` validates each model name (`MODEL_RE`), caps a run at 6
models and 20 repetitions, and the panel asks before more than 60 sessions;
`--shared-session` refuses both flags. Steps beyond prompts: `command` (a
slash command such as `/compact`, waited out before the turn count is
re-read), `edit` (the human edits a file between turns), `relaunch` (a
second session in the same workspace), and `clarify` (a scripted reply when
a turn ends on a question). Turns stay scripted: a model-played user would
put a second sampled model into every verdict.

**Agents.** The launch row starts with an agent picker: Claude Code, Codex
CLI, OpenCode, OpenClaw (`WATCH_TARGETS`; `--target`,
drill-runner.md §3.2–§3.4). The runner's `--list-json` gives each scenario
`unsupported: {<target>: reason}`, and the picker greys a row only under
the agent it names, and `notRunLive: {<target>: reason}` for a scenario an
agent can run but no live run has graded yet, which stays checkable with a
"not yet run live on <agent>" note
(`dashboard-drill-catalog.test.ts` holds the served notes equal
to the runner's). The unattended switch maps to each agent's
skip-permissions flag (none for OpenClaw, whose drill config has no
approval step). Batch, rows, recording and verdicts are target-agnostic.

**Catalog vocabulary.** Drills have area-prefixed slug ids
(`util-reasoning`, `conf-hold-once`; test-reorganization.md §8 step 4) and an
**area** (`util`, `fidelity`, `conf`, `integ` = the frozen integrity axis,
`policy`, `demo` = the scenarios made for a video; `DRILL_AREAS` mirrors the
catalog's `AREAS`). `buildWatchArgv`
accepts an id only as `^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+){1,7}$`, at most 48
characters (`isDrillId`), so it can never read as a flag; `POST
/api/drills` reads `area` and answers 400 to the retired `category`.
Postures became named **settings** (`secrets`, `secrets-mock-sites`,
`secrets-no-reply-filter`, `off` (observe only: the attack-path recordings, 2026-10-04), `off-cc-mask`, the baselines `baseline-none`, `baseline-cc-mask` and `baseline-cc-deny` (the agent with no Mandu, graded by a neutral recorder of its model traffic, 2026-10-16), and the frozen lane's
`frozen-*`; the drill catalog's `settings.ts`), validated by
`DRILL_SETTINGS` and held equal to the catalog by
`drill-settings-parity.test.ts`; the `MANDU_BATCH_MEMBER` tag
keeps its `posture:` prefix as an environment contract. Each catalog row
carries `area`, `proves`, `agents`, `labels`, `setting`, `frozen`, `core`,
`holds`, `default` and more; the picker groups by area, offers the quick
picks **default set**, **★ core**, one per area, **frozen** and **none**,
and checks exactly the runner's `default` rows (setting `secrets`, no label
precondition, no approval hold). Stored runs are history: a run recorded
under the old ids, postures or categories is read as written, never
renamed.

**Out of scope, on purpose.** Live playback of a running recording (the
panel shows the `tmux attach` hint), applying a scenario's label
preconditions (a label is the human's act; it is printed, not applied),
and more than one run at a time. Local replay runs of one drill are the
dialog's second panel (§4.35 "Replay a drill").

**Tests.** `drill-runs.test.ts`, `session-batches.test.ts`,
`recorded-source.test.ts`, `drills-js.test.ts` (cast clock, holds, markers,
the URL fallback, the agent notes), `app-js-sidebar.test.ts`,
`replay-js.test.ts`, and the component tests `drills-area.test.ts`,
`drill-record-lost.test.ts` (a fixture home with event logs and no store
over the real server: every row and batch lost, 404s, never a 500) and
`drill-missing-record.test.ts`. A CI live run's event lanes:
`event-source/ci-live-source.test.ts` (what is listed, owned and read; the
names the collector writes) and the component test `ci-live-sessions.test.ts`
(a store as the collector writes it over the real server: the Drills batch,
the trace, the 403, the matrix link, nothing sent to the tenant's store);
`scripts/test/ci-collect-results.test.mjs` reads what the collector wrote
back through the source. A local run's own arbiter:
`event-source/own-arbiter-source.test.ts` (what is listed and owned, a
growing log and a new session, the incremental reader, symlinks, the cap,
the polling `subscribe`, the composite's routing and one-row rule, the
runner's work-dir place) and the component test `own-arbiter-sessions.test.ts`
(an in-progress own-arbiter run over the real server: the Drills batch's
live rows, the trace, the log growing in `/api/sessions`, `/api/events` and
`/api/stream`, a new session, the 403, nothing sent to the tenant's store).

### 4.23 Secret posture — confined / read-blocked / gated

Source: [`rootless-confinement-ubuntu-2404.md`](../confidentiality/rootless-confinement-ubuntu-2404.md)
§3.4. A launch with confidentiality on runs at one of three secret postures.
On a stock Ubuntu 24.04 (no AppArmor `userns` grant for bwrap) it is
`gated`: the model never sees a labelled secret and egress is gated, but a
program the agent runs can still read credential files. The dashboard says
so, in the same words as the launch notice and `mandu doctor`.

- **Wire.** The launcher puts `secrets: { posture, gap? }` on
  `launch_posture` (first-class, no banner parsing). `session-health.ts`
  lifts it to `SessionHealth.secrets` with one honest `sentence` and, where
  the gap has one, the `fix` command (`mandu setup` for `apparmor-userns`,
  `sudo apt install bubblewrap` for `no-bwrap`). The sentences mirror
  `launcher/src/confinement-posture.ts`; a parity unit test loads the
  launcher module and holds them equal.
- **Verdict.** `gated` is a known host condition, not an incident: it makes
  the §4.21 verdict **degraded (amber)**, never **broken (red)**, with one
  plain reason.
- **Protection chip.** The chip stays `🛡 Protected · …` (the masking claims
  still hold) and gains `· ⚠ secrets gated` in amber (`.prot-gated`) —
  neither the "⚠ Not protected" off state (a choice) nor the red
  "⛔ Protection failed" banner (an incident). The plain-terms card adds
  "Your secrets are gated, not confined.", the sentence and the upgrade
  command as copyable text.
- **🛡 drawer.** The "Your secrets" header carries a posture chip (green for
  `confined` / `read-blocked`, amber for `gated`) and, when gated with a
  fix, the same command. No posture on record renders nothing, never an
  invented state.
- **Tests.** `session-health.test.ts` (amber not red, one reason, fix table,
  parity), `app-js-protection.test.ts`, `protection-js.test.ts`,
  `test/component/secrets-posture.test.ts` (the launcher's own
  `launchPostureEvent` → file source → `/api/sessions`).

### 4.24 Flow taint on the dashboard — readers, secret items, the note

The flow-taint design
([`confidentiality-plan-10-flow-taint.md`](../confidentiality/confidentiality-plan-10-flow-taint.md))
changed what a `secrets`-mode session does: a program on a file's reader
list opens the real file and its output reaches the model as one secret
symbol with a `[mandu:secret]` note (rule (i)); every other program reads
the structured twin, or is refused once a reader list exists (§3.3). The
dashboard speaks that model:

- **"No list" is not "empty list".** The arbiter's `confidentialityState`
  sends `readers` only when a reader list exists, and with it `others`
  (`deny`, the §3.3 default, or `twin`). The Secrets panel
  (`view-model/secrets.ts readersTextOf`) renders no list as "twin for every
  program", names as "a, b; every other program is refused" (or "gets the
  twin"), and an empty list as "none: every program is refused (the reader
  list is empty)". `SecretRow.readersListed` and `others` carry the
  distinction.
- **The `confined` sentence states the guarantee.** A listed reader (or a
  known consumer) does get the real bytes; it is the reader's output that
  is masked. The sentence says so, identically in
  `launcher/src/confinement-posture.ts` and `dashboard/src/session-health.ts`
  (the §4.23 parity test).
- **Secret items are not "untrusted items".** `SessionFlowStats.secret`
  counts flows rooted at a `nomodel_` / `anymodel_` twin or carrying a
  secret level (`isSecretFlow`); `itemsPhrase` names each kind ("2 secret
  items", "2 untrusted items and 1 secret item"). The lineage summary, the
  protection chip, the plain-terms card, the hero sentence and the drawer's
  verdict all read it, so a secrets-mode session never claims "the AI never
  saw the untrusted contents". `app.js` keeps a client twin of
  `itemsPhrase`.
- **What the note says.** The `[mandu:secret]` note has four forms (plan 10
  §11.8): `masked:` (rule (i) or a backstop hit), `note:` (a listed reader
  whose rule released the output), `denied:` (an open the law or the human
  refused) and `held:` (a hold whose §12.2 ceiling passed). The AgentView
  lane shows the note verbatim under the tool result's symbol; the HumanView
  lane shows the program's real output.
- **Tests.** `secrets-view-model.test.ts` (no list / empty list / `others:
  twin`), `lineage.test.ts` (`itemsPhrase`, `isSecretFlow`),
  `session-health.test.ts` (parity), and the live approval-hold drills
  (the denied note, one hold per program, the masked note under `once`).

### 4.25 Two front-ends on one server — the product page at `/`, the inspector at `/dev/`

**Why.** One page serving two audiences served neither: the §4.18 Simple
register was a hide-list over the expert page, and a hide-list leaks (drill
panels, eleven topbar controls, test sessions and duplicate rule lists all
reached the end user). So the end user gets **their own page**, the inspector
stays as it is, and the two share the server.

**Layout.**

| URL | Directory | Audience | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/` | `dashboard/public/` | the end user (§1 audience 4) | the PRODUCT: Home · Approvals · Rules · Settings |
| `/dev/` | the developer view's (§4.25ac) | developers, reviewers, the invariant auditor (§1 audiences 1–3) | the inspector, §§4.1–4.24, where the build carries it |
| `/api/…`, `/slides/…` | shared | both | the same routes, the same auth, the same tenancy |

`server.ts` serves `publicDir` at the root and `devDir` under `/dev/`. Pages
are paths (§4.25v, `server/page-routes.ts`): each front-end's `index.html`
answers exactly its route table (product: `/`, `/approvals[/<id>]`,
`/agents/<id>`, `/rules`, `/settings`; inspector: `/dev/<page>[/<sub>]`,
`/dev/<page>/<id>`, §4.32), `/dev` is a 302 to `/dev/` with the query kept, a
retired query-string page URL is a 302 to its path form, and every other path
is a static file or a 404. Both index pages get the SAME `<meta
name="base-path">`, so the inspector's `BASE + '/api/…'` fetches hit the shared
root and its relative assets resolve under `/dev/`. The cache-bust token
(`?v=`) is computed per directory from its `*.html|css|js`. No second port,
auth or service unit: the front proxy and `mandu dashboard` land on the
product, and the inspector is one click away (the product's "Details" /
"Developer view" links → `dev/sessions/<id>`; the inspector's **Product ↗**
→ `/`).

**Page frame.** One left-aligned column (`max-width: 1040px`); the top
bar's contents (brand, nav, the protection status) share that width.
Under 640px the bar wraps and nothing scrolls sideways.

**The top bar says on or off (2026-10-15).** The status read "Protection:
Secrets", a level name, when the product ships one level and its Settings
switch says on or off. It now says what the switch says
(`renderTopStatus`):

| The level running | The top bar |
|---|---|
| any level that protects (`secrets`; a frozen one too) | green dot, **Protection on** |
| `off` | amber dot, **Protection off** |
| `unknown` (no protection service) | grey dot, **Protection unknown** |
| no answer from the server | red dot, **Not connected** |

A change saved for the next start adds "· off from the next start" or
"· on from the next start". A change between two levels that protect adds
nothing. `home-js-top-status.test.ts` pins each row and sweeps every pair
for a level name. The developer view's own top bar still names the level.

*Its words lead to the switch (2026-10-18).* The top bar is the one
protection signal on every page, and until 2026-10-18 it led nowhere: on
Rules, Approvals or History a person who read **Protection off** had to know
the switch is Settings' first card. Home's hero links Settings (*The hero
links where it points*), but only on Home. Now, while the top bar says
anything but a plain **Protection on** (off, unknown, not connected, or a
change saved for the next start), its words, tail included, are one link to
Settings (`protectionLink`); the dot stays beside it. A click opens Settings
at the Protection card through `openAtCard` (`openProtection`, as *A link
opens at its card* lands Sensitivity labels): the card scrolls to the top,
and the focus goes to the Protection switch, or to the card's heading while
the switch is disabled (the setting could not be read). On Settings itself
the link still scrolls and focuses. `focusMarked` gives `tabindex="-1"` only
to what is not focusable already, so the switch keeps its place in the tab
order. A modifier click is the browser's: Settings, whose first card is
Protection. **Protection on** stays words, as there is nothing to do. The
link's name says where it goes ("Protection off: open Settings"), and it
draws in the status's own ink, size, gap and nowrap (`.top-status-link`,
underlined on hover and focus), so the bar is no wider: in Chromium the
status measured the same 95 px for "Protection off", and the same bar
heights at 320 to 700 px for the longer tail, before and after. The live
region is still written only when its words change (`sameAsDrawn`). In the
same change, Approvals' intro links the Rules page it names ("remembered
under Rules"). Tests: `home-js-top-status.test.ts` (each row, the click
from Rules, the disabled switch, a modifier click, the level-name sweep over
the link's name, Approvals' intro) and `tests/stack/top-status-opens-protection`
(real arbiter and dashboard, the served styles: from Rules at 1280 and
390 px the click lands on the focused switch, the bar still fits from 641 px,
and at 375 px with a request waiting the page links still fit their row).

**The projection: one GET.** The product page is fed by server projections,
never by the inspector's client. `GET /api/home` (`server/home-routes.ts`)
composes what Home needs so the page makes one fetch per poll (10 s, visible
tab only):

- the session list split by `session-batches`; the product shows **Live**
  only (a drill or e2e session is never someone's work; those stay in the
  inspector's Drills and Tests pages);
- for each live session in the **24-hour window** (`HOME_WINDOW_HOURS`, cap
  `HOME_SESSION_CAP` = 25, newest first, plus every other session in the
  window the listing flags `violated`, so the cap never hides a failure;
  *A busy day* below), its `toSessionViewModel` lineage
  stats, invariant verdict and cwd, and the steps its page's story blocked
  and the sends that left with a real value filled in (`storyCounts` over
  `buildStory`, the agent page's own count), cached per `(id, eventCount,
  lastTs)` in `HomeFacts`, one cache per tenant source, so an unchanged
  session is never re-read;
- the policy-panel VM through the SAME loader the inspector's Policy panel
  uses (`loadPolicyPanel`): posture and the approval queue;
- the configured mode (`readAxesState`), reported beside the RUNNING level.

`view-model/home.ts` (pure, unit-tested) turns that into the `HomeVM`:

- **The verdict ladder**, red never hidden behind green: `unknown` (no
  arbiter: nothing is claimed, Approvals is unknown too) > `failed` (any
  violation in the window) > `off` (both axes off) > `waiting` (asks or rule
  changes pending; with asks, "Protection is holding while you decide: what
  it asks for happens only if you allow it.", "what each one asks for" for
  several; and at Secrets the mode's "Untrusted content is not masked in
  this mode." after it) > `secrets-only` (the built-in
  default; the sentence SAYS untrusted content is not masked, and that keys
  and secret files "leave this computer only where a rule or your OK allows".
  Until 2026-10-05 it said they "cannot leave this machine", while the
  session pages show sends with a secret filled in for its bound host) > `quiet`
  (masking on, nothing untrusted yet) > `protected`. Each carries a headline
  and one sentence; the page never composes copy from counts. The place a
  sentence sends the person is a link (*The hero links where it points*,
  below): `off` says "Turn it back on in Settings", where the switch is. Until
  2026-10-07 the `waiting` sentence went on "Nothing leaves your machine
  until you answer.", at every level. A rule sends a secret to its own host
  while a question waits (§4.25d), most asks are not sends (a program's
  read, a write to a file that runs later, a command), and a held message
  goes masked when nobody answers in time, so the sentence now says only
  what holds for every family. At Secrets it had also hidden the level's
  "not masked" sentence, which the product must say (`CONTRIBUTING.md`,
  protection modes). Tests:
  `home-view-model.test.ts` (each family, Secrets and the frozen levels) and,
  over a real arbiter whose gate lets the secret go to its bound host while
  a question about it waits, `tests/stack/home-waiting-verdict.test.ts`.
- **The hero counts the rule changes waiting, as the badge does** (2026-10-18).
  The Approvals badge and Home's *Approvals waiting (N)* count questions plus
  rule changes (the pending policy proposals the page reads from
  `/api/policy/proposals`), so the hero does too: `buildHome` reads the
  pending proposals through a narrow `proposals` dep (the arbiter's
  `policyProposals`, the same read that route serves) and passes only their
  number (`HomeVM.ruleChangesWaiting`), never a proposal's words; a read that
  fails or an arbiter without the op counts none, and the hero is as before.
  The headline names both: "One question is waiting for you." / "2 questions
  are waiting for you." (questions only, unchanged); "A rule change is
  waiting for you." / "2 rule changes are waiting for you." with "Your rules
  stay as they are until you answer." (rule changes only: a pending proposal
  is not applied until approved, and a held hand edit leaves the rules in
  force, policy-surface.md §8.4.6); "One question and one rule change are
  waiting for you." / "2 questions and 1 rule change are waiting for you."
  (both, with the questions' sentence). At Secrets the mode's disclosure
  follows each. Until then a rule change alone left the hero green, "Your
  secrets are guarded.", over "Approvals waiting (1)" and a badge of 1. The
  ladder's order is unchanged, so a failure is never hidden behind amber;
  under `failed` the facts line's "N waiting for you" counts both. For one
  poll after an answer the hero (`/api/home`) and the badge (the page's own
  proposals read) may differ; they agree once both reads settle. Tests:
  `home-view-model.test.ts`, `home-rule-changes.test.ts` (the read and its
  failures), `home-js-home.test.ts`, and over a real arbiter, a real
  proposal and the production adapter, `tests/stack/home-rule-change-waiting.test.ts`.
- **Asks as sentences.** `describeAsk` (`view-model/ask-words.ts`, shared
  with the inspector's Approvals page, §4.34) renders a queue row by family (send /
  run / read / show) as text parts, plain text plus `code` values: "Claude
  Code wants to send text from a file to `evil.example`", "The program `cat`
  wants to read a secret file: `.env`", plus *why it stopped*, *what the AI
  has now* and *if you click Allow* (§4.25u). A send of a secret names it:
  "Claude Code wants to send your secret `STRIPE_KEY` to `api.stripe.com`"
  (§4.34, *A send names its secret*). A send of a secret the AI read before
  it was marked never says the AI never read it (§4.34, *Read before it was
  marked*). The raw key (`$MDU:…`,
  `open:cat`, `exec-program:`) never reaches the page. Who asked comes from
  the row's `sessions` → the session's agent kind ("Claude Code", "Codex CLI",
  "OpenClaw", "OpenCode", "Goose"; unknown → "The agent"), with the
  generation its own version check names ("OpenCode 2", §4.21 *The name says
  the generation*), looked up over EVERY session (`agentOf`), so an ask raised from a test session still names its agent
  while the session stays off the product. **The asker is the session that
  raised the row last** (`home.ts askedBy`; the arbiter keeps `sessions`
  most-recent-last). One row is one (item, destination) pair, so two sessions
  that send the same secret to the same host share it: the sentence, the
  agent row's `waiting` state, the agent page's asks and the page's "See what
  the agent was doing" link all follow the latest one, and `agents` still
  lists every agent that raised it. Until 2026-10-05 an answered row named
  the FIRST session's agent and a waiting one shared by two agents said "The
  agent": a `mandu codex` send of a secret a Claude Code session had sent to
  api.stripe.com read "Claude Code wants to send a secret to
  api.stripe.com".
- **Agents, not sessions.** One row per live session in the window: agent
  name, label, cwd, its own masked/blocked counts, and a state (`waiting` /
  `running` by the sidebar's recency rule / `idle`). **Every row's first
  line is what you asked and where** (home.js `promptLine`, shared by
  Running now, Earlier and History): the prompt label, then " in
  `~/projects/shop`" from `cwd` (`shortPath`, the folder whole), both whole
  on hover; "No prompt yet" running, "No prompt reached the AI" ended. **A
  `waiting` row keeps it too** (2026-10-18): the amber dot says it waits,
  and its counts lead with "1 question waiting for you", History's words,
  after "protection failed" when that holds. From 2026-10-07 the state took
  the prompt's place ("Waiting for your OK", before that "Paused, waiting
  for your OK", but a refused send, command or file open does not stop the
  agent; nothing says paused still), with "1 waiting for you" trailing the
  counts. So Home and History described the same session two ways, and two
  agents waiting at once (when Approvals is busiest) read alike, their
  *Details* named alike unless their folders differed; the prompt tells
  them apart. Earlier drew no folder until then, so a session lost it on
  its way from Running now to Earlier, though `homeAgentRow` serves `cwd`
  for every row. Tests: jsdom `home-js-home.test.ts`,
  `home-js-row-control-names.test.ts`, component `home-earlier.test.ts`,
  `approvals-after-answer.test.ts`, stack `history-says-waiting.test.ts`
  (Home's rows and History's share their first line over the real server).
  The window's `blocked`
  and `sent` add up the sessions' counts (below, *Home counts what the
  session page shows*). **A recorded exit ends "running"**: `HomeFacts`
  carries `exited` from the session page's own rule (agent-page.ts
  `sessionExited`: a `session_exit` with no model call or tool step after
  it), so a `/exit`ed agent leaves *Running now* at once, as its page says
  "ended", instead of after the listing's five quiet minutes (2026-10-05: it
  stayed there beside the agent started after it). The inspector's sidebar
  uses the same rule since 2026-10-06 (`SessionRef.exited`, §4.10.4).
  **The system logs are not agents**
  (`home.ts isAgentSession` over registry.ts `systemLogKind`): the arbiter's
  admin audit log `arbiter-admin`, the net-guard fallback `net-guard` and
  net-proxy's `eg_<a>_<b>` sit in Live's System logs group for the
  inspector's sidebar, but Home never lists them, counts them ("N agents are
  running", the window's counts, History's number) or takes one for a first
  session (the first-run card). Their events stay in the inspector's folded
  System logs group; an approval verdict in the admin log already shows as
  an *Answered earlier* row. Until 2026-10-05 the route took every Live
  batch, so a fresh install's first `mandu claude` read "3 agents are
  running" with two rows named "The agent" (the admin row even said "1 item
  masked": its verdict events name the approved item). Tests:
  `home-view-model.test.ts`, and `home-first-session.test.ts`: the real
  server's `/api/home` and served page over the recorded first sessions
  (`first-session-fixture.ts`): one `mandu claude` that read `.env` (one
  agent, no system-log row, nothing blocked or sent), then that agent
  exited and a `mandu codex` asked to send the same secret (one running,
  the ask named for Codex).
- **Answered earlier**: resolved rows newest-decision-first (newest 20,
  then *Show more*: *Past the newest 20* below; `answeredTotal` counts them
  all) with the
  §8.7 scope made plain ("Always allowed" / "Blocked" / "Allowed once,
  unused" / "Allowed once"), the row's one-click reversal, and the
  `sessions` that raised it, most recent last, as a waiting ask carries
  them: the page links the latest, where it was asked (§4.25h; until
  2026-10-08 the answered row dropped them).

**Past the newest 20 (2026-10-18).** Approvals keeps two lists of past
decisions, *Answered earlier* and *Rule changes*, and until 2026-10-18 each
stopped at 20 rows with nothing after the last: no count, no *Show more*.
Each row carries the only one-click reversal of its answer (*Allow
instead*, *Block instead*, *Send masked instead*) or its *Undo*, and an
*Allowed once* answer is listed nowhere else, so the 21st answer of a busy
afternoon was gone from the page, a reader took the 20 rows for everything,
and `/approvals/<id>` for an older answer said "That question is no longer
waiting for you." as if Mandu had lost it. Both now page as History does
(§4.25ae):

- *Answered earlier* ends with "Showing 20 of 63 answers." and **Show
  more**, which reads `GET /api/home/answered?after=<id>&limit=20`
  (`answeredPage`, view-model/home.ts: the same sort, ties in the queue's
  order, and the same projection as `/api/home`'s `answered`, which is its
  first page; `{ rows, total, next }`; a queue that is not known answers
  503, so the page says why). Its first new row takes the focus; a read
  that fails says why beside the button, which keeps the focus
  (*A Show more that fails*, §4.25ae). The route is `open`, as `/api/home`
  is: it carries nothing `/api/home` does not carry for the newest 20.
- *Rule changes* asks the arbiter's `policyChanges` for one more row than it
  draws (`?limit=21`, then 41, …, up to the route's 500), since the answer
  has no total: when that row came, "Showing the newest 20 changes." and
  **Show more**, which behaves as above.
- The poll keeps the rows brought: on Approvals it reads as many answers
  as are drawn (`followAnswered`, as `followHistory` does), an answer given
  since comes in on top and the rows pushed down stay (`historyFollowed`);
  *Rule changes* re-reads as many as it draws. *Answered earlier* has its
  own redraw key (`sameAsDrawn('answered', …)`), so a poll never draws the
  newest 20 over the 40 brought, and the words of an answer on row 30 go
  back on it (`putBackAnswers('answered', …)`).
- `/approvals/<id>` for an answer past the rows drawn reads the answers
  once (`seekAnswered`, up to 500), draws down to the page that holds it and
  marks it in place: "That question was already answered. Its answer is
  marked below, under Answered earlier." It says "no longer waiting" only
  when the answer is nowhere.
- A link to Approvals starts both lists over at 20, as a link to History
  does; Back keeps the rows brought. The three *Show more* lines share
  `moreLine` (home.js).

Tests: `home-view-model.test.ts` (`answeredPage`: order, the `after`
boundary, ties, `total`; Home's list is its first page),
`home-js-answered-more.test.ts` (jsdom: the count line, Show more, a failed
read, the poll keeping 40, `/approvals/<id>` for the 30th, *Rule changes*
with its limit grown, starting over), `read-gate.test.ts` (the entry), and
`tests/stack/approvals-answered-more.test.ts` (a real arbiter and the
net-proxy on its production client, 45 answered asks: 20 drawn, Show more
brings 21-40 with their reversals, the 30th's *Block instead* over the real
route, and no value or token on the route signed out, nor more than
`/api/home` carries).

**The pages** (`public/index.html` + `app.css` + `js/home.js`, no framework,
every server string inserted as text):

1. **Home** — the hero (icon, headline, sentence, only the non-zero count
   facts); *Approvals waiting (N)* (N = the nav badge; the first three asks
   with Allow once / Always allow / Block through the
   `egress/approvals/<id>/{approve-once,approve,deny}` routes, CSRF header as
   everywhere, then "N more questions in Approvals"; with none, "Nothing is
   waiting for you.", or "No question is waiting for you." above the link
   to the rule changes that wait, *An empty list never says nothing waits
   over a rule change*); *Running now* (running
   or waiting agents, never an ended one whose question still waits: that
   one is under *Earlier*, counting it, §4.34 *After you answer*; "Details"
   → the agent page; a preview agent's name
   carries a **Preview** tag, as its agent page's does, §4.21 *A preview
   agent*); *Earlier in the last 24
   hours* (the window's ended sessions, newest 10, then "N more sessions in
   the last 24 hours"; each row names its folder, as Running now's does,
   *Agents, not sessions*); and the collapsed *Where your data lives* (§4.25q).
   **On a phone the hero's icon sits above its headline** (2026-10-18). At
   640px and narrower (the stylesheet's phone breakpoint) the hero is a
   column: the icon is 40px (its glyph 22px) above the headline, and the
   headline (28px), sentence and counts take the column's whole width.
   Before, the 56px icon and its 24px gap sat beside the words at every
   width, a quarter of a 320px window's column for an `aria-hidden` icon
   that repeats the headline's verdict in colour. Headless Chromium drew the
   tour's waiting hero at 320px with the headline in 4 lines and the
   sentence in 6, 494px tall, so the waiting card started below a 568px
   screen; now 2 and 4 lines, 386px (at 390px: 372px, now 338px). Each
   verdict keeps its icon and colours, "Not connected." too; 641px and wider
   are unchanged. Tests: `css-hero-phone.test.ts`, and
   `tests/stack/home-hero-links.test.ts` (the served styles at 390px).
   **The earlier list is headed by its window, not the calendar.**
   home.js writes the heading from `window.hours`, the window /api/home
   counts (`HOME_WINDOW_HOURS`, the lead of the hero's counts, "In the last
   24 hours:", *The counts name their window* below). It never
   says "today": the window is rolling, so after midnight it still holds
   yesterday evening's sessions. Until 2026-10-05 it was the static "Earlier
   today", so every morning it called the night before "today", while the
   inspector's list said "Yesterday". If the window's length is not known,
   the heading is just "Earlier" and the overflow line names no span. **Each
   row says when it ended** ("ended 3 hours ago", the clock time on hover,
   compact rows keeping the relative form, §4.25u). Before, the time showed
   only when a row had no counts, so a row that said "2 items masked, 1 send
   blocked" did not say when. Its `lastAt` unknown: no time line, not a bare
   "ended". "Ended" means not running: a recorded exit, or no event for
   `RUNNING_WINDOW_MS`, as everywhere on the page.
   **A row reads its counts under its prompt** (2026-10-06). Both lists
   draw a row the same way (home.js `agentRow`): the agent; the prompt on
   one ellipsized line with the counts on the line under it, in the row's
   widest column (`.agent-what`, `minmax(0, 1fr)`); when it started or
   ended, alone in a 150px column (`.agent-when`); then *Details*. Before,
   the counts and the time shared a 220px third column, so the tour's "1
   secret masked, 1 secret read before it was marked, 1 action blocked, 1
   send with a real value filled in" wrapped to four lines beside a prompt
   column that was mostly empty, and the facts that say whether a session
   was safe were the hardest text on Home to read. The counts wrap, never
   cut (`text-wrap: pretty` where the browser has it). A running row now
   says when it started ("started 3 minutes ago", the clock time on hover)
   whether or not it counts anything; before, its counts took the place of
   its start time. With no recorded start it says nothing, not a bare
   "started ". A narrow screen (≤ 760px) still stacks the row in one
   column. Words and numbers are unchanged. Tests: `home-js-home.test.ts`
   (the cells, the running row's time, the app.css contract),
   `home-earlier.test.ts` and `home-first-session.test.ts` (the served
   rows over the real server).
   **Home counts what the session page shows** (2026-10-05). A row's
   "N actions blocked" is the tile on the page its *Details* opens, the
   same number in the same words: `HomeFacts` counts the blocked steps of
   the story that page tells (`storyCounts`: a command, a file, a send).
   Before, rows said "N sends blocked" from the lineage's `egressBlocked`,
   the masked *items* whose worst outcome was a block at any gate, the exec
   gate's too. A session whose only blocks were a command and a file read
   said "1 send blocked" on Home and "2 actions blocked" on its page, which
   shows no send. The hero's facts follow: "N actions blocked" (the rows'
   sum) and "N sends with a real value filled in" (the stories' `sent`
   steps, the inspector's *Data out* words; titled "Each went to a
   destination allowed to receive it.", "It went …" over one), in place of "N sends allowed by
   you". That one summed `egressAllowed`, items whose worst outcome was
   allowed, so a token sent to its bound host and blocked elsewhere counted
   for nothing, and a command let run or a reply shown to you counted as a
   send. The payload: `HomeAgent.blocked`, `window.blocked` and
   `window.sent` (`window.allowed` is gone); the lineage counts stay in
   `stats` for the developer view. Tests: `home-view-model.test.ts`,
   `agent-page.test.ts`, `home-js-home.test.ts`, `home-counts.test.ts` (the
   served Home and agent pages over the real server).
   **Home counts secrets as the session page does** (2026-10-05). The

3. **Rules** — no switch (2026-10-05: the on/off moved to Settings, below;

4. **Settings** — first the **Protection** card: ONE on/off switch
   (`#switch-protection`, the confidentiality axis), its state as On / Off
   and one sentence, POSTing `{mode}` to `/api/config/axes`: on is `secrets`,

   until the answer, *The switch holds while its change is on its way*,

   secrets, so the frozen integrity axis (§4.25o) has no switch: a flip keeps
   it as it is only under the opt-in (`full` / `injection`), and otherwise
   turns a leftover one off too, which the server always allows. In the same
   row, under its sentence, the protection-service line from
   `/api/control/summary` (`view-model/service-summary.ts`; *One Protection
   row*, below): Mandu's own service as Running / Starting / Stopped /

   offers no Restart (*The service row answers its button*, below). The row
   follows the service on the page's poll, and a service that is starting
   offers no button (*The service row follows the service*, below). The
   model and network helpers are not listed: every `mandu` session brings its
   own (runtime-instances.md), so "stopped" is their normal state and would

   inspector's Services panel (`/api/control/status`), which keeps every row.
   Then *Models* (§4.25l), the sensitivity-label and prompt-filter blocks
   (later sections), *Notifications*, *Appearance* (below), and the
   developer-view link. The
   switch's dot and sentence say what runs now, its name what is saved
   (*The on/off says what runs*, below).

**One Protection row (2026-10-11).** Until then the card had two rows, "On"
with the switch and, under it, "Running" with Restart, each with its own
dot. A person read two answers to one question (is Mandu protecting me?),
and the service row's sentence, "Mandu is protecting the agents you start
with mandu.", stayed beside an "Off" that said the opposite. Now the card is
ONE row (`#settings-protect-row`): the name and the switch are the saved
on/off as before; the middle column holds the on/off's sentence and, under
it, the service line (`#settings-services` › `#settings-service-main`),
written "<state>. <sentence> Started <time>." with Start or Restart inline:
"Running. Started 10:02. [Restart]", "Stopped. It starts again by itself
when you next start an agent with mandu. [Start]", "Stopped unexpectedly.
Press Start, or start an agent with mandu. [Start]", "Starting.". The
service's sentences no longer say Mandu protects anything (a service runs
with protection off too) nor repeat the state (`WORDS`, `ADOPTED_SENTENCE`).
Restart's question opens under the whole row. The row has one dot
(`home.js protectDot`): red when the service stopped unexpectedly; amber
while it starts or while protection is off, saved or running; green only
when on is saved and running and the line does not say Stopped; else grey.
Everything the service line did (its answers, the poll, the adopted
service, the fallbacks, the helper note) is unchanged. Tests:
`home-js-settings.test.ts` (one row and one dot, running, off and running,
the line's words in each state, the question under the row),
`view-model/service-summary.test.ts` (no sentence says protect or repeats
its state), stack `settings-service-answers` and `settings-service-follows`
(the served page: one row throughout, the red dot on a crash).

**The service row answers its button (2026-10-10).** Until then the row's
`act` threw the POST's answer away and drew the row again. Every control
POST needs the admin session (§6.x) while `/api/control/summary` is an open
read, so signed out a Start changed nothing on the page, and a Restart's
question vanished as if it had restarted. Now the button waits while its
request is out (one Start, not two). A start that worked draws Settings
again, as before. Any other answer draws the row again from a fresh summary
(a start that failed can leave it *Stopped unexpectedly*), then puts the
answer on the row drawn now: `refusalText`'s words (*Refusals*, below:
signed out, "Sign in first: …" with `mandu dashboard` as code), else the
server's error as written, else "could not start the protection service
(<status>)", and with no answer at all the *Refusals* sentence for status 0
(*A click with no answer says so*).

A service this dashboard ADOPTED (already listening when the supervisor went
to start it, `ServiceStatus.adopted`) is not its to stop: `Supervisor.stop()`
refuses it, so every Restart failed, signed in too, and nothing said so
(the inspector's rows disable it, §4.8 *Adopted services*; the shared
stack's promoted arbiter outlives a dashboard restart and is adopted by
design). Now `buildServiceSummary` gives a running adopted service no
button, the sentence "It was already running when this dashboard started,
so this page cannot restart it." (`ADOPTED_SENTENCE`, after "Running." since
*One Protection row*), and no "Started …" (its `since` is when
the dashboard found it). Once it is no longer running, Start comes back (a
start adopts or spawns). The control
routes, the admin gate and the supervisor's refusal are unchanged; the
inspector's Services rows keep Replace for an adopted arbiter (§4.8).
Tests: `home-js-settings.test.ts` (jsdom: a 403 with the gate's real body
on Start and on Restart now, a 503 start failure under the repainted row,
no body, no answer, a second press while the first is out, the adopted
row), `view-model/service-summary.test.ts` (the adopted projection and its
vocabulary) and stack `settings-service-answers` (a real Supervisor over
stand-in services and a real DashboardServer with an admin token; the served
page signed out, then signed in; an adopted stand-in, whose real restart
route answers 503 even signed in; the token oracle).

**The service row follows the service (2026-10-10).** Until then the row
was read once, when Settings opened (`loadSettings`), and again only after
its own button. The supervisor's state changes on its own while the page is
open: a crash turns a running service *Stopped unexpectedly*
(`watchForCrash`), and a start made elsewhere in this dashboard (the
inspector's Start, another tab, its own start at boot) turns it *Starting*,
then *Running*. So
after a crash the row still said "Running · Mandu is protecting the agents
you start with mandu. Started …" with Restart, while the same page's top bar
said "Not connected" and the on/off above it said the service was not
reachable. A row drawn while starting said "Starting" until you left
Settings, with a Start whose POST only waited for the start under way
(`Supervisor.start` coalesces on the one in flight).

Now the page's poll (every 10 s while the tab is shown, and on a return to
it, as Home's) also runs `home.js followServices` while Settings is the
page. It reads `/api/control/summary` again and draws the row only when the
summary differs from the one it was drawn from (`S.services`), as *The poll
keeps your place* does for Home's sections. So a crash, a start or a finished
start shows within one poll, with no click, and in step with the top bar,
which the same poll redraws. A poll that finds the same service draws
nothing, so the answer to the row's button ("Sign in first: …", a failed
start) stays until the service changes. The row is not read or drawn again
while the Restart question is open, nor while a request of the row is out
(`S.serviceOut`: its Start or Restart, or Settings' own read); the answer of
that request draws it. A poll that gets no summary (no answer, a refusal)
leaves the row as drawn: the top bar says "Not connected" when the server
cannot be reached.
Off Settings the poll does not read the summary. `buildServiceSummary` gives
a *starting* service no button (`action: null`; it reads "Starting." since
*One Protection row*), since the poll now redraws it once it is running or stopped.
The control routes, the admin gate and the supervisor are unchanged. Tests:
`home-js-settings.test.ts` (jsdom: running → crashed → starting → running
over the poll, an unchanged poll keeping the answer, the open question and
a request out holding the row, no answer, Home failing, off Settings),
`view-model/service-summary.test.ts` (starting has no button) and stack
`settings-service-follows` (a real Supervisor over stand-ins whose main
service listens only once a gate file exists, a real DashboardServer, the
served Settings page held open and signed out: the service is killed, a
signed-out Start's answer survives unchanged polls, a start held at its
gate reads *Starting* with no button, released it reads *Running*; the token
oracle).

**The service row keeps the focus (2026-10-13).** Every other Settings card
keeps the keyboard focus across its changes (*A Settings row's button names
its row; a change keeps the focus*, below), and Home's lists across the poll
(*The poll keeps the focus*), but the service line was left out. Its Start
and *Restart now* turn the button off while the request is out, and a
browser drops the focus of a button turned off to `<body>`; the answer then
draws Settings or the row again and gave nothing the focus, whether the
press worked or was refused. Restart turned itself off and opened its
question under the row with the focus on `<body>`: a screen reader heard
nothing, and Tab started over at the top of the page to find *Restart now*.
The poll drew the line anew from nothing whenever the service changed, so a
focused Restart left the page. Now (`home.js serviceFocus`,
`inProtectionCard`, `followServices`):

- **The question.** Restart pressed with the focus on it gives the focus to
  the question's words (`focusThere`; the question keeps `role="alert"`).
  Escape is Cancel (`plainEscape`), and Cancel gives Restart, on again, the
  focus back, as before. Once *Restart now* is on its way it cannot be
  called back, so Cancel goes off with it and Escape does nothing.
- **An answer that worked** (Start, *Restart now*): Settings is drawn again
  and the line takes the focus, reading what the service does now
  ("Starting.", "Running. Started 15:31 · just now. Restart"), as an
  Approvals row that took an answer does (*An answer keeps the focus in
  its list*).
- **A refusal** gives the focus to the row's button pressed (Start, or
  Restart for *Restart now*), drawn again and on, described by the
  refusal's words (`aria-describedby`, "Sign in first: …"), as a Settings
  card's refusal does; when the row now offers no such button (a start
  already under way reads "Starting." with none), the line, which holds the
  words.
- **The poll** takes the focus's place in the Protection card before it
  draws the row and gives it back after (`pollPlace` / `pollRefocus`): the
  control drawn again that reads the same (Restart, after a restart made
  elsewhere), the line that had the focus, drawn anew; else the card's
  heading (Restart gone after a crash: never Start).
- **Nothing is taken.** The focus moves only if it fell, and only for a
  press made with the focus in the Protection card: a press made without
  it (a browser that does not focus a clicked button), and a focus moved
  elsewhere meanwhile, move nothing; the question then takes no focus
  either.

Sighted readers see no change but the question's Cancel turning off while
the restart is out. The words, the control routes, the admin gate, the
POSTs and the question's text are unchanged. Tests:
`home-js-service-focus.test.ts` (jsdom; a button turned off drops its focus
at that moment, as Chromium's does: a Start that worked and the poll after
it, the question with Escape and Cancel, *Restart now* with Cancel off while
it is out, both refusals, a refusal with no button, the poll after a
restart and a crash with a focus outside left alone, presses without the
focus) and stack `settings-service-focus` (a real Supervisor over stand-in
services, a real DashboardServer with an admin token, the served Settings
page: signed out a refused Start keeps its focus, described by the sign-in
words, with nothing started; signed in, Start, the question, Escape,
*Restart now* (a new pid) and a crash drawn by the poll; the token oracle).

**The on/off says what runs (2026-10-07).** The product page has two
sources for protection. `GET /api/config/axes` is what is SAVED: the config
file, which the next cold start of the protection service runs. Home's
`protection` (`GET /api/home`) is what RUNS: the arbiter's posture, and
whether a protection service is connected at all. A flip writes only the
file (`config-axes-routes.ts`), so the two differ until the service restarts,
and with no service connected nothing is known of what runs. Settings and
Rules used to tell the saved state as fact. With no service, Settings showed
a green "On: … not sent anywhere without your OK" right under Home's "Not
connected … or open Settings". A flip to on over a service running off read
the same. A direct visit drew the row before Home answered and never again.
Now (`home.js secretsRunning`, on the secrets axis: `secrets`/`full` on,
`off`/`injection` off, else unknown):

| saved | runs now | Settings › Protection: dot, sentence | Rules, the line above the rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| on | on | green; "Keys and secret files leave this computer only where a rule or your OK allows." | none |
| off | off | amber; "Mandu only watches. Your secrets are not masked, and nothing is stopped." | "Protection is off, so these rules are kept but not enforced. Turn it on in Settings." |
| on | off | amber; "Still off until the protection service restarts: Mandu only watches, and your secrets are not masked." | "Protection is still off until the protection service restarts, so these rules are kept but not enforced." |
| off | on | amber; "Still on until the protection service restarts: keys and secret files leave this computer only where a rule or your OK allows." | "Protection is saved as off: once the protection service restarts, these rules are kept but not enforced. Turn it on in Settings." |
| on / off | unknown | grey (on) or amber (off); "Saved as on/off." + "The protection service is not reachable, so Mandu cannot say what is on now."
