(no service, or Home unreadable) or "Mandu cannot say what the protection service runs now." (a service that reports no posture) | none (on), the saved-as-off line (off) |

The switch, its name ("On" / "Off") and `aria-checked` stay the saved
setting: that is what a flip changes. Green means on is both saved and
running. The note under the row is unchanged ("Saved. It applies when the
protection service next starts." while what runs differs, else "A change
applies …"). Home's poll repaints both (`followRunning`), keyed on what runs
(`runningKey`). So a late Home answer or a restart updates them, and a poll
that changed nothing repaints nothing: a refusal in the note stays, and the
`role=status` line is not announced again. The switch's behaviour (the POST,
the typed-OFF gate, the frozen axis) is unchanged. A read of the saved
setting asked before your flip, or before a newer read, never draws the
switch (*The protection switch keeps what you saved*, 2026-10-12). Tests:
`home-js-settings.test.ts` and `home-js-rules.test.ts` (every pair, the late
answer, the poll), `protection-running.test.ts` (the served page over the real
server with a real config file and a served posture, or none).

**A change waits (2026-10-07, first-session tour item 17).** While a rule
change waits in Approvals, Rules lists the rules in FORCE, which can differ
from `policy.yaml`: a loosening hand edit is in the file but held until the
human answers (policy-surface.md §8.4.6). The tour read "Rules lists no
rules" beside a file that named a label, with nothing saying why. Now a
second line above the rules (`#rules-pending`, `home.js
renderRulesPending`, the same box as the on/off line) says so: "policy.yaml
has a change that waits for your OK, so it is not in force yet." (any held
file change) or "N rule change(s) wait(s) for your OK." (requests only),
then "Until you answer, the rules below are the ones Mandu enforces." and a
"Review it/them in Approvals" link. It reads the same pending list as
Approvals (`GET /api/policy/proposals?status=pending`), loaded with the
Rules page and on Home's poll; with nothing pending it is hidden. A request
the law already says is closed by the arbiter (policy-surface.md §8.4.5),
so it never lingers here. Tests: `home-js-proposals.test.ts` ("tour 17"),
`tests/stack/policy-pending-in-force.test.ts` (the Rules projection over a
real arbiter with a held edit, before and after the agent's lock and a
restart).

**Cards and folds (2026-10-05).** On Rules and Settings every section is a
card (`section.block.card`: its own panel, so where one ends is never in
doubt) that says ONE line about itself under its title; the rest of the
explanation is folded under **More** (`details.more`) or behind a "?" help.
A long explanation in index.html is written as `<span data-help="label">`,
which `home.js wireStaticHelp` turns into the same help button as the
"masked" one (§4.25u), so a form reads as its labels first (the model form's
three checkboxes). Lists inside a card keep a lighter edge. Tests:
`home-js-settings.test.ts` (the six cards, the folds, the helps).

**The per-agent page** (`/agents/<id>`, `GET /api/home/agent`, pure
`view-model/agent-page.ts`). Every "Details" link and Approvals' "See what the
agent was doing" (on a question's card, and on the card of a rule change the
agent asked for) open it; "Detailed trace" goes on to the inspector. It tells
ONE session as "What happened", one card per turn (§4.25b), with that
session's pending asks (expanded, with the verbs) and a link to the rule
changes it asked for (*A rule change and the agent that asked*), count
tiles, and the main model line (§4.25l). A test session has a page too (an ask can come from one),
though Home never lists it. A session with no conversation (a launch probe)
says so. The agent's name carries what its Home row's does: a preview
agent's **Preview** tag and the version's warning mark (§4.21 *A preview
agent*, *The version's warning on the agent page*).

**The header says how long it ran and when it ended** (2026-10-05). Under
the title, the time line used to read "ended 11 hours ago, started 11 hours
ago" for a 36-second session: the same moment twice, no clock time, no
length, and a bare "ended " when `lastAt` was unknown. The inspector's row
for the same session read "22:10 · 36s". home.js `agentWhenParts` now
writes:

- ended: "ran 36 seconds, ended Oct 4, 22:10 · 11 hours ago". The end is a
  `whenNode` `<time>` (§4.25u). "ran" counts from the first recorded step to
  the last, and its tooltip says so, with the start's clock time;
- running: "running now, started Oct 5, 09:30 · 3 minutes ago";
- under a second, no "ran". With only one moment recorded, "ended …" or
  "started …" alone. With neither, no time at all.

`spanWords` spells out the inspector's buckets (`elapsedLabel`: "36s", "3m
12s", "2h 5m"), so both views give the same length. "Ended" means not
running. The listing's "running" was recent activity only (an event in the
last 5 minutes, session-batches `RUNNING_WINDOW_MS`), so a session closed
with `/exit` a minute ago read "running now" (tour, 2026-10-05). The page
now reads the launcher's `session_exit` too (`sessionExited`,
view-model/session-exit.ts): an exit with no model call or tool step after
it is the end; activity after an exit (a resumed session on the same log)
keeps it running. Since 2026-10-06 the listing applies the same rule
(`SessionRef.exited`, §4.10.4), so the inspector's row agrees. The workspace follows (", in `~/app`"). Tests:
`home-js-agent.test.ts`, `session-walkthrough.test.ts` (the served header
and the inspector's row for the same session).

**A session on more than one day names its days** (2026-10-19). A turn's
head showed only its clock time, "10:24", in a plain span with no day and
no moment on hover. A Claude Code or Codex window left open overnight
showed turns at "23:50" and "00:10" with nothing to say a day went by, and
a turn at "09:12" the next morning read as if it came before the "23:50"
above it; the header's line names only the end. Every other moment on the
product page has its day (§4.25u). Now home.js:

- each turn's time, and that of a message Mandu stopped, is a
  `<time datetime>` (`turnTime`). It still reads "23:50" in its 56 px
  column, and its tooltip is the whole moment, "Oct 16, 23:50"
  (`clockWords`). The times in a turn's background list carry the same
  tooltip. A turn with no time keeps an empty span;
- when the cards drawn cover more than one of the viewer's local days, a
  line naming the day, "Thursday, Oct 16", goes before the first card of
  each day, the first day's too, so the page starts with its date
  (`storyDayLines`, after the turns and the stopped messages are placed).
  A session within one day draws none and looks as before. The line is a
  `.story-day` separator in the note's ink and the column heads' small
  capitals, not a heading. A card with no time starts no day. The year is
  added when it is not this year, as `clockWords` does;
- the lines come from the cards drawn, so with the earlier turns not shown
  they follow the turns that are, and "Show them" draws them again. They
  sit between the cards, so the switch's folds (*Only where Mandu stepped
  in*, §4.25ae) fold each day's quiet turns behind their own line, under
  that day's line. They come from the turns' own times, never from the
  clock's day, so a poll that draws the page again draws the same lines.

Tests: `home-js-story-days.test.ts` (unit, `TZ` pinned to a zone east of
UTC: no lines within a day and the `<time>` tooltips; 23:50, 23:58, 00:10
and a stopped message at 00:02; the switch's folds; a poll), the
`.story-day` contrast in both themes (`css-shared-system.test.ts`), and
the stack `tests/stack/agent-story-days.test.ts` (a seeded session whose
turns cross midnight, served over a real `DashboardServer`).

**The tiles count what the page shows** (2026-10-05). Under the header,
the tiles used to read "3 items masked before the AI saw them · 3 of them
secrets · 1 action blocked" for the first-session tour. *Your secrets*,
right under them, listed 2 secrets and said the AI read the second
(`deploy/staging.conf`) as it was, before it was marked a secret. The tiles
counted lineage flows (`stats.flows`, `stats.secret`), where one file
masked to two tokens is two flows, and they called every flow masked before
the AI saw it. The send that left with `STRIPE_KEY` filled in had no tile,
though Home's hero counts it. home.js `renderAgentPage` now draws:

- "N secrets masked before the AI saw them": the *Your secrets* entries
  whose card says "The AI got only a placeholder, never the real value"
  (`SecretsStory.counts.masked`, every entry, past the cap too);
- "N secrets the AI read before they were marked secrets" (amber):
  the entries whose card says the AI read the real value before the label
  (`counts.early`). Both counts come from the function that picks each
  card's first line (secret-story.ts `aiSaw`), so a tile never claims more
  than its card. A level that lets a model read it, Off and a fired leak
  check count in neither; their card says why;
- "N untrusted items masked before the AI saw them": the non-secret flows,
  only where a frozen masking level (or an unrecorded mode) masks untrusted
  text, never in Secrets or Off;
- "N actions blocked", as before (`storyCounts`);
- "N sends with a real value filled in" (`AgentPageVM.sent`, the same
  `storyCounts` as Home's hero), when there is one;
- "waiting for you", as before.

With nothing recorded the row still says "0 secrets masked before the AI
saw them" and "0 actions blocked". It says nothing about masking when the
leak check fired (the red tile) or when every listed secret is at a level
the AI may read. Each tile's tooltip says what it counts. Tests:
`secret-story.test.ts` (`counts`, `aiSaw`), `session-page-record.test.ts`
(unit, over the recorded tour: 1 masked, 1 early, 1 blocked, 1 sent),
`home-js-agent.test.ts` (words, plurals, the amber tile, the zero row, the
frozen-mode tile, the leak check), and the end-to-end
`test/component/session-page-record.test.ts` (the served page's tiles over
the tour, beside its cards and steps). Home's rows and hero count the same
secrets with the same call (*Home counts secrets as the session page
does*, above).

**A tile takes you to what it counts** (2026-10-18). The blocked and sent
tiles' tooltips said "What happened, below, shows it", and *Needs your OK*
was further down still: on the tour's 4,670 px page (up to 60 turns) the
reader hunted for the one row the tile counted. Now home.js `drawAgentPage`
draws three tiles as buttons (`button.tile[data-goes]`, the same look, an
accent edge and "Show" in the corner on hover and keyboard focus, a focus
ring; in forced colors the edge is `Highlight`):

- **"N actions blocked", "N sends with a real value filled in".** A press
  (`goToOutcome`) goes to the story's first step with that outcome (each
  action step carries `data-outcome`), through `showStep` as a Your secrets
  time does (*A time opens its step*): its folded run (*Only where Mandu
  stepped in*) and its "Show N more steps" fold open, the accent bar marks
  it (`.step.shown`, not the ask's `.focus`, whose tag and note say Mandu
  asked you there), the keyboard focus goes to it, and it is scrolled to
  the middle. The next press goes to the next one, after the last to the
  first; the tile then adds where it is, "Showing 2 of 3" (only past one
  step). The place is kept per visit (`S.agentTileAt`, by step id), so a
  poll redraw keeps it, as it keeps the mark, the focus and the story's
  toggles (*The poll keeps your place*).
- **Steps in turns not drawn.** The counts (`storyCounts`) cover every turn,
  each up to `TURN_STEP_CAP` steps, and the story always draws those steps
  of a turn it draws, so a counted step the page lacks is in a turn before
  the newest `TURN_CAP`. Then the press asks for every turn first (the
  *Show them* read, `turns=all`, §4.25ad) and goes on once it is drawn
  (`landAgent`). Past `TURN_ALL_CAP`, which no *Show them* lifts, the presses
  go round the steps drawn ("Showing 1 of 4" counts what the tile counts);
  a tile with none drawn and none to ask for stays a plain tile.
- **"N waiting for you"** focuses the first card in *Needs your OK* and
  scrolls it to the middle.
- **At 0**, and the secrets' tiles, stay plain tiles: nothing to go to.

The tooltips say so: "… Press to go to each in turn under What happened."
("… to it …" for one), "Press to go to Needs your OK, below.". A tile at 0
keeps "What happened, below, shows it.". Tests: `home-js-agent-tiles-go.test.ts`
(buttons only when non-zero, the presses, the wrap, the waiting card, the
Show them read, the poll redraw) and the end-to-end
`tests/stack/agent-tiles-go.test.ts` (a real stack's three blocks and three
waiting rows: the served page at 1280 and 390 px, and the oracle).

**The page links the trace it names** (2026-10-08). The page told the
person in eight places that something was "in the detailed trace", and
none of those words was a link: the only way there was the *Detailed
trace* button at the top, up to 60 turns away. Each is now a link to the
developer view's trace of the session the page shows
(`/dev/sessions/<id>`), in a new tab like the button:

- the red tile's "Open the detailed trace", "N earlier turns are in the
  detailed trace." (past `TURN_CAP`), "N more steps are in the detailed
  trace." (past `TURN_STEP_CAP`), and an unrecorded original's "The
  detailed trace may have it.";
- "N more secrets are in the detailed trace." (past `SECRET_CAP`) opens
  the trace's Secrets tab (`?tab=secrets`, §4.33), which lists every
  masked value;
- opened for an ask it cannot place (§4.25h), "The detailed trace has
  every step." opens the trace at that ask (`?ask=<id>`, §4.35), where the
  developer view marks the moment if it has it;
- the server's own sentences: a step that reached the AI unmasked ("This
  reached the AI without a mask. Open the detailed trace.", an OS step's
  "Open the detailed trace to see what.") and two *Your secrets* lines
  (the fired leak check's, and "Mandu released it N more times after a
  check. The detailed trace says where.").

A server sentence marks the words with a text part's `trace` (a tab name,
`"trace"` or `"secrets"`, never an address), as `ask` marks an Approvals
row; an action step's note comes as `noteParts` when it holds one, and
`note` keeps the same words joined. home.js `traceLink` builds the address
from the page's own session id (encoded); a tab it does not know opens the
trace itself, off an agent page the words stay text, and a payload without
parts (an older server) reads as before.

**A step's own link opens that step** (2026-10-08). Three of those links
are about one step, and they opened the top of the trace, where a session
may hold hundreds of steps before it: a step that reached the AI unmasked
("Open the detailed trace"), an unrecorded original under a step ("The
detailed trace may have it."), and "N more steps are in the detailed
trace.", whose steps come after `TURN_STEP_CAP` others of the same turn.
Each now opens the trace at its step (`/dev/sessions/<id>?step=<stepId>`,
the id encoded), which the developer view marks (§4.35, *`?step=<stepId>`
opens one step*): the step's own id for the first two (home.js
`stepNode` passes it to its note's parts and its hidden box, `sentenceNode`'s
`at`), and for the third the first step left out, which the turn now names
(`StoryTurn.moreFrom`, a step id, never a value or an address; absent when
nothing is left out). Both views number steps the same way (the dual-lane
step's id, `vm.dualLanes.steps`), so nothing is looked up. A server part
still names only a tab; the page adds the step it draws the words under. A
reply's unrecorded original, the red tile, the earlier turns (the top of
the trace is where they are) and the *Your secrets* lines keep the trace
itself, and a payload without `moreFrom` (an older server) does too.

Tests: `agent-page.test.ts` and `secret-story.test.ts` (the parts, the
joined words, no address; in the first, `moreFrom` is the first step past
the cap and absent under it), `home-js-agent.test.ts` (each link's address, new tab
and encoding; an unknown tab; an old note; the step links and their
encoded ids; no `moreFrom`), and across the real arbiter and
anthropic-proxy `tests/stack/agent-page-trace-links.test.ts` (13 `.env`
reads: the 13th secret's line opens the Secrets tab and the lost ask's
note the trace at that ask, each read back by the developer view's own
route table; no value or token on the page) and
`tests/stack/agent-page-step-links.test.ts` (`TURN_STEP_CAP` + 1 reads in
one turn, the last a `.env`: the turn names that read, "1 more step is in
the detailed trace." links it, the developer view's route table reads it
back, and the real inspector bundle over the real `/api/sessions` and
`/api/events` marks exactly that card, signed out, and the step rail
shows that read's row, the 82nd of 83; no value anywhere).

Since 2026-10-15 (§4.25ad) the three lines past a cap read "… not shown
here." with a **Show them** that draws the rest on the page, the trace
following as "The detailed trace has them." (the same link, the same
address); and in a build without the developer view none of these words
points to the trace.

**Notifications.** Each ask this browser has not seen raises one browser
notification ("Mandu: Claude Code needs your OK" plus the ask's sentence; a
click opens Approvals), at most three per poll (since 2026-10-19 a rule
change waiting for you too, and one more line past three: below). The first visit in a browser
records the backlog silently (`mandu.home.notifyPrimed`,
`mandu.home.seenAsks` in localStorage), so opening the page never floods.
Permission is asked only from a button (the Home offer row while permission
is `default`, and Settings › Notifications, which also says when the browser
blocked it or cannot notify on a non-secure address). The tab title carries
the count ("(3) Mandu") and the favicon a badge, as §4.20 does for the
inspector. The 10 s poll is the transport, so a hidden tab notifies on its
first poll after it becomes visible.

*Turn off for this browser (2026-10-19).* A page cannot take a granted
permission back, so until then the row read "On. …" with no control, and
the browser's site settings were the only way to stop them. With permission
granted, the row's button (`#notify-enable`, described by the row's words)
reads *Turn off* while they are on and *Turn on* after; the choice is this
browser's (`mandu.home.notifyOff` in localStorage; another browser or
profile still notifies; where storage fails, as in private mode, it holds
for the tab, as priming does). The row reads "On. You get a notification
when an agent needs your OK." (since the alarms below, it names all three) /
"Off in this browser. The tab title still
counts what waits.", and the Home offer row stays hidden. While off nothing
is shown, but every new ask is still recorded as seen (the priming rule), so
turning them on again never brings the backlog: only asks raised after it
notify. A press redraws only that row, so the button keeps the focus (*A
Settings row's button names its row; a change keeps the focus*); another open tab's row follows on the
`storage` event, and every tab's poll reads the choice before it notifies.
Pressing *Turn on* while the permission is `default` (the browser's own
prompt) also clears a stored "off": asking means wanting them. `default`,
`denied` and a browser that cannot notify read as before. Tests:
`home-js-notify-off.test.ts` (jsdom) and `tests/stack/settings-notify-off`
(the served page over a real arbiter's asks, in jsdom and a real Chromium).

*Protection failed, and the service stopped under a running agent
(2026-10-19).* Until then only asks notified, so the product's two worst
states reached a person with the tab in the background only when they
opened it. home.js `notifyAlarms` adds two kinds, both on the answer
`loadHome` keeps (an older poll's dropped answer never notifies), behind the
same gate as asks (permission granted, not turned off):

- **Protection failed.** A session in `home.agents` with `holds: false` that
  this browser has not seen failed raises "Mandu: protection failed in
  Claude Code" (the row's agent), body "Something reached the AI unmasked.
  Open its page to see what.", tag `mandu-failed-<session id>`; a click
  opens that session's page. Seen ids are kept under
  `mandu.home.seenFailed` (the last 500; per tab where storage fails); the
  first visit in a browser, with no such key, records the sessions already
  failed silently, and while turned off they are still recorded, so neither
  brings a backlog.
- **The service stopped.** A poll that finds the service down (the 503
  `unreachable`, `readFailure` → `down`) right after a kept read that
  listed a running or waiting agent raises "Mandu: the protection service
  stopped", body "Your agent's requests are blocked until it runs again.
  Open Settings to start it.", tag `mandu-service-stopped`; a click opens
  Settings, which has its Start. Once per stop: any failed poll forgets the
  running agent, so the next failed polls say nothing, and a stop with no
  agent running (a normal state between agents) says nothing at all.

The fixed tags make two open tabs show one notification. The words name
the agent only, never a file, host, prompt or secret: a desktop
notification can be mirrored off the machine (the reasoning of *Not built:
telling the person with no dashboard tab open*, below). Settings ›
Notifications' "On" line names all three: "On. You get a notification when
an agent needs your OK, when protection fails, and when the protection
service stops under a running agent." Tests: `home-js-home.test.ts` (jsdom,
the *alarms:* cases) and `tests/stack/home-hero-failure-words` (H5: a real
arbiter stopped under a running session, one notification, the H4 oracle
on its words).

*Rule changes notify too, and a burst says how many more (2026-10-19).*
Until then a rule change waiting for the person (the pending list
`loadProposals` reads on the same poll) was counted in the tab title and
the Approvals badge but never notified, though the agent is told it is not
applied until the person answers it on Approvals. `notifyNewAsks` now
gathers the poll's new asks, then its new rule changes:

- one **your agent asked for** (`askedByAgent`: not `onDisk`, `byAgent`
  not false) raises "Mandu: your agent asks to change a rule"; a **held
  change to policy.yaml** (`onDisk`, policy-surface.md §8.4.6) raises
  "Mandu: a change to policy.yaml waits for your OK"; both with the body
  "Open Approvals to answer it.", tag `mandu-proposal-<id>`. One you asked
  for yourself that is left waiting (`byAgent: false`) raises nothing: you
  know about it. The words are fixed: never the card's rows, its headline,
  the agent's `reason` (UNTRUSTED agent text) nor the file or host the rule
  names, by the reasoning above.
- A click opens Approvals at that card (`setPage('approvals', true,
  undefined, id)`, the address `/approvals/<id>`): `markApprovalsAsk` finds
  `#approvals-proposals .proposal` by its `data-id` (compared as a value)
  before the asks, and the poll marks after the rule-change cards draw, so
  a redraw keeps the mark.
- Seen ids are kept under `mandu.home.seenProposals` (the last 500; per tab
  where storage fails), so ids of the two kinds never collide. The asks'
  priming rule, under its own key: a browser with no such key records the
  waiting ones silently, also one already primed for asks (it would
  otherwise get the backlog on its first poll after the change). While
  turned off, or without permission, they are still recorded. Only a read
  that answered with a list counts: a viewer refused the rule changes (no
  admin session) gets none and primes nothing.
- **At most three per poll, then one more.** Until then the rest of a
  burst was recorded as seen with nothing said, so five new asks showed
  three. Past three (asks and rule changes together) one more line says
  how many: "Mandu: 2 more need your OK" ("1 more needs"), body "Open
  Approvals to see them.", tag `mandu-more`; its click opens Approvals.

Settings › Notifications' "On" line is unchanged: "when an agent needs your
OK" covers a rule change it asks for. Tests: `home-js-home.test.ts` (jsdom,
the *notifications:* cases) and `tests/stack/proposal-notifies` (a real
arbiter's loosening request whose reason holds a fake key and the host, in
jsdom and a real Chromium: one notification, neither in its words).

**Appearance (2026-10-18).** Until then the product page always followed
the system's light or dark (§4.25k): only the inspector had a picker, so a
person who picked Dark there was back in light on `/`, and a person with
only the product page could not pick at all. Settings now ends (before the
developer-only card) with *Appearance*, one row, "Colours", and a menu:
*Same as this computer* (the default), *Light*, *Dark*.

- **One choice for both pages.** The menu stores `system` | `light` |
  `dark` under `mandu.theme` in localStorage, the key and values the
  inspector's Appearance row (§4.8) already used. Both pages are served
  from one origin, so a pick on either is the other's on its next load.
  `system` leaves `<html>` bare (mandu.css follows `prefers-color-scheme`);
  `light` / `dark` set `data-theme`. A stored value the page does not know
  (the retired `theme-*` palettes) reads as *Same as this computer*.
- **It applies at once.** home.js `wireAppearance` sets the attribute on
  change; nothing reloads.
- **No flash of the wrong theme.** home.js is a module, run after the
  first paint, so a stored Dark applied from it would paint light first.
  `js/theme-early.js`, a classic script in `<head>` before the
  stylesheets (never a module, `defer` or `async`), applies the stored
  choice by the same rule before anything paints.
- **A private window.** Where localStorage throws, the menu still switches
  the page, and the row says "Not remembered in this window."
- The forced-colors and reduce-motion rules (§4.25k) key on media queries,
  not on the theme, so they hold under a pinned one.

**Not built: telling the person with no dashboard tab open** (designed
2026-10-11, left). Every signal above needs a tab: the title count, the
badge and the notifications all ride the page's poll. The agent tells the
person in its reply ("tell the user … on the Mandu dashboard's Approvals
page"), which is the one signal that reaches a person with no tab, and only
once the model has read the refusal. The obvious second signal, `mandu`
printing a line in the agent's terminal, is unsafe as a line: under a live
TUI the agent owns the screen, and a row it did not paint shifts its next
repaint (reply-row-reservation.md §1; the unwalled-launch WARNING is
painted over today). The design that does not touch the cell grid:

- **Where.** The reply filter (interceptors/reply-filter), the one process
  between the agent and the terminal for the whole run, with an arbiter
  client already. It follows its own session's events (the arbiter's
  `subscribe`), and a gate event whose `policy.approvalId` it has not seen
  is a new ask of this session. No new arbiter op, no other session's asks.
- **What.** One OSC 9 desktop notification (`ESC ] 9 ; Mandu: <agent>
  needs your OK in Approvals BEL`, OSC 777 `notify` for the terminals that
  speak that form), no BEL of its own. Terminals that show it raise a
  desktop notification; an xterm-compatible parser that does not know it
  drops the sequence whole (the filter already passes OSC through as
  column-neutral, filter.ts). The words name the agent and the page, never
  the ask's sentence: the sentence can name a secret's key or file, and the
  terminal's notification may be mirrored off the machine.
- **When it is safe to write.** Only between the agent's chunks with the
  filter's escape parser in its ground state (never inside a CSI, OSC or
  DCS the agent began), and never inside a reserve block. At most one per
  ask and one per 30 s, so a re-asking hold does not repeat.
- **Off switch and pipe mode.** `MANDU_TERMINAL_NOTIFY=0` turns it off;
  with no TTY (pipe mode, `-p`) nothing is written, since the bytes would
  reach a program, not a terminal.
- **Tests it needs.** Unit: the parser-state gate (a chunk ending mid-OSC
  or mid-CSI defers the write) and the one-per-ask throttle; the PTY relay
  e2e: a gated send in a live session yields exactly one OSC 9 in the
  terminal stream, a screen model of the stream is cell-identical with and
  without it, and the sequence carries no token or value.

It was left because it changes the byte stream of every live TUI session
(the reply filter's fidelity gates would all need re-running on Claude Code,
Codex and Goose), which is outside a page change. The browser's own path,
a service worker with a push channel, needs a push service and was not
considered further.

**Rule changes your agent asked for** (policy-surface.md §8.6). The
confined agent may tighten the policy on its own and must ask for anything
that loosens it (policy-surface.md §8.3); the ask lands on Approvals.

- **Routes** (`server/policy-proposal-routes.ts`): `GET
  /api/policy/proposals`, `POST /api/policy/proposals/<pp-id> {verdict}`, `GET
  /api/policy/changes`, `POST /api/policy/changes/<pc-id>/undo`. GETs read the
  human socket (the data socket answers them with each prompt exception's
  pattern a placeholder; the adapter falls back to it only when the arbiter
  names no human socket) and are served to every reader, but a prompt exception's
  pattern only to one with the CSRF header AND the admin session
  (`server.ts adminRead`); any other read gets the row with the pattern
  hidden and `patternsHidden: true`, and the page says so in one plain line
  (plan 15 §13.7 item 4). POSTs sit behind the mutating gate (CSRF header + admin
  session) and ride the admin channel. Ids are shape-checked before the
  arbiter is called; its refusals map to 409 with its text.
- **The card** (`view-model/policy-proposals.ts`, pure): "Your agent wants to
  change a rule", one sentence per typed edit from a fixed grammar (all twelve
  ops, §4.25d terms), then *This would let*, one line per delta row by facet,
  then the agent's `reason` LAST in a muted box labelled "Your agent says",
  inserted as text. **Security property:** the facts come from the grammar
  and the delta, so the card is decidable without trusting the reason (in the
  default `secrets` mode a page the agent read may have written it). **Not
  now** is the primary button. A change with no limit on one side (an allow
  with no `from` or `to: *`, a wildcard trusted origin, a connect to any
  address) keeps **Allow** disabled until ALLOW is typed. Its foot says
  what the change opens, in its row's words, and why it asks for the
  word: "This lets your agent's programs connect to any address. Type
  ALLOW if you mean it." (*A wide change says what is open*). An Allow answered
  `refiled` (the policy moved and approving would now give up more) shows
  "The rules changed since your agent asked; here is the updated request".
  A request that is not the agent's (your own, left waiting when its
  approval failed) says "You want to change a rule", labels its reason
  "Note" and says "since this was asked" (`byAgent`, *A rule change you
  asked for is never credited to your agent*).
- **Where it shows**: Approvals' *Rule changes your agent asked for* block
  (hidden when empty; *Rule changes waiting for you* while one is not the
  agent's), a line on Home, a line on the agent page of the agent
  that asked, whose page the card links (*A rule change and the agent that
  asked*), and a line on the inspector's
  Approvals that links here (§4.34 *A rule change your agent asked for is
  never "nothing"*). The nav badge and the tab title
  count pending proposals plus pending asks; the hero's verdict is asks-only.
- **History**: Approvals' *Rule changes* block (newest 20, then *Show more*:
  *Past the newest 20*, §4.25) says who did it
  (§4.25i `changeWho`), with **Undo** on each undoable change; a 409 shows the
  arbiter's words in the row. A change your agent made or asked for links
  that agent's page (*A rule change and the agent that asked*).

**Describe what you want** (policy-surface.md §8.5.2). A box on the Rules
page: the user writes what they want ("This is my work repo. I use GitHub and
PyPI. Keep .env and ~/.ssh secret."), presses **Suggest rules**, and reviews
the result. Nothing changes until **Apply**.

- `POST /api/policy/assistant {sentence}` (1–2000 characters) runs the helper
  model on the server and answers `{model, note, rows, loosens, edits,
  expected}`. The page lists `rows` (one sentence per suggested rule, written
  by the server's grammar from the rule, never by the model) with a *loosens
  protection* tag where it applies, then *This would let*, then the model's
  `note` LAST in a muted box ("The assistant says"), as text. The over-broad
  typed-ALLOW gate of the proposal card applies and survives a failed Apply.
- **Apply** sends `POST /api/policy/assistant/apply {edits, expected}`
  exactly as previewed; a 409 (the rules changed and applying would now
  loosen more than was shown) offers **Describe it again**.
- **Try it** on a `tryable` row: `POST /api/policy/assistant/try {edits,
  index}` runs the arbiter's Test a flow now and with the whole suggestion
  (nothing written) and shows "Now:" / "After:".
- **Fail-closed**: with no helper model, 503 `{unconfigured: true}` and a link
  to Settings, never a guessed rule; a 422 (not a valid rule change) shows its
  problems. **Models are read-only here** (policy-surface.md §8.4.3a): an
  answer or Apply carrying a model op is a 422, and Settings › Models
  (§4.25l) is the only model editor.
- Tests: `home-js-describe.test.ts`; `policy-assistant.test.ts`;
  `tests/stack/dashboard-assistant.test.ts` (production wiring, models refused
  on both paths). The keyboard focus: below.

**Describe what you want keeps the focus (2026-10-14).** *Suggest rules*,
*Try it* and *Apply* go off while they ask the server, *Cancel* hides
when the answer comes, and *Describe it again* and *Discard* go with
their card. A browser drops the focus of each to `<body>`, and until
2026-10-14 nothing gave it back. In headless Chromium, at 390 and at 1280
px, a press of any of them with the focus on it left the focus on
`<body>`. For *Suggest rules* that lasted the whole time the helper
worked, up to a minute, and the next Tab started at the top of the page.
Now (`home.js` `describeWaits` / `describeAnswered`, `tryRow`,
`applySuggestion`), as Scan for keys and the model picker's preview do
(*While a scan runs, the focus waits on the heading*; §4.25t *The
preview keeps the focus*):

- **While the helper works, the focus waits on the heading.** *Suggest
  rules* or *Describe it again* pressed with the focus on it first gives
  the focus to the card's heading, *Describe what you want*
  (`focusThere`: no Tab stop, no ring). The status line beside the
  button, `role="status"`, says what runs.
- **The answer takes it.** Suggestions open on their first line,
  *Suggested rules* (`focusThere`), as the preview opens on its
  headline. A refusal (no helper, not a valid rule change), or no rule
  change at all, gives it back to *Suggest rules*, on again. The button is
  then described by what came back (`aria-describedby="describe-result"`:
  the reason, its problems, *Open Settings*). Suggestions drop that
  description. A request cancelled gives it to *Suggest rules*, and the
  status line says "Cancelled."
- **Cancel and Discard.** *Cancel* hidden with the focus on it, whether
  pressed or put away by the answer, gives the focus to *Suggest rules*.
  *Discard* does the same, its card gone.
- **Try it** has the focus back once its answer is drawn (`focusBack`).
  The answer describes it: *Now: … After: …*, or the refusal's words.
- **Apply.** Applied, the card is gone, and the line "Applied. Your rules
  are updated, …" takes the focus. Refused (a 409 when the rules changed,
  a stopped service), *Apply* has it back, described by the refusal. On a
  409, *Describe it again* follows it in Tab order.
- **Nothing is taken.** The focus moves only from where the press left it,
  still there or fallen to the page. A move off the heading to another
  place (a `focusout` with a `relatedTarget`) ends the wait. A focus the
  person moved meanwhile stays, and a press made without the focus moves
  nothing.

Headless Chromium after: every case above, at both widths, ends on the
place named, inside the window, and the page does not scroll. Sighted
readers see no change. Presentation only: no route, request, gate or
server text changed. Rejected: keeping *Suggest rules* focusable with
`aria-disabled` (a second Enter would press it, as the scan's doc says),
and moving the focus to *Cancel* while the helper works (a held Enter's
repeat would cancel the request).

**Not covered:** a typed ALLOW changed while *Apply* is out leaves *Apply*
off after a refusal. The focus is then in the ALLOW box, where the person
put it, so nothing falls.

Tests: jsdom `home-js-describe-focus.test.ts` (`press` drops the focus of
a button turned off, as Chromium does, while it still has it). It covers
the wait and the suggestion's first line; the three refusals, each then
followed by suggestions; *Cancel* with and without the focus; *Cancel*
put away by the answer; a focus moved to the box; a press without the
focus; *Try it* answered and refused; *Apply* applied, refused (409) and
*Describe it again*; a focus moved during *Apply*; *Discard*. Eight of
the nine fail on the old page; the ninth is the guard for a press without
the focus. Stack `tests/stack/describe-focus.test.ts` (`secrets`): a real
arbiter with a file-backed policy, the production adapter, a real
dashboard serving Rules signed in, and only the helper model faked. It
walks Suggest rules, Try it (the arbiter's own probe), ALLOW and Apply
(written to policy.yaml), a 409 made by moving the law, and Describe it
again, with the focus at each step. Its oracle: the `.env` value reaches
neither the helper, a drawn page nor an answer.

**First-run card.** Until the first live session is recorded, Home shows a
setup card between the hero and *Approvals waiting*. It is driven by the
projection: `HomeVM.firstRun` (`buildFirstRun`, pure) is present exactly when
`history.total` (live sessions on record, any age) is 0; a test session does
not count. It carries what Mandu does in the running mode (or the saved one,
"Mandu starts with your first agent, in the … mode", when no service answers;
the `secrets` paragraph says untrusted content "is not masked in this mode",
and that secrets "leave this computer only where a rule or your OK allows",
§4.25d);
*Start your agent* (`mandu claude`, `mandu codex`, `mandu openclaw`, `mandu
opencode`); *Mark what is secret* (the catalog is found by itself; anything
else under Rules › Files and folders or `paths:` in `~/.mandu/policy.yaml`;
`mandu doctor --secrets` and `mandu why <file>` explain); and *Check this
computer* (`mandu doctor`). `home.js renderFirstRun` inserts every string as
text, hides the card on a failed `/api/home`, and clears it when `firstRun`
stops coming.

*The card's own sentences draw their commands as code (2026-10-08).* Each
step carries `parts` beside `text`: the same sentence, with each command,
file, variable pattern and policy key a code part ("Put `mandu` in front of
…", "such as `~/.aws/credentials`, `.env` files …, named like `*_TOKEN` or
`*_API_KEY`", "under `paths:` in `~/.mandu/policy.yaml`", "Run `mandu
doctor` in a terminal …"). Until then the step's sentence was one text node,
so it named `mandu doctor` in plain words right above its own `mandu doctor`
chip, and "under paths: in ~/.mandu/policy.yaml" read like a broken
sentence. `buildFirstRun` writes each sentence once, with backticks around
the code spans in its own literals (`ownSentence`), and `text` is the parts
joined, so the words did not change. `renderFirstRun` draws the parts with
`textParts`: each code part as `<code>`, every part a text node, never
markup. A step without `parts` (an older server) shows its `text`.

**Empty states.** A fresh install, before its first agent runs, shows mostly
empty and fallback states, so they follow the rest of the page:

- A command inside a sentence the page writes is `code`, as on the first-run
  card. That covers Home › Running now with no agent (`mandu claude`,
  `mandu codex`); Where your data lives, both when its list fails and in its
  "open to others" note (`mandu paths`); and Settings › Protection service
  on a dashboard started without the service controls (`mandu dashboard`).
  The words are unchanged. A sentence the server writes stays plain text,
  and the page does not parse it.
- Approvals › Answered earlier says "Could not check your earlier answers"
  while the queue is unknown (no protection service), as *Waiting for your
  answer* does above it. It is never a bare heading. The words after each
  "Could not check" name the cause the page knows (*A could-not line names
  the cause the page knows*, below).
- A text button (`button.link-btn`: an action inside a sentence, such as
  Rules › Files and folders' "Browse all files") is drawn as a link. It is in
  the accent color, with no border or fill, and underlines on hover as
  `a:hover` does.
  - The rule is `:where(button.link-btn)`, with zero specificity, so a text
    button with a class of its own (`.rule-source-btn`, `.file-open`,
    `.crumb`, `.file-hosts-edit`) keeps its look.
  - The agent page's "Detailed trace" is a link drawn as a button. It keeps
    its hover without an underline (`a.link-btn:hover`), which no longer
    overrides the text buttons' own hover.
- An empty state has one frame: its dashed box (`.empty`). Most of them sit
  in a list (`.table`, a white framed box), which used to draw a second
  frame around the dashed one, while the same sentence in a card list
  (Approvals waiting) had only the dashed one.
  - A list that holds only its empty state draws no frame or fill of its
    own (`.table:has(> .empty:only-child)`), so it looks as in a card list.
    A browser without `:has()` keeps the old double frame.
  - A note among a list's rows is drawn as a row, with the rows' padding
    and divider and no box of its own. Examples are Settings › Prompt
    filters' "cannot be changed from this page" and "Protection is off",
    and the note under Sensitivity labels.
  - A list with nothing in it is not drawn (`.table:empty`), rather than
    leaving a stray line. Settings › Prompt filters › Exceptions showed one
    while the filters could not be read.
- A list that could not be read says so. It never says "none yet", and it
  offers nothing that needs the list.
  - **Rules.** With no protection service, `/api/policy/panel` still
    answers 200, with a panel that says `available: false` and holds no
    rules. `home.js loadRules` reads that panel as unread. The page used to
    say "No file or folder has a rule of yours yet" and "No rules yet",
    which is false when policy.yaml has rules.
    - The Labeled view now says "Your rules could not be read.", then the
      cause the page knows (below), and with no cause known "The
      protection service may be unreachable." It keeps an *add a rule*
      link, because the file browser works without the service and marks
      its labels unknown; with no answer at all it offers none, since the
      file browser does not work without the dashboard.
    - The list under the explorer is not drawn, so the sentence appears
      once for all of *Your rules*.
  - **Settings › Models.** An unread list hides *Add a model* and closes
    the form if it was open, until a read succeeds. With no service behind
    the route, it says "The model list could not be read.", then the cause
    the page knows, as the Rules page does for the same route. A service
    that answered without a model list (an older one) gets the first
    sentence alone.
  - **Settings › Prompt filters.** Unread (refused, or `available: false`),
    the block is its refusal alone. The meanings with their *What the
    choices mean* fold, the *Exceptions* heading, its note, the list and
    the form are hidden. The block's own *More* stays, since it says what
    the block is.
    - *The fold goes with the meanings (2026-10-09).* Until then
      `home.js loadPromptSettings` hid the meanings' list but not the fold
      around it, so a signed-out reader saw "What the choices mean" under
      the sign-in note, and it opened on nothing. Now the fold is hidden
      whenever it has no meaning to show: while unread, and when a server
      sends none. Tests: UI `home-js-empty-states`, component
      `product-empty-states`, stack `settings-prompt-signed-out` (a real
      arbiter and dashboard, the served page signed out and then signed
      in, and the oracle).

- *A could-not line names the cause the page knows (2026-10-10).* Home's
  hero said each failure in words (*The hero says why in words*, item 1),
  but every line under it, and every list on the pages without a hero,
  still guessed one cause: "The protection service may be unreachable."
  With the dashboard server gone that named the wrong component, under a
  hero that said the dashboard could not reach its own server, and Rules
  still offered "You can still add a rule", whose file browser opened
  empty over an unhandled `fetch failed`. Now a line names a cause only
  when the page knows it, and keeps the hedge otherwise:

  | What the page knows | Home › Approvals waiting, Running now; Approvals › Answered earlier | Approvals › Waiting for your answer; Rules › Your rules; Settings › Models; *Show in policy.yaml* |
  |---|---|---|
  | The service is not running: the server's 503 `unreachable`, the failed dial (*Refusals*), or a panel that answered `available: false` while the latest Home poll knows the service is down | "… The protection service is not running." | "… The protection service is not running. Start it under Settings, or try again in a moment.", the link opening Settings |
  | The dashboard server answered an error | "… The dashboard server answered with an error (500). Refresh in a moment." | the same |
  | No answer at all (the dashboard is gone; for a panel that answered `available: false`, also when the latest Home poll got none) | "… The dashboard could not reach its own server. Refresh in a moment." | the same; Rules offers no *add a rule* |
  | Nothing (`available: false` with a Home poll that answered, as a dashboard with no service configured reads; a home that answered without its queue) | "… The protection service may be unreachable." | the same |

  - One link to the service's Start per page: the hero has it on Home,
    *Waiting for your answer* on Approvals, so the lines under them go
    without.
  - The cause comes from the failed read itself (`home.js readFailure`:
    `unreachable`, the status, or a fetch that threw), shown by
    `cannotCheck`. `/api/policy/panel` answers `available: false` both
    with the service stopped and with none configured, so a panel read
    alone never says "not running": it takes the cause of the latest Home
    poll (`panelCause`). A poll that ends after the panel was read, or
    knows another cause now, draws Rules › Your rules and Settings ›
    Models again (`followCannotCheck`), only when the cause changed, so a
    focused *add a rule* stays. A poll that answers after one that failed
    reads them again instead (*What could not be read is read again when
    the service comes back*, below). Home and Approvals redraw a could-not
    line only when its cause changed, as `sameAsDrawn` does for their lists.
  - *Show in policy.yaml* says the page's own words for a known cause
    (`ownRefusal`: the failed dial, no answer, "arbiter not connected"),
    else the status, never the server's own error, which for the admin
    channel's 503 is developer text.
  - `apiGetControl` (the file browser, a file's *What the rules say*,
    Keys Mandu found, Settings › Sensitivity labels and Prompt filters,
    the rule-change reads) answers a fetch that threw as status 0, never
    a throw its caller leaves unhandled; `refusalText` says status 0 as
    "The dashboard could not reach its own server. Refresh in a moment."
    So with the dashboard gone, *Add a rule* at the top of Rules opens the
    file browser with that sentence in its note. `apiPost` and `apiSend`
    answer the same way since *A click with no answer says so* (under
    *Refusals*).
  - Presentation only: no route, gate or server string changed. Tests:
    `home-js-could-not.test.ts` (each cause on Rules, Settings › Models,
    *Show in policy.yaml*, the file browser and Sensitivity labels; the
    follow and its kept focus), `home-js-home.test.ts` (Home's and
    Approvals' lines per cause, their links, a redraw only on a changed
    cause), the unchanged hedge in `product-empty-states` (the real server
    with no service configured) and across the real arbiter
    `tests/stack/product-could-not-check-words.test.ts`: the served page
    held open signed out while the arbiter stops (each line says not
    running, with its one link per page) and then the dashboard stops
    (each says no answer, no *add a rule*, the file browser's note, no
    unhandled rejection), with the oracle that no page carries a secret's
    value or a token. `tests/stack/product-service-down.test.ts` pins the
    service-stopped lines.
  - *The agent page, Settings › Protection and Prompt filters (later on
    2026-10-10).* These three were left out at first:
    - **The agent page** said "Session not loaded" and "The dashboard
      could not load this session. Refresh in a moment." for an error and
      for no answer alike. `loadAgent` now takes `readFailure`, and under
      "Session not loaded" says "This session could not be loaded.", then
      the error's status or the hero's words for no answer. The 503
      `unreachable` keeps its "Not connected" words, and `found: false`
      is still "Session not found".
    - **Settings › Protection** said "The protection settings could not
      be read." alone, also with the dashboard gone. `loadProtection` now
      keeps why (`S.axesFailure`), and the row adds the cause: an error
      with its status, or no answer. Its read is config.toml, which the
      dashboard reads itself, so with no cause known (an answer without
      settings) the sentence stands alone. It never adds the hedge about
      the protection service.
    - **Settings › Prompt filters** said "The protection service did not
      answer." while Models and Sensitivity labels beside it said "The
      protection service is not running. Start it under Settings, or try
      again in a moment." Its route says that for the failed dial to a
      stopped service: a 502, as for a service that hangs. Now a 502 while
      the latest Home poll knows the service is not running says the
      siblings' words, with the link (`promptUnreadWords`). A poll that
      learns it after the read draws the line again (`followCannotCheck`,
      only when its words changed). A 502 while Home answers still says
      "did not answer", and every other refusal keeps its words.
    - Presentation only (`home.js`): no route, gate or server string
      changed. Tests:
      - `home-js-could-not.test.ts`: each cause on the two Settings
        blocks, and the follow.
      - `home-js-agent.test.ts`: the agent page's words for an error and
        for no answer.
      - `tests/stack/product-could-not-read-why.test.ts`: a real arbiter
        behind the production adapter. A session's agent page is served
        signed out and Settings signed in, both held open while the
        arbiter stops (Prompt filters says it is not running) and then
        the dashboard (the agent page and Settings › Protection say no
        answer). No unhandled rejection, and the oracle: no page carries
        the session's secret value, and the signed-out page no token.
      - `product-service-back` now expects the siblings' words on Prompt
        filters.

- *What could not be read is read again when the service comes back
  (2026-10-10).* Rules and Settings read their lists when opened, and
  after their own buttons. The poll redraws Home, the agent page,
  Approvals' rule changes and Settings' service row, but not these lists.
  So with the service started again under an open page, from a terminal,
  the developer view or another tab, the hero said the secrets were
  guarded while Rules › Your rules and Settings › Models said "… The
  protection service may be unreachable." Signed in, Sensitivity labels
  still said the service was not running. They stayed that way until the
  page was opened again.
  - Now a Home poll that answers after one that failed (`S.homeFailure`
    was set) is a return. On a return, `home.js readAgainUnread` reads
    again, on the page shown, what could not be read:
    - Rules › Your rules (no panel), with the rest of `loadRules`;
    - Settings › Protection (no setting read), Models (`M.unread`: no
      service answered), and Sensitivity labels or Prompt filters, whose
      loaders record an unread block in `S.unread`.
  - On a return, this runs in place of `followCannotCheck`, so the hedge
    never shows on the way. The line keeps its cause until the read
    answers, and is then drawn from the new read.
  - A list that was read stays as you left it, and an unread block has
    no form to lose: while it is unread, Add a model and the Exceptions
    form are hidden, and no label row is drawn.
  - The return is decided after the poll's answer, so of two overlapping
    polls only one reads again. A poll after an answered one reads
    nothing.
  - Not covered:
    - A service that stops and starts within one poll is never seen as
      gone, so a list read in that window stays unread until the page is
      opened again.
    - (Until the next item, the file browser under *Add a rule* also
      kept its note: *The file browser reads its folder again*.)
  - Presentation only: no route, gate or server string changed. Tests:
    - `home-js-could-not.test.ts`: on Rules, the panel is read again once
      and the rule is listed, never the hedge on the way. On Settings,
      only the unread blocks are read again (Models and Prompt filters
      after the service, all four after the dashboard), each once. A poll
      after that reads nothing, and a return on Home reads none of them.
    - `tests/stack/product-service-back.test.ts`: a real arbiter and the
      production adapter, with the served page held open signed in. The
      arbiter stops, and Rules, then Settings, say it is not running. A
      new arbiter on the same sockets brings them back within one poll,
      with no visit and never the hedge. No unhandled rejection, and the
      oracle that no page carries a secret's value or a token.

- *The file browser reads its folder again (2026-10-10).* The browser under
  Rules › *Add a rule* (§4.25m) reads a folder only when you open one.
  With the service stopped, its note carried the failed dial as the route
  got it: "Labels could not be read: the protection service did not answer
  (connect ENOENT /…/arbiter.sock). You can still choose rules." When the
  service came back, Your rules was read again but the browser kept that
  note, every row's "Label unknown" and "No rule" on a file that has a rule
  of yours. After a dashboard restart it kept "The dashboard could not
  reach its own server. …". Each stayed until another folder was opened,
  and opening the browser again cleared the ticked rows and the typed
  path.
  - The note says a failed dial in the page's words, with the link to
    Settings (§4.25m).
  - `F.unread` marks the folder shown as unread: its labels could not be
    read (`labels: "unknown"`, whatever the cause), or its listing got no
    answer or a 5xx (a 4xx is the folder's own: missing, a file, not
    allowed). Two things read it again, once each, through
    `readFolderAgain`:
    - a return (`readAgainUnread`), on whatever page is shown: a visit to
      Rules does not read the browser, so it is read where it stands;
    - the next Home poll that answers after the browser's own read failed
      (`'new'`): an outage too short for the 10 s poll to see, such as a
      click during a restart. A read again that is still unread becomes
      `'again'` and waits for a return, so a lasting cause (an adopted
      service whose labels cannot be read) costs one extra listing, never
      one per poll.
  - A read again (`openFolder(path, {again: true})`) keeps what the person
    did meanwhile: the path box is not rewritten (unless the browser had
    shown no folder yet), the ticked rows stay ticked with what the new
    listing says of them, the opened row stays open while it is listed or
    typed, a typed path's row stays, and the changes waiting are untouched.
    The text typed in the opened row's hosts box and in the hosts box of
    the ticked rows, and the focus with its caret, are put back after the
    redraw (`keepTyping`). A browser that never showed a folder opens
    where it starts.
  - *As far as it was shown (2026-10-15).* A folder is listed 500 entries
    a page, and Show more reads the next page. A read again asks for the
    first page, then the next ones at the offsets Show more reads
    (`pagesUpTo`), until it has as many entries as were drawn
    (`opts.upTo`, `F.entries.length`) or the folder ends, and draws once.
    Until then it read the first page only: every row a Show more brought
    went, *Show more (N more)* came back, a row opened among them closed,
    and a focus on one of them moved up to the last row of the first page
    (`renderFiles` keeps the focus by row index). Worse, a Show more whose
    page came back without labels marks the folder unread itself, so with
    the labels unreadable its rows went at the very next poll. Now the
    rows stay, with their labels as read now, a tick, the opened row and
    the focus on its row.
    - A page whose labels could not be read leaves the whole folder's
      labels unknown: the note stays and the folder stays unread, never a
      note gone while rows say "Label unknown".
    - A later page that fails leaves the pages read and says why over
      Show more, in the words of a failed Show more (`moreRefusal`); a
      press tries again.
    - A folder that changed between two pages may list an entry twice at
      the seam: the read again keeps it once.
  - A listing on its way (`F.answered` below `F.seq`: a folder you just
    opened, or the pages of a folder read again) is never overtaken: the
    return then reads nothing, and that listing's answer decides. A folder
    opened while the pages are read wins over them.
  - On a return, a "What the rules say" box that could not be read asks
    again in place (`readWhyAgain`), in the browser and in the Labeled
    tree; a read again of the folder drops those answers too. Answers that
    were read are kept.
  - Not covered: a "What the rules say" that failed while its folder was
    read, in an outage no poll saw, asks again only after the next return
    or a save.
  - Presentation only: no route, gate or server string changed. Tests:
    - `home-js-files-again.test.ts`: the note's words per cause (a dial,
      ENOENT or ECONNREFUSED, gives the linked words and no socket; an
      adopted service's error as written); a return reads the folder once
      and keeps the path box, the tick, the change waiting, the opened row
      with its typed hosts, focus and caret; a failed "What the rules say"
      asks again; a browser that got no answer opens where it starts; a
      listing with no answer in an outage no poll saw is read by the next
      poll that answers; a lasting failure is read again once, never on
      every poll; a folder opened during the return is not overtaken; a
      folder that was read is not read again; off Rules the return reads
      the browser, and the visit to Rules reads nothing more.
    - `tests/stack/product-files-back.test.ts`: a real arbiter behind the
      production adapter with its secrets surface, a real DashboardServer
      and the served Rules page signed in, the browser in the project
      folder. The arbiter stops: Go shows the linked words, unknown labels,
      a row is ticked and a path typed. A new arbiter on the same sockets:
      within one poll the labels are back, the tick and the typed path
      kept. The dashboard stops with no poll to see it, and Go says no
      answer; a new dashboard on the same port, and the next poll clears
      it. Never a socket in the note, no unhandled rejection, and the
      oracle that no page carries the labelled file's value or a token.
    - `home-js-files-again-pages.test.ts` (as far as it was shown): the
      service's return reads both pages once, and the rows, their labels,
      the tick, the opened row and the focus stay; labels a Show more
      could not read while Home answers: the next poll reads both pages,
      the note stays, later polls read nothing and a return reads again;
      a later page that fails leaves the first, with its words over Show
      more, which tries again, and the focus stays in the list; a folder
      of one page reads no offset; a folder opened meanwhile wins, and a
      poll meanwhile reads nothing; an entry repeated at the seam is
      listed once; a first page without labels keeps the note.
    - `tests/stack/product-files-again-pages.test.ts`: a real arbiter
      behind the production adapter, a real DashboardServer and the
      served Rules page signed in, the browser in a real folder of 521
      entries whose labelled file sorts past the first page. The arbiter
      stops; Go, then Show more: 521 rows, every label unknown, a row
      past the first page ticked and another focused. A new arbiter on
      the same sockets: within one poll 521 rows, no Show more, the
      labelled file shows "Your rule", the tick and the focus kept. No
      unhandled rejection, and the oracle.

Tests: `home-js-empty-states.test.ts` (jsdom over the fetch stub, and the
CSS rules read as text) and `test/component/product-empty-states.test.ts`
(the served page and its styles against the real server with no protection
service). The frame tests apply the page's styles with the theme's tokens
resolved (`css-flatten.ts resolveCssVars`): jsdom reads a border that holds
a `var()` as no border at all.

**Vocabulary.** Product copy uses the plain product words (protected /
masked / blocked / waiting / allowed / secret / agent / rule, plus the
glossary of §4.25d). `home-view-model.test.ts` sweeps the projection's copy
across every verdict and mode AND the page and script's string literals for
inspector terms (`FORBIDDEN`: symbolize, desymbolize, egress, invariant,
T-LLM, U-LLM, quarantine, AgentView, HumanView, lineage, chokepoint, arbiter,
`$MDU:`); the one allowed "egress" is the shared approval route path. Each
later section's copy (proposals, Describe, rules, files, data locations) is
covered by its own sweep.

**Refusals.** The sweep covers the page's own strings, but a refused request
shows the server's `error`, and three of the server's refusals are written
for a developer. `home.js refusalText` says those three in the page's words
wherever a refused request is shown (a Settings block, an answer on a card,
Undo, Save, the file explorer, Suggested, Describe, Models, the protection
service's Start and Restart):

| The server's refusal | The page says |
|---|---|
| 403 from the admin session gate (`server.ts ADMIN_SESSION_REQUIRED`: `mandu dashboard`'s sign-in link, `DASHBOARD_PASSWORD`; §6.x "Signing in") | "Sign in first: in your own terminal, run `mandu dashboard` and open the sign-in link it prints (each link works once), or sign in with the dashboard's password if it has one." |
| 404 "arbiter not connected" (`server/approval-routes.ts arbiterDisabled`) | "The protection service is not connected." |
| 503 `unreachable` (`server/tenant.ts unreachableBody`, "start it under Services") | "The protection service is not running. Start it under Settings, or try again in a moment.", with "Start it under Settings" a link to Settings |
| Any status whose error is the failed dial to the service's socket: `connect ENOENT` or `connect ECONNREFUSED` before an absolute path, bare or inside a route's words ("the protection service did not answer (connect ENOENT /…/arbiter.sock)"), or the arbiter client's `arbiter connection failed` / `closed` | The same sentence, with the same link |
| No answer at all to any request of the page (`answerOf` status 0: the dashboard server is gone; *Empty states*, *A could-not line names the cause the page knows*; *A click with no answer says so*, below) | "The dashboard could not reach its own server. Refresh in a moment." |

Every other error is shown as the server wrote it: the protection service's
own refusals (409 with its text), any other 403, 404 or 503, a validation
problem. No body at all keeps the page's own fallback. The matchers are regex
literals, so the server's text stays out of the page's string literals that
the sweep reads. Presentation only: no gate, status or server string changed.
Tests: `home-js-refusals.test.ts` (jsdom, fed the server's real refusal
bodies, so a rewording on the server fails it) and
`test/component/product-refusal-words.test.ts` (the served page against the
real server with no protection service, with and without the admin cookie:
Settings, the file explorer, Suggested and a refused Describe POST).

*A change that is not valid says why (2026-10-15).* The protection service
checks a change of the rules before anything changes, and the route answers
one it finds not valid 422 with the service's `problems`, each a line in the
terms of policy.yaml: `paths[1].path: pattern "<path>": <why>` for a typed
pattern it cannot use, `edits[0] (<op>): <why>` for a change that no longer
fits the rules. Settings › Models, Sensitivity labels and Prompt filters
already showed them (`modelError`); Your rules' Save
(`file-browser-routes.ts`), a rule's menu (`rule-action-routes.ts`) and
Describe's Apply (`applyAsHuman`) showed only the route's error, so a pattern
typed in Add a rule was refused as "this change is not valid" with no reason.
`home.js changeRefusal` now shows, for a 422 with problems, "Not saved:",
"Not changed:" or "Not applied:", then each problem, one after the other
(`problemWords`): a pattern's line as its path and the reason, without the
file's place for it ("Not saved: ~/notes/[draft: '[' in '[draft' is never
closed (a literal '[' is '\[')."); a change's line without its `edits[N]
(<op>)`; a path in a line as the page shows paths (`shortPath`, `~` only for
the dashboard's home); a line of any other shape as the service wrote it.
Describe's Apply refused that way offers *Describe it again*, as a 409
already did. Changes to save works out what the changes would do before
Save (`files/impact`), and the service refuses the same change there as one
line, "withEdits: " and the problems joined by "; " (arbiter `pathLevels`);
the page printed it whole ("What this changes could not be worked out:
withEdits: paths[6].path: pattern "/home/…": …"). `impactProblems` cuts the
line where each problem starts (its `paths[N]` or `edits[N]`, never at a
"; " inside a problem), so the line before Save reads as Save's does. Any
refusal without problems keeps `refusalText`'s words.
Presentation only: no request, route or service string changed.
Tests: `home-js-change-problems.test.ts` (jsdom: each place, the line
before Save, several problems, a pattern with a quote in it, a page with no
home folder, the words kept without problems) and
`tests/stack/product-invalid-change-words.test.ts` (the served Rules page
against the real arbiter: an unclosed `[` and `/**` typed in Add a rule,
then a valid path saved), which pins the match to the arbiter's own lines.

*A typed pattern says why on its row (2026-10-15).* A pattern typed in Add
a rule is worked out as its row is drawn (`previewPattern`, the same
`files/impact` with the pattern as the only change, §4.25m *Impact*), and
the service refuses one it cannot use there with the same "withEdits: …"
line. The row said only "Which files it matches could not be worked out.",
so the reason came after a label was chosen (Changes to save) or Save
pressed. `home.js patternRefusal` now reads it with `impactProblems`:
"Mandu cannot use this pattern: '[' in '[draft' is never closed (a literal
'[' is '\[')." on the row and in the opened row. The row names the pattern,
so a problem about it is its reason alone; a problem about another path, or
one the page cannot match to the typed text (`shortPath` of the problem's
path is not the row's name, e.g. a page with no home folder), keeps
`problemWords`. Any other refusal names its cause as the line under Changes
to save does: the server's error after a colon, the page's own words as
their own sentence (the Settings link, the command as code), the hedge with
no cause. A pattern the service can use reads as before ("Matches 2 files
under ~/ws: …"). Presentation only: the request and every route are
unchanged. Tests: `home-js-typed-pattern-words.test.ts` (jsdom: the reason
alone on the row and the opened row, several problems, another path and a
page with no home folder, each other refusal, a usable pattern) and
`tests/stack/product-typed-pattern-words.test.ts` (the served Rules page
against the real arbiter: an unclosed `[`, `/**` and `a**b` typed, then
`*.md`, which matches a file; nothing written).

*A click with no answer says so (2026-10-10).* Until then `apiPost` threw
when no answer came (the dashboard server gone, the network down), and its
callers took that three ways:

- Eight had no catch: a rule's effect menu and Remove, a past answer
  turned around or removed, the Undo of the Rules, Models, Sensitivity
  labels and Prompt filters notices, and Settings › Protection's switch.
  Their row stayed disabled over an unhandled rejection, and nothing was
  said.
- An answer on a card, a proposal's verdict, History's Undo, the Saves,
  Describe, Apply and the protection service's Start caught it and said
  "could not reach the server", under a hero that says "The dashboard
  could not reach its own server. Refresh in a moment." for the same cause.
- Suggested's preview, Send, Scan and dismissal caught it as no answer,
  then said "could not reach the server" also for a server that answered
  with no error of its own.

Now every request of the page goes through `home.js answerOf`, which
answers a fetch that threw as `{ ok: false, status: 0 }`, as `apiGetControl`
already did. So each caller takes its refusal path, which gives its row
back and says the table's sentence for status 0 through `refusalText`. Only a
request the page cancelled itself still throws (Describe's Cancel, which
says "Cancelled."). Suggested's fallbacks name what failed with the status
("could not scan (<status>)"), and no caller words no answer itself any more.
Presentation only: no route, gate or server string changed. Tests:
`home-js-click-no-answer.test.ts` (jsdom: each kind of caller says the
sentence, gives its controls back, and leaves no unhandled rejection;
Describe's Cancel; the old words are gone from `home.js`) and
`tests/stack/product-click-no-answer.test.ts` (a real arbiter over the
production adapter with a send rule and a waiting send of a registered
key; three served tabs, signed in, on Rules, Settings and Home while the
dashboard stops: the rule's effect menu and Remove, the switch and the
card's Block each say it in place, no unhandled rejection, and the oracle
that no tab carries the key or a token). The inspector keeps the same
contract in its own words (§4.8 *No answer*).

*The command is code (2026-10-08).* The sign-in sentence, here and in
"Sign in to see real values" (§6), was the one place the page wrote a
command in quotes (`run "mandu dashboard"`), while every other command it
names is code (`mandu claude`, Settings' "Start it with `mandu dashboard`")
and the server's own sign-in pages write `<code>mandu dashboard</code>`.
On Settings the two forms sat one block apart. Now `home.js` keeps the
page's own sentences that name a command as parts (`ownWords`): the plain
string reads "run mandu dashboard and open …", with no quotes or backticks
(what a test's `textContent` or any string-only use sees), and `words()` /
`setWords()` draw it with the command as `<code>` at every place a refusal
or the values note shows (an ask's error line, the Rules, Models, Labels
and Prompt notices, the Settings blocks, the file explorer's note, why and
impact lines, Suggested, Describe, the session page's banner and each
values-withheld note). Any other text, a server's error included, is shown
as written, as one text node, backticks and all. The inspector's lines say
it the same way: its values-withheld line (`SIGN_IN_VALUES_HTML`), the
*Why is this masked?* refusal and the Prompt filters' gated note draw
`mandu dashboard` as code, where they showed quotes or literal backticks;
its drill status lines and the top bar's tooltip keep their plain text.
Presentation only. Tests: `home-js-refusals.test.ts` (every display path,
the code's neighbours, a server's backticks kept), `home-js-agent`,
`home-js-empty-states`, the inspector's `app-js-dual-lanes`,
`app-js-why-symbol`, `prompt-filters-js`, and the served pages over the real
server: `product-refusal-words` (Settings and Rules), `session-page-record`
(the tour signed out: the banner and both Reads' lines, no real value) and
`inspector-record` (its four lines).

*A stopped service, however the route says it (2026-10-10).* The 503
`unreachable` body comes only from the routes behind the tenant's event
source (`server.ts handleTenant`): `/api/home` and `/api/home/agent`, which
the hero and the agent page read, not `refusalText`. Every other route the
page shows a refusal from passed the failed dial on, so with the arbiter
stopped (the production adapter, `arbiter-adapter.ts makeApprovalsArbiter`)
a card's answer said `connect ENOENT /…/admin.sock` (the approval routes
over `MANDU_ADMIN_SOCK`), and Settings › Sensitivity labels, a file's *What
the rules say*, Keys Mandu found, Rules' saves and Describe said
`connect ENOENT /…/arbiter.sock`, bare or after "the protection service did
not answer". `refusalText` now reads that dial as the service being down
(`UNREACHABLE_REFUSAL`, a regex literal like the other two matchers, the same
test as `tenant.ts isArbiterUnreachable` plus the errno before an absolute
path): the dashboard's server dials no unix socket but the arbiter's on
these routes, and a TCP refusal (an address and a port: a model) or a spawn
error is not one, so those stay as written. And "Start it under Settings"
is a link to Settings, whose first block has the Start of the service, as
in the hero and on the agent page: `ownWords` takes a `{ to, text }` part
that `words()` draws with `placeLink`. On Settings itself the link brings
the page back to its top. Left as the server writes it: a refusal without
the dial ("The protection service did not answer.", "… did not answer;
nothing was changed"), which can also be a slow service, and the
admin-channel 503 of a supervised arbiter that stopped ("admin channel
unavailable: … (adopted instance) …", `arbiter-adapter.ts`), server text
for a later change. Presentation only: no route, status or server string
changed. Tests: `home-js-refusals.test.ts` (each form of the dial, the link
and where it goes, the look-alikes kept), and
`tests/stack/product-service-down-refusals` (a real arbiter, net-proxy and
the production adapter; the arbiter stops; the served page's Allow once on
a card drawn before, Settings › Sensitivity labels, Keys Mandu found and
Describe each say the sentence with its link, and no value, token or socket
path shows).

*A connection cut on its way (2026-10-11).* A request already sent when
the service stops gets no failed dial: the arbiter client rejects it with
its own words, "arbiter connection closed" (`arbiter/ipc/client.ts`
`onClose`). `UNREACHABLE_REFUSAL` took those words only at the start of
the error, so where a route wraps them they were shown as written: Keys
Mandu found said "the protection service did not answer (arbiter
connection closed)" under a hero that said the service is not running (the
stack e2e `product-could-not-read-why` caught it once on master, a list
read on its way when its arbiter stopped), and so would Settings ›
Sensitivity labels, a file's *What the rules say*, a suggestion's Save
("…; nothing was saved (…)") and a rule's change ("arbiter: …"). The
matcher now takes the client's words bare, in the brackets of a route's
words, or after "arbiter: ", the three forms the routes write; the errno
form was already taken anywhere. A cut that is a restart rather than a
stop reads the same, and "or try again in a moment" covers it, as
`tenant.ts isArbiterUnreachable` reads the cut as unreachable for the
inspector. A scan the stopping service cut short kept its own server
words, "The scan did not finish: arbiter connection closed" (or the
failed dial with the socket path) under Scan for keys; the page now says
"The scan did not finish because the protection service stopped. Press
Scan for keys to try again." The line is drawn from a read that answered,
so the service runs again and it has no Start link; any other scan error
(another scan running, a folder it could not read) is shown as written.
Presentation only: no route, status or server string changed. Tests:
`home-js-refusals.test.ts` (the forms as the real suggestion,
sensitivity-label, apply and policy-doc routes write them, a look-alike
kept, Keys Mandu found's list, the scan line) and
`tests/stack/product-service-cut` (a real arbiter and the production
adapter behind a pass-through on its data socket that closes the
connection carrying a chosen request: a scan cut by a restart, then the
arbiter stopping with Keys Mandu found's read on its way; the page's
sentences, no value, socket path or "arbiter").

*A write to a connection already closed (2026-10-11).* One more form of
the same stop: the service closed the client's socket after `connect()`
found it open and before the request was written. The write then failed
with Node's own words, "Cannot call write after a stream was destroyed",
which the client passed on bare, so Keys Mandu found said "the protection
service did not answer (Cannot call write after a stream was destroyed)"
(the stack e2e `product-could-not-read-why`, pipeline 10532). The client
now rejects a failed write as the closed connection it is, "arbiter
connection closed (<Node's words>)" with the socket error as its `cause`,
so `UNREACHABLE_REFUSAL` and `isArbiterUnreachable` read it as a stopped
service. It still rejects (fail closed). Test: `arbiter/test/unit/ipc.test.ts`
(a client over a socket whose close already fired).

**The poll keeps your place (2026-10-09).** The page reads Home every 10 s
(`POLL_MS`) and on a return to the tab. Until 2026-10-09 every read drew these
sections again from nothing, whether or not the answer had changed: Home's and
Approvals' waiting cards, *Answered earlier*, the rule changes your agent asked
for, *Rule changes* and the open agent page. So:

- signed out, Block said "Sign in first: …" on its card, and the next poll
