  erased it within 10 s, so the click looked dead (as the inspector's buttons
  did until !1161 and !1181);
- a typed ALLOW on an over-broad rule change was emptied, Allow was turned off
  again and the focus went to the page, so a person who read the warning first
  could not allow it;
- an agent page opened from an answer (§4.25h) scrolled back to the marked step
  every 10 s, wherever the reader had scrolled;
- every fold, "Show all" and "Show what was hidden" the reader had opened on
  that page closed again, and so did the mark a Your secrets time puts on a
  step.

Now (`home.js sameAsDrawn`, the idiom of Settings › Protection's
`runningKey`; Settings' service row follows the same rule, *The service row
follows the service*; Rules and Settings read their unread lists again only
on a poll that answers after one that failed, *What could not be read is
read again when the service comes back*):

- **A poll that brings nothing new draws nothing.** Each of those sections
  keeps the answer it was drawn from. A poll whose answer for the section is
  the same leaves it as it is, with what was typed, the focus, an answer's
  words and what was opened.
  - Since 2026-10-11 this also holds for the rest of Home: the top status, the
    hero, the first-run card, the exposure notice, *Running now* and
    *Earlier*. It also holds for Rules' *Built-in protections* and its line
    on rule changes waiting.
  - Until then these were drawn again at every poll, whatever the answer. A
    headless Chromium showed a focused *Details* and the hero's `?` falling
    to `<body>` within 10 s. The note the `?` had opened (*What masked
    means*) closed, and the top bar's live region (`aria-live`) was written
    again every 10 s.
  - Each section is keyed on what it shows: a row on its agent without its
    stats, and with only its own moment; the hero on its words, its counts
    and the level its `?` names.
- **The moments stay current.** Every moment the page writes
  (`whenNode`, "Oct 9, 14:12 · 3 minutes ago") is written again from its own
  `datetime` at each poll (`refreshWhen`), so a section left as it is never
  reads "just now" an hour later. A Home row's "started 3 minutes ago" or
  "ended 2 hours ago" (`whenLine`, `time.ago`) is too, with its clock time on
  hover.
- **Your own write draws at once.** A write of your own that worked (an
  answer, Allow or Not now on a rule change, Undo) draws every section again,
  so the answered card leaves even if the next answer still lists it.
- **A changed answer is drawn again.** A new question, another rule change, or
  the agent doing more redraws the section, and then:
  - the agent page puts the story's toggles back as the reader left them (each
    fold, "Show all", "Show what was hidden" and file list, by its turn, its
    kind and its place among that kind there; new steps come last, so an
    earlier place holds), and the step a Your secrets time marked stays
    marked. "Show the real value" is not put back: it asks the server for the
    value, so it asks only on a click. An answer to a click made before the
    redraw goes to the same box drawn now (§4.25b *An answer that comes
    after a redraw*);
  - each over-broad change keeps its typed ALLOW, by its id, and the focus
    when its field had it;
  - each card or row of Home's and Approvals' waiting cards, *Answered
    earlier*, the rule changes your agent asked for and *Rule changes* keeps
    the words of the answer to its last button (2026-10-09, run 2130). Until
    then a changed list took them away. The list changes often while an agent
    works: an agent whose send was stopped usually tries it again, and the
    arbiter counts the try on the same question, so its count and moment
    change. So signed out, "Sign in first: …" under Block lasted until the
    agent's next try, and the click looked dead again. Now the words live in
    `S.answers`, keyed by the card's place and id, with the state of the item
    they answered (`data-state`: the outcome of an *Answered earlier* row,
    whether a *Rule changes* row still has Undo). Each draw of the place
    writes them again on the card with that id in that state
    (`putBackAnswers`). They go with the next button pressed on the card, or
    once the card is no longer drawn there in that state: answered elsewhere,
    answered otherwise, undone. A question that comes back with the same id
    (a spent Allow once asks again) has no old words. The inspector keeps
    `E.rowAnswers` much the same way (§4.34), by question id alone. Here
    each place keeps its own: the words of Block on Home's card are not put
    on the same question's card on Approvals. An answer that comes back
    after a poll drew its card again shows on the card drawn now, never on
    the detached one.
  - the agent page does the same (2026-10-09, run 2230). While an agent
    works its page changes at nearly every poll (a new step, the stopped
    send tried again), and until then each redraw took away the words of an
    answer there: "Sign in first: …" under Block on its Waiting card, and
    under **Let it through** in the note under your message (§4.25y).
    Signed in, "Let through in this message." went too, and both buttons
    came back until the agent's next request recorded the answer, so the
    page asked again what the person had just answered. Now the Waiting
    cards are a place of their own (`agent`), and so are the note's rows
    (`note`, each by its finding: the event and index the let-through route
    takes, with its outcome as the state). A let-through that worked is
    kept as its line, drawn in place of the buttons. The next request
    records the answer in a new event, so the line goes once the server
    says it in its own words ("… you let it through in this message").
- **The marked step is scrolled to once a visit,** as the marked Approvals card
  is; a new visit to the page scrolls to it again (§4.25h).
- **Allow stays off after a refusal.** A refused answer re-enables a card's
  buttons, and on an over-broad change Allow stays off until ALLOW is typed.
  Before, the next poll's redraw turned it off again within 10 s.
- **The rows you read stay still (2026-10-15).** Home's *Running now* and
  *Earlier* and History (§4.25ae) keep, when they draw again, every row
  whose session is drawn from what it was (`home.js keepRows`; the key is
  the session id and `rowDrawnFrom` with the list's moment, the key
  `sameAsDrawn` reads). A kept row is the node already in the list, left
  in place. A new or changed row is drawn and put in its place. The rows
  no longer listed are taken out first, so a kept row is never moved. An
  empty state, a could-not line and a Show more line are drawn anew.
  - Until then a changed list was drawn again from nothing. Chromium's
    scroll anchoring holds the rows in view still when something above
    them changes height, but only while its anchor node stays in the page,
    and that redraw removed it. Measured in headless Chromium, with a real
    arbiter, dashboard and served page:
    - History at 1280×800, scrolled to its 20th row: a new session moved
      every row in view down 73 px, a whole row.
    - Home at 390×844, scrolled into Earlier: a session that had just ended
      came in on top and moved every row in view down 148 px. A new
      *running* session, which leaves Earlier as drawn, moved nothing,
      because the browser shifted the scroll by the 148 px itself.
  - Now the rows in view keep their place. A focused *Details* on a kept
    row keeps its focus, and a note opened on a kept row stays open. A
    changed row's focus comes back as before (`pollPlace`/`pollRefocus`).
    *Show them* and Show more keep the rows above them and land on the
    first row they bring.
  - *Not covered:* the changed row itself, when it holds the browser's
    anchor, is drawn anew, so the rows under it may move by the difference
    in its height.
  - Presentation only: no route, gate, count or server text changed.
  - Tests: `home-js-rows-stay.test.ts` (jsdom). It checks:
    - the kept rows are the same nodes, never taken out (a
      MutationObserver);
    - a changed row is drawn anew;
    - the answer's order, the focus, an opened note, and the empty and
      could-not states.

    `home-js-history-poll.test.ts` P2 (the focus on the changed row).
    Stack `tests/stack/product-rows-stay.test.ts`: four real sessions
    through the anthropic-proxy, two real exits, and the served History
    and Home drawn by their own poll, with no value.

Presentation only: no route, gate, status or server text changed. Tests:
`home-js-poll-keeps.test.ts` (jsdom: the same answer leaves the agent page,
Approvals, Home and Rule changes as they are, with their moments refreshed; a
redraw keeps the toggles and the mark; the scroll happens once a visit; your
own write redraws; a typed ALLOW keeps its text and focus; Allow stays off
after a refusal; a changed list keeps the words of an answer on each card
still drawn in the state it answered, drops them with the next button, a
card that left, another outcome or an Undo done, and puts an answer that
comes back after a redraw on the card drawn now; on the agent page, the
Waiting card's words and the note's let-through, refused or done, across a
redraw, gone with the question or once a new event records the answer),
`home-js-approvals-focus.test.ts` (the mark across a poll with the same
answer and across one with a changed answer), and stack
`tests/stack/product-poll-keeps.test.ts`. The stack test uses a real arbiter,
the net-proxy in production wiring and a real dashboard, with the served page:

- signed out, Block meets the real 403, and the card and its words outlast a
  poll while the question still waits;
- the agent sends the same again, which the arbiter counts on the same
  question; the next poll draws the card again ("2 times"), still with its
  words and working buttons;
- signed out, Block on the agent page's Waiting card says how to sign in;
  the agent sends again, and the next poll draws the changed page ("3
  times") with the words still on the card;
- signed in, the agent page opened from the answer is left as drawn and is not
  scrolled by a poll;
- a second stopped send is drawn, keeps the mark and is not scrolled to;
- Block lands and the card leaves;
- the oracle holds.

**An older poll's answer never draws over a newer one (2026-10-12).** Home's
reads overlap: the read when the page opens, the 10 s poll, a return to the
tab, and the read after your own write. Until 2026-10-12 the answer that came
last drew the page, even when its poll was asked first. On a slow network or
a loaded host:

- the read the page opened with, answered from before the protection service
  stopped, drew "Your secrets are guarded." over a newer poll that had found
  it stopped. Settings › Prompt filters says the service is not running only
  while the latest Home poll knows it (*A could-not line names the cause the
  page knows*), so it then said "The protection service did not answer."
  Master pipeline 10542 failed on this (`product-could-not-read-why`, after
  its 60 s wait);
- a poll that failed drew "Not connected." over a newer poll that answered,
  until the next poll;
- a poll asked before you answered a question drew the question again as
  waiting, with live buttons, until the next poll.

Now `loadHome` numbers each read (`S.homeAsked`) and keeps the number of the
latest one whose answer it took (`S.homeTaken`). An answer or a failure to a
read asked before that one is dropped before it touches anything: no state,
no section, no *back* (*What could not be read is read again when the
service comes back*). Answers that come in the order they were asked are
each taken, so a slow read is never lost when nothing newer answered.

*Not covered:* a read whose answer was taken still reads the proposals and
the suggestions before it draws, and a newer answer taken meanwhile is then
drawn by both, as before. The other reads of the page each have their own
guard: the suggestions' follow the next one, the rule changes' (the
proposals and the history) the one after it, and the agent page's, Rules'
and three of Settings' cards' *A read asked before your change never draws
over it*.

Presentation only: no route, gate or server text changed. Tests:
`home-js-poll-order.test.ts` (jsdom, a route that holds an answer: the read
the page opened with, sent after the poll that found the service stopped; a
failure sent after a newer answer; a poll asked before a Block, sent after
it; answers in their order each taken) and stack
`tests/stack/home-poll-order.test.ts`. The stack test uses a real arbiter,
the production adapter and a real dashboard, with the served Settings page
reaching it through a relay that holds one `/api/home` answer:

- the first read, held while the service stops, never draws over the poll
  that found it stopped, and Prompt filters says the service is not running
  with the link;
- a poll held while the service was down never draws over the one after it
  came back, and the prompt filters stay listed;
- the oracle holds.

**A read asked before a change never draws over it (2026-10-12).** Rules ›
*Keys Mandu found* (§4.25r) is read by every Home poll, when the card
opens, and every 3 s while a scan runs. A change made on the card answers
with the server's new list, which the page draws at once: *Scan for keys*,
*Save*, *Not a secret*, and each step of a model run. Until 2026-10-12 a
read asked before the change that answered after it was taken too. On a
slow network or a busy protection service:

- a key marked *Not a secret*, or saved, came back on the next draw (a
  tick, a ⋯), ticked, and waited in *Changes to save* again, right under
  the notice that said it was gone. The next *Save* sent it again;
- a scan's new rows went away, its line went back to the last scan's, and
  *Scan for keys* came back on while the scan still ran;
- a read made after the change (the next poll, the scan's 3 s read) waited
  on that older read and got its answer, and the Home poll waited with it;
- a read after a change was compared with what the last read drew, so a
  key a change took away that came back with the list as it was before
  (*Undo* under *Rule changes*) was never drawn.

Now `setWritten` takes a change's list and counts it (`G.wrote`). A read
notes that count when asked (`G.loadingAt`); if a change's list was taken
while it was on its way, its answer or its failure is dropped before it
touches anything, since the change's list is newer. A call made then reads
again rather than wait on the older read. A read asked after the change
is taken and, the change's list having been drawn, drawn even when it lists
what the last read did. A change's own list is always taken: it is the
server's state after that change. Reads with no change between them are
each taken, as before; at most one read that can still be taken is ever on
its way, so their order needs nothing more.

*Not covered:* two changes made at once (a second *Not a secret* pressed
while the first is on its way) are each taken as they answer; the next read
corrects a list an earlier-sent change answered last.

Presentation only: no route, gate or server text changed. Tests:
`home-js-suggestions-order.test.ts` (jsdom, the next read held: *Not a
secret* and the *Save* after it; *Save*; *Scan for keys* while the scan
runs; a model run's step; a poll after the change reads again; a held
failure; a key *Undo* brought back; reads in order each taken) and stack
`tests/stack/suggestions-order.test.ts`. The stack test uses a real
arbiter's workspace scan, the production adapter and a real dashboard, with
the served Rules page reaching it through a relay that holds one
`/api/suggestions` answer (`tests/lib/holding-relay.ts`, shared with the
Home poll's test):

- *Not a secret* on a key while a read from before it is held; another scan
  files a fourth key, and the next poll draws it while the older read is
  still held;
- the held read, with the key in it, is dropped: a tick draws the list
  without it, and *Changes to save* does not list it;
- *Save* saves the three still waiting and refuses none, and `policy.yaml`
  never names the key marked as not a secret;
- the oracle holds.

**A read asked before your answer to a rule change never draws over it
(2026-10-12).** Approvals' two rule-change lists are read by requests that
overlap. *Rule changes your agent asked for* (§8.6 of policy-surface.md) is
read by every Home poll, by the read after an *Allow* or a *Not now*, and
by Rules for its "waits for your OK" line. *Rule changes*, the history, is
read by every poll while Approvals is open, when it opens, and after an
*Undo*. Until 2026-10-12 the answer that came last drew, even when its read
was asked first. On a slow network or a busy protection service:

- a request you allowed or turned down came back as waiting, with live
  *Allow* and *Not now*, and the Approvals badge and the Rules line counted
  it again, until the next poll;
- a change you undid lost its "Undone" and got a live *Undo* back;
- an older read that failed hid the history a newer read had drawn.

Now `readsInOrder()` in home.js numbers the reads of each list. An answer
or a failure to a read asked before the latest one taken, or before your own
answer to that list answered, is dropped before it touches anything:
*Allow* and *Not now* mark the requests' reads, *Undo* the history's. An
answer that worked also takes the request out of the list the page holds,
since the server no longer lists it as waiting, so a poll that draws before
the read after your answer draws without it too. A refused answer marks
nothing. Reads answered in the order they were asked are each taken, as
before.

Presentation only: no route, gate or server text changed, and *Allow*,
*Not now* and *Undo* send what they sent. Tests:
`home-js-proposals-order.test.ts` (jsdom, a route that holds an answer:
*Allow* and *Not now* with an older read answering after, and before, the
read after the answer; a refused *Allow*; reads in order; the Rules line;
*Undo* both ways; an older failed history read) and stack
`tests/stack/proposals-order.test.ts`. The stack test uses a real arbiter
(`secrets`) where the agent asks to let two `no-model` files be sent to a
host and locks a third, the production adapter and a real dashboard, with
the served Approvals page reaching it through a relay that holds one answer
(`tests/lib/holding-relay.ts`):

- a poll's read of the requests is held, *Allow* is pressed on one, and the
  server approves it; the held read, listing it, never draws it again, and
  only the other request's buttons are live;
- a poll's history read is held, *Undo* is pressed on the agent's lock, and
  the server undoes it; the held read never brings *Undo* back;
- the oracle holds.

**A read asked before your change never draws over it (2026-10-12).** The
agent page is read when it opens, by every Home poll while it is open, and
after an answer to one of its questions. *Your rules* on Rules is read when
the page opens and after each change made there. Settings' *Models*,
*Sensitivity labels* and *Prompt filters* cards are each read when Settings
opens and after each change made in them. A change turns off only its own
row while it is on its way, so a second change can start before the first
one's read answers. Until 2026-10-12 the answer that came last drew, even
when its read was asked first. On a slow network or a busy protection
service:

- a question you answered on the agent page came back as waiting, with live
  *Allow once*, *Always allow* and *Block*, until the next poll;
- after two changes in *Your rules*, the read after the first, answered
  last, drew the second rule with its old effect under the notice "Now
  always allowed.", and an answer you removed came back;
- after two *Remove*s in *Models*, the second model came back under
  "Removed lab.". The same happened to a label and a prompt filter.

Now each of these five lists has its own `readsInOrder()` in home.js
(`AGENT_READS`, `RULES_READS`, `MODEL_READS`, `LABEL_READS`,
`PROMPT_READS`). An answer or a failure to a read asked before the latest
one taken, or before a change of yours to that list answered, is dropped
before it touches anything. Each change that worked marks its list:

- on the agent page, an answer and *Always* for one file;
- on Rules, a rule's or an answer's menu, *Remove* under either, the
  notice's *Undo*, *Save* (the files and Mandu's suggestions), *Move them
  into policy.yaml*, and *Apply* under *Describe what you want*;
- in Settings, each card's *Save*, *Remove*, *Bring back*, *Use the
  default* and the notice's *Undo*.

A refused or declined change marks nothing. Each marked change is followed
by its list's read (the agent page's by the Home read after the answer), so
a list is never left undrawn. Reads answered in the order they were asked
are each taken, as before.

*Not covered:* an answer given on Home or Approvals does not mark Rules'
reads; Rules reads its rules again when it opens. The protection switch has
its own guard, shared by two readers (*The protection switch keeps what you
saved*, below).

Presentation only: no route, gate or server text changed, and every button
sends what it sent. Tests: `home-js-reads-order.test.ts` and stack
`tests/stack/product-reads-order.test.ts`. The jsdom test answers each read
with what the stub server holds at that moment, and marks each read with a
row of its own. It covers:

- the agent page's answer and *Always*, with an older read answering after,
  and before, the read after it;
- two changes in *Your rules* and in *Models*;
- every change listed above, with a read from before it held across it;
- a refused change on each page;
- reads in order on each page, and an older read that fails after a newer
  one on the agent page.

The stack test uses a real arbiter (`secrets`), the net-proxy in its
production wiring stopping a registered key's sends to two hosts, the
production adapter and a real dashboard. The served pages reach it through
a relay that holds one answer (`tests/lib/holding-relay.ts`):

- a poll's read of the agent page is held, *Block* is pressed on one
  question, and the server resolves it. The held read, listing it, never
  draws it again, and only the other question's buttons are live;
- on Rules, the read after *Remove* under the first answer is held, and the
  second answer is removed. The held read, listing the second, never draws
  it again, and the server lists neither;
- the oracle holds.

**The protection switch keeps what you saved (2026-10-12).** The switch in
Settings › Protection, its name and its sentence show the setting saved in
config.toml (`GET /api/config/axes`, *The on/off says what runs*). Settings
reads it each time it opens, Rules reads it with its rules for the line
above them, and a flip draws the answer to its POST. Until 2026-10-12 the
answer that came last drew, even when its read was asked first. On a slow
network or a busy dashboard:

- protection turned off drew Off, then a read from before the flip drew On
  again with "Keys and secret files leave this computer only where a rule
  or your OK allows.", while config.toml said off. Turned on, it went back
  to Off the same way;
- a read made by Rules, answered after Settings had read a newer setting,
  put the older one back in the page. The next Home poll after a restart
  then drew the switch On with "Still off until the protection service
  restarts", although it had just restarted.

Now one `readsInOrder()`, `AXES_READS` in home.js, orders both readers and
the flip. An answer or a failure to a read asked before the latest one
taken, or before a flip that worked, is dropped. Settings' read is then
neither drawn nor kept. Rules still draws its rules from its read and keeps
the newer setting. A refused flip, or one not confirmed with OFF, marks
nothing. Reads answered in the order they were asked are each taken, as
before.

Presentation only: `config/axes`, its CSRF gate, the typed-OFF question and
the frozen axis are unchanged, and the switch posts what it posted. Tests,
in `home-js-reads-order.test.ts` (jsdom, a stub config.toml that a flip
writes and a terminal can change):

- turning it off, and turning it on, with Settings' read from before the
  flip answered after it, then the next Home poll after a restart;
- a refused flip;
- Rules' read answered after Settings read a newer setting;
- reads in order, and an older read that answers, or fails, after a newer
  one.

Stack `tests/stack/protection-switch-order.test.ts` uses a real arbiter
(`secrets`), the production adapter, and a real dashboard with its
config.toml in a scratch `MANDU_HOME`. The served Settings page reaches
it through a relay that holds one answer (`tests/lib/holding-relay.ts`):

- Settings' read is held and the switch is turned off. The dashboard saves
  off, and the held read never draws On again;
- the same the other way, for on;
- the oracle holds.

**The switch holds while its change is on its way (2026-10-13).** Until
2026-10-13 the switch stayed live while its `POST /api/config/axes` was
out, with the press it had (`flipProtection(!on)`) until the answer drew
it again. A second press, a double click or a press because nothing seemed
to happen, posted the same setting again. Turning protection off, it asked
for the typed OFF again although the person had confirmed it, and a second
OFF posted off again; someone who meant to turn it back on was asked to
confirm OFF. The service line in the same row already held its button
while its request was out (`S.serviceOut`).

Now a flip holds the switch from its POST (after the typed OFF, when one is
asked) until its answer, whatever it is (`S.protectOut`, home.js
`flipProtection`):

- **A press while held does nothing.** It asks no question and posts
  nothing.
- **The switch stays focusable.** It is held with `aria-disabled="true"`,
  dimmed as a disabled switch (app.css), not `disabled`, which would drop
  the focus to `<body>`. A screen reader reads it as unavailable, and the
  focus stays on the switch through the answer, which then reads its new
  state.
- **A redraw keeps the hold.** Home's poll, which redraws the row when what
  runs changes, or a read of the setting (Settings opened again, Rules) may
  draw the switch while the POST is out; it leaves the hold as it is.
- **The hold always ends.** Every request answers (`answerOf`: status 0
  with no answer), and the hold ends in a `finally`. A refusal or no answer
  leaves the switch live and says why in the note, as before, so the next
  press is a change of its own. A press not confirmed with OFF holds
  nothing.

*Not covered:* the row says nothing while the change is on its way; the
dimmed switch is the only sign (the dashboard writes config.toml and
answers at once, so the hold is usually too short to read).

Presentation only: what is posted, the typed-OFF question, the frozen axis
and the `config/axes` gate are unchanged. Tests:

- `home-js-settings.test.ts` (jsdom, a POST held by the stub):
  - turning it off, then two more presses and a press after Home's poll
    redrew the row: one question and one POST, the focus on the switch, the
    switch live again on the answer, and the next press posts;
  - turning it on with a double press posts once;
  - a refusal and no answer each end the hold;
  - a press not confirmed with OFF holds nothing;
  - app.css draws a held switch as the disabled one.
- Stack `tests/stack/protection-switch-holds.test.ts` (`secrets`; a real
  arbiter, the production adapter, a real dashboard with its config.toml in
  a scratch `MANDU_HOME`). The served Settings page goes through the relay,
  which now also holds a POST's answer (`holdNext(path, "POST")`) and lists
  what it relayed. It checks that:
  - the dashboard saves off at once while the answer is held. The switch
    holds, keeps the focus and still says On. Two more presses ask nothing
    and post nothing;
  - Settings opened again draws Off, still held, and a press there posts
    nothing;
  - the answer leaves the switch live with the focus, after one question
    and one POST;
  - turning it on with a double press posts once;
  - the oracle holds.

**A page change moves the focus (2026-10-10).** The pages are sections of
one document, and a page change hid every section but one without moving the
keyboard focus. Enter on a link inside a page (Home's *Start it under
Settings*, *Details in Approvals*, an agent's row) left the focus on the
link the change hid. A browser drops it to `<body>`, and a screen reader said
nothing of the new page: the title a `pushState` changes is not read. From a
link to an earlier page (Settings' *Keys Mandu found*, Rules' *Review them in
Approvals*, *See what the agent was doing*), the first Tab left the document
and the second came back at the brand, above the nav. Back and Forward left
the focus where it was. The page also scrolls by itself, once a visit, to
the marked Approvals card, the step where Mandu asked, and the card a link
opens at (§4.25r *A link opens at its card*). The focus stayed behind
there too, so the first Tab scrolled back up.

- **The heading.** Every page change the person makes (a link, Back or
  Forward, a notification, a link that opens at a card) gives the focus to
  the new page's `<h1>` (`home.js focusPage`; `tabindex="-1"`, so it is no
  Tab stop). That is Home's verdict, the agent's name, Approvals, Rules or
  Settings. A screen reader reads it, and the next Tab is the page's first
  control. The first load leaves the focus where the browser puts it.
- **The mark.** Where the page scrolls by itself, what it scrolls to takes
  the focus from that heading (`focusMarked`): the marked Approvals card, its
  *Answered earlier* row or the note that it is no longer waiting, the
  agent page's step (or turn) marked *Mandu asked you here*, and the heading
  of the card `openAtCard` opens at. If the person moved the focus first
  (the agent page is read after the click), they keep it.
- **Drawn again.** A poll that draws the marked card or step again (a
  changed answer, the agent did more) gives the new one the focus back. It
  does so only if the mark still had the focus, which the redraw dropped to
  the page. A focus moved elsewhere leaves the mark (a `focusin`), and no
  redraw takes it back.
- **No ring.** These targets are not controls. The heading has no outline,
  and a marked card or step keeps its accent mark instead, as a step opened
  from a time does (§4.25b). preventScroll keeps each page's own scroll.

Presentation only: no route, gate or server text changed. Tests:
`home-js-page-focus.test.ts` (jsdom; each link is focused before its click,
as Enter does). It covers: the nav's four pages; an agent row and Back to
home; Back and Forward (it waits for the URL to change, see
test-organization.md §8.4); the first load at five URLs; Details marking the
card; the answered row and the gone note; a redraw giving the new card the
focus, but not a focus moved to another card; the agent page's marked step;
a focus moved while the agent page is read; and `openAtCard`'s card
heading. Also stack `tests/stack/product-page-focus.test.ts`. There, a real
arbiter, the net-proxy in production wiring and a real dashboard put a real
question in Approvals, and the served page is driven signed in:

- Details focuses the marked card, never the hidden link;
- *See what the agent was doing* focuses the agent's name while the page is
  read, then the marked step;
- Back focuses the card again;
- the nav focuses Rules', Settings' and Home's headings;
- nothing rejects unhandled, and the oracle holds.

**Back and Forward keep your place (2026-10-18).** Until then every page
change scrolled to the top (`setPage`'s `window.scrollTo(0, 0)`), Back and
Forward included, and History read itself again from nothing. Opening a
session from History or an Approvals card and coming back lost your place.
The rule now: **Back and Forward restore; a link starts fresh.**

- **The place is kept in the page's own history entry.** Before a page
  change pushes a new entry, `savePlace` writes the page left into its
  entry's `history.state.place`: how far it was scrolled (`y`), how many
  History rows were loaded (`rows`), and the session the push opens
  (`opened`). A debounced `scroll` listener and each History draw keep it
  current, so a page left by Back or Forward (whose entry can no longer be
  written once `popstate` fires) keeps its place too. The pushed entry names
  the page it came from (`history.state.from`), which the agent page's back
  link reads (§4.25ad *The back link names where you came from*).
- **Back and Forward hand it back.** `popstate` passes the entry's place to
  `setPage`. History, Approvals and Home go back to it; Rules, Settings and
  the agent page start at their top as before. The page decides, never the
  browser (`history.scrollRestoration = 'manual'`): the browser's own
  restore landed before History's rows were read again. History reads the
  rows you had loaded and lands on the row you opened (§4.25ae *Back returns
  to the row you opened*). Approvals keeps your place over its marked card's
  (`approvalsPlace`: the card still takes the focus, but is not scrolled
  to), and, if the page was shorter until its rule-changes
  read drew, scrolls there again once it has (`keepPlace`), unless you
  scrolled meanwhile. A card answered meanwhile is simply gone; the place is
  kept as near as the page allows. While a place is still landing,
  `placeHeld` keeps a scroll on the way from overwriting it.
- **A link starts fresh.** A top-bar link, Home's *History* link and every
  other in-page link push a new entry: the page starts at its top, and
  History reads one page.
- **The focus** still goes to the page's heading first (*A page change moves
  the focus*); History's opened row then takes it as a marked card does.

Presentation only: no route, gate or server text changed. Tests: unit
`home-js-back-restores.test.ts` (jsdom: the place saved on a push, Back and
Forward into History, more rows than one read, the poll waiting, a link
starting fresh, the back link's names and its Back, Approvals' place); stack
`tests/stack/history-back-restores.test.ts` (below, §4.25ae).
`home-js-page-focus.test.ts`'s *Back to home* now waits for the URL, as its
Back and Forward test does: opened from Home, the link is Back.

**An answer keeps the focus in its list (2026-10-11).** Every answer button
on the page turns its card's buttons off while the answer is on its way, and
a browser drops the focus of a button turned off to `<body>`. A headless
Chromium showed it 50 ms after Enter on *Allow once*. The list was then drawn
again, and the focus stayed there: a screen reader read neither the next
question, nor "Nothing is waiting for you.", nor a refusal's words. The next
Tab went wherever the browser guessed, and a refused answer's button, on
again, had lost the focus. This covers every button whose card or row the
poll draws (the answer places of *The poll keeps your place*): Home's and
Approvals' waiting cards, the agent page's *Needs your OK*, *Answered
earlier*'s *Block instead* / *Allow instead*, Allow and Not now on a rule
change your agent asked for, *Undo* under *Rule changes*, and the agent
page's *Let it through*.

- **Pressed with the focus in its card.** Only then does anything move
  (`home.js holdFocus`, kept beside the answer's words by `dropAnswer`). A
  click made with the focus elsewhere (a browser that does not focus a
  clicked button) moves nothing.
- **An answer that worked.** The next draw of its list gives the focus on
  (`focusOn`, from `putBackAnswers`), to the first of these that is shown:
  - the card or row with the answered id, when it is still drawn (an
    answered row's new outcome, an undone change);
  - the card that took its place, else the one before it;
  - the list's own line ("Nothing is waiting for you.", or "No question is
    waiting for you." while a rule change waits: *An empty list never says
    nothing waits over a rule change*);
  - its section's heading;
  - the page's heading (the agent's name once *Needs your OK* is hidden,
    Approvals once no rule change is left).

  It is never an answer button, so a second Enter never answers another
  question. A row still drawn keeps the focus across the next draws while it
  has it, as a mark does.
- **An answer that was refused.** The button pressed, on again, gets the
  focus back. The refusal's words describe it (`aria-describedby`), so a
  screen reader reads them with the button (`focusAnswered`). A card drawn
  meanwhile in another state takes the focus itself. A let-through that
  worked leaves its row in place without its buttons, and the row keeps the
  focus.
- **Nothing is taken back.** A poll while the answer is on its way moves
  nothing. A focus the person moves elsewhere meanwhile (a `focusin`) drops
  the answer's place, also when the same draw removes that control.
- **The ring.** A card, row, line or heading takes the focus with
  `tabindex="-1"`, so it is no Tab stop, and with preventScroll. A keyboard
  answer shows the browser's focus ring on it (`:focus-visible`), as on the
  page's buttons; a mouse answer shows none.

Presentation only: no route, gate or server text changed. Tests:
`home-js-answer-focus.test.ts` (jsdom; `press` drops the focus of the
button turned off to `<body>`, as Chromium does). It covers each place, the
last card, a refusal, a poll mid-answer, a focus moved out of the list or to
another card, and a press without the focus. Also stack
`tests/stack/product-answer-focus.test.ts`. There, a real arbiter, the
net-proxy in production wiring and a real dashboard put three real questions
in Approvals. Signed out, a refused Block gives its button the focus back,
described by "Sign in first: …". Signed in, Block gives the focus to the next
card, then the one before it, then "Nothing is waiting for you."; nothing
rejects unhandled, and the oracle holds.

**The poll keeps the focus (2026-10-11).** A changed answer still draws its
list again from nothing. The agent working on Home brings a new count or a
new question, Approvals' questions are tried again, and the agent page gets
a new step. The focused control leaves the page, and until 2026-10-11 the
focus fell to `<body>` there: a screen reader lost its place, and the next
Tab started over. Only an answer's own focus and the marks were put back
(above). Now the poll keeps it, as the inspector's repaint does (§4.32 *A
repaint keeps the focus*):

- **The place.** Before the poll draws, `home.js pollPlace` says where the
  focus is in `#main`, in terms the draw makes again:
  - each keyed element on the way down and its rank among those keyed alike.
    A key is an id or the `data-*` an element is drawn with: a card's
    `data-id`, a Home row's and its *Details* link's `data-session`, a
    question's link's `data-ask`. Keys are compared as values, never put in a
    selector. Ids the page numbers as it draws (a help note, an answer's
    words) are no keys;
  - then the control's tag, its rank there and its words.

  This runs in `loadHome` (over `#main`), the agent page's draw
  (`renderAgentPage`, once its answer changed) and `loadRuleHistory` (over
  *Rule changes*). While an answer holds the focus (`holdFocus`), the answer
  says where it goes, and the poll takes no place.
- **Given back.** After the draw, `pollRefocus` acts only if the focus
  fell. An answer's or a mark's own focus stays, and so does one the person
  moved. It goes to the first of these:
  - the control drawn at that place that reads the same: the same agent's
    *Details*, by its session, even when a new agent was drawn above it;
  - the card, row or step that had the focus itself, found by its key
    whatever its words say now. A card or a list's line an answer landed
    on carries the `tabindex="-1"` that `focusThere` gave it, and its new
    copy is drawn without one, so `focus()` alone does nothing on it: a
    non-control that `focus()` did not reach is given the focus through
    `focusThere` (2026-10-12; until then the card that took an answered
    question's place, or "Nothing is waiting for you.", lost the focus to
    `<body>` on the next poll that drew its list again). A control, or a
    scroll box a browser makes focusable, takes it with `focus()` and gets
    no `tabindex`;
  - else, when the control is gone (the agent ended and its row moved to
    *Earlier*, the question was answered elsewhere), its section's heading;
  - else the page's heading, as an answer does.

  Never another action, and never `<body>`. A control must also be reachable:
  on, not hidden, not in a closed fold. A help note open at the place opens
  again, so the hero's *What masked means* stays open while the agent's
  counts change under it.
- **Nothing is taken.** A focus outside what was drawn again (the nav, a
  block's own link), or none, is not moved.
- **In proportion to the page (2026-10-15).** The place and its return
  list the elements of a tag under a keyed element with `listed`, which
  reads the live collection's length once. They spread it until then, and
  a spread reads the length again at every step; in jsdom that read scans
  the whole collection for an element named `length`, so the cost grew
  with the square of the elements drawn. With the file browser's 521 rows
  under *Add a rule* and the focus in one, one poll took 7 s on an idle
  host and over a minute on the CI guest, and
  `tests/stack/product-files-again-pages.test.ts` failed: the folder was
  read again only after the served page's wait ran out (pipelines 10830 to
  10834). For the same reason a row's second menu looks up the glossary's
  words (`sendMeaning`) under `#rules-glossary`, not with a query over the
  whole page once a row. Test: `home-js-files-big-folder.test.ts` (a poll
  with the focus in a folder of 600 rows reads each collection's length
  once; drawing it asks the document no query per row).

Presentation only: no route, gate or server text changed. Tests:
`home-js-poll-focus.test.ts` (jsdom), covering:

- an unchanged poll keeps Home's nodes, the focus and an opened note;
- the top status is written only on a change;
- a row's moment is refreshed in place;
- each section draws again when what it shows changed;
- a changed answer gives the same agent's *Details* the focus when the
  rows moved;
- a gone control gives Running now's heading the focus;
- the hero's `?` keeps the focus and its note;
- the agent page's opened toggle keeps the focus;
- Approvals' question link keeps the focus, and no `tabindex`;
- Home's card an answer gave the focus keeps it when a poll brings another
  question, and Approvals' line "Nothing is waiting for you." keeps it when
  a poll draws the lists again (2026-10-12; both fall to `<body>` on the
  old page);
- a focus outside, or none, is not moved.

Also stack `tests/stack/product-poll-focus.test.ts`: a real arbiter, the
net-proxy in production wiring and a real dashboard, with the served Home
signed out:

- a poll with the same answer leaves *Details* and the opened `?` as they
  were;
- after a second stopped send, the session's own new *Details* has the
  focus;
- after a third, the hero's new `?` has it with its note open;
- nothing rejects unhandled, and the oracle holds.

**A question has a name (2026-10-11).** The cards of a page offer the same
answer buttons beside their words. Three waiting questions are three
*Allow once*, *Always allow* and *Block*, in `.ask-actions`, outside the
sentence. Until 2026-10-11 a card was a bare `<div>`, so a screen reader
that Tabbed to a button read "Allow once, button" with no word of what it
allows. The card an answer gives the focus to (*An answer keeps the focus
in its list*, above) had no name either: a focused generic `<div>`
(ARIA 1.2 forbids naming one) is read differently by each screen reader,
or not at all.

Now each card or row that asks for an answer, or records one, is a group
named by its own words (`home.js nameBy`: `role="group"`,
`aria-labelledby`). That covers:

- Home's and Approvals' waiting cards and the agent page's *Needs your OK*:
  the question's sentence ("The agent wants to send your secret
  `STRIPE_KEY` to `collector3.example`");
- *Answered earlier*'s rows: what was asked;
- a rule change your agent asked for: its headline;
- *Rule changes*' rows: the change's sentence, not the rows under it;
- the "Mandu found N possible keys" card;
- the rows of the note under your message (*Let it through*): the
  finding's words, else its category.

A screen reader reads the name once, as the focus enters the card ("The
agent wants to send your secret STRIPE_KEY to collector3.example,
grouping. Allow once, button"), and when an answer gives the focus to the
card itself. The name is the words alone, never the buttons, the moment
or a link. The id is numbered as drawn (`ask-name-N`), because Home and
Approvals draw the same question at once and ids are server data. A poll
that draws nothing new keeps it. Like an answer's words, it is no key of
the poll's focus place (`DRAWN_ID`). A refused answer's words still
describe its button (`aria-describedby`), and the card keeps its name.
Sighted readers see no change. Presentation only: no route, gate, server
text or CSS changed. Tests: `home-js-question-names.test.ts` (jsdom: every
place above, server text kept as text, unique ids while Home and Approvals
both draw a question, a poll with and without a change, the focus kept
across it, a refusal), and stack `tests/stack/dashboard-question-names.test.ts`
(below, §4.32).

**A Settings row's button names its row; a change keeps the focus
(2026-10-11).** Settings › Models, Sensitivity labels and Prompt filters
draw a row per model, label, kind and exception, each with the same few
buttons. Until 2026-10-11 a headless Chromium read 27 controls on
Settings, and 16 shared a name with another: "Remove" ×7, "Test
connection" ×3, "Edit", "Save" and "Use the default" ×2. A screen
reader's list of buttons said "Remove" seven times, with no word of what
each removes. Every change there also left the focus on `<body>`: the
row's buttons go off while the change is on its way (`busyRow`), a browser
drops the focus of a button turned off, and the card's list is drawn again
after it. Enter on a label's Save, on *Use the default*, on a model's
Remove, even on *Test connection* (which draws nothing again), and on a
notice's Undo, sent a screen reader back to the top of the page.

- **The names.** Each row's button is named by its row (`aria-label`), its
  own words first, so a voice command that says what it sees still works
  (WCAG 2.5.3): "Test connection to ollama", "Edit the model lab", "Remove
  the model lab", "Bring back the model corp-big", "Save the level for
  Confidential", "Remove the level for Confidential", "Use the default for
  an email address", "Remove the exception for an email address matching
  `*@example.com`". The menus beside them were already named by their row.
  A kind's words keep their capitals inside the sentence (`promptKindWords`:
  "What happens to a secret Mandu already knows", no longer "… mandu …").
- **The focus.** `home.js settingsPlace` takes where the focus is in the
  card before the buttons go off, as the poll takes it (*The poll keeps the
  focus*: `pollPlace`). A row is found by its `data-id` (a label),
  `data-name` (a model), `data-category` (a kind) or `data-category` and
  `data-match` (an exception: two of one kind are two places). After the
  change, `settingsRefocus` acts only if the focus fell (`pollRefocus`):
  - the control drawn at that place that reads the same: Save on the same
    label, drawn again; Save on the row a label with no level became; *Test
    connection* on the same model;
  - else, when it is gone (a model or an exception removed, *Use the
    default* used, an Undo done), the card's heading. The card's notice, a
    live region, says what changed.

  Never another row's button: removing one of two exceptions of a kind
  never hands the focus to the other's Remove.
- **A refusal, or a change not made.** A refused change gives the focus
  back to the button pressed, on again, described by the refusal's words
  (`aria-describedby`), as an answer does. A change cancelled at its
  question gives it back too.
- **Nothing is taken.** A focus moved elsewhere meanwhile, or a press made
  without the focus in the card (a browser that does not focus a clicked
  button), moves nothing.

Sighted readers see no change. Presentation only: no route, gate, question
or server text changed. The Models form's Save and Cancel follow since the
same day (*The Models form keeps the focus*, below), and so do the Rules
page's changes (*A change in Your rules keeps the focus*, below). Tests: `home-js-settings-focus.test.ts` (jsdom over the
server's own view models; `press` drops the focus of the button turned off,
as Chromium does): the names and no shared one, a label's Save (also on a
label with no level), a model's Remove and Bring back, *Test connection*,
*Use the default*, one of two exceptions of a kind, a refusal, a cancelled
question, Undo, a focus moved elsewhere and a press without the focus. Stack
`tests/stack/settings-row-names.test.ts`: a real arbiter with the models,
labels and exceptions in policy.yaml, a loopback model server and a real
dashboard serve Settings. Signed in, the names hold; a label's Save keeps its
focus and reaches policy.yaml; one of two exceptions and a model are removed
(read back from policy.yaml and the arbiter) with the focus on the card's
heading; *Test connection* keeps its focus. Signed out, a refused Remove
gives its button the focus back, described by "Sign in first…", and changes
nothing. The oracle holds. The names above were checked with no notice open;
a notice's Undo follows (*A notice's Undo says which change it undoes*,
below).

**A notice's Undo says which change it undoes (2026-10-11).** A change made
in Rules › *Your rules* or in a Settings card (Models, Sensitivity labels,
Prompt filters) shows a notice above the card's list, a live region, with
*Undo* when the change has one (`home.js rulesNotice`, `modelsNotice`,
`labelsNotice`, `promptNotice`). A notice stays until the next change in
its own card. So a model removed, then a label saved, then a kind's choice
changed leave three notices on Settings. Until 2026-10-11 each button was a
bare "Undo": a screen reader's list of buttons said "Undo" three times, and
a Tab onto one read "Undo, button", with no word of what it reverses. The
words beside it were a `<span>` that nothing pointed to. Now
(`noticeWords` / `noticeUndo`):

- **The name.** Each notice's Undo is named by its card, its own word first
  (WCAG 2.5.3): "Undo the change in Your rules", "Undo the change in
  Models", "Undo the change in Sensitivity labels", "Undo the change in
  Prompt filters". With every notice open, no two controls on Settings
  share a name.
- **The description.** It is described by its notice's words
  (`aria-describedby` → `<notice id>-words`), so a Tab onto it reads, for
  example, "Undo the change in Models, button, Removed lab. New sessions use
  …".
- **Nothing else moves.** A sighted reader still sees "Undo". Undo in one
  card leaves the other cards' notices, and their Undo, as they were. An
  undone or refused notice has no button. The focus after an Undo is as
  before: the card's heading.

Presentation only: no route, gate, question or server text changed. The
rows of Approvals › *Rule changes* keep their own rule: each is a group
named by its sentence (*A question has a name*), and since 2026-10-12 their
Undo is named by what the change did (*Details, Undo and the agent link
name their row*, below). Tests:
`home-js-notice-undo.test.ts` (jsdom over the server's own view models)
covers:

- three notices open on Settings: their names, their descriptions, and no
  shared name;
- Undo in one card, with the others unchanged;
- a refused Undo;
- the Rules notice.

Stack `tests/stack/notice-undo-names.test.ts` uses a real arbiter with two
models, a label, a kind's choice and a sending rule in policy.yaml, and a
real dashboard over the production adapter, signed in:

- the three Settings changes give three named, described Undo buttons;
- Undo in Sensitivity labels puts the level back (read through the
  arbiter), while the model stays removed, the kind keeps its choice and
  the other two notices are unchanged;
- on Rules, the notice's Undo is named and described, and makes the rule
  allow again;
- the oracle holds.

**Details, Undo and the agent link name their row (2026-10-12).** Two lists
on the product page repeat one control on every row:

- Home's *Running now* and *Earlier* end each agent's row with *Details*,
  each to a different agent's page.
- Approvals › *Rule changes* ends a row with *Undo* and, for a change your
  agent made or asked for, "See what the agent was doing" (*A rule change
  and the agent that asked*, above).

A Home row is no group. A *Rule changes* row is a group named by its
sentence, and two rows often share it ("Your agent tightened your rules",
once per file). Until 2026-10-12 a headless Chromium read three links named
"Details" on Home, and three "Undo" and four "See what the agent was doing"
on Approvals. A screen reader's list of links or buttons said the same
words once per row, with nothing to tell them apart. A Tab onto two of
those Undo buttons read the same group name.

Now each such control is named by its row (`home.js rowControlName`,
`aria-label`), its own words first (WCAG 2.5.3), as a Settings row's
buttons are (*A Settings row's button names its row*):

- **Details:** "Details: <agent>, <what its row says>", in the row's own
  words (`agentRow`): its first line, what you asked and where, also on a
  row waiting for your OK (*Agents, not sessions*), so two agents waiting
  in one folder get two names. Examples: "Details: Claude Code, Fix the
  test in ~/ws", "Details: Claude Code, Deploy the site in ~/api" (waiting),
  "Details: Codex CLI, No prompt reached the AI".
- **Undo and the link:** "Undo: <what the change did>" and "See what the
  agent was doing: <what the change did>" (`loadRuleHistory`,
  `changeWords`). *What the change did* is the first line drawn under the
  sentence, with ", and N more" for a longer change. A change that lists
  no line uses its sentence instead. Example: "Undo: Make ~/proj/ci.conf a
  secret no AI may read".

Nothing else moves:

- The eye still reads "Details", "Undo" and the link.
- The addresses, the rows' group names (still the sentence alone), the
  focus (the poll keeps a focus on a named control: it finds a control by
  its drawn words), Undo and the links work as before.
- A name is the text the row already draws, set as an attribute, never
  markup, and nothing the page did not show.
- Links outside these two lists keep their name: Answered earlier, the
  question cards, and the Rules lines. Those are named by their group,
  whose words differ. The request cards were the exception; their
  answers are named too since the same day (*The answers on a request
  card name their request*, below).

Presentation only: no route, gate, server text, CSS or focus rule changed.
Tests:

- jsdom `home-js-row-control-names.test.ts`:
  - the names under Running now and Earlier, unique;
  - a poll that changes a prompt renames the link and keeps its focus;
  - two rows with one sentence;
  - ", and N more", and the sentence fallback;
  - the group names unchanged;
  - a named Undo that still undoes, with the poll keeping its focus;
  - markup kept as text;
  - Answered earlier's link unchanged.

  On the old page 6 of the 8 cases fail (the other two are guards), and 11

- Stack `tests/stack/row-control-names.test.ts` (`secrets`): a real

**A click on a session's row opens it (2026-10-18).** Every session on Home
(*Running now*, *Earlier*) and on History is a row of four cells
(`agentRow`). Until 2026-10-18 only the *Details* at its right end opened
the session: at 1280 px a 90 × 21 px target in a 942 × 72 px row, under
WCAG 2.2's 24 px minimum (2.5.8). The prompt, what a person recognises and
reaches for first, did nothing on a click.

Now a pointer click anywhere on the row opens its session, as *Details*
does (`home.js rowClick`, one listener with `wireNav`'s, so a row `keepRows`
kept behaves the same as a new one):

- a plain click opens it in place, through the same `setPage` call as the
  link. Back returns to the list as it does from *Details*;
- a Ctrl/⌘/Shift-click or a middle click opens the link's address in a new

- the row shows it: a pointer cursor and the page's row hover
  (`background: var(--bg)`, as the Rules rows have) in both themes. Under

What a row click leaves alone:

- a click that ends a text selection (a drag across the prompt to copy it)
  opens nothing;
- the keyboard and screen readers. The row gets no `role`, `tabindex` or
  name, *Details* stays its one tab stop with its name (above), and a list
  reads as before.

Not a stretched `::after` link over the row, which would cover the help
buttons and stop text selection. Tests:

  - `home-js-home.test.ts`: a running row's prompt and an Earlier row's

  - `home-js-history-poll.test.ts` P7: a click on the third row, a node

**The answers on a request card name their request (2026-10-12).** Every
request your agent makes has one headline, "Your agent wants to change a
rule" (`toProposalCard`), and the card on Approvals is a group named by it
(`proposalCard`, `nameBy`). Until 2026-10-12 two waiting requests drew two
buttons named "Allow", two named "Not now", two links named "See what the
agent was doing" and, for two wide changes, two fields named "Type ALLOW to
confirm this wide change", in two groups of one name. A screen reader's list
of buttons said "Allow, Not now, Allow, Not now" over the buttons that loosen
your rules, with nothing to say which request each one answers.

Now each is named by what its request changes, in the words of a *Rule
changes* row's Undo above (`rowControlName`, `changeWords`), its own words
first:

- *What the request changes* is the card's first drawn line, with ", and N
  more" for a longer request. Example: "Allow: Make ~/proj/.env a secret no
  AI may read, may be sent to api.stripe.com".
- A held change to policy.yaml (§4.6) lists no edit, so it is named by its
  first "This would let" line. A card with neither uses its headline.
- The four controls are *Allow*, *Not now*, "See what the agent was doing"
  and the wide change's field ("Type ALLOW to confirm this wide change:
  …"; its placeholder is unchanged).
- A name is built only from the lines drawn above the reason, so it never
  carries the reason your agent gave. That reason is untrusted words, and
  it stays drawn last, as text.

The group names (still the headline), the visible words, the addresses,
the typed ALLOW gate, what Allow and Not now post and the focus are as
before. Presentation only: no route, gate, server text or CSS changed.
Tests:

- jsdom `home-js-request-control-names.test.ts`:
  - two requests with one headline, each control named by its own line,
    no two alike;
  - ", and N more", and the ALLOW field;
  - the held disk change and the headline fallback;
  - the reason never a name;
  - markup kept as text;
  - a named Allow and Not now answering their own request, with a poll
    that brings a third request keeping the focus on the same card.

  On the old page 5 of the 6 cases fail (the reason case is a guard).
- Stack `tests/stack/request-control-names.test.ts` (`secrets`): a real
  arbiter, the real anthropic-proxy on its production client with two
  sessions, two agents' requests to send `.env` to two hosts (one with a
  reason) and a real dashboard. The served Approvals names each card's
  controls by its own host and never by the reason. The Allow named for
  `api.github.com` approves that request alone: the other still waits, and
  the one change recorded is its own (read back from the listings). The
  oracle holds. It fails on the old page.

**The Models form keeps the focus (2026-10-11).** Settings › Models adds and
edits a model in one form, opened above the list by *Add a model* or by a
row's Edit. Until 2026-10-11 a headless Chromium left the focus on `<body>`
after every Cancel (the form hides with the focus on Cancel), every Save
that worked (Save goes off while the change is on its way, then the form
hides and the list is drawn again), Enter in a field that saved, and every
refused Save, whose error line did not describe it. The token field was
also named with its hint ("Token variable name (optional) An environment
variable's name. …"), as was the exception form's pattern box under
Prompt filters.

- **Closed: back to what opened it.** Cancel, and a Save that worked, give
  the focus to the control that opened the form (`home.js modelFormBack`):
  *Add a model*, or the Edit of the model's row, drawn again (after a Save,
  the row under the name saved, so a rename still finds it). That control
  gone or hidden (the list could not be read again): the Models heading. The
  notice, a live region, says what was saved. The control is brought into
  view: a row far down the list may be off the screen.
- **Not saved: back to Save.** A refused Save, or one declined at its
  question, gives the focus back to Save, on again. Save is described by the
  form's error line (`aria-describedby="model-error"`, empty when nothing
  was refused), so a screen reader reads the refusal with it. Enter in a
  field that is refused leaves the focus in the field, to fix it.
- **Nothing is taken.** The focus moves only if it was in the form at the
  press and fell (to `<body>`, or into the hidden form) by the time the
  answer came: a focus moved elsewhere meanwhile, also onto a row the list
  then draws again, and a press made without the focus in the form (a
  browser that does not focus a clicked button), move nothing.
- **The names.** The token field is named by its label, "Token variable name
  (optional)", and described by its hint; the exception form's pattern box
  is named "When it matches" and described by its hint
  (`aria-labelledby`).

Sighted readers see no change but the focus ring. Presentation only: no
route, question or server text changed. **Not covered** then: the form had
no Escape to close it; it has now, *Escape closes it*, below. Tests:
`home-js-model-form-focus.test.ts` (jsdom;
`press` drops the focus of the button turned off, as Chromium does): Cancel
from *Add a model* and from a row's Edit, a Save that worked (an add, an
edit under a new name, Enter in a field), the row gone or *Add a model*
hidden after it, a refusal and a declined question, Enter in a refused
field, a focus moved elsewhere (also onto a row drawn again) and a press
without the focus, the names. Stack `tests/stack/model-form-focus.test.ts`:
a real arbiter with two models in policy.yaml and a real dashboard over the
production adapter serve Settings. Signed in, Edit then Cancel gives lab's
Edit the focus; an edited model saves (the arbiter lists the new model)
with the focus on lab's Edit, drawn again; an add with a bad address is
refused with the focus on Save, described, then saves with the focus on
*Add a model*; the token field's name holds. Signed out, a refused Save
gives Save the focus back, described by "Sign in first…", and policy.yaml
is unchanged. The oracle holds.

**Escape closes it (2026-10-11).** Until then only Cancel closed the Models
form: in a headless Chromium, Escape did nothing in any of its fields, its
API style menu or its tick boxes. Now Escape in the form is Cancel
(`home.js wireModelForm`): the form closes, what was typed is dropped (as
Cancel drops it; nothing is saved before Save), and the focus goes back to
what opened it by the same rule (`modelFormBack`: *Add a model*, or the
Edit of the model's row, else the Models heading). Not:

- **an Escape an open note takes.** A `?` note in the form (*About your
  own model*, …) closes on Escape and marks the key taken
  (`preventDefault`), so the form stays open; the next Escape closes it;
- **an Escape that ends an IME composition** (Korean, Japanese or Chinese
  input: `isComposing`, or keyCode 229 where a browser does not say so),
  nor one with Shift, Ctrl, Alt or Meta;
- **while Save's change is on its way** (Save is off, as after Enter in a
  field): the change cannot be called back, so the form stays and the
  answer decides, as before (closed with the focus back, or the refusal
  said). After a refusal, Save is on again and Escape closes the form;
- **an Escape outside the form**, including on *Add a model*.

Presentation only: no route, question or server text changed. Tests:
`home-js-model-form-escape.test.ts` (jsdom) covers Escape from *Add a
model* in a field (the typing dropped) and from a row's Edit on the menu and
on a tick box, the note first, Save on its way and after a refusal, and a
composition, keyCode 229, each modifier and three places outside the form;
each case fails on the page before the change, and thirteen mutations of the
change are each caught. Stack `tests/stack/model-form-escape.test.ts`: a
real arbiter with two models in policy.yaml and a real dashboard over the
production adapter serve Settings, signed in. Escape after lab's address is
retyped gives lab's Edit the focus; Escape in an add gives *Add a model* the
focus and the form reopens empty; a note takes the first Escape; policy.yaml
and the arbiter's list are unchanged. An Escape while a real Save is on its
way closes nothing, and the change lands with the focus on lab's Edit,
drawn again. The oracle holds.

**A change in Your rules keeps the focus (2026-10-11).** Rules › *Your
rules* changes a sending rule, a program or connection rule, or one of your
answers at once: its row's menu (*Always allowed* / *Always blocked*),
*Remove* under the row opened with its ⋯, and the notice's *Undo*. Each
turns its row's menu or button off while the change is on its way
(`busyRow`), and the list is drawn again after it (`renderRules` draws
`#rules-list` from nothing). Until 2026-10-11 nothing gave the focus back, so
each left a screen reader on `<body>`, at the top of the page. A refused
change turned the menu back on without the focus, and its words described
nothing. The rule is now the one Settings follows (*A Settings row's button
names its row; a change keeps the focus*, above), with the same
`settingsPlace` / `settingsRefocus` (`changeRule`, `answerAgain`,
`forgetAnswer`, `rulesNotice`'s Undo):

- **A change in a row's menu.** The focus goes back to that row's menu,
  drawn again, which now shows the new effect. The row is found by its
  `data-rule` (a rule's id, or `answer:<id>`).
- **Two changes to the place rules**, both in `home.js`, so a menu whose
  value changed is still the same place:
  - a menu that has a name reads as its name ("What happens for
    api.example.com"), not its options (`readsAs`);
  - a menu's colour (`data-effect` on its wrapper, an answer's or a send
    rule's *allowed* or *blocked*) is not part of the row's key
    (`placeKey`).

  The poll's place (*The poll keeps the focus*) follows the same two rules.
- **Remove, and Undo.** The row, or the notice's button, is gone, so the
  focus goes to the *Your rules* heading. The notice, a live region, says
  what changed ("Rule removed.", "Answer removed. You will be asked again
  next time.", "Undone.") or why an Undo was refused. It never goes to
  another row's menu or button.
- **A refusal, or a change not made.** A refused change gives the focus
  back to the menu or button pressed, on again, described by the refusal's
  words (`aria-describedby`). A Remove declined at its question gives it back
  too.
- **Nothing is taken.** A focus moved elsewhere meanwhile, or a press made
  without the focus in the block, moves nothing.

Sighted readers see no change. Presentation only: no route, gate, question
or server text changed. The *Changes to save* bar and *Move them into
policy.yaml* follow since the same day (*Changes to save keeps the focus*,
below). Tests:
`home-js-rules-focus.test.ts` (jsdom; `press` and `pick` drop the focus of
the control turned off, as Chromium does) covers:

- a rule's menu and an answer's menu, with the focus back on the same row's
  menu drawn again;
- Remove on a rule and on an answer;
- Undo, and a refused Undo;
- a refused menu and a refused Remove, each described;
- a declined question;
- a focus moved elsewhere, and a press without the focus.

Stack `tests/stack/rules-change-focus.test.ts` uses a real arbiter with two
sending rules in policy.yaml and a registered key whose send the person
answered *always block*, and a real dashboard over the production adapter
serving Rules:

- signed in, a rule's menu keeps its focus, and the arbiter's panel has
  the rule blocking;
- Undo gives the focus to the heading, and the rule allows again;
- Remove gives the focus to the heading, and the rule is gone;
- the answer's menu keeps its focus, and the arbiter lets that send go;
- signed out, a refused change gives the menu the focus back, described
  by "Sign in first…", and changes nothing;
- the oracle holds.

**Changes to save keeps the focus (2026-10-11).** The *Changes to save* bar
(§4.25n) saves, at once, the file labels chosen in Your rules, in Add a rule
and in Keys Mandu found. Its Save goes off while the changes are on their
way (`saveFileChanges`); a save that worked hides the bar, and Discard hides
it under its own button; each row's Drop, or Skip on a suggestion, draws the
list again under its own. Until 2026-10-11 each left a screen reader on
`<body>`, at the top of the page. *Move them into policy.yaml* went off and
was drawn away the same way. The bar is no card: it sits after them, sticky,
and hides once nothing waits. So it has its own rule (`home.js barPlace` /
`barRefocus`), in the words of the one above:

- **The bar gone** (saved, discarded, the last change dropped or skipped):
  the *Your rules* heading. The notice under it, a live region, says what
  was saved ("2 changes saved.", with Undo).
- **A change dropped or skipped while others wait:** the bar's own heading,
  "Changes to save N", which reads the new count. Never another row's Drop.
- **A weaker change asked about first:** the question's first line ("These
  changes make protection weaker. Check them before you save."), a line,
  not a Tab stop; the next Tab is its *Why?* box. Never *Save anyway*: the
  Enter that pressed Save, pressed again, must not loosen a rule.
- **A refusal** (the save refused, a 409 after the question, a suggestion
  refused): Save, on again, reading "Save changes" after a 409. Save is
  described by the bar's error line (`aria-describedby="lock-error"`), so
  the refusal's words are read with it.
- **The move.** The notice sits in *Your rules*, so it follows the rule
  above (`settingsPlace` / `settingsRefocus`): after the move, the *Your
  rules* heading, with "Moved N rules into policy.yaml." in the notice. A
  refused move says why in the move notice's own box (`showAskError`, on its
  own line), and its button gets the focus back, described by those words.
  Until 2026-10-11 a refused move wrote its words into the bar's error line,
  hidden while nothing waits to be saved (the usual case): signed out,
  *Move them into policy.yaml* said nothing at all.
- **Nothing is taken.** A press made without the focus in the bar (a browser
  that does not focus a clicked button), or a focus moved elsewhere while the
  changes were on their way, moves nothing. A focus left in the hidden bar
  counts as fallen (jsdom and a browser that has not yet moved it).

Sighted readers see no change but the refused move's words. Presentation
only: no route, gate, question or server text changed; the weaker-change
question still takes a second, separate press. The Models form's Save and
Cancel (Settings) follow since the same day (*The Models form keeps the
focus*, above). A label chosen in the tree or the browser follows too (*A label chosen in Your rules keeps
the focus*, below). Tests:
`home-js-pending-focus.test.ts` (jsdom; `press` holds the page's POST and
drops the focus of the button turned off, as Chromium does): Save, the
question then *Save anyway*, a refused Save and a 409, Drop of one of two
and of the last, Skip on a suggestion, Discard, the move and a refused
move, and nothing taken (a focus elsewhere, no focus, a focus moved
meanwhile). Stack `tests/stack/pending-save-focus.test.ts` uses a real
arbiter with a policy.yaml rule on a key file and a rule made on the page
before rules lived in policy.yaml (`setPathLabel`), and a real dashboard
over the production adapter serving Rules:

- signed out, a refused move says so in its box and keeps its button's

- signed in, a file chosen in the browser and saved: the *Your rules*

- the same file made *Not secret*: the question, then *Save anyway*: the

- two changes: Drop on one gives the bar's heading, Discard the *Your
  rules* heading, and nothing is saved;
- the move: the heading, and the page rule is in policy.yaml;
- the oracle holds.

**A label chosen in Your rules keeps the focus (2026-10-11).** Choosing a
file's label is the Rules page's main task. Each row of the *Your rules*
tree (§4.25f) and of the browser under *Add a rule* (§4.25m) has two menus
(§4.25p), and the row opened with its ⋯ has *Update*, *Remove my rule*,
*Show in policy.yaml* and *Show in its folder*. A choice waits in *Changes
to save*, and `home.js pendingChanged` draws the tree and the browser again
from nothing. Until 2026-10-11, in headless Chromium:

- a choice in a tree row's menu (either one), *Remove my rule*, *Update*,
  and Enter in the hosts field left the focus on `<body>`, at the top of the
  page;
- the same choice in the browser moved the focus to the row's tick box
  (`renderFiles` gives a focused row back by its tick box);
- *Show in policy.yaml* goes off while it reads the lines
  (`toggleSourceInto`), and Chromium drops the focus of a button turned
  off, also under an opened sending rule (§4.25g);
- *Show in its folder*, and an answer's *Show in the file browser*, scrolled
  the page down to the browser with the file's row opened, but left the
  focus on the button, out of view, so the next Tab went on in the tree;
- the opened row's buttons read "Remove", "Show in policy.yaml", "Update",
  with no word of the row they act on.

Now:

- **A choice, Remove my rule, Update.** `pendingChanged` takes the focus's
  place in the *Your rules* card before it draws, as the poll takes it
  (`pollPlace`). A row is found by its `data-path`, and a button or the
  hosts field by its id. A menu reads as its name ("Which AI may read ~/proj/old",
  "Where ~/proj/old may be sent"), and its colour (`data-level`,
  `data-send`, `data-from` on `.label-pick`, like a rule's `data-effect`)
  is no key: the colour is what the menu shows, not which menu it is. After
  the draw, only if the focus fell, the place is given back to the control
  drawn there that reads the same, else to the *Your rules* heading
  (`pollRefocus`). `renderFiles({ placed: true })` then skips its tick-box
  fallback. *Changes to save* keeps its own rule (`barRefocus`, above): its
  focus is outside the card.
- **Show in policy.yaml** gets the focus back after its read, reading *Hide
  policy.yaml*, if it had the focus and the focus fell.
- **Show in its folder** and **Show in the file browser** pass the button
  pressed to `setFilesView` (`at.by`). Once the folder is read, the focus
  goes to the opened row's ⋯ ("Close ~/proj/deploy.token"), or to the path
  box when the file is not listed (`focusPicked`). It moves only if the
  button had the focus at the press and still has it, or the focus fell.
  A file past its folder's first page is listed too: the folder is read
  on down to it (§4.25m *Browsing*, *A picked entry past the first page*).
- **The names.** Each button under an opened row names its row, its own
  words first (WCAG 2.5.3):
  - actions read as a sentence: "Remove my rule on ~/proj/old", "Update
    where ~/proj/deploy.token may still be sent", "Remove the rule for
    b.example", "Remove your answer about ~/proj/notes.md", "Open
    ~/proj/old";
  - the links to elsewhere take a colon: "Show in policy.yaml:
    ~/proj/deploy.token" (then "Hide policy.yaml: …"), "Show in its folder:
    …", "Show in the file browser: …".
- **Nothing is taken.** A choice, or a press, made while the focus is
  elsewhere (or nowhere) moves nothing.

Sighted readers see no change, except that the focus ring follows *Show in
its folder*. Presentation only: no route, question or server text changed,
and a choice still only waits until Save. *Keys Mandu found*'s opened row
(its *Show in policy.yaml* and *Not a secret*) has its own section, *Keys
Mandu found keeps the focus*, below. **Not covered:** a redraw the page
makes by itself while the focus is in the browser (a save's own read of
Your rules) still gives a focused row back by its tick box.
Tests: `home-js-choice-focus.test.ts` (jsdom; `press` drops the focus of the
button turned off, as Chromium does) covers:

- either menu in the tree, and the browser's menu (never the tick box);
- *Remove my rule*, *Update* and Enter in the hosts field;
- *Show in policy.yaml* in the tree and under a sending rule, and *Hide*;
- *Show in its folder*, and *Show in the file browser* for a file not listed

- the names, with no name shared;
- nothing taken: the focus elsewhere, or nowhere.

Twelve mutations of the change are each caught. Stack
`tests/stack/rules-choice-focus.test.ts` uses a real arbiter with a
policy.yaml rule on a key file, a sending rule and a rule made on the page,
and a real dashboard over the production adapter serving Rules:

- signed out, a menu keeps its focus with the choice waiting, *Show in

- signed in, the page rule's menu keeps its focus, and Save gives the

- the sending rule's row names its buttons, and *Show in policy.yaml* keeps
