  the tour's log, `dashboard/test/fixtures/tour-1791164083-1418381.ndjson`),
  `agent-page.test.ts`.
- **A secret the AI read before it was marked** (2026-10-06). After the
  label, the proxy re-sends the AI's own earlier read as a placeholder, so
  the AI may say it never saw the value. At 10:42 the tour's AI wrote "I
  never saw the actual contents … Nothing from the file entered this
  conversation" about `deploy/staging.conf`, which it had read as it was at
  10:41. The page agreed: the line under that reply said only that it held
  the secret, and every `secret` chip of the file was titled "the AI never
  got the real value". Only *Your secrets* said otherwise. Now the turns
  say what the card says:
  - **The reply's line** (`StoryReply.kept`) adds "The AI read its real
    value at `<time>`, before it was marked a secret." With more than one
    secret it reads "the real value of `X`" ("of a secret of yours" with no
    name). It says this only of a read at or before the reply.
  - **The chip** (`StoryPart.early`, the ISO moment) is titled "A secret,
    masked here. The AI read its real value at 10:41, before it was marked
    a secret." ("Your secret `X`, …" when named). This covers the Read's
    "Got ⟨secret⟩" and every chip in a reply, a command or a question.
  - **One source.** secret-story.ts `earlyReads` gives the tokens of each
    *Your secrets* entry whose first line is "read before it was marked"
    (`aiSaw` `early`), with that entry's moment (`pageEarlyReads`, the same
    arguments as `pageSecrets`). It reads the believed events, the full
    leak check, the mode and the level, as the card does. So where the
    card makes no such claim (a fired leak check, Off, a level that lets
    the AI read it), neither does a turn. A secret masked from the start
    keeps its "never" title.

  Times and names only: no token or value enters the page's data. Tests:
  `session-page-record.test.ts` (unit and component),
  `agent-page.test.ts`, `home-js-agent.test.ts`.
- **Labelled after the session** (2026-10-12). A session learns of a label
  only when one of its later requests carries the earlier read masked
  (`maskedLater`). One that ended first, or sent nothing after, never does:
  in the first-session tour, a person who exited Claude Code and then
  applied the rule on `deploy/staging.conf` saw its read on the first
  session's page as a plain one ("Nothing here needed guarding."), though
  the AI got what is now a secret. Now the page asks when each file it read
  was labelled:
  - **The times** (server/label-times.ts, three reads, each made once per
    request): `pathLevels` names the rule that decides each file a Read
    reached the AI as it was (later-labels.ts `plainReads`: any agent's
    read tool, nothing masked, no check stopped it; the file is the
    recorded origin, or the argument placed under the session's folder or
    `~`). A policy.yaml rule's time is the newest recorded change that
    wrote its row (`lock:<path>`, the rule-change log, §4.25i
    `ruleOrigins`); a Rules page label's is its own record's
    (`confidentialityState`). No record, a removed row, a later unrecorded
    edit, a built-in rule, `public` or `any-model`: no time, no claim. An
    arbiter without the reads, or one that fails, leaves the page as the
    session's own record.
  - **The step.** A Read strictly before its file's time reads outcome
    `raw`, note "The AI got this as it was: nothing marked it a secret when
    it read it.", `later` "Marked a secret at `<time>`, after this read: the
    AI saw its real value."; the summary names the file ("The AI read your
    secret `staging.conf` as it was: it was marked secret only later.").
  - ***Your secrets*.** A file no entry tells of gets one with no
    placeholder: no `ref` (no "Show the real value"), no send, fill or
    block line (the AI had the value itself, so "Mandu did not fill in its
    real value" would read as safety), "The AI read its real value at
    `<time>`, before it was marked a secret at `<time>`, so nothing in this
    session masked it." and "If it holds a key or a password, change it:
    the AI saw it as it was."; `saw` `early`, the tag's `since` the label's
    time. An entry that already tells of the file (a later read of it was
    masked, which alone said "never the real value") takes the earlier read
    as *A secret the AI read before it was marked* does. Off and a fired
    leak check keep their own first line.
  - **Home.** A row counts such a file as read before it was marked, as
    the page's tiles do. `HomeFacts` keys its cache on the label times of
    the files a session read as well as on its listing, so a label made
    after a session ended changes its row without the session moving; a
    waiting card about the file learns the AI read it (`readFirstFiles`,
    §4.34).

  Paths, levels and times only. Tests: `later-labels.test.ts`,
  `label-times.test.ts` (unit), `session-page-later-label.test.ts` (stack:
  a real arbiter, proxy and dashboard; one file marked through the
  rule-change log, one on the Rules page, after the session ended).
- **Originals on a click, a secret's value on its own click.** A masked
  result's right half has "Show what was hidden", revealing the original as
  escaped text under "Content from outside. Mandu kept it away from the
  AI." (harness `<system-reminder>` blocks stripped, 4000 characters max).
  A secret ships no text: signed in it has "Show the real value", which
  asks the server for that one value (*Showing a real value*, §4.25b);
  signed out it says how to sign in (§6).
- **The question** stays plain text in `prompt` (the page title; items
  spelled "[masked]"), and `promptParts` carries it with each item as a chip,
  never its value. A Claude Code shell escape (`!cmd`, sent as
  `<bash-input>`/`<bash-stdout>` tags) reads "You ran" with the command and
  its output. `firstUserPrompt` tries every user message and never falls back
  to a transcript role marker. OpenClaw's time envelope before the typed text
  (`[Sun 2026-10-11 05:20 GMT+9] `, its `formatEnvelopeTimestamp`) is not
  part of the question and is left out (2026-10-11, the OpenClaw tour walk;
  `promptOf`, test `home-first-session`).
- **Code looks like code, and markdown like formatting** (2026-10-05): in
  the reply (both halves), the question and the agent's narration, markdown
  spans and fences render as code; `**bold**` renders bold when its pair is
  on the same line and each `**` touches a word (code and chips inside it
  stay code and chips); a line starting `- `, `* `, `+ ` or `1. ` is a list
  item with its mark in a hanging indent (two spaces of indent per level,
  three levels), and `#` to `######` plus a space a heading line. Code takes
  precedence: a `**` or `- ` inside a span or a fence stays as written. The
  rest stays as written: no links, tables or italics, so an `_` or `*` in a
  name such as `STRIPE_KEY` never turns italic, and an unpaired `**` (a
  prompt clipped mid-pair) is drawn as typed. Before, every reply of the
  first-session tour read `- **STRIPE_KEY**: …` and `**The lock:** …` with
  the markers as text. Built from text nodes and plain elements only, never
  HTML parsing (home.js `markdownNode`); the inspector quotes replies as
  recorded. Tests: `home-js-agent.test.ts` (each rule and what stays as
  written), `session-page-record.test.ts` (the served tour).
- **Caps**: the newest 60 turns (`TURN_CAP`; "N earlier turns are not
  shown here." and its **Show them**, §4.25ad), 80 steps per turn (the same,
  per turn); past its first 6 steps the browser
  folds each run of ordinary steps behind its own "Show N more steps", and a
  `blocked`, `waiting`, `unmasked` or `sent` step stays in sight in its place
  (the blocked exfiltration used to hide behind the fold). So does the step
  just before each such step (2026-10-05): the fold used to hide the agent's
  `curl … collector.evil.example` right above "Mandu blocked a request to
  collector.evil.example", so the block answered a request nothing on the
  page had made. The step is drawn in time order and nothing claims it
  caused what follows (a net event carries no call id to say so). A run of
  one step is drawn, not folded: its button took the same room. An ask's
  moment opens the fold that holds it (§4.25h). The "actions blocked" tile
  counts the story's blocked steps. Tests: `home-js-agent.test.ts` (the
  fold boundaries), `session-walkthrough.test.ts` (the served story).
- **A long reply folds** (2026-10-19, nightly run 1930). Every reply was
  drawn whole: a recorded 1,392-character reply took 883 px of a 2,028 px
  page at 1280 px and more than a phone screen at 390 px, and a coding
  agent's summary of a task is often 3,000 to 6,000 characters, so the
  steps where Mandu stepped in sat far below it. Now a reply taller as
  drawn than 12 of its lines shows its first 10, fading out at its foot
  (`.reply-text.folded`: `max-height: 10lh`, a mask), and one button under
  it reads **Show the whole reply**; pressed, the whole reply shows and it
  reads **Show less** (`aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` the text; the focus
  stays on it). home.js `foldReply`:
  - **Measured where it is drawn.** The rule reads the rendered height, not
    characters, so a phone folds sooner than a desktop; a ResizeObserver
    measures again when the width changes, and a reply that fits shows no
    button and looks as before. A ~4,000-character reply is 900 px at
    1280 px and 2,453 px at 390 px; folded, 225 px at both.
  - **A split folds both halves together**, to the same height, under one
    button below the row, so the two sides stay level. Only the height
    changes: the AI's half never gets the filled-in text.
  - **What a reply held stays in sight.** The *kept* line and the *not
    filled in* note are drawn under the text, outside the fold, and the
    button comes after them: a folded reply never hides that it held a
    secret.
  - **A choice per reply while the page is open.** A poll that draws the
    page again keeps a reply you opened open (`storyToggles`, kind
    `reply`); a new visit starts folded.
  - **Find in page.** The fold is a plain `max-height` with `overflow:
    hidden`, so the folded text stays in the page and the browser's find
    reaches it. A browser that scrolls a folded text to show something in
    it (its find in page, a Tab to a link there) opens the fold, and the
    page moves by what the text had scrolled, so the words stay where the
    browser put them. The spec asked for `hidden="until-found"` on the
    folded rest; the reply is one block of text and inline marks with no
    rest to hide apart, so the scroll stands in for `beforematch` in every
    browser.

  Tests: `home-js-reply-fold.test.ts` (the fold and its button, a short
  reply, the split, the notes outside it, a redraw, a reveal by scrolling),
  `tests/stack/reply-fold.test.ts` (the real stack in `secrets`, a real
  Chromium at 1280 and 390 px, and the oracle: no key and no admin token in
  any read, signed out or in).

**Security property: secrets at any depth.** (What the page CARRIES; a
signed-in click can still ask for one secret's value, *Showing a real value*
below.) The inspector's reveal uses the
arbiter's DEEP `desymbolize`, which would expand a secret nested inside an
ordinary item, so the product route never uses it. `valueScope` gathers the
session's recorded values plus a secret set (twin prefixes
`nomodel_`/`anymodel_`/`localmodel_`, every symbol of a secret lineage flow,
any non-public level), and `revealParts` expands ONE level at a time: a nested
secret becomes a `secret` chip, a token the session never recorded stays
`masked` (unknown level: fail toward hidden). Missing values come from
`revealValues` through `EventSource.resolveSymbol` (the arbiter's SHALLOW
`resolve` op) under the same checks and a 200-call budget, so a secret is
never even requested. An unreachable arbiter leaves items masked.
**Signed out** (§6 "Reads and the admin session", 2026-10-05) the route
builds the page from the signed-out projection of the events and resolves
nothing (`buildAgentPageFor(…, values=false)`): no original at any depth
reaches the page, `valuesShown` is false, and home.js says "Sign in to see
real values: in your own terminal, run `mandu dashboard` and open the
sign-in link it prints." (the command as code, §4.25 "Refusals") above the tiles and in place of each "Show what
was hidden" (`#agent-values-note`; the prompt filter's reveal button is not
drawn).

**Showing a real value (2026-10-05).** "Do we have any security issues if
showing the real value in the dashboard?" Only while any process on the
host could read it; with the read gate (§6) a signed-in person may see a
secret's real value, one at a time, on a click. Where the page shows a
secret, a signed-in viewer gets a **Show the real value** button: on a
masked step whose result held a secret (one button per secret, its words
naming the secret when it held more than one) and on each **Your secrets**
card; each button is named by its secret (*Show the real value names its
secret*, below). Never inline by
default: a page left open, shown or screenshotted (the first-session tour's
screenshots had to be redacted) shows placeholders until someone clicks.
- *The data.* The page still never carries a value or a token: a secret
  is named by an opaque ref, `secretRef(session, token)` = 24 hex of
  sha256 (`view-model/secret-ref.ts`), on `StoryHidden.secrets[]` and
  `StorySecret.ref`. The ref is not a secret; the route is what is gated.
- *The route.* `POST /api/home/reveal {session, ref}`
  (`server/secret-reveal-routes.ts`). A POST, so the global gate has
  already required the CSRF header and the admin session. It recomputes
  the refs of the secrets the session RECORDED, over its believed events
  only (`agent-page.ts revealableSecrets`: the tokens the session's symbol
  rows, bands and lineage name that the page's own rule calls a secret),
  and resolves only a match, one token, through the source's human-plane
  `desymbolize`. An ordinary item, another session's secret, a claimed
  event's token, an unknown or malformed ref resolve nothing (404, 400);
  no protection service is 501; a token the arbiter no longer holds is
  404. The value goes back in the answer only, never in a log line
  ("showed one secret value of session …"). Mirrors
  `/api/prompt-filters/reveal`'s scoping (§4.25y).
- *The page.* `home.js secretValueBox`: the value lands as text in a
  `<pre>` with "Only you see this. The AI still has only the masked
  version."; "Hide it again" empties the box, so the value leaves the
  page. A refusal is shown in the page's words (`refusalText`). Signed
  out there is no button, only the sign-in sentence.
- Tests: `test/unit/server/secret-reveal-routes.test.ts` (the gate, the
  scoping, the one token asked), `test/unit/view-model/agent-page.test.ts`
  (the refs on a step), `test/unit/ui/home-js-agent.test.ts` (the click,
  text not markup, hide empties it, the card, the refusal, signed out), and
  the stack e2e `tests/stack/dashboard-value-gate.test.ts` G3 (a same-host
  process is refused; the signed-in human gets the arbiter's value; a ref
  the session did not record gets nothing).

**Show the real value names its secret (2026-10-12).** A session that read
two secret files draws four *Show the real value* buttons: one on each Your
secrets card and one on each step. Until 2026-10-12 a button was named by
its secret only when one step held several. A headless Chromium read four
buttons named "Show the real value" for two different files, and a pressed
one read "Hide it again" with no word of whose value it shows. A screen
reader's list of buttons gave the one control that puts a secret's value on
screen the same name four times.

Now each is named by the words the page draws for its secret, its own words
first (`home.js secretValueBox`, `rowControlName`, `aria-label`; WCAG
2.5.3), as the rows' controls are (*Details, Undo and the agent link name
their row*):

- **A Your secrets card:** by its heading (`renderAgentSecrets`,
  `lineWords`): "Show the real value: The file ~/ws/.env".
- **A step that held one secret:** by the secret's short name, the one its
  line already draws (`StoryHidden.secrets[].name`): "Show the real value:
  .env".
- **A step that held several:** its words already say it ("Show the real
  value of API_KEY"), so it has no other name.
- **Once pressed:** "Hide it again: <the same secret>", for all three; a
  second click gives the first name back.
- A secret the page has no name for keeps the bare words, as before.

A name is only words the page already draws, set as an attribute, never
markup; it never comes from the answer, so it never carries the value. The
visible words, the box's group name ("The real value", §4.25 *A box that
scrolls says what it holds*), the ref posted, the sign-in gate and the
value as text are as before. Presentation only: no route, gate, server
text or CSS changed.
Tests:

- jsdom `home-js-reveal-names.test.ts`: two cards and two one-secret steps
  named apart; *Hide it again* named, its box still "The real value", the
  name back on a second click, no name with a value; a several-secret step
  keeps its words and names its *Hide it again*; a nameless secret
  unchanged; markup kept as text. On the old page 4 of the 5 cases fail
  (the nameless case is a guard), and 9 of 9 mutations are caught.
- Stack `tests/stack/reveal-names.test.ts` (`secrets`): a real arbiter with
  `.env` and `creds.json` at `no-model`, the real anthropic-proxy on its
  production client with one session that reads both, and a real
  dashboard. The served page's four buttons have four names, each with its
  own file; the card button named for `creds.json` shows that file's value
  and not the other's, and reads "Hide it again: …/creds.json"; no name
  carries a value; signed out there is no button and no value; neither
  value reached the model. It fails on the old page.

**Show the real value keeps the focus (2026-10-14).** *Show the real
value* goes off while it asks the server for the value
(`secretValueBox`), and so does a prompt filter's *Show what was hidden*
(`promptReveal`, §4.25y). A browser drops the focus of a button turned off
to `<body>`. Until 2026-10-14 nothing gave it back. In headless Chromium,
at 390 and at 1280 px, a press with the focus on the button left it on
`<body>`:

- once the value showed, so a screen reader heard neither *Hide it again*
  nor that the box had opened;
- after a refusal ("the protection service no longer holds its value"),
  whose words described nothing, so the reader lost its place.

Now both buttons call `home.js focusBack` once the answer is drawn, as
*Show in policy.yaml* does (*A label chosen in Your rules keeps the
focus*):

- **The value shown.** The button has the focus back, reading *Hide it
  again* with its secret's name, `aria-expanded="true"`.
- **Refused.** The button has the focus back, described by the refusal's
  words (`aria-describedby`, the line `showAskError` drew). A retry that
  works drops the description.
- **Only a focus that fell.** The button gets the focus back only if it
  had it at the press and the focus is on `<body>` or gone at the answer.
  A focus the person moved meanwhile stays, and a press made without the
  focus moves nothing.

*Hide it again* asks nothing, so it keeps its focus as before. Headless
Chromium after: the focus is on the button in both cases at both widths,
and the page does not scroll. Sighted readers see the focus ring stay on
the button. Presentation only: no route, gate, value handling, server
text or CSS changed.

**An answer that comes after a redraw (2026-10-15).** The agent page is
drawn again from nothing when a read brings a changed answer: the agent
did more, or the protection service stopped. That can happen while a
reveal is on its way. Until 2026-10-15 the answer then went to the box the
redraw had replaced: the value or the refusal showed nowhere, and
`focusBack` could not give the focus to a button no longer on the page,
so it stayed on `<body>`. CI job 16259 hit this in
`tests/stack/reveal-focus.test.ts` F3: the boot's last read came after
the test stopped the arbiter, and the page said *Not connected*. Now each
reveal button registers its box (`home.js REVEALS`): a key and an
`answered` that draws an answer in that box. The key is the secret's ref
and its names, or a finding's event and index. `revealAnswered` sends an
answer to:

- **The box pressed**, while it is on the page, as before.
- **Else the same box drawn now.** That is the box with the same key, at
  the pressed one's rank among them, in the same session and not hidden.
  It gets the value or the refusal's words, and the focus under
  `focusBack`'s rules. A value goes only to a box of its own ref, never to
  another secret's card that took its place. A box drawn now that asks
  for itself (pressed again) or already shows its value keeps its own
  answer, and the first answer moves nothing.
- **Else nowhere.** With no such box (the page says *Not connected*, or
  the session is left), nothing is drawn, not even off the page. A focus
  that fell goes to the section's heading while it is shown, else to the
  page's (`focusHeading`, shared with `pollRefocus`).

A redraw still does not put back a value already shown. *Show the real
value* asks again only on a click (*The poll keeps your place*), and this
answers the click that was made. The button drawn now stays live while
the answer is on its way: a reveal only reads, so a second press asks
again, harmlessly. Presentation only: no route, gate or server text
changed. The value goes only into a box the page draws for that same
secret of that same session, signed in.

Tests:

- jsdom `home-js-reveal-focus.test.ts` (`press` drops the focus of the
  button turned off, as Chromium does). It covers a Your secrets card and
  a step, a refusal and then a retry, a focus moved meanwhile, a press
  without the focus, *Hide it again*, and the prompt filter's button
  shown and refused. On the old page 3 of the 4 tests fail; the other is
  the guard for a focus the person moved.
- Stack `tests/stack/reveal-focus.test.ts` (`secrets`): a real arbiter with
  `.env` at `no-model`, the real anthropic-proxy on its production client
  with one session that reads it, and a real dashboard serving the page
  signed in. Enter on the card's button shows the file's value with the
  focus back on *Hide it again: The file …/.env*. With the arbiter
  stopped, the next Enter is refused, and the focus is back on the button,
  described by the refusal. Signed out there is no button and no value,
  and the value never reached the model. It fails on the old page. Since
  2026-10-15 it lets the page's boot reads end before it stops the
  arbiter, so no read draws *Not connected* under F3.
- jsdom `home-js-reveal-redraw.test.ts` (the reveal answers held, the
  page read again with the agent's next turn). It covers:

  - a card and a step showing the value after a redraw, and a refusal
    there;
  - two cards drawn in the other order, also with headings that read
    alike (A's value only in A's card);
  - the same secret on two steps (the one pressed), and another session
    opened meanwhile (nothing on its page);
  - *Not connected* with a value and with a refusal (nothing drawn, the
    page's heading focused);
  - a focus moved meanwhile, a press without the focus, and a box pressed
    again;
  - the prompt filter's button, shown and refused.

  All 7 tests fail on the old page.
- Stack `tests/stack/reveal-redraw.test.ts` (`secrets`), wired as
  `reveal-focus`, the real answer held in the page. R1: the agent does
  one more turn through the real proxy and the page's read draws the card
  again, then the file's value shows in the card drawn now, with the focus
  on *Hide it again*. R2: the arbiter stops and the page says *Not
  connected*, then the value that comes is drawn nowhere and the page's
  heading has the focus. The value never reached the model. It fails on
  the old page.

**Your secrets** (`view-model/secret-story.ts` → `AgentPageVM.secrets`;
home.js `renderAgentSecrets`, the `#agent-secrets-block` above "What
happened"; 2026-10-05). A first-time reader of a Secrets-mode session could
not tell which secrets came up or where they went: a bound send folded into
"Plus N routine checks", and the tiles counted secrets without naming them.
The block lists each secret the session's lineage recorded (`isSecretFlow`,
model-authored tokens left out; 12 at most, then a count), named by what it
stands for, never by its token, hash or value: "The environment variable
`GITHUB_TOKEN`", "`PASTE_KEY` in `~/app/.env`", "The file …", "Output of
a `Bash` step whose command named your secret file `./.env`" (§4.25b
*Your secrets says why too*), with
its level in the Rules page's terms (`rule-words.ts` `TERMS`). A file under
the person's home folder reads `~/…` (2026-10-05: the first-session tour's
screenshots had to be redacted, since "The file
/home/<account>/mandu-try/deploy/staging.conf" spelled out the account
name): the route passes its home folder, the one the Rules page's file
browser calls `~` (`os.homedir()`, the server's `fileBrowserHome` test
seam; `HomeDeps.home`), to `pageSecrets`, and `secretWhat` shortens with
`file-browser.ts` `tildePath`. Any other path stays as recorded, another
account's home folder included, so `~` never names the wrong folder (the
rest of the product page follows the same rule since 2026-10-07: §4.34
"`~` is the dashboard's home"). Home's
`HomeFacts` groups under the same names, so a row still counts what the page
lists. A file read's key or whole-file token with no recorded origin is
named by the read step that minted it (2026-10-19): the first-session tour
reads the registered `~/mandu-try/.env` through its twin, whose key is
already a token, so the proxy mints nothing for that Read and the token's
later uses record no origin; the card read "`STRIPE_KEY` in a file" while
the step said "Read `.env`" and Approvals named the file.
`secret-story.ts` `mintedPaths` takes the first tool step whose result held
the token (the rule of `maskCauses`); when that step is a file read
(`tool-family.ts`), the token is one it kept from the AI (`heldTokens`, not
one its call echoed), and its file can be placed as a `Read`'s path is
(`later-labels.ts` `readStepPath`: an absolute recorded origin, else the
argument's path, absolute, `~/…`, or under the session's folder), the card
reads "`STRIPE_KEY` in `~/mandu-try/.env`" ("The file `~/…`" for a whole
file). A recorded origin always wins, and a path that cannot be placed (a
relative path and no folder recorded, a path holding a token) or a token
first held by any other step keeps "in a file", so the card never names the
wrong file. Two flows of one key, one with its origin and one without, now
read the same and are one entry; Home's counts follow (the stack test
`secret-card-names-file` replays the tour's read through the real arbiter
and proxy). The agent's own words (its replies, its commands) are quotes and keep
the path as the agent wrote it, and the inspector keeps full paths. Flows that
stand for the same thing at the same level are ONE entry (2026-10-05): the
tour's `staging.conf` was masked to two tokens (the history re-send after
the label, and the re-read's stub), and the page listed "The file …
staging.conf" twice, "2 requests" and "1 request". A merged entry counts
each model request that carried any of its tokens once. Each line follows
from a recorded event:

- **The AI**: "The AI got only a placeholder, never the real value (it went
  to the AI that way in N requests)", for a `no-model` or unknown level only.
  A secret the AI read as it was before it was labelled (a dual-lanes
  `maskedLater` step whose tokens are the entry's) never claims that: "The
  AI read its real value at `<time>`, before it was marked a secret. From
  `<time>` on it got a placeholder in its place, in N requests." (amber;
  2026-10-05, the tour's `deploy/staging.conf`, which the page said had never
  reached the AI). When later requests carried it (N > 0), a second amber
  line follows: "Anything the AI wrote from its real value went back to the
  AI as written with each later request: Mandu does not mask the AI's own
  words." (2026-10-06). The first line used to end "it got only a
  placeholder", which reads as if the label took the value back from the AI.
  It did not: the proxies forward the AI's own replies as written
  (confidentiality.md §7.1, the residual), and the tour's 10:41 reply had
  quoted the file's host and the start of its token, so every later request
  carried them beside the placeholder. The line says only what the proxies
  do, never whether this reply quoted the value, which the page does not
  check. `tests/stack/early-read-own-words.test.ts` replays the tour through
  the real arbiter, policy tool and anthropic-proxy: the reply quoting the
  file goes on as written, and the real page's card says these two lines.
  A level that lets a model read it says so instead (`any-model`: "Its level
  lets the AI read it"; `local-model`: only your own model). If the leak
  check fired anywhere in the session (full or believed view-model), every
  entry says the page cannot say what the AI saw, and no entry claims a
  placeholder. Off says Mandu did not mask it.
- **Where the real value went**: the net-proxy's `forwarded` events whose
  `resolved` named the secret (lineage `egress` edges to `snk:net:<host>`):
  "Mandu sent its real value only to `api.github.com` (1 request), where it
  was allowed to go" (in the past: *A send claims no standing permission*
  below). "only" is said when no other release was recorded (an
  egress-queue approval, a non-reply `desymbolize`, each its own line); with
  none at all, "Mandu did not fill in its real value for any request off this
  machine" (not in Off).
- **What Mandu stopped**: each `blocked` send that withheld it, by host
  ("The request never left this machine", the net-proxy's 403 path), egress
  refusals, the OS gates that stopped a call that used it, and the steps
  still waiting for an OK. A block or a stopped action that filed an
  Approvals row says so ("…, and asked for your OK in Approvals", *A block
  says Mandu asked you* below).
- **Where you saw it**: a reply-filter `desymbolize` that resolved it ("You
  saw its real value in the agent's reply. The AI kept the placeholder.").

**In the order it happened** (2026-10-05). The tour's `STRIPE_KEY` card
read "Mandu sent its real value only to `api.stripe.com` (1 request), where
it is allowed to go" (the words of then; *A send claims no standing
permission* below) above "Mandu blocked 1 attempt to send it to
`api.stripe.com`": the same host allowed and blocked, the send first, and
neither said when. The record says the block came first (10:38, no rule let
it go there) and the send a minute later, after the person allowed it once.
Now the send line and each block line say when, from the events that prove
their lineage edges, as a `time` part the page draws as the viewer's clock:
"(1 request, at 10:39)", "…to `api.stripe.com`, at 10:38. The request never
left this machine."; for more than one, "the first at" ("None of them left
this machine" after N attempts). The send line and the block lines run in
time order (a tie keeps the send first). Without a send, the block lines
keep their place after "did not fill in", in time order among themselves.
A time the record does not hold (an event missing, a time that cannot be
read) is not said, and then the lines keep their old order: no order and no
"first" is guessed. Counts and claims are unchanged. Why the 10:39 send went
(the person's OK) is not said: the forwarded event records no rule or ask,
and the session route has no answered asks.

**A block says Mandu asked you** (2026-10-06). The tour's `STRIPE_KEY` card
read "Mandu blocked 1 attempt to send it to `api.stripe.com`, at 10:38. The
request never left this machine." and then "Mandu sent its real value only
to `api.stripe.com` (1 request, at 10:39), where it is allowed to go". A
first-time reader saw the same host blocked and then allowed a minute
later, with nothing between. The 10:38 step under *What happened* already
said "Mandu asked for your OK in Approvals." (*A stop says Mandu asked
you*), and the block's `net_action` records the row (`policy.approvalId`,
`egr-1`), but the card, the per-secret summary, left it out. Now:

- **The words.** A block line whose blocks filed a row reads "Mandu blocked
  1 attempt to send it to `api.stripe.com`, at 10:38, and asked for your OK
  in Approvals. The request never left this machine." When only some of a
  host's blocks filed one: "…, the first at 10:01, and asked for your OK in
  Approvals for 2 of them. None of them left this machine." The stopped
  actions line does the same ("Mandu stopped 1 action that used it, and
  asked for your OK in Approvals.").
- **Which row.** Each lineage edge's own evidence event (`eventId`: the
  net-proxy's `net_action`, or the OS gate's event), read by the trace's
  rule (dual-lanes `askIdOf`: a stopped check, an id of the queue's shape).
  The link is the earliest such row, by its event's time; when no time can
  be read, the first recorded. A send's event is never read for an ask. The
  card reads only the believed events, so a claimed block is no line and no
  ask.
- **The link.** "Approvals" is a `text` part carrying `ask`
  (`StoryPart.ask`); home.js `sentenceNode` draws it as the step's link
  (`askRowLink`, `/approvals/<id>`, `data-page-link`), which opens the
  Approvals page at that row. A renderer that does not know `ask` still
  draws the word. The id is data in an attribute, never markup.
- **Not said:** that you answered, how, or that the 10:39 send went out on
  that answer. The card says only that Mandu asked, in the past.

**A send claims no standing permission** (2026-10-06). The tour's 10:39
send to `api.stripe.com` went out after the person allowed the 10:38 ask
once ("I allowed it once on the dashboard"), yet the card said "Mandu sent
its real value only to `api.stripe.com` (1 request, at 10:39), where it is
allowed to go". In the present tense that is a permission that still holds,
and the one-time OK left none: the next send there would be blocked and
asked again. A secret leaves only at a destination a rule binds it to or
with the person's OK (the egress gate, confidentiality.md §3.2), and the
send's `forwarded` event records neither which one nor whether the OK was
for one request. So the line now says "…, where it was allowed to go", in the
past: it is true of both, and it claims neither. It names no OK either,
since the card never says that you answered (*A block says Mandu asked you*).
The same pass makes one request read as one. The turn's banner used to say
"1 request left this machine with your secret `STRIPE_KEY` filled in, each
to a destination allowed to receive it." It now says "…filled in, to a
destination allowed to receive it." ("each" stays for two or more, see
*The summary names the secrets*). The title of the sends tile on the page,
and of the sends fact on Home, says "It went to a destination allowed to
receive it." over a count of one ("Each went …" over more). Counts, tones,
order and links are unchanged. Tests: `secret-story.test.ts` (the tour's
once-allowed send and a send under a binding alone: past tense, never "is
allowed", no OK), `agent-page.test.ts`, `leaves-machine.test.ts` and
`home-js-agent.test.ts` (one and many), `home-js-home.test.ts` (Home's one),
and `session-page-record.test.ts` (the served tour: the card line, the 10:39
turn's banner, the tile's title).

**A time opens its step** (2026-10-06). The page tells a session twice:
*Your secrets*, one card per secret, and *What happened*, the steps turn by
turn. The cards say when ("…to `api.stripe.com`, at 10:38, and asked for
your OK…", "(1 request, at 10:39)", "The AI read its real value at 10:41"),
but a first-time reader who wanted to check a line against the step that
proves it had to scroll a long page and match clock times by eye (at
1280px the tour's 10:38 block is 1,380px below its card line, its 10:41
Read 2,850px, on a 4,600px page). Now:

- **Which step.** A card time carries the id of the page's step that shows
  the same moment (`StoryPart.step`, a turn step's `id`): for the send line
  and each host's block line, the step of the line's own evidence event, the
  one its time comes from (the first send; each host's first block, a tie
  keeping the first recorded), by the trace's rule (dual-lanes
  `stepIdOfEvent`: `tool:<call id>` when the event names a call the page
  shows, else `os:<event id>`; `locateAsk` finds an answer's step by the
  same rule); for the read before the label, that read's own step (the
  dual-lanes `maskedLater` step of the first such read).
- **Only a step the page draws.** `buildAgentPage` passes the ids of its
  shown turns' action steps (the ones drawn with `data-step-id`) to
  `pageSecrets`; a moment no such step holds stays plain: "From 10:42 on"
  (a model request, not a step), a turn past the turn cap, a step past the
  per-turn cap, an event not in the record. Home passes no steps, so its
  facts and words are unchanged.
- **The link.** home.js `sentenceNode` draws such a time as a button
  (`.step-link`, the `<time>` inside, "Show this step under What
  happened"): it moves the page rather than going anywhere. A click
  (`showStep`) finds the step by value (ids are data, never spliced into a
  selector), opens the fold that hides it as its own button would, marks
  it with the accent bar (`.step.shown`, the bar only, so a blocked step
  keeps its colour; one mark at a time), gives it the keyboard focus and
  scrolls it to the middle. A step not on the page does nothing.
- **Unchanged:** the words, the counts, the order, and what the page shows.
  A step id is a page id, never a token or a value.

**The tag agrees with the card** (2026-10-06). Each card's head carries
the secret's level as a tag, in the Rules page's terms ("Secret, hidden
from the AI"). It was always green (`.tag.secret`). On the tour's
`deploy/staging.conf` card, the green "Secret, hidden from the AI" sat right
above the amber "The AI read its real value at 10:41, before it was marked
a secret.". A first-time reader got the most visible claim on the card
backwards: the tag gives the label, and the line under it gives what the AI
got. The same held under Off ("Protection was off, so Mandu did not mask
it.") and in a session whose leak check fired. Now:

- **The answer.** Each `StorySecret` carries `saw`, its first line's answer
  (`aiSaw`: `masked`, `readable`, `own-model`, `early`, `off`, `flagged`).
  The tiles count by the same answer, so the tag, the first line and the
  tiles cannot disagree.
- **The colour.** home.js `secretLevelTag` draws the tag (`.tag.level`).
  It is green (`secret`) only where the level held: `masked`, or a level
  that lets a model read it, which its line says. It is amber (`raw`, as
  the step's "Masked only later") for a read before the label and for Off,
  and red (`unmasked`) for a fired leak check. An answer the page does not
  know (none sent, or an unknown word) draws the tag neutral, never green.
- **Since when.** An `early` card also carries `since`, the moment its
  first line says the AI got a placeholder from (`ReadBeforeLabel.maskedTs`,
  the first request that carried it masked). The tag reads "Secret, hidden
  from the AI since 10:42", drawn as a `<time>` in the viewer's clock. It
  is not a link: a model request is not a step (*A time opens its step*).
  No other card has `since`.
- **Unchanged:** the level's words, every line, the counts, and Home. The
  tag still names the level. It only stops looking safe above a line that
  says the level did not hold.

The claims read only the BELIEVED events (`believedVm`, the route's
`scopeVm`; arbiter-human-plane.md §10.2): a claimed block never becomes a
"blocked" line. Under the list, the limits, always: Mandu protects only the
secrets you registered and the files you labeled; in Secrets mode, it does not
stop prompt injection (protection-modes.md); in Off, it only watched. With no
secret recorded the block says so in one line.

**Tests.** `agent-page.test.ts` (sentences, the outcome ladder, `osSentence`,
one-level reveal with a nested secret and an unknown token, `revealValues`
asking for neither, a secret result shipping no text, the title fallback,

Your secrets: `secret-story.test.ts` (names, each line by its event, "only",

A time opens its step: `secret-story.test.ts` (the send's and each block's

The tag agrees with the card: `secret-story.test.ts` (each answer's `saw`;
