#### 4.25c Rules page: every button acts in place

**Design.** A row is what the rule covers, ONE effect, and a ⋯; nothing on
the Rules page opens `/dev/`. Why: a product page that sends people to the
expert editor for most edits, or whose Remove silently fails, is not one.

**2026-10-05: one effect per row, the rest under ⋯** ("Your rules" was hard
to follow: a fourth column of counts, two buttons and links on every row).
A row (`ruleRow`) shows the subject, its reach under it, and the effect: a
menu (`effect-select`, the effect in force and the one it can turn into,
*Always allowed* / *Always blocked*) where the rule has a flip, else the
effect in words. The ⋯ (`file-more`) opens `ruleDetail` under the row: the
answer's when-and-where line (§4.25h), the origin line (§4.25i), the use
count or "Your answer, asked N times", where it is kept, Show in policy.yaml
(§4.25g), Show in the file browser, and **Remove** (or "Set in the rules
file"). A failed flip shows the server's words on the row and the menu goes
back to the effect in force. The bullets below stand, with "a button" read as
the menu or the ⋯'s Remove.

**2026-10-08: the subject's chip fits it.** The subject is a `code` chip at
the top of `.rule-text`, a flex column, and a flex column stretches its
items. So until this date every host in *Sending data* and *Programs and
connections* was a grey bar across the column (504px for `pypi.org:443` at
1280px), like an empty field to type in, unlike the file rows above it. Now
the chip keeps its own width (`.rule-text code { align-self: flex-start }`),
and a long host still breaks inside it (`overflow-wrap: anywhere`; a flex
item that does not stretch is held to the column's width). The reach line
and a warning under it still span the column.

- **Grouped by the question a person asks**, not by where a rule is stored:
  *Sending data* (send rules and past send answers), *Trusted sources*,
  *Programs and connections* (connection allowances, a built-in ask set to
  block, past run answers), and *Your answers about files* (file rules live in
  the explorer, §4.25n). Empty groups are hidden. Each group's heading says in
  a few words what it decides (§4.25e).
- **Remove on every row that has an edit op.** The browser posts `POST
  /api/policy/rules/change {id, action}` naming the ROW and the action, never
  an edit; the server plans the edit from the raw policy in force
  (`src/rule-actions.ts`): lock → `unlock-path`, trusted source →
  `distrust-origin`, send rule → `retire-rule`, connection →
  `remove-connect`, blocked built-in → `set-disposition ask`. Row ids are the
  compiled ones (`~` expanded, host lower-cased, default port), and a rule
  that is gone comes back as a refusal, never a 200.
- **One flip where a rule has two states**: *Allow instead* / *Block instead*
  on a send rule (`release` with the same id, ends and expiry) and on a past
  answer (the verdict route).
- **Friction follows direction.** The server previews the edit. A change that
  only tightens applies at once; one that loosens answers `{applied:false,
  confirm:true, expected}`, the page asks ("… makes protection weaker for X.
  Continue?") and re-posts with `expected`. The apply is `applyAsHuman`
  (propose on the admin channel, approve at once as `human:rules-page`, refuse
  with nothing written if the policy moved and the change now loosens more
  than was confirmed).
- **Undo.** Every applied change shows a notice ("Rule removed." / "Now
  always allowed." / "Now always blocked.") with Undo (`POST
  /api/policy/changes/<id>/undo`).
- **Remove on a past answer forgets it**: `POST
  /api/egress/approvals/<id>/forget` → the admin-only arbiter op
  `forgetEgressApproval` deletes the verdict so the same send is asked again.
  It never loosens (allow → ask, block → ask), so there is no confirmation; a
  pending ask cannot be forgotten (409).
- **What cannot be edited here says so.** A per-program output rule (`apps:`)
  shows "Set in policy.yaml" and no button; that form is deprecated
  (confidentiality-plan-13 D3), so the row says the output is masked and names
  the reader-entry form `readers: [{ app, output }]`. A trusted source or
  connection reached through a named list or a category default is refused
  with that sentence instead of a no-op.
- **No YAML editing on the product page.** The rules file stays the expert
  surface; a row can only SHOW its own lines, read-only (§4.25g).

**Tests.** `rule-actions.test.ts` (the planner per row kind and its
refusals, the two routes over a real `DashboardServer` with a fake arbiter);
`home-js-rules.test.ts` (groups, no `/dev/` link, confirm → `expected` →
Undo, a declined confirmation sends nothing, a refusal on the row, forget;
the subject chip's width with the page's own styles applied, and the
`app.css` contract);
arbiter `egress-approvals.test.ts` (forget: resolved only, persisted, asks
again) and the admin-channel catalog test; `tests/stack/dashboard-rules-page.test.ts`
presses every button by the SERVED row id over a real ArbiterServer and the
production adapter (parity for `forgetEgressApproval`); `tests/stack/rules-chip-fit.test.ts`
renders the SERVED Rules page with its served styles over a real arbiter's
send rules and connections, and checks each host's chip keeps its own width
(the no-value/no-token oracle on the page).

#### 4.25d Rules page: one vocabulary, explained on the page

**Design.** A fixed set of terms, one meaning each, listed on the page under
*What the words mean* (a closed `<details>`), and every row built only from
them (`src/view-model/rule-words.ts`, `TERMS` + `GLOSSARY`). Why: the page had
said the same thing several ways and explained none of them.

| Term | Meaning shown |
|---|---|
| Masked | Before the AI saw it, Mandu replaced the real text with a short code that stands for it. You still see the real text. |
| No AI | Every AI sees it masked, Mandu's helper included, and your OK does not change that. Only the programs allowed to open it get the real file: ssh, and programs you name, never a database shell. It is sent only where a rule or your OK allows. |
| Your own AI only | §4.25l. |
| Any AI, when it asks | The AI first sees it masked. When it needs the contents, Mandu's helper reads them for it, or the AI reads them itself. Each read is logged, and your AI provider gets what is read. It is sent only where a rule or your OK allows. |
| Not secret | Treated like any other file, even if it looks like a secret. |
| Trusted source | What comes from it reaches the AI unmasked. |
| Always allowed | Happens without asking you. |
| Always blocked | Stopped without asking you. |
| Needs your OK | The default: Mandu pauses and asks you first. One exception: a key whose shape names the company that issued it, such as a Stripe or GitHub key, goes to that company's own API without asking (issuer_bindings in policy.yaml turns this off). |
| Your answer | §4.25e. |

"Needs your OK" is the phrase Home and Approvals use for an ask, so the
default has one name across the product.

**Two questions per secret (2026-10-11).** The three secret levels were
"Secret, hidden from the AI", "Secret, your own model only" and "Secret,
the AI may read it" (menu: Hidden from the AI, Your own model only, The AI
may read it). Checked against the policy lattice (confidentiality plan 13
§4.2: a label is `Release(d) = Models(level) ∪ Bindings ∪ {human, local
storage}`), each name answered only the model half and misstated it:
"hidden" read as absolute although the AI sees the file and its shape;
"the AI may read it" hid that an `any-model` file starts as a placeholder,
is read only when the AI asks (the quarantined helper, or a logged
in-context read) and then reaches the AI provider; "programs you allow"
hid that only `ssh` and `ssh-add` are vetted and a database shell is never
a reader. The terms are now **Secret, no AI**, **Secret, your own AI
only** and **Secret, any AI when it asks** (menu: No AI, Your own AI only,
Any AI, when it asks), one noun ("AI"; "model" stays in Settings ›
Models), each meaning saying that no approval widens the model half, and
Masked says "a short code that stands for it" ("label" means the rule, and "placeholder" stays retired, §4.25u). Since 2026-10-11 the
glossary, the tooltips and every summary use the menu names themselves
(§4.25ab): "Secret, no AI" and its two siblings are gone. Sentences: "Make `x` a
secret no AI may read / only your own AI may read / any AI may read when it
asks" (arbiter `policy-model.ts`, `policy-suggestions.ts`, the dashboard's
`policy-proposals.ts`, `mandu why`, which also stopped calling a
`local-model` file hidden). The destination half keeps "may be sent to
<host>" and the closing "only where a rule or your OK allows" (below). The
two-menu row, one menu per half, is the follow-up.

**A send is never promised an OK that a rule skips (2026-10-07).** Each
secret level used to end "It is not sent anywhere without your OK.", and so
did Settings › Protection ("Keys, tokens and secret files are not sent
anywhere without your OK."), the built-in list ("Secret files are not sent
anywhere without your OK.") and `mandu why` (`launcher/src/why.ts`, which
uses this glossary's words). The first-run card said they "cannot leave
this computer unless you allow it". But a rule sends a secret's real value
with no question asked: a file's "may be sent to" host (the row on this
same page reads "Secret, the AI may read it, may be sent to
`api.example.com`"), an Always-allow, or a row an administrator locked. The
session pages show those sends. Home's sentence and the inspector's 🛡 card
stopped promising this on 2026-10-05 (§4.25 *The verdict ladder*, §4.16).
Now every one of these says "only where a rule or your OK allows", Home's
words: the levels "It is sent only where a rule or your OK allows.", the
switch and the built-ins "Keys, tokens and secret files leave this machine
only where …" / "Keys and secret files leave this machine only where …",
the first-run card "they leave this computer only where …". Before the
setting is read, the switch row's first paint says "Checking…", as Home's
headline does, instead of the on sentence (a flash of about 100 ms, even
when protection is off). Copy only: no route, rule or decision changed.
Tests: `policy-panel.test.ts` (each level's meaning names a rule, beside a
bound row's words), `home-view-model.test.ts` (the built-ins and the
first-run card, Secrets and Full), `home-js-settings.test.ts` (the first
paint, the on row), and `protection-running.test.ts` (the served page over a
real `DashboardServer` with a bound file: Settings, Rules' host chip, the
glossary and the built-ins, Home's first-run card; no old promise anywhere
on the rendered pages).

The inspector and the gated posture followed the same day. The inspector at
`/dev/` said a file the AI may read "can't leave": its Secrets level line
("Your keys and credentials cannot leave."), the *Usable secrets* matrix row,
the prepared-workspace label chips (`dev/js/drills.js`, above a line that
reads "may be sent to: example.com"), and *Your rules* (`policy-panel.ts`
`LEVEL_EFFECT`), whose row for a bound file read "the AI may read it — it
can't leave · may go to api.example.com". The `gated` posture sentence
(`session-health.ts` and its launcher twin `confinement-posture.ts`, shown
on the inspector's session card and by `mandu doctor`) said "nothing is sent
out without your OK". Now they say "leave this machine only where a rule or
your OK allows" (the level line), "sent only where a rule or your OK allows"
(the matrix row, the chips, the rule rows and their *What it does*) and "a
secret is sent out only where a rule or your OK allows" (the posture). The
frozen Full verdict ("… and nothing left your machine without your OK")
reads "… and keys and secret files left this machine only where a rule or
your OK allowed."; injection's, which guards no secret, ends at the masking
fact. Copy only. Tests: `policy-panel.test.ts` (the bound rows and their
detail), `drills-js.test.ts`, `protection-js.test.ts`,
`protection-js-level.test.ts`, `session-health.test.ts` and the launcher's
`confinement-posture.test.ts` (the posture, both twins),
`home-view-model.test.ts` (the frozen verdicts), and over a real
`DashboardServer` `protection-running.test.ts` (`/api/policy/panel` and the
served `/dev/` scripts) and `secrets-posture.test.ts` (a gated launch built
by the launcher's own event, through `/api/sessions`). Still to word the same
way, with the release wording: `mandu mode`'s summaries
(`launcher/src/mode.ts`, `launcher/src/config.ts`) and the modes table in
`docs/usage.md`, which still say keys "cannot leave".

Home's `waiting` sentence was the last product line to promise it: while any
question waited it said "Nothing leaves your machine until you answer.", and
a rule sends meanwhile. It now says only that what each question asks for
happens only if you allow it (§4.25, *The verdict ladder*, 2026-10-07).

- Each `yourRules` row carries `plain {subject, reach, effect}` built from the
  terms (the inspector keeps its own `effect`/`detail`): "`~/work/.env` this
  file only · Secret, hidden from the AI[, may be sent to <host>]"; a send rule
  "`api.example.com` sending any masked data from X · Always allowed / Always
  blocked / Only counted, still needs your OK / Expired / Turned off"; a
  trusted source "`pypi.org` a website · Trusted source, reaches the AI
  unmasked"; a connection "Always allowed, from the agent's next start"; a
  blocked built-in by its words, "Always blocked, instead of asking you".
- The secrets switch and the built-in sentence read the same, "Keys and
  secret files leave this computer only where a rule or your OK allows."
  (§4.25 *The on/off says what runs*, §4.25z).
- The Approvals / Describe grammar (`policy-proposals.ts` `editRow`) uses the
  same terms ("Make `/x` a secret hidden from the AI", "Always allow sending
  masked data from `a` to `b`", …).

**Tests.** `policy-panel.test.ts` pins every row kind's words, that each
effect starts with a term, sweeps them for inspector words, and pins the
page's glossary and the label buttons to `GLOSSARY`;
`policy-proposals-view-model.test.ts` and `policy-assistant.test.ts` the
grammar; `home-js-rules.test.ts` the rendered row and confirmation.

#### 4.25e Rules page: each group says what it decides; an answer names its data

**Design.**

- **Each group says what it decides** in a line under its title (`home.js`
  `RULE_GROUPS[].about`). *Sending data*: where data may go; the default is to
  ask; a rule covers any masked data (from one source or anywhere), an answer
  only the one piece you were asked about.
- **An answer names its data.** A verdict is keyed symbol × destination, so it
  covers ONE piece of data going to that host; a row reading "`host` · Always
  allowed" would overstate it. Several placeholders of one registered file
  in one request (a `.env`'s keys, a personal document's lines) are one card
  keyed on the file's base symbol (egress-hold.md "One card per file",
  2026-10-19): its `source` is the file, so the card reads "wants to send a
  secret from `~/…/statement-2026-09.md`" and the answer "sending only the
  file …", and the answer covers that file's values at that host. A lone
  placeholder keeps its own card, named by its key. The arbiter attaches `source {tool, origin}`
  (the symbol table's provenance columns) to every approval at READ time
  (`withProvenance`, on the `egressApprovals` op and the snapshot's
  `verdicts`); nothing is persisted, and it is provenance, never the value.
  `rule-words.ts answerWords` reads "`notes-sink.test` sending only the file
  …/ws/notes.md", "sending only what was fetched from httpbin.org/get",
  "sending only the output of "cat x"", or, with no source, "sending only the
  data you were asked about". Long paths keep their last three parts, the full
  target in the tooltip. The file, the address and the command are drawn as
  code (2026-10-16, §4.25u *Rules names what a send covers*).
- **Send rules say "any"** ("sending any masked data [from X]"), so a rule and
  an answer read as the contrast they are.
- **The term *Your answer***: "Your choice when Mandu asked and you picked
  always. For sending, it covers only the data you were asked about, going to
  that one place. Other data sent there still needs your OK."

**Tests.** `arbiter/test/unit/user-rules-gate.test.ts` (the read-time `source`
on the op and the snapshot, and that the value never appears);
`policy-panel.test.ts` (every answer shape; two answers to one host read
differently); `home-js-rules.test.ts`; `tests/stack/dashboard-rules-page.test.ts`
(the served row over the real arbiter and production adapter).

#### 4.25f Rules page: Files and folders as a tree

**Design (`home.js` `fileTree` / `renderFileTree`).** The Labeled view of the
file explorer (§4.25n) lays the person's file rules out by path, labels
relative to the node above, full path in the tooltip, so rules under one
workspace do not repeat it and an override sits under the rule it overrides.

- **Inside a folder rule.** A literal rule covering a folder "and everything
  inside" holds the rules on paths inside it as children. That nesting is the
  enforced truth: among literal labels the longest segment-prefix wins
  (`arbiter/policy/path-labels.ts`).
- **Under a shared folder.** Rules under a folder no rule names are grouped
  under a folding heading where two or more branches meet; single-branch
  folders are skipped, and `~`, `/`, `**` are never headings.
- **Patterns are never parents.** A `**` pattern has an empty literal prefix,
  so between two such patterns a tie goes to the STRICTER level, not the
  deeper one. Patterns are listed first and share headings as siblings; a
  trailing `/**` places a pattern on its folder's node.
- The server marks each file rule's reach as `covers: subtree | exact |
  pattern` (`YourRuleRowVM.covers`) so the page never parses its own wording.

**A rule on a file reads as a file (2026-10-11).** A `paths:` entry with no
`recursive:` key reaches everything inside its path, folder or not
(`compiled-policy.ts`), and *Keys Mandu found*'s Save writes exactly that on
a file (the arbiter's suggestion edit carries no `recursive`), as does a
hand-written rule or a label made with the inspector's *Lock it*. Until
2026-10-11 the page drew every such rule as a folder: "deploy/staging.conf
and everything inside" with a folder icon, an opened row saying "Your rule,
and everything inside" and "A folder label covers everything inside it,
except files with a rule of their own", *Changes to save* adding ", and
everything inside" to a change made to it, and *Who may get your secrets*
(§4.25aa) listing "~/proj/deploy/staging.conf and everything inside". A file
has nothing inside, so the words were wrong, and the first rules a new user
saves from the scan all read that way.

- **The server looks at the disk** (`server/path-kinds.ts filePaths`): for
  each literal, absolute path a rule reaches everything inside, an async
  `stat` (following a link, as the guard judges an open) says whether it is
  there and is not a folder. `loadPolicyPanel`, `loadByWho` and
  `getSecrets` pass that set to their pure projections. Display only, and
  bounded: a path that is missing, unreadable, a pattern, or not answered
  within 500 ms (a hung mount) keeps the words the rule says.
- **The projections word it as that file.** `policy-panel.ts` gives such a
  row `pathIsFile: true`, `plain.reach` "this file only" and a detail line
  without "and everything under it"; `rules-by-who.ts` lists it with no
  reach, as a one-file rule; `secrets.ts` marks such a label
  `pathIsFile: true`.
- **The page draws it as that file** (`home.js ruleShape`): the file icon,
  the opened row's "Your rule, this file only" with no folder note, a label
  made elsewhere reading "this file only" (`labelReach`), and a change
  waiting in *Changes to save* without ", and everything inside".
- **The rule is unchanged.** `covers` stays `subtree`: it is what the rule
  reaches, and the page's edits read it, so a level or hosts change made on
  the row is saved with the entry's reach as written (no `recursive:
  false`, so nothing is narrowed and no "weaker" question is asked), and the
  tree still nests a rule under it if one names a path inside. A file later
  replaced by a folder reads as a folder at the next read.
- **The weaker-change question asks about it as that file (2026-10-13).**
  Until then the question before a weaker Save (§4.25m *Saving*) said of
  such a rule "Becomes Any AI, when it asks, which lets more reach an AI or
  leave this computer than now. This covers everything inside it that has
  no rule of its own." (`looseningWords`), and of an older rule kept in the
  page's own store ", and so does everything inside it that has no rule of
  its own", though its row in *Changes to save*, just above, already said a
  change to the file: the commonest weaker change a new user makes (a key
  saved from the scan, later let reach an AI) read so. Now `POST
  /api/files/labels`, only in the answer that ASKS (nothing applied), looks
  up which of the changed paths are files (`filePaths`, the same bounded
  look as the read routes; a link counts as what it points to) and words
  each as that file: `looseningWords(r, edits, home, files)` leaves the
  inside sentence out, and `pageLooseningWords` takes the page-store
  loosening's `fileDetail` ("Becomes Any AI, when it asks."). A folder, a
  pattern, and a path the look did not answer keep their words. Words
  only: every loosening is still listed and confirmed by the same keys,
  the impact list is unchanged, and what is saved is the same (the rule
  keeps its reach).

- **The inspector's Labels table says it too (2026-10-13).** Rules ›
  Secrets › Labels (`dev/js/secrets.js scopeCell`) painted every label's
  raw scope, so a label on a file read "subtree", a folder's word, whether
  it came from policy.yaml, *Keys Mandu found* or the inspector's own form
  ("Apply to the whole subtree", ticked by default). Now a label the server
  marks `pathIsFile` reads "this file only", the product page's words, with
  a tooltip saying it is written as a whole-subtree label on a file. A
  folder's label keeps "subtree", a this-path-only label "exact", a pattern
  "pattern · matches + below" or "pattern · matches only", and a path the
  look did not answer the word its label says. Words only: no route, field
  or label changed.

**The tree is as long as its rules (2026-10-14).** The tree (`#files-tree`)
wore `files-list`, the file browser's class, from the days the two shared
one explorer box (§4.25n): `max-height: min(60vh, 560px); overflow-y: auto`.
Since §4.25p it is a list of its own in *Your rules*, beside *Sending data*
(`#rules-list`, never capped), so a person's own rules sat in a box inside
the page. A headless Chromium over a real arbiter holding six file rules and
two sending rules measured, on the page signed in: at 390×844 a 504px box
over 1654px of rules, one row whole, one cut, four hidden; at 1280×800 four
whole, one cut, one hidden; at 1920×1080 the last row cut. The scrollbar took
no room, so only a row cut at the box's edge said there were more, and on a
phone a swipe on the list scrolled the box, not the page. Now the tree has
no class of the browser's: it is as long as its rules, every row in the
page's flow, as *Sending data* is (the rounded table still clips at its
corners, `.table`). The lists that hold what a folder or a scan holds keep
their box (`.files-list`): *Add a rule*'s folder entries (`#files-list`) and
*Keys Mandu found* (`#files-suggested-list`), since a folder or a scan can
hold thousands. A long set of rules makes a long page, as *Sending data* and
*Who may get your secrets* do; the column heads above the tree
(`.files-heads`) scroll away with it. Presentation only: no route, word,
POST or rule changes.

**Tests.** `home-js-explorer.test.ts` (the whole tree for a fixture with nested
rules two deep, a shared-folder heading, a lone path and three patterns, fold
and unfold; the tree and *Sending data* have no height of their own and do
not scroll, with the page's styles applied, while a folder's entries keep
their box); the stack e2e `tests/stack/rules-tree-whole.test.ts` (a real
arbiter holding twelve file rules, the production adapter, the served page
and styles signed out and in: every rule a row of the tree, no box of its
own, the browser's box kept; the oracle); `policy-panel.test.ts` (`covers`;
a rule on a file: "this file only", `pathIsFile`, `covers` kept, the folder
and pattern unchanged, and the words the rule says when nothing was looked
at); `rules-by-who.test.ts` and
`secrets-view-model.test.ts` (the same for the card and a label);
`path-kinds.test.ts` (a file, a folder, links to each, a missing path, a
pattern, a relative path, and a hung look that answers late);
`home-js-file-rule.test.ts` (jsdom: the words and icons in the tree, the
opened row, a label made elsewhere, and a change that waits as a change to
the file and is sent with `recursive: true`); and the stack e2e
`tests/stack/file-rule-words.test.ts` (a real arbiter, the real workspace
scan with its suggestion saved, a hand-written file rule and a folder rule,
a label made through the inspector's route; the panel, by-who and secrets
answers; the served page signed out and in; a tighter level saved on the
page leaves the entry with no `recursive:` key and the arbiter still
reaching everything inside; the oracle). The question: `file-browser.test.ts`
(`looseningWords` and `pageLooseningWords` for a file, a folder, a rule on
that path only, and no look; the same keys planned),
`file-browser-routes.test.ts` (a real disk: a file, a folder, a link to a
file and its target, a page-store rule on a file and on a folder; the keys
asked and the edits saved unchanged), and the stack e2e
`tests/stack/file-rule-weaker-words.test.ts` (a real arbiter, the real scan's
suggestion saved, a label made in the inspector and a folder rule; Any AI
chosen for the three on the served page signed in; the question's words for
each; *Save anyway* applies them with the file's entry keeping no
`recursive:` key; the oracle). The inspector's table: `secrets-js.test.ts`
(jsdom over the real view-model: a whole-subtree label on a file, a folder,
a this-path-only label on a file, two patterns, and the same file with no
look answered) and the stack e2e `tests/stack/inspector-file-label-scope.test.ts`
(a real arbiter whose policy.yaml holds a rule on a file, a folder, a
`recursive: false` rule and a pattern; the served `/dev/rules` signed out
and in; a file labelled with the inspector's form; the file rule's path
replaced by a folder reads "subtree" at the next poll; the oracle).

**Find a rule (2026-10-19).** Your rules draws every rule at once, and the
card grows with use: rules come from this page, Approvals' *Always allow* and
*Block*, the agent's accepted rule changes and *Describe what you want*. The
questions people bring to it are about one thing ("what did I say about
`deploy.token`?", "which rule lets data go to `api.github.com`?", "what may
`docker-compose` open?"), and the answer is one row among dozens, perhaps
inside a folded folder. A search box, "Find a rule", sits in the card's head
between the heading and *Add a rule* (under the heading on a phone), and
typing keeps only the rows whose **drawn words** hold the text,
case-insensitive (`home.js` `ruleWords` / `ruleMatches`):

- a file or folder of the tree by its path as drawn (`~/…`, and in full, as
  its tooltip shows it), its reach, its label, its *Opens it* line and the
  hosts it may be sent to (per value, with the value's name);
- any other row (*Sending data*, *Programs and connections*, *Trusted
  sources*, *Your answers about files*) by what it covers (a host, a
  program, an address and port), its second line (the file a send covers,
  from where) and what it does.

The tree keeps the folders and folder rules on the way to each match
(`findTree`: the nesting is the truth, so a match keeps its place), drawn
open; a folder rule kept only as the way there is drawn but not counted.
Folding a folder while the box holds text changes only what is drawn, so
emptying the box gives back the person's own folds (`F.folded`). A group
with no match is not drawn, its title (and the tree's column heads) with
it. The count reads "3 of 27"; nothing found says "No rule mentions
“stripe”." with *Clear*, and, when the text looks like a path, a line
offering *Add a rule*, which opens the browser with a full path or pattern
already in its path box. Escape empties the box (an empty box leaves Escape
alone).

- **Presentation only.** No read and no server change: it narrows what the
  page already drew. It matches only the words a row draws, never the raw
  subject a row keeps for its tooltip, so a form the server holds back
  (a pattern hidden while signed out, `patternsHidden`) can never be found by
  its real text.
- **Never kept.** The text is not in the address and every page change
  (`setPage`) empties it: a filter you forgot must never make a rule look
  missing on your next visit. The page's own re-read after a change
  (`loadRules`) keeps it and applies it again, and the box is never redrawn,
  so the focus stays in it while typing.
- **Changes to save is never narrowed.** It lists every waiting change
  (`F.pending`), on a row the box hides too, and saves them all. A row the
  box hides is closed (its ⋯ goes with it).
- **A jump to a row clears a hiding text.** A file pressed under *Who may get
  your secrets* (§4.25aa, `openRuleRow`) empties the box first when it would
  hide that file's rule.

Tests: `home-js-rules-find.test.ts` (jsdom: each row kind, the `~/` form, an
*Opens it* program, a send host, a connection's port, the tree kept and
opened, a folded folder and the person's fold back, a group hidden, "N of
M", the nothing-found line with *Clear* and *Add a rule*, Escape, a re-read
after a change, *Changes to save* on a hidden row, a raw subject not found, a
page change, the jump from *Who may get your secrets*), and the stack e2e
`tests/stack/rules-find.test.ts` (a real arbiter with 27 rules, the
production adapter and the served page: a host keeps its send rule and the
two files that may go there, a program its file, a port its connection, no
request made while typing; in a real headless Chromium at 1280 and 390 px,
the box and the count fit the card, beside and under the heading; the
oracle).

#### 4.25g Rules page: "Show in policy.yaml" on each row

**Design.** A row says a rule in the page's words; the person can also see
the rules-file text behind it, to check the words against the policy or find
the entry for a hand edit.

- **"Show in policy.yaml"** on each rules-file row opens a read-only panel
  under it: "policy.yaml line N" (or "lines A to B") with the file's path,
  then the lines as on disk, numbered, the rule's lines marked and the comment
  lines directly above shown as context.
- **Rows kept elsewhere say so**: "Saved by Mandu, not in policy.yaml" (a
  page-store label) and "Saved when you answered, not in policy.yaml" (an
  answer).
- **The button names its row and keeps the focus (2026-10-11)**: "Show in
  policy.yaml: b.example", then "Hide policy.yaml: b.example"; it goes off
  while the lines are read and gets the focus back after (§4.25 *A label
  chosen in Your rules keeps the focus*).
- **The server finds the lines** (`GET /api/policy/rules/source?id=<row id>`,
  `src/rule-source.ts locateRule`) in the on-disk text from the
  `policyDocument` op. js-yaml reports no positions, and a new YAML dependency
  for one read-only view was rejected, so the file is cut by indentation into
  top-level items (with their leading comments), each parsed alone and matched
  to the row id by the compiled policy's identity. A commented-out entry never
  matches. A rule the file does not hold answers `found: false` ("from Mandu's
  built-in settings").

**Tests.** `rule-source.test.ts` (every row kind, block and flow style,
comments, `~` and trailing slash, a key holding a colon, missing and broken
entries); `home-js-rules.test.ts` (button, panel, numbering, marks, the two
"not in policy.yaml" notes); `tests/stack/dashboard-rules-page.test.ts` (every
row the real arbiter serves finds its own lines).

#### 4.25h An answer links to the moment it was asked

**Why.** A standing "Always allow" is justified by the situation it was given
in: a task the person asked for, or a page that steered the agent into
asking. Showing that moment lets the person re-examine an answer given to an
injected ask instead of guessing.

**Design.**

- **An answer row says when and where**: "You answered 2 days ago. See what
  the agent was doing" (the same words and target as Approvals), opening the
  product's agent page. With several sessions (the queue row's `sessions`,
  most recent last): "(asked in 3 sessions, this shows the latest)"; the
  latest is the one answered, since an answered row short-circuits the gate.
  A row older than session attribution says "Where it was asked was not
  recorded". Approvals' *Answered earlier* rows end their when line with the
  same link and count (2026-10-08, §4.25 Approvals, *An answer links where
  it was asked*), so an *Allowed once* answer, which Rules does not list,
  leads to its moment too.
- **The link opens the moment.** Both links carry `ask=<egr-id>`; `GET
  /api/home/agent?session=…&ask=…` looks the id up and `locateAsk`
  (agent-page.ts) finds the step:
  1. **exact:** the first event whose `policy.approvalId` is the id, mapped
     to its tool step by call id, else its own OS card. The model proxy's
     fs/exec gates and the net-proxy's blocked `net_action` stamp it on the
     event only; the agent's 403 body leaves it out (`agentWithheld`,
     policy-surface.md §9.5).
  2. **destination,** network asks only, for older records: the first STOPPED
     send to the ask's host (a blocked connection card, or a tool step whose
     gate note or result names the host as blocked/withheld), the host matched
     as a whole name; an allowed connection is not the ask.
  A file or command ask without the id is not located. Nothing found is
  reported as such (`turnId: null`), never guessed.
- **The page marks it**: a leading note ("The marked step is where Mandu
  stopped and asked you", plus "found by where the data was going" for a
  destination match), an accent bar and "Mandu asked you here" on the step,
  its fold opened, scrolled to once a visit: the poll never scrolls back to
  it, and a redraw keeps what the reader opened (2026-10-09, §4.25 *The poll
  keeps your place*). The focused turn is always in the story, even past
  `TURN_CAP`. A session past the 90-day event retention reads "Session
  not found" with that reason.
- **Attribution only.** Nothing here decides; the page shows only what the
  story already held (no new originals, no secret).

**Tests.** `agent-page.test.ts` (exact match, the destination fallback
skipping an allowed connection and a look-alike host, not found marks
nothing); `home-js-agent.test.ts`; net-proxy `egress.test.ts` +
`forward-proxy.test.ts` (the id on the event, absent from the 403 body);
`tests/stack/ask-moment-link.test.ts` (real arbiter, net-proxy in production
wiring, dashboard: block → Always allow over HTTP → the page marks the exact
step); `tests/stack/answered-ask-link.test.ts` (the same join from the served
Approvals row, at the `secrets` axes).

#### 4.25i Rules page: who put each rule there

**Why.** A rule can come from a button on this page, Describe, the agent (a
tightening it may apply alone, or a loosening you approved), or a hand edit.
The one that matters most is a rule an agent asked for: if a page talked the
agent into asking, the row should lead back to that session.

**Design.** Every change through the policy surface is kept in
`policy_changes` (policy-surface.md §8.4.2) with `via`, `requestedBy`, the
agent's `sessionKey`, and the items touched with their before/after values.

- **The arbiter names the rows.** `policyChanges` carries per change
  `proposedBy` (the requester; `requestedBy` on an approved change is the
  approver) and `rules`: each touched item as the Rules page's row ids
  (`compiled-policy.ts panelRowIds`, compiled exactly as the policy compiles
  it), whether it was `added` or `removed`, and whether it is still `current`.
- **The dashboard joins.** `GET /api/policy/rules/origins` reads the newest 500
  changes and gives, per row id, the NEWEST change that touched it
  (`ruleOrigins`). A row whose newest change removed it reads as no record.
  `complete` is false when the record holds more than was read or the arbiter
  predates `rules`; a row the answer does not name then says nothing, never
  "no record".
- **One line per rules-file row**: "Your agent asked for this and you approved
  it, 2 hours ago. See what the agent was doing" (the session's top: a rule
  request has no ask to mark); "Your agent added this. It only makes your
  rules stricter, so it did not need your OK"; "You added this on the Rules
  page" / "with Describe a rule"; "Mandu suggested this, and it was applied
  from the terminal or by your agent. It only makes your rules stricter, so
  it did not need your OK" (a scan suggestion applied on the data socket,
  which never names a person: plan 14 §14.14); "This came back when you undid a change";
  "… It was changed in policy.yaml after that." when not `current`; "No
  record of who added this."
- **Who, in one place.** `changeWho` reads a change as agent / agent with your
  OK / a scan suggestion applied on the agent's channel (`scan-applied`:
  `agent-tighten`, or an older arbiter's `tighten` by `data-plane`, with
  `proposedBy: mandu:scan`; never "you", never a session) / Rules page /
  Settings / Describe / you / a file edit (held and
  approved, or not) / developer view / Mandu / moved / Undo, from `proposedBy`
  (or the approver's name on an older arbiter); Approvals' history uses it
  too, and links the agent of an agent's row as this line does (§4.25 *A
  rule change and the agent that asked*).
- **The agent's session** is its scope id (`MANDU_SCOPE_ID`, the policy tool's
  session key), the id the proxy files its events under.

What stays unrecorded is a rule that predates the record or was written while
Mandu was not running (§4.25j).

**Tests.** arbiter `policy-agent-ops.test.ts` (`panelRowIds`, `current`
after a hand edit); `policy-proposals-view-model.test.ts` (`changeWho`,
`ruleOrigins`); `rule-actions.test.ts`; `home-js-rules.test.ts`;
`tests/stack/rule-origins.test.ts` (real arbiter + production adapter +
dashboard: hand-written rows, an agent's approved request, an agent's
tightening, a Rules page button, a later hand edit, the history).

#### 4.25j Every write to policy.yaml is recorded

**Design.**

- **One choke point.** Every write passes through `PolicyDocumentStore`
  (`apply` for a wire write, `pollDisk` for a hand edit picked up within 2 s),
  whose audit hook receives the document before and after. The arbiter
  (`recordOutsideChange`) records a change for the writes the policy surface
  does not record itself (`OUTSIDE_VIAS`: `disk`, `apply`, `mint-rule`,
  `export-labels`, `pin-reader`, `move-labels`) with the same item record
  (`diffItems`) and delta. A write that changes no item records nothing, and
  the arbiter's own write is not re-read as a hand edit (the store remembers
  the hash and file identity of what it wrote).
- **A hand edit that loosens a rule is held** (policy-surface.md §8.4.6):
  it is not in force until its Approvals card ("policy.yaml was changed on disk
  and would loosen N rule(s). Nothing changes until you approve") is approved,
  then recorded as an approved proposal asked by `file`, undoable. A hand edit
  that only tightens is recorded as below.
- **A hand edit is not undoable** otherwise: Undo would reverse a change the
  person made to their own file behind their back, so `undoPolicyChange`
  refuses it ("change the file directly instead"). The developer view's writes
  are undoable.
- **Undo while a hand edit waits** (2026-10-09, first-session tour item 17):
  Undo works; the revert is made to the law in force and to the held edit,
  which stays in the file with its comments and is asked about again on a
  fresh card (policy-surface.md §8.4.6). An Undo of a rule the held edit
  changes too is refused (409, "the change to policy.yaml waiting in
  Approvals changes the same rule") until that card is decided.
- **The writes outside the surface while a hand edit waits** (2026-10-18,
  tour item 17 after !1095): the developer view's apply, a minted rule, the
  label migrations (`export-labels`, the Rules page's `move-labels`) and a
  reader pin are layered onto the held edit the same way, item by item, and
  keep the file's comments; each is recorded as before. One that changes an
  item the held edit changes too, or that lands just after a hand edit the
  poll had not read yet, is refused (409 on `/api/policy/document`,
  `/api/policy/rules`, `/api/policy/export-labels` and
  `/api/files/move-page-rules`, the arbiter's words); a move refused moves
  no row (the file is written first).
- **A whole-file apply names the law it was built from** (2026-10-18, after
  !1973; policy-surface.md §8.4.6). `GET /api/policy/document` answers the
  law's version (`lawHash`) with it, and `POST` requires it back (400
  without). One built from a law that moved since (the agent's own lock, a
  hand edit, an answer in Approvals) is refused 409 with `stale: true` and
  the arbiter's words naming what changed; nothing is written, so that
  change is never undone. The developer view's Lists buttons and Add rule's
  trusted website and connect allowance say it in their answer line ("Not
  saved: the policy changed since this page read it (…), and saving would
  have undone that. Nothing was written, and what you entered is kept:
  reload the policy, then press … again.") with a *Reload the policy*
  button; what was typed stays in its field, the button reads the panel
  again and gives the focus back to the button to press, and pressing it
  reads the law as it is now.
- **Wording.** Whoever wrote the file is unknown, so a hand edit is never
  called "you": "Added to (or Changed in) policy.yaml directly, not through
  Mandu"; the developer view: "You added this in the developer view"; a pinned
  reader: "Mandu updated this when you let a program read the file".
- **Why it matters for the defense.** An edit that loosens a rule without
  going through Mandu is held for approval and shows up in the history and on
  the row, wherever it came from.

**Tests.** arbiter `test/component/policy-change-record.test.ts` (real
sockets: a hand edit recorded and refused by Undo, the file untouched; a
developer-view mint recorded and undoable; a re-applied document records
nothing; a surface change recorded once); `policy-proposals-view-model.test.ts`
(the origins and sentences, never "you" for a hand edit);
`tests/stack/rule-origins.test.ts` (a hand edit on the real stack).

#### 4.25k The inspector wears the product's stylesheet

**Design.** One stylesheet foundation, loaded by both pages before their own,
so moving between the front-ends does not change the whole look (this
replaces §4.1's IDE palettes). Presentation only: no security surface.

- **`public/mandu.css`** holds the color tokens (`--bg --panel --panel-2
  --line --line-2 --ink…--ink-4 --accent --ok --warn --bad`, their tints,
  `--code-bg`, `--code-ink`), the type (`--sans` for every word: the
  wordmark, headlines and body; `--mono` for data), radii, bare elements and the `.brand`
  wordmark. Light by default; a dark set follows `prefers-color-scheme`, and
  `data-theme="light" | "dark"` on `<html>` pins either. Both pages set it
  from one stored choice (`mandu.theme`): the product's Settings ›
  Appearance (§4.25, with a head script so the first paint has it) and the
  inspector's Appearance row (until 2026-10-18 the product page never set
  it). Four extra hues serve only the inspector: `--sym`,
  `--pink` (the quarantined U-LLM lane), `--purple`, `--cyan`. Components stay
  per page (app.css for the product, dashboard.css for the lanes).
- **The inspector** links `../mandu.css` then `dashboard.css`; every legacy
  variable maps to a shared token and its chrome follows the product (the
  wordmark, page-tab nav, product buttons). Prose and chrome are sans;
  trace DATA (payloads, symbols, commands, logs, times, ids) stays monospace
  through one selector list.
- **Fonts.** IBM Plex Sans and IBM Plex Mono, self-hosted
  under `public/fonts/` as latin-subset woff2 (SIL OFL 1.1, licenses beside
  the files; licensing.md §2), `font-display: swap` with a `unicode-range`. No
  CDN: the dashboard is loopback-first and works offline. Woff2 is served with
  a week's `max-age`, a license `.txt` never; css/js caching is §4.30.
- **One sans family, upright (2026-10-05).** Headlines and the wordmark are
  Plex Sans at weight 650 / 700, not a serif display face, and nothing is
  slanted: no italic face is vendored, `em`/`i`/`cite`/`dfn`/`var`/`address`
  are set upright, and emphasis or a muted aside is weight or ink, never
  italics. Mono stays for data (paths, code, hosts), where fixed width reads
  better. The Instrument Serif headline face and the Plex Sans italic were
  retired for a plainer, more consistent modern look.
- **Type floor**: 11px in the inspector, 12px on the product page.
- **Cache-busting.** `serveIndex` stamps `../`-relative css/js, and the
  inspector's version token also counts the product directory, so an edit to
  mandu.css reloads both pages.

**Text on a filled color reads in both themes (2026-10-14).** The count of
asks waiting in each page's top bar (the product page's `.count` beside
Approvals, the inspector's `.area-badge` in its page row) was a fixed white
on `--warn`: 5.09:1 on the light theme's amber `#a35d00`, but **2.23:1** on
the dark theme's light amber `#e0a24a`, under WCAG AA's 4.5:1 for text and
under the 3:1 floor for large text. This was the page's main "needs you"
signal, on every page. A headless Chromium audit of every page of both
front-ends in the dark theme found it. They were the only fixed text colors
in either stylesheet. Now both count in `var(--panel)`:

- the light theme is unchanged (`--panel` is `#ffffff` there);
- the dark theme draws dark ink on the amber (`#1f2126`, 7.24:1).

The fill stays `--warn`. That token is also the dark theme's warning text
on dark panels, where it must stay light, so the ink follows the fill and
not the other way round.

The rule: a page's text color is a token (or `inherit`, `currentColor`,
`transparent`), never a fixed color, which can read in one theme only. Text
on a box filled with an ink or a color (`--ink…`, `--accent`, `--ok`,
`--warn`, `--bad`, the inspector's hues) reads at least 4.5:1 in both
themes. Presentation only.

**The faintest ink reads too (2026-10-17).** The faintest ink, `--ink-4`,
draws a lot of small text on the product page: Approvals' 12 px cell labels
(`.ask-detail .k`, `.ask-sources .k`, `.proposal-k`), the counts beside
headings (`.muted`), a row's times and counts (`.row .dim`), the session
page's turn times, half labels, hidden captions and routine list, Rules'
column heads (`.files-heads`, `.q-cap`, `.file-opens-k`), `.files-selected`
and the source chip `.host-chip.from`. It read under WCAG AA's 4.5:1 in both
themes, and the light theme (the default) was the worse one. The human
approved a palette change (nightly queue item #4):

| token | theme | was | now | on panel / bg / panel-2 / code-bg |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--ink-4` | light | `#8a8a92` (3.43 / 3.08 / 3.28 / 2.97) | `#6c6c74` | 5.20 / 4.68 / 4.98 / 4.51 |
| `--ink-4` | dark | `#7c7b76` (3.80 / 4.18 / 3.98 / 3.29) | `#989791` | 5.50 / 6.06 / 5.76 / 4.77 |
| `--ok` | light | `#1e7f4f` (4.16 on `--ok-bg`) | `#1b7448` | 4.81 on `--ok-bg`, 5.77 on white |

`--ink-3` stays where it was (6.83:1 light, 6.29:1 dark on the panel), so
times and labels stay visibly fainter than notes; the page has a little
less tonal range. The dark `--ok`, `--warn` and `--bad` and every hue are
unchanged. `--ink-4` as a non-text color (the grey `.dot`, the hover
border, the agent-says rule) only darkens (light) or lightens (dark)
slightly. The inspector reads the same tokens from `mandu.css`, so its
`--ink-4` text gets the same fix.

The rule: every text token reads at least 4.5:1 on every ground it is drawn
on, in both themes.

*Not covered* (one gap left, for the human): the light theme's `--warn` on
`--warn-bg` (the secret chip `.mask-chip.secret`, the waiting and raw tags
and turn summaries) reads **4.45:1**. `#985700` would read 4.96:1 (and
white on it 5.68:1), but the top bar's count is pinned as "white on
`#a35d00`, as before" by a stack test that an unattended change may not
edit, so the token stays until the human moves it with that test.

*Tests*: `dashboard/test/unit/ui/css-shared-system.test.ts` (the token
table in both themes, the `--ink-3` / `--ink-4` order, the light `--warn`
gap pinned at its value; every `app.css` rule whose `color` is
`var(--ink-4)` reads ≥ 4.5:1 on its own background or on every plain
ground), `dashboard/test/unit/ui/css-dim-ink.test.ts` (D3: a row's `.dim`
too) and `tests/stack/dim-ink.test.ts` (K4: the served Approvals card's
labels and Rules' column heads, both themes, from the served styles).

**Secondary words read as secondary (2026-10-16).** The product page marks
the words that explain something else with the class `dim`: a caption, a
note, a status line, an empty list, where a label comes from. `app.css`
gives every `.dim` the note's ink, `--ink-3` (as `.note` and `.empty`),
with one page-wide rule beside `.note`. A row's own times and counts keep
the fainter `--ink-4` (`.row .dim`, more specific); the first-run card's
commands and an answer's outcome already had `--ink-3`.

Until then only those scoped rules named `.dim`, so a `.dim` anywhere else
drew in its parent's ink. A headless Chromium over a real arbiter and
dashboard (signed in; Rules with Add a rule, Keys Mandu found, a scan and
every row opened; Approvals with a wide change from the real
`policyPropose`; Home, a session, History, Settings; light and dark)
found these in the full `--ink`:

- Approvals (and *Describe what you want*): a wide change's foot "This
  change has no limit on one side." (since 2026-10-19 it says what the
  change opens, *A wide change says what is open*);
- Your rules: the *Patterns* and *Places* captions, and the empty line "No
  file or folder has a rule of yours yet." (the page's other empty states
  are `--ink-3`);
- an opened rule: "Your rule, this file only" beside its chip, where the
  rule came from ("No record of who added this. …"), the folder note;
- Add a rule's "This folder:"; Keys Mandu found's not-offered line and its
  empty list; Describe's status ("Working out the rules. …").

A folder's count of its rules ("5 rules") and the ticked bar's note took
`--ink-2` from their parents. After the change every `.dim` the probe drew
is `--ink-3` outside a row and `--ink-4` in one; the contrast audit of
each page is unchanged in both themes (no `--ink-3` line under 4.5:1; the
low items were the `--ink-4` ones, fixed by *The faintest ink reads too*).
Nothing moves and no word changes.
Presentation only.

*Tests*: `dashboard/test/unit/ui/css-dim-ink.test.ts` (every `.dim` on
Rules, Approvals and Home by its ink, both themes; the rule is page-wide;
each one, in a row or outside it, reads ≥ 4.5:1 on its ground) and
`tests/stack/dim-ink.test.ts` (the real arbiter, the production adapter
and the served pages and styles; no value or token, policy.yaml
unchanged).

**Motion follows the system's setting (2026-10-14).** Neither page read
`prefers-reduced-motion`. A headless Chromium with the setting emulated still
drew three pulses that never stop (`flare`, 1.1 s, infinite: the red banner
of a flagged session, a running session's **R** chip in the list, a starting
service's dot in Settings › Services). WCAG 2.2.2 asks that such motion can
be stopped. It also slid every dialog in, faded a glow on every jump,
rotated carets, slid the switch's knob, and scrolled every scripted jump for
about 800 ms. Chromium animates a script's `behavior: 'smooth'` whatever the
setting, and a script's choice outranks the stylesheet's `scroll-behavior`.
Now, under the setting only:

- **mandu.css** (both pages) ends every transition at once:
  `*, *::before, *::after { transition: none !important }`. The
  `!important` keeps a page's own later rule from bringing one back;
- **dashboard.css** stops the three pulses and the dialog's slide
  (`animation: none`). Each jump's highlight (`ruleref-flash`, `jump-flash`,
  `cardflash`) is held still for its usual time and then goes
  (`steps(1, end)`): the cue that shows where a jump landed stays, the fade
  does not;
- **every scripted jump** of the inspector (13 calls, in app.js, egress.js,
  protection.js and sub-menus.js) asks render-helpers.js `scrollMotion()`,
  which answers `'auto'` under the setting and `'smooth'` otherwise. It reads
  the setting at each jump, so a change holds at once.

Without the setting, every computed animation and transition is as before
(the Chromium probe's output is identical to master's). No script waits on
`transitionend` or `animationend`, so nothing hangs on an end that now comes
at once. A new animation gets its line in the reduce block: the sweep below
fails on one that has none. Presentation only.

*Not covered*: the vendored asciinema player's loading ring
(`dev/vendor/asciinema-player/`, its own stylesheet) still turns while a
recording loads.

**Forced colors (2026-10-14).** Under a forced palette (Windows' contrast
themes, a browser set to its own colors; `forced-colors: active`) the
browser draws every color a page sets in the person's palette, keeps only
the CSS system colors (`Canvas`, `ButtonText`, `Highlight`, …), draws a
fill in the page's own color, and draws the page's color behind every word
(the backplate). Neither stylesheet had a forced-colors rule. A headless
Chromium with the mode emulated (light and dark palettes; the product
page's Home, agent, Approvals, Rules and Settings pages, the inspector's
Sessions, a session, Rules, Settings and Approvals) found three states on
the product page that only a fill or a colored edge drew:

- **Settings › Protection's switch was not drawn at all**, on or off: its
  track and its knob are fills (`border: none`), so both became the page's
  color. The row's word (*On*) stayed; the control a person presses and its
  state did not;
- **Rules › Who may get your secrets' tabs looked alike**: each tab's
  `transparent` edge was drawn in the text color, the picked one's too;
- **the top bar's current page** kept only its weight (500 against 400):
  its fill was gone.

Now app.css draws each in system colors inside `@media (forced-colors:
active)`, as the system draws its own controls: off is an outline, a picked
or "on" thing the palette's selection color.

- **The switch**: a 1px `ButtonText` edge on a `ButtonFace` track with a
  `ButtonText` knob on the left; on, the track filled in `Highlight` with a
  `HighlightText` knob on the right. The edge narrows the box the knob is
  placed in, so its offsets are 1px less (2px; on, 20px): the knob stays on
  the pixels it has without forced colors. Held or turned off, it is dimmed
  as before (`opacity`, which a forced palette does not touch);
- **the tabs**: the picked tab's edge is `Highlight`; an unpicked tab draws
  no edge (`border-bottom-style: none`: a transparent edge would be drawn,
  and one in the page's color would cut the row's line) and takes the 2px
  as padding, so every tab keeps its height;
- **the current page** is underlined in `Highlight` (2px, 6px below the
  words; the count beside Approvals with it). Not a `Highlight` fill: the
  backplate is drawn in the page's color behind its words, so
  `HighlightText` on `Highlight` lost the word (the probe's first try).

**The inspector (2026-10-14, a later run).** dev/dashboard.css drew every
picked thing by its fill. The same Chromium survey, run on a real served
inspector (the first-session tour's session; Sessions, a session's Trace and
Files, Drills, Tests, Rules, Settings), compared each picked thing with an
unpicked one of its group as the browser drew them: the current page, the
picked session tab, Files' Commits | Both views tab, Drills' Runs | Matrix
and Replay | Live differed by their weight alone; the open session in the
list, the picked step in the trace's rail and the picked row of the Rules,
Settings and Tests menus not at all (each row's `transparent` edge was
drawn, every row's alike, and their fill was the page's color). A commit
opened in Files › Commits and the picked half of its *this session | all*
scope are drawn the same way (no tour session has commits; jsdom checks
them). dev/dashboard.css's `@media (forced-colors: active)` block marks the
picked one in `Highlight`, by one of two rules:

- **underlined** where it has no edge of its own, or one its whole group
  shares (a segment's): the current page, the session tabs, Files' tabs,
  Replay | Live and the commits' scope (2px, 4px below the
  words, inside each box: a segment clips what overflows it). Not a fill:
  the backplate would hide its words;
- **edged** where the row's edge is `transparent`: the session rows, the
  steps, the commits and the Rules, Settings, Tests and Drills menus' rows
  (Drills' menu is a row list since 2026-10-16, no longer a segment). Each
  row's edge is drawn in `Canvas` (not seen) and the picked row's in
  `Highlight`. A step keeps its left bar (its kind, drawn as the palette
  draws it); the picked step's is `Highlight` too. Tests' menu is a
  sub-nav as well, so its picked row drops the sub-nav's line
  (`text-decoration-line: none`): one mark, the menus' edge.

Only colors and lines change: every edge keeps its width and every box its
padding, so nothing moves. The ⚙ Control drawer's `.topbar-btn.active`,
which no script has set since the six-page nav, is gone.

The rules: a forced-colors block holds only system colors (any other is
replaced anyway), and no other rule uses one (it would draw the OS palette
in a themed page); a state drawn with a color (`[aria-checked]`,
`[aria-selected]`, `[aria-current]`, `[aria-pressed]`, `.selected`,
`:checked`, and the inspector's `.active` and `.sel`) has a forced-colors
rule of its own, or one for the thing a page-wide qualifier names
(`body.tenant-test .page-nav a[aria-current="page"]` is the current page);
a selection-color fill never holds words. Without forced colors nothing
changes (a Chromium probe of the three controls, every state, light and
dark, computes and draws them as master does; for the inspector, every
picked and unpicked thing computes as on master). Presentation only.

*Not covered*:

- a ticked file row's tint (`.row.file.selected`): its own checkbox is
  ticked, and the browser draws a checkbox in the palette;
- a disclosure button's open state (`aria-expanded`): the content it opens
  is drawn beside it;
- the status dots (`.dot`): each sits beside the words that say the same
  (*On*, *Running*, *ended …*), and a dot in one system color would tell
  nothing, so they go with their fill;
- the inspector's `.sel` (the trace's row, or the system log's entry, of
  the step picked in the rail): an outline, which the browser keeps in the
  palette's text color (the survey's picture shows it), and no other row
  has one;
- a hover's fill: hovering picks nothing, and the pointer shows where it is.

**Tests.** `test/unit/ui/css-shared-system.test.ts` (both pages load mandu.css
first; no page redeclares a palette token; no legacy variable survives; every
token the inspector reads is defined; dark sets identical and complete; a
text color is a token, never a fixed color; every rule that fills its box
with an ink or a color and sets its text reads 4.5:1 in both themes, the two
counts among them; each count drawn in jsdom with its page's styles, each
theme's tokens resolved (css-flatten `resolveCssVars(css, "dark")`,
`contrastRatio`): light white on `#a35d00` as before, both themes 4.5:1;
every `@font-face` vendored with swap and a unicode-range, licenses present,
no remote font; only Plex Sans and Plex Mono, upright, with no serif or slanted
rule on either page; the type floors; heading and tab look); `app-js-layout-nav.test.ts`
(theme pick and persistence); `test/unit/server/static-fonts.test.ts` (the
route: type, max-age, no license file, no traversal); `two-front-ends.test.ts`
(both pages link the shared file first, every `url(fonts/…)` resolves); stack
`tests/stack/approvals-badge-theme.test.ts` (`secrets`; a real arbiter's gate
files a real ask, a real dashboard over the production adapter; the served

sweep of the three stylesheets: every animated rule has a reduce rule for

one that does; the shared rule ends every transition, `!important`, and no
reduce block sets one; both pages load mandu.css first; jsdom with the

true })` and `perSelector` (jsdom drops a selector list that names a
pseudo-element): the pulses and the dialog stand still, each highlight

`scrollMotion`, its 13 jumps counted; a jump to a rule in egress.js scrolls
`auto` under the setting, `smooth` without it and with no `matchMedia`);
stack `tests/stack/reduced-motion.test.ts` (`secrets`; a real arbiter's
built-in rules and a real ask, a real dashboard over the production
adapter; the served inspector's Rules page, signed out: a jump to a served
rule scrolls the panel and the row at once under the setting and smoothly
without, its highlight held or faded, the pulses and a dialog's panel
still or moving; the served product page's Settings switch; the oracle).
Forced colors: `test/unit/ui/css-forced-colors.test.ts` (a sweep of app.css:
every state drawn with a color has a forced-colors rule, the one exception
named with its reason; across the three stylesheets a forced-colors block
holds only system colors and no other rule uses one; no selection-color
fill holds words in the page's markup; jsdom with the forced block

1280 and 390 px: the switch off and on, its knob where it is without

height; only the current page underlined, no word on a fill; the

`tests/stack/forced-colors.test.ts` (`secrets`; a real arbiter's gate files
