#### 4.25l Your own model: the `local-model` level, the declared models, and who read a datum

**Status: LANDED.** The dashboard side of
[`model-endpoints.md §1`](../confidentiality/model-endpoints.md)
D6 and of
[`model-endpoints.md §2`](../confidentiality/model-endpoints.md),
in the product's words ("your own model" / "an outside model", "the AI" /
"the helper"; confidentiality.md §3.5).

**The fourth level.** Every dashboard copy of the level list knows
`local-model` (`public < any-model < local-model < no-model`):
`secrets.ts CONFIDENTIALITY_LEVELS` (the label route rejects an unknown level
with 400 rather than coercing it), the `LevelClass` `local-only` (not a
model-ok grant), the `$MDU:localmodel_` marker in the lineage and agent-page
secret checks, and every inspector level word. An unknown level renders
strict.

**Rules page.** The glossary term **Secret, your own model only**: "Only
models you or your organization run, on this computer or on your
organization's network, and listed in Settings, Models, can read what is
inside…". The label control offers it only when the policy panel's `models`
holds a `local: true` row; otherwise it is disabled with "Add one in Settings"
(the HTML ships it disabled, so a page that cannot read the panel never offers
it). The server does not refuse the level without a declared model: such a
label behaves as `no-model` (plan 11 D2), which loses nothing and leaks
nothing, and the row carries the warning "No AI of your own is listed, so
no AI reads this file. Add one in Settings, Models." The inspector's label
dropdown (`dev/js/secrets.js gateLocalModel`) gates the same way.

**Settings › Models.** One row per declared model: name, address, API style,
model, "key from `<ENV>`" when a `tokenEnv` is set, and "Your own model, on
this computer" / "… on your network (host)" / "Outside model" (placement by
`view-model/model-endpoints.ts endpointPlacement`, one of four mirrors pinned
by `tests/stack/model-placement-parity.test.ts`). **No token value is ever
shown:** the projection copies the snapshot's fields explicitly, so a
value-shaped field cannot reach the page. The row also shows plain http to
another machine ("Not encrypted: …"), its TLS checks (never a path), its
`perimeter:` restriction, the helper mark, and for an administrator's entry
(`/etc/mandu/policy.d/`) "Set by your administrator" with no Edit.

- **Add / Edit / Remove** in one form (name, url, wire, model, "This is my own
  model" = `local`, "Read my own-model files with this one" = `helper`,
  `token_env`, and "Send without encryption" = `allow_plain_http`, enabled
  only for a local `http://` address). The browser sends `POST
  /api/policy/models/change {action, name?, model?, version?, expected?}`;
  `server/model-routes.ts` plans it into the grammar's `add-model` /
  `update-model` / `remove-model` (moving the helper mark is an extra
  `update-model` in the same list), and the arbiter's `checkModels` judges the
  entry, so no model rule is repeated here. An update carries the entry's
  `tls` in force, so the form never drops it.
- **A save names the model as it was read (2026-10-18).** Each row carries
  its entry's version (`version`, from the snapshot's `modelVersions`, an
  opaque keyed hash; policy-surface.md §8.4.6 "An item-level version"); Edit
  keeps it (`M.formVersion`) and the update sends it, required (400
  without). The route refuses at once, before asking, a version its own
  read finds moved, and sends the arbiter `basedOn`: the entry at the
  page's version, plus any entry whose helper mark the change moves at the
  route's read; the arbiter refuses the propose, or the approval, once one
  of them changed. Either way the answer is 409 `{ stale: true, changed }`
  and nothing is written. Until then a change to the same model landing
  between the page's read and Save (another window, a hand edit) was
  overwritten with what the form was filled from, `tls` included; a change
  to another model never refuses it. The form says "*lab* was changed
  somewhere else while you were editing it, so nothing was saved. What you
  typed is still in the form: compare it with *lab* as it is now, then save
  again.", keeps every field as typed, reads the list again
  (`modelFormReread`), so the row shows the model as it is now and the next
  Save names that version; a model gone meanwhile says "Nothing was saved:
  *lab* is no longer in your list." The preview gate is unchanged: every
  loosening is still asked and judged at apply.
- **Always a question first.** Every models change is a relaxation in the
  delta core (policy-surface.md §8.3.2): the first send previews (`{confirm,
  expected, rows, wouldLet, warnings}`, with a warning for an own model not on
  this machine or a local network), the second applies through
  `applyAsHuman` on the admin channel as `settings`. Undo is offered. Every
  applied change says "New sessions use this. Restart a running agent to use
  it there." (a session's model binding is fixed at launch, plan 11 §7.1). A
  validator refusal is a 422 shown under the form; writes sit behind CSRF and
  the admin session.
- **The only model editor**: the Describe box and the agent's policy tool
  cannot change a model (policy-surface.md §8.4.3a).
- **Test connection.** `POST /api/policy/models/test {name}` probes the entry
  IN FORCE by name (never an address from the request) with `mandu doctor`'s
  checks, mirrored in `src/model-probe.ts`: a TCP connect (3 s), `GET
  {url}/v1/models` (3 s, `redirect: "error"` so a bearer token never follows a
  redirect), the placement grading, one TLS handshake with the entry's checks,
  and the perimeter check (an address outside it gets no handshake). The token
  named by `token_env` is read from the dashboard's environment for the
  listing only; the answer never carries it. `tests/stack/model-probe-parity.test.ts`
  runs one case table through doctor and this probe.

**On Approvals.** `editRow` renders the model ops with the address in full;
`toProposalCard` adds `warnings` for a `local: true` entry whose host is not
on this machine or a local network, and such a card needs the typed ALLOW
(`isOverBroad`): it is the one way a steered agent could ask for "your own
model only" files to leave the machine. Changes that drop or widen
`perimeter.networks`, or turn on plain http to another machine, get their own
warning lines.

**Main model on the agent page.** `/api/home/agent` asks the source's optional
`sessionUpstream(sessionKey)` and shows "Main model: your own model (ollama)"
or "Main model: an outside model (gw)" when the session is bound to a declared
entry; otherwise nothing.

**Who read a datum.** An inspect `ullm_call` may carry `endpoint: { name,
location: "local" | "external" }`. `dual-lanes.ts` puts it on the inspect step
as `readBy` (joined by token, since inspect-mcp emits no `callId`) and
`paired-rows.ts` adds `readByWords` ("read by your own model (ollama), on your
network", "read by the helper"); the inspector and the product's reader card
show it. An event without the field renders as before.

Presentation only: the arbiter decides every admission, and every write is
the edit grammar on the admin channel.

**Tests.** `model-endpoints.test.ts` (no token leak, `local` only for a
literal true), `server/model-routes.test.ts` (ask-then-apply, refusals, CSRF +
admin, the probe answering with no token), `policy-proposals-view-model.test.ts`
(the warning and typed ALLOW), `home-js-models.test.ts`, and the unit suites of
each projection named above; `two-front-ends.test.ts` (the choice enabled or
disabled in the served page by the declared models);
`tests/stack/dashboard-models-settings.test.ts` (production wiring over a real
arbiter and a loopback model server: add asks then applies, Test connection
with the token on the wire only, edit, remove, Undo, a cloud model as "my own
model" refused, the main-model line), `model-probe-parity.test.ts`;
for the version, `server/model-routes.test.ts` (400 without, 409 before the
preview, `basedOn` sent, the arbiter's stale refusal at propose and at
approve, no carried-over write to an arbiter without versions),
`home-js-models.test.ts` (the refusal said, the typed fields kept, the list
read again, the next Save at the new version), arbiter
`policy-item-version.test.ts`, and `tests/stack/model-update-stale.test.ts`
(the served page over the real arbiter: an unrelated model's change does not
refuse the save; another change to the same model does, nothing written).

#### 4.25m Add a file or folder: a file browser with each file's label

**Status: LANDED.** The browser is the All files view of the explorer
(§4.25n), and the labels are columns of its list (§4.25p).

**Why.** Labeling a file by typing its path from memory hid what was there,
which label each file already had, and where that label came from (a folder
rule, a pattern, a built-in secret such as `.env` or `~/.ssh`), so a person
could mark "Not secret" a folder holding a key the catalog protects. Patterns
taken from other tools: the tree shows the computed result, every mark says
where it came from, built-ins are shown but locked, and a weaker label asks
with an optional reason. Avoided: a folder label that silently overwrites the
labels inside it, pattern rules with no "which rule matched", and treating a
hidden listing as access control.

**Design.**

- **Browsing.** `GET /api/files/list?path=<abs or ~>&offset=N` answers one
  folder: breadcrumbs, entries folders-first then by name, 500 per page, and
  the folder's own label. An entry carries name, absolute path, `~` spelling,
  kind (a symlink to a folder is a folder) and a symlink's target. The route
  reads the directory and `stat`s link targets; it never opens a file. Hidden
  files are shown by default, because they are what people label. Past the
  first page, **Show more (N more)** reads the next (`moreFiles`); the first
  entry it brought then takes the focus, on its tick box where the arrow
  keys move, and a read that fails says why over the button, which stays
  and keeps the focus (§4.25ae *A Show more that fails*). A folder read
  again after a return reads as far as it was shown (§4.25 *The file
  browser reads its folder again*, *As far as it was shown*).
  *A picked entry past the first page (2026-10-15).* Go with a file's
  path, *Show in its folder* and *Show in the file browser* open a folder
  with one entry picked, its row opened and scrolled to. When
  the pick is not on the first page, the folder is read on at the offsets
  Show more reads (`pagesUpTo`), down to the page it is on, and shown that
  far, *Show more* bringing the rest. The read stops at the pick, at the
  folder's end, at 10,000 entries (20 pages, completion's bound), or once
  the listing's order has passed it (`pickAhead`: after a file whose name
  sorts after the pick's, it cannot follow; a file gone since stops the
  read there, with the pages read shown and nothing opened). Only a pick
  in the folder read is followed, and a folder opened meanwhile wins. A
  page that fails leaves the pages read and says why over *Show more*.
  Until then the pick was looked for on the first page only: in a folder
  of more than 500 entries a file past them was not opened, it stayed
  behind *Show more*, the path box that named it read the folder, and
  *Show in its folder* gave the focus to the path box. Presentation only:
  the reads are the listing's own, under its gate.
  *A pick is its read's own (2026-10-15).* The pick travels with the read
  asked for it (`openFolder`'s `opts.pick`; a file's answer hands it to the
  read of its folder), never in the page's state. A read that is refused
  or gets no answer, or that another listing or a *Show more* overtakes,
  takes its pick with it: the next listing shows what it was asked for,
  a Go to the folder its first page with nothing opened, even while the
  pick's own read is still out. Until then the pick (`F.pick`) waited for
  the next listing of its folder (a Go, a quick start, a read again after
  a return), which opened that row unasked and read the folder on to it,
  up to 20 pages.
- **Typed paths and Tab completion.** The path box takes a path starting
  with `/` or `~`, or a pattern; Go opens a folder (a file: its folder,
  with the file opened; a path not there yet, or a pattern: a row of its
  own). Tab at the end of the box completes the name being typed
  (`completePath`): the rest of the one name that matches (a folder with
  its `/`), or the part that several share. Typing fills the box's
  suggestions list (`#files-suggest`, at most 20) and completes the same
  way, with what it added selected so the next key types over it. Hidden
  names are offered while the list shows hidden files, or when the name
  typed starts with a dot. *The whole folder (2026-10-15).* The names are
  the folder's listing (`completionNames`): its pages read once each, at
  the offsets Show more reads, up to 10,000 names (20 pages); the folder
  the browser shows lends the pages it read (`openFolder`, `moreFiles`);
  a keystroke while a read is out waits for that read. Until then
  completion knew a folder's first page only: past 500 entries a name
  could not be completed, and, folders sorting first, in a folder of more
  than 500 folders a name a folder and a file share completed to the
  folder (`~/big/not` to `~/big/notes/`, with `notes.md` beside it).
  Where some names are not read (past 10,000, or a page that failed,
  which the next Tab reads again), the listing's order tells whether one
  could match (`unreadMayMatch`): after the last folder read, a file of any
  name may follow; after a file, the files sorting after it. If one could,
  the box keeps what was typed and the suggestions list the names read.
  An entry repeated at a page seam counts once, and a page that brings
  nothing new ends the read. *Tab moves on (2026-10-15).* The box keeps
  a Tab only while it can finish a name (`tabCompletes`, decided as the
  key is pressed): the selection ends at the end of the text but is not
  all of it (a Tab into the box selects it all), the text is a path, not
  a pattern, and a name is started after its last `/`. Then the box keeps
  the Tab when what typing added is selected (Tab takes it: the caret
  goes after it, and a folder's name is not filled in further), when the
  folder's names read add something (`completionOf`, the arithmetic
  `completePath` uses), or when they are not all read yet (a folder not
  read, a page on its way or one that failed) and no Tab on this same
  text has added nothing yet. Every other Tab moves the focus on, as on
  any field: after Go (`~/ws/`), on a whole name, on a pattern, and the
  second Tab on a folder that cannot be listed; typing gives Tab another
  try. Until then the box kept every Tab without Shift while its text
  ended at the caret or the selection, and only then asked whether there
  was a name to finish. The box always holds the folder shown, so the
  keyboard could not leave it but backwards (Shift+Tab), and Go, the
  list, the ticked items and the rest of the page were out of Tab's
  reach. A Tab on a folder's path ending with `/` no longer fills in the
  name its entries share (`~/ws/config/` stays, never
  `~/ws/config/db.yaml`): no name is started there, and it is the text Go
  leaves; typing the `/` still lists the folder's names under the box.
  Not covered: the names read for a folder the
  browser does not show are kept for the page's life, so a file made
  later is completed only once that folder is opened; a Tab kept while
  the names are read that then add nothing leaves the focus in the box
  (the next Tab moves on). Presentation only:
  the reads are the listing's own, under its gate.
- **Who may browse.** Anyone who can open the dashboard, remote viewers
  through the front included: seeing the dashboard already carries the
  person's authority. The route guards against the OTHER local caller: a GET
  is open to any same-host process, the agent's included, so the listing
  requires the CSRF header AND the admin session (policy-surface.md
  §2.6), like a labeling act.
- **Labels.** One arbiter op, `pathLevels {paths[], home?}` (a data-socket
  read, at most 1000 paths), answers the folder and its page of entries in one
  round trip with `pathLevel`'s own derivation (the level a read would mint
  today), the deciding rule and where it is kept (`policy`, `page` for the
  mandu.db store, `models`). It answers with the confidentiality axis off too,
  and the page then says "Protection is off. These rules take effect when
  you turn it on in Settings." `view-model/file-browser.ts fileLabel` words it ("Your
  rule", "From your rule on ~/proj", "Matches your rule **/*.pem", "Built in:
  environment files", "Written by the AI after it read a secret", "Like any
  other file"). **Fail-closed display:** a label that cannot be read (arbiter
  down or too old) is `null` and shown as "Label unknown", never as "Like any
  other file". The note over the list says why: a failed dial to the
  service's socket (the route passes it on as "the protection service did
  not answer (connect ENOENT /…)") reads "Labels could not be read. The
  protection service is not running. Start it under Settings, or try again
  in a moment. You can still choose rules.", the link opening Settings, and
  never a socket path (`home.js labelsUnknownNote`, the page's
  `UNREACHABLE_REFUSAL`); any other cause is shown as the server wrote it.
  The folder is read again when the service or the dashboard comes back
  (§4.25, *The file browser reads its folder again*).
- **Saving: one change, confirmed when weaker.** Choices wait in *Changes to
  save* (before → after, each with Drop; kept in `localStorage` per viewer
  across a reload). `POST /api/files/labels {changes, expected?, reason?}`
  plans them on the server (`planFileChanges`) into `lock-path` /
  `unlock-path` on policy.yaml, applied as ONE recorded, undoable change
  through `applyAsHuman`. A change that loosens protection by the arbiter's
  own preview (`policyDelta`) first answers `{confirm, expected, loosens}`; the
  page lists the loosenings in its words (a rule reaching everything inside
  a file as that file, §4.25f), takes an optional reason (kept on
  the change), and applies only when the same list comes back, else 409 and
  ask again.
- **A save names the rules as they were read** (2026-10-18). A label chosen
  is a `lock-path` that replaces the path's rule whole, carrying over what
  the row read (its hosts, its reach). Each listed entry carries the version
  of its path's own rule (`version`; the `absentVersion` when it has none;
  read before the labels, so a rule that changes between the two reads is
  refused rather than let through), and so does each file rule of Your
  rules (the snapshot's `pathVersions`, the panel row's `version`). A choice
  keeps the version of the row it was made on, and Save sends it with each
  change. The route names every policy.yaml edit's rule in `basedOn`
  (`paths`, the arbiter's `pathIdentity`): at the page's version, else (a
  typed path, a symlink's target, a change from an older page) at the
  version its own read finds just before it proposes. A rule moved since
  the page read it is refused at once, before anything is asked; one moved
  after is refused by the arbiter; either way 409 `{ stale: true, changed }`,
  nothing written, and no page-store change made either. *Changes to save*
  says "*~/proj/.env* was changed somewhere else while you were choosing, so
  nothing was saved. Your choice still waits in Changes to save: look at the
  label as it is now, then save again."; the choices stay waiting, Your
  rules and the folder are read again, and each waiting change takes its
  row's label and version as they are now (`pendingVersionsNow`), so the
  next Save asks again if it is weaker and names the rules as they are now.
  A change to another path's rule never refuses it. An arbiter that sends
  no versions is sent no change that names one (501). The page store's
  rules have no versions.
- **The page store.** Labels the old form made live in mandu.db, which wins
  over policy.yaml on the same path, so a change there is made in place
  (`setPathLabel` / `removePathLabel`, admin channel), its loosenings named by
  the same rank test and confirmed on the same screen, but not part of the
  undoable change. **Move the older rules**: "Move them into policy.yaml" runs
  the admin op `movePageLabels` (each row into `paths:`, replacing a shadowed
  entry, then the rows deleted); enforcement does not change, the change is
  recorded as `move-labels`, and Undo refuses it (the rows are gone).
- **Symlinks.** The kernel guard judges an open on the file it reaches, but a
  rule is matched on the path as written, so a rule on one spelling alone
  leaves reads by the other uncovered at the model-context layer. The listing
  gives each symlink its fully resolved `target` and, when labeled
  differently, `targetLabel`; a rule chosen for a link is also written on the
  target server-side (`withSymlinkTargets`, so a client cannot skip it).
  Removing the link's rule leaves the target's rule, the safe direction.
  **Open:** a rule written by hand on one spelling still has the gap; resolving
  links in the label lookup is a hot-path change (listed in guarantees.md).
- **Impact.** `pathLevels` takes `withEdits` (evaluated like
  `testFlow.withEdits`, nothing written). `POST /api/files/impact {changes,
  folder?}` walks the files under each changed folder (names only, breadth
  first, 8 levels, at most 5000 files, no symlinked folders), compares each
  file's label now and under the edits, and answers `{scanned, truncated,
  changed, weaker, files[≤50, weaker first], decidedBy}`. The pending list
  shows it live ("Changes the label of 12 files, 3 of them less protected"),
  and the question before a weaker Save names those files, so a folder made
  "Not secret" names the built-in `.env` inside it. A truncated scan says so.
  A typed pattern previews which files it would decide (`decidedBy`); one
  the protection service cannot use says why on its row (§4.25
  *Refusals*, *A typed pattern says why on its row*).
- **Why.** `GET /api/files/why?path=` (CSRF + admin session) over the
  arbiter's `whyPath`, in the page's words (`whyWords`): where the label comes
  from, which programs get the real file and what others get, where it may be
  sent (each host a code, and for a file whose values are bound one by one,
  the *Per value* sentence: §4.25u *Rules names each host*), your answers,
  and a stricter pattern a closer rule outranks. In an opened rule of Your
  rules, a *Warning* the row already says beside the box is left out of it
  (§4.25p, *A warning is said once*). "The
  masked copy" says what the arbiter makes of the file as it is (`twin`,
  `maskedCopyWords`: its shape kept with each secret value Mandu recognizes
  hidden, the whole file hidden, or the file as it is); until 2026-10-09 it
  said "only the values are hidden" of any file whose path has a structured
  shape. An older arbiter's answer falls back to the path's shape, worded
  as depending on what the file holds.
- **Developer view.** Its lock form (`dev/js/secrets.js`) writes through `POST
  /api/files/labels` too, with a confirm naming the loosenings. `POST|DELETE
  /api/secrets/label` remains for the developer view. Its Remove still
  sends `DELETE /api/secrets/label`, which removes only a label the
  protection service stores: on a label written in policy.yaml, as the form
  writes one now, it answers `removed: false` and changes nothing, and the
  panel says so (§4.32 *Remove and Clear taint say what they did*). Sending
  Remove through `files/labels` instead would change how a loosening is
  asked for, and is left to a human decision.

**Tests.** `arbiter/test/unit/path-levels-op.test.ts`,
`arbiter/test/component/path-levels.test.ts` (agreement with `pathLevel`,
`withEdits` writing nothing, `movePageLabels` admin-only and
enforcement-neutral); `view-model/file-browser.test.ts`;
`server/file-browser-routes.test.ts` (the admin gate on the GET, no contents,
unknown labels, loosen only when confirmed, a stale confirmation refused,
symlink expansion, the scan limit); `home-js-files.test.ts`;
`home-js-files-complete-pages.test.ts` (Tab past the first page: a name
past it, a folder and a file sharing a name, the shown folder's pages lent,
a page that fails, the 20-page bound, typing while a read is out, the seam;
each page read once) and `tests/stack/product-complete-pages.test.ts` (a
real folder of 500 folders and three files behind the real arbiter and
dashboard, at `secrets`: Tab completes past row 500 and to the shared
start, and reads nothing once the browser has read the folder);
`home-js-files-pick-pages.test.ts` (a picked entry past the first page:
Go to a file on the second page, *Show in its folder* on a rule written
with `~` landing on the row's ⋯, a pick on the first page, a file gone
since, a page that fails, the 10,000-entry bound, a pick an overtaken
read left, a folder opened meanwhile; the pick is its read's own: a read
refused, a *Show more* or a Go to the same folder while it is out, a file's
folder refused, each followed by a Go that opens nothing) and
`tests/stack/product-files-pick-pages.test.ts` (a real folder of 500
folders and three files, at `secrets`: Go to a file past row 500 and *Show
in its folder* on its policy.yaml rule open its row, each page read once)
and `tests/stack/product-files-pick-own-read.test.ts` (a real folder of
three files, at `secrets`: *Show in its folder* whose read gets no answer,
then a Go to its folder, and one with a Go to its folder before its read
answers, both open nothing; small on purpose, as the stack files run side
by side and the defect needs no second page);
`tests/stack/dashboard-file-browser.test.ts`
(production adapter and a real arbiter: `pathLevels`, `whyPath` and
`movePageLabels` parity, every listed label equals `pathLevel`, a tightening
enforced and undone, a loosening inert until confirmed, a link's rule covering
both spellings, the impact naming the built-in `.env`, the move keeping
enforcement identical).

#### 4.25n Files and folders is one file explorer

**Design (`home.js`, "Files and folders: the file explorer").** The rules
list's file group (§4.25f) and the browser (§4.25m) are one explorer, in the
**Your rules** card. The side panel it first had was replaced by §4.25p's
columns, and those by one label menu per row (2026-10-05); the pending list
and Save stand.

- **Panels, not views (2026-10-05).** The three view tabs (Labeled / All
  files / Suggested) are gone. The §4.25f tree of the person's rules on
  files, folders and patterns is always shown, under "Files and folders".
  **Add a rule** (`#rules-add`, aria-expanded) opens the §4.25m browser and
  the path bar in a panel above it (`#lock-form`; Close shuts it), kept open
  across a reload in `mandu.files.view` (`all` / `labeled`); nothing is read
  from disk until it is opened, and a folder with rules inside carries "N
  rules inside". **Keys Mandu found** (§4.25r) is a card of its own, opened
  with Review (`mandu.files.suggested`); a page that remembered the old
  `suggested` view opens it. `setFilesView('all' | 'labeled' | 'suggested')`
  stays the one entry point (Show in its folder, the empty rows' "Add a
  rule", the Approvals card).
- **Changes to save** (`#files-pending`) sits after the cards and is sticky
  at the bottom of the window while anything waits, so a label chosen in the
  list, in the browser or in Keys Mandu found is saved from one place.
- **Its buttons never scroll away (2026-10-06).** The bar used to be one
  scrolling block (`max-height: 50vh; overflow-y: auto`): with 30 changes
  waiting, Discard and Save sat below the last change, and so did the
  weaker-change question with its Why? field. Now the bar is a flex column
  in which only the lists give way and scroll in place. The list of changes
  (`#files-pending-list`) scrolls and keeps at least two rows. The impact
  note (`#files-impact`) gives way first, down to its headline, its "Show the
  files" and, when open, the first file. The question's two lists
  (`#files-confirm-list`, the files under it) scroll within
  `min(10em, 10vh)`. The heading, the question's words, the Why? field and
  `.form-actions` keep their size (`flex: none`), outside every scrolling
  part. The bar grows to at most half the window, or 20rem where half the
  window is less and the window has room. While Save asks, it may take the
  window's height less its 12px margins, and the impact note gives way down
  to its headline and "Show the files", since the question names the files.
  Measured in Chrome with 32 changes: the question, the Why? field and both
  buttons are on screen at 1280×800, 1280×600, 1280×520, 700×600 and
  390×844. Below about 520px tall, while asking, even the fixed parts do not
  fit; there the bar's own scroll is the fallback, which is how it behaved
  before. Nothing is reordered, so the focus order is unchanged: the Drop
  buttons, "Show the files", Why?, then Discard and Save. Chrome and Firefox
  make a scrolling list that has no button of its own (the question's lists)
  a tab stop, so a keyboard can scroll it. Presentation only: Save, Discard
  and the rules API are unchanged.
- **It never hides the focus (2026-10-14).** The bar is sticky over the
  rules, and the page kept no room for it: a Tab moving down the page
  scrolls the next control just into the window, at its bottom edge, which
  is under the bar. Measured in a headless Chromium over a real arbiter
  with six file rules and three changes waiting, Tab through the whole
  page and back: at 1280×800, 48 of 118 stops (every rule's menus, ⋯ and
  *Edit where*, Add a rule, Sending data's menus) lay entirely under the
  bar and 21 partly; at 390×844, 75 forward and 33 back. And a label
  chosen in a row near the window's bottom left that menu under the bar
  that came up with it (0 of 15 points of it in view at 1280×800). WCAG
  2.4.11 (*Focus Not Obscured*). Now:
  - the window keeps the bar's room below whatever it scrolls into view
    (app.css `scroll-padding-bottom: var(--bar-room)` on `html`): a Tab's
    control, a row opened with `scrollIntoView({block: 'nearest'})`;
  - `home.js trackBarRoom` measures it with a `ResizeObserver` on the bar:
    the bar's height, its 12px margin and 8px more while it is shown, and
    nothing while the bar or its page is hidden, so the other pages and a
    Rules page with nothing waiting scroll as before;
  - a bar that comes or grows over the focused control (a first change,
    the impact note, the weaker-change question) scrolls that control
    into view, above it;
  - a control **in** the bar keeps the browser's own scrolling: the rule
    holds only while the focus is outside the bar
    (`html:not(:has(#files-pending:focus-within))`). With the room kept for
    them too, Chromium moved the page by up to 594px, towards the bar's own
    place in it, whenever the focus entered the bar (Save, Discard, Drop).

  After, in the same survey: no stop hidden at either size, no jump into
  the bar, and the changed menu whole above it. One stop stays partly
  under the bar at 390×844: *Describe the rules you want*, a textarea that
  Chromium scrolls by its caret, which is in view. Not covered then: at
  390×844 the label choice itself scrolled the page up 360px, so the
  changed menu ended below the window, not under the bar. That was the
  tree's redraw, not the bar's (next bullet). Presentation only: no route,
  rule, Save or focus rule changed.
- **A label chosen keeps its menu on screen (2026-10-14).** Every choice
  in Your rules (a label, where it may be sent, ⋯, *Remove my rule*,

  `clear(host)`, then every row anew). On a phone the tree is longer than
  the window, and Chrome's scroll anchoring kept its anchor on a node
  inside it, a node each redraw removes; the page moved as it went.
  Measured in a headless Chromium over a real arbiter with six file
  rules: at 390×844 a label or sending choice in the fourth rule, near
  the window's bottom, moved the page up 360px at once (400px with a
  change already waiting), and the menu, which keeps the focus, ended
  below the window (its top at 1152-1228 in an 844px window). 1280×800
  held. Bisected with `overflow-anchor: none` on one box at a time: on
  the tree, its card or the whole page the page holds; on the bar or the
  other cards it still moves. Now app.css takes the tree, and nothing
  else, out of anchoring (`.files-tree { overflow-anchor: none }`, which
  leaves out its whole subtree): the page holds still, and the bar's room

  at 553-587 (bar 596); with a change already waiting, 368-402 (bar 410).
  - Measured the same before and after: every 1280×800 case; ⋯, which
    scrolls its opened row into view itself; the menus of Add a rule's
    browser, a box that scrolls on its own; Sending data's list, also
    drawn again after its answer, where the anchor keeps its menu in
    place (so it stays anchored); the Tab survey above (no stop hidden).
  - The cost: an anchor in the tree never outlived a redraw anyway, but
    between redraws content that changes height above the window (Add a
    rule's list arriving) no longer holds the tree's rows in place; Chrome
    anchors to what follows the tree when that is in view, else to
    nothing, as a browser without anchoring does.

  Presentation only: no route, rule, Save or focus rule changed. Tests:
  `home-js-tree-anchor.test.ts` (the one rule, and each choice drawn again

- **Changes stay one change**: everything queues into §4.25m's pending list,

#### 4.25o The integrity levels are frozen

The integrity axis is frozen ([`protection-modes.md §10`](../architecture/protection-modes.md)).
`POST /api/config/axes` answers 403 `{frozen: true}` to any write that leaves
integrity on unless the dashboard runs with `MANDU_EXPERIMENTAL_INTEGRITY=1`
(`GET` reports `integrityAllowed`); `secrets`, `off` and `integrity: false`
always pass. The product page has no switch for it (Settings' one on/off is
the confidentiality axis, and turns a leftover integrity axis off unless the
opt-in is set), and the `/dev/` Protection drawer offers only `secrets` and
`off`.

#### 4.25p Files and folders: one label menu per row

**2026-10-11: two questions, two menus.** A label is a set of places the
real bytes may go, `Release(d) = Models(level) ∪ Bindings ∪ {human, local
storage}` (confidentiality plan 13 §4.2), and the one menu showed only its
model half: a rule with no hosts said nothing about sending. Every row now
answers both questions, under heads that name them (`.files-heads`, "Which
AI may read it" and "Where it may be sent"; on a phone, where the heads
are hidden and the menus stack under the name, each menu's cell carries the
same words as a caption, `questionCells` / `.q-cap`):

- **The first menu** is the level, as below (No AI, Your own AI only, Any
  AI, when it asks, Not secret; §4.25d). A model outside it is a hard deny
  no approval changes, which its glossary sentence says.
- **The second menu** (`sendPick`, `select.send-select` in a `.label-pick`
  whose dot is red, amber or green by `data-send`) is the bindings: *Needs
  your OK* (no hosts: the default, now said on every row), *Listed hosts
  without asking* (its hosts as chips under it with Edit, which opens the
  row with the hosts field; choosing it does too, and Update queues them)
  and *Not secret*. Not secret is the lattice's one point where both
  halves are open, so it is the same choice in both menus; leaving it from
  the second menu keeps the AI's answer it had (Any AI, when it asks) and
  changes only where the value may go. *Needs your OK* on a row with hosts
  queues the same level with none, and on the rule as it stands drops the
  change. It is not "nowhere without asking": an Always-allow answer or a
  rule an administrator locked may still send it (the 2026-10-07 note in
  §4.25d), so the glossary's *Listed hosts without asking* entry ends
  "Any other send still needs a rule or your OK", and adds that a program
  that read two secrets may send only where both may go (the join is
  intersection, plan 13 Figure 3). A row with no label of its own shows the
  inherited choice greyed ("(inherited)"), disabled: a label starts in the
  first menu.
- **Per value** (2026-10-11, confidentiality plan 13 §5.2). A rule with
  `values:` binds each value of the file on its own, so neither *Needs your
  OK* nor one row of host chips would be true of it. Its second menu then
  holds one state, *Per value* (`perValuePick`, `data-send="values"`, an
  amber dot), disabled, and under it the sentence of plan 13 §5.3 in
  `.file-values` (`rule-words.ts` `perValueWords`, carried as `plain.send`
  on the rule and `send` on a browser entry's label, and as parts beside
  them, `sendParts`, each key and host a code: §4.25u *Rules names each
  host*): "STRIPE_KEY may be
  sent only to api.stripe.com; AWS_* only to amazonaws.com; a program
  holding the whole file may send it nowhere without asking." A value with
  no entry is named only when the file has hosts of its own ("any other
  value only to …"). Read only because another choice would have to
  rewrite the per-value hosts, which only policy.yaml says; the first menu
  still changes the level, and the save keeps `values:` (`lock-path` keeps
  it, at every level), so nothing is dropped silently. *Not secret* has
  nothing to send per value, so the second menu says Not secret then. The
  glossary gains *Per value*.
- **Opens it**, read only, under a rule's name: the third relation
  (Openers, plan 13 §4.2) as the server words it (`rule-words.ts`
  `opensWords`, carried as `plain.opens` on each file rule of
  `yourRules`): "ssh (checked by Mandu)" for a vetted reader, "deploy (your
  word)" for an entry with `prints: nothing`, "psql never gets the real
  file: it prints or runs what it reads" for one that admits nothing, then
  whether other programs get a masked copy or are refused; "Programs get a
  masked copy." with no `readers:`. Adding a reader stays a loosening made
  in policy.yaml and confirmed in Approvals.

Both menus queue into Changes to save; the save route's own preview decides
what loosens (a host added, a level lowered) and asks before it is written.
Tests: `home-js-explorer.test.ts` ("§4.25p two questions", "§4.25p per
value"), `per-value-words.test.ts`, the
`policy-panel.test.ts` Opens-it test, and `tests/stack/rules-two-questions.test.ts`
(the three choices through the save route over a real arbiter, and the
egress gate's answer for the file's key at its host before and after).

**The name keeps its room (2026-10-15; app.css).** Three lists draw file
rows: Your rules (`#files-tree`, `.row.file-rule`), Add a rule's browser
(`#files-list`, `.row.file`) and Keys Mandu found (`#files-suggested-list`,
`.row.file`). Each row is a grid of the name and the two menus, which have
fixed columns (220 px and 250 px; 240 and 230 since 2026-10-17, *A menu
says its words whole* below). The menus went under the name only at
720 px and below, so above that width the name got whatever was left.
A headless Chromium measured the name column of Your rules at 41 px in a
721 px window, 77 px at 760, 114 px at 800 and 188 px at 880. A rule
nested in a folder loses 24 px more per level. The browser was worse,
because its list sits in the padded Add a rule panel and its rows have the
tick box: 0 px at 721 (an entry 372 px tall), 32 px at 800 and 216 px at
1000. Names and their *Opens it* line were drawn one or two letters per
line (`.env`, `**/*.pem every matching file`), and words such as
`deploy/staging.conf` and `docker-compose` broke in the middle. Such a
window is common: half of a 1440 or 1920 px screen, or a tablet held

Now every file row of the three lists keeps the narrow layout up to
1000 px: the name on its own line, then each menu under it with its caption
(`.q-cap`), and the heads hidden (from 801 px the two menus side by side:
*The middle layout* below). The opened row goes to one column with
it. From 1001 px the columns come back, and the name has at least 200 px in
every list: the browser's, the tightest, gets 217 px at 1001 px, or 203 px
with a 15 px classic scrollbar. 200 px fits a 19-character name two folders
deep on one line. The menus are drawn at their own width in the narrow
layout, so "Your own AI only (none listed)" is no longer cut there. The
other rows of Rules (*Sending data*, `.row.rule`) have at least 228 px down
to 721 px, so they keep the 720 px rule, as does the ticked bar's grid of
buttons. One width rule covers all three lists, so the browser and Your
rules never show the same rows in two layouts at once. A container query
would follow each list's own width, but no stylesheet here uses one yet.

Sighted readers between 721 and 1000 px see the phone's layout: rows two or
three lines taller, every name readable. Presentation only: no script,
route, gate or server text changed. Tests: `css-files-name-room.test.ts`.

**The middle layout (2026-10-15, later; app.css).** Stacked, a rule in a
window up to 1000 px was about 2.5 times as tall as beside the name. A
headless Chromium measured six rules of Your rules at 1298 px in an 860 px
window and 506 px at 1001 px. Each menu took a line of its own while a

225 px against 357 for the browser's two entries. No menu is cut from 721
to 1000 px.

Why 800 and not 720: each menu's column is at least as wide as the wide
layout gives a menu beside the name (220 and 250 px then, 240 and 230 now;
both columns are alike, so both get 250 px). So the middle layout cuts no
menu that the wide layout draws whole. "Your own AI only (none listed)" is
238 px, and the wide layout cut it at 220 until 2026-10-17 (*A menu says
its words whole*, next). The browser's columns, in the padded Add a rule
panel and beside the tick box, are the tightest: 257.5 px at 801 px, and
220.6 px at 721, where "Listed hosts without asking" (221 px) would be cut.

"Your rules" hard to follow. Every row (a rule in the tree, an entry of the
browser, a typed path or pattern) now has ONE label menu (`labelPick`: a
`select.label-select` in a `.label-pick` with a coloured dot): the four
labels in the glossary's order (`LEVEL_BUTTONS`, each option's tooltip the
glossary's term and sentence), preceded by "Remove my rule" on a rule of the
person's own, else "No rule", or "<label> (inherited)" when a read gets a
label from elsewhere (the dot is then a ring in that label's colour, the
origin under the name). The menu shows the change waiting, else the
person's own rule; a waiting choice is dashed. Choosing queues the label as
the dot did, choosing what the person's own rule says drops the change, and
"Remove my rule" queues the removal. "Your own model only (none listed)" is
disabled until a model of your own is declared; a rule set in the rules file
has its menu disabled. Hosts show as chips only when there are some (Edit),
added under ⋯. The ⋯ replaces the chevron. A menu keeps its own arrow keys
(the row keys skip it). Narrow (up to 1000 px since 2026-10-15, *The name
keeps its room* above): the menu and hosts go under the name, the two menus
side by side from 801 px (*The middle layout*). A
suggestion's row shows its label as a chip; its tick saves or skips it. The
design below is the columns' and is superseded where it says otherwise.

**Design (`home.js`, "The label columns", retired).** There are only four labels, in a
fixed order from strictest to loosest, so each was a column of the explorer's
list and a set of rules read down a column.

- **Columns** in the glossary's order (`LEVEL_BUTTONS`): Hidden from the AI,
  Your own model only, The AI may read it, Not secret, then **May still be sent
  to**. A header (`files-cols`) names them with icon and colour stripe; the
  tooltip is the glossary's term and sentence (checked by
  `policy-panel.test.ts`).
- **One dot per label on every row** (`level-dot`, a button named by its
  label, `aria-pressed` on the one in force). **Solid**: a rule of the person's
  own on exactly that target. **Ring** (`from`): the label a read gets from
  elsewhere (a folder, a pattern, a built-in secret, a model key, a written
  file), the origin in the tooltip. An ordinary file has no dot marked (empty
  dots show on hover).
- **A click on a dot queues that label** into §4.25m's pending list; the new
  dot is circled (`waiting`), the replaced one dashed (`was`). Clicking the dot
  the person's own rule already sets, with the same hosts, drops the waiting
  change. A secret label starts from the hosts in force or waiting.
- **Hosts** show as chips with **Edit** / **Add**, which opens the row with
  the hosts field focused; **Update** (or Enter) queues the same label with the
  new hosts. A label from elsewhere shows its hosts greyed.
- **A row that opens in place** (`file-detail`, one at a time): path, the
  label in words and its source, the change waiting, the hosts field, notes
  (set in the rules file; a folder covers what is inside; a link covers its
  file), Remove my rule, the local-model warning (§4.25l), where it is kept,
  the origin line (§4.25i), the use count, Show in policy.yaml (§4.25g), Show
  in its folder, and Why (§4.25m).
- **Ticked rows** (All files) get a bar (`files-selected`): one button per
  label, the hosts field, Remove my rules where every ticked item has a rule
  of yours, and Clear.
- **Your own model only** is greyed with "Add one in Settings" until a model
  of your own is declared; its dots are off. **Rules set in policy.yaml**
  show a "Set in policy.yaml" tag and greyed dots.
- **Narrow (≤ 720px)**: no header; each row puts its four labels under the
  name as named buttons.

**Tests.** `home-js-files.test.ts`, `home-js-explorer.test.ts`,
`home-js-models.test.ts` (the menu's options and order, a choice queueing
and shown waiting, the label it replaces named in Changes to save, the label
in force dropping it, inherited labels, hosts Edit/Update/Enter, the ticked
bar, the opened row, the own-model choice on and off, arrow keys staying in
the menu, folds kept); `two-front-ends.test.ts` (over a real arbiter and
server, a policy.yaml local-model rule chosen in its menu, the choice on or
off by the declared models).

#### 4.25q Home page: where your data lives

**What the page shows.** A collapsed "Where your data lives" `<details>`, the
last section of Home (on-disk-layout.md §9): fetched when opened, each
location Mandu keeps files in (the data `mandu paths` prints), what it holds
in plain words, and whether it exists. Each store in the home carries an
"only you" or "open to others" badge (a dangling symlink: "broken link"), and
a note says so when any store is open to others (fixing modes is `mandu paths`
/ `mandu doctor`'s job, not the page's).

**Developer-only places (2026-10-19).** Sixteen rows of the path table are
places only Mandu's own developers use (test stores, run results, CI caches,
`dev-root`: `DEVELOPER_LOCATIONS` in `src/data-locations.ts`). On a user's
machine none exist, so the page leaves out each one that is not there; one
that is there (a developer's machine) is listed after the rest of Mandu's
folder under its own `.data-where-group` line, "For Mandu's developers",
before "Outside Mandu's folder", and keeps its badge. The open-places note
still counts every place that is there, developer stores included (a
developer store with loose modes, such as `docker-e2e-home`, which holds
logins, is still reported; a place that is not there has no mode to warn
about). The intro says the terminal has the full list: "To see every place,
including the ones only Mandu's developers use, run `mandu paths`." Rows from
an older server, without the field, are drawn as before. `mandu paths`
itself is unchanged.

**The projection.** `GET /api/data-locations` (`src/data-locations.ts`), GET
only, behind the same source-IP gate, auth and session as every product route,
the same for every tenant:

```
{ home: "~/.mandu",
  locations: [{ name, path, where: "home" | "outside", holds, developer,
                exists, brokenLink, mode: "0700" | null,
                ownerOnly: true | false | null }] }
```

- The rows are `mandu paths`' rows in the path table's order
  (on-disk-layout.md §5); `path` is `~`-abbreviated; `holds` mirrors
  `launcher/src/paths-command.ts`' description verbatim (mirrored, not
  imported: the dashboard is a standalone package).
- `ownerOnly` is set for the stores the agent may not read
  (`agentReadable: false`); `null` for the runtime dir, the install, the bin
  dir, and a location with no mode.
- **Only locations, never content.** Each path is `stat`ed (following a
  symlink) and never opened or listed, so no byte of a store reaches the
  response.
- A dangling symlink is `exists: true, brokenLink: true` with no mode, as in
  `mandu paths`.
- `developer` is true exactly for `DEVELOPER_LOCATIONS`, whether or not the
  place is there; the page, not the projection, leaves out the ones that are
  not there. A unit test fails when a description that says "(developers)"
  or "Mandu's own tests" names a place outside the set, or the set names
  another, so a new developer path cannot slip onto the product page.

**Tests.** `dashboard/test/unit/data-locations.test.ts` (rows, modes and
`ownerOnly`, a relocated home, symlinks, parity with `paths-command.ts`'
descriptions, the product vocabulary, `developer` and its drift guard);
`dashboard/test/component/data-locations.test.ts` (the route over a real
server, a developer place there and one absent);
`dashboard/test/unit/ui/home-js-home.test.ts` (the section: developer places
hidden or grouped, counted in the note, an older server's rows).

#### 4.25r Keys Mandu found (was: the Suggested view)

**2026-10-05:** no longer a third view of the explorer but a card of its own
on the Rules page, **Keys Mandu found** (`#suggested-block`), with its count,
one line on where the keys were found, and Review / Close
(`#suggest-open`); the scan bar, its "More" fold, the model picker and the
rows are inside. Its rows show the label as a chip, not dots. Opening it is
what makes ticked suggestions wait in Changes to save (`G.shown`), as before;
the Approvals card opens it, and so does Settings › Sensitivity labels' note
(§4.25s). The CLI's pointers say "Keys Mandu found".

**Status: LANDED.** The dashboard half of
[`confidentiality-plan-14-policy-suggestions.md`](../confidentiality/confidentiality-plan-14-policy-suggestions.md)
§5.4: the arbiter's policy suggestions (keys Mandu's scans found that no rule
covers, filed as `kind: "suggestion"` proposals, plan 14 §5.6) are reviewed
in the file explorer of §4.25n/§4.25p, not on a page of their own. Every
suggestion only adds protection.

**The view (`home.js`, "Suggested: keys Mandu's scan found").**

- *A third view,* **Suggested**, beside Labeled and All files, with a count
  badge. It holds **Scan for keys**, an optional folder field, **Also look
  in your home folder**, and a status line ("Scanning ~/proj… This can take
  a minute.", then the scan's summary).
- *Rows in the label columns* (the four label dots of §4.25p). A
  `lock-path` suggestion is a row on its path; a path that exists only in
  git history is greyed and tagged "only in git history". A `lock-blob`
  suggestion is a sub-row ("1 old version of config.py") under the file as
  it is now.
- *Pending as if clicked.* Once the view is opened, each applicable
  suggestion waits in Changes to save, ticked, with its "Hidden from the AI"
  dot pressed as a waiting change; the other dots are off. Unticking or
  Skip skips it (kept in this browser, `mandu.files.skipped`). A suggestion
  the arbiter marks `applicable: false` cannot be ticked and says why.
- *One Save* sends the ticked suggestions (`POST /api/suggestions/apply
  {ids}`), then any other waiting change through the usual `files/labels`
  flow. Each suggestion becomes its own change in History
  (`resolvePolicyProposal`). The arbiter applies one only as a pure
  tightening of the law in force, so the weaker-change question never fires;
  a suggestion the law moved under comes back in `refused` with the
  arbiter's reason and stays waiting. Each row states its own impact ("Hides
  2 old versions in git history from the AI. No file you have now
  changes."). On macOS a history row adds "on Linux" and
  "On macOS the committed versions stay readable to the AI."
  (`suggestionRows.platform`, plan 14 §11.3); a workspace row is unchanged.
- *The opened row* (§4.25p): the rule in the arbiter's words, the other
  paths the same key had, what Save changes, advice to replace an exposed
  key, **Show in policy.yaml** (the `paths:` or `blobs:` lines Save adds),
  **Not a secret**, and "What the scan found": each detector in plain words
  with the scan's fixed mask, and when ("Added in a1b2c3d, removed in
  e4f5a6b"). Its buttons name the row (by its path where another row has
  the same name: §4.25 *Keys in files of the same name are named apart*),
  and the card keeps the keyboard focus through its redraws (§4.25 *Keys
  Mandu found keeps the focus*).
- *Not a secret* asks first, then `POST /api/suggestions/dismiss {id}`: the
  arbiter denies it and never files that finding again.
- *The Inbox card* ("Keys Mandu found", with where: "in this
  project's git history", "in the files of 2 projects", "in your home
  folder") opens the Suggested view. Card, badge and view follow the page's
  10-second poll (every 3 s while a scan runs), which also covers a scan or
  dismissal made from the terminal. A read asked before a change made on
  the card answered never draws over that change's list (§4.25 *A read
  asked before a change never draws over it*).

**Sources.** The same row shape serves every source the arbiter files
(`SuggestionRowVM.source`):

- *Git history* (above): greyed history-only rows and blob sub-rows.
- *Workspace scan* (`source: "workspace"`, plan 14 §13.6): a file whose
  current content holds a key the catalog and labels miss. An ordinary row;
  "What the scan found" gives each detector, its mask and its line; the note
  "Found in the file as it is now, on this computer."; the impact "Hides
  this file from the AI from the next time an agent starts."; and softer
  advice ("If an AI session read this file before, rotate the key"), since
  nothing shows the key left the machine.
- *Sensitivity labels* (`source: "sensitivity-label"`, plan 14 §14.1): an
  Office document whose Purview/MIP label a mapping (§4.25s) gives a level.
  Its dot is the mapped level (`SuggestionRowVM.level`); "From the
  document's sensitivity label"; "What the scan found" is the label and the
  mapping's name, never a word from the document; no rotation advice. A
  level below "hidden from the AI" is a `humanOnly` suggestion, which Save
  applies on the admin channel like any other. A note says a label lowered
  later in Office does not lower the rule (`LABEL_NOTE`).
- *A model's suggestion* (§4.25t): `model-names` ("Your model saw only file
  and folder names, never what the files hold.") or `model-contents` ("Your
  own model read the start of this file (at most 16 KB). Nothing of it went
  to an outside model."), with the reason in the arbiter's words and no
  rotation advice. The run leaves one `policy_model_call` event (counts
  only) on the arbiter-admin stream.

**Scan for keys** runs the history and workspace scans and sends
`countLabels: true` (an explicit scan counts documents' labels even while
no mapping is in force; a launch never does). The summary (`scanSummary`)
names both scans ("Scanned the git history of ~/proj and 1,204 files in
~/proj and your home folder. 2 possible keys to review."), names a folder
that could not be scanned with a plain reason, says what a cap left
unchecked from the `capped` counts and `limits` (never the arbiter's
`capped.lines`, which name environment variables), and adds the label
sentences ("12 files carry a sensitivity label you have not chosen a level
for…", the encrypted documents, and what the label read left unchecked,
below).

**The line counts what it read and links where a level is set**
(2026-10-08). The arbiter never reads an Office file as text. Its label
read opens the file under its own budgets and counts it apart, in
`workspaceScan.labels` (`read`, `cached`, `covered`), and the line counted
only the text reads. So a scan of a folder of labelled documents read
"Scanned 0 files in ~/docs. … 1 file carries a sensitivity label you have
not chosen a level for: set it in Settings, Sensitivity labels.", and a
document a rule covers was never said to be left closed. The place it
named was plain text. Now:

- "Scanned N files" adds the documents whose labels it read (`labels.read
  + labels.cached`), and "N files your rules already protect were not
  opened" adds the documents it left closed (`labels.covered`). Both apply
  only when the label read ran (its `mode` is not `off`). The walk visits
  a path once, so nothing is counted twice. That folder now reads
  "Scanned 1 file in ~/docs.".
- `scanSummaryParts` sends the line as the hero's link parts (§4.25 *The
  hero links where it points*), and `scanSummary` is the parts joined. The
  label sentence's **Settings › Sensitivity labels** is a link part naming
  the place `labels`, never an address. The scan state keeps both
  (`ScanStateVM.summary`, `summaryParts`; null while a scan runs), in the
  scan answer and in `GET /api/suggestions`.
- `home.js scanStatus` draws the parts (`textParts`). `placeLink` builds
  `<a href="/settings">` for `labels`, and its plain click runs
  `openLabels()`: Settings, scrolled to the Sensitivity labels card
  (`#settings-labels-block`), where the label waits with its level
  picker. A modifier click is left to the browser. A line without parts
  (an older server) is its text, and a place the page does not know is
  text.

The page opens Settings at that card once it has drawn (*A link opens at
its card*, below). Tests: `sensitivity-labels-view-model.test.ts` (the counts with
read, cached and covered documents and with no label read; the one link
part; no link with nothing to set), `sensitivity-label-routes.test.ts`
(the parts in the scan answer and the listing), `home-js-suggested.test.ts`
(the link, a plain and a modifier click, a line without parts, an unknown
place), and across the real arbiter
`tests/stack/rules-scan-labels-line.test.ts`: a real scan of a folder with
a text file, a labelled document and a covered one ("Scanned 2 files", "1
file your rules already protect was not opened"). The served Rules link
opens Settings with the label listed, and neither the registered key, a
document's text nor a token is in any answer or page.

**A link opens at its card** (2026-10-08). Three links open another page
at one of its cards: Settings › Sensitivity labels' note (**Keys Mandu
found**, §4.25s) and Approvals' **Review them** open Rules at Keys Mandu
found (`openSuggested`), and the line under Scan for keys (**Settings,
Sensitivity labels**) opens Settings at that card (`openLabels`). Each
scrolled at the click, before the page's reads answered, and what they
drew above the card then pushed it down. With ten rules, Keys Mandu found
went from 512 px to 997 px below the top of a 900 px window, off the
screen, which showed Your rules and no Scan for keys. Sensitivity labels
settled 198 px down under Protection and Models (the shortfall this
section used to record). Now:

- `setPage` returns the reads of Rules and Settings, done once drawn.
  Rules' reads are `loadRules()` and, on the first read with Add a rule
  left open, the folder it opens with (`F.listing`). Settings' are every
  card (`loadSettings` waits for Protection, Models, Sensitivity labels,
  Prompt filters and the service row).
- `home.js openAtCard(page, id)` opens the page and scrolls the card to
  the top once those reads have drawn. A read that fails still scrolls
  (the card says what it could not read). If the person scrolls, presses
  a key or taps (`wheel`, `touchmove`, `keydown`, `pointerdown`) before
  then, or opens another page, the scroll is theirs and nothing moves.
- In a browser at 1280 px both cards now land at the top. Keys Mandu
  found stops 248 px down when the page ends below it, in view with
  Scan for keys.

Presentation only: the reads and what they draw are unchanged. Tests:
`home-js-open-at-card.test.ts` (each link with its reads held open: no
scroll before they answer, one after; Add a rule's folder; a scroll, key,
tap or another page first; a failed read) and across the real arbiter
`tests/stack/open-at-card.test.ts` (six rules in policy.yaml, a real
scan, the three served links, each scroll recorded with what the page had
drawn, and the no-value/no-token oracle); `rules-scan-labels-line.test.ts`
S2 records its scroll after Models and the label are drawn.

**Section links** (2026-10-18). Rules is the product page's longest page.
At 1280 px it was 2,938 px tall with eight rules, so *Who may get your
secrets* and *Keys Mandu found* started two screens down. Settings has
five cards. Neither page had in-page navigation, and no card had an
address: `parseRoute` read no hash, so the links above scrolled by script
and, opened in a new tab, landed at the top. The inspector had both (its
sub-menu and `#<key>` address, §4.34). Now:

- **A row under the title.** One plain link per card, from home.js
  `SECTIONS` (`drawSectionLinks`). Rules: *Describe · Your rules · Who
  may get your secrets · Keys Mandu found · Built-in protections*.
  Settings: *Protection · Models · Sensitivity labels · Prompt filters ·
  Notifications · Appearance* (*Appearance* since 2026-10-18). The developer-only *Developer view* card has none. The
  row wraps on a phone, a "·" ending a line rather than starting the
  next. It stays in the page's flow and never sticks, so it never covers
  the focus.
- **An address per card.** `/rules#describe`, `#your-rules`, `#who`,
  `#keys-found`, `#built-in`; `/settings#protection`, `#models`,
  `#sensitivity-labels`, `#prompt-filters`, `#notifications`,
  `#appearance`. The keys
  are not element ids, so the browser's own jump to a fragment does
  nothing and the page decides. `parseRoute` reads a key only on its own
  page. Any other hash opens the page at its top, and `setPage`'s
  canonical `replaceState` removes it from the address.
- **A click** scrolls the card to the top and gives its heading the
  focus. It writes the key into the address with `replaceState`: no new
  history entry, because a pushed one would make Back reload the page
  (`popstate` → `setPage`). Back still leaves the page. A modifier click
  is left to the browser, and the `href` carries the key, so a new tab
  opens at the card. If the card is hidden (*Who may get your secrets*
  before the rules are read), the page stays where it is.
- **Opening an address with a key** (a typed address, a new tab, a
  reload, Back or Forward) lands on that card as a link does
  (`landAtSection` → `landAtCard`, the code `openAtCard` now shares). It
  waits for the page's reads and, on the first load, for Home's first
  read too, which draws *Built-in protections* and the top bar. In a
  headless Chromium over a real arbiter, landing before that read left
  `/rules#who` 117 px down: the page grew under it after the scroll. The
  focus goes from the page's heading to the card's heading. The person's
  own scroll, key or tap before then wins, as in *A link opens at its
  card*.
- **The links that open a card** write its address too. `openAtCard`
  replaces the address with the card's key. *Keys Mandu found* (the note
  under Sensitivity labels) and *Settings › Sensitivity labels* (the line
  under Scan for keys) carry the key in their `href`, so a modifier
  click opens the right card in the new tab instead of the page's top.
  A nav link to Rules or Settings opens the page at its top, with no key.

Presentation only: no route, read or server text changed. Tests:
`home-js-section-links.test.ts` (each link names its card, in order; a
click scrolls, focuses and replaces the address; a modifier click; an
address with a key lands once the page and Home's first read have drawn;
an unknown key or another page's key; `openAtCard` writes the key, a nav
link none, Back lands again), `home-js-routes.test.ts` (`parseRoute`'s
`section`), the two `href`s in `home-js-labels.test.ts` and
`home-js-suggested.test.ts`. Across the real arbiter,
`tests/stack/section-links.test.ts` uses a real headless Chromium (the
DevTools plumbing of `scripts/tour-screenshots.mjs`; self-SKIP without a
browser). `/rules#who` and `/settings#prompt-filters` at 1280×800 and
390×844 open with the card's heading focused and in view, the card at the
top or the page at its end. The row is static, five links inside the
page's width, and no page carries the registered key or a token.

**The line says which documents the label read left unchecked**
(2026-10-08). The label read has its own budgets (`labels.limits`: 2,000
documents, 32 MB read in all) and its own gaps, apart from the text read's
`capped`: `labels.capped.overFiles` (documents past its file cap, never
looked at), `labels.capped.overBytes` (past its byte budget, some cut off
mid-read) and `labels.unreadable` (not an Office file it can read: Zip64,
multi-disk, malformed). The arbiter names them for the terminal
(`capped.lines`), and the line left them out, so a folder of 3,000
documents could read "1 file carries a sensitivity label …" with no word that a
thousand were never looked at. Now `labelGapWords` ends the label
sentences, after the encrypted one: "Not checked for a sensitivity label:
2 documents past the 2,000 it looks at, 1 document past the 32 MB it reads
in all and 1 document it could not read." The numbers come from
`labels.limits`; an answer without them (an older arbiter) says "past its
file limit" / "past its size limit", never a number it does not know. It
adds no link, and nothing when the label read did not run. Tests:
`sensitivity-labels-view-model.test.ts` (each gap alone and together,
singular and plural, with and without `limits`, its place on the full
line, the vocabulary sweep), and across the real arbiter
`tests/stack/rules-scan-labels-line.test.ts` (S4: the label read's file
cap lowered to 2 over a malformed `.docx` and three labelled documents; the
scan answer, the listing and the served Rules page end with "Not checked
for a sensitivity label: 2 documents past the 2 it looks at and 1 document
it could not read."; the same oracle). Settings › Sensitivity labels ends
its note with the same sentences (§4.25s *The note says what the scan left
unchecked*).

**Server (`src/server/suggestion-routes.ts`, rows from
`src/view-model/suggestions.ts`).**

    GET  /api/suggestions              {suggestions: SuggestionRowVM[], count, scan}
    POST /api/suggestions/scan {root?, includeHome?} {scan, suggestions, count}
    POST /api/suggestions/apply {ids}  {applied: [{id, changeId}], refused: [{id, error}], suggestions, count}
    POST /api/suggestions/dismiss {id} {dismissed, status, suggestions, count}

- *Gates.* The GET names paths where keys were found, and a GET is open to
  any same-host process, the agent's included, so it is served only with
  the CSRF header and the admin session (like the file browser's listing,
  §4.25m). The POSTs sit behind the global mutating gate. Apply and Not a
  secret ride the arbiter's admin channel (`resolvePolicyProposal`,
  `dismissSuggestion`); an adopted arbiter answers 503 and nothing changes.
- *Which folders a scan reads.* A folder the person typed (absolute or
  `~`), else the folders recorded live sessions worked in (each session's
  `cwd`, newest first, no time window: a project from last month still holds
  its history; `home-routes.ts recentWorkspaces`), at most eight
  (`SCAN_ROOTS_MAX`). With neither and no home-folder request, the route
  answers 400 `{needsRoot}` and the page asks for a folder. The dashboard
  keeps no workspace list of its own. `includeHome` must be a boolean and
  HOME absolute, checked before the arbiter is called.
- *A scan in flight.* The route waits at most `SCAN_WAIT_MS` (20 s); a scan
  still running continues, the route answers `scan.running`, and the GET
  reports the summary when it ends. A second Scan meanwhile starts nothing;
  a scan started elsewhere is named as such.
- *Apply.* At most 50 distinct ids, each looked up among the pending
  suggestions; one no longer waiting or not applicable is refused without
  an arbiter call.
- *What is served.* Paths, commit ids, the detectors' plain words and fixed
  masks. The scan reads file contents only in the arbiter; no response
  carries a value.

**Adapter.** `arbiter-adapter.ts` forwards `suggestPolicy` and
`policySuggestions` on the data socket, and `dismissSuggestion` and
`resolvePolicyProposal` on the admin channel.

**Tests.** `test/unit/view-model/suggestions-view-model.test.ts`,
`sensitivity-labels-view-model.test.ts` (rows per source, words, impact,
policy.yaml lines, summaries; every string through the product vocabulary
sweep), `test/unit/server/suggestion-routes.test.ts` (over a real
DashboardServer: every route refused without CSRF or the admin session, the
folder rules, "still scanning", apply refusals and validation, dismiss and
a second dismiss 409, the adopted arbiter 503),
`test/unit/ui/home-js-suggested.test.ts` and `home-js-labels.test.ts`
(jsdom). The e2e is `tests/stack/dashboard-suggestions.test.ts`
(`secrets`): the production adapter over a real arbiter, a fixture
repository with keys committed and deleted and a key in a current file;
the gates; a scan filing them; one Save putting the `lock-path` and
`lock-blob` in the law; Not a secret refused by an adopted arbiter; a
rescan filing nothing; and no response body holding a secret or any

#### 4.25s Settings: Sensitivity labels

**Status: LANDED.** The dashboard half of plan 14 §14.1: policy.yaml
`sensitivity_labels: [{id, site?, name, level}]` maps a Purview label's
GUID (optionally its tenant's) to the level Mandu's scan suggests for every
document carrying it. It changes what is suggested, never what is
protected now. Beside Settings › Models (§4.25l), on the same pattern.

**The section (`home.js loadLabels`).**

- *Your mappings*: name, GUID, a level picker, **Save** and **Remove**.
- *Your administrator's* (`/etc/mandu/policy.d`): shown with "Set by your
  administrator." and no buttons. The arbiter merges both by (id, site),
  the stricter level winning, so a user entry can only add or raise.
- *Labels with no level yet*: each GUID the dashboard's last Scan for keys
  found that no mapping names, with its file count, a name box and a level
  picker defaulting to "Secret, hidden from the AI", plus the hint of
  confidentiality.md §3 (a label your organization lets cloud AI read is
  usually "Secret, the AI may read it"). Mandu reads no tenant policy, so
  the person picks.
- *Save* shows the result with Undo. A change that lowers what is suggested
  (Remove, a lower level, a new "Not secret" mapping; the arbiter's
  `sensitivity-labels` delta facet) is asked about first with the Models
  question (`modelConfirmText`).
- **A change names the label as it was read** (2026-10-18). Each row
  carries its mapping's version (`version`: the listing's `itemVersions`,
  an opaque keyed hash; a label with no level yet the `absentVersion`; an
  administrator's row none; policy-surface.md §8.4.6 "An item-level
  version"), and Save and Remove send it, required (400 without). The route
  refuses at once, before asking, a version its own read finds moved, and
  sends the arbiter `basedOn` with the mapping (`sensitivity-labels`,
  `id|site`); the arbiter refuses the write once it changed. Either way the
  answer is 409 `{ stale: true, changed }` and nothing is written. Until
  then a level set somewhere else between the page's read and Save (another
  window, a hand edit) was put back to what the row was filled from; a
  change to another label never refuses it. The row says "*Highly
  Confidential* was changed somewhere else just now, so nothing was saved.
  The level you picked is still on the row: compare it with *Highly
  Confidential* as it is now, then save again." (Remove: "… so nothing was
  removed. It is shown as it is now: look at it, then remove it again if
  you still want to."), the list is read again (`labelStaleReread`), and the
  rebuilt row keeps the level picked and the name typed, so its next Save
  names the mapping as it is now; a label gone from the list says so where
  the notice goes. An arbiter that sends no versions gets no change (501).

**A row's controls fit it** (2026-10-08). A label row and a prompt filter
row (§4.25y) end in a cell of controls: the level picker with **Save** and
**Remove**; the name box, the picker and **Save**; a kind's choice with
**Use the default**. Until then that cell was the plain service row's
120 px third column with no layout of its own, since only Models laid out
its `model-actions`. In a browser the picker read "Secret, hidden from th"
past the row's border, Save and Remove stacked, every prompt filter choice
lost its arrow, and the hint under a label with no level filled the 180 px
name column. Now (`app.css`):

- the two rows' third column fits its controls, up to half the row
  (`fit-content(50%)`), and the name and who-set-it columns take the rest;
- the controls cell is a wrapping flex row in every Settings service row,
  Models' included; the name box is as tall as the picker beside it;
- "Set by your administrator.", the hint under a label with no level, and a
  refusal span the row, in the small grey text Models uses;
- on a narrow screen (≤ 760 px) the rows stack as every row does, the
  controls on the left. That includes Models', which used to sit right.

**The note links where Scan for keys is** (2026-10-08). One line closes
the list when there is something to say about the last scan. Until then,
before any scan it read "Press Scan for keys in Rules, Keys Mandu found,
to look for them." with no link, and Rules shows that button only once
Keys Mandu found is opened (§4.25r, **Review**). After a scan that found
no document with a label, it read "Every sensitivity label the last scan
found has a level." over an empty list: a claim about labels the scan
never found. Now `labelSettingsVM` sends the note as `noteParts`, the
hero's link parts (§4.25 *The hero links where it points*), and `note`
stays the parts joined:

- before any scan: "Mandu lists here the sensitivity labels it finds on
  your documents. To look for them, open **Keys Mandu found** in Rules and
  press Scan for keys.";
- after a scan that found no labelled document (the stored scan's
  `files`, the files carrying a label, is 0): "The last scan found no
  sensitivity label on your documents. To look in another folder, open
  **Keys Mandu found** in Rules.";
- once every label the scan found has a level: "Every sensitivity label
  the last scan found has a level." (text only); while one has none, no
  note, unless the scan left documents unchecked (*The note says what the
  scan left unchecked*, below). A stored scan without `files` (an older
  arbiter) reads as before.

The link part names the place `suggested`; `home.js placeLink` builds an
`<a href="/rules">` whose plain click runs `openSuggested()`, as
Approvals' **Review them** does: Rules, with Keys Mandu found open and
scrolled to once Rules has drawn (§4.25r *A link opens at its card*). A modifier click is left to the browser. A page without parts
(an older server) shows `note` as text. The way back is a link too: the
line under Scan for keys names **Settings › Sensitivity labels**, which
opens this card (§4.25r *The line counts what it read and links where a
level is set*).

**The note says what the scan left unchecked** (2026-10-08). Rules' scan
line names the documents the label read never checked (§4.25r *The line
says which documents the label read left unchecked*) and the encrypted
ones whose label is not known. This note never did. So after a scan that
read 2 of 4 documents and could not read one of those, the card said "The
last scan found no sensitivity label on your documents.", and under a label
listed with "2 files carry it" nothing said a third was never looked at.
The stored scan already kept the counts (`lastLabelScan` keeps the whole
label answer), so `labelSettingsVM` now ends the note with the scan line's
own sentences (`suggestions.ts labelUncheckedSentences`: the encrypted
documents, then `labelGapWords`), one source of words for both places:

- found no labelled document: "The last scan found no sensitivity label
  on the documents it checked. Not checked for a sensitivity label: 2
  documents past the 2,000 it looks at and 1 document it could not read.
  To look in another folder, open **Keys Mandu found** in Rules." The claim
  narrows from "your documents" to the ones it checked, and the one link
  stays;
- every label found has a level: "Every sensitivity label the last scan
  found has a level." and the same sentences, text only;
- a label still waits for a level: the sentences alone close the list,
  after the label rows, with no link. Until then there was no note there;
- nothing left unchecked, a label read that opened nothing (`off`), or an
  older stored answer without the counts: the notes as before. Before any
  scan, unchanged.

It adds no link and no count of its own: the numbers are the arbiter's
(`labels.capped`, `labels.unreadable`, `labels.encrypted`, `labels.limits`),
as on the Rules line.

**Server (`src/server/sensitivity-label-routes.ts`).**

    GET  /api/policy/sensitivity-labels          {labels: LabelSettingsVM}
    POST /api/policy/sensitivity-labels/change   {action: "map", id, site?, name, level, expected?}
                                                 {action: "unmap", id, site?, expected?}
      → {applied: false, confirm: true, expected, rows, wouldLet}   (it lowers what is suggested)
      → {applied: true, changeId, note}

- *The listing* (`labelSettingsVM`) is the `policyDocument` op's in-force
  and admin label lists plus the unmapped label ids from this dashboard's
  last scan, and that scan's counts of documents it left unchecked (kept in
  memory per arbiter surface). That source is a
  decision: no new arbiter op; a terminal scan (`mandu policy suggest`)
  lists them there.
- *The change* is planned into the edit grammar
  (`map-sensitivity-label` / `unmap-sensitivity-label`; GUIDs normalized; a
  one-line name of 1–64 characters; one of the four levels; a form mistake
  is a 400 before the arbiter) and applied like Settings › Models:
  preview, refuse a loosening that was not shown, propose on the admin
  channel as `settings`, approve as `human:settings`. A validator refusal is
  a 422, a mapping removed meanwhile a 409.
- *Gates.* The GET needs the CSRF header and the admin session (it reports
  what the last scan found); the POST sits behind the global mutating gate.
- *What is shown.* GUIDs, the names people gave them, levels and file
  counts; never a path, never a word from a document.

**Tests.** `sensitivity-labels-view-model.test.ts`,
`test/unit/server/sensitivity-label-routes.test.ts` (gates, the listing
before and after a scan, map applied at once, unmap asked first, 400, 422,
409), `test/unit/ui/home-js-labels.test.ts`. The row layout:
`test/unit/ui/home-js-settings-rows.test.ts` (every label and prompt filter

`home-js-labels.test.ts` (the link's address, a click that opens Keys
