#### 4.25t Suggested: the model picker and its preview

**Status: LANDED, offered only behind `MANDU_EXPERIMENTAL_POLICY_MODEL=1`**
on the dashboard server. The dashboard half of plan 14 §14.5 (§14.10 names
only, §14.11 contents). Under Scan for keys:

- *The picker* "Ask a model too": **Off** (the default, never remembered),
  **Names only** (a model reads file and folder names, never contents), or
  **Contents (your own model)** (a model declared `local: true` reads the
  start of the documents the rules leave unprotected, including the text
  Mandu extracts from Word, Excel and PowerPoint files). Without the flag
  every choice but Off is disabled with "not offered yet"; Contents is
  disabled with its reason when no local model is set up. The server builds
  the picker (`modelPickerVM`) from the flag and `modelEndpoints`.
- *See what it would send* asks for a preview (`POST
  /api/suggestions/model/preview` → `modelSuggestPreview`), shown in place
  as a dialog: the headline ("This sends 38 file and folder names from 1
  folder to Claude (claude -p) (Anthropic, an outside model, outside this
  computer). No file's content is sent."), the destination, which folder
  each `root N` is (folder names are not sent), the list (every line
  exactly as sent for names; each file and its byte count, never its text,
  for contents), what was left out (files a rule or sensitivity label
  protects), and whether the request can reach only that model's address.
  Nothing is sent until **Send**.
- *Send* posts exactly the preview's digest (`POST
  /api/suggestions/model/send {digest, tier}` → `modelSuggest`, once per
  digest), follows the run until it ends, and shows its line and the new
  rows (§4.25r). Refusals come back in the page's words; an expired preview
  is 410.

**Gates.** Both POSTs need CSRF + admin session and answer 403 unless the
picker is offered; an arbiter without the ops answers 501. The consent
binds what the arbiter's service built and keeps, not what the page shows:
the page shows the service's own words and counts and nothing a model
wrote (the service keeps only an id and two enums per answer).

**Tests.** `suggestion-model-view-model.test.ts`,
`test/unit/server/suggestion-model-routes.test.ts`,
`test/unit/ui/home-js-suggest-model.test.ts`, and the production adapter
over a real arbiter in `tests/stack/policy-model-contents.test.ts`.

**The preview keeps the focus (2026-10-12).** Until then, in a headless
Chromium, Enter on *See what it would send* left the focus on `<body>`
while it asked (the button goes off) and after the preview opened; Escape
did nothing in the preview; Cancel hid the preview with the focus in it,
and Send went off, both leaving the focus on `<body>`. Cancel also stayed
on while a send was on its way and said "Nothing was sent." of names the
model already had, until the run's answer (up to 20 s) wrote its line. Now
(`home.js`, *the model picker*):

- **It opens on its headline.** The preview takes the focus on its
  headline, the server's sentence Send agrees to ("This sends 8 file and
  folder names … No file's content is sent."), not a control, so no ring
  and no Tab stop (`tabindex="-1"`). Never on Send: a second Enter sends
  nothing. Tab goes on to Cancel, then Send.
- **Escape is Cancel.** Escape in the preview, Cancel and Close send
  nothing, say "Nothing was sent.", and give the focus back to *See what
  it would send*, else (the picker went to Off) the picker, else the card's
  heading (`modelPreviewBack`). Not an Escape a note took, one that ends an
  IME composition, one with a modifier (`plainEscape`, shared with the
  Models form), nor one outside the preview.
- **A send cannot be called back.** While it is on its way, Send and Cancel
  are off, Escape closes nothing, and the focus waits on the headline. When
  the run ends the preview closes, the run's line shows, and the focus goes
  back to *See what it would send*. A refused send keeps the preview (Send
  stays off: look again), and the focus goes to Cancel, on again.
- **Refusals are read with the button.** A refused preview gives the focus
  back to *See what it would send*, on again. It and Cancel are described
  by the card's error line (`aria-describedby="suggest-error"`), as *Scan
  for keys* is.
- **Nothing is taken.** The focus moves only from where the press left it
  (still there, or fallen to the page): a focus moved elsewhere meanwhile,
  and a Cancel pressed without the focus in the preview, move nothing.

Sighted readers see one change: Cancel is off while a send is on its way.
No route, digest, request or server text changed. Tests:
`home-js-suggest-model-focus.test.ts` (jsdom; `press` drops the focus of
the button turned off, as Chromium does): the headline, Escape from the
headline and the list, Cancel and Close, the picker when the button is off,
a held send (Send and Cancel off, Escape and Cancel close nothing, the
run's end), a refused preview and a refused send, a focus moved elsewhere,
a press without the focus, and the Escapes that close nothing. Stack
`tests/stack/suggest-model-focus.test.ts`: a real arbiter walks a work tree
with a registered key in `deploy/app.conf` and starts its fake classifier
through a wrapper that holds each run; a real dashboard over the production
adapter, the picker offered, serves Rules signed in. Names only: the
preview opens on its headline; Escape closes it and the classifier got no
run; a held Send keeps Cancel off, Escape and Cancel close nothing, and the
run's end gives the focus back with exactly one run; the classifier's
request (names only), the page and the answers carry no key.

#### 4.25u Approvals: the page's name, its cards in the AI's terms, moments, and "masked"

**Why.** "Inbox" did not say what the page is for (the questions Mandu asks
you). "Asked 2 days ago" gave no way to match a card to what you were doing.
"Locked file" was a third word beside *secret* and *masked*. And an expanded
card's cells used one fixed sentence for every kind of question and switched
subject between the AI and a program, which made the one family where the
difference matters (a program reading a secret file) easiest to misread as
"the AI reads it". The changes are wording only: routes, the `?page=inbox`
key (retired by §4.25v), attributes and element ids were unchanged.

- **The page is *Approvals*** wherever a person reads its name: nav,
  heading, tab title, links and notices on the page, and every message
  outside the dashboard that sends someone there (the launcher's `mandu
  why` hint, exec refusals in `exec-wrap`, `exec-supervisor` and both
  proxies, the `held:` note, the hold-timeout reason, the policy-file
  messages and `policy.yaml` header, and the agent-facing policy tool
  descriptions and handling prompt: "the Mandu dashboard's Approvals
  page"). The inspector followed in §4.25w.
- **Home summarizes it explicitly**: "Approvals waiting (N)", N equal to the
  nav badge (set in one place, `renderTopStatus`), with "Open Approvals →".
- **Every moment reads absolute and relative.** home.js `whenNode` renders
  `<time datetime="<ISO>">Sep 30, 14:12 · 2 days ago</time>` (local 24-hour
  time, the year when not this year, month names written out so every
  viewer reads the same words), wherever the page showed a bare "ago".
  Compact agent rows keep the relative form. The agent page's header
  followed on 2026-10-05 (§4.25, *The header says how long it ran*).
  - **A moment keeps its number with its word (2026-10-15).** Until then a
    moment's words wrapped anywhere. Headless Chromium, with a real
    arbiter, dashboard and served page, measured on every product page at
    1280, 980, 720, 390 and 320 px:
    - History at 1280 and 980 px: a running row read "running now,
      started 1" over "minute ago", in the row's 150 px time column;
    - the session page's header at 390 px: "ran 9 minutes 7 seconds,
      ended Oct 15, 15:31 · 2" over "minutes ago".

    Now a compact row's relative words (`home.js whenLine`, `time.ago`) stay
    on one line, so the line broke before "1 minute ago" (since
    2026-10-17 before "started 1 minute ago": *A row's moment keeps its
    verb*, below). A whenNode
    moment is written in two parts by `home.js sayWhen` (whenNode, and
    `refreshWhen` on every poll): `<span class="when-at">Oct 15, 15:31
    ·</span> <span class="when-ago">2 minutes ago</span>`, each on one line
    (`app.css`), so it breaks, if it must, only between the clock time and
    the relative words. The text, and so what a screen reader says, is
    unchanged. The longest part, "Sep 30, 2025, 14:12 ·", fits every
    column that holds one; after the fix the same survey found no moment
    split inside a part and nothing wider than its column, at 320 px with
    the year form too.
    - Counts broke from their word the same way; see the next item.
    - Presentation only: no route, gate, count or server text changed.
    - Tests: `home-js-when-lines.test.ts` (jsdom: the two parts on the
      session page and a question card, again after a poll in the same
      `<time>`, the rows' `time.ago`, and the `app.css` contract),
      `home-js-approvals.test.ts` (text only: the moment's only elements
      are its two parts, each one text node), and stack
      `tests/stack/product-when-lines.test.ts` (two real sessions through
      the anthropic-proxy, one real exit; the served History, Home and
      session pages under their served styles at 1280 and 390 px, with no
      value).
  - **A row's moment keeps its verb (2026-10-17).** The entry above lets
    a row's line break before its `time.ago`, so History's running row
    read "running now, started" over "1 minute ago" in its 150 px time
    column at 1280 and 980 px (headless Chromium over a real arbiter and
    dashboard, seeded with the tour's sessions). The verb was cut from
    its moment while the line's own pause, after "now,", went unused.

    Now home.js `whenLine` puts the verb's last word and the moment in one
    `.when-phrase` (`<span class="when-phrase">started <time
    class="ago">…</time></span>`, the words before it, "running now, ",
    outside), and app.css draws it as an inline box no wider than its line
    (`display: inline-block; max-width: 100%`, the `.name-fit` pattern).
    The line breaks before the phrase: "running now," over "started 1
    minute ago". A phrase wider than its line wraps inside, before its
    `time.ago`, so nothing runs past the column. Home's rows and an ended
    row ("started …", "ended …") are the phrase alone and read as before.
    - After the fix the survey read History's running row as "running
      now," over "started 1 minute ago" at 1280 and 980 px, on one line at
      390 and 320 px, and "started 59 minutes ago", the longest, on one
      line in the 150 px column; Home's rows unchanged; no page wider than
      its window.
    - Presentation only: the text (and so what a screen reader says),
      `refreshWhen`, the routes and the server are unchanged.
    - Tests: `home-js-when-lines.test.ts` W5 (jsdom: History's running and
      ended rows, Home's row, the phrase kept by a poll) and W6 (the
      `app.css` contract), and stack `tests/stack/product-when-lines.test.ts`
      L1 (the phrase's computed box on the served History and Home pages at
      1280 and 390 px).
  - **A moment line ends where it ends (2026-10-17).** A card's line under
    its headline ended with a period whatever came after it, so Approvals'
    waiting card read "Oct 17, 02:31 · just now." and the rule-change card
    "Seen Oct 17, 02:31 · 2 days ago.", a period after a moment with
    nothing after it (headless Chromium over a real arbiter and
    dashboard, seeded). Under them on the same page an *Answered earlier* row
    (`answeredWhat`) put the period only before its link, and History's
    and Home's rows (`whenLine`) never had one.

    Now home.js `askCard` ends the moment (and its count, ", 3 times")
    with a period only when something follows it: the sentence of an
    agent that has ended, or, on Home's short card, *Details in
    Approvals*. `proposalCard` draws the moment alone ("Seen" before it
    for a change found on disk). A card with no recorded moment draws
    nothing, not a bare "." or "Seen".
    - Presentation only: the moment's `<time>`, `refreshWhen`, the routes
      and the server are unchanged.
    - Tests: `home-js-approvals.test.ts` (jsdom: each card's line, with
      and without a count, an ended agent's, no moment, the two kinds of
      rule change, an *Answered earlier* row and Home's short card; the
      two older pins of the trailing period now pin its absence), and
      stack `tests/stack/ask-top-row.test.ts` A3 (the served Approvals
      page's rule-change and waiting cards and Home's short card, over a
      real arbiter).
  - **A question says which session asked (2026-10-18).** Two agents of
    one kind, say Claude Code in `~/projects/shop` and Claude Code in
    `~/projects/blog`, raised questions whose cards both read "Claude
    Code wants to send your secret …", and Home and Approvals had no
    word to tell them apart. Which project asks is what decides between
    *Always allow* and *Block*.

    Now a waiting card's moment line names the session that asked last,
    where it works: "Oct 17, 10:34 · just now · from Claude Code in
    `~/projects/shop`", and, when more than one session raised it, "·
    from 2 sessions, last Claude Code in `~/projects/shop`". It shows on
    Approvals' full card and Home's short card.
    - The agent name repeats the headline's on purpose: with two kinds
      running, the headline says who and the line says where.
    - The folder is a name as the cards draw one (`nameCode` over
      `shortPath`): kept whole up to 24 characters, else cut only at
      its slashes.
    - The period rule above holds: the period follows the folder, and
      only when the ended agent's sentence or *Details in Approvals*
      follows.
    - When no folder is known (the trace names none, or the session is
      not one Home models), nothing is added: the line is as before.
    - *See what the agent was doing* still opens that session.
    - Server: `buildHomeViewModel` adds `HomeAsk.askerCwd` (the facts'

  - **A count keeps its word (2026-10-15).** Until then a count in the

  - **A waiting change names each host (2026-10-16).** A change waiting
    to be saved said its level with the hosts as one plain text, in five
    places: *Will be: … (not saved)* under a row's name and in the opened
    row (home.js `levelText`), *Changes to save* (the label before, the
    words the row showed when the change was queued, and the one after),
    its *Show the files* rows, and Save's two lists, *These changes make
    protection weaker* ("Becomes …", `looseningWords` and the page-store
    loosening) and *Files that become less protected* (the impact rows'
    `before` / `after`, `levelWords`). The survey (headless Chromium over
    a real arbiter and dashboard and the served Rules page; `.env` bound to
    four hosts, one more added with Update, then Save; 1280, 980, 720, 390
    and 320 px) found "alerts-" over "eu.example.com" (21 characters) in
    the row, the opened row and *Changes to save* at 1280 px, "deploy-"
    over "hooks.example.com" (24) at 720 px, and nine splits at 390 and
    320 px, while the opened row's *May be sent to* names each host in
    code (the entry above).

    Now:
    - `rule-words.ts` `levelParts` gives a level and its hosts as parts,
      each host a code (`hostParts`); `levelWords` is their joined text,
      byte for byte. An impact row sends `beforeParts` / `afterParts`
      beside `before` / `after` (`/api/files/impact` and Save's
      question), and a loosening that names hosts sends `detailParts`
      beside `detail` (`looseningWords`; a page-store loosening carries
      `detailParts` / `fileDetailParts`, and `pageLooseningWords` sends a
      copy of the ones it picks). Lines that name no host (Not secret, a
      removed rule) send no parts. The keys Save asks to confirm
      (`expected`) are untouched.
    - home.js `levelNodes` draws *Will be* and the label after in
      *Changes to save* from the change itself. The label before is drawn
      the same way when the change kept its level and hosts (`queueChanges`
      stores `beforeLevel` / `beforeHosts`, kept in localStorage only,
      never sent) and those say exactly its words; a change kept by an
      older page, or a label whose words say more (a per-value file), is
      its words as written. The impact rows and Save's lines are drawn from
      their parts, an older server's as their words.
    - These lines sit in columns narrower than 24 characters of code: the
      Rules row under its name is 134 px at 320 px, and a 24-character
      host there is 178 px. A nowrap `.code-whole` ran past it in the first
      try. So they draw a name through `fitName`, not `nameCode`: one of
      at most `WHOLE_MAX` (24) characters is a plain code in a `.name-fit`
      with the punctuation right after it (`fitWords` moves a leading
      ", " / "." into the box). `app.css` draws `.name-fit` as an
      inline-block no wider than its line: the name moves whole to the next
      line when it fits one, and wraps inside only when the column is
      narrower than the name. A comma in the box never starts a line (the
      reason inline-block alone was rejected above). A longer name is a
      plain code, and these lines' codes wrap anywhere
      (`overflow-wrap: anywhere`), as `.files-pending-list code` did.
      `.code-whole` keeps its contract (never wraps); a `.name-fit` never
      sets `white-space`. The file each line names is drawn the same way.

    its column can hold it, at 1280, 980, 720, 390 and 375 px. Nothing
    runs past its column at any width from 320 to 1280 px. What still
    wraps: the 27-character host (the design call above). Below 375 px it
    is the hosts wider than the Rules row's column (the 24-character host
    at 360 to 320 px, the 21-character one at 340 and 320 px), and at
    320 px the 24-character host in Save's lists (202 px against a 201 px
    column).
    - *Not covered:* the opened row's level chip (the entry above); the
      rest of the page still draws a short name as a nowrap `.code-whole`,
      measured to fit those columns.

      The Save route's answer gains parts beside its unchanged words; what

  - **A rule change names its port (2026-10-16).** A rule change that
    lets the agent's programs connect somewhere said less than the line
    under it. `editWords` read an `allow-connect` to host `*` as "any
    address" and dropped its port, while *This would let* (`relaxWords`,
    the arbiter's `destinations` subject) said `*:22`. A
    `remove-connect` of the same rule read as the raw code `*:2222`, a
    port of `*` as a `:*` suffix (`*.example.org:*`), and the subject's
    `udp:` was stripped, so a UDP allowance read as a TCP one. The survey
    (headless Chromium over a real arbiter and dashboard, the served
    Approvals page at 1280 px; an agent's waiting change with those three
    edits) found "connect to any address" over "could connect to `*:22`".

    Now one function, `connectTarget(host, port)`, words a connection
    target for both ops and for the would-let line, which parses the
    arbiter's `proto:host:port` (`connectSpecWords`):
    - host `*` is "any address"; with a port, "any address on port `22`"
      (the port a code); with port `*`, "any address on any port";
    - a named host, a pattern or a list keeps its code, with a numeric
      port as before (`db.internal:5432`, `pypi.org`); with port `*`,
      "`*.example.org` on any port";

    to any" / "address"), a glossary entry. Now app.css balances a heading
    or a label over its lines (`h1, h2, h3, .k, .proposal-k {
    text-wrap-style: balance }`) and lets prose move a word down where
    the browser judges its last line too short (`p, li, dd, .v {
    text-wrap-style: pretty }`).
    - The longhand on purpose: the `text-wrap` shorthand also sets
      `text-wrap-mode: wrap`, which would undo a `nowrap` a row inherits.
      Where a line may break (`white-space`, `.code-whole`, `.name-fit`,
      `.name-part`, `.when-phrase`) is unchanged, and a browser without
      `text-wrap-style` wraps as before.
    - After: none at 1280 px; at 390 px one, Rules' "Your rules are
      checked first, then the built-in protections." (Chromium's `pretty`
      keeps a long last word: its call); at 320 px only a path's own break
      after its last slash (`~/mandu-try/deploy/` / `staging.conf`, by
      design). Every page's height and overflow the same at 1280 and
      390 px.
    - Presentation only: no route, string, gate, verdict or answer
      changed.
    - Tests: `css-no-word-alone.test.ts` (N1, the app.css contract: the
      two rules, the longhand only, no `white-space` in them, no later
      rule taking the style back; N2, jsdom under app.css: a label and a
      heading compute `balance`, a note, a cell, a row and a glossary
      entry `pretty`, a `.code-whole` stays `nowrap`); stack
      `tests/stack/no-word-alone.test.ts` (a real arbiter's waiting send
      and the agent's waiting rule change; the served Approvals, Rules,
      History and Settings pages, signed in, under their served styles at
      390 px; the oracle on every page and answer read).
- **Secret file, not locked file**, in every product sentence, the user
  docs and the agent-facing tool descriptions. Internal names (`lock-path`,
  `LockEdit`, `lock-*` ids) stay.
- **"Masked", with a help button.** The word stays ("stand-in" was
  rejected) and "placeholder" is gone. Next to prominent mentions sits
  home.js `helpButton`/`maskedHelp`: a real `<button>` with `aria-expanded`
  / `aria-controls` toggling a short note (keyboard and click, Escape and
  click-away close; never hover-only). Its last sentence follows the
  running mode so the default does not over-claim: at `secrets` (and off,
  and unknown) "only secrets are masked; untrusted content reaches the AI
  as-is"; at `full`/`injection` "In this mode, untrusted content, such as a
  web page, is masked too". Its first sentences say what the glossary's
  *Masked* says: Mandu replaced the real value "with a short code that
  stands for it" (until 2026-10-11 "with a label", a word the page also
  uses for a file's rule and for Sensitivity labels). **An open note stays in the window** (2026-10-09, home.js
  `keepInWindow`): a note opens under its button, at most 320 px wide; one
  that would run past the window's right edge (a mark far along a phone's
  row: at 390 px the OpenCode row's Preview note ended at 456 px, and the
  page scrolled sideways) moves left until it ends 16 px inside the
  window, never past the 16 px left margin. Every help note gets it.
- **A card has one subject, the AI.** The cells are *Why it stopped* /
  *What the AI has now* / *If you click Allow once or Always allow*.
  `describeAsk` (`view-model/ask-words.ts`, so the inspector's Approvals
  card reads the same words, §4.34) returns `aiNow`, `why` and `ifAllowed`
  (each also as parts, *The cells name things as the headline does*),
  worded per family from what the gate actually does. The read family's
  *why* carries the instruction: "`.env` is a secret file, and Mandu keeps
  secret files from the AI. If you want `psql` to read it, click Allow once
  or Always allow."

  | Family (queue key) | What the AI has now | If you click Allow |
  |---|---|---|
  | send (`$MDU:…` × host) | only the masked version | the AI's request goes to the host with the real value filled in |
  | a program reads a secret file (`open:<exe>#…`, plan 10 §11.1) | its program has not read the real file | the AI's program reads the real file; what it prints still reaches the AI masked. Never "the AI reads it": that would be a false security statement |
  | a file that runs later (`write:<exe>#…`, write-protection.md) | its program has not changed the file | its program changes it; what it wrote runs the next time the file is used |
  | the agent's tool on a guarded path (`fs:<tool>:<mode>`, fs-sync.md §1.4.1) | its tool got an error | its tool can open (change) it on retry; the sentence says *a secret file*, *a file outside its work folder* or *a protected file* from the row's reason |
  | a tool sends a local file off the computer (`fs:<tool>:upload`, Claude Code's DesignSync, Artifact and ArtifactData, supported-agents.md §2) | its tool has not sent the file | its tool sends the file as it is on retry; the family is *send*, and the block words come from the `fs:upload-*` rule |
  | downloaded code (`exec-program:<host>`, exec-routing.md §8.7a) | its command was stopped before it ran | when the AI runs it again, the downloaded code runs on this computer |
  | escalation (`exec-escalate:<network\|original-fs>`, exec-routing.md §5) | the command ran without the network / on the masked copy | on a rerun it gets the network / runs on your real files |

**Tests.** `home-view-model.test.ts` (every family's cells with the AI as
subject; the read family's exact sentences and that none says the AI reads
the file; a sweep that no product string says *Inbox*, *locked file* or
*placeholder*), `home-js-approvals.test.ts` (nav, heading, title, the
waiting count equal to the badge, `<time>` and the year rule, the cells,
the help button's ARIA and the mode-dependent sentence). Each package whose
message was reworded updated its own test (`launcher/test/unit/why.test.ts`,
the proxies' `exec-gate` and `rewrite-request` tests, `exec-wrap`'s
`gate.test.ts`, `exec-supervisor`'s `refusal.rs`,
`tests/stack/secret-hold-timeout.test.ts`).

#### 4.25v Page URLs are paths

**Problem.** Both front-ends kept their page in the query string
(`/?page=inbox&ask=<id>`, `/dev/?area=policy&session=<id>`): the resource a
link names was one key among several, and the server could not tell a page
from a typo.

**Decision.** Pages are paths under the base path, routed client-side with
the History API and answered server-side with the front-end's one
`index.html`. The path names the resource; the query carries only view
state.

| URL (under `DASHBOARD_BASE_PATH`) | Page |
|---|---|
| `/` (also `/index.html`) | Home |
| `/approvals`, `/approvals/<askId>` | Approvals; with an id, that question marked and scrolled to |
| `/rules`, `/settings` | Rules, Settings |
| `/agents/<sessionId>` | the agent page; `?ask=<askId>` marks the moment it was asked (§4.25h) |
| `/dev/` (also `/dev/index.html`) | the inspector on its persisted page (`mandu.area`), else Sessions |
| `/dev/sessions`, `/dev/drills`, `/dev/tests`, `/dev/approvals`, `/dev/rules`, `/dev/settings` | an inspector page (§4.32); `/dev/status`, `/dev/policy` and `/dev/inbox` are a 302 to `/dev/sessions`, `/dev/rules`, `/dev/approvals` |
| `/dev/sessions/<id>`, `/dev/drills/<id>`, `/dev/tests/<id>` | that page, showing that session (a drill or test id under `/dev/sessions/` moves to its own page client-side); `?tab=secrets` / `files` / `checks` opens that tab (view state, §4.33; Trace, the default, is never written); `?ask=<askId>` marks the moment an approval was asked (§4.35), `?step=<stepId>` one step (§4.35) |
| `/dev/drills/matrix`, `/dev/drills/agents`, `/dev/drills/comparison`, `/dev/tests/suites`, `/dev/tests/coverage`, `/dev/tests/vm`, `/dev/tests/ci` | a tool sub-page (§4.32); where the path holds no session, it rides along as `?session=<id>` |

- **Segments** are `encodeURIComponent`-encoded, so an id with `/`, `?`,
  `#` or spaces is one segment. A missing or extra segment, an unknown path
  or garbled encoding is no page: the server answers **404**.
- **Server** (`src/server/page-routes.ts`, at the end of `handle`): GET and
  HEAD only. Every page route sits behind the same gates in the same order
  as before (source IP, Basic auth, cookie session: an unauthenticated page
  path is the `/login` redirect before any route, a 404 or a redirect
  included).
- **Assets from a nested route.** `serveIndex` injects `<base
  href="${basePath}/">` (inspector: `${basePath}/dev/`) as the first
  element of `<head>`, so every relative URL, the scripts' own included,
  resolves without a list of attributes to keep in sync. The cost: an
  in-page `href="#"` resolves against the base and must keep its
  `preventDefault`. Clients build routes from the base-path meta (home.js
  `routeHref` / `parseRoute`, dev/js/pages.js `devHref(devBase, {page, sub,
  session})` / `parseDevRoute`, §4.32).
- **Retired URLs keep working.** The query form is a server **302** to its
  path (`legacyRedirect`), other keys such as `tenant` kept:
  `/?page=inbox&ask=x` → `/approvals/x`, `/?page=agent&session=s&ask=a` →
  `/agents/s?ask=a`, `/dev/?session=s` → `/dev/sessions/s`,
  `/dev/?area=policy` → `/dev/rules`; an unknown page goes to Home, an
  unknown area to Sessions. The clients read the old form too.
- **History.** A product or inspector nav click pushes one entry and Back
  re-reads the route (`popstate`); a session pick, a module's page jump
  (`mdu:go-page`, alias `mdu:go-area`) and the boot-time canonical form
  replace. A `#<key>` (a section of the inspector's Rules or Settings,
  §4.34) stays in the address while the page stays, and goes with it.
- The product page key `inbox` became `approvals`, with its element ids
  (`#page-approvals`, `#approvals-*`).

**Tests.** `test/unit/server/page-routes.test.ts`,
`test/unit/ui/home-js-routes.test.ts` (under `/mandu` and unprefixed),
`page-nav.test.ts`, `dev-pages.test.ts` and `app-js-layout-nav.test.ts` (the
inspector's `/dev/<page>[/<sub>]` and `/dev/<page>/<id>`, the session as a
query where the path holds none, push vs replace), and over the real server
`test/component/page-routes.test.ts` (each route's `index.html` and
`<base>`, assets at a nested route, 404s, the retired URLs, every link the
served script builds, and the cookie, Basic-auth and source-IP gates on the
new routes), plus `two-front-ends.test.ts` and `approval-loop.test.ts`.

#### 4.25w The inspector's Approvals area

After §4.25u and §4.25v the inspector still called the same queue *Inbox*
at `/dev/inbox`: two names for one queue across the front-ends. The
inspector's area is now **Approvals** too: tab label, `aria-label`, page
key (`approvals`; pages.js and page-routes.ts), path `/dev/approvals`, and
the internal ids, classes and egress.js functions. A rule minted from an ask
there is recorded as `requestedBy: "dashboard approvals"`. This was a rename;
§4.34 later gave the page the product's card, answers and headings
("Waiting for your answer", "Answered earlier"), with a developer line under
each card.

The old name keeps working: the server answers `/dev/inbox[?…]` and
`?area=inbox` with a **302** to `/dev/approvals` (query kept;
`INSPECTOR_PAGE_ALIASES`), and the client maps the old key, so a saved
`mandu.area` of `inbox` opens Approvals and is rewritten. Kept on purpose: the `?page=inbox` and `/dev/inbox` aliases,
the retired register key `simple-inbox`, and "Inbox hold" as the drill
runner's and suite manifest's term for an ask a drill expects.

**Tests.** `page-routes.test.ts` (unit and component: `/dev/approvals` is a
page, `/dev/inbox` is a redirect with the query kept), `page-nav.test.ts`
(the stored-area migration, every old spelling opening Approvals, no
visible "Inbox" left in `dev/index.html` or egress.js), `index-html.test.ts`,
`egress-js-approvals.test.ts`, `egress-js-document.test.ts`.

#### 4.25x Another agent can reach Mandu's own controls: the exposure, shown

While a launch with no wall around the arbiter's human-plane socket runs
(`--mode off`, or `--no-net-guard` without the mount layer), the arbiter
believes no guard or proxy report on that socket, so every confined session
beside it gets placeholders, refused protected writes and masked shell
output (arbiter-human-plane.md §10.1). That stays: it fails closed. Both
front-ends show it, with the launch that causes it and the fix
(arbiter-human-plane.md §10.1.1 has the arbiter and launcher halves).

**Where it comes from.** `loadPolicyPanel` (server/api-routes.ts) asks the
event source's `humanPlaneStatus` (a human-plane-only op: the answer names
sessions) and sets `PolicyPanelVM.humanPlane` (view-model/human-plane.ts
`toHumanPlaneVM`: `walled | exposed | unknown`, with each launch's pid,
mode, posture, session and start). No answer is `unknown`, never walled.
`/api/policy` and `/api/home` read it through that one loader, so the two
front-ends cannot disagree. The arbiter's audit stream also carries a
`config_change` event per state change.

**The inspector.** The Policy panel draws a chip after the posture chips:
`human plane walled` (quiet), `human plane exposed · pid 4242 (claude-…)
+1` (loud), or `human plane unknown` (dashed). Its ⓘ drawer explains the
state, lists each launch, what the exposure costs, and the fix.

**The product page.** `/api/home` carries `exposure` (`homeExposure`) only
while exposed and the service is reachable: "Another agent can reach
Mandu's own controls.", what happens to the other agents ("Your secrets
stay protected; some work in those agents may fail."), one line per cause,
when it began, and the fix ("Stop that agent, or start it again with the
file guard on (without `--mode off` or `--no-net-guard`)."). The fix also
comes as `fixParts`, the same words with the two launch flags as code parts
(2026-10-08), and Home draws them as `<code>` (`textParts`, as the first-run
card does, §4.25). Home shows it as an alert card (`#home-exposure`,
`role="alert"`, text nodes only) until a poll has none. The Home verdict is unchanged (secrets stay guarded), and
the copy passes the §4.18 vocabulary sweep.

*Each cause names its agent as Home does (2026-10-10).* Until then a cause
read "process 4242, session claude-1791840000-ab12, protection off, no file
guard": the launcher's scope id, which the product page shows nowhere else,
and nothing on the card led to the agent the fix says to stop. Now
`buildHomeViewModel` passes its own agent rows to `homeExposure`, and a
cause whose session (the launch record's, the same scope id the session is
listed under) has a row reads "Claude Code, process 4242, protection off,
no file guard": the row's agent name, a link part (`to: "agent"`) that
Home's `placeLink` draws as an in-page link to that agent's page, like
*Details*. Each cause also carries `parts` (`words` is them joined). The
process id stays: it is the launch record's own, while the name is the
row's, derived from the session's events, which while the plane is
exposed are claims (arbiter-human-plane.md §10.2; display only). There
is no folder: those claims are never read for one (`sessionCwd`), so the
row has none either. A cause with no row keeps the old words, its session
id as code; an unreadable launch record still reads "an agent Mandu could
not name". The inspector's chip and drawer are unchanged.

**Tests.** `test/unit/view-model/human-plane.test.ts` (each cause's parts
and words, with and without a row, and through `buildHomeViewModel`),
`test/unit/ui/home-js-home.test.ts` (the link opens the agent page in
place; server parts stay text), `test/unit/ui/egress-js-panel.test.ts`,
`test/component/two-front-ends.test.ts` (the served Home's fix, its flags as
code), and `tests/stack/human-plane-exposure-notice.test.ts` (both projections
through the real `ArbiterEventSource` over a real arbiter, while an
unwalled launch runs beside a confined one and after it ends or its
launcher dies; and, with the unwalled launch's posture event sent as
run.ts sends it, `/api/home` from the real server names its agent and the
served product page opens that agent's page from the link).

#### 4.25y Settings: Prompt filters, and the note under your message

**Status: LANDED.** The product half of
[`confidentiality-plan-15-prompt-filter.md`](../confidentiality/confidentiality-plan-15-prompt-filter.md)
phase 4 (§11, §13.7): what Mandu does with what it finds in what the person
types, chosen in Settings, and a plain line under the person's message when
the filter changed part of it. Settings carries only the action per kind of
finding and the exceptions list; the switches, packs, plugins and test
bench stay in the inspector's Prompt filters panel (§4.31), linked as the
developer view (`/dev/rules`).

**The section (`home.js loadPromptSettings`).**

- *Each kind* ("An email address", "A secret Mandu already knows", "A
  GitHub token", or an organization's own category) shows who decides it
  ("Set by you", "Mandu's default", "Locked by your administrator
  (10-org.yaml).") and a choice: **Hide it** (`mask`), **Remove it**
  (`redact`), **Ask me** (`ask`), **Block the message** (`block`), **Just
  note it** (`log`); `pass` ("Send as written") only on a row that has it.
  The person's own row has **Use the default**. The choice and its button
  share the row's last cell, sized to them (§4.25s *A row's controls fit
  it*).
- *A lock* from an administrator's rule names the file and offers only
  choices as strict or stricter.
- *Exceptions*: kind, pattern (`*@example.com`), who added it, **Remove**
  on the person's own, "Not in force" when a lock keeps it out. Adding one
  lets more through, so it is asked about first. Each reads as a sentence
  (*An exception reads as a sentence* below).
- Every change is one typed edit; one that lets more reach the AI is asked
  about first with the Models question (`modelConfirmText`), then resent
  with what was shown. It applies to the next message, with Undo.

**An exception reads as a sentence** (2026-10-08). An exception row is the
kind and its pattern as one sentence ("An email address matching
`*@example.com`") in the row's widest cell, who added it on the line under
it ("Added by you.", "Set by your administrator (10-org.yaml)."), and
**Remove** at the end (`home.js promptExceptionRow`, its
`prompt-exception-what` cell; `app.css` `.row.service.prompt-exception`,
`minmax(0, 1fr) auto`). Until then it was a plain service row: the sentence
was the name cell's flex box in the 180 px name column, three to five lines
tall, and a pattern or an organization's kind wider than the column ran
over the words beside it (the chip `*@corp.example.com` over "Set by your
administrator"). Now the sentence wraps as words, and a chip in a Settings
row's name breaks inside it (`.row.service .name code`, `overflow-wrap:
anywhere`), so a kind with a long name keeps to the kinds' name column. On
a narrow screen (≤ 760 px) the row stacks, Remove on the left. Tests: UI
`home-js-settings-rows` and stack `settings-rows-fit` (F4, over a real
arbiter with the person's and the administrator's exceptions and an
organization's pack).

**An exception that cannot be added says why** (2026-10-16). The add form
names a kind only if it is not a registered secret, which has its own ways
out (its kind's choice, the note under your message), and not a kind an
administrator's lock covers, whose exception the arbiter refuses
(`exceptionKinds`). With no such kind the form is not drawn. A default
install is in this state: the only check on by default is the
registered-value one (`arbiter/prompt-filter/policy.ts` `DEFAULT_ON`), so
the one kind listed is *A secret Mandu already knows*. Until this change the
note over the list still said how to write a pattern ("Use a `*` for any
text, as in `*@example.com`.") for a form that was not there. Now:

- The note's first sentence ("What matches an exception goes to the AI as
  you wrote it.") always shows. Its how-to sentence shows only with the form
  (`index.html` `#settings-prompt-exceptions-how`, hidden with
  `#prompt-exception-form`).
- Without the form, the server's words say why
  (`view-model/prompt-settings.ts exceptionNotOffered`, drawn as text into
  `#settings-prompt-exceptions-why`):
  - only registered secrets: "Exceptions are not offered for a secret Mandu
    already knows: the choice above decides what happens to it.";
  - registered secrets and kinds the administrator locked: "Exceptions are
    not offered for a secret Mandu already knows, and your administrator
    locked the other kinds.";
  - only locked kinds: "Your administrator locked every kind above, so none
    can have an exception.";
  - no kind at all: "There is no kind to add an exception for."
- Read only, neither: the note above the kinds already says nothing can be
  changed from this page.
- A server without the field (an older one) gives no reason, and the how-to
  still goes with the form.
- Under a reason, an empty list says only "No exceptions." (2026-10-16,
  nightly run 1130). The reason already says what happens to what Mandu
  finds, and the full empty line would say it again one line lower: on a
  default install, "… the choice above decides what happens to it." over
  "No exceptions. Everything Mandu finds gets the choice above.". With the
  form, read only, or from a server that gives no reason, the empty line
  keeps its second sentence. A list with exceptions in it (written before a
  lock, say) shows them under the reason, with no empty line.
  `home.js loadPromptSettings` draws the list after it decides the form and
  the reason, and picks the line by whether the reason shows.

The list's rows are unchanged, and so is the arbiter: it still decides every
exception. Tests: unit `prompt-settings-view-model` (each mix of kinds), UI
`home-js-prompt` (the how-to with the form, the reason without it, neither
read only, server words as text; under each of the four reasons the short
empty line, with the form, read only and from an older server the full one,
rows and no empty line under a reason; a redraw that brings the form back
swaps both), and stack `settings-exceptions-not-offered`. That one runs a
real arbiter at its defaults (the reason over "No exceptions."), then with
`key-shapes: on` (the form, the how-to and the full empty line; the arbiter
asks before such an exception), then with the administrator's lock on that
kind (the reason names the lock, over "No exceptions."; the arbiter refuses
the exception, naming the file), with the oracle.

**The note under your message (`home.js promptNoteNode`).** On the agent
page, under "You asked", one line per outcome ("One value in your prompt
was hidden from the AI (an email address).", "Your message was not sent to
the AI: it holds a card number."). Per finding: **Show what was hidden**
(fetches the original, shown as text; it keeps the keyboard focus through
its request, §4.25b *Show the real value keeps the focus*) and **Let it through in this
message / for this session** (asked first). A message the filter blocked
is its own card, placed in the story by time. The answer to a let-through
(its line, or a refusal's words) stays on its row when the page is drawn
again, until the agent's next request records it (§4.25 *The poll keeps
your place*).

*A lock* (2026-10-07, the work ledger's P1). The arbiter refuses every
let-through of a kind whose strictest locked administrator row is not
`ask` (`mask`, `redact`, `block`), and the event does not say so. The
agent page reads the locks in force (`promptLocks`, as the panel's
findings route does, §4.31), only for a session with a `prompt_filter`
event: such a finding shows neither button and says why
(`PromptNoteItem.lockedWhy`, `lockedWords`): "Your administrator set this
to block the message every time, so it cannot be let through." (*be
hidden*, *be removed*). Show what was hidden stays: it lets nothing
through. A locked `ask` row in force keeps the session button away and
says "this message only", as the event's `onceOnly` does. With no locks to
read (no arbiter, one without the rows, an error) the event alone decides,
and the arbiter still refuses.

**Server.**

    GET  /api/policy/prompt-filters                {settings: PromptSettingsVM}
    POST /api/policy/prompt-filters/change         {edit, expected?}
      → {applied: false, confirm: true, expected, rows, wouldLet}
      → {applied: true, changeId}
    GET  /api/home/agent?session=                  each story turn's `promptNote`, the page's `unplacedNotes`
    POST /api/prompt-filters/reveal                {session, eventId, index} → {original}
    POST /api/prompt-filters/let-through           {session, eventId, index, scope}

- *The listing* (`promptFiltersProjection` → `promptSettingsVM`) is
  served only with the CSRF header and the admin session: an exception's
  pattern may hold the person's own words. The developer view's reads of
  the same exceptions are gated the same way (§4.31: the filters GET and
  the policy file's GET), through one gate (`server.ts requireAdminRead`).
- *The change* reuses the panel's write path (`applyPromptEdit`: preview,
  `confirm` on a relaxation, `applyAsHuman` on the admin channel), narrowed
  to `set-prompt-action`, `remove-prompt-action`, `add-prompt-exception`
  and `remove-prompt-exception` (anything else is a 400 before the
  arbiter); a validator refusal is a 422. Behind the global mutating gate.
- *The note* (`view-model/prompt-notes.ts`) is built from the session's
  believed `prompt_filter` events (the human's own text, the
  confidentiality axis enforcing, findings that changed something), grouped
  by the segment's `turn` and placed under the story turn whose request
  carried it. It holds categories, words, counts, the event id and the
  finding's index: no symbol, offset or value, so `/api/home` and the agent
  page carry no found value.
- *Show what was hidden* resolves the finding by event and index
  (`noteRevealSymbol`) from the session's own unclaimed event, and only for
  a span the filter minted itself outside the `secret.*` kinds, through the
  human-plane `desymbolize`. The product page never shows a secret Mandu
  knows. Behind the global mutating gate.
- Prompts equal but for the filter's marks are one message
  (`dual-lanes.ts samePromptMessage`), so a resend in another form (masked
  after a policy change, as written after a let-through) does not break the
  conversation's trace.
- *A resend with nothing found* (an exception added, a kind set to `pass`)
  clears the message's note: both proxies record a `prompt_filter` event
  with no findings under the message's remembered `turn` when a segment
  they recorded with a finding is now answered with none
  (`PromptEventLedger`; plan 15 §13.7 item 10), and the note reads the
  newest event. A proxy restarted since the note was written clears it
  too: the arbiter remembers which messages it answered with a referenced
  finding (`holds.ts`, noted messages, kept in mandu.db) and names the
  message's `turn` on its answer with none, so the proxy files the cleared
  outcome under the note it never saw. Nothing in the transcript marks a
  note, so nothing a model or a tool writes can clear one.
- *Under a locked administrator's `ask` row* (plan 15 §12, 2026-10-04) a
  finding is let through for its message only. The arbiter marks such a
  finding `onceOnly` in its `filterPrompt` answer (`lockedAsk`, holds.ts),
  both proxies copy the mark into the `prompt_filter` event (a lock that
  comes or goes is a changed outcome, so the ledger records it), and the
  note offers no **for this session** button: it says why instead
  (`LET_ONLY_THIS_MESSAGE`: "Your administrator set this to ask every time,
  so it can be let through in this message only, not for the whole
  session."), even when no message reference allows the once button. The
  page does not decide: the arbiter refuses a session let-through under the
  lock whatever the event says, and the route answers that refusal 409 with
  its reason (another arbiter refusal stays 422).

**Tests.** `prompt-settings-view-model.test.ts`, `prompt-notes.test.ts`,
`test/unit/server/prompt-settings-routes.test.ts`,
`test/unit/ui/home-js-prompt.test.ts`,
`tests/stack/settings-exceptions-not-offered.test.ts` (above), and
`tests/stack/dashboard-prompt-settings.test.ts` (the production adapter, a
real arbiter and the real anthropic-proxy: a choice in force on the next
request, a lock refused naming the file, the note and its let-through, an
exception asked first, the excepted messages' notes clearing, no found
value in `/api/home` or the agent page) and its Codex twin
`tests/stack/dashboard-prompt-settings-codex.test.ts` (the real
openai-proxy on the Responses wire). The clearing event: each proxy's
`test/unit/prompt-event-ledger.test.ts` and
`test/component/prompt-filter-events.test.ts`; across a proxy restart,
`arbiter/test/unit/prompt-filter-holds.test.ts` (the noted messages) and
`tests/stack/prompt-filter-note-restart.test.ts` (both real proxies).

#### 4.25z Rules page: the built-in protections follow the mode

The Rules page's "Built-in protections" were once a static list whose first
line was "Untrusted content is masked before the AI reads it". In the
default `secrets` mode the integrity axis is off and untrusted text is NOT
masked, so the page claimed a protection the mode does not give
(architecture/protection-modes.md: user-facing copy must say so). The list
comes from `/api/home` (`HomeVM.builtIn`, `builtInProtections(level)` in
`view-model/home.ts`) for the level running now (the posture's two axes,
the same `level` the top bar shows), and `home.js renderBuiltIn` paints it;
the static HTML lists nothing, so nothing is claimed before the home loads.

| Level | Note | Items |
|---|---|---|
| `full` | always on in the Full mode | untrusted content masked; masked text used as a command, or sent to a new place, needs your OK; keys and secret files reach the AI masked unless a rule lets it read them; keys and secret files leave this computer only where a rule or your OK allows (§4.25d) |
| `injection` | always on in the Injection mode | the three masking lines; "Your secrets are not guarded in this mode." |
| `secrets` | always on in the Secrets mode | keys and secret files reach the AI masked unless a rule lets it read them; "Keys and secret files leave this computer only where a rule or your OK allows." (§4.25d); "Untrusted content is not masked in this mode: the AI reads it as-is." |
| `off` | protection is off | Mandu only watches: nothing masked, secrets not guarded; turn it on in Settings |
| unknown | not connected | the protection service is not reachable, so Mandu cannot say what is on (the page says the same when `/api/home` fails) |

**Tests.** `home-view-model.test.ts` (Secrets mode never claims masking and
says so; Full and Injection keep the sentence; Off and unknown claim
nothing; the home carries the list for the posture; the copy passes the
product vocabulary sweep) and `home-js-rules.test.ts` (the page paints the
server's list for each mode; the HTML's list is empty; a failed home claims
nothing).

#### 4.25aa Rules page: who may get your secrets, per program, host and AI (2026-10-11)

**Why.** A label is three relations per file (confidentiality plan 13
§4.2): which AI may read it (the level), where its value may be sent
(`bindings`) and which programs may open the real file (`readers:`). The
Rules rows answer them per file (§4.25p). Plan 13 §5.3 asks for the other
read too, per principal, because the questions a reviewer asks are often
about the principal: what may `deploy` open, what reaches
`api.stripe.com` without asking, does any AI see anything raw. Plan 13's
Figure 7 (`figures/reader-set-labels.html`) is that read for its example.

**Where.** A card of its own under Your rules, **Who may get your
secrets**, with the note "Your file rules read the other way round: what
each program, host and AI may get. To change one, press its file to open
it under Your rules." (until 2026-10-18: "… use its file's menus under
Your rules", which named a place the card did not link). It is read only:
the per-file menus stay the one place a rule changes, so this card's
controls are its tabs and its files, and none of them writes. Each file,
folder or pattern whose rule has a row in the tree drawn now is a button
(`.by-who-link`: the same code chip in the link colour, underlined on
hover, inline so a long name wraps as plain code does), named "Show the
rule for ~/x/.env in Your rules". Pressing it (`home.js` `openRuleRow`)
unfolds the folder headings above that rule's row, opens the row (its
*What the rules say*, as a click on its name does) and, through the row's
own `afterToggle`, scrolls it into view and puts the keyboard focus on its
⋯; the window's `scroll-padding-bottom` keeps it clear of Changes to save
(§4.25n). A per-value item ("~/x/.env: STRIPE_KEY") opens its file's row.
An item whose rule has no row (Your rules could not be read, or the two
reads disagree for a moment) stays plain code, and a rule gone by the time
it is pressed redraws the card: nothing points to a row that is not there.
On a page with dozens of rules the row named was several screens up,
perhaps inside a folded folder, and the reader had to remember the path to
find it (queue item #15, 2026-10-18). Three tabs over
one list (`role=tablist`, arrow keys, Home and End, one tab stop), the one
chosen kept in `localStorage` (`mandu.rules.byWho`, a per-viewer
convenience). A card of its own rather than a third view of the Files and
folders tree: the tree's rows carry the menus, and hiding them behind a
toggle would hide where a change is made.

| Tab | One row per | Its lists | The closing row |
|---|---|---|---|
| Programs | program a `readers:` entry names (an interpreter with its pinned script is its own program, "python3 running ~/proj/report.py") | *Opens the real file* (each with "checked by Mandu" or "your word", the §4.25p words), *Gets a masked copy*, *Never gets the real file: it prints or runs what it reads*, *Refused* | *Any other program*: a masked copy where a rule has no list or `others: twin`, else refused |
| Hosts | host on a secret rule's `bindings` | *Gets the real value without asking* | *Any other host*: "No secret goes there without a rule or your OK.", and the Not secret files, which may go anywhere |
| AI | *Any AI* ("Your agent's AI and Mandu's helper. Your AI provider gets what they read."), then each declared `local: true` model ("Your own AI, on this computer.") | *Reads it as written* (`public`), *May read it when it asks* (`any-model`; for your own AI `local-model` too), *Always sees it masked* (the rest) | none; with `local-model` rules and no own AI declared, a *Your own AI* row says none is listed, so no AI reads them |

Each list is a set of paths (`~` for the dashboard's home), with "and
everything inside" or "every matching file" for a folder or pattern (a rule
on a path that is a file is listed alone, §4.25f *A rule on a file reads as
a file*), under
a mark coloured by what it allows (green the real file or value, amber when
it asks, red masked or refused). Each tab ends with a line: opening a file
does not let a program send it; a program that read two secrets may send
only where both may go (the join is intersection, plan 13 D1) and an
answer may add one place for one piece of data; no approval lets an AI read
a file its rule keeps from it.

**Server (`view-model/rules-by-who.ts`, `server/by-who-routes.ts`).** `GET
/api/policy/by-who` → `{byWho}` (read gate: open; paths, program names,
hosts and model names, never a value). Each item carries `path` (the
display form: `~`, and ": KEY" for a value) and `rule`, the rule's own
path exactly as policy.yaml or the page label gives it (the string the
Your rules rows hold), which the page matches to a tree row. It reads the two places file rules
live: the policy snapshot's `document.paths` with each reader entry's
judgment (`pathOpeners`, the same function the Rules row's *Opens it* line
now uses, so the two reads cannot disagree: a listed printer such as
`psql` or `mysql` is never an opener, a listed program with neither a
vetting nor `prints: nothing` gets the masked copy, plan 13 D8 (12)) and the
labels made on the page (the confidentiality state's labels whose source is
not the policy file; one per path, policy.yaml first). An unknown level
reads as `no-model`, the fail-closed direction. No snapshot (no protection
service, an older one): `available: false`, and the card stays hidden (Your
rules already says the rules could not be read); the page labels
unreadable: `partial: true`, and the card says the lists may miss files.

**Not covered.** The built-in protections (the catalog of credential files)
and your answers are not in the lists; the Hosts note says an answer may add
a place.

**Per value (2026-10-11, plan 13 §5.2).** A rule with `values:` sends each
value to its own hosts, so a host row names the value, "~/ws/app/.env:
STRIPE_KEY", not the file; a host of the file's own `bindings` lists the
file as "~/ws/app/.env: any other value" (the values with no entry); and
only a host where the whole file may go (every value and the file allow
it, the snapshot's `wholeBindings`) lists the file itself. Test:
`rules-by-who.test.ts` ("per host, plan 13 §5.2").

**Tests.** `rules-by-who.test.ts` (Figure 7's example per program, host and
AI; the pinned script needing your word; an unknown level; page labels
joining; unread is not empty; the vocabulary sweep with the retired words;
the *Opens it* line and the per-program view reading the same judgment;
every item's `rule`, a value's and a pattern's included),
`home-js-by-who.test.ts` (hidden until read; the rows and their lists per
tab; arrow keys and the remembered tab; no control in the list but the
files, and no write; a file in each tab opening its row with the focus on
its ⋯, a value its file's; a folded folder unfolded first, another left
folded; an item with no row, or Your rules unread, as plain code; the
note's words; the link chip's look and its 4.5:1 in both themes; the empty
and partial lines; the sweep over the rendered card; the
12px floor and one column at phone width), and the stack e2e
`tests/stack/rules-per-principal.test.ts` (over a real arbiter and
dashboard: policy.yaml rules and a label made on the page, every tab, and
the egress gate releasing the file's key at the host the view names and at
no other; the levels as the arbiter reads them; no value in the answer;
the served page at 1280 and 390 px, where a file in the Programs tab
opens its row under a folded ~/ws, focused, and no value is shown).

#### 4.25ac The product page alone: front-ends beyond it are extensions (2026-10-15)

The product page at `/` is the dashboard every build serves. A front-end
beyond it, the developer view at `/dev/`, is an **extension**
(`src/server/extension.ts`): an object with a `name`, a `mount` (`/dev`) and
a `handle`, handed to `DashboardServer` as `extensions`. The server answers
every request under a mount (the mount itself, or a path below it; never a
sibling such as `/devices`) by calling that extension, after every gate of
`handle` has run: source IP, Host, sign-in, CSRF and the admin session for
a mutating verb, the read gate, the tenant. An extension adds pages; it
cannot skip a gate.

**The default.** With `extensions` not given, the server mounts the
inspector (`src/inspector-extension.ts`: its pages, the `/dev` → `/dev/`
redirect, its static files) over `devDir` when that directory holds an
`index.html`, and nothing otherwise. `extensions: []` serves the product
only. Without the inspector, `/dev`, its pages and its files answer 404,
never the product's index (its pages, since, a page that says so: *A page
under `/dev` without it* below).

**What the product page knows.** The product's `index.html` is served
with an `extensions` meta naming the mounted extensions (`inspector`, or
empty). `home.js` reads it once (`HAS_DEV`). Without the inspector,
nothing on the page links into `/dev/`:

- every element marked `data-dev-only` is hidden: the agent page's
  **Detailed trace** button, the Settings card
  **Developer view**, and the Prompt filters note's pointer to the
  developer view;
- a part that names the detailed trace (`placeLink`'s `trace`, `traceLink`)
  is drawn as text.

§4.25ad makes the agent page show what those words pointed to, and the
server and `home.js` leave them out of a build without the inspector.
Home's *History* link was `data-dev-only` until §4.25ae gave the product
its own History page; it now opens that page in both builds.

**What an extension brings (2026-10-15, second step).** Beyond its pages, an
extension may bring:

- **`route`:** routes outside its mount, asked before the product's routes,
  with the request's tenant and `values`;
- **`readRoutes`:** the read gate's rows for its GETs. The server gates
  with `READ_ROUTES` followed by each extension's rows, and a GET no row
  names is `admin`, so a server without the inspector refuses its reads;
- **`sessionRuns`:** the runs whose sessions are not the person's own,
  which Home and the Suggested view's folders leave out;
- **`attach`:** what the server lends it: the log, the live store, the
  supervisor, the config env, the admin-read gate;
- **`start`, `listening`, `close`:** its lifecycle.

The inspector is now the developer view's `inspector.ts`. Its routes moved there
from `server.ts` unchanged:

- the session list, a session's events and stream, and the delete, all over
  the recorded runs too;
- the ask moment, the rule table, a queue row's verdict, the handling
  prompt, `/api/git`, `/api/fs`;
- the run samples, the suite specs, the context pack, `/slides/`;
- the prompt filter panel's own routes (filters, findings, bench, change,
  packs, pack edit), why-symbol, the two label DELETEs;
- the policy document, mint, test-flow, posture, sandbox config;
- the service console beyond start and restart (status, self-restart, all,
  stop, replace, logs);
- the agent, test and drill runners, and the recorded runs (matrix, CI,
  replay, drill matrix, coverage);
- the listing cache, the boot warm-up.

Its rows are `INSPECTOR_READ_ROUTES`, and the route modules only it uses
moved with it.

The product's server keeps the session list, events and stream over the
tenant's store alone, as a read API with no page. It also keeps Home, the
agent page, the held message's routes, labels, files, suggestions, rules,
models, sensitivity labels, assistant, axes, approvals, and a service's
start and restart.

**Loaded, not imported (third step).** The server no longer knows the
developer view, and `extensions` defaults to none: the product page only.
`server-main` loads it through `extension-loader.ts`, first found wins:

1. `dashboard-dev.mjs` beside a bundle (packaging.md §5, *The developer
   view is optional*);
2. from source, the module `dashboard/package.json` names in
   `mandu.devExtension` (the developer view's `index.ts`).

No environment variable names a module: the dashboard is the human's view,
and code loaded into it runs with the human's sign-in.

The module's `createDashboardExtensions(ctx)` builds the inspector with its
runners (agent, test, drill), its run stores, the test setup panel's repro
context per tenant, and the dashboard's self-control. `server-main` no longer
builds them. Without its pages beside it, the module builds nothing. A module
that fails to load or to build costs the developer view only: it is logged,
and the server starts with the product.

To keep the product's code free of the developer view's:

- the public event-source barrel no longer re-exports the recorded, CI-live
  and own-arbiter sources (the developer view's `sources.ts` does, for the
  inspector and its tests);
- `/api/sessions` takes the developer view's extras (`SessionListExtras`:
  test and drill runs, drill badges, what it can start);
- `/api/events` takes an `extra` that adds the test setup panel;
- the developer view's reads beside the session list moved to
  the developer view's `session-routes.ts`;
- the posture and why-symbol arbiter surfaces' types moved to
  `src/server/arbiter-surfaces.ts`, beside the adapter that builds them;
- `DashboardServerOptions` lost every developer option, and `TenantState`
  lost the test context.

A unit test walks `server-main`'s static imports and fails on any developer
module (`extension-loader.test.ts`). A test that drives the developer view
builds its server with `withInspector` (`test/inspector-server.ts`).
`product-only-build.test.ts` is now the default server. Its `/dev/` pages
are 404, the developer routes are refused signed out and not found signed
in, and the session read API answers, with nothing to start.

**A page under `/dev` without it (2026-10-15).** A bare "Not found" read
as a broken link. In a build without the developer view, a GET or HEAD of
`/dev`, or of a path under it whose last segment names no file, answers
404 with a short page (`serveDevAbsent`, `static-routes.ts`):

- it says the developer view is not included in this version and is
  available on request, with the address to write to;
- it says where this build shows a session's trace: its own page, from
  Home or History;
- it wears the product's stylesheets, links back to the product page,
  and carries no script.

The developer view's files (`/dev/js/app.js`, `/dev/dashboard.css`) stay a
plain 404, never a page. A sibling of the mount (`/devices`) is not under
it.

**View as public (2026-10-15).** A maintainer running a build with the
developer view can see the product page as the public version shows it,
without a second build. The Developer view card in Settings has a **View
as public** button. It keeps the choice in this browser (`localStorage`
`mandu.home.viewAsPublic`) and reloads, and `home.js` then reads `HAS_DEV`
as false although the server serves the inspector (`SERVES_DEV`):

- every `data-dev-only` element is hidden, and the trace words are text,
  exactly as in a build without it;
- a bar under the top bar says so on every page; its **Show them again**
  button forgets the choice and reloads.

It changes this browser's page only. The server still serves `/dev/` and
its routes. Another browser, or the developer view itself, is unaffected.
A build without the developer view ignores the choice and shows no bar.
`home-js-view-as-public.test.ts` covers the button, the bar, the agent
page and the build without it.

**Out of the public tree (2026-10-15, fourth step).** The developer view
now lives outside this package and is not part of the public source:

- its pages and scripts;
- its extension and the modules only it uses: the runners, the run stores,
  the recorded sources, its route modules, the git and file readers;
- its tests: the unit, component and stack suites that drive it.

`dashboard/package.json` names its module for the loader, and the launcher
bundle builds it as an optional module (packaging.md §5). The public tree
carries neither, so its dashboard and its package serve the product page
only.

**What stays public.** Every test that guards the product stays in the
public tree. Each check that covered both front-ends was split, so its
product half runs here and its developer-view half runs with the developer
view:

- the read gate's registry and its value walks: `value-gate.test.ts`,
  `read-gate.test.ts`, the stack walks `dashboard-value-gate` and
  `signed-out-symbolize`;
- the admin-session gate;
- the path-table parity and the git-hardening oracle.

The suites that check both front-ends' stylesheets and words find the
developer view's pages through the loader (`test/unit/ui/dev-pages.ts`):

- with it, they check both;
- without it, as in the public tree, the developer view's half skips.

The dashboard's `npm test` runs them that way too (`test:product-only`,
`MANDU_TEST_NO_DEV_PAGES=1`).

The read-gate tests check each dispatch against its own table: the
product's routes against `READ_ROUTES`, and the inspector's against
`READ_ROUTES` plus `INSPECTOR_READ_ROUTES`. Every inspector route is
`admin` on a server without it.

**Tests.** `test/unit/server/extension.test.ts` (the mount rule, the first
mount wins, the inspector only over an index.html);
`test/component/product-only-build.test.ts` (both product-only builds,
`extensions: []` and a dev directory without an index.html: `/dev`, its
pages and its files are 404 and never a page; the product page, its
script and `/api/home` are served, with an empty `extensions` meta; the
full build names `inspector` and serves `/dev/`);
`test/unit/ui/home-js-no-dev.test.ts` (without the meta's `inspector`, no
link into `/dev/` is reachable on Home, Settings or an agent page, and
the trace words stay as text; with it, the links are back).

#### 4.25ad The agent page is where you check what the model saw (2026-10-15)

A build may carry the product page alone (§4.25ac), with no developer
view. So the place a user checks what the AI saw, what Mandu
stopped and where a secret went is the agent page (`/agents/<id>`,
`GET /api/home/agent`), and nothing on the product page may send the
reader to a trace their build does not have.

**The page shows what it leaves out.** The view-model builds every turn
and every step, then caps what it ships: the newest `TURN_CAP` (60) turns,
each turn's first `TURN_STEP_CAP` (80) steps, *Your secrets*' first
`SECRET_CAP` (12). Each cap's line now reads "2 earlier turns are not shown
here.", "3 more steps are not shown here.", "1 more secret is not shown
here." with a **Show them** (**Show it** for one), in every build. The
press asks the same route again with the cap lifted:

| Query | Lifts | Up to | The page then says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `turns=all` | `TURN_CAP` | `TURN_ALL_CAP` (500 newest) | `allTurns: true` |
| `steps=<turn id>` (repeatable, at most `SHOW_STEPS_MAX` = 50) | that turn's `TURN_STEP_CAP` | `TURN_STEP_ALL_CAP` (1000) | the turn's `allSteps: true` |
| `secrets=all` | `SECRET_CAP` | `SECRET_ALL_CAP` (200) | `allSecrets: true` |

Any other value is the caps (`agentShowOf`, home-routes.ts). The ALL caps
keep a huge session one page: a list the page already asked for whose
count is still above zero reads "… are past what this page shows." with no
button. The route is the same path, so the read gate's row for
`/api/home/agent` (`projection`: originals only with the admin session)
covers every query; the page that asked is the signed-out projection
signed out. The tiles count as Home does (each turn's first
`TURN_STEP_CAP` steps, `HomeFacts`), so a row and its page agree whatever
the page shows; *Your secrets*' counts were over every secret already.

The step an ask was raised at (§4.25h) is found past `TURN_STEP_CAP` now:
its turn is shown with every step up to `TURN_STEP_ALL_CAP` (`allSteps`),
and only a step past that counts as not found.

`home.js` keeps what a visit asked for (`S.agentShow`, keyed by the visit
and the session) and every read of that visit asks for it, the polls too;
a new visit of the page starts with the caps. The pressed button turns off
while its read is out; once a read that asked for the rest is drawn
(`AGENT_READS` numbers them, so an older poll's answer never lands it),
the first thing it brought takes the focus, as a card does (`focusThere`,
tabindex -1, in view): the oldest turn, the first step past the old cap
(its fold opened, as `markFocus` opens one), or the first new secret card;
if it is not there, its section's heading. The button is described by its
line (`aria-describedby`). Home's **Earlier** list does the same with the
sessions it already has (the server sends every ended session in the
window): ten, then "2 more sessions in the last 24 hours." and **Show
them**, which draws the rest and gives the eleventh row the focus.

**Words without the developer view.** The server knows whether it mounts
the inspector (`DashboardServer.hasDev`, an extension named `inspector`)
and hands `dev` to the home deps, the view-models and the service line.
With it, every sentence is as before (§4.25, *The page links the trace it
names*), and a cap's line adds "The detailed trace has them." (the link).
Without it:

| Where | With the developer view | Without |
|---|---|---|
| A call that reached the AI unmasked (agent-page.ts) | "This reached the AI without a mask. Open the detailed trace." | "This reached the AI without a mask. What the leak check found, at the top of this page, says what." (§4.25ae) |
| An OS step that did (its sentence: "Something reached the AI without a mask") | "Open the detailed trace to see what." | "What the leak check found, at the top of this page, says what." (§4.25ae) |
| *Your secrets*, a fired leak check (secret-story.ts) | "… cannot say what the AI saw. Open the detailed trace." | "… cannot say what the AI saw. What the leak check found, at the top of this page, says what." (§4.25ae) |
| *Your secrets*, a release after a check | since §4.25ae, both builds: "Mandu released it N more times after a check: to `host` at 10:42; in a command at 10:43." | the same |
| Home's hero, protection failed (home.ts) | "Open the detailed trace to see which." (one session, or the trace's list) | one session: "Open that agent's page to see which." (`to: "agent"`); several: "Each agent where it happened says "protection failed" below, and its page shows which." |
| Settings, a crashed helper (service-summary.ts) | "… for the developer view stopped unexpectedly. … The developer view has the details." | "A helper the dashboard runs stopped unexpectedly. Your agents are not affected." |
| Settings, no protection service | "… The developer view lists what it does run." | "This dashboard does not run the protection service." |
| The red tile (home.js) | "reached the AI unmasked. Open the detailed trace." | "reached the AI unmasked." |
| An unrecorded original | "The original was not recorded here. The detailed trace may have it." | "The original was not recorded here." |
| A moment the page could not find (§4.25h) | "… The detailed trace has every step." | "Mandu could not find the moment it asked in this session." |
| The background line's tooltip | "Steps that needed nothing from you. The detailed trace lists each one." | "Steps that needed nothing from you." (and **List them** lists them, §4.25ae) |
| Home's counts title, partly counted | since §4.25ae, both builds: "… History lists every session with its own counts. …" | the same |

**Left for step 2b, now done (§4.25ae)** (what the trace showed and the
product page did not; each sentence above said what happened and pointed
nowhere): the leak check's finding, where each release after a check
went, the rest of a revealed original past `HIDDEN_CAP`, each background
step, and a History list of every session past the 24-hour window. Still
open: a session past the ALL caps (500 turns, 1000 steps in a turn, 200
secrets) shows only its newest.

**Tests.** `test/unit/view-model/agent-page-show.test.ts` (each `show`
lifts its cap to its ALL cap and says so; the tiles do not move; a step
an ask was raised at past the cap is found and its turn shown whole;
`capTurn`; `dev: false` names no trace for an unmasked step, `dev` absent
as before; Home's failed sentence and the service line both ways;
`agentShowOf`), `secret-story.test.ts` (the flagged and the released lines
without the developer view; `secrets=all` and its ALL cap),
`test/unit/ui/home-js-agent-show.test.ts` (each Show them: the query, the
focus on the first thing it brought, a fold opened; the polls keep
asking and a new visit does not; a list already asked for; without the
developer view, no word on the agent page points to the trace), the
**Earlier** list's Show them in `home-js-home.test.ts`,
`test/component/agent-page-show.test.ts` (over the fixtures: the
queries, the read gate signed out, and a product-only server whose agent
page names no trace while the full build's does), and across the real
arbiter and anthropic-proxy `tests/stack/agent-page-step-links.test.ts`
(`steps=` brings the 81st read) and `agent-page-trace-links.test.ts`
(`secrets=all` lists the 13th secret, with no value).

**The back link names where you came from (2026-10-18).** The agent page's
link above its name (`#agent-back`) always read "Back to home" and went
Home, even when the page was opened from History or from an Approvals
card's *See what the agent was doing*. It now reads **Back to History**,
**Back to Approvals** or **Back to home** for the page it was opened from in
this tab (`agentBack`, from the entry's `history.state.from`, which a
pushed page change writes; §4.25 *Back and Forward keep your place*), and a
plain click on it is the browser's Back (`history.back()`), so that page
keeps your place. Its `href` is that page, for a click that opens a new
tab. Opened from a fresh tab, a typed address, a reload with no entry
before it, or from Rules, Settings or another agent page, it reads "Back
to home" and is a link Home, as before. Tests: `home-js-back-restores.test.ts`
B4, stack `tests/stack/history-back-restores.test.ts`.

#### 4.25ae The product page is a whole trace: History, the finding, releases, originals, background (2026-10-15)

The maintainer's requirement: a user with the product-only build sees, for
every session, what the AI saw against what really happened, without the
developer view. §4.25ad made the agent page show every turn, step and
secret; this closes the gaps it left, in both builds.

**History** (`/history`, a product page in `page-routes.ts`
`PRODUCT_FIXED`, drawn by `home.js`). Every session on record, newest
first, no time window: the same live agent sessions Home reads
(`buildSidebarSections`' live section, `isAgentSession`), so test, drill and
watch runs and the system logs stay out. Each row is Home's row
(`homeAgentRow`, shared with Running now and Earlier): the agent, its prompt
label, where it ran, when it started or ended, "protection failed", its
counts (from `HomeFacts`, cached per session, so a row, its Home row and its
page agree), the questions it raised that still wait (*History says what
waits for you*, below), and **Details** to its agent page. The data is
`GET /api/home/history?after=<id>&limit=<n>&q=<words>&only=stepped-in`
(`HistoryVM`: `total`, `rows`, `next`, `query` for a search, *Finding a
session* below, and `only` for the switch, *Only the sessions where Mandu
stepped in* below), a page at a time (`HISTORY_PAGE` 25, at most
`HISTORY_PAGE_MAX` 100) past the last row drawn; an id no longer listed
starts over, and the page drops a row it already drew. Its read row is
`open`: names, times and counts, what `/api/sessions` and `/api/home` serve
already. The page reads it when opened; **Show more** (not "Show them": it
brings a page, not the rest) reads the next page and gives its first row
the focus; a failed read says why (`cannotCheck`), beside Show more
(*A Show more that fails*, below). Home's *History: N
sessions* link opens it in both builds (it was the developer view's session
list, hidden without it), and Home's partly-counted title says "History
lists every session with its own counts."

*History is a page link* (2026-10-18). Until then the top bar linked Home,
Approvals, Rules and Settings, and the only way into History was Home's
*History: N sessions* link, which is not there before the first session
is recorded. From any other page History was two clicks away, and on
History no link in the top bar was marked as the current page. Nothing
above chose to leave it out: it was the developer view's list when the
nav was drawn. Now **History** is the fifth page link, after Settings
(`data-page-link="history"`, in both builds). On History it carries
`aria-current="page"`, as the others do on theirs; a session page marks
none. Home's link stays, as a count and a shortcut. On a phone the Home
word gives way to the brand so the links fit (§4.25 *The page links fit a
small phone*, *History joins the links*).

*History follows the poll* (2026-10-15). Until then the page read History
once, when opened: an agent that exited kept "running now", a session
