started later never came in, and the counts stayed as they were until the
person opened the page again. Now each Home poll that answered (every 10 s
while the tab is shown, and on a return to it) reads the rows again while
History is shown (`followHistory`): as many as are drawn
(`?limit=<n>` past one page; the server reads at most `HISTORY_PAGE_MAX`),
so an ended session says "ended", a new one comes in on top, and each
row's counts and "N more sessions" are current. `historyFollowed` merges
the answer: its rows, newest first, then the rows drawn past the last of
them, which it did not reach (pushed down by new sessions, or past the
most one read brings), with Show more's cursor kept for those; a row the
read should have brought and did not is no longer listed, and goes. As
the poll's other sections (*The poll keeps your place*, §4.25): the list
is drawn again only when what it shows changed (`sameAsDrawn`, each row by
`rowDrawnFrom`, its moment kept current by `refreshWhen`), then only the
rows that changed (*The rows you read stay still*, 2026-10-15), and the
focus goes back where it was (`pollPlace`/`pollRefocus`: the same row's
Details, Show more, else the page's heading). A read that fails leaves
the rows drawn (a page whose first read failed reads again on the next
poll, and draws its rows then); no read while one of the page's own is
out, nor for a poll asked before one answered (opening the page reads
once, not twice); an answer after the page was left is dropped
(`HISTORY_READS`, the visit). Tests: unit `home-js-history-poll.test.ts`,
stack `tests/stack/history-follows-poll.test.ts` (a real exit and a new
session drawn on the open page by its poll, with no value).

*Sessions sit under their day* (2026-10-19). Until then a row gave its
moment only as relative words, "ended 99 days ago", with the clock time
on hover (compact rows keep the relative form, §4.25u): nothing on the
page said which day a row was from, and two sessions ten hours apart on
two days read alike. Now a heading line goes before the first row of each
day, in the viewer's local time zone: "Today", "Yesterday", then the day
in the words the session page's day lines use (`localDay`, §4.25 *A
session on more than one day names its days*), "Friday, Jul 10", with the
year when it is not this year ("Thursday, Jul 10, 2025"), built by hand
from `WEEKDAYS` and `MONTHS` as `clockWords` is, so every viewer reads the
same words (`dayWords`). A row ended belongs to the day it ended
(`lastAt`); a running row to the day it started (`startedAt`), the moment
its line names. The list is in the server's order (newest activity
first), so a running row that started yesterday sits under its own
"Yesterday" above "Today", and a later "Yesterday" gets a heading of its
own. A row with no time starts no day. The heading is an `h2` under the
page's `h1` (a screen reader goes from day to day), a child of
`#history-list` drawn as a slim line between the rows (`.history-day`:
13 px, `--ink-3`, the row inset, no card), its day the `datetime` of its
`<time>`. The rows do not change: the heading carries the date, and a
row's hover keeps the whole moment. A search, the switch and Show more
draw headings the same way over the rows they keep: all the rows loaded
are drawn together, so a page that Show more brings on the last day drawn
continues it with no second heading, and the first row it brought (not a
heading) takes the focus. The poll keeps them still as it keeps the rows
(*The rows you read stay still*): each heading is a `keepRows` part keyed
by its day (`data-session="day:2026-07-10"`, `:2` for a day listed again),
so one already there stays in place; `refreshWhen` says each heading's
words again from its day on every poll, so past midnight "Today" reads
"Yesterday" with no row drawn again. Home's Running now and Earlier stay
as they are: they are short lists. Nothing new is served. Tests: unit
`home-js-history-days.test.ts` (a fixed clock in Seoul: today, yesterday,
three days ago and last year each once before its rows, a running row
under the day it started, UTC against Seoul, a poll with a new session on
top keeping every heading and row the same node, midnight, Show more on
the same and on a new day, a search), stack
`tests/stack/history-days.test.ts` (`secrets`; a real arbiter, the
anthropic-proxy in production wiring and the launcher's real
`session_exit`, one of them a day later: the served page at 1280 and 390
px draws "Today" and "Yesterday", each an `h2` before its rows, a slim
line that wraps; no value or token on the page, `/api/home/history` or
`/api/home`).

*Back returns to the row you opened* (2026-10-18). Until then a page
change read History again from nothing (`loadHistory(false)`, "A page
change starts over"): after Show more twice and the 60th row's *Details*,
Back showed the first 25 rows at the top, and comparing old sessions meant
pressing Show more again for each one. Now Back or Forward into History
(§4.25 *Back and Forward keep your place*) hands `loadHistory` the place
saved in its entry: it reads as many rows as you had loaded, the first
read `?limit=<n>` (at most `HISTORY_PAGE_MAX` 100) and then
`?after=<id>&limit=<n>` a page at a time (`historyReadOn`) until those rows
and the row you opened are in (it may have been pushed down by sessions that
came in since), at most `HISTORY_RESTORE_MAX` (300) rows. The reads count as
one of the page's own (`h.out`), so the poll (`followHistory`) waits for
them. A read past the first that fails stops there with the rows read, and
Show more goes on from them. Then `historyLand` scrolls to where you were,
brings the opened row into view if the rows moved, and gives it the focus
through `focusMarked`'s `scrolled` path (only if the heading still has it,
so a focus you moved meanwhile stays). A row no longer listed leaves the
place alone. A link to History (Home's *History* link) still starts at one
page, at the top. Nothing new is served. Tests: unit
`home-js-back-restores.test.ts`, stack `tests/stack/history-back-restores.test.ts`
(a real arbiter at `secrets`, the anthropic-proxy in production wiring, 59
launcher `session_exit`s, the served page: Show more twice, row 55's
Details, then Back and then *Back to History* each return at least 55 rows
with row 55 focused and no page of 25 drawn on the way; no value or token).

*Finding a session* (2026-10-18). Until then History was the list and
nothing else: someone after "the session where I asked about
deploy/staging.conf last week" pressed Show more page by page and read
every row, and a daily user has hundreds (Mandu keeps a session's record
for 90 days). Now a search box sits above the list, **Find a session**
(`<form role="search">`, `#history-q`). It keeps the sessions whose
agent's name or prompt label, as the row reads them, holds every word
typed, case aside: `historyMatches` in `view-model/home.ts`, pure, over
`agentName` and `promptLabel` (so a session with a fallback label, which
the row shows as no prompt, is found only by its agent). The server
matches, not the page: `GET /api/home/history?q=<words>` filters the live
agent sessions *before* `historyPage` cuts the page, so `total`, `next`
and Show more count and page through the matches, and the answer adds
`query: { text, all }` (`all`: every session on record). A search is cut
at `HISTORY_QUERY_MAX` (200 characters); a blank one is no search. The
page reads once the typing stops (250 ms), or at once on Enter; a search
that changed starts the list over, as a page change does, and only the
list is drawn again, so the focus stays in the box. The search lives in
the address, `/history?q=staging` (replaced as you type, never one entry
per key): a shared link and Back from a session's page keep it, Back's
reads (`historyReadOn`) and Home's poll (`followHistory`) carry the same
`q` (a poll that dropped it would fill the list again unfiltered), and a
link to History starts without one. With a search, a status line under
the box counts "3 of 214 sessions"; none found reads "No session matches
“staging”." with **Clear**, which empties the box and the address, lists
every session again and gives the box the focus.

*Why the match never reads an original.* The History read is open signed
out (`read-gate.ts`), and a search answers one bit per query: had it
matched originals, anyone who can reach the page could ask "does any
prompt hold `sk_live_…`?" and read a masked value off the row counts, a
character at a time. So it matches only what the row already serves: the
label is derived from what the AI saw (`registry.ts` `sessionLabel` reads
the symbolized input), and before matching each masked item in it is
spelled "[masked]", so neither a secret's value nor its placeholder's own
words find anything. (The row's title still shows the placeholder as
served; the match reads it as "[masked]".) Tests: unit
`view-model/history-search.test.ts` (agent, label, case, every word, no
label, blank, the cap, a label holding a masked key never matched by the
key, a piece of it or the placeholder), jsdom
`home-js-history-search.test.ts` (one read after the typing stops, the
count, `?q=` replaced in the address, the focus kept, Show more and the
poll keep `q`, no match and Clear, `?q=` on load, Enter, a link starts
over), stack `tests/stack/history-search.test.ts` (a real arbiter at
`secrets`, the anthropic-proxy in production wiring, 33 sessions: two
asked about staging, past the first page, found exactly by `?q=staging`
and drawn by the served page; a session whose prompt pasted a registered
key, which the proxy masked, found by its other words but never, signed
out, by the key or a piece of it; no answer carries the value).

*Only the sessions where Mandu stepped in* (2026-10-18). A daily user
has hundreds of sessions on record, and most are ordinary work where Mandu
did nothing; the few a person opens History for (a secret masked, a step
blocked, a value filled in on a send, a question still waiting) were found
only by reading every row, page by page, though each row's counts line
already said so. Now a switch sits under the search box, **Only sessions
where Mandu stepped in** (`#history-only`, a `role="switch"` button in the
session page's switch look, named by its label). Off, the default, the page
is as before. On, the list keeps the sessions whose row says Mandu stepped
in (`steppedIn` in `view-model/home.ts`, pure, read off the row
`homeAgentRow` builds, so the switch keeps exactly the rows whose counts
line says something): a secret masked before the AI saw it or read before
it was marked, an untrusted item masked (a count the row shows only where
the level masks them), a step blocked, a send with a real value filled
in, a question still waiting (`rowContext`), or protection failed (the
leak check's finding, or the listing's verdict for a session that cannot
be read). The server filters, not the page, because a page of 25 might
hold none: `GET /api/home/history?only=stepped-in` (any other value is no
filter) walks the sessions past `after`, counting each as now (`HomeFacts`,
cached per session), and keeps matches until `limit` rows or
`HISTORY_SCAN_BUDGET` (200) sessions looked through (`historyPageWhere`),
so one read never counts every session on record and the first filtered
read of a long history stays quick (the cache makes the next ones cheap).
`next` is the last session looked through, matched or not, so a sparse
history still pages; the answer adds `only: { through }`, the sessions
looked through from the newest. `total` still counts every session (with
`q`, the search's matches: the two filters hold together, the search
first). With the switch on, the status line under the box reads "Showing
the sessions where Mandu stepped in" (with a search, ", of 30 sessions
found"), and Show more, since how many more it will keep is not known
before every session is read, says how far the look went: "Looked through
200 of 950 sessions.", or, a read that found none yet, "Mandu has not
stepped in in the newest 200 of 950 sessions.", never the end while
sessions are left. None at all reads "Mandu has not stepped in in any
session on record." (with a search, "in any session that matches “…”")
with **Show every session**, which turns the switch off and gives it the
focus. Pressing the switch starts the list over, as a search that changed
does, and only the list is drawn again, so the focus stays on it. The
choice lives in the address, `/history?only=stepped-in` (after `q=` when
both, replaced, not pushed): a shared link and Back from a session's page
keep it, Back's reads (`historyReadOn`) and Home's poll (`followHistory`)
carry it, so a running session that gets its first block comes in on top
while the switch is on, and a link to History starts with it off. A poll
whose look ended on its budget before the first row drawn (rows brought by
Show more deep in a sparse history) reached none of them, and
`historyFollowed` keeps them all with their cursor. The read gate is
unchanged: the filter reads the counts the open route already serves
(metadata only, nothing an original could be told from), so a signed-out
read answers the same rows as a signed-in one. Tests: unit
`view-model/history-stepped-in.test.ts` (`steppedIn` per kind and for
none, the row over facts, waiting and the listing's verdict;
`historyPageWhere` keeping matches only, stopping at the limit and at the
budget, `next` going on past a long run of plain sessions, `through`),
component `history-stepped-in.test.ts` (the route over the fixtures and two
plain sessions: the same rows as the plain read keeps, paged; a question
waiting keeps a plain session; with `q`), jsdom
`home-js-history-only.test.ts` (the switch, `?only=` written and read,
Show more's words and reads, the empty state and its button, the poll, Back
and a link), `home-js-routes.test.ts` (the canonical address), stack
`tests/stack/history-stepped-in.test.ts` (`secrets`; a real arbiter, the
anthropic-proxy and the net-proxy in production wiring, three sessions:
plain, a masked `.env` read, a send the net-proxy blocks and the person
answers Block; on shows the two, off all three, on the served page too;
signed out the same rows as with the real sign-in; no value).

*History says what waits for you* (2026-10-16). Until then the History
route never read the approval queue (`buildHistoryFor` passed
`buildHistoryViewModel` no `waiting`), so every row had none: a running
agent that waited for your OK read "running now" with the green dot, where
Home's Running now gave it the amber dot and "Waiting for your OK", and an
ended session whose question still waited said nothing of it, where
Earlier said "1 question waiting for you". History is the only list of
sessions older than Home's window. Now the route reads the policy
snapshot Home reads (`loadPolicySnapshot`, the panel without its cards'
words) and both build their rows with `rowContext(panel)`: each pending
ask counted once, on the session that raised it last (`askedBy`), none
while the queue is not known, and `masking` for the agent notice. So a
row's `state` and `waiting` are Home's. The page draws the count in
Earlier's words, "1 question waiting for you" (the row keeps its prompt,
as Home's rows do, Running now's since 2026-10-18),
and a running session that waits gets Running now's amber dot
(protection failed keeps the red one). The next poll after an answer
draws the row without it. Nothing new is served: the queue and its
session ids are already open (`/api/egress/approvals`, `/api/home`). Tests:
unit `view-model/history-waiting.test.ts` (`rowContext`, History's rows,
Home's and History's rows agree), jsdom `home-js-history-waiting.test.ts`
(the count, the dots, the poll after an answer), component
`history-waiting.test.ts` (the route over a stub snapshot; an older
arbiter's queue from the approvals op; no arbiter), stack
`tests/stack/history-says-waiting.test.ts` (`secrets`; a real arbiter,
the anthropic-proxy in production wiring, the launcher's real
`session_exit`, the production approvals adapter, the served page: a
running and an ended session's questions as Home says them, a Block
over the real route cleared on the poll, no value or token).

*A Show more that fails* (2026-10-15). The product page has two Show more
buttons that read the server for the next page: History's and the file
browser's under Rules › Add a rule (§4.25m). Until then a History Show
more that failed was drawn away, "Could not read more of the history. …"
in its place: the focus it had fell to `<body>` (a button turned off drops
it) and nothing tried again until a poll brought the button back. The
file browser's said nothing when its read failed, and when it answered,
the list was drawn again without the button and the focus fell to
`<body>` too. Now, on both:

- a read that fails says why where the count was (History: "Could not
  read more of the history. The protection service is not running.";
  the file browser, over the button: "Could not read more of this folder:
  That folder does not exist. Use ~ to go to your home folder.", an error
  the server worded after a colon as a typed pattern's row says one,
  `moreRefusal`, else the page's own words for the cause, a stopped
  service with its link to Settings). Show more stays, on, described by
  those words (`aria-describedby`), and a press reads the same page again;
- the focus that fell with the press comes back to Show more after a
  failure; after an answer it goes to the first thing it brought (a
  History row, as before; a file's tick box, else Show more again when
  the filter hides all it brought, else the last row shown). A focus the
  person moved while the read was out stays where it is;
- the words go with the next answer, a poll's answer (History) or a new
  listing of the folder (the file browser).

Tests: unit `home-js-show-more-answers.test.ts` (both buttons: a failure's
words per cause, the button kept, described and focused, the same cursor
read again, the first new row focused, a moved focus kept, the words
dropped; all five fail before), stack `tests/stack/show-more-answers.test.ts`
(`secrets`; a real arbiter, the anthropic-proxy in production wiring, the
launcher's real `session_exit`, the production adapter and a served page:
History's Show more with the service stopped and started again, the file
browser's over a real folder of 502 entries renamed away and back; no
rendered page carries a value or a token).

**What the leak check found** (agent page, under the tiles;
`leakFinding`, `AgentPageVM.finding`, null when the check never fired).
Each place a recorded event says something reached the AI without its mask
(the timeline's flagged rows, one per step), oldest first, at most
`FINDING_CAP` (20) and the rest counted:

- a tool call's result: "At 10:42, the result of this step reached the AI
  without a mask: Read `.env`. It held your secret `PASTE_KEY`." (the step's
  own words, its secrets by name);
- a request to the AI: "At 10:43, a request to the AI carried an item as it
  was, though Mandu had masked it.";
- anything else: "At …, a step reached the AI without a mask."

A time the story shows is a button that opens its step (`stepLink`, as a
*Your secrets* card's). The check's own detail is never read: the proxies'
`invariantDetail` quotes up to 120 characters of the span that survived
its mask, which can be a secret's value. A value appears only where the
step already shows one, signed in (*Show what was hidden*, *Show the real
value*). The same quote was served signed out by `/api/events` until now:
`redactEvent` keeps `violatedInvariant` and drops `detail`. Without the
developer view, the unmasked step's note, an OS step that did and *Your
secrets*' flagged line point here: "What the leak check found, at the top
of this page, says what." (`FINDING_POINTER`).

**Where each release after a check went** (*Your secrets*, both builds). An
`approved` lineage edge (an arbiter egress request a check let through)
records its event; the line now names each place and time, in time order,
the first `RELEASES_SHOWN` (5), then "and N more": "Mandu released it 3 more
times after a check: to `api.example.com` at 10:42; in a command at 10:43;
to `hooks.example.org` at 10:44." `releaseWhere` reads a structured
`destination`, else the host the masked request names ("… to host"), else
the boundary ("off this machine", "in a command", "to a file"), else "to a
place its record does not name"; releases with no time to the same place
read once, counted. A time a shown step shows opens it. Never a token: the
host comes from the AI's own (masked) form.

**The whole original** past `HIDDEN_CAP` (4000 characters). Signed in, an
original the page cut shows **Show the whole original** under it while the
box is open; it reads `GET /api/home/original?session=<id>&step=<step id>`
and puts the text in the box, which takes the focus (a refusal says why
beside it). The route is `admin` in `READ_ROUTES` (403 signed out, before it
runs), builds the page as the signed-in agent page is with that step's cap
lifted to `ORIGINAL_ALL_CAP` (1,000,000; `AgentPageShow.original`, which the
page's own query never sets), and answers that step's original only: a step
whose original holds a secret has none (404), as on the page.

**Each background step.** The background line ("In the background: 4
connections to `api.anthropic.com`; 1 command Mandu checked.") gets **List
them** in both builds. It asks the page again with
`&background=<turn id>` (repeatable, at most `SHOW_STEPS_MAX`, under the
agent page's `projection` row), and that turn's `routine.items` lists each
step oldest first, up to `BACKGROUND_ALL_CAP` (1000, `moreItems` past it):
"Connected to `api.anthropic.com` (4 times)", "Mandu checked a command:
`git status`" (a masked item a chip), "Translated a file path …". The first
line takes the focus (`landAgent` kind `background`); the polls keep asking,
as for the other *Show them*. The button sits in the line's row, before its
words, so the line still ends its turn until the list comes.

**Only where Mandu stepped in** (2026-10-18). Most turns of a real session
are ordinary work where Mandu did nothing, yet each was a full card: at 60
turns, finding the one block meant scrolling tens of thousands of pixels.
A switch beside the *What happened* heading (`#agent-only`, a
`role="switch"` button in the Settings › Protection switch's look, named
by its label) reads "Only where Mandu stepped in (4 of 23 turns)", counting
the turns the page drew. Off, the default, the page is as before. On, each
run of **quiet** turns folds into one line in its place ("5 turns where
Mandu did nothing", `.story-quiet`), whose **Show them** / **Hide them**
(`aria-expanded`, described by the line) shows them in place. A turn is
quiet when its `tone` is `plain` (every step plain, no workspace masking)
and it has no note under your message (`promptNote`: the prompt filter
changed it). The spec first keyed this on a null `summary`, but
`turnSummary` is null only for a turn with no step at all; a turn of
ordinary steps says "Nothing here needed guarding." and is quiet too. A
message Mandu stopped (an unplaced note's card) is never quiet and breaks
a run, and the turn an ask opened the page for (`?ask=`, `vm.focus`) never
folds, so its run splits around it. The switch reads nothing from the
server (the page has every turn it drew) and keeps the focus. Its state is
kept for the visit (`S.agentOnly`; a poll that draws the page again folds
it again, and the runs you opened stay open, by their first turn,
`storyToggles`) and in the address, `?only=stepped-in`, replaced, not
pushed, as History's search is (any other value reads as off): a link
written with it opens the page filtered, Back and Forward and a typed
address keep it, a link inside the product opens the session whole. A
focus the fold hides (in a turn of a run it folds, or after a redraw
whose run is new and so closed) goes to the button of the line it folds
into, never the heading or `<body>` (`quietRefocus`); a time that opens a
step (`showStep`) and a *Show them* that brings earlier turns
(`landAgent`) open or land on a folded run. Tests:
`test/unit/ui/home-js-agent-only.test.ts` (jsdom: the count, the runs and
their lines in place, a stepped-in turn and a prompt note never folded,
the focus turn never folded, `?only=` read and written, a link opening it
whole, a poll keeping the switch and an opened run, the focus to the
line), `home-js-routes.test.ts` (`parseRoute` / the canonical address),
and across the real arbiter, anthropic-proxy and net-proxy
`tests/stack/agent-only-stepped-in.test.ts` (seven turns: a masked `.env`
read and a send the net-proxy blocks among ordinary reads and a reply;
`?only=stepped-in` shows exactly those two, three lines count the rest,
a line's button brings its turns back, off shows all; no value or token on
the page).

**Tests.** `test/unit/view-model/agent-page-trace.test.ts` (the finding's
places, words, step links and cap; the projection drops the quote and keeps
the flag; `show.background` and its cap, a chip for a masked command;
`agentShowOf` reads `background` and never `original`; `show.original` past
`HIDDEN_CAP` and none for a secret; `historyPage` paging and the system
logs; `buildHistoryViewModel` rows), `secret-story.test.ts` (each release's
place and time, `RELEASES_SHOWN`, the pointer without the developer view),
`agent-page-show.test.ts` (the unmasked notes' pointer),
`test/unit/ui/home-js-history-trace.test.ts` (product-only build: Home's
link opens History, rows to agent pages, **Show more** and its focus, empty
and failed reads; the finding block and its step links; **List them** and
its focus; **Show the whole original** signed in, its refusal, and none
signed out), `home-js-no-dev.test.ts` (the History link in both builds),
`test/component/product-trace.test.ts` (a server with no extensions over
the fixtures: `/history` served, `/api/home/history` paged and with no
payload signed out, the flagged session's finding signed out and in with
no quote, `/api/events` signed out without the quote,
`/api/home/original` 403 / 200 / 404 / 400, `?background=`),
`test/component/value-gate.test.ts` and `tests/stack/dashboard-value-gate.test.ts`
(both new rows walked signed out with a canary; signed in, the whole-original
route never carries a secret), and across the real arbiter and
anthropic-proxy `tests/stack/product-history-trace.test.ts` (a product-only
dashboard: History lists the session counted, its row opens the agent
page, whose Read shows *What the AI saw* against *What really happened*
with no value or token signed out, and no link into `/dev/`).

#### 4.25af On web pages: a browser agent's run (2026-10-18)

A browser agent under `mandu --browser-cdp` (jev-ultrafast) talks to its own
AI services, so no conversation passes through Mandu's model proxy, and its
page used to say only "No conversation was recorded for this session". The
DevTools relay now sends its trace (`browser_action` events,
devtools-relay.md §5.1), and the page shows a block **On web pages** under
*Your secrets* (`view-model/browser-story.ts`, `AgentPageVM.browser`; home.js
`renderAgentBrowser`), one line each, secret names only (the field of a
placeholder: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`; "a secret" without one):

- what was masked in what the agent read from the pages, and how many times,
  or that no secret of the person's was on them;
- each secret the agent typed: filled in on a site it may go to (the site's
  host), or not typed on a page that may not receive it;
- a masked value the agent typed that is none of the person's secrets (a
  mistyped or made-up placeholder, the relay's `unknown placeholder`,
  devtools-relay.md §3.2; 2026-10-19), one amber line with its count and no
  name (the name it spelled is not a secret of theirs): nothing was typed
  and the agent was told to copy it exactly as the page shows it;
- each kind of command Mandu stopped (screenshot, cookie read, debugging
  access…), with why in plain words;
- page messages held back because they could not be checked;
- each AI service the agent called itself (the egress proxy's forwarded
  requests whose secrets were sent masked, `keptOpaque`), with the request
  count and the secrets that went masked.

With no turn, the story line under *What happened* says no conversation went
through Mandu and points to the block. A session without a browser has no
block. Tests: `test/unit/view-model/browser-story.test.ts` (each line from
its events, names only, no placeholder anywhere in the data), and
`tests/stack/cdp-relay.test.ts` (the relay's events read back from a real
event store, the story built from them).

### 4.26 🖥 VM matrix — the OS test matrix's recorded runs

**What.** The inspector's **Tests › VM matrix** sub-page (`/dev/tests/vm`,
§4.32; a ▶ Run drawer tab before). It shows the runs
`scripts/matrix/run.sh` records under `<state>/mandu/matrix/<runId>/`
(`os-test-matrix.md` §9), which otherwise exist only as the tail of the
terminal that ran them.

**Layout (`dev/js/matrix.js`).**

- **Grid.** One row per target, one column per suite. The axes are the
  declared `SUITES=` of each `scripts/matrix/targets/*.conf` when the checkout
  is there (an installed bundle has none, so only recorded pairs show), plus
  any pair seen in a recorded run. A cell shows the pair's latest run: ✓/✗/–,
  commit, age, and a `live` chip for a fresh-install run with the live leg. A
  declared pair with no run says "never run" and its tooltip gives the
  command; an undeclared pair is hatched; a recorded but undeclared pair
  carries a "not declared" chip.
- **Detail.** The newest run, or the clicked cell or history row: result
  (with the guest's RESULT reason), commit and ref, time and duration,
  executor and host, labels; the suite's `steps.log` parsed into
  PASS/FAIL/NOTE rows; log buttons (`suite.log`, `run.log`, `serial.log` on a
  FAIL, the `all` suite's `logs-<pkg>.log`) fetched on click into a `<pre>`.
  The file route needs the admin session (§6). Signed out it answers 403,
  and a line under the buttons says "Sign in to read this log: run `mandu
  dashboard` in your own terminal and open the sign-in link it prints. A
  log can print a real value, so the dashboard shows it only after you sign
  in." with no log box. Any other failure keeps "could not load
  `suite.log`". Until 2026-10-09 a 403 read as that failure.
- **History.** Every recorded run, newest first, with step tallies.

**Server (the developer view's `matrix-runs.ts` and `matrix-routes.ts`).** GET only:

    GET /api/matrix                     {grid, runs}
    GET /api/matrix/runs/<id>           {meta, steps, files}
    GET /api/matrix/runs/<id>/file/<f>  whitelisted: meta.json, suite/steps/run/serial.log, logs-<pkg>.log

The run id and file name each match a fixed shape (no separators, no
traversal). A directory without a valid `meta.json` is skipped, never an
error for the whole list. `matrixDir` is `defaultMatrixDir()`, the path
table's `matrix-results` (`${MANDU_HOME:-~/.mandu}/runs/matrix`, the same rule
as `record.sh`; on-disk-layout.md §5); without it every `/api/matrix` route
answers 404.

**No run button, on purpose.** A VM run takes 6 to 40 minutes, needs KVM, and
the fresh-install live leg hands a guest a copy of the operator's agent
login. Starting it is a deliberate terminal action; the empty states name the
command. **Guest output is text:** step text and logs (the live leg's model
reply among them) are inserted with `textContent` only.

**Tests.** `matrix-runs.test.ts`, `matrix-js.test.ts` (jsdom; signed out,
the sign-in line), and the `matrix-area` e2e (the real `run.sh host smoke`
into a temp store, read back through a real `DashboardServer`). The stack e2e
`tests/stack/inspector-logs-signed-out.test.ts` covers the log signed out and
in (§6).

### 4.27 CI — recorded CI runs

**What.** The inspector's **Tests › CI** sub-page (`/dev/tests/ci`, §4.32;
the ▶ Run drawer's ⚑ CI tab before). It reads the CI run records the VM
collector writes. `scripts/ci/vm-run.sh` runs the per-push suites in a disposable KVM guest
(anyone can run it, `continuous-integration.md` §6); its collector
(`scripts/ci/collect-results.mjs`) validates the guest's results and copies
each run's `summary.json`, `junit.xml` and `logs/<entry-id>.log` into the path
table's `ci-runs` directory, `${MANDU_HOME:-~/.mandu}/runs/ci/<run>/`. The
dashboard reads only that directory: it fetches nothing from any CI service
and holds no token. It is a tool sub-page, not a page of the nav: the pages
are about the protected sessions, and CI results are an operator's lookup. The product page
`/` does not show it.

**Layout (`dev/js/ci.js`).**

- **Freshness line.** "newest run 3 hours ago" with its local time, the number
  of runs listed and of invalid runs skipped (reasons in its tooltip). Past a
  day without a finished run it turns amber: a CI that stopped running is
  otherwise green by absence.
- **Red default-branch banner.** When the newest recorded run of `master`
  from a hosted pipeline (`source: gitlab`) is `fail` or `error`, a banner
  names that run, its commit, finish time and reason, and how many such runs
  in a row were red, so a branch's red run is not misread as its own failure.
  It is advisory: only runs recorded on this host are seen, and the summaries
  are untrusted (a forged run could raise the banner; a forged green one must
  still validate). No such run, a green one, or an older server leaves it
  empty.
- **Runs**, newest first by `finished`: a PASS / FAIL / ERROR badge, ref,
  short commit, a `source` chip, finish time, duration (and an `error` run's
  `reason`), then one line per kind (`test-organization.md` §3 order) with its
  summed pass, fail and skip counts and how many of its entries are red.
- **One run** (the newest by default): result and reason, full commit,
  source, start and finish, image, stages; then the entries table (kind,
  result, pass, fail, skip, time), **failures first** (fail, error, timeout,
  skip, pass; then kind order, then id). An entry with a log has a `log`
  button; a red run opens its first red entry's log, as text, its `not ok`
  blocks marked and listed (`entry-log.js`, shared with the Tests page,
  §4.35).
- **A failure outside the tests reads INFRASTRUCTURE** (`ci.js
  failureSide`). An `error` run produced no test verdict (its `reason` says
  why: "qemu exited 1", a guest timeout, "run-suites exited 2 without
  writing summary.json", unreadable results), and a `fail` with no red
  entry, or with a failed stage other than the suites (the build, the
  guest's setup), is the same. Such a run's badge reads INFRASTRUCTURE
  (amber), its tooltip and its detail's result line say "a failure outside
  the tests"; a run with a red entry reads FAIL. The sub-menu's count reads
  `master red` when the banner shows (§4.35).

**Server (the developer view's `ci-runs.ts` and `ci-routes.ts`).** GET only:

    GET /api/ci/runs                     {runsDir, dirExists, runs, omitted, invalid, rejected, staleness, master}
    GET /api/ci/runs/<run>               {summary, stages, entries}   entries failures first, each with logAvailable
    GET /api/ci/runs/<run>/log/<entry>   text/plain: the log's last 1 MiB (X-Mandu-Log-Truncated, X-Mandu-Log-Size)

`staleness` is `{newestFinished, ageSec}`. `master` (`masterStatus`) is
`{red, run, commit, finished, result, reason, streak, since}` for the banner,
or null. Each listed run carries its kind rollups (`kinds[]`: kind, worst
entry result, entries by result, summed counts; an older summary's `tier` is
read as the kind). The routes sit behind the same source-IP gate, Basic auth
and session as every route. Being reads, they need no CSRF header. The log
route also needs the admin session (the read gate, §6: a log can print a
value). Signed out, it answers 403, and the log's place says "Sign in to read
this log: run `mandu dashboard` …" (the sentence §4.26 quotes), with no log
box. That holds for the red log the page opens by itself too. Any other
failure keeps "could not load the log of `<entry>`". Until 2026-10-09 a 403
read as that failure. `ciRunsDir` is `defaultCiRunsDir()` (the path table's `ci-runs`, the
collector's rule); without it every `/api/ci` route answers 404.

**The runs directory is untrusted.** Code from the commit under test produced
every file in it, so the reader trusts none of it:

- Every `summary.json` is re-validated against schema 1, strictly: an unknown
  field at any level, a wrong type, a value outside its enum (results,
  `source` `gitlab|local`), an id outside `^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,120}$` (or `.`
  / `..`), a log path other than exactly `logs/<id>.log`, a duplicate entry
  id, control or bidi characters, a non-hex commit, a non ISO-8601 time, or a
  `run` that differs from its directory name rejects the whole run, which is
  skipped and counted (`invalid`, up to 20 `rejected` reasons), never
  half-shown.
- Nothing follows a symlink: directories are checked with `lstat`, every
  file is opened `O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK` and must be a regular file on the
  opened descriptor (a FIFO cannot hang a request). Hidden names (the
  collector's staging) are ignored.
- Sizes are capped: a `summary.json` over 1 MiB rejects its run; a log answer
  is its last 1 MiB behind a `[… log truncated …]` marker, with terminal
  escapes and control characters stripped. At most 200 runs are listed and
  5,000 directory entries looked at; parsed summaries are cached by inode,
  size and mtime.
- A request names a run and an entry only by ids that pass the same pattern,
  and a log is served only for an entry its run's valid summary lists, so no
  URL reaches outside the runs directory. The log route answers `text/plain`
  with `nosniff` and a `sandbox` CSP. `ci.js` inserts every field with
  `textContent` and has no `innerHTML`.

CI sessions never enter the live event store.

**Tests.** `ci-runs.test.ts` (validation, the projection, the log tail,
readers over a hostile runs dir: symlinks, an oversized summary, a FIFO);
`ci-js.test.ts` (jsdom, hostile text lands as text, INFRASTRUCTURE and
`failureSide`, the count, a refused log's sign-in line); the `ci-area` e2e (a
real `DashboardServer` over a hostile fixture dir: the routes, traversal, the
1 MiB cap, Basic auth, the real `server-main`'s default runs dir).

### 4.28 ⟲ Replay drills — the replay runner's recorded runs

The replay runner and the differential harness are the maintainers' and are
not in the public tree (§4.22); the re-run commands below run in the
maintainers' repository.

**What.** The inspector's fourth sidebar group (§4.10) and its session panel
(test-reorganization.md §7.1–§7.3). The replay runner (§6.7 there) runs each
drill under Mandu and the plain agent beside it, in a CI guest or a throwaway
home, each against a private arbiter, so its sessions are in no arbiter this
dashboard talks to. It writes a run record instead, which the CI collector
copies into the host's store:

    ${MANDU_HOME:-~/.mandu}/runs/drills/replay/<runId>/
      run.json                   ReplayRunMeta (schema 1)
      sessions/<key>.json        ReplaySessionRecord (schema 1), one per drill × agent × size
      events-<key>.ndjson        the Mandu arbiter's events plus one `assertion` event
      casts/<key>.mandu.cast     asciicast v2 of the Mandu side
      casts/<key>.plain.cast     asciicast v2 of the plain agent (the control)
      panes/<key>/<file>         pane captures

The record shapes are `replay-model.ts`'s; the dashboard
keeps its own copy in `src/replay-run-store.ts`, because the packages ship
standalone. A record names each file by exactly one shape (`casts.mandu` null
or `casts/<key>.mandu.cast`, and so on). The store is `defaultReplayRunsDir()`,
the path table's `replay-drill-runs`. As with the CI tab, nothing fetches from
CI or holds a token. The dashboard's validator is a SUPERSET of the runner's:
whatever `replay-model.ts` accepts, this accepts (its extra consistency
checks, such as the derived key or the recomputed tally, are the writer's
business; the reader only needs the record safe to show).

**The store is untrusted** (test-reorganization.md §10): code under test wrote
every file in it. `src/replay-run-store.ts` follows `ci-runs.ts` (§4.27):

- Every `run.json` and record is re-validated against schema 1 as strictly
  as a CI summary (unknown fields including `__proto__`, types, enums, id and
  key patterns, plain relative file paths, control or bidi text, the runner's
  size caps, a check time outside `[0, durationS]`), and must sit where it
  says: `runId` is its directory's name and `sessionId` is exactly
  `<runId>/<key>`, so a record cannot pose as another run's session. A
  rejected run or record is skipped and counted, never half-shown. Nothing
  follows a symlink (`lstat` on every directory, `O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK`
  and a regular-file check on every file).
- Sizes are capped: `run.json` 64 KiB, a record 4 MiB, an events log or cast
  32 MiB (read whole or refused), a pane capture its last 1 MiB (cleaned of
  terminal codes). Each reader has its own listing window, kept apart from the
  store's disk retention: `/api/replay` lists the newest 300 runs
  (`REPLAY_LIST_LIMIT`), the recorded event source the newest 50
  (`REPLAY_SESSIONS_RUN_LIMIT`), the drill matrix the newest 50
  (`REPLAY_RUN_LIMIT`, §4.29); 5,000 directory entries and 500 records per run
  are looked at. Parsed files are cached by identity; the listings read only
  the runs they list, and only each record's head (§4.30).
- **A lost run is shown as gone, not as broken.** The collector prunes the
  store to the newest 300 runs (continuous-integration.md §6), at least every
  listing window above, so a prune never removes a run a view shows (a test
  pins that relation). A pruned run is first renamed to a hidden name, so a
  listing sees it whole or not at all; a run gone between `readdir` and its
  reads is skipped, not counted invalid, and its detail, files and trace then
  answer 404 or empty (`test/component/replay-retention.test.ts`).

**Server (the developer view's `replay-routes.ts`).** GET only, behind the same gates as
every route:

    GET /api/replay                         {replayDir, dirExists, runs, omitted, invalid, rejected}
    GET /api/replay/runs/<run>              {run, meta, sessions: [{record, available}], invalidSessions, rejected}
    GET /api/replay/runs/<run>/file/<name>  one allowlisted file; <name> URL-encoded

A run lists `verdicts` (PASS, WARN, FAIL, TIMEOUT counts), its sessions and
invalid sessions, and `finishedAt`. `available` says which of a session's
casts and events log exist as regular files. The file route serves, for a
session its run's valid records list, only: `run.json` and
`sessions/<key>.json` as their VALIDATED re-serialization (never the bytes on
disk); `events-<key>.ndjson` and the two casts as bytes, only when the record
names exactly that file; `panes/<key>/<file>` as cleaned text. Every answer
carries `nosniff` and a `sandbox` CSP. Without a store every `/api/replay`
route answers 404.

**The recorded event source (`src/event-source/recorded-source.ts`).** So a
replay row opens with its trace like any session, `RecordedEventSource`
serves each valid record's session under the namespaced id `<runId>/<key>`
(every private arbiter mints ids from zero, so runs would otherwise collide):
the row (`SessionRef.replay`: drill, agent, lane, size, mode, verdict, tally,
which recordings exist, `recordLost` when the record names the Mandu cast and
it is gone, §4.22; `batchId` = the run id) and the events, each stamped with
the namespaced id. `subscribe` is a no-op. `CompositeEventSource` puts it
beside a tenant's store: `listSessions` merges the two (a failing recorded
side leaves the store's list), each per-session call goes to the source that
owns the id (`sourceFor`; no store mints an id of that shape), deleting a
recorded session is refused (403), and no store-wide op is forwarded. An id
both sides list (possible only for an own-arbiter run's un-namespaced ids,
§4.22) is listed once, the recorded side's row, where its reads go.

Which routes see recorded sessions:

- **`/api/sessions`, `/api/events`, `/api/stream`, `DELETE /api/session`** use
  the composite for every tenant (the sessions are in no tenant's arbiter;
  their group is Replay drills, §4.10).
- **`/api/events` for a recorded id reads the recorded source ALONE**, which
  has no `desymbolize`. A recorded log's `$MDU:*` tokens belong to the private
  arbiter that minted them; resolving them against the live arbiter would show
  the live table's values under a recorded trace (and let the code under test
  choose which), so the trace's reveal never runs for a recorded session.
- **`/api/git` and `/api/fs` keep the store**: they read host files at paths
  the events name, and a recorded log's paths are untrusted output. A recorded
  id there finds no events and answers the honest empty state.
- **The product page `/` is unchanged**: `/api/home` and every product route
  read the tenant's store, so a replay session never appears there.

**The panel (`dev/js/replay.js`).** It shows when the selected session is a
recorded one (`mdu:session-selected` with a `<runId>/<key>` id; the 🎬 Watch
panel stays hidden), fetches `/api/replay/runs/<run>`, and fills the drill
strip's tabs (§4.35):

- **Recording & checks** (`#replay-panel` in `#tab-recording`): **two
  players on one clock**, the Mandu recording and the plain agent's side by
  side, the Mandu clock mapped onto the plain one piecewise-linearly between
  shared turn starts (`dev/js/cast-clock.js alignTime`), so play, pause and
  every seek drive both (signed out each cell says "Sign in to watch this
  recording: …" in place of its player and "▶ play both" is hidden, §6;
  a cast gone after the read says "Record lost"); the turn chips; then the
  **checks** as one compact
  table (check · kind · plain · Mandu · expected · at, security first), a
  row unfolding its evidence and seeking both recordings to the moment it
  was decided (its `at`, differential-interactive.md §25). A
  `not-exercised` check says "gate not reached on the plain run".
- **Setup** (`#replay-setup`): drill, lane, mode, agent and version, script
  origin, the run's source, ref and commit, the session id, the start and
  length, the command that re-runs this one drill (`cd tests &&
  MANDU_DIFF_ONLY=<drill> MANDU_DIFF_LANES=<lane> MANDU_DIFF_SIZES=<size> npm
  run drills:replay:diff` for claude, `MANDU_DIFF_AGENT=<agent>
  MANDU_DIFF_ONLY=<drill> npm run drills:replay:diff-agents` for the others)
  and every replay drill (`scripts/test-all.sh --kind replay-drill`), and
  the baseline and its origin.
- **Files** (`#replay-files`): links to the files that exist.
- The verdict, with its security, utility and fidelity tallies, as chips in
  the session header (app.js, from the head replay.js publishes,
  `mdu:drill-head`); the trace is the Trace tab.

A missing recording says why. Every field is inserted with `textContent`.

**Tests.** `replay-run-store.test.ts` (validation, the file allowlist,
readers over a hostile store); `event-source/recorded-source.test.ts` (rows,
the composite's routing and delete refusal); `ui/replay-js.test.ts` (the
panel in jsdom, shared seeks, hostile text as text); the `replay-area` e2e (a
real `DashboardServer` over a hostile store: traversal and symlinks, the
trace, `/api/git`, a product home without replay sessions, Basic auth, the
runner's golden run `tests/fixtures/replay-run/`); and
`replay-dashboard-parity.test.ts` (the fixture copy identical to
the runner's; the dashboard accepts every variant the runner accepts and both
refuse the hostile ones).

### 4.29 ▦ Drill matrix and ◫ Coverage — two views across runs

**What.** Two tool sub-pages (§4.32): **Drills › Matrix**
(`/dev/drills/matrix`) and **Tests › Coverage** (`/dev/tests/coverage`),
beside VM matrix (§4.26) and CI (§4.27); both were ▶ Run drawer tabs before;
test-reorganization.md §7.4. Both read
records that already exist; neither starts a run, and the product page `/`
shows neither.

- **▦ Drill matrix** (`dev/js/drill-matrix.js`). A row per catalog drill
  (`drills.json`, catalog order), a column per replay
  agent (claude, codex, openclaw, opencode) and per live agent × model seen in
  the live store (at most 24, most recently run kept). A cell shows the newest
  run's verdict (PASS, WARN, FAIL, TIMEOUT, and in a live column PAUSED: the
  model's safeguards paused the drill, ranked between TIMEOUT and WARN) and a
  strip of up to 12 earlier runs, oldest left. A run's verdict is its WORST
  session's, and the cell links that session (`mdu:go-session`): a replay cell
  opens the replay panel (§4.28), a live cell the recording panel (§4.22). A
  cell no run touched shows `·` (or the drill's replay form when it has no
  script: `no script`, `off`, `frozen`); a cell the catalog rules out shows
  `n/a` with the reason on hover. A live cell of a drill with no live form
  says why (since 2026-10-16: `drills.json` carries the catalog's
  `live.skip` as `liveSkip`, so the hover reads "no live form: the
  administrator's layer: …", not the bare words). **Replay passes but live warns, at a
  glance:** a row where an agent's replay verdict differs from a live model's
  carries an amber band and a `≠` badge naming each pair, and a filter keeps
  those rows. Other filters: not passing, hide frozen (protection-modes.md §10),
  area, id or title, or the drill's short index exactly (`util-c7`, any
  case) or its area and axis (`util-i`: every frozen util drill; the first
  2026-10-16 spelling, `ucon-7` or `uint`, reads as these). `?drill=<id>`
  (since 2026-10-18: the link from Drills › Videos to the drill a promo
  scene films, drill-runner.md §3.11) marks that row and scrolls to it once;
  when the filters hide it they are lifted and the search names it, and an
  id the matrix lacks is ignored. The page keeps `?drill=` in the address
  bar while it shows (`pages.js` `parseDrillFocus`, `withDrillFocus`). A row leads with
  that index (`util-c5`, the badge its replay and live rows carry, §4.35); the
  catalog's `short` and `was` are validated with the other fields (a
  malformed one, or one another drill holds, skips the drill). The summary line counts drills, runs, disagreements,
  rows not passing, frozen drills, skipped records, and sessions of drills the
  catalog no longer lists. Hide frozen starts checked (2026-10-16): the
  frozen drills run only on purpose, so the page opens on the ones that run.
  The table scrolls both ways under a pinned header: the `drill` header
  spans both header rows and holds the top-left corner, and the second row
  sticks under the first at its measured height. (A blank corner cell in the
  second row used to scroll away sideways and shift every agent header off
  its column.)

  **A live cell counts the drill as the catalog has it (2026-10-17).** A
  live session counts only when it ran at the drill's OWN setting (the
  catalog's `setting`; each chapter records the setting it ran at). Until
  2026-10-17 every graded live chapter landed in its agent × model cell,
  whatever its setting, so a demo battery's baseline runs (a `baseline-*`
  setting runs the agent with no Mandu, and its FAIL, the secret leaking
  with no protection, is the measurement) sat in the same claude × sonnet
  cell as Mandu's and made the demo drills read as mostly failing. Now a
  session at a baseline, at a control (`off`, `off-cc-mask`, a
  `*-no-reply-filter` setting) or of a frozen drill forced to `secrets` is
  in no cell and no live column, and is never silently dropped: the answer
  counts them (`excluded`: sessions, runs, and per setting how many, each
  marked baseline or not) and the summary line says "N live sessions at
  another setting than the drill's own not shown (M baseline: no Mandu) —
  see Comparison", whose button opens Drills › Comparison (§4.32b), where
  they are shown beside Mandu's. Without a catalog (no drill's own setting
  to compare with) the settings a drill never sits at (the catalog's
  forced-only ones, mirrored in the developer view and held equal by a
  parity test) are left out the same way, and a chapter naming no setting
  at all (older than settings) still counts. Replay cells are untouched:
  a replay run is the drill's own script. The other views were checked for
  the same mixing: the Drill sessions list groups by run (one run is one
  setting), and since 2026-10-17 a run forced to a forced-only setting
  names it in its label (`🎬 watch · demo-scam-email · at
  baseline-cc-mask`), so its FAIL reads as that setting's; Drills › Agents
  and Tests › CI read CI entry results (a battery entry passes when every
  side ran to a grade), not session verdicts; the product page shows no
  drill verdicts.

  **A stand-in's runs are not the model's (2026-10-18).** A rehearsal (the
  demo battery's scripted stand-in, which plays each drill's own script, or
  any other stand-in model on the machine) records the model name it
  launched the agent with, so its runs used to land in the real model's
  cell: demo-c8's sonnet cell read PASS, the scripted battery's newest
  verdict, while its one real Sonnet run had failed. The run's record now says who
  answered (`meta.json` `standIn`: `scripted` or `external`; a run from
  before the field is known by the stand-in line at the head of its run
  log, read bounded), and the live columns are agent × model × stand-in:
  the real model's column first, then the same model tagged **scripted**,
  then tagged **stand-in**. Each column summarizes its own runs only (the
  last verdict, the strip, the count), and its per-column read limit is
  its own, so a stand-in run can neither stand in for nor push out a real
  run. A stand-in cell's verdict is muted grey and dash-bordered (not a
  model's green or red), the tag in its header and cell, and every tooltip
  says it proves the launch and the plumbing, not how a model behaves. A
  stand-in column is in no replay-versus-live disagreement. The summary
  counts the live runs a stand-in answered (`sources.live.standIn`);
  "hide stand-in runs" (off at first) drops those columns. The Videos
  page marks a rehearsal take the same way.
- **◫ Coverage** (`dev/js/coverage.js`). The §5.2 table of
  test-reorganization.md: a row per property, a column per kind (all but
  `install`), the row's status (OK, WARN, NONE) exactly as `suites.mjs
  coverage --json` computes it, never recomputed here. A cell shows its suite
  count and one mark per suite: the result of the suite's last recorded run
  (✓ ✗ ! ⏱ –) or `·` when this host has none. The last run is the newer of
  the suite's last CI run (§4.27) and its last run from Tests › Run a suite
  (below); the mark says which. A CI mark opens Tests › CI on that run with
  the entry's log (`mdu:ci-open`); a Run-a-suite mark opens that run's row
  and, where the run kept one, that entry's log (`mdu:test-open {runId,
  entry}`, §4.35), each asking for its page with `mdu:go-page`. **Gaps** are a row that is not OK, or a suite of a
  per-push kind above unit (component, stack, replay-drill, sandbox) with no
  recorded run or a red one; "only gaps" keeps those rows.

**Server.** GET only (anything else 405), behind the same gates as every
route:

    GET /api/drill-matrix   {catalog, columns: {replay, live, liveDropped}, rows, outside, excluded, totals, history, sources}
    GET /api/coverage       {available, reason?, kinds, rows: [{property, status, cells: {kind: [{id, last}]}}], totals, ci, tests}

- `src/drill-matrix.ts` reads the catalog index through `bounded-read.ts`
  (4 MiB, no symlink, regular file) and validates each drill on its own (only
  the fields it uses survive; a bad or duplicate one is skipped and counted).
  Without a source checkout the rows are the drills the records name, marked
  "not in the catalog". Replay runs come from the strict store reader (§4.28,
  newest 50); live runs from `listWatchRuns` / `readRun` (§4.22). Which live
  runs are read is decided from the run summaries, no report read
  (`selectLiveRuns`, 2026-10-17): a run none of whose drills ran at its own
  setting (a battery's baseline runs) can reach no cell, so it is not read
  and its graded sessions go straight into `excluded` (per scenario, else
  the run's one setting); the limits count only the rest, newest first, at
  most 50 per agent × model column (a model-matrix run counts in each of its
  models' columns) and 300 in all (`sources.live.skipped` and `beyond` say
  how many were not read, and the summary line says so). Until then the
  newest 100 runs were read whatever their setting, so one battery (90 runs
  of baselines and Mandu) pushed the other agents' runs off the matrix.
  That reader is tolerant, so every field the matrix uses is checked again
  (agent, model name, verdict, ISO start, a plain session id: a path is no
  link, a setting of the settings' form), and a live run is kept only when
  its own `meta.json` agrees with its directory name, so a run cannot pose
  as another or count twice. The catalog's `settings` (each one's title,
  mode, forced-only mark and, for a baseline, its agent config) and
  `caveats` (§4.32b) are validated the same way, each on its own. The live
  store is read through `bounded-read.ts` (16 MiB, no final symlink, no FIFO).
  A cell carries run and session ids, never a path.
- `src/coverage-view.ts` reads the table and the shard ids through the
  manifest's CLI in a child process (`node scripts/suites.mjs coverage
  --json`, `list --json --unsharded`), cached on the manifest files' mtimes
  and 60 s (`CoverageCache`). A malformed table (unknown kind, bad property or
  suite id, bad status) rejects the whole table, which says why; an installed
  bundle has no manifest and says so. A suite's last CI run is the newest
  VALID run in the CI runs directory that lists it (any `source`, newest 100
  runs); a sharded suite takes the worst of its shards and links the first
  red one. An invalid summary is counted and never consulted, so it cannot
  hide a red run or forge a green one.

**The Tests tab's own runs.** A test-all.sh run started from the Tests tab
(`kind:<k>`, `all`) keeps run-suites' `summary.json` under its run id in the
test-runs directory (§4.10), and `src/test-runs/test-run-attribution.ts`
decides which suites each finished run is a run OF: a test-all.sh run, the
entries of its summary read through the CI reader's strict `getRun` (for
`kind:<k>`, only entries of that kind); a one-entry run, that entry with its
result from the run's end state; a whole run with no valid summary (below),
its own recorded lines; nothing else. The `e2e` batch, a canceled run, and a
whole run with no summary whose lines name no current suite count for NO
suite; the answer's `tests` counts them by reason. `lastTestRuns` folds the attributed runs like the CI ones, and
`newestOf` keeps per suite the newer by `finished` (a tie keeps CI). Without a
test runner (the read-only dashboard) or a results directory the view is the
CI one.

**Older runs (2026-10-03).** Runs from before the results directory stayed
unattributed. The reason was not a missing field: a summary needs no
suite → property mapping or run kind, since the view takes both from the
manifest at read time and an old CI summary's `tier` already reads as its
kind (§4.27). It was that such a run has **no summary at all**: the runner
began asking test-all.sh for one on 2026-10-02, so every `kind:<k>` or `all`
run before that, and every retired `tier:<t>` run, read "no valid
summary.json". Their history rows still hold what the run printed: since
run-suites (2026-09-28) test-all.sh prints `▶ <entry id>` and its `✓ PASS`,
`∅ SKIP` or `✗ FAIL` for each entry it ran, and the runner parsed those into
the row live. So such a run now counts from those lines
(`entriesFromRecordedLines`, basis `lines`): each line whose name is an entry
or shard id of the manifest as read now (`coverage-view.ts manifestIds`,
from `suites.mjs list --json`) is that suite's result, an entry named twice
keeps its worst, and a TAP case never counts. The mark says "no summary:
read from its recorded lines". A valid summary still wins over the lines,
and without the manifest's list nothing is read from them. **What cannot be
recovered**, and stays unattributed with its reason: the `e2e` batch (it
runs one file of each of several entries, `stack/proxy-replay.test.ts` of
`integration` for one, so not even its pass is an entry's pass); a run
whose lines name no current suite (before run-suites, test-all.sh labelled
its suites by package and description, "launcher (net-proxy live)", and only
a bare package name that is an entry id now, such as `arbiter`, counts; an
entry renamed since has no rename table); a canceled run; and, for the
lines, a commit and a ref (none is invented) and a timeout or error, which a
verdict line prints as FAIL. A run the history dropped (it keeps 50) is gone
with its row.

**Tests.** `drill-matrix.test.ts`, `coverage-view.test.ts` and
`test-runs/test-run-attribution.test.ts` (the validators, the pure
projections, readers over fixture stores with hostile, posing and symlinked
records; a run with no summary counted from its recorded lines against the
manifest's ids, the e2e batch's cases never); `ui/run-views-js.test.ts`
(both modules in jsdom, hostile text as text, a Run-a-suite mark opening its
entry's log); the `run-views-area` e2e (a real `DashboardServer` over the real
catalog and manifest: both routes, the disagreement, a link opening its
recorded trace, Tests-tab runs attributed through `POST /api/test`, one with
no summary by its recorded lines, hostile records kept out, no checkout,
read-only, Basic auth).

### 4.30 A fast session list — caches, one copy on the wire, a polite poll

**Why.** With a replay store of 150 runs (about 10,000 session records and
1.6 GB of events logs), `GET /api/sessions` took 4–7 s of synchronous CPU per
request, stalling every other request, and the inspector asked for it every
4 s. The causes: a parsed-events cache that cleared itself whole when full,
listings that re-read every record of every run, a 9.5 MB answer carrying the
list three times, a blind poll, a sidebar drawing every row, and `no-store`
static assets. The design below fixes each.

**Readers (`src/replay-run-store.ts`, `src/identity-cache.ts`).**

- The parse caches are `IdentityCache`s: bounded LRU, keyed by path, valid
  only at the file's identity. A full cache drops its oldest entry, never
  everything.
- Listings read a record's **head** (`ReplaySessionHead`: the record minus
  `checks`, `turns`, `plainTurns`, `files`, `baseline`) through a head cache
  of 50,000. A head is cut from the fully validated record, so an invalid
  record fails here too. Full records (a run's detail, one session, the file
  route) have their own cache of 1,000.
- `listReplayRuns` and `listReplaySessions` pick runs from the `run.json`
  files alone and read only those runs' records. A run's directories are
  checked once per run, and one lstat of a session's events log also yields
  its identity. A warm listing costs two lstats per session.

**Recorded source (`src/event-source/recorded-source.ts`).** A sidebar row
needs only its log's count, first and last time, violation flag and the
row's masked / asks / blocked counts (§4.33) (`RecordedEventsSummary`), cached per events-file identity and pruned to the
last listing; a row is rebuilt only when its inputs changed. Parsed events
are kept only for the last 16 sessions a trace view opened. A cold listing
yields to the event loop every 25 ms, and concurrent listings share one pass.

**The answer (`src/server/api-routes.ts` `sessionsPayload`,
`server/http-util.ts`).**

- The list goes out once per role: `sessions` is the flat label and selection
  map without the replay annotation; `sections` carries the rows the sidebar
  draws; `batches` is gone. A replay row keeps only what the row draws; the
  run's commit, ref, source and start ride the batch once
  (`SessionBatch.replayRun`), and the panel reads the rest from
  `/api/replay/runs/<runId>`. Only fields were removed; nothing new is
  exposed.
- `jsonConditional` tags the body with a weak ETag over its bytes and answers
  a matching If-None-Match with a bodiless 304. The answer stays `no-store`;
  the inspector keeps its last body and sends If-None-Match itself.
- A body of 1 KiB or more is gzipped when accepted, in libuv's thread pool,
  off the event loop; the last 32 compressed bodies are kept by ETag.
- These change how bytes travel, never which bytes a client may have (same
  gates as every route). Only routes that echo nothing from the request and
  carry no secret inventory are compressed (the session list, the test-data
  listings, static assets), since a compression side channel (BREACH) needs
  attacker-chosen text beside a secret; see *Payload budgets*.

**Static assets (`server/static-routes.ts` `assetCacheControl`).**
`serveIndex` stamps every css/js URL with `?v=<newest asset mtime>`, so a
versioned request is served `private, max-age=31536000, immutable`. An
unversioned one (a module's relative import) is `no-cache` with an ETag and a
304 when unchanged. Text assets are gzipped; fonts are `max-age=604800`;
`index.html` stays `no-store`, so a refresh always picks up the newest token.

**The inspector (`dev/js/app.js`).** One list load at a time: a call during a
load asks for ONE more pass after it (a delete or page change still sees its
change). The 4 s poll skips while a load is in flight or the tab is hidden,
and a returning tab loads at once. `fetchSessions` sends If-None-Match and
reuses its body on a 304; the render-signature guard skips the redraw. A
folded batch draws no rows until it opens (`fillBatchRows`); selecting a
session opens its batch (`expandBatchOf`); a batch 🗑 takes its members from
the list, not from drawn rows.

**Result** on that store: a warm listing pass 45–75 ms (from 5–6 s), the body
3.5 MB and about 180 KB gzipped (from 9.5 MB), nothing for an unchanged poll,
heap after listing about 140 MB (from about 1.5 GB). `/api/replay` and the
replay half of `/api/drill-matrix` share the listings and dropped to about
50 ms warm.

#### The cold start

The caches above are in memory, so every restart started cold (the first
session list 4–5 s, the drill scenarios about 1 s, and the live drill store
re-read on every request). Three mechanisms remove that wait.

**An identity that survives a restart.** A cache identity is device, inode,
size, mtime, ctime and mode (`replay-run-store.ts statKey`, the live run
cache, the catalog). ctime moves on any write, rename, chmod or mtime reset
and cannot be set back, so a same-size rewrite with its mtime restored is
seen, which is what lets an identity be trusted across processes.

*The racy window* (git's racy-index rule; `identity-cache.ts fileIdentity`).
The kernel stamps files from a coarse clock, so two writes inside one tick
can leave the identity unchanged (seen in the CI guest as a same-size rewrite
served from cache). A file whose mtime or ctime is less than 2 s old (or in
the future) gets an identity that matches nothing: it is re-read on every use
and neither cached nor persisted until older. Any later write then stamps a
time past the cached one, so a matching identity is safe. Tests that pin cache
hits on fresh files turn the window off (`setRacyWindowMs(0)`).

**The persisted listing cache (`src/listing-cache-file.ts`).** The replay
listings' small derived rows are saved to `listings.json.gz` in the path
table's `dashboard-cache` entry (`<home>/cache/dashboard/`, on-disk-layout.md
§5; regenerable), and a restart loads them before it listens. Each entry
carries the identity of the file it came from: a run's validated `run.json`,
a record's head (or the reason it is invalid), an events log's summary
(schema 2 adds the row's counts, §4.33; a schema-1 file is discarded and the
summaries are rebuilt once; schema 3, 2026-10-06, splits `early` out of
`masked`, so a schema-2 file is discarded the same way; schema 4,
2026-10-07, counts a program's refused read of a secret file as blocked,
§4.25b, so a schema-3 file is too; schema 5, 2026-10-07, joins a proxy's
check to its call, §4.2f, so a call two checks stopped counts once and a
schema-4 file is discarded; schema 6, 2026-10-09, leaves a token the AI
composed itself out of `masked`, §4.33, so a schema-5 file is too). Every
field is one `/api/sessions` or `/api/replay` already serves: no check,
reason, prompt, turn, file list or event text, and no original a symbol
stands for (a canary in every record and log never reaches the file:
`listing-cache-file.test.ts`, `boot-warmup.test.ts`). The file is 0600 in a
0700 directory of the agent-denied home, and nothing in it is trusted:

- the schema, kind and replay directory must match, else the file is ignored
  (a schema bump discards every old file);
- every meta and head is re-validated by the store's strict validators,
  pinned to the run and key its entry names; a summary is checked field by
  field;
- a seeded entry is served only while its file's identity is unchanged (every
  lookup lstats first);
- a missing, symlinked (O_NOFOLLOW), non-gzip, corrupt or oversized file
  (16 MiB compressed, 64 MiB inflated, inflation stops at the cap) is ignored,
  never fatal. The worst a hand-edited file can do is show an unchanged valid
  record as invalid until it changes.

Saves are off the request path: a 5 s timer saves once the caches changed and
went quiet (at least once a minute while they keep changing), the warm-up
saves at its end, and `close()` saves once more. A save exports only entries
whose file still has its cached identity, so a pruned run leaves memory and
the file. The body is gzipped in the thread pool and written atomically (a
fresh 0600 temp file, flushed, renamed). At the 300-run listing window
(20,700 heads) the file is about 1.1 MiB gzipped and loads in about 0.3 s;
`PERSIST_HEAD_MAX` (30,000) holds a full replay page (a test pins 300 × 69 or
more).

**The boot warm-up (`src/server/cache-warmup.ts`).** Once the server listens
it warms, in the background and in the order a first inspector load asks:
the replay heads (yielding every 25 ms), the recorded session list, the live
drill runs, the CI live sessions and the own-arbiter runs' sessions (§4.22),
the `/api/sessions` body, the
child-process steps (coverage table, drill scenarios, suite manifest), the
drill matrix, the CI summaries, the coverage view, and a save. Each step
waits a turn of the event loop first, so
a request is answered before it; a failing step is logged and skipped; a
closing server starts no further step. No request ever waits for the warm-up.
Tests leave it off (`warmCaches`, `listingCacheFile` unset).

**The live drill store (`src/drill-run-store.ts`).** `readRun` and
`listWatchRuns` answer from a run cache while the run directory's identity and
each of `meta.json`, `chapters.json`, `report.json`, `matrix.json` are
unchanged. The one non-file input, whether a `running` run's runner is alive,
is part of the key, so a dead runner reads `aborted` at once.

**The rest.** The drill catalog index is cached by identity.
`WatchRunner.scenarios()` is cached while its inputs are unchanged and
concurrent callers share one child. `CoverageCache` past its 60 s with an
unchanged stamp answers at once and re-reads in the background (stale while
revalidating; dev tooling, not security state). **Not cached, deliberately:**
the arbiter-backed data (home facts, approvals, secrets), so a new approval
appears on the next poll.

**The scenario list (`src/scenario-cache-file.ts`).** `/api/drills/scenarios`
runs the drill runner in a child (about 1 s). Its list is saved to
`drill-scenarios.json` beside the listing cache (atomic, 0600) with the STAMP
it was computed under, and a restart serves it at once. The stamp is each
input file by name and identity (`drill-runs.ts scenarioInputs`: the runner
and every source file directly in the drill catalog's directory, its `areas/`
and the drill runners' shared library, since the child imports the catalog's modules); a file
added or removed changes it, and `dashboard-drill-catalog.test.ts`
fails when a module the listing imports is not stamped. The file is not
trusted (schema, kind, checkout and stamp must match, rows are shape-checked,
a symlinked, corrupt or oversized file is ignored, a racy stamp is never
written), and the warm-up asks the runner once anyway, catching a change the
stamp cannot see. Saves are chained and `DashboardServer.close()` awaits
them. The runner exits only once its stdout is flushed: the listing (about
75 KB) exceeds a pipe buffer, and an early exit truncated the JSON.

With the cache files, a restart answers the session list in under 1 s at once
(about 0.15 s once warm) and the drill scenarios in about 30 ms.

#### Payload budgets

`test/component/payload-budget.test.ts` keeps the hot routes small: a real
`DashboardServer` over a large fixture, with a byte budget per route.

*The fixture*: 301 replay runs (the newest 50 with 70 recorded sessions each,
with events logs and casts; the rest one record each), a 100-drill catalog, a
live drill store of 100 runs × 30 chapters, 150 live sessions, a policy
snapshot with 45 tools, 5 gates of 8 rules, 30 user rules and 200 approval
verdicts, and 300 registered secrets, 40 labels, 30 derived labels and 10
tainted programs.

*The budgets* (bytes, about 1.5× the fixture's measurement; "plain" = sent
uncompressed on purpose):

| route | budget raw | budget gzip |
|---|---|---|
| `/api/sessions` | 5,000,000 | 160,000 |
| `/api/home` | 92,000 | plain |
| `/api/replay` (300 runs) | 128,000 | 6,000 |
| `/api/drill-matrix` | 1,450,000 | 52,000 |
| `/api/policy/panel` | 423,000 | plain |
| `/api/secrets` | 174,000 | plain |

The test also rebuilds the session list as a regression would ship it
(`batches` back, the replay annotation back on each flat row: about 7 MB) and
asserts it fails, so the budget means something. A budget is raised only with
its reason written here.

*The session list's counts* (§4.33). Every live and recorded log of the
fixture ends in a masked Read result, a blocked connection and a command
held for an OK, so every one of its 3,650 rows carries `counts: {masked: 1,
asks: 1, blocked: 1}` (the worst case: no row without counts). That adds 43
raw bytes a row to `/api/sessions` (+156,950, 4.7%); identical values hide
the gzip cost, so the test also gzips the body with every row's three counts
drawn from 1..40 (about 7 bytes a row, still under the 160,000 budget). No
budget moved; the test pins at most 48 raw bytes a row
(`PER_ROW_COUNTS_BUDGET`), the counts on the section rows only (not the flat
label map), and the varied body under the gzip budget.

*No row is running.* The fixture's live sessions end a full RUNNING window
(`RUNNING_WINDOW_MS`, the recency rule `SessionRef.status` uses) plus five
minutes before the test's `NOW`, and the test asserts no row is running: a
session inside the window would flip to not-running between the plain
request and the gzipped one, and "the same bytes either way" would compare
two different bodies.

*Compression, per route.* `/api/sessions`, `/api/replay`,
`/api/drill-matrix`, `/api/coverage` and `/api/drills/scenarios` use
`jsonConditional` (ETag, 304, gzip when accepted, still `no-store`): they are
test data and echo nothing from the request. `/api/home`,
`/api/policy/panel` and `/api/secrets` stay uncompressed on purpose: they
carry the approval queue and the secret inventory (paths, symbols, levels)
beside text an agent chose (a destination, a session's words), the
combination a compression side channel works on; compressing them would need
its own review. The test pins both halves.

#### The policy panel's rows

The arbiter's approvals store (`arbiter/policy/egress-approvals.ts`) keeps
every verdict, so a panel whose rows carried a ~900-byte ⓘ drawer each
(`detail`, the policy-surface.md §9.8.3 template, re-shipped on every 3 s
poll) grew without bound. Now:

- **The drawer is built when it opens.** `QueueRowVM` has no `detail`. The
  inspector's ⓘ (`dev/js/egress.js` `verdictInfoBtn`, over the shared
  drawer's `lazyInfoBtn`) fetches `GET /api/policy/verdict?id=<id>`, which
  loads a fresh snapshot and answers `{ detail }` from `verdictDetailOf`. It
  exposes nothing the panel did not. Not fail-soft: 400 no id, 404 an unknown
  id, 503 when the verdicts cannot be read, and the drawer then says "could
  not read this decision". Read-only, same gates, uncompressed like the
  panel.
- **The history is windowed, the law is not.** Every pending ask, standing
  answer and unspent single-use answer is in `queue`: each still decides
  something (invariant 2 of `view-model/policy-panel.ts`). Spent single-use
  answers decide nothing; the newest `SPENT_HISTORY_LIMIT` (50) are listed
  and the rest counted in `queueOmitted`. `queueCounts` counts every verdict
  (the omitted ones too) and feeds the standing count the inspector
  broadcasts and the "N older decisions not listed" lines. The product home's
  newest-20 answered list falls inside the window.
- **A row carries only what a client reads** (the product home's rules list,
  the inspector's egress panel, the server's home and agent pages); requesting
  sessions are capped at 8 by the arbiter. Nothing in a row grows with use.

Result: about 850 bytes per standing answer since the rows carry the
question's words (§4.34; 657 before; the test's `PER_VERDICT_BUDGET`, 1,000,
pins it) and nothing per spent answer past the window.

#### `/api/secrets` once

The body was the arbiter's raw `confidentialityState` spread beside its
projection `panel` (`view-model/secrets.ts`), so every secret, label, derived
record and tainted program went out twice, and no client read the raw copy.
The body is now `{ enabled, panel }` (`SecretsResponse`). This is also defense
in depth: the panel copies each field it shows by name, so a field the
arbiter adds to its state no longer reaches the browser unread.

#### Tests

Unit: `identity-cache.test.ts` (LRU, the racy window),
`replay-run-store.test.ts` and `recorded-source.test.ts` (a listing reads
only heads; a change, including a same-size rewrite with its mtime restored,
is re-read), `drill-run-cache.test.ts`, `coverage-view.test.ts`,
`server/sessions-payload.test.ts`, `server/conditional-response.test.ts`
(ETag, 304, gzip per route, the asset rule), `ui/app-js-session-poll.test.ts`
and `ui/app-js-sidebar.test.ts`, `listing-cache-file.test.ts` (no canary in
the file, tampered or corrupt files ignored, the atomic write),
`scenario-cache-file.test.ts`, `server/cache-warmup.test.ts`,
`view-model/policy-panel.test.ts`, `server/policy-routes.test.ts`,
`ui/egress-js-panel.test.ts`, `server/secrets-routes.test.ts` (each symbol
once). Component: `sessions-scale.test.ts` (3,000 recorded sessions: warm far
below cold, a request answered during the cold pass), `boot-warmup.test.ts`
(a restart lists from the file without reading a record),
`scenario-cache-restart.test.ts` (the restart's re-asking child is held
until the list is answered, so "no wait on the child" is proved by order;
its old bound, under 300 ms, failed on loaded CI guests at 321 and 348 ms
while still served from the file), `payload-budget.test.ts`.

### 4.31 Prompt filters — the inspector's panel for the prompt filter

The model proxies cut each request's user-role text into segments by who
wrote them and ask the arbiter's `filterPrompt` what the model may read; a
registered secret pasted into a prompt reaches the model as its symbol
