([confidentiality plan 15](../confidentiality/confidentiality-plan-15-prompt-filter.md)
§8.1). The inspector (`/dev/`, `dev/js/prompt-filters.js`) shows and edits
that filter in a **Prompt filters** panel on the Rules page, after the Policy
panel: the Rules sub-menu's **Prompt filters** entry
(`/dev/rules#prompt-filters`, its count says how many filters are on;
§4.34), each of its tables scrolling in its own box on a phone. The product page carries the held-message card (below) and
Settings › Prompt filters over this panel's projection, plus the note under
the person's message (§4.25y).

**Reading.**

| Part | Route | What it shows |
|---|---|---|
| Filters | `GET /api/prompt-filters/filters` | each filter, on or off, who set it (`default`, `you`, `administrator` with file and lock), its `on_error`, whether it can run (a pack missing, refused or unsigned under `signed_only` says why), category → action rows with who set each, the fallback (`redact`), where it runs and the floor there (`human`: values of 12+ characters and 3.0+ bits per character; `harness`, `side-call`: every registered value), whether the confidentiality axis enforces or only logs, the exceptions, each pack's place and COUNTS (never a regex or keyword), refused pack files, lock conflicts, the digests, `editable`. From the arbiter's `promptFilters` (a data-socket read; no value in it). Behind the CSRF header AND the admin session (plan 15 §13.7): an exception's pattern may hold the person's own words; without the session it is a 403 with nothing of the exceptions in it, and the panel shows a plain note that the admin sign-in is needed (`gatedNote`, also on the packs and held messages) |
| Recent findings | `GET /api/prompt-filters/findings?session=` | the session's `prompt_filter` events, newest first (at most 200): when, who wrote the segment, agent, filter, category, action, the symbol, how many values the prompt floor left as typed, how a hold ended and whether a verdict let it through. Copied field by field from the event's `promptFilter` detail, never from its panes, so no original rides the list. The session is read from its owner, as `/api/events` does (`sessionSource`): a recorded replay id (§4.28) from the recorded sessions, never sent to the store; such an answer carries `recorded: true` and no finding `canLet`, and the panel offers neither "show original" nor "let through" (no arbiter holds the symbols) |
| …a row's original | `POST /api/prompt-filters/reveal {session, symbol}` | on a click only, through the SAME human-plane read the transcript's reveal uses (the arbiter's `desymbolize` on the human socket), only for a symbol one of that session's findings names (404 otherwise: not a general desymbolize) |
| Test bench | `POST /api/prompt-filters/bench {text, origin}` | a DRY RUN: `filterPrompt` with `dryRun: true`, which the arbiter serves only on the HUMAN socket (on the data socket a dry run would let the agent's processes test guesses against registered values with no trace). Origin `human` or `harness`; empty text or a bad origin 400, over 64 KiB 413, before the arbiter is asked. Answers the findings, each action and the text the model would receive; nothing is minted, cached or logged |
| Packs | `GET /api/prompt-filters/packs` | every pack in full (patterns with regex, check and level; plain keywords; hashed keywords as a count), from the HUMAN-plane `promptFilterPacks`. Behind the CSRF header AND the admin session: it carries an organization's patterns. The panel's GET helper (`pfGet`) sends `X-Mandu-Control` on EVERY read, so no read of the panel can forget it (the header only proves the page is ours; a cross-site page cannot set it) |

**Editing.**

| Part | Route | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| a switch, an action, an exception | `POST /api/prompt-filters/change {edit, expected?}` | ONE typed `PolicyEdit` (`set-prompt-filter`, `set-prompt-action`, `remove-prompt-action`, `add-prompt-exception`, `remove-prompt-exception`; anything else 400 before the arbiter is asked) through the policy write path Settings › Models uses (`applyAsHuman`): previewed; a relaxation answers `{confirm: true, expected, rows, wouldLet}` in plain words and the panel asks before resending with `expected`; then proposed on the ADMIN channel, approved, recorded and undoable from History. A locked row has no control, and the arbiter's validator refuses a change the lock forbids. `ask` is an action a row may take (raising a row to it is a tightening) |
| a pattern or a keyword | `POST /api/prompt-filters/pack-edit {edits, dryRun?, sample?}` | typed edits to ONE of the person's own packs (`set-prompt-pattern`, `remove-prompt-pattern`, `add-prompt-keyword`, `remove-prompt-keyword`; a new pack id creates `<id>.yaml`) via the arbiter's `promptPackEdit` on the ADMIN channel. Check is a dry run: RE2 must accept the regex, and the panel shows its matches over a fixed corpus of ordinary prose and over the bench text, so a pattern that matches everything is seen before it is saved. Removal asks first. An administrator's pack and a signed pack are read-only |

A saved change applies on the next request (the arbiter's cache key holds the
policy and pack digests); a pack does nothing until its switch is on.

**No answer** (§4.8 "No answer", 2026-10-10). With the dashboard server gone
every read and control of the panel says "the dashboard server did not
answer — reload this page once it is running again" in its place (`errorOf`,
`problemsOf`):

- a read: "cannot read the filters (…)", and the same for the findings, the
  held messages and the packs' patterns;
- a change: "Not changed (…)";
- the pack editor: "Not saved: …" and "Not changed: …". Check says the
  sentence alone, never "invalid: ";
- a held message's answer: "Not answered: …";
- "show original" and "let through" each say it too;
- the test bench: "dry run failed: …".

"let through" gives its button back after any refusal; it stayed disabled
until then. Before, a read left its part empty, a click left its button
disabled or said nothing, and the bench said "running a dry run…" for
good.

**What a change did** (2026-10-11). Each part with a control (Filters,
Actions, Exceptions, Packs, Held for your answer, Recent findings) has its
own line right under it, `pf-<part>-status` in `dev/index.html`: a
`role="status"` region in the page from the start, outside the part's host.
A click writes what it did into the line of its part (`status(part, …)`;
`change(edit, part)`) and clears the other lines, so one line speaks, at
the last click. The redraw after a change (`paintAll`) empties the hosts,
not the lines, so the words stay:

- a filter's switch, its *On error* or model, an action, an exception:
  "Saved to policy.yaml; it applies on the next request.", or "Not
  changed (…)", or "Not changed." when the person declines a relaxation;
- the pack editor: "Saved to <file>; it applies on the next request (turn
  the pack on above if it is new).", "Keyword saved.", "Removed <id> from
  <pack>.", "Removed the keyword <word> from <pack>." (a keyword's × said
  nothing on success), or the refusal;
- a held message's answer: "Answered <id>: <answer>." under Held;
- a let-through: "Let through (once|session); it applies on the next
  request." under Recent findings. Picking another session clears that
  line; the same session picked again keeps it.

Until then the panel had one line, which `paintFilters` drew at the end of
the Filters table each time. A change wrote "Saved …" into it and then drew
the tables again, the line with them, empty, so no success was ever seen; a
held answer or a let-through was said five parts above its row; and signed
out (no Filters table, only the sign-in note) there was no line at all, so a
let-through refused for want of the admin session said nothing. A refusal
is drawn `svc-err`, a success as a plain note. Presentation only: no route,
verb, gate or server text changed.

**Plugins.** On a plugin's row (`kind: "plugin"`) the filters route carries
its pinned program (path and SHA-256, and the script's), its model
(`endpoint`), its last run (latency, runs, errors, last error) and the
sandbox legs it runs under (network guard, Landlock, seccomp filter,
namespaces, and why any is off), copied field by field; and `clearedModels`,
the declared models a classifier may name (`local: true`, read through the
adapter's `modelEndpoints`). A classifier's model is chosen only from that
list through the change route (`set-prompt-filter` with `endpoint`), which is
ALWAYS a relaxation and so always asks first; the arbiter's validator refuses
a model that is not `local: true`. A plugin pack is a file: the pack editor
refuses it.

**`ask` and "let it through."**

| Part | Route | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Held for your answer | `GET /api/prompt-filters/holds` | the messages a proxy holds now: session, category, filter, the human's own FOUND TEXT (HUMAN-plane `promptHolds`; absent when the arbiter has not seen the message since it started), the time left before the default. Behind the CSRF header AND the admin session; repainted every 3 s while one is listed |
| …an answer | `POST /api/prompt-filters/holds/answer {approvalId, answer, scope}` | `send` (as written), `mask` (the default) or `cancel`; `once` (default) or `session`: `resolvePromptHold` on the ADMIN channel. Anything else 400 before the arbiter is asked |
| …let it through | `POST /api/prompt-filters/let-through {session, eventId, index, scope}` | names a finding by event and index; the route reads the session's own events (`letThroughPlan`: an unknown or claimed event 404; harness text, a registered value, or `once` with no message reference 409) and sends `letPromptFindingThrough` the category, reference and message reference FROM THE EVENT, never from the body (ADMIN channel). A finding offers it (`canLet`) only for an opaque reference, an enforced action, the human's own text, not a registered value, from a proxy-recorded event. The panel asks first. A finding the arbiter marked `onceOnly` on its event (a locked administrator's `ask` row, plan 15 §12, 2026-10-04) is listed `onceOnly: true`: the panel offers "let through once" only, with "this message only: locked to ask by your administrator" in place of the session button; the arbiter's refusal of a session let-through is a 409 with its reason. **The locks in force** (2026-10-07, the work ledger's P1): the findings route also reads the arbiter's `promptFilters` rows (`promptLocks`, `lockOf` in `prompt-settings.ts`, a display mirror of the arbiter's `lockedAction`/`lockedAsk`), only for a session with a `prompt_filter` event. A finding whose strictest locked administrator row is not `ask` is listed with no `canLet` and `locked: <action>`, and the panel says "cannot be let through: locked to block by your administrator" in place of both buttons (the arbiter refuses it, 422); a locked `ask` row in force marks `onceOnly` as the event would. No arbiter, or one without the rows: the event alone decides, and the arbiter still refuses |

**The product page's card** (Approvals and the home's waiting list): a row
keyed `prompt:` is the family `prompt`: "<agent> wants to send your message to
the AI. It holds <category>." with Send as written, Send masked and Cancel
the message (and on Approvals, Send as written for this session). The card
fetches the found text from the holds route (with the CSRF header; it is
never part of `/api/home`). The Rules page words a past answer by category
and reach (`promptAnswerWords`), under *Sending data*, the category as code
(§4.25u *Rules names a held message's answer*). The inspector's Approvals card offers the
same four answers and sends them on the hold route, as the product does
(§4.34).

**Wiring.** The routes ride the policy surface: `PolicyDocArbiter`
(`makeApprovalsArbiter`, `src/arbiter-adapter.ts`) forwards `promptFilters`
(data client; the exceptions there carry no pattern, so the adapter reads
them from `promptExceptions` on the HUMAN client and puts them back, plan
15 §13.7 item 4), `filterPromptDryRun` (HUMAN client, always `dryRun: true`),
`promptFilterPacks` and `promptHolds` (HUMAN client), `promptPackEdit`,
`resolvePromptHold` and `letPromptFindingThrough` (ADMIN channel); the change
route uses `policyPreview`, `policyPropose` and `resolvePolicyProposal`. An
arbiter without these ops answers 501, no arbiter 404. The POSTs sit behind
the global mutating gate (CSRF header + admin session). History and the Inbox
describe the prompt edits in plain words (`view-model/policy-proposals.ts`).
The event kind `prompt_filter` is in `EVENT_KINDS` (`src/event-model.ts`,
`PromptFilterDetail`; lane category GUARD).

**Tests.** Unit: `server/prompt-filter-routes.test.ts` (findings never carry
an original even when the event's pane does, the reveal only for the
session's own symbols, the bench's refusals and gate, plugin rows, 404 /
501), `server/prompt-filter-edit-routes.test.ts` (the change route's op
allowlist, a relaxation applied only with `expected`, the packs gate, the
pack editor's dry run), `server/prompt-filter-hold-routes.test.ts`
(`letThroughPlan`'s refusals, the holds gate, a let-through forwarding the
event's own category and reference), `ui/prompt-filters-js.test.ts` (jsdom
over the real `dev/index.html`: hostile strings and regexes stay text, no
original before the click, the CSRF header on every GET as the server
requires it, a recorded session's findings with no control, controls only
on unlocked rows, the confirm before a relaxation, a model chosen only from the cleared list,
every read and control with no answer, each said in its part's line; *What
a change did*: each part's line a live region outside its host, every
success said under its part after the redraw with the other lines cleared,
a let-through refused signed out said under Recent findings with its button
given back, another session clearing the findings line),
`policy-proposals-view-model.test.ts`, `home-view-model.test.ts`. Component:
`prompt-filters-panel.test.ts` (a mock arbiter that keeps the data and human
sockets apart: the dry run and the reveal only on the human socket) and
`replay-area.test.ts` (a real server over a recorded run carrying a
prompt-filter finding, with a store that refuses namespaced ids as the
arbiter does). Stack, the production adapter over a real `ArbiterServer`:
`dashboard-prompt-filters-parity.test.ts` (a registered key as its symbol,
nothing minted, the data socket refusing a dry run),
`dashboard-prompt-filter-editing.test.ts` (a pattern saved from the panel
enforced by the next `filterPrompt`, the administrator's lock),
`dashboard-prompt-plugins.test.ts` (a plugin against two fake local models, a
non-local model refused), `dashboard-prompt-holds.test.ts` (with the real
anthropic-proxy: `ask` raised from the panel, the found text behind the gate
and absent from `/api/home`, an answer sending it as written with the
registered key still a symbol, a redacted ticket let through once),
`inspector-pf-status.test.ts` (*What a change did*: with the real
anthropic-proxy recording a finding, the served Rules page in jsdom; signed
out, a let-through refused under Recent findings in the server's words, its
button given back and the next message still held back; signed in, an
action changed said under Actions after the redraw and written to
policy.yaml, a keyword added said under Packs with the Actions line cleared
and written to the pack, a let-through for the session said under Recent
findings and the next message's finding reaching the model; every line a
live region; the oracle over the pages and the answers).

### 4.32 The developer view: one nav, six pages

**Why.** The inspector's top bar had grown thirteen controls: a ⌂ Home
link, the §4.16 protection chip, ● live, a "which sessions" switch of four
(● Sessions / 🎬 Live drills / ⟲ Replay drills / 🧪 Tests), an area nav of
four (Status / Approvals / Policy / ⚙ Settings), 🛡 Protection and ▶ Run.
Two tab groups sat side by side and looked alike, though one picked a store
and the other a page, and some of their sixteen combinations meant nothing
(Tests × Settings). Three controls opened the same place (🛡, the chip,
Policy). ▶ Run opened a drawer of seven tabs holding three apps, mostly
about drills and tests, which had their own views in the bar. And the main
column showed panels by DENY-lists, one per area, so a panel added later
(`#prompt-filters-panel`, §4.31) was on none and showed on every area.

**Decision.** One nav row and six pages, with the product's names where the
product has one. The page is named **Developer view** (brand "Mandu ·
Developer view", the served `<title>` the same, with the page's name added
once a page is shown, *The tab title names the page*; the `/dev/` URL stays); Policy is
**Rules** and Status is **Sessions**. This was the second of five steps of
a redesign (1 the bugs, 2 this structure, 3 the Sessions page, §4.33, 4 the
Drills and Tests pages, §4.35, 5 Approvals, Rules and Settings in product
words, §4.34); all five have landed.

**The top bar.** Brand · **Sessions · Drills · Tests** | **Approvals**
(the pending-ask badge, §4.20) **· Rules · Settings** · the status line ·
**Product ↗**. Every nav item is a real link (`<a href>` to its path), so a
middle-click opens a new tab and a plain click routes in place (pushState).
Settings keeps the id `#settings-toggle`: control.js's stale-dashboard flag
lands on it (§4.8). The red invariant banner sits in the bar only while it
fires (§4.6).

- **The status line** (`#status-line`, app.js `renderStatusLine`) reads
  "● Protection: Secrets · live" in the product's words: the RUNNING level
  from the posture egress.js publishes (`window.__mduPosture`,
  `mdu:posture-updated`; Secrets, Off, and the frozen Injection / Full), and
  the session's live feed (`#live-dot`, `live` / `not live`, painted by
  `openStream`). Until the posture arrives it says "checking…", never a
  guess. When the panel answers without a level, it says "Protection: not
  known", and the tooltip says the protection service did not report the
  level. That happens with no protection service behind the panel (a
  dashboard over recorded logs, whose `/api/policy/panel` is `available:
  false` on every poll) or with one too old to report its posture. In that
  case egress.js publishes the panel's own `unknown` states, never an
  invented Off, and both counts as unknown (`null`). The next answer with a
  level replaces it. With the store down (§4.35, `S.storeDown`) it says "Test
  store: offline · not live" ("Mandu: offline" for the live store). With the
  dashboard server not answering (the session poll's read throws,
  `S.serverGone`, §4.8 *No answer to a poll*) it says "Dashboard: not
  answering · not live", ahead of the store and the posture, until the next
  answer. At the Off
  level it is amber, "⚠ Protection: Off" (a choice); on a violation it turns
  red beside the banner. Its tooltip says what the level does, and for
  Secrets that untrusted text is NOT masked. It links to Rules › the
  Protection block: a click routes there, scrolls the block on screen,
  flashes it and re-reads the saved setup (`mdu:refresh-axes`).
- **The protection chip** (§4.16) is a per-SESSION summary, so it lives on
  the selected session's own line: `#session-bar` holds the session header
  (§4.33) and `#protection-chip`, on the three session pages. Same text, the
  same §4.19 off-state, the same click-through plain-terms card.
- **Product ↗** is the product root, base-path aware (`data-base-href="/"`,
  control.js `wireBaseHrefs`).
- **Phone (≤ 760px):** two rows. ☰ (only on a page with a sidebar), "Mandu ·
  Dev", the status line without its word ("● Secrets · live") and Product ↗;
  then the six pages as one row that scrolls sideways.

**The pages.** pages.js (`dev/js/pages.js`, pure, imported by app.js) holds
the table; page-routes.ts holds the server's copy, and a unit test keeps
them equal.

| Page | URL | What it holds | Was |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sessions | `/dev/sessions[/<id>]` | the live store's real agent runs: the list, the session header and tabs; **+ New run** (a dialog) | view ● Sessions × area Status; the Run drawer's Run agent tab |
| Drills | `/dev/drills[/<id>]` | replay or live drill sessions (a **Replay \| Live** switch in the sidebar, `mandu.drills.kind`), each with its recording and checks (§4.35); **▶ Run drills** (a dialog) | views 🎬 Live drills and ⟲ Replay drills × Status; the drawer's 🎬 Drills tab |
| Drills › Matrix | `/dev/drills/matrix` | the drill matrix (§4.29) | the drawer's ▦ Drill matrix tab |
| Drills › Agents | `/dev/drills/agents` | each agent's pinned version, its last full run and core check in CI, the newest release seen; report only (§4.32a) | new (2026-10-15) |
| Drills › Comparison | `/dev/drills/comparison` | Mandu beside each baseline over a battery's live runs: the secret kept, the task done, per side and per drill × side; the browser agents' demos, each without and with Mandu (§4.32b) | new (2026-10-17) |
| Drills › Videos | `/dev/drills/videos` | the promo film's takes, a scene × agent grid, and a player that keeps a take's terminal, dashboard recording, sink and captions on one clock (`?take=`; `&render=1` the 1920×1080 stage alone, for the render) | new (2026-10-18) |
| Tests | `/dev/tests[/<id>]` | Test sessions: the test store's sessions (the test tenant), or the live store's test-tagged ones where no test store runs | view 🧪 Tests × Status |
| Tests › Run a suite · Coverage · VM matrix · CI | `/dev/tests/suites`, `/coverage`, `/vm`, `/ci` | the suite runner, history and specs (§4.10), coverage (§4.29), the VM matrix (§4.26), CI (§4.27) | the drawer's 🧪 Tests, ◫ Coverage, 🖥 VM matrix, ⚑ CI tabs |
| Approvals | `/dev/approvals` | the asks waiting and Answered earlier (§4.25w, §4.34) | area Approvals |
| Rules | `/dev/rules` | the Protection block, the Policy panel, Prompt filters, Secrets, under a sub-menu (`#<section>`, §4.34) | area Policy; the 🛡 Protection button |
| Settings | `/dev/settings` | services, sandbox, Protection axes, the dashboard server, appearance, docs (§4.34) | area ⚙ Settings |

The three session pages have the sidebar: its head names the page, its top
holds the page's own tools (`.page-tools`: + New run; ▶ Run drills, the
Drills sub-menu Drill sessions · Matrix · Agents · Comparison · Videos and Replay | Live; the
Tests sub-menu Test sessions · Run a suite · Coverage · VM matrix · CI),
and the list below lists that page's sessions only (test-reorganization.md
§7.1: one group at a time). Approvals, Rules and Settings have no sidebar
(`body[data-layout="full"]`); a tool sub-page (`list`) keeps the sidebar
with its sub-menu alone, no list (Tests; Drills since
2026-10-16, §4.35); a session page keeps the list
beside the session's header and tabs (`trace`). Where the path holds no
session, the selected one rides along as `?session=<id>` (the Rules page's
"This session only" reads it). Switching between session pages returns to
the session last shown on that page (`S.lastOfGroup`), else the newest; a
page whose group is empty selects nothing rather than pull in a session of
another page.

**Path URLs and the old forms** (§4.25v has the whole table). A session id
is one encoded segment (a replay id's `/` included); a sub-page name is
reserved under its page (`/dev/tests/ci` is CI, never a session "ci"). The
server 302s every renamed path, the query kept: `/dev/status` →
`/dev/sessions`, `/dev/policy` → `/dev/rules`, `/dev/inbox` →
`/dev/approvals`, and `/dev/?area=status|policy|inbox|…&session=S` to the
new page (`legacyRedirect`, `INSPECTOR_PAGE_ALIASES`). The server does not
look sessions up to route, so `/dev/sessions/<a drill id>` is the Sessions
page there; the client moves it to `/dev/drills/<id>` (Replay or Live as
the session is) or `/dev/tests/<id>` as soon as the session list says which
group the session is in (app.js `followSessionPage`). The client reads every
old form itself too (a tab opened before the change): a saved `mandu.area`
of `status`, `policy` or `inbox` opens the new page and is written back; the
old view switch's last choice (`mandu.sideFilter` of `drills` / `replay`)
opens Drills on the matching kind. The retired drawer's keys
(`mandu.drawer.open`, `mandu.drawer.runtab`) are dropped: nothing opens on
load. The product page's links follow: "developer view" in Settings ›
Prompt filters → `/dev/rules`, "History: N sessions" → `/dev/sessions`,
"Detailed trace" → `/dev/sessions/<id>`, and so does each "detailed trace"
the agent page names (`?tab=secrets` for its secrets past the cap, `?ask=`
for a moment it could not place, `?step=` for a step's own link; *The page
links the trace it names*).

**The test store only while on Tests.** The server serves one tenant per
request (the `mandu_tenant` cookie, policy-surface.md §2.7), and the cookie
is set only while the Tests page is open and a test store exists (§6.y has
the rule, and why the product page ignores it). Sessions ↔ Drills ↔
Approvals never reload (one store).

**Panels on an allow-list.** Every element that belongs to some pages says
which in `data-pages` (a page key or `page/sub`), and app.js
`applyPageChrome` stamps `data-off-page` on each one not declared for the
current view (`body[data-view]`); ONE rule, `[data-off-page] { display:
none !important; }`, hides it. The session surfaces (`#session-bar`, the tab
strip `#session-tabs` and its panels `#tab-trace`, `#tab-secrets`,
`#tab-files`, `#tab-checks`, `#tab-recording`, `#tab-setup`, §4.33, §4.35)
are on `sessions drills tests`; `#protection-panel`, `#egress-panel`,
`#prompt-filters-panel` and `#secrets-panel` on `rules`; `#approvals-area`
on `approvals`; `#settings-area` on `settings`; each tool panel on its
sub-page; the sidebar and its gutter on the pages they serve. A test checks
that EVERY child of `<main>` declares its pages with known keys, so a new
panel cannot leak again; without a stamped page (a bespoke test DOM) nothing
is hidden.

**What moved where, and what went.**

- ▶ Run's seven tabs: Run agent → **+ New run** on Sessions
  (`#new-run-dialog`); 🎬 Drills → **▶ Run drills** on Drills
  (`#run-drills-dialog`); ▦ Drill matrix → Drills › Matrix; 🧪 Tests,
  ◫ Coverage, 🖥 VM matrix, ⚑ CI → the Tests sub-pages. The panels and their
  render code are unchanged; control.js `wireDialogs` opens the two dialogs
  (✕, the backdrop, Esc, a page change or `mdu:close-dialog` close them; one
  at a time) and `wireSubpages` pings the module that paints a sub-page when
  it shows (`mdu:page-changed`, and once at load: `mdu:coverage-tab`,
  `mdu:matrix-tab`, `mdu:ci-tab`, `mdu:drill-matrix-tab`, and since
  2026-10-15 `mdu:drill-agents-tab` for Drills › Agents, §4.32a, and since
  2026-10-17 `mdu:drill-comparison-tab` for Drills › Comparison, §4.32b, and since
  2026-10-18 `mdu:drill-videos-tab` for Drills › Videos; Run a suite re-reads
  its history and specs), so each loads only when seen. A coverage mark asks
  for Tests › CI or Run a suite with `mdu:go-page`; the 📖 spec button and
  `mdu:test-open` too.
- **Removed:** the ▶ Run button and drawer (`#run-toggle`, `#run-drawer`,
  `.drawer-tab`s), the 🛡 Protection button (`#protection-toggle`; the
  status line links there), the view switch (`#tenant-group`, `data-view`),
  the area nav (`#area-nav`, `data-area`, `body[data-area]`, the deny-lists),
  ⌂ Home (now Product ↗), the bar's chip (now on the session bar), the
  `mdu:area-changed` event (now `mdu:page-changed` {page, sub, view}).
  `mdu:go-area` still works as an alias of `mdu:go-page` {page, sub, id}.
  `mdu:go-session` and `mdu:select-session` (a Policy-panel row's session
  link) open the session ON ITS PAGE, pushing a history entry.
- **The retired `--fs-preload` box.** The launcher retired the flag and
  rejects it at parse time, so the Run-agent form's "Filesystem AgentView
  (--fs-preload)" box printed an equivalent command that did not run. The box
  and its flag are gone (two boxes remain: `--net-proxy`, `--exec-wrap`); the
  body no longer sends `fsPreload`, and the server still accepts and ignores
  an old client's (agent-runner.ts).

**A page change moves the focus (2026-10-10).** The pages are parts of one
document, and a page change hid the old one without moving the keyboard
focus; the page had no `<h1>` either. Enter on a link inside a page
(Approvals' *Open in session →*, a Rules queue row's session, a drill-matrix
cell, a Coverage mark) left the focus on the link the change hid. A browser
drops it to `<body>`, and a screen reader said nothing of the new page. The
step *Mandu asked you here*, which *Open in session →* scrolls to, did not get
the focus either. Back left it on the nav item of the page left, and a nav
click left it on the nav. The product page got the same rule the same day
(§4.25 *A page change moves the focus*).

- **The heading.** One `<h1 id="page-heading">` names the page shown:
  "Sessions", "Drills", "Drills › Matrix", "Drills › Agents", "Tests", "Tests › Run a suite",
  "Tests › Coverage", "Tests › VM matrix", "Tests › CI", "Approvals",
  "Rules" or "Settings" (`applyPageChrome`). It is read, not drawn (visually
  hidden). It is the first thing in `#app`, before the sidebar, so the next
  Tab is the page's own first control: the sidebar's on a session page, the
  main column's on the others.
- **When.** Every page change the person makes gives the heading the focus
  (`app.js focusPage`; `tabindex="-1"`, so it is no Tab stop; preventScroll):
  a nav or sub-menu link, the status line, Back or Forward, and another
  module's request (`mdu:go-page`, `mdu:go-session`, `mdu:select-session`).
  A request for the page already shown moves nothing. The first load, a
  page move that follows a session pick (`followSessionPage`) and a
  crossing into the test store (a reload) leave the focus where it is.
- **The mark.** After *Open in session →*, the marked step takes the focus
  from the heading once the trace is drawn (`focusMarked` in `markAsk`). If
  the person moved the focus first, they keep it. A moment not found leaves
  it on the heading, and the note above the trace, a status, is read as it
  changes. A redraw (a live session's next event replaces the cards) gives
  the new marked card the focus back only if the old one still had it; a
  focus moved elsewhere leaves the mark (a `focusin`).
- **No ring.** Neither the heading nor the marked step is a control: the
  heading is not drawn, and the step keeps its accent mark.

Not covered: the targets other modules scroll to after their page request
(Tests › Run a suite's opened run, a 📖 spec's row, Tests › CI's opened
run) keep the focus on the heading, and the next Tab starts at the top of
that page. Presentation only: no route, gate or server text changed.

**The tab title names the page (2026-10-14).** The tab title read "Mandu ·
Developer view" on every page and sub-page. Two tabs of the developer view
(Rules and a session, say) read alike in the tab strip, the window switcher
and the browser's history, and a screen reader announced the same title on
every page (WCAG 2.4.2, *Page Titled*).

- **The words.** `paintDocTitle` puts the page's name after "Mandu":
  "Mandu · Rules · Developer view", "Mandu · Tests › CI · Developer view".
  The name is the heading's words (`S.pageName`, which `applyPageChrome`
  sets with the heading). The product page's tabs read the same way,
  "Mandu · Rules" (§4.25). The name comes before "Developer view", so a
  tab the browser shortens still shows it.
- **The prefixes.** The approvals count and the test store's prefix stay in
  front (§4.20, §4.35): "[TEST] (2) Mandu · Tests · Developer view". A page
  change keeps the count, and a count change keeps the page.
- **Before the scripts run** the served `<title>` is "Mandu · Developer
  view", unchanged.

Not covered: a session page names the page, not the session it shows.
Tests: `page-nav.test.ts` (every page and sub-page, a nav click, a jump,
Back, the count across a page change), `app-js-badge.test.ts`,
`app-js-drills-tests.test.ts`, `tests/stack/inspector-page-focus.test.ts`.
Presentation only: no route, gate or server text changed.

**The top bar never hides the focus (2026-10-14).** The top bar is fixed
over the page (`#topbar`, its height measured into `--topbar-h`), and on a
phone's Rules and Settings the sub-menu is one row that sticks under it
(§4.34). The window kept no room for either. Shift+Tab up a long page
scrolled the control it went to just into the window, at its top edge,
under the bar. Measured in a headless Chromium over a real arbiter, Tab
through each page and back, 250 stops each way: at 1280×800, 20 of
Rules' controls, 8 of Settings' and 2 of a session's lay entirely under the
bar (3 more partly); at 390×844, 20 of Rules' (6 partly), 13 of Settings'
and 5 of a session's (4 partly), some of them under the row. WCAG 2.4.11
(*Focus Not Obscured*). A Tab down the page had none. The page's own
jumps had the same gap: a phone's sub-menu click put its section's
heading under the row (at 94px, the row ending at 128px), and a trace step
without a margin of its own (a turn's background step) jumped to the
window's top, under the bar. Now:

- **The window keeps the room.** dashboard.css `html { scroll-padding-top:
  calc(var(--topbar-h) + var(--sub-menu-h, 0px) + 8px) }`: the bar, the
  phone's row and 8px stay free above whatever the window scrolls into
  view. That covers a control the focus goes to, a sub-menu click, a
  `#<key>` link, a jump of the page's own (*→ audit trail*, *Where each
  went →*, the step rail) and a Page Up or Down step.
- **The row's room.** sub-menus.js `trackRowRoom` measures the page's menu
  into `--sub-menu-h` while it is the phone's sticky row, with a
  `ResizeObserver` on each menu (its page shown or hidden, the window
  crossing 761px) and on every page change. A menu beside the sections, or
  a page without one (Sessions, Approvals, Tests), keeps no row's room.
  The spy's line (§4.34) moves down by the row too, so the section a click
  showed below the row is the one marked.
- **The same landings.** The room and a target's own `scroll-margin-top`
  add up, so the two margins drop the bar they counted: a section
  (`.sub-body [id]`) keeps 4px and lands 12px below the bar, and a trace
  step (`.pr-row`) keeps 2px and lands 10px below it, where each landed
  before on a desktop. A target with no margin of its own now lands 8px
  below the bar instead of behind it. A jump centred on its target
  (`block: 'center'`) centres it in the room below the bar.

After, in the same survey: no stop hidden or partly hidden on Rules,
Settings, a session, Approvals or Tests, at either size, either way. A
phone's sub-menu click lands its section at 140px, below the row's end
at 128px, and the trace's background step at 64px, below the 56px bar.
Page Up and Page Down step 644px instead of 700px in an 800px window, so no
line passes behind the bar unseen. Tests:
`inspector-topbar-room.test.ts` (the served stylesheet at 1280 and 390px:
the room, each landing, no margin counting the bar twice; sub-menus.js in
jsdom with the stylesheet applied: the row's height kept on a phone, none
beside the sections, on Sessions or once the window is wide, the
`resize` fallback, and the spy's line below the row; fails on master) and
the stack e2e `tests/stack/inspector-topbar-room.test.ts` (a real arbiter,
the production adapter, the served stylesheet and the served Rules and
Settings pages laid out at 390×844: the room, every entry's section below
the row and marked, Sessions without the row's room, a desktop's Settings
without it, the oracle; fails on master). Presentation only: no route,
rule, request or focus order changed.

**A dialog takes the focus and gives it back (2026-10-10).** The inspector
has eleven dialogs: *+ New run* and *▶ Run drills* (control.js), the
lazily built modals of app.js (a tool call's ⚖ Rules, ⊕ Masked values,
⤢ Full prompt, the 🛡 card, *Why is this masked?*, the symbol card, a
file's content), the shared ⓘ drawer (detail-drawer.js) and the value
popup (render-helpers.js `showSymValue`, the 🔒 reveal and the manual-copy
fallback). None moved the keyboard focus. Enter on the 🛡 chip or *+ New
run* left it on the opener, and Tab walked the page behind the backdrop.
✕, the backdrop and *Where each went →* dropped it to `<body>`. The value
popup had no ✕, and Esc closed the ⊕ table under it instead; with *Why
is this masked?* over the ⊕ table, one Esc closed both. The panels said
`role="dialog"` but not `aria-modal`, so a screen reader could read the
page behind.

- **One module.** Every dialog is a `[role="dialog"][aria-modal="true"]`
  element: a `.drawer-panel`, or the value popup. `dev/js/dialog-focus.js`,
  loaded by its own `<script>`, watches the document (a MutationObserver
  on `hidden` and on added and removed nodes), so the modules show and
  hide their dialogs as before and none imports it. control.js, whose
  text the test harnesses evaluate as is, stays import-free.
- **Shown.** The panel takes the focus (`tabindex="-1"`, preventScroll),
  and a screen reader reads the dialog's label; the next Tab is its first
  control. A dialog shown over another goes on top. What had the focus is
  remembered as its opener.
- **Inside.** Tab from the last control goes to the first, and Shift+Tab
  from the first (or from the panel) to the last. A focus behind the
  backdrop is brought in by the next Tab. A dialog that draws its own
  content again while open drops a focused control to `<body>`; its panel
  takes the focus. The 🛡 card, drawn again on a live update, first gives
  it back to the control drawn at its place (*A repaint keeps the focus*,
  below), so its panel takes it only when that control is gone. Tab
  stops are found by structure (not disabled, not `[hidden]`, not inside
  a closed `<details>` but its summary), since jsdom draws no layout.
- **Esc** presses the top dialog's ✕ (`.drawer-close`), in the capture
  phase, and stops the key there, so only that dialog closes, through its
  own module's close. The dialogs' own Esc handlers stay for a page
  without the module. The value popup now has the same ✕
  (`aria-labelledby` its title).
- **Hidden.** A focus left inside the dialog, or dropped to `<body>`,
  goes back to its opener. A redraw may have replaced the opener while
  the dialog was open (Rules repaints its tables every 3 s): then the
  control at its place takes it (the opener's id, else its rank among the
  elements of its tag and classes under the nearest ancestor with an id).
  With no such control, the dialog under it takes it, else the page
  heading. A dialog that opens another as it closes (the symbol card's
  *⊕ table at birth*) hands the new one its opener.
- **A way out that leads elsewhere** gives the focus to where it leads,
  and the module leaves it there: *Where each went →* to the Secrets
  tab's *Where each went* heading, the symbol card's *→ minting step* and
  *trace →* and the ⊕ table's *born* to the trace step (`app.js
  focusLanding`; `tabindex="-1"`).
- **No ring** on the panel or a landing: neither is a control.

**A dialog says which item it shows (2026-10-13; app.js `nameDialog`).**
A shown dialog takes the focus, so a screen reader reads it by its name.
Six of the session page's dialogs open for one item, but each was named
once, when its shell was built: a browser probe of a Secrets-mode session
opened "Full prompt" from each of three turns' ⤢, "This tool call's
rules" from the ⚖ of `Read .env`, `Bash npm test` and `Bash ls -la`,
"Symbol card", "Why is this masked?" and "Masked values" whatever token or
mark, and every file "File content". Only the ⓘ drawer was named per open
(detail-drawer.js `ariaLabel`, `surface` since), by the surface that opened
it (and by its title since, *A check's ⓘ names its call* and *A Rules
drawer says which row it shows* below). Now each is named by its item each time it
opens, and its body (a group, a Tab stop once it overflows) takes the same
name:

| Dialog | Name | Title |
|---|---|---|
| ⤢ full prompt | "Full prompt: Turn 2" (its button's turn) | "⤢ Full prompt · Turn 2 · what T-LLM received" (was without the turn) |
| ⚖ a call's rules | "This tool call's rules: Bash npm test" (the call as its ⚖ names it, §4.33 *A step names what it touched*) | "Rules · Bash npm test" (was the tool alone; an MCP tool keeps its full name here, the short one in the name) |
| ⊕ Masked values | "Masked values: as of turn 1 · Read · 2 symbols" (its moment and count, as its title says: two marks of one turn's reads differ by the count) | unchanged; a step with no recorded turn says "as of this step", never "as of turn undefined" |
| *Why is this masked?* | "Why is $MDU:… masked?" (its title's words) | unchanged |
| the symbol card | "Symbol card: $MDU:…" | unchanged (its placeholder, "the story of one secret item") |
| a file's content | "File content: HumanView · original — docs/invoice.txt" | unchanged (its view and path) |

A name holds only words the page draws: a turn, a call's args as the AI
wrote them (a secret is a placeholder), a placeholder, a moment and a
count, a view and a path. It never holds a value, signed in or out. The
🛡 card stays "Protection summary" (one per session), and *+ New run* and
*▶ Run drills* keep their names. Tests: `app-js-dialog-names.test.ts`
(each dialog opened for two items, its name, its body and its title; an
MCP tool; *⊕ table at birth*; a file in both views; no value in any name,
signed in; none alike) and `tests/stack/inspector-dialog-names.test.ts`
(two prompts, a secret read and two commands through the real arbiter,
proxy and server; the served page signed out and in; each dialog takes
the focus; the no-value oracle).

**A check's ⓘ names its call (2026-10-13; app.js `gateTitle`).** A tool
card's check line ("✓ Mandu checked this command and let it run.
[exec_action] ⓘ", §4.2f) has an ⓘ that opens the check's facts in the
shared drawer. Its name and the drawer's title were the check's recorded
text alone, and the proxy's shell gate records only its kind, so in a
real Secrets-mode session every command's ⓘ was "Details: exec_action"
and every drawer opened as "ⓘ exec_action", a drawer that hides the card
it was opened from. Every drawer the trace opened, a check's or an
action's, was named "Trace event detail" whatever it showed. Now:

| Item | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| a check's ⓘ | "Details: exec_action" | "Details: exec_action · Bash npm test" (its recorded text, then the call as its ⚖ names it, §4.33 *A step names what it touched*) |
| a check's drawer title | "ⓘ exec_action" | "ⓘ exec_action · Bash npm test" (the ⓘ is still named by it, *A button says what it does*) |
| a trace drawer's name (a check's or an action's) | "Trace event detail" | "Trace event detail: <its title>" ("Trace event detail: net_action · blocked collector.example"); its body takes the same name |

An fs check keeps its path and sentinel before the call ("Read.file_path →
/etc/shadow · DENIED → /mandu/denied/shadow · Read shadow"), and a blocked
fetch its host ("net_action · blocked evil.example · WebFetch
evil.example"). The line's words and pill, the drawer's sections and the
click are unchanged; the Rules drawers were named per row the same day
(*A Rules drawer says which row it shows*, below). A name holds only drawn
words: the check's recorded text (its
symbolized summary) and the call's args as the AI wrote them, so a
placeholder, never a value, signed in or out. Tests:
`app-js-check-info-names.test.ts` (two allowed commands, a blocked one that
used a placeholder, a held read and a blocked fetch: each check's ⓘ, its
drawer's title, name and body, none alike; an action's drawer with a
hostile destination; no value in any name, signed in) and
`tests/stack/inspector-check-info-names.test.ts` (a secret read and two
commands through the real arbiter, proxy and server; the served page signed
out and in; each check's ⓘ and drawer, which takes the focus; the no-value
oracle).

**A Rules drawer says which row it shows (2026-10-13; detail-drawer.js
`showDetail`, egress.js `DRAWER_OPTS`).** The Rules panel opens the same
shared drawer from its law source, *View the handling prompt*, each
posture chip, each of *Your answers*, each of your rules, each built-in
rule and each tool's inbound trust. Every one was named "Policy row
detail", whatever it showed, while the ⓘ that opened it was named by its
title ("Details: rule fs:sensitive-path"), so the dialog hid the row it
was opened from. Now the drawer is always named "<surface>: <the title it
opens with>", the surface being the words of the panel that opened it
(`opts.surface`; the shared drawer adds the title, so no surface can name
every drawer alike again), and its body takes the same name:

| Opened from | Name |
|---|---|
| a rule's ⓘ (yours or built-in) | "Policy row detail: rule fs:sensitive-path" |
| an answer's ⓘ | "Policy row detail: your answer egr-1" |
| a tool's inbound-trust ⓘ | "Policy row detail: inbound trust · WebFetch" |
| the law source's ⓘ | "Policy row detail: Law source" |
| *View the handling prompt* | "Policy row detail: Handling prompt" |
| a posture chip | "Policy row detail: egress: lockdown" (its drawer's title) |
| a trace event's ⓘ | "Trace event detail: <its title>" (unchanged) |

The titles, sections, the ⓘ's names, the clicks and the focus are
unchanged. A name holds only the drawer's title, which the drawer draws:
a rule's or an answer's id, a tool's name, a posture's state, never a
value, signed in or out. Tests: `egress-js-drawer-names.test.ts` (every
drawer the panel opens, a hostile tool name among them: its name, its
body's and its ⓘ's; none alike; named again at every open) and
`tests/stack/inspector-rules-drawer-names.test.ts` (a stopped send through
the real arbiter, net-proxy and server; the served Rules page signed out
and in; every drawer, which takes the focus; the no-value oracle).

A redraw outside a dialog keeps the focus too since 2026-10-11: Rules and
Approvals across their poll, a live session's trace across its next
event (*A repaint keeps the focus*, below), and an answer's list after the
answer (*An answer keeps the focus in its list*, below). Presentation only: no route,
gate or server text changed, and no value is shown that was not before.

**A repaint keeps the focus (2026-10-11).** egress.js draws the Rules panel
(with Test a flow and the Audit trail) and the Approvals cards again on
every 3 s poll, so each control is a new element. A focused button, status
filter or gate fold left the document with the focus, which fell to
`<body>`. A keyboard user had 3 s to act on a control after reaching it
(*Allow once* on a waiting question), and a screen reader lost its place
every 3 s. Only a text field or a select held the panel (§4.34 *Typing*).

- **The place.** Before it paints, `paintPanel` takes the focused
  control's place under the five painted hosts (`#egress-approvals`,
  `#rules-test`, `#rules-audit`, `#approvals-waiting`,
  `#approvals-history`; `render-helpers.js focusPlace`). The place is each
  keyed element on the way down, with its rank among those keyed alike.
  A keyed element has an id, or the `data-*` keys its row is drawn with
  (`data-id`, `data-rule-id`, `data-ruleref`, `data-gate`, `data-list`,
  `data-answer`, `data-filter`, …). Then come the control's tag, its rank
  under the last keyed element, and its words (tag, type and text).
- **A count apart (2026-10-14).** A control whose action does not depend
  on a count it shows can draw that count as `<span data-count>`, and its
  words then leave the count out (`render-helpers.js wordsOf`), so a new
  count does not make it read otherwise. Only *→ your answers · N* does
  (*The Protection block*, below). Every other control is compared on all
  its words, digits too: no number is masked unless the control says so.
- **Back.** After the paint, `refocus` focuses the control drawn there
  (preventScroll), so the next Tab goes on from it. A question that
  arrives above the focused one moves nothing: rows are found by their
  keys, not by their rank on the page.
- **Only the same control.** The focus is given back only if it fell (a
  focus the person moved stays). It goes only to a control that reads the
  same and can be reached: the one at that rank, else the first alike
  under the same keyed element. Some controls are not there to take it: a
  question answered elsewhere (its card is gone), a row whose answers
  changed (no *Block* any more), or a field the repaint drew inside a
  closed fold (an added rule's form). Then the focus stays where it fell,
  never on another action.
- **No new ring.** A focus given back looks like the one taken. In
  Chromium a keyboard focus keeps its ring, and a control clicked with the
  mouse gets none.
- **Dialogs.** A focus inside an open dialog is not under the painted
  hosts, so only the dialog module (above) handles it.

**A live session (2026-10-11).** Each new event of a live session reads
the session again (the stream's `append`, then `loadEvents`), and `ingest`
draws again the session bar (the header, *Copy id*, the summary), the
Trace tab (the step rail and the trace), the Secrets and Checks tabs, the
top bar's invariant banner and an open 🛡 card. A browser probe on master
had each of these fall to `<body>` within 3.5 s while the session ran: a
trace fold, ⤢ full prompt, ⚖, a `$MDU:` token, a *masked* chip, a rail
item and *Copy id*.

- **The same rule.** `ingest` takes the place before it draws and calls
  `refocus` after, as `paintPanel` does. The place is taken under the six
  hosts it draws (app.js `SESSION_HOSTS`: `#session-bar`, `#tab-trace`,
  `#tab-secrets`, `#tab-checks`, `#banner`, `#protection-modal`). A trace
  card is keyed by its step (`data-id`) and a symbol row by its name, and
  the trace grows at the bottom, so a new step moves nothing. In a real
  session, no control on the Trace or Secrets tab or in the 🛡 card shared
  its words with another under its keyed row. `readSession`'s second
  trace draw (the files summary) does the same.
- **The same session only.** A read of another session (a pick, a link)
  gives nothing back, even where it draws a control alike at the same
  place (its own *Copy id*).
- **The 🛡 card** is drawn again on egress.js's posture (its 3 s poll) and
  on the session list's poll too. Each time, its focused control gets the
  focus back the same way, and its panel takes it only when that control
  is not drawn again.
- **A control that reads otherwise** is left, and the focus stays where it
  fell. Examples: the newest reply's own controls once a newer reply
  arrives, a flow on the Secrets tab whose steps changed, *Load all N* as N
  grows.

Not covered: a control a poll or a read removes leaves the focus where the
browser puts it. After an answer, the next card takes it (*An answer keeps
the focus in its list*, below); after a list change, the list's name or
*Lists (N)* (§4.34 *The Lists editor says its answer to the button
pressed*). The session list's repaint has a rule of
its own (below), because a row's words (its count and time) change on each
poll. Presentation only: no route, gate or server text changed.

**The Protection block (2026-10-13).** protection.js draws Rules ›
Protection level, the pending bar, the matrix, Settings › Protection axes
and Sandbox again on each posture egress.js publishes (its 3 s poll), on
its own 30 s re-read and after each of its saves. Until 2026-10-13 it took
no place first. In jsdom on master, all 20 controls a Tab reached there
fell to `<body>` on one publish: the level radios, the matrix's jumps and
*⏸ Pause sending*, the two axis switches and the twelve Sandbox switches
(*⟳ Restart services* too, while it shows). A level pick or a switch's
save dropped the focus at once.

- **The same rule.** Each draw runs inside `keepFocus` (protection.js):
  the place is taken under the five hosts it draws (`#protection-level`,
  `#protection-pending`, `#protection-matrix`, `#protection-machinery`,
  `#sandbox-switches`), then `refocus` gives it back.
- **Keys.** A level radio carries its level (`data-level`), so a redraw
  finds it by its level, not its rank: a frozen level's card comes and
  goes with the saved level and moves the radios below it. The matrix's
  buttons and the restart have ids, an axis switch has `data-axis`, a
  Sandbox switch `data-key`.
- **A pick and a save.** The picked radio, drawn again after the save,
  has the focus and is checked. A cancelled OFF gate draws the saved level
  checked and gives the focus back to the radio the person was on. A
  Sandbox switch turns itself off during its save, and a browser may drop
  the focus of a control turned off, so it takes its place first
  (`onSandboxSwitch`).
- **Never another action.** *⏸ Pause sending* keeps the focus while it is
  drawn again. Once the pause is published, *▶ Resume* is drawn in its
  place and does not take the focus, so a second Enter cannot undo the
  pause. A radio or switch the redraw turns off (a failed re-read) takes
  none.

- **A new count (2026-10-14).** *→ your answers · N* draws its count as
  `<span data-count>` (*A count apart*, above): a publish that changes N
  (an answer given in another tab or on Approvals, one removed under Your
  answers, `—` while the count is unknown) gives the focus back to the
  jump, which reads the new count. Until 2026-10-14 the new count read
  otherwise and the focus fell to `<body>`. Its words and its accessible
  name are as before ("→ your answers · 3").

Presentation only: no route, POST body, gate or words changed.

**The restart keeps its state (2026-10-13).** The pending bar's *⟳ Restart
services* POSTs `/api/control/restart-all`, which answers only once every
service is back (`controlRestartAll` awaits `stopAll` then `startAll`).
While the protection service is down, egress.js republishes the last
known posture, so the bar stays up through the whole restart, and each
publish draws it again. Until 2026-10-13 the press turned off the button
it was given and wrote its answer into the bar, and the next publish threw
both away. In jsdom on master, a publish during the restart drew a live
button with no word, and a second press POSTed a second restart. The
sign-in words, the no-answer sentence, the server's error and "restarting
— the running state above catches up in a few seconds" were each gone at
the next publish, within 3 s.

- **Kept in the block's state.** `P.restart` (protection.js) holds the
  restart under way (`{busy}`) or its answer, and `renderPending` draws
  the bar from it. While the restart runs, the button is off and the bar
  says "restarting services…" (control.js's words for the same act). A
  press while one runs posts nothing.
- **A refusal** (sign in first, no answer, the server's error) stays under
  the bar, with the button live, until the bar goes or the next press.
- **An OK answer** says "services restarted — the running state above
  catches up in a few seconds" and keeps the button off for two
  publishes: the first may come from a read that set out before the
  restart ended, and the second set out after it. A count, not a timer:
  egress.js also publishes on its own events, which can only end the wait
  sooner. If running and saved still differ then, the restart did not
  apply the saved setting (an axis or `MANDU_MODE` exported in the
  dashboard's own environment wins over the file, `config-axes.ts
  arbiterAxisSpawnEnv`), and the bar says "the services
  restarted, but the running state above still differs from the saved
  setting", with the button live again.
- **Adopted.** An answer whose `services` shows the arbiter adopted (it
  was already running when this dashboard started; `Supervisor.stop`
  refuses it, so the restart leaves it running) says "the protection
  service was not restarted — it was already running when this dashboard
  started, so this page cannot restart it", the product page's
  `ADOPTED_SENTENCE` in the inspector's words. An adopted proxy does not
  count: the axes are the arbiter's.
- **The bar goes, its words go.** Once running and saved agree, or cannot
  be compared, the bar hides and drops a finished answer. A restart still
  under way is kept, so a posture that comes back unknown for a moment
  does not lose it.
- **Focus.** The press takes its place before it turns the button off
  (`focusPlace`, as `onSandboxSwitch` does). A refusal draws a live
  button, and that button has the focus again if the focus fell; a button
  still off takes none, and a focus the person moved stays.

Tests: `ui/protection-js-restart-state.test.ts` (jsdom; 9 of 10 fail on
master, the tenth is the moved-focus guard) and `tests/stack/inspector-restart-state.test.ts`
(`secrets`: a real arbiter, a real Supervisor over stand-in services and a
real DashboardServer; signed out the real 403 stays across two polls and
nothing restarts; signed in the restart is under way across a poll with
one POST, then its answer is kept and turns into the still-differs
sentence, since the real arbiter is not the stand-in; an adopted stand-in
gets the adopted sentence; the no-value oracle). Presentation only: the
route, the POST, its CSRF header and the server's words are unchanged.

**An answer keeps the focus in its list (2026-10-11).** The inspector's
twin of the product page's rule (§4.25 *An answer keeps the focus in its
list*). Every answer button turns its row's buttons off while the answer
is on its way (egress.js `resolve`; `answerPrompt` for a held message's
four answers; `mintRule` for *Always allow from*, which adds its rule
first). A browser drops the focus of a button turned off to `<body>`, so
the repaint that follows found no place to give back (`focusPlace`). A
headless Chromium on master showed it after Enter on *Allow once*
(Approvals › Waiting for your answer), on *Block* (Rules › Your answers),
on *Allow instead* (Answered earlier) and on a refused *Block* signed out:
`BODY` each time, and the refused button, on again, had lost the focus.
The three lists are `#approvals-waiting`, `#approvals-history` and
`#rules-answers`.

- **Pressed with the focus in its row.** Only then does anything move
  (`holdFocus`: the list, the row's id and rank, the button's words). A
  click made with the focus elsewhere moves nothing.
- **An answer that worked.** After the paint the answer's `refresh` (or
  the poll) draws, the focus goes to the first of these that is shown
  (`focusAfterAnswer`):
  - the row with the answered id, when it is still drawn (Your answers and
    Answered earlier keep an answered row, with its new answers);
  - the card that took its place, else the one before it;
  - the list's own line ("Nothing is waiting for you.");
  - its section's heading (the card's `h3`, Your answers' `h4`);
  - the page heading (`#page-heading`).

  It is never an answer button, so a second Enter never answers another
  question.
- **The poll keeps it there.** The 3 s poll draws every card again, so
  where the focus landed keeps it across the next paints while it has it
  (`keepLanding`): the card drawn again is found by its id, else the same
  way. A new question that replaces "Nothing is waiting for you." takes the
  focus from the line. A landing the focus left (a Tab into the card's own
  controls, a click on the page) is let go.
- **An answer that was refused** (signed out, already answered elsewhere,
  no answer from the dashboard server). The button pressed, on again, gets
  the focus back (`focusRefused`). The refusal's words describe the row's
  buttons (`aria-describedby`; `showRowError` numbers them as drawn, since
  the same question is drawn on Rules and on Approvals), also after the
  poll draws them again. A read that set out before the press may draw
  the row again while the answer is on its way. Then the row drawn now
  gets the words, and its button gets the focus; a row whose answers
  changed takes the focus itself. The words go to the rows drawn now with
  that id also for a press that did not have the focus (a mouse click in a
  browser that does not focus a clicked button), and the focus stays
  where it is (`keepRowAnswer`; until 2026-10-11 they went to the replaced
  row and showed only after the next poll).
- **Nothing is taken back.** A poll while the answer is on its way paints
  nothing (`E.busy`). A focus the person moves elsewhere meanwhile (a
  `focusin`) drops the answer's place.
- **The ring.** A card, row, line or heading takes the focus with
  `tabindex="-1"`, so it is no Tab stop, and with preventScroll. A
  keyboard answer shows the browser's focus ring on it; a mouse answer
  shows none (Chromium, `:focus-visible`). No CSS changed.

Presentation only: no route, verb, gate or server text changed, and no
value is shown that was not shown before.

**A question has a name (2026-10-11).** The inspector's twin of the product
page's rule (§4.25 *A question has a name*). Approvals' Waiting cards,
Answered earlier and Rules › Your answers offer the same answers beside
their words, so a screen reader read "Block, button" with no word of what
it blocks.

- **A Waiting card** is a group named by its sentence (`role="group"`,
  `aria-labelledby`).
- **A table row** cannot be a group, as a `<tr>` keeps its row role. So
  each answer button in it (`.egress-actions`, *Always allow from*
  included; not the ⓘ) is described by the row's question
  (`aria-describedby`, `describeAnswers`). In Answered earlier that is the
  sentence; in Your answers it is what → where.
- **A refusal.** Its words come first, then the question (`showRowError`).
  A card's refused button is described by the words alone, since the card
  is named already.
- **The id** is the list's and the question's
  (`approvals-q-<list>-<encoded id>`). So the 3 s repaint draws the same
  one again, and *A repaint keeps the focus* still finds the same control,
  and the same question drawn in two lists has two. The question's id is
  encoded (an id list is split on spaces) and never spliced into a
  selector. Only the words take it, never a row or a control, so
  `focusPlace` keys nothing on it.

Presentation only: no route, verb, gate, server text or CSS changed.

**A button says what it does (2026-10-11).** A button's name is its words,
and a family of the inspector's buttons had only a glyph for words. Their
`title` is only a description, and it was the same on every row. So a
screen reader read "ⓘ, button" (or "circled latin small letter i") on every
row of the trace and of Rules, and "wastebasket, button" on every session.
Nothing said what each one opens or deletes. A headless Chromium on master
(the accessibility tree, a real arbiter and dashboard, signed in) found 5
of 21 buttons on a session's page with no word in their name. On Rules it
found 4 shown, plus 103 more in the folded Built-in rules and inbound-trust
groups. Now each one is named in words (`aria-label`), and its glyph and
title stay as drawn:

- **An ⓘ** is named "Details: " + the title its drawer opens with
  (`detail-drawer.js infoName`, for `infoBtn` and `lazyInfoBtn`; app.js
  `stepInfoName` for the trace). That is a rule's id ("Details: rule
  fs:sensitive-path"), an answer's id ("Details: your answer egr-3"), a
  tool's trust ("Details: inbound trust · Bash"), a trace step's kind and
  title with the kind said once ("Details: net_action · blocked
  collector.example", §4.2f *The kind, said once*), or a check's text and
  the call it checked ("Details: exec_action · Bash npm test", *A check's
  ⓘ names its call*). So the name says nothing a click on it would not
  show. The drawer opens
  headed by the same words.
- **A 🗑** names what it deletes by the words its row draws: "Delete the
  session: <the row's title>" ("the test session" on a test's row),
  "Delete all 3 sessions in the batch <the batch's title>", "… in the run
  <the run's title>". In the Lists editor it is "Delete @<list>".
- **A dialog's ✕** is "Close", in each of the eleven dialogs: index.html's
  two, app.js's seven, the ⓘ drawer and the value popup.
- **The other glyphs.** The Lists editor's ✕ is "Remove <entry> from
  @<list>", and its ＋ is "Add to @<list>". A prompt-filter keyword's × is
  "Remove the keyword <word>". A log's failure jumps (`✗ 1`) are "Go to
  failure 1".

The Your answers row's ⓘ is not described by the row's question, as its
answer buttons are (*A question has a name*): it is no answer, and its name
already holds the answer's id. Presentation only: no route, verb, gate,
server text or CSS changed, and no name holds words the page or the drawer
does not already show (the names are escaped, or set with `setAttribute`).

**The session list works from the keyboard (2026-10-11).** The list on
the Sessions, Drills and Tests pages (§4.33) is how the inspector picks a
session and folds a day or a run, and no keyboard could reach it. A row
was a `<div>` with a click handler. A fold was a `role="button"` `<div>`
with no `tabindex` and no key. The 🗑 was `display: none` until the row
was hovered (§4.10.5). In a browser on master the list had no Tab stop at
all: Tab from its search box went on to the main pane, and `focus()` on a
row or a fold did nothing.

- **Tab stops.** A row's button part (`.s-main`, its name and meta line;
  `role="button"`, `tabindex="0"`) and every fold (`.batch-head`) are Tab
  stops, in the list's order. A row's 🗑 is its sibling, not inside it, so
  the row's button holds no other control. A folded batch draws no rows
  (§4.30), so its rows add no stops until it opens.
- **Keys.** Enter or Space presses the row or the fold as a click does
  (`app.js wireButtonKeys`, one listener on the document since 2026-10-12,
  *A control the mouse can press, the keyboard can too* below). A row opens its
  session, and the focus stays on the row; a fold opens or closes, and
  `aria-expanded` follows. The key is acted on only when the row or the
  fold itself has the focus: Enter on the 🗑 inside a fold presses only
  the 🗑.
- **The current row.** The selected row's button says
  `aria-current="true"` (`markActiveRow`, beside its `.active` highlight),
  and so does a row a fold draws later.
- **The 🗑.** It is hidden by `opacity: 0` and `pointer-events: none`
  instead of `display: none`, so a Tab reaches it. Hover shows it as
  before. The keyboard focus on its row, on its fold or on the 🗑 itself
  shows it too (`:focus-visible`), so the next Tab after a row is that
  row's 🗑 when the server allows deleting.
- **The ring.** A row's button and a fold draw the accent ring on a
  keyboard focus. A mouse click gets none.
- **The repaint keeps the focus.** The list is drawn again whenever its
  signature changes, and every 15 s while a session runs
  (`loadSessionsOnce`). Before the paint, `paintSessionList` notes what
  the focused control acts on (`listFocusPlace`): a row and its 🗑 by the
  session, a fold and its 🗑 by the batch, the remainder note by itself.
  After the paint, `refocusList` focuses the control drawn for the same
  session or batch. Unlike *A repaint keeps the focus* above, it does not
  compare words: a row's time and count change on every poll, and its
  action does not. The same limits hold. The focus is given back only if
  it fell, never to another row or fold, and never to a control that is
  hidden, disabled or in a closed fold. A row the poll no longer lists
  leaves the focus where it fell.

Not covered: the list is one Tab stop per row, plus its 🗑 when signed
in. A roving tabindex with the arrow keys (the tree pattern) would make it
one stop; it is a larger change. The fold's `role="button"` holds its
batch 🗑, a nested control from before this change. (Until the next
subsection, a pick from the phone's list closed it and the focus did not
move to the session.) Presentation only: no route, gate or server text
changed, and no value is shown that was not shown before.

**The phone's session list works from the keyboard (2026-10-12).** At
760 px and narrower the list column is hidden, and ☰ in the top bar opens
it as a slide-over over the page (`body.nav-open`, §4.1 *Mobile*). A
headless Chromium on master at 390 px, over a real arbiter, proxy and
dashboard, found it unusable from the keyboard:

- ☰ was `button "Open the session list"` with no `aria-expanded`: open or
  closed, a screen reader heard the same thing.
- Enter on ☰ opened the list and left the focus on ☰, so the next Tabs
  walked the six page links before reaching it.
- Escape in the list did nothing; the list stayed over the page.
- A pick (Enter on a row, or a tap) closed the list and hid the row that
  had the focus, so the focus fell to `<body>`. A tap on the backdrop did
  the same.
- A Tests or Drills sub-page picked in the list (*Run a suite*, *CI*,
  *Matrix*) changed the page under the list, which stayed open, and the
  page heading behind the backdrop took the focus.

What it does now (`app.js wireNavToggle`, `setNavOpen`, `landOnSession`):

- **☰ says what it opens and whether it is open.** It is named "Session
  list", with `aria-controls="sidebar"` and `aria-expanded` false or true;
  every change to `nav-open` goes through `setNavOpen`, including the
  close a full-width page makes (`applyPageChrome`).
- **Opening it moves the focus into it:** to the open session's row
  (`aria-current`), else to the list's heading (`#sidebar-title`,
  `tabindex="-1"`, no ring), as on a Tests tool page, which lists no
  sessions, or when a closed fold hides the row. A tap opens it the same
  way; Chromium draws no ring after a tap, and no text box takes the focus,
  so no on-screen keyboard opens.
- **Escape closes it and gives the focus to ☰**, when the focus is in the
  list, on ☰, or nowhere. Not an Escape another handler took: the search
  box's Escape, which clears a typed search, now says so
  (`preventDefault`), so the first Escape clears the search and the next
  closes the list. Not one with a modifier, nor one that ends an input
  method's composition (`isComposing`, `keyCode` 229). An Escape in the top
  bar or a dialog is theirs.
- **☰ and the backdrop close it**, and a focus left in the list, or fallen
  to `<body>` (a tap on the backdrop drops it first), goes to ☰. A focus the
  person moved out of the list stays where it is.
- **A Tab out of it into the page behind closes it.** The list is not a
  dialog: the top bar stays usable (Shift+Tab from its first control
  reaches Product ↗), but a focus that moves into `#main`, behind the
  backdrop, closes the list. The dialogs and the top bar are outside
  `#main`, so + New run's dialog keeps it open.
- **A pick closes it and lands on what was picked.** A session row (a
  click, a tap, Enter or Space) closes the list and notes the pick
  (`S.landOn`). Once the read has drawn that session's title (its trace,
  or the *Could not read this session* header), `landOnSession` gives the
  title (`#session-title`, `tabindex="-1"`, no ring) the focus and scrolls
  it into view if the last session left it above. It waits for the read, so
  a screen reader reads the new session's title, never the old one. A
  sub-page link routed in place (its default prevented) closes the list,
  and the page heading takes the focus as on any page change; a modified
  click opens a new tab and leaves it open. A fold or a 🗑 is no pick.
- **Never a focus the person moved.** The landing happens only if the
  focus fell (on `<body>`, or still in the closed list, where jsdom keeps
  it). A focus moved elsewhere during the read stays, as does a list
  opened again. A later pick drops an earlier one (`selectSession` clears
  `S.landOn` for another session), and a pick with the list closed (the
  desktop list) keeps the focus on its row, as above.

Desktop is unchanged: ☰ is not drawn there. Presentation only: no route,
gate or server text changed, and no value is shown that was not shown
before. Tests: `app-js-nav-drawer.test.ts` (jsdom: ☰'s name and states, a
full-width page; the focus on opening, row and heading; Escape and the
search box's, its modifier, composition, taken and away cases; the
backdrop and ☰; a focus into the page behind; a pick's landing after a
held read and a failed one; a moved focus and a reopened list; a later
pick; a sub-page and a modified click. Each case fails on master but the
two guards, and all 22 mutations of the new code are caught) and stack
`tests/stack/inspector-nav-drawer.test.ts` (`secrets`: a real arbiter
with a labelled `.env`, the real anthropic-proxy on its production
adapter, three sessions through it, a real dashboard and the served
app.js signed out: ☰ opens on the open row, Escape gives ☰ the focus, a
pick lands on the title the real read drew, the backdrop and a Tab into
the page close it; the oracle). Not covered: Tab still reaches the main
page from the list's last control (and closes it), rather than wrapping
inside it as a dialog would.

**A row stays a row (2026-10-11).** Rules › Your answers and the Secrets
panel's Labels and Derived files tables draw their buttons in a `<td>` of
class `.egress-actions`. The class is also the Approvals cards' flex row,
and it made the `<td>` a flex box, which is no longer a table cell. A
headless Chromium on master (a real arbiter, the net-proxy stopping three
sends and a real dashboard) found three faults:

- **A refusal one letter wide.** Signed out, *Allow once* on a Your answers
  row is refused, and egress.js `showRowError` puts the refusal's words in
  that cell. There they were a flex item beside the buttons, 22 px wide,
  one or two letters per line. The row grew to 1128 px and the table
  overflowed its section.
- **The cell outside its row.** The answers cell was 34 px high in a 44 px
  row, so its bottom line was 10 px above the row's line, and the row's
  tint (a pending row, a declassified label) stopped at it.
- **A host broken at any letter.** `.queue-what code` and `.rule-what
  code` had `word-break: break-all`, so the What cell read "$MDU:…
  → c" / "ollector3.example" at window widths from about 1290 to 1430 px
  (1366 included). The Secrets panel's model-readable note did the same.

Now `td.egress-actions` is a table cell. Its buttons sit on one line, 4 px
apart, and the row's line and tint run across it. A refusal's words go
under the buttons and wrap. With `contain: inline-size` they take the
width the buttons give the cell and do not widen it, but they take at
least 22em, for a row with one narrow button. So the table keeps its
shape. A host, a path or a rule id moves whole to the next line where it
fits there (`overflow-wrap: anywhere`), and breaks only where it is wider
than its cell. Neither front-end's stylesheet uses `break-all` any more.
The Approvals cards keep their flex row (`div.egress-actions`).
Presentation only: CSS, with no route, words or markup changed.

**A row's control names its row (2026-10-11).** The Secrets and Prompt
filters panels on Rules draw a control per row, and none said which row it
acts on. A headless Chromium on master (a real arbiter with a policy.yaml
that sets prompt-filter actions and exceptions, the person's pack, three
labelled paths and a real dashboard, signed in) read 48 controls in the
two panels. Nine selects had no name at all: each filter's *On error*, each
action's select, the add forms' action and check, and the label form's
Level. Nine buttons read "Remove", with no word of which label, action,
exception or pattern. "Turn off" and "Turn on" came twice each, three boxes
were named "category", and the label form's Path and Bindings boxes were
named by their placeholder examples ("/home/you/notes"). Two repaints also
dropped the keyboard focus to `<body>`: the Secrets panel's 5 s poll drew
its tables again whatever the answer, and a change in Prompt filters
(`paintAll`) drew them again after it was saved.

- **Names.** Each row's control is named by its visible words, then its
  row (`aria-label`, so the words a person sees start the name): "Remove
  the label on <path>", "Clear taint on <path>", "Turn off <filter>", "On
  error for <filter>", "Model for <plugin>", "Action for <category>",
  "Remove the action for <category>", "Remove the exception for
  <category> matching <match>", "Remove the pattern <id> from <pack>". The
  add forms' boxes say which form they fill ("New row's category", "New
  exception's category", "New pattern's check", "New keyword's pack id");
  a box whose placeholder already says it keeps that. The label form's
  Path and Bindings are named by the words above them
  (`aria-labelledby`), and its Level by its word, then its form (since
  2026-10-13, *No two controls on Rules share a name*, below). A path or a match is untrusted, so a name is set
  with `setAttribute`, never as markup, and holds nothing the row does not
  show.
- **The Secrets poll draws only on a change.** `render` compares the panel
  with the one it drew last and draws nothing when they are the same, so a
  focused control keeps the focus and a screen reader is not sent back to
  the top every 5 s. A write (Label path, Remove, Clear taint) draws it
  again regardless, since it disabled its row's buttons; an error clears
  what was drawn.
- **A repaint gives the focus back by name.** Before a redraw, each panel
  notes the name of the control with the focus (`focusedName`); after it,
  the one control drawn with the same name gets the focus back
  (`refocusNamed`). The rule is `render-helpers.js` `refocus`'s (both files
  stay import-free, for their tests): only when the focus fell, only a
  control that is not disabled, and never another. A row the change
  removed, or a filter whose *Turn off* now reads *Turn on*, leaves the
  focus where it fell.

Not covered then: a refused Remove or Clear taint said so in the label
form's line, away from its row, and a browser that blurs a disabled button
dropped the focus when the write was sent (covered since 2026-10-12, *Remove
and Clear taint say what they did* below). Prompt filters' *Held for your
answer* and *Recent findings* rows follow next. Presentation only: no
route, verb, gate or server text changed.

**No two controls on Rules share a name (2026-10-13; index.html,
egress.js).** A survey of the served Rules page read 170 controls signed
in and 151 signed out. It loaded every module the page loads over a real
arbiter and dashboard, with one waiting answer, a labelled file and a
prompt-filter pack. Two selects were both named "Level": the Secrets label
form's and Test a flow's. A screen reader's list of the page's controls
read "Level, combobox" twice, one labelling a path and one setting the
level of a tested flow. The Audit trail's kind filter had no name at all
("combobox, every kind"). Now:

| Control | Name |
|---|---|
| Secrets › the label form's Level | "Level of the new label" (`aria-label`; the word "Level" above it stays) |
| Test a flow's Level | "Level of the data to test" |
| the Audit trail's kind filter | "Kind of audit entry" |

Each Level's name starts with the word on screen, then says which form it
fills (*A row's control names its row*). The kind filter has no word
beside it, so its name says what it picks. Every other control on the page
already had a name of its own. The exception is several waiting answers:
their verbs repeat by design, and each is described by its question (*A
question has a name*). The visible words, the options, what a test sends,
what the filter shows and the focus are unchanged. `focusPlace` keys on a
control's tag, type and text, not on its name, so the repaint still gives
the focus back. Tests: `egress-js-form-names.test.ts` (the three names;
neither form nor the Audit trail shares a name with any control on Rules;
