named again on every repaint; the named controls still send the level and
filter the trail) and `tests/stack/inspector-rules-form-names.test.ts` (a
stopped send answered over the real route and a locked path; the served
Rules page signed in and out, where no control shares a name or has none;
the named filter over the real admin stream; the named Level through the
real Test a flow; the no-value oracle). Presentation only: no route, verb,
gate, server text or CSS changed.

**A level radio is named by its word (2026-10-13; protection.js
`renderLevel`).** Each level of Rules › Protection level (§4.19) is a
card: a `<label>` that wraps the radio, the level's word, its tags
(`default`, and `frozen` on an integrity level) and its sentence. The
radio had no name of its own, so a browser named it by the whole card.
A headless Chromium read `radio "Secrets DEFAULT Your keys and credentials
leave this machine only where a rule or your OK allows. Untrusted content
is not masked."`, and a screen reader read that sentence at every arrow
key between the levels. Now each radio is `aria-labelledby` its drawn
word and `aria-describedby` its tags, then its sentence, in the order
they are drawn (ids `prot-level-<level>-name`, `-default`, `-frozen`,
`-desc`). The same Chromium now reads `radio "Secrets"`, described "DEFAULT
Your keys and credentials …". A saved frozen level, offered disabled, is
"Full", described "FROZEN: NEEDS MANDU_EXPERIMENTAL_INTEGRITY=1 Both: …"
(the tags are drawn in capitals). The description follows what is drawn,
so the default tag rides the server's `defaultMode` there too, and a card
without a tag is described by its sentence alone. `renderLevel` empties
its block before it draws, so each id is on the page once. The Machinery
and Sandbox switches in Settings keep their names: each one's label is a
single sentence, with no word apart from it. Tests:
`protection-js-level-names.test.ts` (four cards opted in, two without the
opt-in, a saved frozen level, a payload with no `defaultMode`, and a level
change that draws the cards again; each id is used once) and
`tests/stack/inspector-protection-level-names.test.ts` (the served Rules
page over a real arbiter and dashboard, signed out and in; the radio named
"Off" saves `mode = "off"` through the real route, and the redrawn radios
are named the same; the no-value oracle). Presentation only: no route,
POST, typed gate, word on screen or CSS changed.

**Remove and Clear taint say what they did (2026-10-12).** The Secrets
panel's row writes said their answer in the wrong place or not at all.
`removeLabel` and `clearDerived` wrote a refusal into the label form's line
(`secrets-label-err`): for Remove, under the form below the Labels table;
for Clear taint, above the *Derived files* heading, a part away from its
row. Neither line was a live region. A write that worked said nothing, and
its row just went. A Remove on a label written in policy.yaml
(`source: "policy-file"`, which every label the panel's own *Label path*
makes now is, since it writes through `files/labels`) answers `200
{"removed": false}`: `DELETE /api/secrets/label` removes only a label the
protection service stores. Nothing changed, the row stayed, and the panel
said nothing. The button was turned off while the write was on its way, and
Chromium drops a disabled button's focus to `<body>`; nothing gave it back.

- **A line under each table.** The Labels table and the Derived files table
  each have their own line under them (`secrets-labels-status`,
  `secrets-derived-status` in `dev/index.html`). Each is a `role="status"`
  region in the page from the start, outside the table's host, so the
  redraw after the write keeps the words, as Prompt filters' lines do
  (§4.31 *What a change did*). The label form keeps its own line for
  *Label path*. One line speaks: a click writes into its part's line and
  clears the other two (`say`), so does *Label path*.
- **The words.** A refusal is the server's words, the sign-in sentence
  (§4.19.v3) or the no-answer sentence (§4.8), drawn `svc-err`. What a write
  did is a plain note: "Removed the label on <path>." and "Cleared the taint
  on <path>. A later write by a high session taints it again." An answer
  that changed nothing is said as a refusal: on a label written in
  policy.yaml, "Not removed: the label on <path> is written in policy.yaml,
  which Remove does not change. Change it there, or under Rules on the
  product page."; on a label or taint already gone, "Nothing removed: there
  was no label on <path> any more." / "Nothing cleared: no taint was
  recorded on <path> any more." A path is untrusted: text, never markup.
- **The focus** (`land`), only for a press made with the focus on the
  button (`pressedName`, taken before the button is turned off). A write
  that worked lands on its table's heading (`secrets-labels-head`,
  `secrets-derived-head`, `tabindex="-1"`), never another row's button, so
  a second Enter removes nothing else. One refused, or that changed
  nothing, gives the focus back to the same row's button, drawn again and
  on again, described by its part's line (`aria-describedby`). A focus the
  person moved while the write was on its way stays. `mutate` now awaits
  its redraw, so the focus lands on what was drawn.

Presentation only: the same routes and verbs, and no server text changed.
Remove is not made to change policy.yaml: that would change which
control-plane path a loosening takes, and is the human's decision (the
*Developer view* bullet of §4.25m).

**Held and Recent findings say which row, and keep the focus
(2026-10-12).** Prompt filters' *Held for your answer* offers each held
message "Send as written", "Send as written (session)", "Send masked" (or
"redacted") and "Cancel", and *Recent findings* offers each finding "show
original", "let through once" and "let through (session)". With two
messages held, a screen reader read "Cancel, button" twice, with no word of
which message each cancels. While a message is held, its table is drawn
again every 3 s, and a focused answer, or *Refresh*, fell to `<body>`
within 3 s. An answer turned its button off, which drops the focus in a
browser, and then the row went; "show original" replaced itself with the
value; a let-through that worked drew the list again; and a refused one
turned its button back on after the focus had fallen. Each left the focus
on `<body>`.

- **Each control is described by its row.** These answers are questions
  (*A question has a name*), and a table row cannot be a group, so each
  control is described by its row's own cells (`aria-describedby`). A
  held message's answers are described by its category and filter, its
  found text and its session ("acme.codename (acme-dlp) falcon s1"). A
  finding's controls are described by its category, its symbol when it
  has one, and its time, so the same category in two messages reads
  apart. The names stay the visible words. The cells' ids carry the
  approval or event id, encoded (`pf-hold-<id>-…`,
  `pf-finding-<event id>-<n>-…`), so an id list never splits. They are
  never spliced into a selector.
- **The 3 s repaint gives the focus back by row.** Each row is keyed
  (`data-row`: `hold <approval id>`, `finding <event id> <n>`), and a
  control's name for *A repaint gives the focus back by name* starts with
  its row's key. So after the repaint the same message's control gets the
  focus back, never another message's control with the same words. A
  message that left the list, or a focus the person moved, is left where
  it is.
- **An answer to a held message.** One that worked gives the focus to the
  *Held for your answer* heading, never to an answer button, so a second
  Enter answers no other message. The part's line says what was answered.
  A refused one gives the focus back to the button pressed, drawn again,
  with the refusal said in the part's line. With the list unreadable, the
  heading takes the focus.
- **A finding.** "show original" gives its focus to the value it shows in
  its place. A let-through that worked gives the focus to the finding's
  words drawn again ("redact · let through (this message)"), and a refused
  one to its button, back on.
- **Only from where the press left it.** These apply only when the press
  was made with the focus on its button, and the focus then fell (a
  browser) or stayed on that button (jsdom, a slow blur). A press made
  with the focus elsewhere, or a focus the person moved meanwhile, moves
  nothing. None of the places the focus lands is a control, so none is a
  Tab stop or draws a ring.

Presentation only: no route, body, confirm, gate or server text changed.

**A box that scrolls says what it holds (2026-10-12).** The inspector's
twin of the product page's rule (§4.25): Chromium makes a box that
overflows and holds nothing to focus a Tab stop of its own, read by its
role and name. Until 2026-10-12 none of the session page's had a name. A
headless Chromium on a real session, signed in, stopped on three. The
".env contains" half of a Read was a `generic` named by the file's 3,023
characters, the labelled secret's line among them. The AI's reply was
named by its 2,102 characters, and the symbol card's hidden content by
the value. Now each such box on the session page is a `group` named by
the words drawn by it (`boxName` in app.js, as `aria-label`):

| Box (dashboard.css) | Where | Name |
|---|---|---|
| `.dv-preview` | the paired story: your prompt, a call's args and result, what the AI received, the reply, the context summary, the sandboxed model's instruction | "Your prompt"; the label's words ("input: args issued by the AI", "output: result", "got: what the AI received"); "AI replied"; "Context summary written by the AI's harness"; "Asked the sandboxed model" |
| `.dv-preview.pr-orig` | the story's right half | the words above it: "notes.md contains", "The real result", "You saw", "The sandboxed model read" (or the reader's words), "It answered" |
| `.fp-block-body` | the full prompt | its pill's words, without the glyph ("agent system prompt", "injected by Mandu", "User (original prompt)", a context block's label) |
| `.symcard-value` | the symbol card | its heading's words, "The hidden content" |
| `.fx-seed-content` | a test session's seeded files | the file's path |
| `.git-detail pre` | Files › Commits | "The changes in" and the commit's short hash |
| `.fs-explorer` | Files › Both views | its view's words ("AgentView · symbolized", "HumanView · original") |
| `#fs-file-modal pre` | a file's popup | its title's words ("HumanView · original — docs/invoice.txt") |
| `.detail-pre` | the ⓘ drawer's verbatim block | its section's heading |
| `.watch-screen` | Drills › Recording & checks, a turn's Terminal block (2026-10-17) | "Terminal: " and its turn ("Terminal: Turn 1 · reply"); the launcher's lines folded above it, "The launcher's output" |
| `.drawer-body` | each dialog of the session page | its dialog's name, per open since 2026-10-13 (*A dialog says which item it shows*: "Full prompt: Turn 2", "Symbol card: $MDU:…", "This tool call's rules: Bash npm test", "Masked values: as of turn 1 · Read · 1 symbol", "Why is $MDU:… masked?", "File content: HumanView · original — docs/invoice.txt"; "Protection summary"; the ⓘ drawer's, the trace's "Trace event detail: <its title>" and Rules' "Policy row detail: <its title>" since 2026-10-13) |

A name is never what the box holds: the hidden content's box and a Read's
original never name the value. A dialog's body is named because a body of
text alone (the ⓘ drawer's, or a full prompt with no masked item) is a
stop once it overflows. A box holding a box that is a stop is no stop
itself (a static Chromium check), so a dialog that holds a named block
reads once. A box that holds a control is never a stop: what the AI
received holds its token's button, the commit list its scope buttons and
rows, both views' trees their files' rows (since 2026-10-12, below), the
symbol table each row's *why masked?*, and the evidence graph its nodes;
Drills › Videos' script beside the player (`.fv-script`, 2026-10-18) holds
each line's time button and its Copy and `.srt` buttons, and is named
"Voice-over script" besides.
They keep their names, which do nothing there. No `tabindex` is added.
Sighted readers see no change. Presentation only: no route, server text or
value changed.

**Not covered:** the Run, Tests, CI and VM-matrix tooling's boxes
(control.js, ci.js, drills.js, matrix.js, and the Replay and drill checks
tables) are not yet surveyed; the guard below lists them so. Settings ›
Services' log boxes are named by their service since 2026-10-12 (§4.8 *Each
fold names its service*). The tables of
Approvals and Rules are named since 2026-10-12 (*A table's box says what
it holds*, below). The Files tab's commit rows and tree rows, which a keyboard could
not reach, are buttons since 2026-10-12 (*A control the mouse can press, the
keyboard can too*, below): the trees now hold controls and are no stops of
their own, named as before.

Tests: `app-js-scroll-names.test.ts` (jsdom with mandu.css and
dashboard.css applied; `scrollStops` / `scrollFaults` from
`control-names.ts`):

- every rule of `dev/dashboard.css` that scrolls is listed as holding
  controls, named, or not yet surveyed, so a new one is a decision;
- the paired story (a long prompt; a masked Read of `.env`; a Grep whose
  result holds a token; a sandboxed model's read and answer; a reply filled
  in on the right), the compaction summary, the full prompt, the symbol
  card, each dialog the trace opens, the seeded files, the Files tab and a
  file's popup, and the ⓘ drawer's handling prompt;
- on each surface, every box that may scroll and holds nothing to focus
  has a role and a name, and no name holds the value.

Eight of its nine cases fail on the old page (the sweep is a guard), and
31 of 31 mutations are caught. Stack `tests/stack/inspector-scroll-names.test.ts`
(secrets) serves the session page with the served styles. A real arbiter
labels a 40-line `.env`. The real anthropic-proxy, on its production
wiring, carries a turn in which a scripted model reads it and replies at
length. A real dashboard serves the page signed in: the prompt, the Read's
original and the reply are named groups, and so are the symbol card's
hidden content and the full prompt's blocks. Signed out, the original is
withheld and no box is unnamed. The oracle: the secret reached no model
raw, no name the page drew carries it, and no signed-out page or answer
carries it.

**A table's box says what it holds (2026-10-12).** The same rule for the
tables of the Approvals and Rules pages. Each sits in a `.table-scroll`
box (§4.34), which scrolls sideways once the table is wider than the page,
as it is on a phone. A headless Chromium at 400 px, on a real arbiter with
three stopped sends and two labelled paths, signed in, stopped on the
Secrets › Confined files box: a `generic` with no name, so a screen reader
said nothing of it. Now every table's box on those pages is a `group`
named by the words of the heading drawn before it (render-helpers.js
`scrollBox(table, name)`, and its import-free twins in secrets.js and
prompt-filters.js `table(name, …)`):

| Page › part | Boxes, by name |
|---|---|
| Rules › the law | "Your answers", "Your rules", each built-in gate's title ("File path gate", "Egress gate", "Exec gate", …), "What gets masked on the way in" |
| Rules › Audit trail | "Audit trail" |
| Rules › Prompt filters | "Filters", "Plugins", "Actions", "Exceptions", "Packs", a pack's patterns by its heading ("mine (user, yours)"), "Held for your answer", "Recent findings", "Test bench" |
| Rules › Secrets | "Confined files", "Labels", "Derived files", "Programs holding a secret" |
| Approvals | "Answered earlier" |

A name is a heading's words, never a row's path, host, symbol or found
text. The boxes whose tables hold no control (Confined files, Programs
holding a secret, Audit trail, and Prompt filters' read-only tables) are
the ones Chromium stops on. The rest hold buttons, so they are never a stop,
but they are named all the same: a reader hears which table it entered,
and a table that loses its last control later is named already. The
Secrets tables' hosts (`#secrets-list`, `#secrets-labels`) had their own
`overflow-x: auto` from before the boxes. They never overflowed, since
their boxes do, so the rule is dropped from them, with `#egress-queue`,
which no page draws. Settings draws no table in a box (its Services
logs are named by their service, §4.8). Sighted readers see no
change. Presentation only: no route, server text or value changed.

Tests: `inspector-table-names.test.ts` (jsdom with mandu.css and
dashboard.css applied): egress.js's Rules and Approvals tables, secrets.js's
four, and prompt-filters.js's, read-only. Each box is a group whose name
starts the heading drawn before it, no panel has a nameless box that may
scroll, and no name holds a path or a value. All four of its cases fail on
the old page. Stack `tests/stack/inspector-table-names.test.ts` (secrets)
uses a real arbiter, the net-proxy in its production wiring stopping three
sends of a registered key (one answered), two labels, and a real dashboard
on the production adapters. The served Rules and Approvals pages are read
signed in and out, with the served styles. The oracle: the key's value is
in no answer, page or name.

**A control the mouse can press, the keyboard can too (2026-10-12).** On
a real session (a labelled `.env`, two agent writes synced by fs-sync, a
Read through the proxy), a headless Chromium on the session page found no
Tab stop for five controls a click opens, and two that a Tab reached but
Enter did not press:

| Control | Before | What it opens |
|---|---|---|
| Files › Commits: a commit row (`.git-commit`) | a `<div>` with a click handler | its changes |
| Files › Both views: a file row (`.fs-row`) | a `<div>` with a click handler | the view's content, in a popup |
| Secrets: a symbol's name (`.sym-card-link`) | a `<span>` with a click handler | the symbol card |
| Secrets: its value (`.sym-value-cell`, signed in) | a `<span>` with a click handler | the value, in a popup |
| Secrets: its flow (`.flow-steps`) | a `<span>` with a click handler | the symbol card |
| The symbol card's evidence graph: a node (`.lin-node`) | `role="button"` and a Tab stop, but Enter did nothing | the event, in the trace |
| Files › Commits: a scope button | a `<button>` whose press drew the list again and dropped the focus to `<body>` | the scope |

- **Buttons.** Each row and cell above is `role="button"` with
  `tabindex="0"`, in the page's order. Its look is unchanged, and a
  keyboard focus draws the accent ring, as the session list's rows do
  (`dashboard.css`); a click draws none.
- **One rule for the keys.** `app.js wireButtonKeys` (it replaces the
  session list's `wireListKeys`) presses a focused `role="button"` element
  on Enter or Space as a click does, a graph node included (an SVG element
  has no `click()`, so it gets a click event). Only the focused element
  itself: a key on a `<button>`, a link or a field is that control's own.
  Never a key with Alt, Ctrl, Meta or Shift, one that ends an input
  method's composition (`isComposing`, keyCode 229), nor one a handler of
  its own already took (`defaultPrevented`).
- **Names.** A commit row is named by its words (hash, subject, file
  count). A file row is named by its whole path and size ("docs/plan.md,
  25 B"): the folder line above it says the folder only to the eye. A
  symbol's name cell is named by the symbol. The value cell is named for
  its row, "The value of <symbol>", never by the value it shows. The flow
  cell is named for its row and its steps in words ("Flow of <symbol>:
  symbolize t2, tool_result t2").
- **State.** The commit whose changes show is `aria-current="true"` and
  stays so through the list's redraw (`S.gitShown`); a session read anew
  has none open, so its pane asks for one rather than keep another
  session's changes. A scope button says `aria-pressed`.
- **The focus.** A scope press draws the list again, and the focus goes
  back to the button drawn at its place (*A repaint keeps the focus*). A
  row keeps the focus when it opens its changes. A popup or card opened
  from a row or cell takes the focus and gives it back to it on Escape or
  ✕ (*A dialog takes the focus and gives it back*, which a non-focusable
  opener defeated). A live session's redraw gives it back to the same cell
  of the symbol table, found by its symbol; a flow cell whose steps a new
  event changed reads otherwise, and keeps the focus where it fell.

**Not covered:** a revealed original in the story (`.dv-orig`) has the
rule too, but no caller draws one today. The evidence graph's `<svg>`
was `role="img"`, whose children ARIA calls presentational; it is a
`group` since the next subsection. The
legacy rail rows an older server's sessions draw (`dvNavHtml`) stay
`<div>`s. Presentation only: no route, gate or server text changed, and no
value is shown that was not shown before.

Tests: `app-js-press-keys.test.ts` (jsdom; app.js with dialog-focus.js):
the commit rows, the scope buttons, a session read anew, the ring's CSS,
the file rows and their popup, the symbol table's three cells signed in
and out and an untabled row's two, a live redraw, a graph node, and the
guards (a modifier, a composition, a key already taken, a link that says

**The Files strip is a tab strip, the evidence graph a group
(2026-10-12).** On the same kind of real session, a headless Chromium
found two structures that said one thing and did another:

| What | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Files › *Commits · Both views* (`.git-tabs`) | a `tablist` with no name; both tabs Tab stops; ←/→ did nothing; no tab named its panel; the panels a bare `generic` | named "Files"; the session strip's tabs pattern (tabs.js, §4.33) |
| The symbol card's evidence graph (`svg.lineage-svg`) | `role="img"` holding focusable `role="button"` nodes | `role="group"`, named "symbol lineage graph" as before |
| A graph node (`.lin-node`) | named by its `<title>`: "action · evidence: event … — click to open", never the words drawn on it | the `<title>` starts with the node's whole label and its badges |

- **The strip.** app.js `setGitTab` paints the strip with `paintTabs`
  and `wireGitTabs` wires it with `wireTabs`, as the session strip is: the
  selected tab is the one Tab stop (a roving tabindex, so Tab goes from
  Commits to the panel's first control); ← / → (and ↑ / ↓) move to the
  other tab, show its panel and take the focus with them, wrapping;
  Home / End go to the first / last; a click selects as before. Each tab
  carries `data-tab` and its panel's `aria-controls`; each panel is a
  `tabpanel` named by its tab (`aria-labelledby`). Both views still reads
  its trees when it shows, by a key as by a click; a session read anew
  keeps the tab chosen.
- **The graph.** A screen reader's browse mode reads an `img` as one
  picture, so its nodes, which Enter presses (the previous subsection),
  were reachable only by Tab, and only because Chromium exposes an `img`'s
  focusable children anyway. As a `group` it also exposes the lane names,
  the trust wall and each edge by its `<title>` ("blocked at the trust
  wall"), which the `img` hid.
- **A node's name.** A node is named by its `<title>`, which the hover
  shows too. It now reads the words drawn on the node first (its whole
  label, which the node cuts at 26 characters, then its badges: "🔒
  strict", the content kind, "birth unrecorded"), then what only the hover
  said (the kind, the tool, the origin, the verdict, the evidence line):
  "$MDU:Read[5c2d] · 🔒 strict · symbol · tool Read · origin /ws/.env ·
  evidence: event … — click to open". The label is the view model's
  AgentView text, which the page already holds and draws, so no name
  carries anything the page did not show.

Presentation only: no route, gate or server text changed.
