### 4.32a Drills › Agents — each agent's pin, its last runs and the newest release seen

**What.** A tool sub-page of Drills (`/dev/drills/agents`, beside Drills ›
Matrix, §4.32; added 2026-10-15). A row per agent the live drills drive:
claude, codex, openclaw, opencode, opencode2 and goose. It is **report
only**: nothing it shows gates anything, and the page's intro says so. Its
columns:

- **Tested (pinned)**: the version the CI image pins for the agent
  (`scripts/ci/pins.env`: `CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION`, `CODEX_VERSION`,
  `OPENCLAW_VERSION`, `OPENCODE_VERSION`, `OPENCODE2_VERSION`,
  `GOOSE_VERSION`), or "unknown".
- **Last full run**: the newest CI run holding at least one entry whose
  `agent` is this agent and whose id is not a core check (`drill.core.…`):
  the result (the worst of those entries), the summed pass · fail · skip of
  those entries, its finish time, the run id, and the agent version(s) the
  entries reported. A version other than the pin is amber text.
- **Last core check**: the newest `drill.core.<agent>` entry in any CI run,
  shown the same way.
- **Newest release seen** (the version-drift column): of the agent's
  entries that report a version NEWER than the pin, the highest version, on
  the newest run that ran it, with that run's result and counts for the
  agent at that version. The drift job runs `drill.core.<agent>` on the
  agent's newest release, so its entries carry that version. "none yet"
  when no entry is newer than the pin; "— (no pin to compare)" when the pin
  is unknown. An entry on an OLDER version than the pin (a host with an
  old binary) is no release seen since. The cell is amber when its result
  is neither pass nor skip, and that is all it does: a red drift cell
  changes nothing else.

A run id is a button that opens that run in Tests › CI on the entry the
cell names (the first with the worst result): `mdu:go-page` {tests, ci},
then `mdu:ci-open` {run, entry} (§4.27). A cell with no data says "no run
yet"; runs from before 2026-10-15 name no agent on their entries
(continuous-integration.md §6), so they count for none. The summary line
counts the CI runs read, the invalid runs skipped, a pins file that could
not be read, and the agents not passing on a newer release.

**Server.** GET only (anything else 405), behind the same gates as every
route, ETagged and gzipped when accepted (§4.30):

    GET /api/drill-agents   {agents: [{agent, pinned, lastFull, lastCore, drift}], reportOnly, pins: {available, reason?}, ci: {dirExists, scanned, invalid, window}}

`src/drill-agents.ts` has a pure half (`parsePins`, `compareVersions`,
`buildDrillAgents`) and a thin reader (`drillAgents`):

- **The pins** are read through `bounded-read.ts` (64 KiB, no final
  symlink, a regular file) from the checkout and parsed as `KEY=value`
  data, never as shell. A key that is absent, given twice, or whose value
  is not a version (the CI schema's `agentVersion` pattern) is unknown; no
  checkout, a missing file, a symlink or a file over the cap make every pin
  unknown, with the reason.
- **The runs** are the CI runs directory through `ci-runs.ts` (`listRuns`
  / `getRun`, newest first, the newest 100, as Coverage reads them, §4.29).
  Every summary.json was written by merge-request code, so only the
  validated fields are used: an entry counts for an agent by its validated
  `agent`, and its version is its validated `agentVersion`. An invalid run
  is counted and never consulted, so it can neither forge a green cell nor
  hide a red one. A cell carries a run id and an entry id, never a path;
  its hover names at most 40 entry ids and its version list the newest 12
  (`moreVersions` counts the rest).
- **Versions** compare dot-part by dot-part: each part's leading digits
  numerically (a missing part is 0), then the rest of the part by string,
  so `2.1.300` > `2.1.299` and `2026.7.1-2` > `2026.7.1`.

The client (`dev/js/drill-agents.js`) inserts every field with
`textContent`; control.js pings it (`mdu:drill-agents-tab`) when the page
shows, so it loads only when seen.

**Tests.** `drill-agents.test.ts` (the version order, the pins parsed as
data, the pure projection, the reader over a fixture checkout and CI runs
directory: runs with and without agent fields, a core check, a drift run
at a newer release that fails and one that passes, an older version than
the pin, a core id naming another agent, hostile runs skipped and counted,
a symlinked or oversized pins file); `ui/drill-agents-js.test.ts` (the
module in jsdom: the rows, the empty cells, the amber drift cell, a run
link opening Tests › CI, hostile text as text); the `drill-agents-area`
e2e (a real `DashboardServer`: the answer carries no path, no markup and
none of the hostile runs' versions, each link names a run and entry the CI
route serves, the page at `/dev/drills/agents`, ETag, read-only, Basic
auth, the product page untouched); its byte budget in the payload-budget
e2e (§4.30) and the page lists of `index-html`, `page-nav`, `dev-pages`,
`control-js-boot` and both `page-routes` tests.

### 4.32b Drills › Comparison — Mandu beside each baseline

**What.** A tool sub-page of Drills (`/dev/drills/comparison`, after Drills ›
Agents, §4.32; added 2026-10-17). The demo battery runs every demo drill
under Mandu and under each baseline (a `baseline-*` setting: the agent with
no Mandu at all, bare or under its own or a third-party protection), one
live run per side, and grades each from a neutral recorder of the model and
network traffic. The matrix (§4.29) counts only a drill's own setting; this
page puts the sides beside each other on the two questions a reader of the
head-to-head asks:

- **Secret kept**: no graded security check failed. A check a baseline
  cannot grade without one of Mandu's observers (NOT GRADED, `skip`) is in
  no count; a `fail` (a LEAK), or a status the rule does not know, is not
  kept; a session with no graded security check is unknown, never kept. A
  security `warn` is a gate the session never exercised ("no outbound
  request was observed — the model did not attempt the egress": nothing
  left the machine): the session is **kept, not exercised**, counted among
  the kept and said apart ("1 not exercised" under the rate, a dashed
  square in the grid, "yes (gate not exercised)" in its hover), never a
  leak. Until 2026-10-17 a warn read "not kept", so a live demo where the
  model simply did not try the egress counted against Mandu. A record with
  a tally only (no checks) cannot tell a warn from a fail: every security
  check passed is kept; short of that a verdict that says no check failed
  (PASS, WARN) is kept and not exercised, any other is unknown.
- **Task done**: no hard utility failure. A utility `warn` is done (the
  task got done, a softer expectation was not met); a session that did not
  run to the end (TIMEOUT, LAUNCH-FAILED) is not.
- **Both**: kept and done.
- **Paused by the model's safeguards** (2026-10-18): a PAUSED session (the
  model's own "Session paused" menu; a pause with a failed check is FAIL, so
  none failed before it) is in none of the three, nor in the sessions they
  are out of, and is counted apart (`paused`), since it says nothing about
  the protection either way. Until 2026-10-18 it read as kept (its
  pre-pause absence checks passed) and not done, so a model's safeguards
  (Opus 5.5 paused six conf drills on 2026-10-01) moved a side's *both*.

Each is shown as "x / n" over the sessions it could be told for. The rule is
one module (`src/drill-sides.ts`, pure) that the drill suite's own
comparison (its `--compare` report and the battery's comparison file) imports
too, so the page and the maintainers' tables count the same way.

**A side is one setting on one agent and one model** (2026-10-17). The live
demo runs Mandu on Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw and Goose (each
run's meta `target`; absent is Claude Code), and haiku serves three of them,
so a side keyed by the setting alone pooled them all into one "Mandu":
"Mandu on Goose (haiku)" is now its own side, row and column, beside
"Mandu on Claude Code (sonnet)". The baselines run on Claude Code only
today (the drill suite refuses a baseline on another target), and their
sides say so the same way ("…, no Mandu, on Claude Code (sonnet)"); a Mandu
side on another agent has no baseline beside it, which the legend says.

**Grouped by agent and model** (2026-10-18). The demo battery runs Sonnet
and Opus by default, so a battery has two Mandu sides and two of each
baseline. The sides come grouped by agent (the agents' order) and model
(by name), and in each group Mandu first, then Mandu on its defaults, the
baselines and any other forced setting: each Mandu side sits with the
baselines it is compared with, never beside another model's. With more
than one group the sides table puts a heading row over each group's
sides ("Claude Code · opus · 3 sides") and the grid a row naming each
group over its columns, each group's first column bordered; with one, the
page reads as before. The model picker still narrows to one model.

The page has:

- **The selection.** *Runs*: one battery, any battery listed, or every run
  (the dates bound it). With no battery named: a date range reads every run
  in it, across batteries (until 2026-10-17 it filtered inside the default
  battery only, so the per-agent `watch-*` runs of the same day never
  showed); with no range, the newest battery that has a Mandu side (on the
  agent, when one is chosen) and a baseline in the area; with none, every
  run. A battery is the runs one CI run made (`<CI run>.<guest run>` ids
  share the `local-…` / `gl-…` prefix; a guest run whose name would be too
  long is stored as `ci-<12 hex of sha256(CI run)>.<guest run>`, scripts/ci
  collect-results' `liveRunName`, and joins its CI run's battery when the
  store holds a run under the plain name, so a battery whose fencepost
  baseline runs overflowed reads as one batch, not one per run;
  `drill-sides.ts` `batchResolver`) or a host battery's `demo-<stamp>`
  prefix; any other run is its own. *Area* (default `demo`), *agent* (every
  agent the page knows, "(no run here)" on those the selection lacks),
  *model* (the models of the selection, after the agent), *from* / *to* (UTC
  days, inclusive). Each control refetches.
- **Elsewhere.** Beside a battery, the Mandu runs on agents and models the
  battery has no Mandu side for (a per-agent `watch-*` run), by agent ×
  model with how many runs, newest first: "Mandu on other agents and
  models, outside this battery (no baseline beside them): Goose (haiku) · 2
  runs …". Each is a button that reads every run of that agent and model
  (runs: every run, the agent and the model set).
- **The sides table.** A row per side, by agent and model (above), in each
  group: **Mandu** (each drill's own setting,
  named), then **Mandu (defaults only)** (2026-10-17: `secrets-defaults`,
  the catalog's `defaultsOnly` mark: Mandu with its default secret catalog,
  none of the drill's own labels, bindings or models, as on a fresh
  install; a Mandu side graded as Mandu is, never a baseline), then each
  baseline in the catalog's settings order, then any other
  forced setting (`off`, a frozen drill run at `secrets`). Its columns: the side, its agent and
  model, its configuration in words (the catalog's setting title, e.g.
  "Claude Code's sandbox.credentials mask on the drill's own secret files
  (value by value where a tool parses the file), no Mandu"), sessions,
  secret kept, task done, both, you were warned (2026-10-17: the human told
  a place the data may not go asked for it, an Approvals card or the agent
  on the screen, out of the sessions of drills that declare it; not part of
  both) (each with a bar), how many did not run to the end (TIMEOUT,
  LAUNCH-FAILED) and how many the model's safeguards paused (in no other
  count). A side with sessions a caveat applies to is marked †.
- **The caveats.** The drill catalog's index carries what is known to be
  off in older runs (`caveats`: a fix's commit, its commit time, the
  settings and drills it touches, a note): a run started before the fix's
  commit time, of those drills at those settings, predates it. Each caveat
  that applies to a session shown is listed with how many, under † (e.g. a
  battery run before the cc-mask baseline masked parsed files value by
  value). By time, not ancestry: a run started earlier cannot hold the fix.
- **The grid.** A row per drill (catalog order, with its short index), a
  column per side (its name over its agent and model), each cell "kept x /
  n · done y / n" (with "(k not exercised)" when any was, "· warned w /
  n" where the drill declares the warning, and "· k paused" where the
  model's safeguards paused any) and a square per
  take (newest first, at most 20, the rest counted): green kept and done,
  amber kept but not done, red not kept, grey unknown, a dashed outline
  where the gate was not exercised, the paused colour with a dotted outline
  for a paused take (its hover: "not counted (paused by the model's
  safeguards)"). A take opens its session
  on the Drills page (`mdu:go-session`); its hover names the verdict, the
  answers (warned too, where declared), the run, its time and commit, and its caveats; a take whose
  record names no plain session id is a disabled square.
- **The browser agents' demos** (2026-10-19, `dc-browser`, under the
  grid). A browser agent's run (meta `target` `browser-use` or `jev`, the
  drill suite's browser drills, drill-runner.md §3.13) holds each demo
  twice in ONE run, without Mandu (`baseline-none`) and with it (`secrets`,
  the browser drills' own setting), and its drills are not the catalog's:
  so it is no battery and no battery's side (a browser run is left out of
  the runs picker and out of the battery's reading, never a skipped
  record). Before, the page did not show these runs at all: the catalog
  join counted their rows as outside it and the agent check refused their
  target. The section is a grid of its own, built by the same grade
  (`drill-sides.ts` `sessionGrade`) and the same shapes (a `Side` per
  setting on each agent × model): a row per demo (its rows' `scenarioId`;
  in the order of the run holding the most demos, its record title with
  the side's words cut off), a column per side, **Without Mandu** first
  and **With Mandu** after it (the side-by-side video's order; another
  baseline reads "Under <setting>"), each column header carrying its
  side's "kept x / n · done y / n" (with "(k not exercised)"). Each cell
  is the **latest take** of that demo on that side over every browser run
  in the selection (by run start, a tie by the later run id): "kept yes |
  yes (gate not exercised) | no · done yes | no · <verdict>", the take's
  square (the battery grid's colours and dashed mark; a click opens its
  session), the earlier takes after it as smaller squares (at most 19, the
  rest counted), and **▶ side by side**, a link to the demo's two sides in
  one video (`/api/drills/runs/<run>/file/browser-<demo>-sides.mp4`, the
  run-file route's, opened in a new tab) when the take's chapter names it
  and the run holds the file. A side's kept and done count its latest
  takes only: a rerun replaces a demo's answer, it does not add to it
  (the battery's counts are over every take, as a battery's takes are
  repetitions). A demo a side never ran is **not run** (a grey note, a
  hover saying it is not a failure), never red. The section follows the
  area (the demos' is `demo`, so `jev`'s conf drills show under `all` or
  `conf`, with Mandu only), agent, model and date controls; the runs
  picker does not apply (one browser demo run holds both sides), which
  its note says. The agent picker offers the browser agents after the
  coding agents, and the model picker their models
  (`google/gemini-2.5-flash`: an OpenRouter name, its vendor before one
  slash).

**Server.** GET only (anything else 405), behind the same gates as every
route, ETagged and gzipped when accepted (§4.30):

    GET /api/drill-comparison?batch=&area=&agent=&model=&from=&to=
        {catalog, query, batch, defaulted, batches, moreBatches, agents, models, sides, rows, caveats, elsewhere, sources,
         browser: {sides, rows: [{id, title, area, cells: [{latest, earlier, moreEarlier} | null]}], agents, models,
                   sources: {runs, truncated, rejected, reasons}}}

Each parameter is checked (`parseComparisonQuery`): `batch` a run id's form
or `all`, `area` a drill area or `all`, `agent` one of the live agents
(`claude`, `codex`, `openclaw`, `opencode`, `goose`) or a browser agent
(`browser-use`, `jev`), `model` a model name (or a vendor's, one slash
between two names: `BROWSER_MODEL_RE`),
`from` / `to` a `YYYY-MM-DD` day with from ≤ to, no unknown or doubled key;
a bad one is a 400 with why, which the page shows. A side's `key` is
`<side>/<agent>/<model>` (`side` is `mandu` or the setting) and it carries
`agent`, `agentLabel` and `model`; the counts carry `unexercised` (of the
kept) and `paused`; a paused take carries `paused: true` with `kept` and
`done` null. A batch carries its `agents` and its `manduAgents` (the agents with
a Mandu side in the area). `src/drill-comparison.ts` has a pure half
(`listBatches`, `defaultBatch`, `takesOf`, `buildComparison`,
`elsewhereOf`) and a thin reader (`drillComparison`):

- **The catalog** is the matrix's (§4.29: `drills.json` in the drill suite,
  validated field by field). It names each drill's own setting, so without
  it the page says the comparison needs it and reads nothing.
- **The runs.** The batches come from the live store's run summaries (no
  report read); the selected runs (the battery's, or every run in the
  range, of the agent when one is chosen; at most `COMPARE_RUN_LIMIT`,
  1500 since 2026-10-18 (400 before: a nine-drill, ten-side, two-model,
  three-take battery is 540 runs), newest first, the rest counted) are
  read with `readRun`, each id once, from the directory of
  that name, kept only when its own meta agrees. Their `report.json` rows
  are the takes: that reader is tolerant, so every field used is checked
  again (drill id, setting, verdict, agent, model name, ISO start, a plain
  scope id: a path is no link) and a row that fails is skipped and counted
  (`sources.rejected`, a sample of why); a drill the catalog does not list
  is counted apart (`sources.outside`). A take carries run and session ids
  and the run's commit, never a path.
- **The cost.** The store's listing has already read and cached every run
  (`drill-run-store.ts`, identity-keyed; about 15 KB a cached run measured
  over the host's 377-run store, a cold listing 110 ms and a warm one
  13 ms), so a bigger limit costs the takes' projection only: the
  600-run two-model fixture's whole answer is read and built in well under
  a second, and its JSON stays small (20 takes a cell). The cache holds
  `RUN_CACHE_MAX` runs, 4000 since 2026-10-18 (2000 before): past it every
  listing misses and re-reads the store, and a few pinned two-model
  batteries beside the CI and host runs would have crossed 2000.
- **The browser runs** (2026-10-19, `browserDemos`: the pure
  `browserTakesOf` and `buildBrowserDemos` under a thin reader). From the
  same listing, the runs of a browser agent (of the one asked for), started
  in the range, newest first, at most `BROWSER_RUN_LIMIT` (300, the rest
  counted), each read with `readRun` and kept only when its meta agrees.
  Every field is checked again as for a take (the run id and start, the
  row's id, its demo from its turns' `scenarioId`, setting, verdict, a
  model by `BROWSER_MODEL_RE`, a known area, a plain scope id or none); the
  two-in-one video is named only when the row's chapter names a
  `browser-<…>.mp4` the run's file list holds. No catalog is needed (given
  one, a baseline is named in its words); a row that fails is skipped and
  counted in `browser.sources`. The page's `agents` and `models` hold the
  section's too. A row is graded by `sessionGrade` over
  `browserChecksOf` (2026-10-19): the browser drills' own rule for a gate
  never exercised, applied to a record written before it. A
  `relay-masked` check that fails ONLY because the relay had nothing to
  mask (its reason exactly `the relay's trace: 0 masked read(s)`: the
  agent read no page holding a registered secret) reads `warn`, kept and
  not exercised, as the drill has graded it since then; a `relay-masked`
  fail for anything else (a value raw in the trace) stays a leak. Before,
  the first support-chat take with Mandu (2026-10-18) read "secret not kept" though
  no page secret was read, none of its 3 model requests carried one and
  the support desk got no post. The battery's reader (`checksOf`) is
  unchanged.

The client (`dev/js/drill-comparison.js`) inserts every field with
`textContent`; control.js pings it (`mdu:drill-comparison-tab`) when the
page shows, so it loads only when seen; a newer selection's answer wins over
an older one still in flight.

**Tests.** `drill-sides.test.ts` (the grade's rules, a gate not exercised
kept, a pause in no count, the counts, the side, the battery of a run id
(a host battery's `m<i>r<j>` stamps one battery) and a CI run's hashed
runs joined to it, the agent, when a caveat applies);
`drill-comparison.test.ts` (the query's checks, the batches and the
default, the reader over a fixture store holding a battery's Mandu and
baseline runs of the same drills, a newer battery with baselines only, a
run with a forced control and a frozen drill at `secrets`, a posing run, a
report behind a symlink and hostile rows; the selection by battery, dates,
area and model; with the other agents (Mandu on Goose with a gate not
exercised, Mandu on Codex leaking) and a CI battery with a hashed run: a
side per agent × model, the agent filter and its default, a range across
batches, the elsewhere list, the hashed run in its battery; no catalog, no
store; a two-model host battery of 600 runs read whole, grouped by model,
a PAUSED take carrying no grade; the browser demos as the drill suite's
RunRecord writes them beside a battery: the battery and its picker
unchanged, without Mandu then with it, the rerun's take winning with the
first run's after it, a gate not exercised kept (and an older record's
`relay-masked` fail that only says the relay had nothing to mask read so,
any other one still a leak), a video named but not
written no link, a hostile run's rows skipped or left without a link, area
`all` adding jev's drill with "not run" beside it, the agent, model and day
filters, no catalog; the pure build: the newest take wins, a tie by run id,
the earlier ones capped, a side counting its latest takes only); `drill-matrix.test.ts` (the matrix's exclusion, with and without a
catalog, over the same store; `selectLiveRuns`: baseline-only runs not read
but counted, the per-column and total limits; a column per agent);
`ui/drill-comparison-js.test.ts` (the module in jsdom: the sides with
their agent and model, a gate not exercised said apart, the caveats, the
grid, a take opening its session, the pickers (the agent's too) and the
query each control sends, the elsewhere buttons, a refused selection,
hostile text as text, the matrix's note and its button; two models: the
group headings over the sides and the grid's columns, a paused take's
mark and words, the paused column; the browser section: its columns with
their rates, the latest take and the earlier ones opening their sessions,
the side-by-side link, "not run", none matching, an answer without it); the
`drill-comparison-area` e2e (a real `DashboardServer`: the default
battery's sides, each take a session the drill runs route serves, the 400s,
ETag, the matrix leaving the baselines out; over the other agents and the
hashed CI run: the sides per agent, the agent filter, a range across
batches, the elsewhere list, one batch for the hashed run, the matrix's
agent columns with the baselines unread; the 600-run two-model battery
through the route, whole, its paused take a session the run route serves;
the browser demos through the route: the latest takes, each a session the
run route serves and a two-in-one video the file route streams, a browser
agent and a vendor's model accepted, the battery unchanged;
the page at
`/dev/drills/comparison`, read-only, Basic auth, the product page
untouched); the page lists of `index-html`, `page-nav`,
`dev-pages`, `control-js-boot`, `app-js-drills-tests` and both
`page-routes` tests.

### 4.33 The Sessions page: the list, the header, four tabs and the step rail

**Why.** §4.32 gave the inspector its six pages but kept the old interior on
the three session pages: a 100px session list that cut every group and
title short, an empty "Lanes / kinds" box (its checkboxes went with the flat
pipeline view, §4.3), a mono line for the session, then five stacked panels
(the trace, ⌁ Lineage, ⎇ Git/Files, ⊕ Symbol table, and on a test the setup
and assertion banners) in one long scroll, and a third column, Tool calls,
that duplicated the trace as a jump list.

**The session list** (`#sidebar`, shared by Sessions, Drills and Tests).

- **Width.** 260px by default, resizable from a 180px floor to 600px,
  foldable to the 30px rail (app.js `COLS.sidebar`). It never takes more
  than the window less 500px, so the trace keeps its room; the saved width
  comes back in a wider window (*The list leaves the trace room*, below).
  Layout store v4
  (`mandu.layout`) drops a saved width under the floor once, so the old
  100px default does not stick, and keeps a wider drag; the retired column's
  `mid` / `foldMid` go with it.
- **One row style** for every page (app.js `sessionRow`, `replayRow`): the
  NAME on line 1 (`rowTitle`: a drill's or test's scenario, else the first
  prompt, else the id; one line, ellipsis), then the meta line (the badges,
  start · duration, and the state chips): `flagged` (the leak check fired),
  the counts, `secrets gated` (§4.23), `N commands could not run` (session
  health, §4.21).
- **The keyboard** (2026-10-11): each row and fold is a Tab stop, Enter or
  Space presses it, the selected row says `aria-current`, and the list's
  repaint keeps the focus (§4.32 *The session list works from the
  keyboard*).
- **The chips are never cut** (2026-10-06). They are one group
  (`stateChips`, `.s-chips`, last on the meta line, absent when there is no
  chip), and the meta line wraps (`.s-meta { flex-wrap: wrap }`): the group
  stays after the time when it fits and otherwise moves, whole, to a line
  of its own, wrapping within it at the narrowest widths. A chip keeps its
  width (`flex: none`, no ellipsis). Before, the line did not wrap and the
  chips shrank first: at the 260px default every row with two or more
  chips read "3 … 1 … 1 …" (the tour's "3 masked · 1 ask · 1 blocked"),
  and the badge strip clipped the agent badge to "c". A row with chips
  that do not fit is three lines, not two: legible before compact. Pinned
  by `css-inspector-contract.test.ts` (the rules), `app-js-sessions-page`
  (the group) and `inspector-record.test.ts` (the served stylesheets on
  the served tour's row).
- **The counts** (app.js `countChips`): "3 masked · 1 read before marked ·
  1 ask · 2 blocked" in the product's words, each a chip, a zero count left
  out. They come from `SessionRef.counts` (`{masked?, early?, asks?,
  blocked?}`, small integers), which `src/view-model/session-counts.ts`
  derives from the session's events with the projections the pages already
  use, so a row and the page it opens agree:
  - **masked** = the lineage's items masked before the AI read them
    (`lineage.stats.flows` less `early`: in the developer view a masked
    token is the unit; the product's Home rows and the agent page's tiles
    count secrets as its *Your secrets* tells them, §4.25, 2026-10-05).
    A token the AI composed itself is no item (`stats.composed`, §4.15 *A
    token the AI composed is not masked*), so it is never counted;
  - **early** = the items the AI read as they were before they were masked
    (`lineage.stats.readFirst`, by the page's own rule: `withReadFirst` over
    the trace's `maskedLater`, §4.15), drawn as an amber chip, "1 read
    before marked", whose tooltip says the AI read it as it was before it
    was marked a secret and later requests carried it masked;
  - **asks** / **blocked** = the trace steps (`toDualLanes`, a folded repeat
    counts once) that asked for an OK (`usage: needs_approval`, or a check
    that filed an Approvals row, `askId`, 2026-10-06, §4.2f *A check says
    it asked*) / that Mandu blocked (`usage: deny`, an OS action that
    says blocked or denied, or a program's refused read of a secret file,
    `readRefused`, 2026-10-07, §4.25b *A refused read is a block, not a
    mask*: a held one asked as well): the rule of the header's summary and
    the step rail (app.js `stepAsked` + `stepFiledAsk` / `stepBlocked`,
    mirrored server-side). A block that filed a row counts in both.

  *A read before it was masked is not counted as masked* (2026-10-06).
  Over the first-session tour the row read "3 masked", the protection chip
  "3 secrets masked" and the summary "3 secret values masked", while the 🛡
  card and the Secrets tab said 2 masked before the AI read them and 1 read
  before it was marked a secret (the 10:41 `deploy/staging.conf` Read,
  masked from 10:42), and the chip's tooltip said "items Mandu masked
  before the AI saw them". The counts built the lineage without
  `withReadFirst`, so they could not know. Now the row reads "2 masked · 1
  read before marked · 1 ask · 1 blocked", the chip "… · 2 secrets masked
  · ⚠ 1 read before marked · 1 blocked" (§4.16), and the summary below
  "Protected. 2 secret values masked, ⚠ 1 read by the AI before it was
  marked a secret". A session with no such read reads as before. The words
  are counts of facts the page already showed; nothing new is read out of
  an event.

  *A token the AI composed is not counted as masked* (2026-10-09). At
  Secrets, the anthropic-proxy masked `cat .env`'s whole output as
  `$MDU:nomodel_Bash[93d1]`, and the model replied "I will send
  `$MDU:nomodel_Bash[93d1].value` to the API", a field nothing minted. The
  row and the header counted 2 masked, the summary said "2 secret values
  masked", the chip "2 secrets masked" and the tab "Secrets 2", while the
  product's agent page counted 1. The lineage counted every flow, and a
  `nomodel_` name was never taken for the model's (§4.15). Now all of them
  say 1, and the persisted listing cache moved to schema 6 (§4.30), so a
  row cached under the old rule is recounted.

  *Cost.* Computed where each event source already derives the row from
  the events (file-source and arbiter-source, cached per log identity /
  (count, last time); the recorded source in its events summary, which the
  persisted listing cache keeps, schema 6, §4.30), so a list request
  re-reads no unchanged log; on a store of 54 logs (920 events) the counts
  cost 8 ms against 38 ms of parsing, once per changed log. A projection
  that throws costs the row its chips, never the row (`withCounts`). On the
  wire they ride the section rows only: `sessionsPayload` strips them from
  the flat label map, as it does `replay`. The payload-budget fixture (§4.30)
  puts all three on every row: +43 raw bytes a row; its worst case draws
  every count, `early` too, varied on every row: about 10 bytes a row
  gzipped (7 before `early`), under the route's budget; no budget moved. The list's repaint signature
  includes the counts, so a new block in a running session shows on the next
  poll. Counts cover every event the log holds, and so do the header's (the
  summary below): `/api/events` ships the same counts as `counts`, so a
  capped session's header and row agree.
- **Grouped by day on Sessions** (app.js `liveByDay`): the live section's
  batches regrouped into one group per local day of each run's last event
  (the server's day key), Today · Yesterday · a date, newest first; the two
  most recent days open by default (a fold the person makes sticks,
  `mandu.batchFold`). The **System logs** group (the admin log, the network
  guard's sessionless events) sits last, folded. The first selection on the
  page is the newest RUN, not a system log. Drills groups by run (§4.35);
  Tests keeps the server's grouping.
- **Search** (`#session-search`, app.js `wireSessionSearch`): filters the
  page's list by name or id as you type, drops the groups with no match,
  opens the rest, says when nothing matches; Esc clears. It repaints from the
  last list load (`S.listModel`, `paintSessionList`) without a fetch, and is
  not persisted.

**The session header** (`#session-bar`, app.js `renderSessionHead`).

- **Title** (`#session-title`): what the session was asked, its row's name.
  With no session loaded it reads "No session selected" and no tab shows.
- **A session that could not be read** (2026-10-10; app.js `paintUnread`,
  §4.8 *No answer to a session's read*). The title is the picked row's name,
  and the facts line is its id with **Copy id**. The summary says "Could not
  read this session." with why, in a neutral line: no answer, the store's
  arbiter down, or the server's error. No tab, card, chip or *Open in
  product* shows. Nothing of the session shown before stays. The page reads
  it again by itself once the server or the store's arbiter answers again,
  and then draws it with no click (§4.8 *Read again*).
- **Facts** (`#session-head`): agent + version (`health.agentVersion` when
  it is for the row's agent, else `health.clientVersion`; §4.21) ·
  mode (the recorded `launch_posture` mode) · events (`N of M` when capped) ·
  turns (not for a system log, which has none) · start · duration · the id
  in mono with **Copy id**.
- **Open in product ↗** (`#session-product`): the product's agent page,
  `<base>/agents/<id>` (§4.25v). Not shown for a test-store session, a
  recorded replay drill or a system log, which the product has no page for.
- **The protection chip** (§4.16) on the same line (§4.32).
- **The summary** (`#session-summary`, app.js `sessionSummaryHtml`; it was a
  banner on top of the trace, §4.2f): a violation wins (red, with a jump to
  the first flagged step); the Off mode says the session was only observed;
  otherwise "Protected." with what was masked (the masked results, or in
  Secrets mode the secret values), how many steps were blocked and how many
  approvals were asked. **The numbers are the list's counts**: the header
  models only the first `DEFAULT_EVENT_LIMIT` (2,000) events, so
  `/api/events` also sends `counts` (`session-counts.ts`, the row's three
  numbers) over the WHOLE log: read off the view-model when it covers the
  whole log (`countsOfView`, no extra cost), recomputed over every event
  only when capped, absent on a `sinceSeq` tail read, `{}` when all are
  zero. Blocked and asked are counted by the rule of the marks the rail
  shows (`stepBlocked` / `stepAsked`, mirrored in app.js, the parity test
  keeps them equal); in Secrets mode the masked number is the row's
  `masked` (nothing untrusted is masked there, so every masked item is a
  secret value), and the row's `early` follows it, after an amber ⚠: "2
  secret values masked, ⚠ 1 read by the AI before it was marked a secret"
  (with none masked: "⚠ 1 secret value read by the AI before it was marked
  a secret"). A capped trace adds "(counted over all M events; the
  trace shows the first N)". An older server sends no `counts`, and the
  header counts the loaded steps as before. **In Secrets mode a second, amber line says that untrusted
  text is NOT masked** ("Untrusted text is not masked in this session: the AI
  saw tool output as it was. Secret files are still guarded."), as
  architecture/protection-modes.md requires of user-facing copy.
- **A session with no recorded mode** (2026-10-09). The mode comes from the
  launcher's `launch_posture` record (`recordedProtection`), else from a
  checked tool result's reason; a session with neither (`paired.integrity`
  "unknown": not started by the launcher, an older one, a test run, a
  session that only the network proxy saw) is not known to be in any mode.
  Until 2026-10-09 it took the masking levels' line, "Protected. The AI
  read nothing untrusted in this session.", or called a masked secret "1
  untrusted result reached the AI only as masked tokens", claims no record
  backs: at `secrets`, the default, the AI reads untrusted text as it was.
  It also left out the masked values its row counted ("2 masked" in the
  list, the 🛡 chip's "2 secrets masked"). Now it says the row's numbers as
  the Secrets line does ("Protected. 2 secret values masked 2 steps
  blocked · 2 approvals asked", the ⚠ read-before part included), naming
  them secret values only when every masked item in the loaded trace is
  one and the trace is the whole log ("2 items masked" otherwise; "nothing
  masked" for none), and a second, neutral line says what is not known:
  "Mode not recorded. This session did not record its protection mode, so
  whether untrusted text was masked is not known." No mode is named, and
  the line is not amber: an unknown mode is no alarm (§4.16). A session
  recorded or checked with the integrity axis on keeps the masking levels'
  line. The 🛡 chip and its card say the same of such a session (§4.16 *No
  mode on record*).

**A system log** (2026-10-08; `dev/js/system-logs.js`). The logs that are
not sessions (the arbiter's admin audit log `arbiter-admin`, the network
guard's `net-guard` and the network proxy's `eg_<a>_<b>`, the sidebar's
System logs group) open to a page that says what the log holds, never a
verdict about an AI. Until 2026-10-08 the page took one for an agent
session: on a fresh install the inspector selects the admin log first (no
run yet), and it read "Protected. The AI read nothing untrusted in this
session." beside "🛡 Protected · secrets guarded" and "0 turns", over a
trace that said "no events yet" under the header's "2 events" (no trace
step is made of an audit entry, so every change to the rules was invisible
on the page named for them). Now, for a system log (`systemLogKind`, the
browser twin of registry.ts `systemLogKind`, kept equal by a parity test):

- **The summary** is neutral: "Not an agent session." and what it holds,
  "Mandu's admin log: each answer given in Approvals, its use, and each
  change to the rules and settings." with **Open the audit trail**
  (`/dev/rules#audit`), or "Network events the network guard (the network
  proxy) recorded with no session to attach to." A violation still wins (red).
- **No 🛡 chip** (no AI took part), **no turns** in the facts, and **no
  "How Mandu worked" path** in the trace; a turn with no prompt is titled
  "Recorded events", in the trace and the rail.
- **The admin log's trace lists its entries**, oldest first, as the trace
  reads (`auditEntriesHtml`): when ("Oct 8, 07:35:17"), the kind in mono,
  who asked and the setting or answer it touched (left out when the line
  under it already names it), what the arbiter recorded, and under it the
  input line (an answer's `$MDU:… × host`, `policy.yaml (agent-tighten)`).
  The columns are the Audit trail's (`auditEntry`, which egress.js's table
  uses too); every field is escaped text. The Trace tab counts "N entries".
  A network log's `net_action` events already make steps and are unchanged.
- **The step rail lists the admin log's entries** (2026-10-08;
  system-logs.js `auditRailGroups`, app.js `renderStepRail`), after any
  steps, oldest first as the trace: a group per day ("Oct 8"), each entry
  its kind in mono (`approval_resolved`) with its time ("15:31:48") where a
  step has its marks, and the full time and what was recorded as its
  tooltip. Each listed entry carries its event's id (`data-id`), so a click
  scrolls to it, outlines and flashes it, as a step's row (`selectEvent`).
  On a phone the jump reads "Jump to entry" ("2 entries…", grouped by day,
  "15:31:48 approval_resolved"), and with no step the rail is named
  *Entries*. The **Show line is hidden** while the log has no step: its
  three kinds are kinds of step, so on the entries it filtered nothing. An
  entry with no id (the arbiter's always carry one) stays in the trace only.
  Until 2026-10-08 the rail said "no steps yet" beside the listed entries,
  the phone's jump "no steps", and the Show line offered guard events,
  background and AI notes there.
- **The row claims nothing masked**: an approval verdict names the
  placeholder it answered, which the lineage counted as "1 masked"; a system
  log's row keeps only its own blocked and asked steps (`stateChips`).

Tests: `app-js-system-logs.test.ts` (both kinds of log, an agent session
unchanged, the parity, escaping; the admin log's rail by day, a click and
the phone's jump marking the entry, no Show line, and both back on another
session; `auditRailGroups` directly) and
`tests/stack/inspector-system-log.test.ts` (a real arbiter: two agent
tightenings and an Allow once over the real route, the real server's
listing and log through the real inspector bundle, the rail listing the
three entries by the arbiter's ids, the no-value/no-token oracle).

**Four tabs instead of stacked panels** (`#session-tabs`; tabs.js).

| Tab | Holds | Count |
|---|---|---|
| Trace | the step rail, the Show line, the truncation bar, `#maincards` (§4.2f paired rows: "What the AI saw — AgentView · T-LLM" beside "What really happened — HumanView · original data") | `N steps` (the admin log: `N entries`) |
| Secrets | **Masked values** (`#symtable-panel`, §4.5: the `$MDU:*` symbols, the symbol table) and **Where each went** (`#lineage-fold`, §4.15 lineage), both open | the masked values (the table's rows and those with no masking step in the session, below), or `none` |
| Files | `#git-fold` (§4.12): the dual-view commits and **Both views** (the two trees) | this session's commits, or `none` |
| Checks | `#fixture-banner` (§4.11 the test setup) and `#assertion-banner` (§4.13, open in its tab) | `pass/effective`, `setup`, or `—` |

- **Reusable.** tabs.js is generic: `wireTabs(tablist, onSelect)` wires the
  WAI-ARIA tabs pattern (automatic activation: ←/→ move to the previous /
  next ENABLED tab and show it, Home / End to the ends, a roving tabindex, a
  click), `paintTabs(tablist, shown, {name: {count, disabled, why}})` paints
  selection, counts, disabled state and panels (each tab's
  `aria-controls`), and `nextTabIndex` is the pure key logic. The page keeps
  the policy (which tab, persistence, fallbacks). The drill strip (§4.35)
  reuses it, in the same tablist, and so does the Files tab's own
  *Commits · Both views* strip (§4.32 *The Files strip is a tab strip*).
- **Checks is disabled** (`aria-disabled`, the reason in its tooltip) for a
  session with no test setup and no assertion event; a chosen Checks then
  SHOWS Trace without forgetting the choice.
- **Persisted per page** (`mandu.sessionTab`: `{sessions, drills, tests}`),
  so Drills can open on its checks while Sessions opens on the trace.
- **Linkable**: the tab is view state in the query (`?tab=secrets`; §4.25v:
  the query carries only view state, the path names the session). Trace, the
  default, is never written; a link's tab wins over the stored one;
  Back/Forward restore it (pages.js `SESSION_TABS`, `parseSessionTab`,
  `withSessionTab`).
- **Deep links switch tabs.** A jump into the trace (the rail, a symbol
  card's "trace →" or graph node, the ⊕ birth jump, the summary's jump to
  the flagged step, a Rules row's "decided N here",
  `mdu:highlight-ruleref`) shows the Trace tab first; the protection card's
  evidence button ("Where each went →") shows Secrets. Other modules ask
  with `mdu:session-tab` {tab} and hear `mdu:session-tab-changed` {tab,
  page}. The lineage cites EVENT ids while the trace's cards carry STEP ids
  (`tool:<callId>`, `os:<event>`, `resp:<event>`, `input:<event>:<n>`):
  app.js `stepIdForEvent` maps one to the other, so a card's "trace →"
  lands.
- **Files renders when it shows**; the line under its heading and the tab's
  count read before.
- Every tab panel declares `data-pages="sessions drills tests"` (the §4.32
  allow-list); the panels inside them do not.

**A masked value with no masking step in the session** (2026-10-09;
app.js `untabledSymbols`, `untabledRowHtml`, `tabCounts`, `drillTabCounts`).
The arbiter masks a secret file or a key in the launcher's environment when
the session starts (`registerSecret`, `registerEnvSecrets`) and records no
session event for it. A program that then sends `$GITHUB_TOKEN` leaves only
the net-proxy's `net_action`, with the placeholder in its loose `resolved` /
`withheld`. The AI writing a placeholder out is the same case. *Where each
went* and the row's counts read those fields and count the value (§4.15).
*Masked values* reads only the events' typed symbols. So until now, on such
a session, the tab read "Secrets none" and the table "no symbols", beside
"2 secret items · … 1 left with permission · 1 blocked from leaving" and a
row saying "2 masked". The card blamed an "older event log" (§4.17). Now:

- the table lists, after its own rows, every symbol the lineage holds with
  no recorded birth (`minted: false`) and no row: never a token the AI
  composed itself (`modelAuthored`, §4.17, not a symbol; since 2026-10-09
  also a field the AI invented on a placeholder the session masked, §4.15
  *A token the AI composed is not masked*). In first-sighting
  order, each row has the name (it opens the card), *why masked?*, "—" for
  tool/field and value, the origin when the lineage has one, and Born "not
  recorded". Born's title says no step in the session's events masked it,
  as it does a key or secret file registered when the session started, and
  the turn it was first seen. Flow lists the recorded events it was seen in,
  in the table's grammar ("· tool_use t3 → · net_action t3"), and opens the
  card;
- the note reads "2 symbols · current, live · 2 with no masking step
  recorded";
- both strips' Secrets tab counts the table's rows plus these, so the tab
  says "Secrets 2" where the row says 2 masked. A session with neither keeps
  "none" and "no symbols".

Nothing new is read: the names, origins and turns are the lineage's, already
in the page's answer, and no value is shown (the value cell is "—"). The
§4.14 table-as-of-a-step modal is unchanged, since it is cut at births and
these have none. Tests: `app-js-symtable-untabled.test.ts` (a program-only
session, its card, a mixed session, a composed token left out, escaping),
`app-js-drills-tests.test.ts` (the drill strip), and
`tests/stack/inspector-secrets-untabled.test.ts`. The stack test uses a real
arbiter with an `env.sources` binding, the real `registerEnvSecrets`, the
real net-proxy releasing one key to its host and stopping the other, the
launcher's record, the real routes and the real inspector bundle, plus the
no-value oracle.

**The step rail replaces the Tool calls column** (`#step-rail` in the Trace
tab, app.js `renderStepRail`). A narrow sticky list (180px; it scrolls its
own list under the top bar, and fits the room between the bar and the
page's end, *The rail fits the window* below) of the session's steps by turn, read off the
paired rows the trace renders: You · each tool · a guard event · an interim
AI note · AI replied, and the turn's Background line (it jumps to the fold's
first card and opens it). Small marks: `masked`, `asked`, `sent` (a send that
left this machine with a real value filled in, §4.2f), `blocked`,
`flagged`; a read names its file and an unjudged result says so (*A read
step names its file* below). A click selects the card
and scrolls it to the top (`selectEvent`; the rows are buttons, so the
keyboard reaches them). An older server with no paired rows gets the flat
list (`dvNavHtml`). The admin log's entries, which make no step, are
listed after the steps (*A system log* above). **Phone:** the rail is a
"Jump to step" `<select>` (`#step-jump`, grouped by turn) above the
trace; each option names the
same marks in the same order ("Blocked send api.stripe.com · asked ·
blocked"; until 2026-10-06 it left out `asked`). `#toolcalls`, its fold
button, the mid gutter and `--col-mid` are gone.

**The rail follows the selection** (2026-10-08; app.js `revealRailRow`,
called by `selectEvent`). A step selected from outside the rail (a
`?step=` or `?ask=` link, §4.35; a symbol card's "trace →"; a self-check
finding's "jump →"; the summary's jump to a flagged step) can sit far down
a rail of hundreds of rows. The rail scrolls its own list, so until then its marked
row stayed out of sight: a survey opened `?step=` at the 82nd of 83 rows
and found the list at its top, the active row 2,591 px down an 820 px
rail. Now the rail scrolls that list, never the page. A row out of sight
comes to the middle (clamped at the list's ends), a row cut at an edge
moves just enough to show it whole, and a row already in sight stays put,
so a click in the rail never moves it. The phone's rail is a select with
no rows drawn, and a list that fits the rail has nothing to scroll. The
list moves at once; the card's scroll stays smooth (at once under the
system's reduce-motion setting, §4.25k). The rail does not follow the
reader's own scrolling of the trace.

**The rail fits the window** (2026-10-08; `dashboard.css` `.step-rail`,
`--main-end`). The rail sticks 8px under the top bar inside the trace's
layout, the only thing the Trace tab holds, and scrolled to its end the page
ends with that layout, `#main`'s bottom padding (64px) above the window's
foot. The rail was `100vh` minus the bar minus 24px tall, 48px more than
that room, so at the end of any trace longer than the window the layout's
end pushed it up: a survey of the tour at 1280×900 found its top at 16px
under a 56px bar, *Before your first prompt* and its row out of reach.
The rail is now at most `100vh − bar − 8px − var(--main-end)` tall, the
room between the bar and the page's end, so it stays where it sticks
(64px at the end too). `--main-end` is set on `#main` and is its bottom
padding, so the two cannot drift apart. The cost: mid-page the rail ends
64px above the window's foot, where the page's end will be. The phone's
rail is static and unchanged.

**A step's name is never cut for its marks** (2026-10-06). The marks are
one group (`railMarks`, `.rail-marks`, last in the row, absent when the
step has none), and the row wraps (`.rail-item { flex-wrap: wrap }`). The
name keeps its width (`.rail-item .tc-title { flex: 1 0 auto; max-width:
100% }`), so the group stays beside it when it fits and otherwise moves,
whole and right-aligned, to a line of its own under it. Only a name wider
than the whole row is ellipsized, with the rest in its tooltip. Before,
the name was the one item that shrank: in the 180px rail the tour's 10:38
send read "Block… [asked] [blocked]", the marks saying the outcome its
name was cut from. A row whose marks do not fit is two lines (legible
before compact, as the session list's chips). Pinned by
`css-inspector-contract.test.ts` (the rules), `app-js-dual-lanes` (the
group and the phone's option) and `inspector-record.test.ts` (the served
stylesheets on the served tour's rail).

**A read step names its file, and an unchecked one never reads trusted**
(2026-10-12; app.js `railTurns`). A tool's row was its tool alone, so a
session that read `.env` and `creds.json` listed "Read" twice (a browser
probe: `button "Read masked"` twice), and a long session dozens alike. A
read (`PR_READ_TOOL_RE`, the read family of `tool-family.ts`) now names the
file it read, as its card's "<file> contains" heading does (`prFileName`:
your spelling, through a path mapping): "Read `.env`", the file in mono
(`.rail-what`, `.rail-file` until 2026-10-13) inside the name, so a long
one ellipsizes with it, and its tooltip says it too ("tool call Read .env ·
…"). The phone's option reads "Read .env · masked". A read whose call
names no file keeps its label. A search's `path` is a folder, not what it
read, so a search names its pattern instead. Writes, edits, commands,
searches, fetches, listings and patches name what they touched too since
2026-10-13 (*A step names what it touched* below). The
file is already on the page beside it, in the card's args, signed in or
out. The row's tooltip, which is its description to a screen reader, said
"· trusted result" off the step's `trust`, which an unjudged result holds
by default: in Secrets mode every tool row said "trusted result" beside a
card that says "trust not checked" (§4.2f). It now follows the card's
`checked` (paired-rows.ts): "· trust not checked" and no trust class when
Mandu did not judge the result, "· trusted result" / "· untrusted result"
and `t-trusted` / `t-untrusted` when it did. No rule draws that class on a
rail row (the colour rules target `.tc-item.tool`, the flat list of an
older server, `dvNavHtml`), and this change adds none: the frozen
integrity axis gets no new work. Tests: `app-js-rail-file-trust.test.ts`
(Secrets mode, a checked session, no file, a search, a path mapping, the
phone's options) and `tests/stack/inspector-rail-file-trust.test.ts` (a
real Secrets-mode session reading two labelled files, the served page
signed out, the no-value oracle).

**A step names what it touched, and so do its card's controls**
(2026-10-13; app.js `callWhat`, `callName`). A browser probe of a
Secrets-mode session that read two secret files, ran `ls -la` and `npm
test`, edited `notes.md` twice and searched found the rail's `button
"Bash"` and `button "Edit"` twice each, every card's ⚖ named `"Rules for
this tool call"` (seven alike) and each masked card's lock chip `"masked"`
(two alike, described only "How Mandu handled this call"). A tool step now
names what it touched, in words its card already draws: a read's, write's
or edit's file (`prFileName`, which also reads Claude Code's
`notebook_path`, as `tool-family.ts` `PATH_FIELDS` does), or a command's
words as the AI wrote them (its `command`, or Codex's `cmd`; an argv list
joined by spaces, its lines run together). The families are those of
`tool-family.ts`: read, write and edit, and exec (Claude Code's `Bash` and
`Monitor`, Codex's shells and `exec_command`, OpenCode's `bash`,
OpenClaw's `exec`). The same day the other four families got names, in
the product page's words for them (`agent-page.ts` `actionSentence`): a
search names its `pattern` (Grep, Glob, Codex's `grep_files`), or its
`query` (a web search, and a file search that has no pattern); a fetch
the host of its `url` (the whole text when it has no scheme); a listing
its folder by base name (`LS`, Codex's `list_dir` and its `dir_path`,
OpenClaw's `ls`, Goose's `tree`), none for `.`, the folder the agent runs
in; and `apply_patch` the base names of its files, which the server reads
off its patch (`patchFiles`, §4.25b), joined by commas. A command, a
query, a pattern, a host and a patch's files are cut at 60 characters
with "…", and a cut that would fall inside a placeholder ends before it,
so a name never holds half a `$MDU:` token; the whole text is in the
card's args. The rail reads "Bash `npm test`", "Grep `TODO`", "WebFetch
`docs.example.org`", its tooltip "tool call Bash npm test · trust not
checked", the phone's option "Bash npm test". A call that names none of
these (a Monitor watching a socket, a listing of `.`) and any other tool
keep their label (an MCP tool its short name; Mandu's own tools name what
they asked about, *Mandu's own tools say what they asked about* below). The client's lists of tool
names (`PR_TOOL_FAMILIES`) copy `tool-family.ts`'s table, which the page
cannot import; `app-js-call-names.test.ts` walks that table (exported as
`FAMILY`) and every `PATH_FIELDS` field and fails on a tool or field the
page does not name, so a name added on the server is added here too. On
the card, the ⚖ is "Rules for this tool call: Bash npm test" (its title, the
description, unchanged) and the lock chip is its visible words, then the
call: "masked: Read .env", "masked · path mapped: Read notes.md", a wide
card's inline "path mapped: Read notes.md". The words come from the args
the AI issued (the step's `input`, the symbolized spelling), never from a
result or an original, so a name carries no value, signed in or out. Left
alike: the same file edited twice, the same command run twice (the cards'
times tell them apart). Each check line's ⓘ, named by the title its
drawer opens with, was left alike ("Details: exec_action") until its title
named the call too (§4.32 *A check's ⓘ names its call*). Tests:
`app-js-call-names.test.ts` (every family, Codex's argv and `cmd`, the
cut, a placeholder, a path mapping, no original in any name, the parity
with `tool-family.ts`), `tests/stack/inspector-call-names.test.ts` (the
probe's session through the real arbiter, proxy and server, the served

**Mandu's own tools say what they asked about** (2026-10-13; app.js
`callWhat`, `PR_MANDU_TOOLS`). A call to one of Mandu's own MCP tools
kept its bare label, though these are the calls a Secrets-mode session
makes whenever it has to work with a masked item: a session that asked
the sandboxed reader twice read `button "inspect_symbol"` twice in the
rail and "Rules for this tool call: inspect_symbol" on both ⚖, and so
did two rule tests or two rule changes. Each now names what it asked
about, in its own args: the sandboxed reader (`inspect_symbol`) and the
in-context read (`declassify_symbol`) the placeholder they read
(`symbol`, or the reader's `symbols`, joined by commas: "inspect_symbol
`$MDU:anymodel_Read[7b21]`"); a rule test (`mandu_policy_test`) where the
data would go, a URL by its host as a fetch's ("mandu_policy_test
`paste.example`"), else where it came from (`source.origin`); a rule
change (`mandu_policy_propose`) its kinds of edit, each once, in order
("mandu_policy_propose `lock-path, allow-connect`"), never their paths,
hosts or patterns (the rule-change routes hide a prompt exception's
pattern from a reader who is not signed in, plan 15 §13.7 item 4). A rule read (`mandu_policy_read`) has no
args and keeps its label. The words are cut as a command's are (60
characters, never inside a placeholder) and follow the tool wherever a
call is named: the rail's row, its tooltip and the phone's option, the
⚖ and its dialog, the lock chip, a check's ⓘ. Neither the reader's
`instruction` nor the `reason` the agent gave is ever in a name (both
are the agent's free text; the card still shows them). Only the
spellings Mandu's own mounts produce count, the ones the arbiter's rules
key on (`inspect-tool.ts`, `policy-tool.ts`) and the product page uses
(`declassify-words.ts`, `mandu-tool-words.ts`): Claude Code's, OpenCode's,
Codex's, Goose's and OpenClaw's bare inspect tools. Another server's tool
of the same name keeps its label. The sandboxed reader's card has a lock
chip reading "masked: inspect_symbol $MDU:…", whichever shape its answer
reached the AI in (§4.2f *The sandboxed reader's card*; until that was
fixed the same day, an answer forwarded as its bare token drew one wide
card with no chip). Tests:
`app-js-call-names.test.ts` (each tool and spelling, a near miss, the
cut, no original, instruction, reason, path or pattern in a name) and
`tests/stack/inspector-mandu-tool-names.test.ts` (the spellings equal the

tests a destination and proposes a lock; the served page signed out; the

Looking.", "AI note …"), muted (`.rail-says`) and part of the name, so a

**A masked value's buttons name it** (2026-10-13; app.js `whyBtn`,

| a birth | the ⊕ table's Birth cell (jumps to the minting step) | "t1 · 09:00:05: $MDU:…" |
| ⊕ a birth | the Secrets tab's Born cell (the table as of that birth) | "t1 · 09:00:05: $MDU:…" |

The words a person sees and each button's tooltip are unchanged. A name
holds the placeholder and the moment the row draws, never a value, signed

**The Show line** (`#trace-show`; replaces the empty "Lanes / kinds" box).
Which kinds of row the trace and the rail list: **guard events** (an
interceptor's decision on its own line, and the workspace setup),
**background** (each turn's folded Background line), **AI notes** (interim
messages and harness summaries). All on by default, persisted
(`mandu.trace.show`). Rows are only hidden (one CSS rule per kind off
`#trace-layout[data-hide]`), never dropped, and a jump to a hidden row turns
its kind back on. The "N repeated guard events folded" note sits here.
A log with entries and no step (the admin log) hides it (*A system log*
above).

**The session's path and the words** (app.js `howPathHtml`,
`traceLegendHtml`; 2026-10-05). Read as a first-time user, the Trace tab
was a wall of cards in two vocabularies (the captions' "AgentView · T-LLM",
"not checked", `$MDU:` tokens, `exec_action`) with no key. Above the
captions, two things:

- **How Mandu worked in this session**: one path, a count per stop, every
  number a row the trace draws (`howPathCounts` over the paired rows): *You
  asked* (the turns with a prompt) → *The AI acted* (tool rows) → *Mandu
  checked* (the checks the turns draw, then the tool and action rows by the
  rail's `stepBlocked` / `stepAsked`: "6 checks, 1 blocked", "1 check, 1
  held for you", "3 checks, nothing blocked", or "no check recorded"; Off
  says *Mandu only watched*) → *Results came back* (masked tool rows) → *Data
  out* (§4.2f's sends: "N sends with a real value filled in, M kept on this
  machine", or "no send with a real value recorded") → *The reply reached
  you* (reply rows). No path on a session with no turns.
  A *check* is a decision Mandu recorded on a step the turns draw: each
  check line on a tool card (§4.2f; a decision recorded on the step with no
  line of its own counts once), and each inline card from a guard
  (`exec_action`, `net_action`, `fs_action`) or with a decision. The
  folded Background is not counted, and the stop's tooltip says so. Until
  2026-10-05 the stop counted only blocks: it read "1 blocked" over three
  "Mandu checked this command and let it run" lines and two sends, as if
  checking meant blocking.
- **What these words mean**: a key (`<details class="pr-legend">`) giving
  each word the cards use its plain meaning, with the paper / repo terms
  beside it: what the AI saw (AgentView, T-LLM), what really happened
  (HumanView, original data), placeholder (`$MDU:…` symbol, token), masked,
  trust not checked (Mandu did not judge whether the result could be
  trusted; in Secrets mode tool output is not checked this way, only the
  registered or labeled secrets in it are masked, and that is why Secrets
  mode does not stop prompt injection), the sandboxed
  reader (U-LLM, `inspect_symbol`), binding, left / kept on this machine,
  guard event (`exec_action`, `net_action`, `fs_action`; on a step, its line
  says what Mandu decided, §4.2f), Background. Open
  until the person closes it; the choice is kept (`mandu.trace.legend`) across
  re-renders and loads.

Tests: `app-js-dual-lanes.test.ts` (the stops and their counts, the checks
with exec gates, a held access and no decision at all, Off, no path or key
on an empty session, the key's terms, closed stays closed) and
`test/component/session-walkthrough.test.ts` (the served inspector over the
real server: the path, the key, the send rows, the checks counted and each
Bash card's "trust not checked" pill beside its check line).

**The trace and its key fit a narrow column (2026-10-15).** From 761 px
the trace shares the window with the session list (260 px by default,
dragged up to 600) and the step rail (180 px), so its column can be
narrow: 273 px in a 761 px window, 512 px at 1000. Two rules let content
decide that width:

- the key's `<dl>` was `max-content minmax(0, 1fr)`: each term took its
  whole one-line width (up to 310 px, *Guard event* with its three event
  names), and the meanings got what was left;
- the trace's grid (`.pr-trace`) declared no columns, so its one column
  was `auto`. Such a column is as wide as its widest child's min-content,
  here the open key's 350 px.

The key is open until the person closes it, so a new reader met both. A
headless Chromium over the served inspector measured, with the default
list, at 761 and 800 px:

- the page was 884 px wide and scrolled sideways;
- the trace's cards ran past the window's edge;
- every meaning had a 0 px column, so the key showed only its terms and
  ran 5590 px down the page.

At 900 px the meanings had 58 px, and 158 px at 1000. With the list
dragged to 600 px, the page scrolled sideways in every window up to
1100 px, and the meanings had 98 px at 1280.

Now the trace's column is `minmax(0, 1fr)`, never wider than its box
(§4.25 *A grid column is never wider than its box*). A child wider than
the column would stick out alone instead of widening every card; none
does today. The key's columns are `fit-content(40%) minmax(0, 1fr)`: a
term takes at most two fifths of the key and wraps beyond that, but never
narrower than its longest word. That word is at most 98 px, so the
meanings keep the rest of the key less the 14 px gap.

Measured again with the default list:

- no sideways scroll at any width;
- the meanings have 131 px at 761, 155 px at 800 (the key 1234 px tall)
  and 275 px at 1000;
- at 1280 only the longest term wraps its last name (`fs_action`);
- from 1293 px every term fits and the key is drawn as before;
- the phone layout (760 px and below, one column) is unchanged.

With the list at 600 px nothing scrolls sideways from 1100 px. A
narrower window left the trace 0–172 px and still overflowed: the list's
drag limit did not leave the trace room. CSS only. The list now leaves it
(*The list leaves the trace room*, below).

Tests:

- unit `css-trace-key-room.test.ts`:
  - the stylesheet on each side of each of its width queries, from 761 to
    1920 px: the trace's `minmax(0, 1fr)`, and a term column that is a

  - at 760 px and below, one column;
  - the drawn session page with its styles at 800 and 760 px: the open

    decides;
- stack `tests/stack/trace-key-room.test.ts` (secrets): a real arbiter,

  - The served stylesheet holds the same rules.
  - The served session page, signed out, draws the trace and its open key

  - No page, stylesheet or answer carries the key.

**The list leaves the trace room (2026-10-15).** The session list could
be as wide as 600 px whatever the window:

- `applySizing` applied the saved width as it was, and nothing applied
  it again when the window changed;
- a drag stopped at the window less 240 px, which is less than the step
  rail (180 px) and a readable trace together.

A list dragged wide on a big screen therefore stayed 600 px in a
half-screen window. A headless Chromium measured the served session page
of a seeded session with a saved 600 px list:

| window | main pane | trace | key's meanings | sideways scroll |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 761 px | 161 px | 0 px | 0 px | 251 px |
| 800 px | 200 px | 0 px | 0 px | 212 px |
| 1000 px | 400 px | 172 px | 30 px | 39 px |
| 1280 px | 680 px | 452 px | 239 px | none |

Narrowing the list in an 800 px window found the edge: the page scrolls
sideways once the main pane is under about 480 px.

Now the list is never wider than the window less 500 px (app.js
`MAIN_ROOM`, `widestIn`), and never under its 180 px floor. 500 px is the
room the main pane has at the narrowest two-column window, 761 px, with
the default 260 px list. That layout is already measured to fit (*The
trace and its key fit a narrow column*, above), so anything that fits
there fits beside any list.

- **The saved width is kept.** The limit applies to the width drawn, not
  to the width saved, and `applySizing` runs again on every `resize`. A
  narrower window narrows the list; a wider one gives back the width the
  person dragged.
- **A drag** stops at the same limit.
- **Only a changed width is saved.** A press on the gutter with no move,
  or a drag back to where it began, used to save the width drawn, which
  in a narrow window would replace the wider saved one. It now saves
  nothing.
- **Unchanged:** from 1100 px any saved width fits as before. The fold
  rail (30 px), the double-click reset to 260 px and the phone layout
  (760 px and below, where the list is a slide-over) are unchanged.

Measured again with a saved 600 px list, loaded at each width and resized
live: the list is 261 px at 761, 300 at 800, 400 at 900, 500 at 1000, 599
at 1099 and 600 from 1100. The main pane keeps 500 px (the trace 272 px,
the meanings 130 px), nothing scrolls sideways, and the saved width stays
600 px. Presentation only.

**"Why masked?"** (app.js `whyBtn` / `showWhySymbol`; plan 15 §13.8 item 8).
A link beside each masked value in the Secrets tab's table, in the ⊕ Masked
values modal, and on the trace's ⊕ marks (each "New token" row), named
"why masked?: $MDU:…" since 2026-10-13 (*A masked value's buttons name
it*, above), asks where
that `$MDU:` placeholder came from, on demand: nothing is fetched before a
click, and each click is ONE `GET /api/symbols/why?symbol=…&session=…` (the
open session as the hint). The answer opens in its own modal (`#why-modal`):
a headline, the facts (Level, Secret, Found by, Kind, What happened, Where,
Your answer, Rule now) and "What you can do".

- **The op.** The route (`inspector/why-symbol-routes.ts`) asks the arbiter's
  `whySymbol`, which reads the session events and so is HUMAN PLANE only;
  the adapter (`arbiter-adapter.ts`, on `PolicyDocArbiter`) sends it on the
  human-plane client, two positional args, never the data client.
- **The gate.** A GET is open to any same-host process, the agent's
  included, so the route is served only with the CSRF header AND the admin
  session, like the held prompts (`/api/prompt-filters/holds`); the page
  sends `X-Mandu-Control` and, refused, says how to get an admin session.
  A malformed name or session hint is a 400 before any arbiter call; no op
  501; no human plane 503; another failure 502.
- **Plain words** (`view-model/why-symbol.ts` `toWhySymbolVM`), after the
  CLI's (`launcher/src/why.ts`) in the dashboard's vocabulary
  (`categoryWords`, `ACTION_WORDS`, `levelWords`): a span of your own
  message, a secret Mandu already holds (the variable's NAME or the file's
  path), the agent's own text, a side call, other data at its level, or no
  such placeholder. The ways out are a person's acts here (let it through,
  Settings › Prompt filters, Approvals for a held message; none for a
  registered secret or under a locked administrator's row). Under a locked
  administrator's `ask` row (the answer's policy row says `onceOnly`, plan
  15 §12, 2026-10-04) "let it through" is for that message only, and the
  line says the administrator set the category to ask every time.
- **No finding: look in another session (2026-10-10).** The op looks for
  the message that carried a placeholder in its own session, the hint,
  then the most recent sessions (at most 24, plan 15 §13.8 `--session`).
  An answer with no finding no longer says "its session log is gone" as a
  fact: a prompt-filter placeholder reads "No record of that message was
  found: its session log is gone, or it is in a session Mandu did not look
  in.", and every answer with no finding carries `looked`, the CLI's
  `--session` line in words: "No message to the AI that carried it was
  found in session <id> (or Mandu has no such session). Mandu looked in N
  sessions in all." (the route hands the view-model its hint). Under it,
  "Look in another session" is a `<select>` of the Sessions page's own
  sessions (its day groups; never a system log, a drill or a test; an
  older server's list less those), newest first, each "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM ·
  <its row's name>", the session just asked picked; **Look** asks again,
  ONE fetch, that session as the hint. It is drawn only when another
  session is listed; an answer with a finding has none. The common case
  needs no choice (the open session is the hint); the choice is for a
  message in a session past the search, such as a key typed in an older
  session's prompt and written out by the AI in this one.
- **Never a value.** The arbiter's answer holds none, and the view-model
  copies the answer's named fields one by one, so a field an answer should
  not carry (a value, the span, an event's panes) is not passed on; the
  page escapes every string.
