`app-js-why-symbol` (the header's counts from `counts` over the loaded
steps, the capped note, `{}` read as zeros, the read-before part after an
amber mark, from `counts` or the loaded lineage; "Why masked?" in the Secrets
tab, the ⊕ modal and the trace's ⊕ marks, one fetch per click with the
symbol, the session and the CSRF header, the answer escaped and without the
value, the 403 and 501 words; with no finding, the `looked` line and the
session choice: the Sessions page's sessions only, newest first, escaped,
the open one picked, Look's one fetch with the session picked, no choice
when no other session is listed). "Why masked?":
`test/unit/view-model/why-symbol.test.ts` (each source in words, the ways
out, a locked row, a pending hold, protection off, no value passed on from
a leaky answer, `looked` per count and hint and never "is gone" as a
fact), `test/unit/server/why-symbol-routes.test.ts` (the gate, 400 before
any arbiter call, positional forwarding, no value in the body, the hint
said back in `looked`, 501 / 503 / 502 / 404) and
`tests/stack/dashboard-why-symbol.test.ts` (the production wiring over the
real arbiter and proxy: both placeholders explained without a value, the
gate, the op refused on the data socket; then a second launch whose AI
writes the key's placeholder into a command, 24 later sessions, and the
real inspector bundle over this server's listing: no message in that
session, 24 looked in, and Look in the first session finds the key typed
in its prompt, no value on the page);
`server/sessions-payload` (the counts on section rows
only); `listing-cache-file` (schema 2 discards a schema-1 file);
`payload-budget` (the cost, §4.30, and no running row).

### 4.34 Approvals, Rules and Settings in the product's words

**Why.** After §4.32 the inspector had the product's page names but not its
words. Its Approvals cards said **✓ Allow · ✓ Allow once · ⛔ Block**, its
Policy table **Approve · Approve once · Deny**, and the product **Allow once
· Always allow · Block**: three vocabularies for one answer, two of them in
a different order. The cards kept copy the product had already replaced ("a
protected file", "If you allow it", "History"; the Protection block's "→
locked files"), and the card's sentence was a second, hand-kept copy of the
product's wording (egress.js `approvalSentence`) that had drifted. The Rules
page stacked the Protection block, the policy panel, 39 built-in rules,
Prompt filters and 144 secrets in one scroll with no way to jump; its
tables pushed a 390px phone to a 524px scroll width. Settings gave each
sandbox switch three lines whatever its value.

**One set of words, from the server.** The question's sentence and the
card's three cells come from ONE function, `describeAsk`, in
**view-model/ask-words.ts** (home.ts re-exports it). policy-panel.ts
`toQueueRow` stamps each queue row with `words`: a waiting row carries
`{family, sentence, why, aiNow, ifAllowed}` and the three cells as parts
(`whyParts`, `aiNowParts`, `ifAllowedParts`, their names as code, §4.25u
*The cells name things as the headline does*), an answered row `{family,
sentence}` only (the "Answered earlier" table needs no more). "The agent"
asks, since the panel does not know which agent ran the session. The
inspector paints those parts as text and code (`sentenceEl`); egress.js
keeps no copy of the wording. The product's read family says "click Allow
once or Always allow" (§4.25u). Cost on the wire: a standing answer adds
about 850 bytes to `/api/policy/panel` (`PER_VERDICT_BUDGET`, 1,000, still
pins it) and the payload-budget fixture's panel is 323,166 bytes (budget
423,000). `/api/policy/panel` stays uncompressed (§4.30: the queue mixes
secret paths with agent-chosen destinations, a compression side channel).

**A send names its secret** (2026-10-07). Every send card read "The agent
wants to send **a secret** to `api.stripe.com`", and its cells "Mandu
masked it … would show the real secret to …". A key of `.env` and an
environment variable bound for one host were the same card twice, and
*Always allow* did not say what it would allow, while the Rules row for
the very answer it records said "sending only the file `~/proj/.env`"
(§4.25e). The arbiter already says where the value came from: it attaches
the symbol table's provenance to each queue row at read time
(`EgressApproval.source = {tool, origin}`), and a registered secret file's
key has its own symbol (`$MDU:nomodel_Read[9bbd].STRIPE_KEY`, the
registry's structured twin, confidentiality plan 10 §2.4). So `describeAsk`
now names it (`secretOf`):

- a key of a registered file: "… wants to send your secret `STRIPE_KEY` to
  `api.stripe.com`", and *Why it stopped* begins "STRIPE_KEY comes from
  ~/mandu-try/.env.";
- an environment variable (origin `env:NAME`): "… your secret
  `GITHUB_TOKEN` …", and "GITHUB_TOKEN is an environment variable.";
- a secret file with no named key: "… wants to send a secret from
  `~/proj/deploy/staging.conf` to …";
- nothing known (an arbiter that predates `source`, an origin that is a
  web address or a command): "a secret", as before.

A field names a key only on a `Read` row beside the file it came from. The
registry mints `KEY`, `default.aws_secret_access_key` and
`DATABASE_URL.password` (`.encoded` marks the decoded value of the same
key). fs-sync names a file's symbol by its path instead (`notes.md`, or
an encoded `__mdu_field_…`), a human edit's pieces end `.__mdu_split[n]`,
and `content`, `text`, `extract_3` and the like say where in a result a
value sat: none of those is a name, so the card names the file. Untrusted
text is never called a secret. The row keeps the origin as `QueueRowVM.origin`
only when it is a path or `env:NAME`, so a web address or a command adds no
bytes and no new data; the payload-budget fixture's rows carry none, and its
numbers are unchanged. The name and the file were already served signed out
(the row's `subject`, `plain.reach`, the session page's *Your secrets*); the
value and the token never are, and the product's asks carry the words only,
not the origin. The product pages write a file under the dashboard's home as
`~/…` (`buildHome` passes the home, `tildePath`: another account's home stays
as recorded, as *Your secrets* does); the inspector's words keep the full
path, as the inspector does elsewhere. The card, Home's card, a session
page's waiting card, *Answered earlier* and the inspector's Approvals page
all say it, since they share the words. The first-session tour's screenshot
was re-taken (docs/first-session.md step 2). Tests: `home-view-model.test.ts`
(each kind of name, the fields that are not names, `~` only with the page's
home, the home VM's waiting and answered rows), `policy-panel.test.ts` (the
row's origin kept only for a path or a variable; the inspector's full path),
component `approvals-names-secret.test.ts` (the served Approvals and Home
pages in jsdom) and stack `approval-names-secret.test.ts` (a real arbiter's
registered `.env` key and environment variable, gated, answered once over
the real route; no route carries a value).

**`~` is the dashboard's home** (2026-10-07). On the product pages `~`
means one folder: the home folder of the account the dashboard runs as
(`os.homedir()`, the server's `fileBrowserHome` test seam), the one the
Rules page's file browser calls `~`. A path under it reads `~/…`; any other
path stays as recorded, another account's home folder included, so `~`
never names the wrong folder. Before, two heuristics turned ANY
`/home/<name>/` into `~`: home.js `shortPath` (Rules' file rules and
labels, an agent's folder on Home and on its page, the explorer) and
`rule-words.ts` `compactPath` (an answered send's "sending only the file
…"). On a dashboard run by one account, `/home/alice/x` read as the
person's own `~/x`, while a macOS home (`/Users/<name>`) or `/root` was
never shortened. Now:

- the server serves the product page with its home folder as
  `<meta name="home-dir">` (server.ts → static-routes.ts `serveIndex`,
  whose meta values are attribute-escaped), and `shortPath` shortens under
  that folder only (`HOME_DIR`); a page served without one writes every
  path as recorded. The inspector's page carries none: it keeps full paths;
- `rule-words.ts` owns `tildePath` (file-browser.ts re-exports it), and
  `compactPath`, `dataWords` and `answerWords` take the home, which
  `toPolicyPanelViewModel` gets from `/api/policy/panel` and the home
  route (`loadPolicyPanel`'s `home`). The Rules row is shared, so the
  inspector's answer rows say `~` of the same folder;
- the Approvals card names a program and the script an interpreter runs
  with the same rule (`ask-words.ts` `programWords`, the `open:`, `trust:`
  and `write:` families): "The program `~/.nvm/…/bin/node running
  ~/proj/x.js` wants to read a secret file: `.env`" on the product pages
  (Approvals, Home, a session's waiting card), the first-session tour's
  item 2 (its screenshots had to redact the account name). The inspector's
  card (`/api/policy/panel`'s words, no home) keeps the full path, as for a
  send's file above. A copy of a program in the person's folders is still
  told apart from the system's (`~/proj/cat`, `/usr/bin/cat`);
- an answer about one file on Rules names it as the file rules do
  (`~/.pgpass`);
- a rule change names its file the same way (2026-10-15). The grammar
  (policy-proposals.ts) has `editWords(edit, home)` and
  `relaxWords(r, home)` beside `editRow` / `relaxLine`, which keep every
  path as recorded for the routes that name no file (Settings' models,
  sensitivity labels and prompt filters). A `lock-path` / `unlock-path`
  edit's path, a `paths` facet's would-let line and an undo's or hand
  edit's `paths` delta read `~/…`; another facet or value (a host, a list
  entry, a program) as written. `GET /api/policy/proposals` and
  `GET /api/policy/changes` take the server's home (`fileBrowserHome`,
  else `os.homedir()`, as the panel), so Approvals' waiting card ("Make
  `~/proj/.env` a secret no AI may read", "`~/proj/.env` would be
  protected less") and Rule changes match the Rules row of the same file;
  and a session page's step for the agent's call to Mandu's own rule tools
  (mandu-tool-words.ts `policyToolSentence(kind, args, home)`, from
  `actionSentence`'s home) reads "Asked Mandu to make
  `~/proj/deploy/staging.conf` a secret no AI may read", a test call's
  file too. Its 120-character cut (`POLICY_VALUE_CAP`) counts the path
  as drawn. Before, all of these spelled the account's home folder out,
  beside a Rules row and a "Your secrets" card saying `~/…`. The POST
  answers are unchanged (the page reads only a refiled card's id and who
  asked). The inspector reads the proposals only to count them;
- so does Rules › Describe what you want's suggestion (2026-10-15).
  `POST /api/policy/assistant` takes the same home, and `suggestRules`
  builds its rows with `editWords` and its *This would let* lines with
  `relaxWords`. Before, they spelled the home folder out, and one card
  could name a file both ways: the assistant may write `~/proj/notes.md`
  (its prompt allows `~/`), while the arbiter's preview names the path it
  normalized (`normalizeLabelPath`), so the row said "Remove the rule for
  `~/proj/notes.md`" over "`/home/<you>/proj/notes.md` would be protected
  less". The answer's `edits` and `expected` are untouched: Apply sends
  the assistant's edits and is bound to the arbiter's own subjects, so the
  words a page draws never reach policy.yaml.

The served page names the home folder signed out too. It is the account's
own `$HOME`, which any program of that account already has, and the open
routes (`/api/home`, `/api/policy/panel`) already carried paths under it.
The words an agent wrote (its replies, its commands) stay as written.
Tests: unit `policy-panel.test.ts` (an answer's file under the page's home,
another account's, a macOS home, no home), `home-view-model.test.ts` (the
card's program and script, another account's, the inspector's full path),
`home-js-rules.test.ts` (the page's labels, an answered file and an agent's
folder under three served homes and none) and component
`home-dir-tilde.test.ts` (the real server's served page and its escaping,
Approvals and Rules in jsdom, the panel's words). The rule-change words:
unit `policy-proposals-view-model.test.ts` (each path-naming row, a
would-let line, delta rows; another account's home, a pattern, `..`, no
home), `mandu-tool-words.test.ts`, `agent-page.test.ts` (the step and its
cut) and `policy-proposal-routes.test.ts` (both GETs, the seam and
`os.homedir()`); stack `rule-change-home-paths.test.ts` (a real arbiter,
the anthropic-proxy and the mandu-policy server on their production
clients, a real dashboard with its home: the listings signed in and out,
the served Approvals and session pages, a file outside the home in full;
no value on any page, answer or model request). Describe: unit
`policy-assistant.test.ts` (an absolute path and an expanded `~/` under the
home, another account's home, a file outside it, a host; `edits` and
`expected` the same with and without a home; the route with
`fileBrowserHome` and with `os.homedir()`) and stack
`describe-home-paths.test.ts` (a real arbiter on the production adapter and
a real dashboard with its home: the POST, the served Rules page's card, an
Apply that writes the full path; no value in the helper's context, a page
or an answer).

**Read before it was marked** (2026-10-07). Every send card said "Mandu
masked it, so the AI never read it" and, under *What the AI has now*, "It
has never read the real one". That is false for a secret the AI read as it
was before its label: the tour's `deploy/staging.conf` was delivered raw at
10:41 and masked from 10:42 (dual-lanes `maskedLater`), and a send of it
would have been asked with that assurance. The session page already tells
the same fact honestly (§4.25b, *Your secrets*: "The AI read its real value
at 10:41, before it was marked a secret"). Now a waiting row whose item the
AI read first says so:

- *Why it stopped*: "Mandu masks it now, but the AI read its real value
  before it was marked a secret. Sending it would show the real secret to
  `paste.example`." (after the "comes from" sentence when the secret is
  named);
- *What the AI has now*: "The AI read the real value before it was marked a
  secret. Since then it gets the masked version, but Mandu does not mask what
  the AI wrote itself." Never "only the masked version" alone, since the
  AI's own replies go back to it as written (confidentiality.md §7.1).

The command family's *What the AI has now* and the show family's two cells
say the same. Text that is not a secret reads "before Mandu masked it". The
sentence and *If you click Allow* do not change.

The fact comes from the dashboard's own reading of the sessions on the row,
not from the arbiter. `HomeFacts` keeps, per session, the earliest raw
delivery of each item by its token's base (`readFirst`, lineage
`readFirstByBase`, the rule `withReadFirst` applies to the lineage). It is
cached with the session's other facts, so a session that has not moved is
not re-read. `readFirstLookup` (home-routes.ts) takes the earliest such time
over a waiting `$MDU:` row's sessions. `loadPolicyPanel` passes the map to
`toPolicyPanelViewModel`, which stamps it on the row (`QueueRowVM.readFirst`,
an ISO time, never a value) and words the row with it. Home, the session
page's waiting card and the inspector's `/api/policy/panel` all pass the
lookup through one facts cache per tenant (`server.ts homeFactsFor`). An
answered row has no card to correct, so it carries no time. Any session on
the row counts: two sessions that send the same secret to one host share a
row, and either one's raw read means the real value already went to an AI.
A session not on record, or an unreadable one, adds nothing, so its card
keeps the words as before. That is the convention for a record that is not
known ("absent: none known", §4.15). The lookup runs only while a waiting
row names an item or a program's read of a file. The product's asks carry
the words, not the time.

A program's request to read a secret file (an `open:` row, or the warning
question `trust:`) had the same gap: *What the AI has now* said "The AI has
not seen the real file, and its program `cat` has not read it", also for a
file the AI read as it was before its label. Its subject names a program, not
an item, so its row is looked up by its file, the row's destination (the
guard's held open names the file it asked about). `HomeFacts` also keeps,
per session, the earliest raw delivery by the file its tokens came from
(`readFirstFiles`, lineage `readFirstByFile`: the session's symbol rows give
each `maskedLater` token's origin, and only an absolute path counts). Such a
card now says "The AI read the file as it was before it was marked a secret,
and its program `cat` has not read it. Since then the AI gets the masked
version, but Mandu does not mask what the AI wrote itself." *Why it stopped*
and *If you click Allow* stay, since both are still true. The match is exact:
a path spelled another way (a link) adds nothing, so the card keeps the
words as before. A `write:` row is about a change, not a read, and is not
looked up.

Tests: `home-view-model.test.ts` (each family's words, read first or not; the
home VM's card carries words, not the time), `policy-panel.test.ts` (the
row's time and words; an answered row and an unnamed row unchanged),
`lineage.test.ts` (`readFirstByBase`, `readFirstByFile`),
`session-page-record.test.ts` (the tour through the real `HomeFacts` and
`readFirstLookup`: staging.conf read first, STRIPE_KEY not, a session not on
record adds nothing; a program's read of staging.conf gets the time, one of
`.env`, an answered one and a `write:` row do not). There is also component
`approvals-read-first.test.ts`: the served Approvals, Home and session pages
over the tour, and the inspector's row, for sends and for a program's
`open:` and `trust:` reads. Stack `approval-read-first.test.ts` uses a real
arbiter: a raw delivery, then the labelling act and a masked re-send, then
the real gate's asks and the guard's held opens of both files. A secret
registered first keeps "never read" and "has not seen the real file", and no
route carries a value.

**After you answer** (2026-10-11). An audit of Approvals with a row of
each kind found the cards silent or wrong about what happens to the
stopped action once the person answers:

- a send's card said "The AI's request goes to `api.stripe.com` with the
  real secret filled in". The gate had refused that request (the proxies
  answer 403) and told the agent to wait for the person ("tell the user,
  and do not retry before they answer"). Only a new try goes, and the agent
  cannot see the answer, so nothing tries again until the person says so;
- a program's held read or change said it "reads the real file" and
  "Mandu holds the change until you answer" an hour after the guard stopped
  holding it (its ceiling, 60 s by default, `MANDU_SECRETS_ASK_TIMEOUT`),
  and "121 times": the guard asks again every half second while it holds,
  and each ask counts;
- a card about a program did not say which agent asked ("The program
  `/usr/bin/psql` wants to read …");
- a card offering no Always allow (one run of a program that runs code no
  pin names) headed its third cell "If you click Allow once or Always
  allow";
- an agent that ended hours ago stayed under Home's *Running now*,
  "Waiting for your OK", while its question waited, and its card did not
  say that nothing waits on the answer now;
- a held message said "Its request is waiting" long after its deadline
  (30 s by default) sent it with the part masked;
- a masked value asked to be shown to the model as it is (the arbiter's
  `declassifySymbol`, keyed to the act `model_context:in-context-read`)
  read "wants to send a secret to `model_context:in-context-read`".

Now (`ask-words.ts`, `home.ts`, `home.js`, `egress.js`):

- every family whose attempt was refused says what a new try does and ends
  "After you answer, tell the agent to try again." (`TELL_AGENT`): a send
  "The AI's next request goes to `api.stripe.com` with the real secret
  filled in. Mandu refused this one, so nothing was sent."; the file path
  gate, an upload, an escalation, downloaded code, a command that uses
  masked text and a show say "when it tries again" and the same line;
- a held open or change (`open:`, `trust:`, `write:`) says whether the
  program still waits. The guard's re-asks bump the row's `lastSeen`, so
  `home.ts heldNow` calls a row asked within `HELD_FRESH_MS` (5 s) held:
  "The AI's program `/usr/bin/psql` is waiting for your answer now, and
  goes on at once: it reads the real file."; else "… stopped waiting and
  could not read the file. If you allow it, it reads the real file the next
  time the AI runs it." and the line. A change's *Why it stopped* reads
  "Mandu held the change for a while, then refused it." One run's change
  (`#run:`) whose program stopped waiting says that no answer helps it now:
  "Your answer covers that run only, so a new try asks again." The card
  shows no count for these rows (`HomeAsk.held` present). The inspector's
  words have no clock and claim neither (`held` absent);
- a program's sentence names the agent: "Claude Code's program
  `/usr/bin/psql` wants to read a secret file: `.pgpass`" ("The agent's
  program" in the inspector, which does not know the agent);
- the third cell is named for the buttons the card offers: "If you click
  Allow once" when there is no Always allow, on both front ends;
- a card whose asking session has ended (listed and not running: a
  recorded exit, or no event for the running window) adds "The agent that
  asked has ended, so nothing is waiting on this now. Your answer counts the
  next time an agent asks." (`HomeAsk.askerEnded`; a session not on record
  claims nothing). On Home that agent is under *Earlier*, its row counting
  "1 question waiting for you"; only a running agent is "Waiting for your
  OK";
- the moment line names the session that asked last and where it works,
  "· from Claude Code in `~/projects/shop`" (`HomeAsk.askerCwd`,
  `askerAgent`, `askerSessions`; nothing when the folder is not known,
  §4.25u *A question says which session asked*);
- a held message's card: "The AI has not seen the message as you wrote it.
  Its request waits for your answer for a short while, then goes with that
  part masked." and, under the answers, "An answer given after the request
  went applies from the AI's next request, which carries your message
  again." (the agents resend the whole conversation; prompt-filter
  holds.ts). The page does not see the deadline, so the words hold either
  way;
- a row keyed `model_context:` is the show family (`policy-panel.ts`
  `toQueueRow`), named as a send names its secret: "Claude Code wants to
  show the AI your secret `STRIPE_KEY` as it is".

Presentation only: no answer, route or arbiter decision changed. Pending
questions still never expire (a held open's row outlives its hold, by
design, so a later answer decides the next try); the card says which state
it is in instead. Tests: `home-view-model.test.ts` (each family's line, the
held states and the inspector's, an ended agent's card and Home row, the
show family), `home-js-approvals.test.ts` (no count on a held row, the
ended line, the third cell's name), `egress-js-approvals.test.ts` (the
inspector's third cell), component `approvals-after-answer.test.ts` (the
served Approvals and Home pages over a row of each state), and stack
`approval-after-answer.test.ts`: the real gate refuses a registered key's
send and the card says so; Allow once over the real route lets the NEXT
request through and the one after asks again; the guard's held change
reads "waiting now" while it re-asks and "stopped waiting" after, and its
next try is allowed with no new question; no route carries the value.

**A held message's answer** (2026-10-11). A held message (`prompt:`
rows, plan 15 §7) records Send as written as approved and Send masked and
Cancel the message as denied, for one message (`model:<session>#turn:<ref>`,
scope once) or, with "for this session", also on a row for the session
(`model:<session>`, scope always; prompt-filter holds.ts `afterResolve`).
*Answered earlier* read those rows as any other: a message that went
masked was "Blocked", with **Allow instead**. That button is the generic
approve, an Always, so on a message's row it filed a standing "send as
written" for the whole session: an answer wider than its words, on a
message that had already gone. Now (`home.ts answeredOutcome`,
`policy-panel.ts toQueueRow`, `home.js answerLabel`, `egress.js
yourAnswer`):

- the outcome says what went to the AI: "Sent as written", "Sent masked,
  or cancelled" (the row does not tell them apart), "Sent as written for
  the session", "Masked for the session". The agent page's "Your answer:"
  says the same (§4.25b);
- a message's row has no reversal; a session's row offers **Send masked
  instead** or **Send as written instead**, which flips that session's
  standing answer and nothing more (the same verdict routes, `deny` and
  `approve`);
- a send, a read or a command keeps Blocked, Allowed once and Block
  instead / Allow instead.

Security: this removes a button that granted more than it said; no answer
grants more than before. Tests: `home-view-model.test.ts` (each outcome and
its actions), `home-js-approvals.test.ts` and `egress-js-document.test.ts`
(both front ends' rows), component `approvals-after-answer.test.ts` (the
served page), and stack `approval-held-message-answers.test.ts`: the real
anthropic-proxy holds two messages; Send masked reads `masked` with no
reversal; Send as written for the session reads `sent-session`, the
session's row offers Send masked instead, the next message goes as written,
and after Send masked instead over the real route the next one goes masked.

**Answers that no longer apply** (2026-10-11). Since 2026-10-02 a question
about a program names its file and contents (`open:/usr/bin/psql#<sha256>`,
`write:/usr/bin/nano#<sha256>`). A row from before (`open:ssh-add`,
`write:nano`) matches no opener or writer, yet a pending one was listed in
Approvals, and an answered one was listed with **Block instead** and on Rules
with its flip: a button that changed nothing. Answers the arbiter already
treats as applying to nothing (about a printer, an interpreter named alone,
an `open:` answer given before the warning question, confidentiality plan 13
D8) were listed the same way; only `mandu why` and the file's *Why* said so.

- **The arbiter.** `flow-taint.ts nameOnlyVerdict` (an `open:`, `trust:`
  or `write:` subject with no absolute path) joins `mootQuestionReason`,
  last, so a printer's or an interpreter's reason stays: a pending
  name-only question is retired at start and before every listing and
  answer (`retireMootQuestions`), and an answer to it is refused, saying
  why (409). `decideSecretOpen` no longer files a question for an opener
  with no absolute path (no answer could name it; `decideProtectedWrite`
  already refused such a writer). `withProvenance` marks every listed
  ANSWERED row that applies to nothing with `noLongerApplies`
  (`verdictNoLongerApplies`: `name-only`, `printer`, `interpreter`,
  `unvetted`), at read time, never persisted. Fail-closed: retiring removes
  only a pending row, and the mark changes no decision.
- **The dashboard.** `toQueueRow` keeps the mark on an answered row, words
  it (`rule-words.ts noLongerAppliesWords`, `QueueRowVM.staleNote`: "This
  answer no longer applies: it names the program by its name only, as Mandu
  asked before October 2, 2026. Mandu now asks about the program's file, so
  it asks again.") and offers no reversal. Approvals › *Answered earlier*
  reads "No longer applies" (what was answered on hover) with the why under
  the words; Rules › Your rules shows the why as the row's warning, no flip,
  Remove kept; the inspector's table reads "No longer applies", the why on
  hover.

Security: removing a pending row grants nothing (the gate decides by the
law, as before the row existed), and the mark only takes buttons away.
Tests: arbiter `stale-answers.test.ts` (the predicates; an older arbiter's
DB rows over a real server: pending ones retired and refused, answered ones
marked on both listings, a live answer not; an opener with no path files no

**A rule change your agent asked for is never "nothing"** (2026-10-12).
The inspector's *Waiting for your answer* lists the gates' questions
(`/api/policy/panel`). A rule change your agent asked for (§4.25,
policy-surface.md §8.6) waits on the product's Approvals, which answers
it, and no inspector page read it. A headless Chromium, with the agent's
binding of `.env` to a host waiting and no question, drew the inspector's
list as "Nothing is waiting for you." while the product's badge said 1
and its Approvals drew the request's *Allow* / *Not now*. The product's
line had been fixed the same day (§4.25 *An empty list never says nothing
waits over a rule change*); the inspector's had not.

Now egress.js `refresh` reads `/api/policy/proposals?status=pending` with
each read of the panel (one `Promise.all`; the route is served `open`, as
to the product's Home poll), and `E.changes` holds how many wait and
whether one is a held change to policy.yaml. While one waits:

- a list with no question reads **"No question is waiting for you."**, the
  product's words; with nothing waiting it still reads "Nothing is waiting
  for you.";
- under the list (after the cards, that line, or "could not check for
  waiting questions"), one muted line links to the product's Approvals
  (`<base>/approvals`) in Home's words, then where: "1 rule change your
  agent asked for is in Approvals on the product page ↗", "2 rule changes
  your agent asked for are …", and for a held change to policy.yaml "1
  rule change waits for you in Approvals on the product page ↗".

The inspector draws no *Allow* for a rule change: answering one stays on
the product page, with the card's facts and its typed-ALLOW guard. A read
of the requests with no answer keeps the last known, as the panel keeps
its last state; any other answer replaces it, so a server that cannot list
requests (an older arbiter's 501) claims nothing. The nav badge and the
heading's count still count the questions. The link's line comes after
the list's own line, so the last answer's focus (§4.32 *An answer keeps
the focus in its list*) lands on the words, never on the link, and a focus
on the link stays on it when a poll draws it again. The Approvals page is
always on the live store (app.js crosses back from the Tests view's
tenant), as the product page is, so the link opens the same requests.
Cost: one small GET more per 3 s poll, beside the panel's ~320 KB. Two
tests that hold the page's reads to order a poll against an answer
(`egress-js-answer-focus.test.ts`) let this read through: what they test
is the panel's read and the answer, and their assertions are unchanged.

Tests: `egress-js-rule-change-line.test.ts` (jsdom, 7 cases):

- no question and one request: the line, the link's words, its href, no
  button, the read and its header;
- two requests, then held changes to policy.yaml, in Home's words;
- a question beside a request: its card, then the link's line;
- nothing waiting: as before, no link (a guard);
- "could not check for waiting questions", then the link;
- a poll that brings a request and takes it away; a read with no answer
  keeps it, a 501 drops it;
- the last answer's focus lands on the line; a focus on the link stays.

6 fail on the old page, and 12 of 12 mutations are caught. Stack
`tests/stack/inspector-rule-change-line.test.ts` (`secrets`): a real
arbiter with the agent's binding waiting, the production adapter, a real
dashboard, and the served `/dev/approvals` (app.js, egress.js) signed out
draws the line and the link, whose page the server serves; *Not now* on
the product's route, then a read: "Nothing is waiting for you." and no
link; signed in, a new request brings both back; no page or read holds the
file's value, the admin token or the session secret. It fails on the old
page.

**The answers, and what each one sends.** The server labels a waiting
row's actions in the product's order and words: **Allow once**
(`{approve: true, scope: "once"}`) · **Always allow** (`{approve: true}`) ·
**Block** (`{approve: false}`); one run of a program that runs code no pin
names (`…#run:`) gets no Always allow (confidentiality plan 13 §8 (c)). The
reversal on an answered row is **Block instead** / **Allow instead** (a
held message's: none, or the session's own, *A held message's answer*). The
verb is read from `scope` and `approve`, never the label, everywhere:

| Button | POST | What it records |
|---|---|---|
| Allow once | `/api/egress/approvals/<id>/approve-once` | one use, then it asks again |
| Always allow | `…/<id>/approve` | a standing allow |
| Block | `…/<id>/deny` | a standing block |
| Block instead / Allow instead | `…/deny` / `…/approve` | the one-click change of an answer |
| Allow this session (a program's send, *A send names every file*) | `…/<id>/approve` | a standing allow on a row keyed to one session |
| Always: add <host> to <file> (the same card, one per file in the way) | `…/<id>/always-source {path}` | no answer: that file's rule in policy.yaml gains the host |
| Send without it (a secret's placeholder in a request, *Send without it* below) | `…/<id>/send-without` | one use: the next such request goes with `[hidden by Mandu]` where the secret was; then it asks again |

**Send without it** (2026-10-17, confidentiality.md §4 "Send without
it"). A card about a secret's placeholder in a request to a host it is not
bound to (`egress:secret-unbound`, `egress:secret-bound-approval`) has a
fourth answer between *Always allow* and *Block*: the next such request
goes, with the neutral marker `[hidden by Mandu]` where the placeholder
was, and the secret stays on the machine. A task such as "open an issue
with the full error" then finishes instead of stopping at a block. The
card gains a note under its three cells (the grid stays three),
*If you click Send without it*: "The next such
request goes with [hidden by Mandu] where the secret was, so the task can
finish. The secret is not sent. This answer covers one request; the next
one asks again."

- **Offered only where the arbiter says.** The arbiter marks a waiting row
  `stripOffered` when it would take the answer (a secret's whole `$MDU:`
  placeholder × a network host, the axis on); the panel keeps the mark on
  the row (never on a program's send, a session's card or a held message),
  and only the product's card adds the action `{approve: false, scope:
  "once", strip: true}` (home.ts `sendWithoutActions`); home.js draws the
  button only when the server lists it (a card from an older server, which
  lists no answers, never shows it). The panel's own `actions`, which the
  inspector draws, stay the three answers: its buttons key a once-scoped
  action to Allow once, so it is never handed this one. A program's send
  (`holder-send:`), a HIGH session's request or command, a file open, a held
  message: never, since their request may hold the data itself. The arbiter
  refuses the answer there anyway; the route answers that refusal 409 with
  its reason.
- **One use.** Stored as a once denial carrying `strip`, spent by the
  net-proxy's ask for the next request; then the card asks again. The
  dashboard adapter refuses to report success when the arbiter stored
  something else (an older build keeps a plain Block, which says so).
- **Answered earlier** reads **Send without it, unused** until the request
  goes and **Sent without it** after (`answeredOutcome` `without` /
  `without-used`), never *Blocked*; it offers no reversal (an answer about
  one request) and, being one-shot, is not a Rules row.

Pinned by `dashboard/test/unit/view-model/send-without-actions.test.ts`,
`dashboard/test/unit/ui/home-js-send-without.test.ts`, the `send-without`
case of `dashboard/test/unit/server/egress-approvals-routes.test.ts`, and
e2e `tests/stack/send-without-net-proxy.test.ts` (the production adapter's
answer over a real arbiter, the real net-proxy, a recording sink).

A held message (`prompt:` rows, plan 15 §7) keeps its four answers (Send
as written · … for this session · Send masked · Cancel the message) and is
answered on the prompt hold route, `POST /api/prompt-filters/holds/answer
{approvalId, answer, scope}`, as the product answers it.

**A session that read a secret asks too** (2026-10-11, confidentiality.md
§4 "The human half"). After the AI reads a secret into the conversation,
its request to a host the content is not bound to, and each of its shell
commands, waits on a card: `session-net:<session>` × host (family `send`,
"Claude Code wants to send a request to `evil.example` after reading
`~/memos/q3.md`"; a web search, which names no place, reads "a request that
names no place") and `session-exec:<session>` × the exact command (family
`run`, "… wants to run `curl …` after reading …"). The arbiter attaches
`sessionReads` (the symbols the session read, with their origins) at list
time; `describeAsk` (`sessionAsk`) names each by its key or its file,
`~/…` on the product pages, with "and N more" past eight. Why it stopped:
the session read those into the AI's conversation and the place is not
one they may go (a command: Mandu cannot tell whether it sends anything);
the request could carry what the AI read in its own words. If allowed:
"This one request goes to … as the AI wrote it, and it may carry text
derived from …" / for a command, under the guard (the row's
`sessionConfined`, `sessionBindings`): "This exact command runs once, held
like a program that read …: it may reach only <hosts>, Mandu refuses any
other connection, and the files it writes are marked secret", and without
it: "… with the network your agent's commands normally have: Mandu cannot
hold it on this computer … the files it writes are not marked secret";
either way "any other command, or this one again, asks again". A bound
host asked only because the session is untrusted-tainted (the frozen
integrity axis) reads "… is a place it may go, but an instruction hidden
in that text could aim the AI's request there". The answers are **Allow
once** and **Block** only: the arbiter keeps an Always on these rows as
once, and the panel offers none (policy-surface.md §9.8.7). The block's
event carries `policy.approvalId`, so the session page's step says "Mandu
asked for your OK in Approvals" with the link and Home counts the ask; an
answered row reads "requests to it from one session that read a secret" /
"running this command in one session that read a secret"
(`sessionAnswerWords`) and takes no one-click reversal (an "Allow instead"
would read as standing; removing the answer under Rules asks again). The
page's card code is unchanged: these rows ride
the existing families and answers. Tests: `dashboard`
`session-asks.test.ts`, `tests/stack/high-session-approvals.test.ts`.

**A held command's refused connection** (2026-10-12, confidentiality.md §4).
Under the guard every command of such a session holds what the session
read; when one of them connects to a place that content may not go, the
arbiter files the session's own network row (`session-net:<session>` × the
host, or the address the guard saw) and attaches `sessionHeld` (its latest
reason starts `HELD COMMAND:`) with `sessionBindings`. `sessionAsk` then
words it as the command's request: "Claude Code ran a command that wants to
connect to `evil.example` after reading `~/memos/q3.md`"; why: the session
read those into the AI's conversation, so every command the AI runs holds
data from them and may reach only <hosts>, and the place is not one, so the
command's request there could carry that data; the AI now: "The command's
request to … was stopped; nothing was sent. The AI was told you were
asked."; if allowed: "Allow once lets the next try through: the next
connection from this session to … goes, once, and it may carry data from
…. The try after that asks again. Block stops this session's requests to …
for good." The answers stay Allow once and Block. The same row is the one
the agent's own request to that place asks, so the card describes the
latest request that asked. Tests: `session-asks.test.ts`,
`tests/stack/high-session-approvals.test.ts` (g),
`tests/sandbox/guard/high-session-command.test.ts`.

**A send names every file** (2026-10-11, confidentiality plan 13 §5.4, §9
R2). A program that read secret files (a holder) may send only where every
one of them may go. Its send to any other host was refused with no card at
all: the proxy's 403 said "approval required" and nothing in Approvals could
approve it. Now the net-proxy files a question (`holder-send:{session,
files}` × host, the arbiter's `holder-send-ask.ts`), and the arbiter attaches
each file the program holds at list time (`holderSources`: the file, the
copy it reached the program through, where it may go now, whether it is in
the way, and whether an *Always* can change its rule, or why not).

- **The card** (family `send`, `describeAsk` `holderAsk`): "Claude Code's
  program wants to send data from `~/ws/app/.env` and
  `~/data/customers.csv` to `hooks.slack.com`"; *Why it stopped* names the
  files in the way; *What the AI has now*: its program has not sent
  anything; the third cell is "What each answer does". On Approvals, under
  the sentence, *What the program holds* lists each file with "may go to:
  `api.stripe.com`, `*.amazonaws.com`" or "may go nowhere", "Not to this place."
  on each file in the way, and the line "The send goes once every file may
  go to `hooks.slack.com`. Still in the way: `~/data/customers.csv`." once some
  file may go and some may not (`holderSourceWords`, `holderLeftWords`,
  `HomeAsk.sources` / `sourcesLeft`). A copy reads "(copied into
  `~/out/copy.txt`)" beside the file it came from. Each file, copy and host
  is code, kept whole when short, as the card's cells name them (the parts
  `nameParts`, `mayGoParts` and `sourcesLeftParts`, 2026-10-16, §4.25u
  *Approvals names things whole*). Home's short card has no list; its link
  opens the card on Approvals.
- **The answers.** **Allow once** (`approve-once`) and **Block** as on every
  card; **Allow this session** is the row's standing verdict (`approve`),
  offered only when the row names its session (the arbiter keeps an Always
  on a row with none as once). There is no *Always allow* for every file:
  each file in the way has its own button, "Always: add hooks.slack.com to
  .env", `POST /api/egress/approvals/<id>/always-source {path}`
  (`approval-routes.ts alwaysSource`): the arbiter's `holderSourceBinding`
  names the edit (that file's rule gains the host, nothing else), and the
  route applies it as the Rules page applies a loosening (`applyAsHuman`:
  previewed with exactly that rule's relaxation expected, refused 409 if the
  preview names any other, proposed and approved on the admin channel).
  The arbiter plans the edit from its own read, the file's level and hosts
  carried over, and names what it read (`basedOn`: the file's rule and the
  rule that decides its label now, at their versions in that read;
  policy-surface.md §8.4.6): the route proposes with them, so a change to
  either landing between the plan and the write is refused, 409 `stale`
  ("This file's rule was changed somewhere else just now, so nothing was
  changed. Press Always again to add this place to the rule as it is
  now."), nothing written (2026-10-18). The
  answer says "Done: ~/ws/app/.env may go there now. Still in the way:
  ~/data/customers.csv." and the card stays; after the last file, "every
  file may go there now, so the program's next send goes" and the card is
  gone (the arbiter retires it: the law answers it). A file whose rule
  covers a whole folder with readers, a rule still kept on the Rules page,
  or a copy whose source is no longer secret shows why it has no button
  ("Change it under Rules."). The inspector's card offers the same three
  answers ("Allow this session" in place of *Always allow*) and no per-file
  buttons.
- **Answered earlier / Rules › Your answers** read "a program in one session
  sending data from <files>" (`holderAnswerWords`); an *Always* is a rule
  change, listed under Rule changes with Undo, never an answer on the row.

Security: an *Always* widens exactly the file it names (the arbiter's
preview check and the route's `expected` both refuse anything else), never
a verdict that would outlive a binding the human later removes; a send with
a file still in the way stays refused. The words carry paths and hosts,
never a value. Text at 12px or more, and the list wraps at phone width
(`.ask-source` wraps, a long path breaks anywhere). Tests: dashboard
`holder-send-asks.test.ts`, `home-js-holder-send.test.ts`,
`always-source-route.test.ts`; stack
`tests/stack/approval-always-per-source.test.ts`.

**Approvals** (`#approvals-area`). "Waiting for your answer" (with the
count) and "Answered earlier", the product's headings. Each waiting card is
the product's card: the sentence; when, absolute and relative, and "asked
N times"; the three cells *Why it stopped* / *What the AI has now* / *If
you click Allow once or Always allow* (*What each answer does* for a held
message); the buttons Allow once · Always allow · Block, Block the primary
one as on the product's card; "Always allow from <host>" (the rule-shaped
answer, policy-surface.md §2.5) after them where offered. Under it a **developer line**: the
gate (`askOrigin`: file path gate, egress gate, exec gate, the file guard
for a program's read or a file that runs later, the prompt filter; its
words name it, so no label goes before them: "egress gate", never "gate
egress gate", 2026-10-12) and the
rule where exactly one rule asks (`exec:tainted-program-text`,
`exec:escalation-approval`), the queue key in mono (a binary's hash shown
as `#…`), the target, the ask id, the newest session that asked (its tail,
all of them in the tooltip) and **Open in session →**:
`/dev/sessions/<session>?ask=<id>`. A plain click opens the session on its
own page (`mdu:select-session`), and the session page marks the moment
(§4.35, as the product's agent page does, §4.25h). The queue row records its
key and the gate's reason, not the rule id (that is on the trace's decision
event, behind the link), so the line names the rule only where the key
implies it. "Answered earlier" is a table: When · What was asked (the
sentence, and under it the ask id, the key, the newest session that asked
and **Open in session →**, the waiting card's link, egress.js
`sessionFields`) · Your answer (Always allow, Allow once unused / used,
Block) · Gate · the change button. **An answer links where it was asked**
(2026-10-08): until then the row kept only the ask id and the key, so an
answered ask had no way back to its moment, the gap the product's
Approvals rows closed the same day (§4.25 Approvals). A row the arbiter
recorded with no session says "no session recorded", as the card does.
The pending-ask badge in the top bar is unchanged. When the protection
service has not answered once (egress.js `renderStale` with nothing
cached), both cards say so: "not connected to the protection service —
cannot check for waiting questions" and "… — cannot read your earlier
answers". Neither keeps its
"checking…" placeholder for as long as the page is open. The product's
Answered earlier does the same (§4.25, *Empty states*).

**Rules** (`#rules-area`). A sticky sub-menu beside the sections, each with
a count where one means something: **Protection level** (the running level)
· **Your answers** ("N waiting", else how many you answered) · **Your
rules** · **Built-in rules** (the rule count) · **Prompt filters** ("N on")
· **Secrets** (the confined files) · **Audit trail** · **Test a flow**. The
four panels keep their ids (all `data-pages="rules"`), inside the area's
`.sub-body`; Test a flow and Audit trail are their own panels
(`#rules-test-panel`, `#rules-audit-panel`), following the menu's order.
dev/js/sub-menus.js: a plain click scrolls the section on screen, marks its
entry (`aria-current="location"`) and writes `#<key>` (replaceState: a place
on the page, not a history step; the path and `?session=` kept); a modified
click follows the href (`rules#built-in`, relative to `/dev/`); a `#<key>`
in the URL scrolls its section on load and on a page change, and again
600 ms later for the modules' late paint, unless the person went to another
entry or page in between (until 2026-10-14 that second try took a quick
click back to the `#<key>`'s section), or moved the page themselves (see
*The second try leaves the person's scroll* below); the entry of the
section at the top is marked as the page scrolls; a menu on a page not
shown does nothing.
A section near the end of the page cannot reach the top, because the page
ends first. So the entry the person went to last keeps the mark at the
page's end, while its section is below the one at the top. That entry is
the one clicked, the one a `#<key>` named, or the one a jump of the page's
own showed. Those jumps are the Protection block's *→ secret files*, *→ your
answers · N* and *→ audit trail*, and egress.js's *secret releases →
Secrets* and *who changed what → Audit trail*. Each says which section it
showed, after its scroll, with render-helpers.js `sectionShown` (the
`mdu:section-shown` event), and sub-menus.js writes that section's `#<key>`
as a click does. A page change forgets it. Scrolling by hand marks the
section at the top, as before, and leaves the address as it is. Until
2026-10-14 the click's own scroll handed the mark to the section at the top.
In Chromium at 1280×800, Audit trail and Test a flow marked Secrets, and
Settings' last four entries marked Sandbox: 6 of 14 entries, at 390, 1280
and 1920 px wide alike. **The address keeps the section.** app.js
`reflectRouteInUrl` keeps the `#<key>` while the page stays: the session
picked after load (`?session=`), a module's jump to the page it is on, an old name of the page (`/dev/policy#audit` →
`/dev/rules?session=<id>#audit`). Another page or sub-page drops it, since a
section belongs to its page, and Back returns to it. So a reload, a copied
address, a bookmark or Back opens the section. Until 2026-10-14 the session
picked after load dropped the `#<key>` (`/dev/rules#audit` became
`/dev/rules?session=<id>`), so all of these opened the page at its top, and
the page's own jumps left the address naming the section clicked before
them. *Not covered:* the status line's jump to Rules › Protection level
writes no `#level`. From another page, the page change's own `#<key>` follow
would cut its scroll short; on Rules, the address keeps the section it
named. The counts are written by the module that owns each one
(render-helpers.js `setSubCount`, or a local twin in the import-free
control.js, secrets.js and prompt-filters.js, which their tests eval as is).
Sub-paths (`/dev/rules/built-in`) were not taken: every Rules panel would
have to declare every sub-view in its `data-pages`, and one scroll with
anchors does the job.

**The second try leaves the person's scroll (2026-10-15).** A `#<key>`'s
second try, 600 ms after the first, is for the modules' late paint. In
Chromium at 1280×800, `rules#secrets` first landed Secrets at 1268 px,
and the paint then put it at 3476. The try was skipped only when the
person went to another entry or page. A person who scrolled by hand in
those 600 ms was pulled back. In Chromium, a wheel up within 200 ms of
the jump put Prompt filters at the top (2742 px), and 1.2 s later the page
was back at Secrets (3476 px). This happened in 2 of 3 loads; in the other
the wheel came after the 600 ms.

The page's `scroll` events cannot tell the person's scroll from a jump or
a late paint, and Chromium's scroll anchoring moves the page too. So
sub-menus.js counts the person's own input: a `wheel`, a `pointerdown` (a
touch, a click, the scrollbar) or a `keydown`, on the window, captured,
passive. The second try runs only if none came since the first. Without
input, it lands the section where the late paint put it, as before. The
test model's scroll by hand (`laid-out.ts` `hand`) now starts with a
`wheel`, as a person's does.

CI found the race. Run on a loaded guest, `inspector-sub-menu-row.test.ts`
R4 opens `rules#secrets` and scrolls by hand through five sections. Its
loop outlasted the 600 ms, and the page jumped back to Secrets ("3260 !==
18"; post-merge master pipeline #10756, which passed on a retry). On a
fast machine the loop ended first, so R4 never saw it there.

*Not covered:* a scrollbar drag in a browser that sends no `pointerdown`
for it, and a script's own scroll, are not the person's input.

- **Built-in rules fold by gate**, every gate closed by default. Each
  header: the gate in plain words, its count and what it decides (egress.js
  `GATE_WORDS`: File path gate · which paths the agent's file tools may
  open; Egress gate · where a masked value (`$MDU:*` symbol) may be sent;
  Exec gate · where a command runs, and commands that use a masked value;
  Session watermark · what a session may send after it read a secret; When
  Mandu is unreachable · interceptors fail closed), the arbiter's gate title
  and id in its tooltip, the arbiter's evaluation caption inside. A gate the
  arbiter adds later shows its arbiter title. Rows keep id, outcome, hits,
  source and activity. A trace chip (`mdu:show-ruleref`) or a Test-a-flow
  "Show the rule" opens the gate that holds the row; the open gates are
  remembered across the 3-second repaints. "What gets masked on the way in"
  (the data-trust spec) sits at the foot of Built-in rules.
- **The developer detail stays, tighter**: the policy header keeps the law
  source, **View the handling prompt**, the policy-file line, **This
  session only** and the posture chips; the "checked in order" sentence
  reads "Checked in order: your answers (an exact item) → your rules
  (policy.yaml; Block beats Allow, however specific) → built-in rules, top
  to bottom, first match wins. Nothing matches → the fail-closed default."
  The status filters read waiting · allowed · blocked; Test a flow names the
  deciding layer the same way ("your rules", "one of your answers").
- **The Protection block's jumps**: "→ secret files", "→ your answers · N"
  and "→ audit trail" (the Audit trail section shows the `arbiter-admin`
  stream on this page). The cross-links line: "secret releases → Secrets",
  "who changed what → Audit trail".
- **Typing.** egress.js repaints the whole panel on its 3 s poll, the
  forms with it. ＋ Add a rule, the Lists editor and Test a flow keep what
  was typed (`E.addRule`, `E.listDrafts`, `E.newList`, `E.testFlow`,
  written on each `input` and `change`) and draw it again on every
  repaint. While a text field or a select of one of those forms has the
  focus, the poll leaves the panel as it is (`typing()`), so the caret and
  an input method's composition stay. The rest still updates: the
  Approvals cards, the badge and the posture. A focused checkbox or button
  holds nothing, so a status filter repaints at once; the control drawn at
  its place gets the focus back (§4.32 *A repaint keeps the focus*). The panel's own
  successful write (Add rule, a list change) repaints at once
  (`refresh(true)`), and an added rule's form folds and empties. A panel
  held while the arbiter is unreachable keeps one stale note. Until
  2026-10-09 every poll emptied the forms and took the focus, so a rule
  had to be typed and sent within 3 s.
- **A write's answer stays.** A question's row (the Approvals card,
  Answered earlier, Rules › Your answers) keeps the answer to its last
  button (`E.rowAnswers`, by question id, so each place that shows the
  question shows it). It stays while the question's status stays, until
  the next button on it. Add a rule, Lists and Test a flow keep their
  answer until their next try (`E.addRuleAnswer`, `E.listsAnswer`,
  `E.testFlowAnswer`). Until 2026-10-09 the next poll erased it, so a
  refused Block read as a click that did nothing.
- **A form keeps its answer and the focus** (since 2026-10-14). `typing()`
  holds no repaint for a button, so the 3 s poll, or the session app.js
  loads after the page (`mdu:rulerefs-updated`), may draw ＋ Add a rule,
  the Lists editor or Test a flow again while its request is out. The
  answer, or the refusal's words, goes to the form drawn now (each draw
  keeps its line and button in `E.addRuleView`, `E.listsView`,
  `E.testFlowView`; egress.js `drawnNow`), as a row's answer does
  (`keepRowAnswer`). *Add rule* and *Test* go off while their request is
  out, and the one a repaint draws meanwhile stays off
  (`E.addRuleOut`, `E.testFlowOut`), so a second rule is not sent while
  the first is out. A browser drops the focus of a button turned off to
  `<body>`. Once the answer is drawn, the button drawn now gets it back
  (`formFocusBack`), as on the product page (§4.25b): only if it had the
  focus at the press and the focus fell, so a field the person moved to
  keeps it, and a press that gave the button no focus moves none. The
  refusal's line describes the button (`aria-describedby`); Test's answer
  box describes Test when there is no refusal. An added rule folds the
  form, and its *＋ Add a rule* takes the focus instead.

  Until 2026-10-14 the answer went to the form the repaint replaced: in a
  browser it showed only at the next poll, and in the stack suite, where
  no poll runs, never. `tests/stack/inspector-rules-form-names.test.ts`
  waited out its 20 s for Test a flow's probe line in CI pipelines 10728,
  10742 and 10743, once the session's load came while its test was out
  (Test a flow was fixed first, the same day). The focus stayed on
  `<body>` after every *Add rule* and *Test* (measured in a headless
  Chromium at 1280×800, signed in and out, with and without a repaint).
- **The Lists editor says its answer to the button pressed** (since
  2026-10-15). The editor has one answer line, after *New list*, and many
  buttons: each host's ✕, each list's ＋ and 🗑, and *New list*. Each is
  drawn with a key for what it acts on (`keyed`: remove a host from a
  list, add to a list, delete a list, a new list), and the key of the one
  pressed is kept (`E.listsPressed`).
  - **A refusal** (the server's, or *New list*'s own name check) describes
    the button pressed, as drawn now, and no other
    (`aria-describedby="lists-answer"`). Each repaint draws it described
    again while the line says something. The next change hides the line
    and clears the description. A Lists button is never turned off, so it
    keeps the focus through a repaint (§4.32 *A repaint keeps the focus*).
  - **A host's chip is keyed by its host** (`data-member`). Every ✕ reads
    "✕" (the host is in its `aria-label`), and `refocus` compares words,
    so the focus of a removed host's ✕ went on to the next host's ✕,
    where a second Enter removed that host too. Keyed, a ✕ is found only
    for its own host.
  - **A change that worked** draws the panel again (`refresh(true)`). If
    the button pressed had the focus and the focus then fell (a host's ✕,
    a list's 🗑: the control is gone), `focusAfterListChange` gives it to
    the list's name (`@docs`, `tabindex="-1"`, no Tab stop) while the list
    is drawn, else to the editor's summary, *Lists (N)*. It never gives the
    focus to another ✕ or 🗑. ＋ and *New list* are drawn again with the
    same words and keep the focus. A focus the person moved meanwhile
    stays, and a press that gave the button no focus moves none. The
    browser's ring shows on the name after a keyboard press. No CSS
    changed.

  Until 2026-10-15 the line described none of the buttons, so a screen
  reader at a refused 🗑 heard nothing. A removed host's ✕ handed the
  focus to the next host's ✕, and a deleted list's 🗑 or the last host's
  ✕ left it on `<body>` (measured in jsdom on master,
  `egress-js-lists-answer-focus.test.ts`). Presentation only: the
  requests are sent as before.
- **Signed out.** Every answer, rule, list change and test POSTs, and a POST
  needs the admin session (§6.x), as does the policy file's read. Signed out
  the server answers 403 `ADMIN_SESSION_REQUIRED`, which is written for a
  developer. Each place says it in the inspector's words, the command as
  code: "Sign in to answer this question: run `mandu dashboard` in your own
  terminal and open the sign-in link it prints." The verb is the control's:
  - Allow once, Always allow, Block and a held message's answers: "answer
    this question";
  - Answered earlier's Block instead and Allow instead: "change your answer";
  - Add rule and "Always allow from …": "add a rule";
  - Add rule for a website: "trust a website"; for a connection: "allow
    connecting";
  - the Lists editor: "change a list";
  - Test a flow: "test a flow".

  egress.js matches the refusal on its text (`ADMIN_REFUSAL`), as
  control.js does; any other refusal keeps the server's words. For a
  website or a connection, the typed TRUST or ALLOW still comes first: the
  page learns the answer only by asking. Until 2026-10-09 each place
  printed the server's text whole, and the next poll erased it.
- **A write the arbiter finds invalid** (since 2026-10-15). The arbiter
  checks every policy write before it writes anything
  (`PolicyDocumentStore.validated`). It refuses one that would leave the
  file invalid with the words it uses at start-up (`PolicyFileError`):
  "policy file <path> is invalid — the arbiter refuses to start rather
  than run a different law than the one on disk:", then one "  - <problem>"
  line each. The server passes them on as "arbiter: …", with 422. On a
  write nothing stops and the file is unchanged, so egress.js says that
  in its own words (`errorText`; `INVALID_POLICY` matches the text, as
  `ADMIN_REFUSAL` does):
  - **any such write** (Add a rule, "Always allow from …", a list's ＋,
    ✕ or *New list*): "Not saved: the change would leave policy.yaml
    invalid, so it is unchanged:", then the arbiter's problems as it wrote
    them, one a line. The file is named by its own name.
  - **a list's 🗑, when every problem is a place that still cites the
    list** (`citedListWords`): "Not deleted: user_rules[0].to.host still
    uses @registries. Change or remove it first; policy.yaml is
    unchanged.", each place the arbiter named ("… and … still use …").
    A 🗑 refused for anything else gets the general words.

  Every other refusal keeps the server's words, and so does a text that
  does not match: the panel falls back to the arbiter's own sentence,
  never to none. `tests/stack/inspector-invalid-policy-words.test.ts`
  pins the match to the real arbiter's text. Until 2026-10-15 the panel
  printed it whole, so a refused 🗑 said that the arbiter refuses to
  start, with what cites the list at the end. Presentation only: the
  requests, the server and the arbiter are unchanged. Rewording
  `PolicyFileError` for a write in the arbiter itself would serve every
  client, and is left to the arbiter's owners.
- **No answer.** With the dashboard server gone, each of these places says
  "the dashboard server did not answer — reload this page once it is
  running again" instead, kept across the poll the same way; a row's ⓘ, the
  handling prompt and the Audit trail say what they could not read, then
  the sentence (§4.8 *No answer to a write in Approvals, Rules, Secrets and
  Protection*). Until 2026-10-10 they said "request failed" or blamed the
  arbiter.

**Settings** (`#settings-area`). The same sub-menu: **Services** ("N of 5
running", the test arbiter counted; none when the control plane is off) ·
**Sandbox** ("10 of 11") · **Protection axes** · **Dashboard server** ·
**Appearance** · **Docs & slides**; `/dev/settings#<key>`. Services is a
compact list, one row per service: dot, name, state, pid / port, its action
(Start, or Stop · Restart; Replace on a verified adopted daemon), the logs
fold (CSS only; control.js's rows, ids and buttons are unchanged). Each
**sandbox switch is one line**:
the switch, its plain sentence, its env key in mono on the right; "off by
default" on an opt-in switch's line. The next-launch facts ("next launch: on
(key absent — the default) · kernel-level, degrades where the kernel lacks
it", the who/when) are in the row's tooltip and shown inline only when the
value is not the default: set in the file, dropped by no-kernel, or changed
by someone. The config path is said once, in the panel's hint
(`#sandbox-config-path`). Every switch keeps its `data-key`, its typed-OFF
gate and its one-key POST.

**The phone.** Every table of the three pages sits in its own
`.table-scroll` box (`overflow-x: auto`; render-helpers.js `scrollBox`,
twins in secrets.js and prompt-filters.js `table()`), and under 761px a
table keeps a 560px minimum width there, so it scrolls in its box instead
of crushing a column to a letter per line; the page body never scrolls
sideways (at 390px the scroll width is 390 on Approvals, Rules and
Settings). Each box is a `group` named by its table's heading, since a box
that scrolls is a Tab stop of its own (§4.32 *A table's box says what it
holds*). The sub-menu becomes one sticky row that scrolls sideways under
the top bar, and the card's three cells stack. The window keeps the row's
room as it keeps the bar's, so a section an entry shows lands below the
row, not behind it, and is the one marked (since 2026-10-14; §4.32 *The
top bar never hides the focus*). **The row shows the entry it marks**
(since 2026-10-14). Its scrollbar is hidden, and at 390px Rules' row is
895px long in a 370px box, which shows Protection level and Your answers;
Settings' is 647px long. Until then nothing scrolled the row. In
headless Chromium at 390×844, the page scrolled by hand to Built-in rules,
Prompt filters or Secrets marked an entry out of sight (Your rules cut at
the edge), as did Rules opened at `#audit`, `#secrets`, `#prompt-filters`
or `#built-in` and Settings at `#docs` or `#appearance`; at 760px
`#audit` was cut. Now, whenever the mark moves (the spy, a click, a
`#<key>`, a jump of the page's own) and when the menu's size changes (a
window narrowed to a phone's width), sub-menus.js `showEntry` scrolls the
row, never the page, as the step rail does its list (§4.33, app.js
`revealRailRow`): an entry out of sight comes to the middle, as near as
the row's ends allow; one cut at an edge just comes in whole; one in sight
stays put. A row the person swiped stays put until the mark moves, and a
menu beside the sections, which does not scroll, never moves. Not
`scrollIntoView`: the row sits in the room the window keeps free above
(html `scroll-padding-top`), so it would scroll the page too. The row
jumps, with no smooth scroll, as the rail does. With smooth motion, the
mark passes the sections between during a click's own scroll, and the
row follows it to the entry clicked. After the fix, in Chromium every
entry marked was whole in the row at 390 and 760px, and at 1280px nothing
changed.

**Tests.** `test/unit/ui/dev-product-words.test.ts`: the inspector's
answers equal the product's labels, order and verbs (parsed from
public/js/home.js), the server's action labels and reversals agree, the
shared headings and cell labels, no retired word ("locked files",
"protected file", "Approve once", "standing decisions", "If you allow it",
"⚖ Policy", "History", "Protection machinery", "Revoke") in the three
pages' markup or scripts and no second copy of the sentence wording, the
two sub-menus' sections in order with a section each, sub-menus.js in a

second try leaving a later click and a page moved by a wheel, a key or a
press, and still landing its section after a late paint, scrolling by hand
unchanged, a page change forgetting), and the CSS contract
(`.table-scroll`, every egress.js table wrapped, the phone rules).
`egress-js-approvals.test.ts` (the card, every button's request: path

Open in session; the sweep over the product words, the developer line
excepted), `egress-js-document.test.ts` (Answered earlier as a table, the

`egress-js-panel.test.ts` (gate folds closed by default, their headers,
