### 4.35 The Drills and Tests pages

**Why.** After §4.33 a drill session still showed its recording panel above
the session tabs, with every check's full evidence inline under the players
(about thirty rows for a replay drill), so the trace sat far below the fold.
The header was a session's (events, turns, a long `<run>/<key>` id), the
verdict and tallies sat inside the panel, and the run's setup lines came
first. The sidebar named each replay run "replay · local · eed3abc6" and
each row by its long title over a strip of seven badges. On Tests, a test
store whose arbiter was down (`/api/sessions` answers 503 `{unreachable:
true, tenant: "test", error}`, §6.y) read "no sessions (set
MANDU_EVENTS_DIR)".

**The Drills list** (`#sidebar`, app.js `drillGroups`, `drillGroupHtml`,
`replayRow`, `liveDrillRow`).

- **The tools** (since 2026-10-16, the Tests page's layout): **▶ Run
  drills** (the primary button) the column's width, then a left sub-menu
  with the Tests menu's look: **Drill sessions** (with the count of the
  kind shown), **Matrix**, **Agents**, **Comparison** (since 2026-10-17,
  §4.32b), **Videos** (since 2026-10-18: the promo film's takes). Drill sessions is the list below,
  with **Replay | Live** over it (the list's full width in two halves) and
  the search. Matrix, Agents, Comparison and Videos are tool pages in the main column, and on
  them the menu stands alone: no list, no search, no Replay | Live. (Until
  then a segmented Runs | Matrix | Agents sat beside ▶ Run drills, which
  wrapped in a narrow column, and the list stayed beside Matrix and Agents:
  a click on one of its rows left the tool for the session, a jump the
  person read as the menu switching back to Runs by itself. A matrix cell
  is still the way from a drill to its session.)
- **One group per run**, named for what it was: a CI pipeline's run
  "Pipeline gl-8398" (run ids are `gl-<pipeline>-<job>`; a retried job's run
  is a second group of the same name, told apart by its time, its job in
  the tooltip), "Local run", or "Live run"; then the day and time it started
  ("Today 11:06"), its failures if any (`1✗`) and its session count. The
  tooltip names the run id, its counts, and the commit, ref and source (the
  server's own title for a live run). Newest first by start, whatever order
  the server sent; the newest is open by default and the older folded (a
  fold the person makes sticks, `mandu.batchFold`, as on Sessions).
- **The shared row** (§4.33): a replay row's name is short, drill · lane
  ("fidelity-echo · inline"; the drill alone when it has no lane), over its
  verdict mark (`pass`, `fail`, `warn`, `timeout`, as a word), the drill's
  short index, the agent badge, the terminal size, the check category that
  fell short ("utility 2/3") and how long it took ("9s"); the full title,
  script and engine are its tooltip. A live row keeps its scenario's title,
  over the verdict mark, the drill's short index, the agent, `record lost`
  where it applies and its duration. The mark, the index and the agent sit
  in the same places on both kinds of row, so the two lists read alike. The
  search matches the short name, the full title, the id, and the short
  index exactly (`u7` finds U7, not U70).
- **Every row leads with a verdict mark** (2026-10-03, app.js
  `drillRowMark`). A live row's is its own scenario's verdict
  (`watch.verdict` when the run names the session's scenario, so a WARN
  reads `warn`), else what the session's events graded (`checksVerdict`,
  through the row's status), else a muted, dashed **`?`** whose tooltip
  says why none can be known: the run's record is not in the live drill
  store (its verdicts were lost with it), the run is still writing it
  elsewhere, or the row is a shared session's that ran several scenarios.
  A verdict is never guessed. A replay row always has its record's verdict;
  the same rule covers it.
- **The short index** (2026-10-03, `drill-shorts.ts`; test-reorganization.md
  §6.1.1). Every catalog drill has one (since 2026-10-16 `util-c5`, `con-i2`,
  `int-i11w`: its area's word, a hyphen, its axis letter, `c` or `i` for a
  frozen drill, and a number never changed or reused; spelled `UCon-5`,
  `CInt-2`, `IInt-11w` for a few hours that day, a spelling the key lookup
  still translates), shown as the same `.s-scn`
  badge on its replay and its live rows, so the two lists line up row by
  row. The server joins it from the catalog index the drill matrix reads
  (`drills.json`, `readCatalog`, cached per file
  identity), so a record written before the index existed is badged too: a
  replay row by its record's drill (`replay.short`), a live row by the
  scenario key it ran (`drillShort`: the run's record, else the launch's
  `batchMember`, else the session id's key slug; a demo side's session,
  `demo-<stamp>-demo-c1-mandu-<drill id>`, by the index its run id leads
  with, the side as the variant tail). A key is a drill id
  (`util-reasoning@sonnet#2`, the variant tail kept on the badge), a short
  index in any case, or an older index, read through the drill's `was`
  (every older index it had: `S6` and `U30` → `util-npm-pack-dry-run`,
  util-c17; `U7` → util-c5); a retired number (`U11`) names no drill and
  keeps the raw key badge. A `drills.json` from before 2026-10-16 (an index
  of the 2026-10-03 form, `was` one string) still reads. The
  tooltip is the catalog id and title, the old key when one was mapped,
  and, for a key read only off the session id, "inferred", the badge dotted.
  No source checkout (an installed bundle): no join, the keys as recorded.
  The rows carry 19 more bytes each at most (`"short":"int-i11w"`), inside the
  §4.30 budget. The Run drills dialog's scenario list, the local replay
  run's drill picker and the drill matrix's rows (`MatrixRow.short`, §4.29)
  lead with the same index; the matrix's search also matches it exactly.

**A drill session's header** (app.js `paintHeadFacts`). drills.js and
replay.js publish what they know about the drill shown (`mdu:drill-head`
{sessionId, kind, agent, agentVersion, commit, startedAt, durationS, setting,
model, rerun, verdict, tally, counts}; kept per session, so a late answer for
another session changes nothing; `{clear: kind}` when that module shows
nothing). The facts line then reads **"Replay drill · Mandu beside the plain
agent"** (or **"Live drill · <setting>"**) · agent + version (the record's,
else the session's, as the session header reads it) · commit ·
start · duration, with **Copy re-run command** (the command in its tooltip)
and **Copy id** (the long id itself is under Setup). Under it the **verdict
chips**: PASS / FAIL / WARN / TIMEOUT, then Security n/m, Utility n/m,
Fidelity n/m (a category that fell short is red). The one-line summary and
the Secrets-mode line (untrusted text is NOT masked) stay under them.

**The drill strip** (`#session-tabs`, tabs.js, pages.js `DRILL_TABS`):
**Recording & checks** · **Trace** · **Secrets** · **Files** · **Setup**.
One tablist holds both strips; app.js hides the other strip's tabs
(`hidden`), and tabs.js leaves a hidden tab out of the arrows. The drill
strip shows on the Drills page and for a drill session listed elsewhere (the
Tests page lists the whole test store, drills included). Recording & checks
is the default, so `?tab=` is never written for it (pages.js
`parseSessionTab(q, 'drill')`, `withSessionTab(href, tab, 'drill')`); the
choice persists per page as on Sessions (`mandu.sessionTab.drills`). Counts:
the checks passed / total, the trace's steps, the masked values (or `none`),
the run's files.

Secrets is the Sessions page's own tab (§4.33: Masked values,
`#symtable-panel`, and Where each went, `#lineage-fold`), not a second one:
app.js paints both panels from the session's view-model on every render
(`renderSymbolTable`, `renderLineagePanel`), and `?tab=secrets` links to it.
Showing it fetches nothing: the symbols ride the `/api/events` answer the
trace already loaded, so no route grows (the §4.30 payload budgets are
untouched). The drill strip has no Checks: a drill's checks are its
Recording & checks.

| Tab | Replay drill (replay.js) | Live drill (drills.js) |
|---|---|---|
| Recording & checks | the two players on one clock and the turn chips (each a row of its own with its prompt whole and wrapped; the scrubber's markers keep a 60-character excerpt), then **the checks table**: check · kind · plain · Mandu · expected · at, security first; a row (click, Enter or Space) unfolds its evidence row (the reason, each side's own reason, "gate not reached on the plain run") and seeks both recordings to the moment it was decided; the At cell's seek alone does not unfold. A side's result is coloured by whether it is the one expected of it, so the control's expected FAIL is no alarm | above the player, **the scenario at a glance**: what it checks (the catalog's "watch for") and the rule it needs set by hand; the player (on a recording shared by several scenarios, a chip per scenario; on a scenario's own, no chips: its turns are the checks table's rows, and a scenario with no turn yet says so here); then **the key files**: the prepared workspace's files named in a prompt or labelled (above public, or public by a rule), the prompt's first, then the strictest; a switch shows only those a prompt names (the default) or all of them; each with its label, where it may be sent, what decided and its content (cut at 400 characters, a click shows it all; the rest stay in the Files tab); then **the checks table**, the page's one per-turn view: a row per catalog step holding EVERY chapter turn of the step in recording order, its prompt and each scripted reply ("Turn 1 · reply"), each with the session's level once it was over (*low* or *HIGH · <level>*, marked where it was raised), its two recording jumps (⏵ prompt, ⏸ answer, on the player's clock), TIMEOUT when it never completed, and labelled blocks that read apart: what was typed (Prompt, or Scripted reply) whole and wrapped, **Terminal** (what the screen showed in the turn), a shut fold with what the model wrote along the way, and the agent's answer, whole up to 1000 characters and cut there with a "show all"; then what was auto-answered and the screen after the step; over the step's checks (check · kind · result · at); a check row unfolds its reason and shows the recording at the step's answer, its last turn's (its prompt when no answer point is known). A step not graded yet shows its turns and says so; a relaunch is a row of its own with a jump to where it happened. A model run's matrix under it. Record lost: one line, the why folded |
| Trace | app.js's own, from the recorded events | the same |
| Secrets | the Sessions page's tab: the masked values (`$MDU:*` symbols) and where each went, from the recorded events | the same |
| Files | the run's files, one link per line (the record, the event log, both recordings, the screens) and the baseline's key; no dual-view commits (a recorded run has no workspace) | the run's files, the 🌱 prepared workspace (opens, and loads, when the tab shows), then the session's dual-view commits |
| Setup | the drill, lane and mode, the agent, the script and engine, the run, the session id, the start and length, **re-run** (this one drill, §4.28), every replay drill (`scripts/test-all.sh --kind replay-drill`), the baseline and where it came from | the run (status, start), the agent and model, the scenario and its setting, the session line with its tmux attach, the workspace, the hand-made precondition, what to watch for, **re-run** (`cd tests && npm run drills:run -- --ids <id>` with `--target` / `--model`) |

A live drill's record holds each turn's prompt and when it went in, not the answer nor the session's level. Both are read on demand, one per chapter turn (a scripted reply included), when the scenario's panel draws, from the run's own event log (`GET /api/drills/runs/<id>/turns/<chapter>`, an admin read like the run's files), in the turn's window, which opens at its prompt and closes at the next prompt on the same recording (the cast header's `timestamp` puts both on the events' clock). The **answer** is the last reply of the agent's own in the window: a reply that called a tool, and a side call that offered no tools (the session title, a quota probe), are not answers. The text is the symbolized one, as the model wrote it, so a masked value stays a `$MDU:*` token. The **level** is the session's confidentiality high-watermark once the window closed: it starts `public` (*low*) and only rises, each rise an arbiter `session_level` event (the symbol read by name and the session's bindings, never content; 2026-10-15+), whoever caused it, the agent's `declassify_symbol` or a drill's own setup. A run older than that event reads its levels from the declassify tool's replies ("[DECLASSIFIED — this session is now HIGH (<level>)") and says so, since a rise made any other way does not show there. **Along the way** are the agent's other replies in the window, in order (2026-10-17): each one's prose with its tool calls split out as compact `→ Name(args)` lines, symbolized as the model wrote them, at most 40 replies (the rest counted, "N more"), each cut at 2000 characters and 8 tool lines of 240. A run without the log (an older run, or an arbiter work dir outside the run dir) shows no answer, no replies and no level, its recording jumps and screens still.

**What the terminal showed (2026-10-17).** The model's words are not the screen: the screen shows each tool call, the commands' output ("report-bug: upload FAILED (HTTP 403)") and the originals the reply filter put back. The runner keeps a whole-scrollback capture once each step was over (`tmux capture-pane -J -S -`, the report row's `paneFile`, "screen after this turn"); the same route cuts it per chapter turn (`drill-screens.ts`) into the turn's **Terminal** block: from the line where its typed prompt appears (the first 40 characters, matched through the TUI's frame, OpenCode's "┃" gutter or Claude Code's "> ", and across a wrap) to the next turn's prompt. A full-screen agent (OpenCode) draws on the alternate screen, so its capture keeps only the last screen: the turn before the first prompt found gets what the capture kept before it, saying its prompt is not there, and a step none of whose prompts is found shows the whole capture on its last turn, saying so; the model's replies along the way then hold what the screen lost. The launcher's own lines at the top (`mandu: …`, `[mandu-secrets] …`) are kept apart, folded on the scenario's first turn. Each slice loses trailing blanks, a full-screen agent's composer box and status line at its foot and the frame-only lines at its end, and is otherwise verbatim; it shows 40 lines, then a "show all", and keeps at most 2000 lines (the rest counted, the whole capture in the Files tab). Every field lands as text. The screen is the HumanView: it holds originals, a real secret on a baseline side, so it is the inspector's alone, behind the same admin read as the run's files; nothing on the product page reads it.

**One per-turn view (2026-10-17).** Until then a scenario's own recording had a chip per turn and per answer under the player, which repeated the checks table, and the table showed only a step's first turn, so a scripted reply (the runner answering the model's clarifying question, the same step) and its answer were chips only. The chips are gone; the table's step row holds every chapter turn with the chips' jumps, and the scrubber's markers still name every turn, the reply among them ("turn 1 reply · …").

**Turn numbers and relaunches (2026-10-16).** A turn is named by its catalog step everywhere on the page, the scrubber's markers and the checks table alike: a step that types nothing (a relaunch, an edit, a wait) has no turn of its own, so the numbers can skip (`conf-derived-label-next-session` reads turn 1, 2, 4; until 2026-10-16 the chips counted prompts, 1, 2, 3, while the table counted steps, so "turn 3 answer" was the table's Turn 4). A **relaunch** starts the agent again in the same workspace as a new Mandu session (`<scope>-s2`) with its own event log and trace. It is a row of its own in the checks table ("Turn 3 — relaunch", a jump to where the new session started on the recording, and "Open the new session →"; a chip under the player until 2026-10-17), the turn after it is read from the NEW session's log (its answer, and its level, which starts low again; until 2026-10-16 it was looked for in the first session's log and showed none), and the header lists the scenario's sessions with their turns ("Session 1 · turns 1–2", "Session 2 · turn 4"), the shown one marked and the other one click away, on the same tab. Opening the second session shows the same scenario's page. The runner writes each turn's `step` and `scopeId` and each relaunch (`relaunches`: its step, its session and when it started on the cast's clock) into `chapters.json`; for an older run the server fills them in on read (`drill-chapter-steps.ts`): a turn's step from the report row with the same prompt, in order, and no step at all when a turn matches none (a TUI command, a scripted reply: the turns are then numbered in order, never a mix); a relaunch where its session's first event was recorded, its step the one missing between the turns around it.

**A HIGH turn stands out (2026-10-16).** The level chip alone was easy to miss. A turn the session ended HIGH is tinted whole in pink, the `--pink` token, as is its level chip (never red: HIGH is not a failure; first the secret's gold, which read as one more symbol), its turn row and the check rows under it, with a pink bar down the left (a step row holding several chapter turns is HIGH when any of them ended HIGH: the level only rises). The turn that RAISED the level has the thicker bar and a line in its own block saying it in words: "▲ The session went HIGH (any-model) in this turn: it read `$MDU:…` into the model's context. From here on it may send only to example.com; anything else stops and asks you." (or "may send nowhere without your OK" when it is bound nowhere). All of it comes from the same per-turn level facts; a run without them shows none.

**Browser steps (2026-10-19).** A browser drill's turn showed only its prompt: the video showed Chrome, but not what the agent asked of it. Under the prompt of a browser drill (its recording a video), a **Browser steps** block lists what the agent did in Chrome, a row per action: its moment on the video, its kind, and a sentence (`Clicked link "Chat with support" (→ helpnest.localhost:44031/chat/acme-shop)`, `Typed "…" into the "Account email" field (email)`, `Opened http://…`, `Switched to tab DEEC`, `Updated its notes (todo.md)`, `Finished: …` or `Gave up: …`), the model's next goal under its step's first action (`aim: …`), and a tooltip with the element (tag, id, name, type, href, xpath) and the page. A row with a time jumps the video there and plays (the side's own video, or the two sides in one: each side is on its own clock there), and while the video plays the row playing is marked. On a side with Mandu, what the DevTools relay did with a placeholder the agent typed sits under that step (`↳ Chrome: Mandu filled in the real value of $MDU:… on ledgerly.localhost:44031 (Chrome typed it; the model saw only the placeholder)`, or `Mandu refused to fill in … (why): Chrome typed nothing`, a refusal of any reason), so the reader sees what the model asked beside what Chrome got; a relay release or refusal no step typed, and a message it withheld, are rows of their own (`Mandu`, a repeat counted once), and the reads it masked and the commands it blocked are one line above the rows (`Along the way Mandu masked 21 page reads, blocked 15 × Page.captureScreenshot (pixels).`). A `$MDU:*` placeholder is a placeholder chip; a page secret the agent typed is a red `secret: <its name>` chip, its row tinted and tagged SECRET: on the side without Mandu that is the leak the demo shows. The record keeps the value out (the driver writes the secret as its mark, `⟦secret: the card number⟧`), so the page shows which secret, never the value. Every text lands as text. The rows come on demand from `GET /api/drills/runs/<id>/browser-steps/<chapter>` (admin: the agent's typed texts; `src/drill-browser-steps.ts`, `dev/js/drill-browser-steps.js`): the agent's record `agent-<chapter>.json` (drill-runner.md §3.13 "What the agent did": since 2026-10-19 its timed `steps`, each element as JSON; an older record's flat `actions`, each element a Python repr string, parsed best-effort, in order with no time), the session's event log (the relay's `browser_action` events), and the chapter's `castClock` (the video's clock, drill-runner.md §3.13), which puts each wall-clock moment on the video; without one (a run before 2026-10-19, a jev run) a row has its time of day, or its place in order, and the block says so. A run before 2026-10-19 wrote no agent record for a side whose steps held a page secret; the block says that too. A jev run has no agent record: its block holds the relay's rows only.

**Drills › Matrix** keeps its content and takes the page header style (the
session header's title and facts line, `.tool-head`), as do the Tests
sub-pages.

**The Tests page.** The sidebar's sub-menu (Test sessions · Run a suite ·
Coverage · VM matrix · CI) takes the look of the Rules and Settings
sub-menus (§4.34), with a count where one is cheap: the test sessions listed
(or `offline`), Coverage's gaps, the VM matrix's and CI's runs (`master red`
when it is). The tool pages still load only when seen (control.js
`wireSubpages`), so a tool's count appears once its page has been opened. On
the tool pages the sub-menu stands alone: the search and the session list
are on Test sessions only.

- **The store is down.** `/api/sessions` answering 503 `{unreachable: true,
  tenant, error}` sets `S.storeDown`; ONE banner on the page
  (`#store-down-banner`, on every session page and Tests sub-page): "The
  test store's arbiter is not running, so test sessions are unavailable.
  Start test-arbiter under Settings › Services. CI and coverage read the
  recorded runs and still work." (for the live store: "Mandu's arbiter is
  not running, so sessions are unavailable. Start the arbiter under Settings
  › Services."), the server's own words in its tooltip, "Settings ›
  Services" a real link (`/dev/settings#services`; leaving Tests reloads on
  the live store and the hash scrolls to the section). The list says "Test
  sessions are unavailable: …", never "no sessions"; the "Pick a session"
  header and the search hide. The next poll that answers clears it.
- **The status line says the store is offline** (app.js `renderStatusLine`,
  `statusOffline`). The protection level comes from the posture egress.js
  publishes off `/api/policy/panel`, which fails soft (200, `available:
  false`) when the store's arbiter is down, so the line would read only
  "Protection: not known" (§4.32), without saying why. It reads the same
  503 `{unreachable}` the banner does: while `S.storeDown` is set, "● Test
  store: offline · not live" (the live store: "Mandu: offline"; a phone
  keeps "offline"), a grey dot (`data-level="offline"`), the tooltip "The
  test store's arbiter is not running, so its protection level is not
  known. Start test-arbiter under Settings › Services." A posture
  republished meanwhile (egress.js's stale repaint of its last panel) does
  not override it. When the store answers again the level shows and, with
  no stream open, the feed is back to its load state ("live", connecting).
- **CI: a failure outside the tests reads INFRASTRUCTURE** (§4.27, ci.js
  `failureSide`).
- **Each entry's log** (Tests › Run a suite, 2026-10-03; control.js
  `loadRunEntries`, `openRunLog`; `src/test-runs/test-run-logs.ts`). A
  finished run's row, when opened, lists its **Entries** the way a CI run
  does (mark · entry · kind · result · pass · fail · skip · time · log,
  failures first, "Entries (n, m red)"), and an entry's `log` button opens
  that entry's own log under the table. Where the logs are:
  `<results>/<runId>/logs/<entry>.log` in the test-runs results directory
  (§4.29): a test-all.sh run's are run-suites' own, listed in its
  `summary.json`; a **one-entry run's** output is now kept there too, by the
  runner itself (`EntryLogWriter`: created fresh, O_EXCL | O_NOFOLLOW, 0600 in
  0700 directories, both streams, stops at 8 MiB with a marker line). The
  e2e batch (one output for several entries' files), a retired whole-tier
  run, a run from before the logs were kept and a run still going list no
  entries and say why; an entry with no log shows `—`, its tooltip saying
  why.

      GET /api/test/runs/<run>               {runId, basis: summary|entry|none, note?, entries: [{id, kind, result, pass, fail, skip, duration_s, logAvailable}]}
      GET /api/test/runs/<run>/log/<entry>   text/plain: the log's last 1 MiB (X-Mandu-Log-Truncated, X-Mandu-Log-Size)

  **Only the run's own files.** The run must be one the runner knows (its
  history or the run in flight, matched by value), both ids must be ids
  (`ci-runs.ts ID_RE`: no `/`, never `.` or `..`), and the entry must be one
  that run lists with a log: in its valid summary (the CI reader's
  `readLogTail`: schema 1, `run` equal to its directory) or, for a one-entry
  run, the run's own suite id. The file is read by `ci-runs.ts
  readRunLogFile`, the CI page's own reader: the run directory and `logs/`
  must be real directories (lstat), the file is opened O_NOFOLLOW |
  O_NONBLOCK and must be a regular file, so a symlink, a FIFO or an unlisted
  file in the directory is never served; anything else is a 404 that names
  nothing. The answer is the CI log's (`sendLogTail`): `text/plain`,
  nosniff, `default-src 'none'; sandbox`, `no-store`, terminal codes
  stripped, the start cut to the last 1 MiB with a marker. GET only, behind
  the same source-IP gate and Basic auth as every route; off (404) without a
  test runner. It also needs the admin session (the read gate, §6). Signed
  out it answers 403, and the log's place says "Sign in to read this log:
  run `mandu dashboard` …" (§4.26 quotes it), with no log box. Any other
  failure keeps "could not load the log of `<entry>`". `entry-log.js
  fetchLog` returns the status for this. Until 2026-10-09 a 403 read as that
  failure.
  **Small payloads.** No log rides `GET /api/test`: a row fetches its entries
  when it opens, and a log when its button is clicked (a Coverage mark that
  names an entry opens that one; nothing else opens a log by itself). A
  finished run's row is kept as it is across the poll that refreshes the
  running row, so an open log stays open and is not fetched again.
  **Failures easy to find** (`dev/js/entry-log.js`, on this page and on
  CI's): the log is split into plain text and failure blocks, a block being a
  TAP `not ok` line at any depth (a subtest's too) with the lines indented
  under it (its YAML: error, expected, actual, stack; a `# TODO` line is no
  failure). Each block is marked (a red rule and tint), a line above the log
  says "n failures in this log:" with a `✗ k` button per failure (its `not
  ok` line the tooltip; the first 40, then "and n more"), a click scrolling
  to it, and the log opens at its first failure, or at its end when there is
  none ("no `not ok` line in this log; it opens at its end"). Every piece is
  inserted as text.

**`?ask=<askId>` marks the moment** (app.js `markAsk`; the Approvals page's
"Open in session →", on a waiting card and on an Answered earlier row,
§4.34, links `/dev/sessions/<id>?ask=<id>`, and its plain click carries
`ask` on `mdu:select-session`). **`GET
/api/ask-moment?session=&ask=`** (api-routes.ts `apiAskMoment`, read-only)
finds the step the way the product's agent page does (§4.25h, agent-page.ts
`locateAsk`): the queue row by id, then the first event stamped with it
(exact), else for a network ask the first stopped send to its host
(destination), over ALL the session's events, answering `{known, stepId,
match}`; an unknown ask or no arbiter finds nothing, never a guess. The page
then shows Trace, marks the step ("Mandu asked you here", an accent bar;
re-applied after every render), opens its fold and scrolls to it (the step
rail shows its row, §4.33 *The rail follows the selection*), and a note
above the trace says where the reader came from (or that the moment was not
found; every step is still there). A lookup that got no answer (the
server's error, a read of the store that timed out, no server) is not "not
found": the note says it could not be looked up and why (§4.8), and
nothing is marked (until 2026-10-18 every failure read as "not found";
`app-js-page-focus.test.ts`). A step past the loaded window loads the
rest first. The ask rides the URL while its session shows (pages.js
`parseAsk`, `withAsk`) and drops when another session is selected. Once
answered, the marked step's line says the answer in the row's words ("…
(`egr-1`). Your answer: Block.", §4.2f *The answer*, 2026-10-09).

**`?step=<stepId>` opens one step** (2026-10-08; app.js `markStep`; the
product's agent page links a step's own "detailed trace" here, §4.25 *A
step's own link opens that step*). The id is the dual-lane step's own
(`tool:<call id>`, `os:<event id>`), the same in both views, so nothing is
looked up: the page shows Trace, marks the card "The step you opened" (the
ask's accent bar and tag; both marks re-applied after every render), opens
its fold, turns its kind back on if the Show line hid it, selects it and
scrolls to it (`selectEvent`; the step rail shows its row, §4.33), and the
note above the trace says "You came
here from a link to one step of this session. It is marked below." A step
the trace does not have marks nothing and the note says so ("… but that
step is not in its trace. Every step is still here."), never a guess. A
step past the loaded window loads the rest first, and the note waits for
it. pages.js `parseStep` reads any id up to 300 characters with no control
character (an agent picks its call ids), and the page compares it as a
value, never in markup or a selector; the step rides the URL while its
session shows (`withStep`) and drops when another session is selected.

**Smaller pieces.**

- **The per-call ⚖ button opens "Rules · <tool>"** (§4.9): "Input fields:
  what the tool is given" (each argument kept masked, a `$MDU:*` symbol in
  AgentView, or sent as the original), "Output fields: what gets masked on
  the way in", "This call: what was decided"; a tool no built-in rule names
  says "the fail-closed default applies" (that the arbiter is not connected
  is said only when there is no snapshot); a rule-reference chip opens
  "under Rules".
- **The "[TEST] " tab-title prefix**: one writer (`paintDocTitle`) composes
  "[TEST] " (the test store), "(n) " (approvals waiting, §4.20) and the
  page's title, so the badge's repaint never drops the prefix.
- **The button cascade.** The base `.ctl-btn` rule precedes its variants
  (warn, danger, primary) at the same specificity, so a `.ctl-btn-primary`
  keeps its face (+ New run, ▶ Run drills, ▶ Start services and every
  primary button), with no page-scoped patch.
- **Cache tests restamp what they change.** `drill-run-cache.test.ts` turns
  the identity cache's racy window off (§4.30) and expects a file added to
  the run directory to move the directory's identity; inside one coarse
  timestamp tick it does not. The test stamps what it changed with a fresh,
  distinct mtime after each mutation (a same-size rewrite, an added and a
  removed file), as a later write does in production;
  `listing-cache-file.test.ts`'s same-size PASS → FAIL rewrite does the
  same. The production cache (identity-cache.ts, the racy-git rule) is
  unchanged.

**Replay a drill** (2026-10-03; test-reorganization.md §7.4). The ▶ Run
drills dialog's second panel (`#replay-run-panel`, `dev/js/drill-replay-run.js`)
starts a **local replay run of one catalog drill** on one agent: Mandu
beside the plain agent, against the scripted model, **never a live model
call**, and shows its progress and result in place.

- **What runs.** The manifest entry `integration.replay.<agent>` (the
  catalog replay runner, `drill-replay.test.ts`) exactly
  as `tests/suites.mjs` declares it (its argv, cwd and env, never built from
  the request), narrowed to the drill (`test-run-suites.ts
  replayDrillSpec`): its own `MANDU_REPLAY_*` selection is dropped and
  `MANDU_REPLAY_AGENT`, `MANDU_REPLAY_DRILLS=<drill>` (one drill at its
  first size) set, with the record variables run-suites gives a
  replay-drill entry (`replayPlan`): `MANDU_REPLAY_STORE` the dashboard's
  replay store, `MANDU_REPLAY_RUN_ID` the run's own id,
  `MANDU_REPLAY_BASELINES` the path table's `drill-baselines`
  (`defaultDrillBaselinesDir`, or the server's `drillBaselinesDir`), and
  `MANDU_REPLAY_BASELINE=use`. The host's model credentials
  (`LIVE_MODEL_CREDENTIALS`: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`,
  `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` and the others) are removed from its
  environment: the replay profiles set their own dummy keys, so no CLI the
  run drives can reach a live model. Timeout 1200 s (`REPLAY_DRILL_TIMEOUT_S`,
  never above the entry's).
- **No new launcher.** It is the Tests page's `TestRunner`
  (`startReplayDrill`, sharing `start`'s spawn: its own process group, the
  timeout and its report, the log ring, history and shutdown). One run at a
  time with the Tests page: a start while any test run is in progress is a
  429, and the panel says the Tests page holds the runner. The handle
  carries `replay: {drill, agent}`, kept in the history
  (`coerceStoredRun`), and such a run is never an entry's result in Coverage
  (`attributeRun`: one drill is not the entry).
- **Routes.** `POST /api/drills/replay {drill, agent}` (behind the global
  gate, CSRF header and admin session, and its own `requireCsrf`): a body
  with any other field, a malformed id (`isDrillId`) or agent is a 400; the
  drill must be in the drill runner's catalog (`GET /api/drills/scenarios`,
  the runner's `--list-json`) with `replay[agent] === true`, else a 400 with
  the catalog's reason ("no replay script yet", "the drill does not run on
  codex", "replayed by the differential harness"); a catalog that cannot be
  read is a 503. The catalog's `replay` field is completeness.ts
  `catalogReplay`, the replay runner's own selection (a `drill-ws` drill with
  a script on that agent), so the panel and the route offer exactly what the
  runner would run. `GET /api/drills/replay` answers `{available, current,
  busy, recent, log}`: the replay run in progress with its last 40 log
  lines, a Tests page run holding the slot, and the last ten finished replay
  runs. Without a test runner, a drill runner or a replay store both routes
  are 404, and the panel is then one note naming `DASHBOARD_CONTROL=0`
  (§4.8 *With the service controls off*). Progress is the Tests page's own stream (`GET
  /api/test/<runId>/stream`), cancel its `POST /api/test/cancel`.
- **The panel.** Agent and drill pickers (the drills grouped by area, only
  the replayable ones for the agent; a note when there are none or the
  catalog cannot be read), ▶ Replay and ■ Cancel, a status line ("Replaying
  `<drill>` on `<agent>` (run `<id>`, scripted model)…", then "Finished:
  `<state>` · n passed, n failed, n skipped"), the log (text), each test's
  result (a skip with its reason), and one **Open** button per session the
  run recorded (`GET /api/replay/runs/<runId>`), which opens it on the
  Drills page under Replay (`mdu:go-session`); the record shows in the
  Replay list as a Local run named by the run's id. A run in progress when
  the dialog opens is picked up with its log. Signed out, `GET
  /api/drills/replay` answers 403 (the read gate, §6: it carries a run's log
  tail). The status line then says "Sign in to replay a drill: run `mandu
  dashboard` in your own terminal and open the sign-in link it prints.", and
  ▶ Replay stays disabled. Until 2026-10-09 it said "Could not read the
  replay runner's state.", which any other failure still says.
- **Not offered:** the fidelity drills seeded by the differential fixture
  (they replay through the differential harness, `integration.differential`;
  their Setup tab keeps its re-run command), and the frozen drills.

## 5. Reuse vs new — adfi `test/dashboard` → Mandu

The dashboard lifts the reference implementation's (adfi-openclaw)
`test/dashboard` under the reuse policy of
[`CONTRIBUTING.md`](../../../CONTRIBUTING.md): a lifted file carries a
`PROVENANCE` header naming its origin.

| adfi `test/dashboard` piece | Mandu dashboard | Action | Adaptation |
|---|---|---|---|
| `js/utils.js` `esc`, `escSym`, symbol regex | symbol highlighting | **reuse** | `escSym` highlights `$MDU:*`; the regex matches `MDU_SYM_FORMAT.pattern`. |
| `js/utils.js` `resolveSymbols`, `hasResolvableSymbols` | "reveal original" in `DualRepr` | **adapt** | The value comes from the arbiter's privileged `resolve` op; the client `symValueMap` is only a cache. |
| `js/utils.js` `highlightAdfiSystemLines`, `toolIcon`, `localTime`, `tryPrettyJson`, `stripTs` | prompt highlight, icons, timestamps | **reuse** | Runtime-agnostic helpers. |
| `js/render-helpers.js` `renderContentBlock`, `renderJsonTree`, `renderAuditHeadBlock` | call-detail panel | **adapt** | The Before/After layout shows `DualRepr.symbolized` / `.original`. |
| `js/render-helpers.js` approval and untrusted-command renderers | egress approval queue (§4.7) | **reuse** | Maps onto `egress_request` / `egress_decision`. |
| `js/conversation.js` U-LLM inlining, trusted/untrusted outline | U-LLM lane (§4.4), turn rails | **adapt** | U-LLM calls pair by `callId`/`parentId`, not by a timestamp window. |
| `js/conversation.js` `showSymValue`, `showArgPopup` | symbol inspector popups (§4.5) | **reuse** | |
| assertion panel (`conversation.js`, `views.js showAssertionPopup`, `tests/lib/assertions.ts`) | assertion panel (§4.13) | **adapt** | The blocking category is `security`; grading reads the model-facing event trace; results ride an `assertion` `ManduEvent` (plus a greppable `MDUASSERT` line); a pure `toAssertionSummary` projector replaces the browser reducer. |
| `js/conversation.js` timeline merge + sort | trace assembly | **adapt** | One `ManduEvent` stream ordered by `seq` (§3.2) replaces the three-family merge and its 50 ms ordering heuristic. |
| `js/views.js` `renderSymbolTable`, tabs, filters | symbol inspector, lane filters | **adapt** | The trusted/untrusted tabs become the AgentView/HumanView lanes. |
| `js/state.js` state + `api()` | front-end state and fetch | **reuse** | Adds an `eventsBySession` cache and an SSE subscription in place of polling. |
| `dashboard.css` tokens, `.trust-badge`, `.sym-marker`, `.exec-badge` | color coding | **reuse** | Adds a HumanView accent and the `.invariant-violation` flare. |
| `server.ts` static serving, `/api/*`, base path, auth | the HTTP server | **adapt** | Attached to the arbiter (`events` op, SSE `/stream`, §3.1) instead of scanning log directories. |
| `api/routes.ts`, `api/sessions.ts`, `api/types.ts` | REST shape, session list | **adapt** | Sessions keyed by Mandu scope ids. |
| `api/workspace.ts`, `bot-sessions.ts`, `git.ts`, `eval.ts`, `logs.ts` | — | **drop** | OpenClaw log-directory scrapers; Mandu reads the arbiter's event log. |
| `api/trusted-view.ts` | AgentView/HumanView root resolution | **adapt** | Used by the file-system views once the git-worktree views exist. |

**New to Mandu (no reference origin):** the canonical `ManduEvent` schema
(§2) with first-class `view`, `DualRepr` and `invariant`; the arbiter
`emit` / `events` ops and the SSE live feed (§3.1); the invariant banner
(§4.6) and per-event `violatedInvariant` rendering; the three synchronized
lanes with cross-lane causal lines (§4.2); the symbol flow trace (§4.5); and
the per-tool-call policy modal (§4.9: the arbiter `policySnapshot` op,
`GET /api/policy`, `ruleForTool`, `toolUnitPolicy`; tests
`policy-routes.test.ts`, `policy-model.test.ts`, `tool-unit-policy.test.ts`,
`app-js-render.test.ts`).

## 6. Tech approach

- **Stack.** The reference dashboard's TypeScript API plus vanilla JS, no
  build step and no SPA framework: it is the proven artifact, its trust
  color language and symbol rendering are what the core requirement needs,
  and the arbiter is already TypeScript, so the `dashboard/` package shares
  its toolchain and consumes `arbiter/ipc/client.ts`.
- **Attachment to the arbiter.** The server holds an arbiter IPC client,
  serves the static UI, answers `/api/sessions/:id/events` from the `events`
  op and relays append notifications over SSE at `/api/sessions/:id/stream`.
  Interceptors add one `emit(event)` call where they already call
  `symbolize` / `classify`; the event log is the arbiter's.
- **Security posture.** The dashboard reveals symbol → original, so it is a
  privileged surface. It must never be reachable by the monitored agent
  (it runs outside the agent's scope) or by an untrusted network.
  - **How the agent is kept off its port**, path by path (2026-10-05):
    a program the agent runs that connects DIRECTLY (the session's
    `NO_PROXY` names loopback) is refused by the connect guard, whose
    loopback rules admit only the session's own service ports
    (`launcher/src/net-guard.ts` rule 1, `net-supervisor` `guard.rs`), and
    by the Landlock port wrap and the macOS Seatbelt profile where they
    run. A request RELAYED through the session's net-proxy (`curl -x
    "$HTTP_PROXY" http://127.0.0.1:4500/…`, a CONNECT, the TLS-inspected
    leg) is refused by the net-proxy itself, which relays nothing to this
    machine: loopback in every spelling, `0.0.0.0`, `localhost`, this
    machine's own interface addresses, a name that resolves to any of them
    (`interceptors/net-proxy/src/blocked-destinations.ts`, exec-routing.md
    §7.5). Before that rule the relay answered 200 with secret values in
    `/api/events`. Residual: a launch with no guard and no wrap (`off`,
    `--no-net-guard` where bubblewrap has nothing to mount) leaves the
    direct connect open, as it leaves the human-plane socket
    (arbiter-human-plane.md §8). Tests:
    `tests/sandbox/dashboard-via-net-proxy.test.ts` (the real launcher,
    guard and net-proxy against a real dashboard), net-proxy
    `test/{unit,component}/this-machine.test.ts`.
  - **Loopback by default.** `DASHBOARD_HOST` defaults to `127.0.0.1`
    (`server-main.ts`), and every entry point agrees: the launcher's stack
    autostart passes no host, and `mandu dashboard` pins loopback.
  - **A remote deployment is explicit and authenticated.**
    `DASHBOARD_HOST=0.0.0.0` plus `DASHBOARD_ALLOW_HOSTS` plus one
    authenticator: `DASHBOARD_PASSWORD` (a cookie-session login form),
    `DASHBOARD_BASIC_AUTH` (§6.z) or `DASHBOARD_TRUST_FRONT=1` (an
    authenticating reverse proxy). A non-loopback bind with none of the
    three is a start-up refusal (exit 2), not a warning: the allowlist says
    which hosts may connect, not who is at the keyboard.
  - **Fail-closed source-IP allowlist**, checked first in `handle()`, before
    any route (even `/login`): loopback is always admitted; any other peer
    must be listed or gets 403. The shipped list (`DEFAULT_ALLOW_IPS`) is
    empty; `DASHBOARD_ALLOW_HOSTS` (hostnames or IPs, resolved once at
    start-up; a name that does not resolve grants nothing) is the whole
    list. `X-Forwarded-For` is ignored; only the socket's peer address
    counts (`server.ts clientAllowed`).
  - **The Host check (DNS rebinding, 2026-10-05).** Second in `handle()`,
    before any route (even `/login`): the `Host` header must name a
    loopback host (`localhost`, 127.0.0.0/8, `::1`) at the bound port,
    the bound address or one of this host's own interface addresses at
    that port, or a name the operator configured (`DASHBOARD_ALLOW_HOSTS`
    entries, and `DASHBOARD_SERVER_NAMES`, the name a front or tunnel
    forwards; `name` admits any port, `name:port` one). Anything else is
    **421**. Why: a web page the human opens can rebind its own name to
    127.0.0.1 and then read the dashboard as its own origin; the Host
    header is the one thing such a page cannot choose
    (`src/server/read-gate.ts hostAllowed`). A front that forwards its
    public name needs `DASHBOARD_SERVER_NAMES`.
  - **Reads and the admin session (2026-10-05).** Until then loopback
    reads stayed open without a password, on "same-host trust". That
    trust was wrong: a program the agent runs is on the same host, and
    through the session net-proxy's relay it could reach the port, so it
    could read `/api/events` (the raw tool output before masking, the
    reply the human saw, and a deep desymbolize of both), the SSE stream,
    the HumanView files and diffs, the service logs and the run output:
    every secret value Mandu had kept from the AI. Now every GET under
    `/api/` is classified in one table (`src/server/read-gate.ts
    READ_ROUTES`):
    - `open`: metadata only (ids, names, paths, counts, rules, statuses);
      served to anyone the gates above admit;
    - `projection`: `/api/events`, `/api/stream`, `/api/fs`, `/api/git`,
      `/api/home/agent`: served to everyone, their values only with the
      admin session. Without it the route works from the **signed-out
      projection** (`src/view-model/redact.ts`): what the AI saw (each
      payload's `symbolized` form, symbol names, origins and levels,
      decisions, paths, counts), with every `original`, every symbol
      `value`, a seeded file's content and a HumanView file's content
      left out (`withheld: true` where a page draws it), the view-model
      derived from that projection, and no reveal against the arbiter.
      A `symbolize` event's input is the value before masking: signed
      out it becomes the symbol the event's output records, whatever its
      `symbolized` form says (logs written before 2026-10-06 carry the
      value there; until then the signed-out `/api/events` and every route
      built on the projection served the value of every masked item, found
      by nightly run 2026-10-06-0330). A reply-filter `desymbolize` event
      keeps only the placeholders its `symbolized` form names (such logs
      carry the whole terminal frame there, which can hold a tool's raw
      output, §4.2 "Reply-filter cards"). The emitters now record only
      what the AI saw in both places (§2.2).
      What an original held of `$MDU:` placeholders is kept by name
      (`DualRepr.originalTokens`, never a value), so the agent page and
      the inspector's trace still tell a placeholder the tool merely
      echoed (Mandu's refusal naming the token the AI sent, §4.25b "A
      refusal is not a mask", §4.2f) from one it kept from the AI.
      The payload says which one it is (`valuesShown`). The agent already
      holds everything in the projection, so a program it runs learns
      nothing new from it;
    - `admin`: a service's log, an agent or test run's output, a drill,
      matrix, CI or replay run's files, the drill replay status (its log
      tail), and the human-plane reads that already needed the session
      (§6.x): **403** `ADMIN_SESSION_REQUIRED` before the route runs.
    A GET under `/api/` that no entry names is `admin` (fail closed), and
    a unit test walks server.ts and the route modules for every path they
    match and fails on one the table does not name. "Has the session"
    for a read means `hasAdminSession` (the cookie, Basic-auth
    credentials, or the trusted front, §6.x) AND a same-origin request:
    the `X-Mandu-Control` header (both front-ends send it on every
    fetch) or the browser's own `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin` (or `none`,
    a typed URL), which is how an `EventSource`, which cannot set a
    header, says it. The cookie is `HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict`.
    Signed out, both front-ends still render (`mandu dashboard` opened
    without its link shows the sessions, the counts and the decisions)
    and say where the values went: the inspector's top bar shows
    "Sign in to see real values" and its file, commit and seeded-file
    views say how. Its run logs (Tests › Run a suite and CI, an entry's;
    VM matrix, a run's) and a service's logs fold (Settings › Services) say
    "Sign in to read this log: run `mandu dashboard` …" where the log would
    be, and ▶ Run drills › Replay a drill says "Sign in to replay a drill:
    …" (§4.8, §4.26, §4.27, §4.35). Until 2026-10-09 the run logs read the
    403 as a failure ("could not load the log of fs-sync"), and the fold
    opened on an empty box. A drill's recording (the live drill's player and each side
    of a replay drill's) says "Sign in to watch this recording: …" in place
    of the player, and its 🌱 Prepared workspace "Sign in to see the files
    … started from: …" (§4.22, §4.28); until 2026-10-09 the players mounted
    on the refused URL and showed their 💥 error frame, and the fold said
    the run "is older than the prepared-workspace capture". Its control
    buttons (Settings › Services, + New run, Run a suite, ▶ Run drills)
    answer a click with "Sign in to start a service: run `mandu dashboard`
    …", the verb being the button's (§4.8 "Signed out"). Until 2026-10-09 a
    service row's line was cleared by the repaint after the click, so the
    click changed nothing, and the others printed the server's developer
    text. Its policy writes (Rules' Protection block and Secrets label
    form, Settings › Sandbox and Protection axes) say it the same way
    with their own verbs, "Sign in to change the sandbox: …" (§4.19.v3
    "Signed out"); until 2026-10-09 they printed the server's text too.
    So do its answers (Approvals, Rules › Your answers) and Rules' Add a
    rule, Lists and Test a flow, "Sign in to answer this question: …",
    each kept past the 3 s poll (§4.34 "Signed out"); until 2026-10-09
    they printed the server's text and the next poll erased it.
    The product page's agent page says it above the tiles and
    in place of each "Show what was hidden".
  - **Residuals.** (1) A process of this user that can read the browser's
    profile (the cookie jar) can lift the session cookie; that is the
    same-uid limit every local secret has, and it is why the cookie is
    per boot and per browser session. (2) Cookies are not port-scoped: a
    page served by another local web server on `localhost` could not read
    our responses (the origin differs), but a cookie set by the dashboard
    is sent to any `localhost` port; the dashboard sets only its own
    random value, and reads also need the same-origin header or
    `Sec-Fetch-Site`. (3) The projection keeps what the AI saw, which
    includes a value whose level admits that model (an `any-model`
    secret reaches the model as it is), and another session's AgentView
    text. (4) An e2e session's assertion reasons are the harness's words
    and are served as they are.
  - Tests: `test/unit/client-allowlist.test.ts`, the real-socket
    `test/component/remote-allowlist.test.ts`, and
    `test/component/bind-default.test.ts` (the real entry point: loopback
    default, the refusal, the three authenticators, the empty allowlist);
    the read gate and the Host check: `test/unit/server/read-gate.test.ts`
    (the table, the route registry walk, `sameOriginRead`, `hostAllowed`),
    `test/component/value-gate.test.ts` (every listed read over a real
    socket, signed out and in, a canary in every place a value sits; the
    421s), `test/component/arbiter-source-reveal.test.ts` (signed out,
    the arbiter is asked for no value), the stack e2e
    `tests/stack/dashboard-value-gate.test.ts` (a separate process on the
    host walks every read with every forgeable header and gets no value;
    the human's one-time link then shows it),
    `tests/stack/inspector-logs-signed-out.test.ts` (a real server's log
    routes and replay state refused signed out, the served log views'
    sign-in lines and no log text, each log signed in),
    `tests/stack/inspector-service-logs-signed-out.test.ts` (a real
    supervisor's service log refused signed out, the served logs fold's
    sign-in line over a real refused stream with no log text, the log
    streamed signed in),
    `tests/stack/inspector-actions-signed-out.test.ts` (a real
    supervisor's control routes refused signed out with no service moved,
    the served Services panel's sign-in lines outlasting a poll, Start
    working signed in),
    `tests/stack/inspector-policy-signed-out.test.ts` (a real arbiter's
    level, axis, sandbox, posture and label writes refused signed out with
    nothing changed, the served Protection, Sandbox, Protection axes and
    Secrets lines, the same writes landing signed in),
    `tests/stack/inspector-rules-signed-out.test.ts` (a real arbiter's
    answers, rules, lists and test writes refused signed out with the
    question still waiting and policy.yaml unchanged, the served Approvals
    and Rules lines outlasting a poll, Add rule and Block landing signed
    in),
    `tests/stack/inspector-recordings-signed-out.test.ts` (a real server's
    drill and replay files refused signed out, the served players' and the
    prepared workspace's sign-in lines with no player built and no recorded
    text, the players and the capture signed in),
    `tests/stack/signed-out-symbolize.test.ts` (the real anthropic-proxy
    masks a no-model file: the arbiter's record keeps its bytes only in

### 6.x The admin session and the admin channel

The source-IP allowlist admits loopback and the CSRF header is one line of
`curl`, so neither tells the human's browser from a same-host process the
agent runs. Two mechanisms do (policy-surface.md §2.6):

- **Admin channel to the arbiter.** The supervisor spawns the arbiter with
  an extra stdio socketpair (`MANDU_ADMIN_FD=3`); the arbiter accepts its
  human-decision ops (approvals, labels, posture, session deletion) only on
  that fd, which has no filesystem name. The dashboard's adapters
  (`arbiter-adapter.ts makeApprovalsArbiter`) read over the data socket and
  write over the admin channel (`Supervisor.adminChannel("arbiter")`,
  resolved per call). An adopted arbiter (one the supervisor did not spawn)
  has no channel: those writes answer **503** with the remedy ("restart the
  services from Settings to regain control"), and session deletion behaves
  the same. The arbiter's service definition is a direct node spawn (the
  bundle, or `node --import <tsx> …` from source; §4.8 "How a service is
  started"), never `npm run serve`, because neither the `tsx` binary nor
  `npm` passes an inherited fd through.
- **Admin session for every mutating verb.** After the CSRF check,
  POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE need the admin session (`hasAdminSession`): the
  `mandu_session` cookie (the password session with `DASHBOARD_PASSWORD`;
  without it, a per-boot admin token — `GET <base>/login?token=…` sets the
  cookie), valid Basic-auth credentials (§6.z), or, with
  `DASHBOARD_TRUST_FRONT=1`, a non-loopback allowlisted peer (the
  authenticating front); loopback never qualifies that way. The admin link
  is printed to stderr only on a TTY or with
  `DASHBOARD_PRINT_ADMIN_LINK=1`, because a headless log is readable by the
  same uid. `DASHBOARD_ADMIN_TOKEN` pins the token (visible in
  `/proc/<pid>/environ` to the same uid; use only where acceptable). A
  read that can carry a value needs the same session (§6 "Reads and the
  admin session"). Tests pin the token and derivation secret
  (`test/unit/admin-session.ts`) and send the precomputed cookie with the
  CSRF header.
- **Signing in: one-time links on the human plane (2026-10-05).** The way a
  person gets that cookie in the default flow, where the dashboard is a
  background daemon and nobody sees its stderr (policy-surface.md §2.6
  "Signing in" has the design and the boundary). After `listen()`,
  server-main serves `src/sign-in.ts serveSignInChannel` on
  `<runtime>/human/dashboard-<pid>.sock` (the arbiter's human-plane
  directory, 0700, verified like the arbiter verifies it; the socket 0600)
  and records it in its registry entry as `signInSock`; a dead dashboard's
  socket is swept at the next boot and its own is removed on every
  deliberate exit. Before sweeping, the directory must be private, real
  and owned by this user; a planted link or shared directory is refused
  without deleting anything. The socket answers one op, `signInLink`, with a login
  path `<base>/login?ticket=<128-bit one-time ticket>` (`SignInTickets`,
  12 h, 64 outstanding), or a refusal: `password` / `basic-auth` (the
  credentials are the session), `exposed` (a launch with no wall is on the
  arbiter's record, named) or `unknown` (the exposure could not be read:
  fail closed). `GET /login?ticket=` spends the ticket and sets the cookie;
  a spent, expired or guessed one gets a 403 page that says what to run
  (a browser already holding the session is redirected in). Without a
  password, `GET /login` is that page, never a form. The launcher prints
  the link on its dashboard line and `mandu dashboard` under its URL, both
  only to a terminal (`launcher/src/dashboard-sign-in.ts`). A start without
  the socket (the directory refused, say) logs why and serves on; the
  launcher then says there is no link and why.

### 6.z HTTP Basic auth for an HTTP-only front

An OAuth reverse proxy on another host is an *authenticating* front, which
`DASHBOARD_TRUST_FRONT` models: the peer is non-loopback, allowlisted, and
already checked a human. A tunnel whose client runs on the dashboard's own
host (for example `cloudflared`) connects from **loopback** and carries no
authentication. Trust-front must not admit loopback (it is the address the
agent's processes use), and the cookie-form password is not HTTP
authentication.

`DASHBOARD_BASIC_AUTH="user:password"` (the `basicAuth` option on
`DashboardServer`; the first `:` splits) adds RFC 7617 Basic auth:

- Gate order in `handle()`: source-IP allowlist → **Basic auth** → `/login`
  routes → password session (`isAuthed`) → CSRF + admin session for
  mutating verbs. A request without valid credentials gets `401` with
  `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="Mandu dashboard"` and a bare
  "Unauthorized" body on every route, so nothing of the app leaks first.
- Valid credentials **are the admin session**: the browser resends them on
  every same-origin `fetch` and `EventSource`, so approvals, labels,
  posture, deletion and the Settings control plane work through the tunnel
  with no cookie and no admin link. The §6.x human/agent boundary holds: a
  same-host process cannot present credentials that exist only in this
  process's environment and the operator's browser (the same same-uid
  `/proc/<pid>/environ` caveat as `DASHBOARD_ADMIN_TOKEN`).
- The comparison is constant-time on the decoded bytes; a wrong user, wrong
  password, truncated value or garbled header is the same 401.
- A malformed value (no `:`, empty user) **refuses to start** (exit 2): a
  typo must never fall through to an unauthenticated server that reveals
  originals. `DASHBOARD_PASSWORD` may be set alongside (both then apply).

Tests: `test/unit/basic-auth.test.ts` (the challenge on every route, wrong
or garbled credentials, credentials as admin session with the CSRF gate
still first, the base-path form, inert without the option) and
`test/component/basic-auth.test.ts` (the real entry point: 401 → 200, no
admin link in the log, a malformed value → exit 2).

**Deployment.** A remote deployment keeps its settings in an env file
(mode 600, never committed) — `DASHBOARD_BASIC_AUTH`,
`DASHBOARD_HOST=0.0.0.0`, `DASHBOARD_ALLOW_HOSTS=<proxy IP>`, and
`DASHBOARD_BASE_PATH` when a proxy mounts it under a prefix (the default is
none). The file is `~/.mandu/dashboard.env`, the path table's
`dashboard-env` entry (on-disk-layout.md §5), so `mandu paths` lists it; the
live suites read their credentials from it (`tests/lib/dashboard-auth.ts`).
The server routes `<prefix>/api/...` and `/api/...` alike, so one process
serves a prefixed proxy and an unprefixed tunnel. The prefix is stripped
only at a path-segment boundary (`stripBasePath`): with prefix `/mandu`,
`/mandu/x` and `/mandu?q` are prefixed but `/mandu.css` is the stylesheet.

### 6.y Two tenants, one store per request

policy-surface.md §2.7. The supervisor runs a fifth service,
`test-arbiter`: the test-tenant arbiter with its own socket
(`<base>/test/arbiter.sock`), symbol DB and event directory (path-table
entries `symbol-db-test`, `events-test`); the live arbiter runs with
`MANDU_TENANT=live`. Test runs land in the test arbiter; `POST /api/test`
ensures it, never the live one. Its Start / Restart / Stop / logs use the
same `/api/control/<id>/…` routes as every service, which accept exactly
the supervisor's `SERVICE_IDS` (`control-test-arbiter.test.ts`), from its
own row in the inspector's Settings › Services (§4.8 *One row per
supervised service*).

The server holds a second event source and arbiter surfaces for the test
tenant (`DashboardServerOptions.testTenant`) and serves every request from
one tenant: `?tenant=` wins, else the `mandu_tenant` cookie, else live.
`GET /api/tenants` → `{tenants, current}`. The inspector crosses tenants
only on its **Tests** page (§4.32: the test arbiter's store when one exists,
else the live store's test-tagged sessions); Sessions, Drills and Approvals
are the live store. The cookie is set ONLY while Tests is open and a test
store exists: entering Tests sets it and reloads, leaving Tests deletes it
(`Max-Age=0`, not `=live`) and reloads, and a page that finds the wrong
store at boot fixes it the same way, except a bare `/dev/` under a leftover
test cookie, which shows Tests rather than reload away from it. A reload
that did not take (cookies blocked) is not retried (`mandu.tenantSwitch` in
sessionStorage). On Tests `body.tenant-test` tints the top bar and the title
gains `[TEST] `. A stale test cookie on a live-only dashboard falls back to
live; an explicit `?tenant=test` there is 404.

**The cookie is the inspector's; the product never reads it.** The cookie
is set with `Path=/`, and the API sits under `/api/` for both front-ends, so
a cookie left by a visit to Tests would otherwise swap the person's own
agents on the product page for the test harness's (and with the test
arbiter stopped, fail the product's Home). The rule (`src/server/tenant.ts`,
`requestedTenant`):

- `?tenant=` (explicit) wins for every request: the choice is in the URL, so
  it is never a leftover.
- A PRODUCT request is served for live whatever the cookie says: a request
  to a route only the product reads (`/api/home`, `/api/home/agent`;
  `PRODUCT_ONLY_ROUTES`), or one carrying `X-Mandu-Front: product`, which
  every fetch of `public/js/home.js` sends (the routes it shares with the
  inspector, such as `/api/policy/panel`, `/api/egress/approvals` or
  `/api/secrets`, cannot tell the pages apart by path). `GET /api/tenants`
  answers `current: "live"` to it too.
- Every other request (the inspector's fetches and SSE streams) follows the
  cookie.

A header and not a cookie path: a cookie scoped to `/dev/` would never reach
`/api/`, and the inspector's EventSource streams cannot carry a header, so
the opt-out is the product's. It is not a security boundary: both stores
sit behind the same gates and are served to the same signed-in person; a
client that forges the header only gets the live store.

**An unreachable tenant answers 503, not 500.** When a tenant's event source
cannot reach its arbiter (a refused or missing socket, a socket closed
before the reply, or no human plane; `isArbiterUnreachable`), the server
answers `503 {error, tenant, unreachable: true}` (`unreachableBody`): the
error names the tenant, the cause and what to start ("start test-arbiter
under Services, or leave the Tests view for the live store"), and the
server logs one line for it. Every other handler failure stays a 500. The
product's Home reads the flag and says "The protection service is not
running, so nothing can be checked. Start it under Settings …" in its own
words (the server's text names the arbiter, an inspector word; since
2026-10-10 without the request and its status, §4.25 *The hero says why in
words*),
and any other product request answered this way, or with the failed dial
itself, says so too, with "Start it under Settings" a link (§4.25
"Refusals"). The inspector's banner and status line read the same flag
(§4.35).

Tests: `tenant-routing.test.ts` (the product routes and the header ignore
the cookie, `?tenant=` still wins, the 503 over a real
`ArbiterEventSource` on a socket nobody listens on, other failures still
500, the pure resolver), `home-js-home.test.ts` (every product request
carries the header; the 503 sentence), `app-js-sidebar.test.ts` (the test
cookie only on Tests, the no-loop guard), `test-tenant-paths.test.ts`,
`tenant-classification.test.ts`.

## 7. Testing (required by CONTRIBUTING.md)

Both unit and end-to-end tests, per [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](../../../CONTRIBUTING.md)
(every change adds or updates both; the e2e suite is the security-invariant
oracle).

### 7.1 Unit tests (`arbiter/test/unit/` + `dashboard/test/unit/`)

- **Event-schema construction.** A builder yields a well-formed
  `ManduEvent` per `EventKind`; `DualRepr.differs` agrees with
  `symbolized !== original`; `symbols[]` provenance round-trips a
  `SymbolEntry`.
- **View tagging.** An untrusted `fs_action` read → `AgentView`, its
  HumanFS sync → `HumanView`; `ullm_call` → `Quarantine`; `tllm_call` →
  `AgentView`; `exec_action` with `policy.shell=HumanShell` → `HumanView`.
- **Symbol provenance rendering.** A `SymbolRef` renders name, tool, field
  and origin; the privileged reveal calls the arbiter's `resolve`; `escSym`
  highlights `$MDU:*`; an event with `original=null` renders "(revealed on
  demand)", not a blank.
- **Invariant flag rendering.** `violatedInvariant=true` ⇒ red banner,
  flared card and quoted `detail`; all false ⇒ green. The UI never computes
  the verdict, it renders the flag.
- **IPC ops.** `emit` appends and `events` reads it back; paging by
  `sinceSeq` is monotonic; framing matches the NDJSON protocol.

### 7.2 E2E test (`dashboard/test/component/dashboard-stream.test.ts`)

A fixture NDJSON trace of a stored-IPI session (the canonical
`ManduEvent` stream) goes through the real `FileEventSource` and the real
HTTP server, and the test asserts the served view model:

1. the stream contains `tllm_call`, `tool_use`, `tool_result` and
   `ullm_call` events;
2. each event is view-labelled correctly (T-LLM and tool events
   `AgentView`, `ullm_call` `Quarantine`, egress `HumanView`);
3. every untrusted-bearing `DualRepr` has `differs===true`, `$MDU:*` in
   `symbolized` and the raw payload in `original`, so both representations
   are available;
4. T-LLM and U-LLM are distinguishable by `kind` + `view`, each with input
   and output;
5. the oracle holds: no event has `violatedInvariant`, and the attack
   payload appears in some `original` but never un-symbolized in a
   `tllm_call` input. A second fixture with a violated event turns the
   banner red.

### 7.3 Dovetail with the §9 invariant oracle

The `violatedInvariant` flag is the same predicate the e2e oracle of
implementation-plan.md §9 asserts (no un-symbolized protected byte in a
model request): the proxy computes it once at emit time, the §9 tests
assert it over the model requests, and the dashboard renders it. The §7.2
test is a presentation of that oracle and shares its corpus rather than
duplicating it.
